48.s: The chaitya and vihara forms developed during the Satavahana period are significant because they:
o: Replaced all structural temples during the Gupta period
Became the base for later Hindu temple architecture
Were used exclusively for Jain religious architecture
Originated only after the construction of the Sanchi gateway
48.x: Satavahana chaitya-vihara forms became the base for later Hindu temple architecture. They were not exclusive to Jain architecture and did not replace all structural temples.
48.tq: Infer the architectural consequence from the stated continuity between Buddhist and Hindu forms.

48.s: Who built the earliest structural Hindu temples referred to in the context of the transition from chaitya-vihara architecture?
48.x: The Ikshvakus built the earliest structural Hindu temples, while Satavahana chaitya-vihara forms provided an architectural base for later Hindu temple architecture.
48.tq: Use the builder–achievement association and avoid swapping neighbouring dynasties.

48.s: The only rock-cut Buddhist cave temple in Andhra Pradesh is identified with:
48.x: Guntupalli is identified as the only rock-cut Buddhist cave temple in Andhra Pradesh.
48.tq: Use the FIRST/LAST or ONLY clue to distinguish unique sites.

48.s:
Which of the following statements about the present cultural and political significance of Amaravati is correct?
1. Amaravati was a Satavahana capital.
2. Amaravati is associated with the Mahachaitya.
3. Amaravati is the modern capital of Andhra Pradesh.
4. Amaravati is listed among India’s three major ancient art schools.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
48.x: Amaravati is described as a Satavahana capital, the site of the Mahachaitya, the modern capital of Andhra Pradesh, and one of India’s three major ancient art schools.
48.tq: Check every item in a multi-dimensional place profile before selecting the inclusive code.

48.s: The Buddha is traditionally believed to have taught the Kalachakra at Amaravati, which is also known by the ancient name:
48.x: Amaravati is identified with ancient Dhanyakataka, where the Buddha is believed to have taught the Kalachakra.
48.tq: Discriminate between ancient place names associated with major Buddhist centres.

48.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Sarnath becomes India’s 45th World Heritage Site
B. Andhra Pradesh is named Best Tourism Promotion State at the GTM awards
C. The Buddhist International Tourism Circuit is listed in the AP Socio-Economic Survey
D. The Discover Andhra Buddhist-circuit campaign is launched
48.x: The order is the listing in the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025–26, the February 2026 Discover Andhra campaign, the May 2026 GTM award, and Sarnath’s designation on 27 July 2026.
48.tq: Arrange events by their stated years and months, using the earliest dated event first.

48.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the heritage status of Buddhist sites is correct?
o: Sarnath and Amaravati Stupa are both permanently inscribed as World Heritage Sites, whereas Odisha’s Buddhist sites have no heritage listing.
Amaravati Stupa is already India’s 45th World Heritage Site, while Sarnath is only on the tentative list.
Only Ratnagiri has been placed on the UNESCO tentative list, while Amaravati Stupa has been excluded from it.
Amaravati Stupa is on India’s UNESCO tentative list, while Ratnagiri-Udayagiri-Lalitagiri in Odisha have also been placed on the tentative list.
48.x: Amaravati Stupa is on India’s UNESCO tentative list, and Odisha’s Ratnagiri-Udayagiri-Lalitagiri have also been placed on the tentative list. Sarnath is identified separately as India’s 45th World Heritage Site.
48.tq: Separate tentative-list status from full World Heritage inscription.

48.s: The sea-trade text associated with the Reddi period is:
48.x: Haravilasam is the text associated with Reddi-period sea trade in this context. Kashikhandam is a different text and is not the required answer here.
48.tq: Distinguish the specifically associated literary work from a closely related textual distractor.

48.s: Which recent legislative development concerns Amaravati?
o: A Bill was cleared to transfer the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh from Amaravati to Nagarjunakonda.
A constitutional amendment declared Amaravati a Union Territory.
A Bill was cleared to make Amaravati the sole capital of Telangana.
A Bill was cleared to make Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
48.x: The Lok Sabha cleared a Bill making Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
48.tq: Identify the correct authority–decision–place combination and reject State-swapping traps.

49.s: Which one of the following works is associated with Acharya Nagarjuna?
49.x: Suhrullekha, meaning ‘friendly letter’, is one of the works associated with Acharya Nagarjuna.
49.tq: Use direct author–work identification and distinguish Buddhist works from Jain and literary works.

49.s: Sriparvata, associated with Acharya Nagarjuna, is identified with which of the following places?
49.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda. Yajna Sri Satakarni built a vihara or Mahachaitya there for Nagarjuna.
49.tq: Distinguish the place associated with Nagarjuna from other Andhra religious centres.

49.s: Yajna Sri Satakarni is said to have built the Sriparvata vihara or Mahachaitya for Nagarjuna with approximately how many rooms?
49.x: The Sriparvata vihara or Mahachaitya built for Nagarjuna is stated to have had 1,500 rooms.
49.tq: Use the numerical-value options to recall the specific size of the vihara.

49.s:
Acharya Nagarjuna was known by which of the following titles?
1. Second Buddha
2. Indian Martin Luther
3. Indian Einstein
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
49.x: All three titles—‘Second Buddha’, ‘Indian Martin Luther’ and ‘Indian Einstein’—are associated with Acharya Nagarjuna.
49.tq: Treat a group of epithets as separate factual statements and verify each one.

49.s: Which of the following statements regarding Nagarjuna in literary traditions is correct?
o: Kathasaritsagara says that he was killed by a Satavahana prince, while Lilavati Parinayam mentions Satavahana patronage of him.
Kathasaritsagara identifies him as a Jain teacher and Lilavati Parinayam as a Vedic priest.
Both Kathasaritsagara and Lilavati Parinayam state that he founded the Satavahana dynasty.
Both works place him exclusively under Mauryan patronage.
49.x: Kathasaritsagara states that Nagarjuna was killed by a Satavahana prince, whereas Lilavati Parinayam refers to his patronage by a Satavahana king.
49.tq: Compare the claims of two literary sources without reversing their accounts.

49.s: The Parasurameswara temple, associated with the oldest Shivalinga of the Satavahana period, is located at:
49.x: The Parasurameswara temple is at Gudimallam in the present Chittoor, now Tirupati, district, and contains the oldest Shivalinga of the Satavahana period.
49.tq: Use the exact site rather than nearby-place distractors.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gudimallam — main centre of the Mahasanghika sect
49.x: Gudimallam is associated with the Parasurameswara temple and the oldest Satavahana-period Shivalinga. The Mahasanghika sect had its main centre at Dhanyakataka, not Gudimallam.
49.tq: Find the one misplaced religious association among closely related Andhra locations.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Naneghat inscription:
1. It was issued by Devi Naganika.
2. Naganika was the wife of Satakarni I.
3. It was composed in Prakrit.
4. Naganika was the daughter of Maharathi Tranakayiro.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All four statements are correct. The Naneghat inscription of Devi Naganika was in Prakrit; she was the wife of Satakarni I and daughter of Maharathi Tranakayiro.
49.tq: Verify the issuer, family relationships and language separately before selecting the combination.

49.s: Which set of sacrifices is recorded in the Naneghat inscription as having been performed by Satakarni I?
o: Two Rajasuya sacrifices and one Ashvamedha
One Ashvamedha, one Vajapeya and one Rajasuya
49.x: The Naneghat inscription records two Ashvamedha sacrifices and one Rajasuya performed by Satakarni I.
49.tq: Separate the number and type of sacrifices instead of relying on a general association with Vedic rituals.

49.s: The gifts made to Brahmins by Satakarni I, as recorded in the Naneghat inscription, included:
49.x: Satakarni I gave cows, land and gold to Brahmins in connection with the Vedic sacrifices recorded in the inscription.
49.tq: Identify the precise gift category rather than a broadly religious but unsupported alternative.

49.s: Which of the following titles is associated with Satakarni I in the Naneghat inscription?
49.x: Satakarni I is described as Apratihatachakra and Dakshinapathapati. Agama Nilaya is used for Gautamiputra in the Nasik inscription.
49.tq: Separate titles belonging to different rulers and inscriptions.

49.s: Which of the following correctly gives the sons of Satakarni I mentioned in the Naneghat inscription?
49.x: The sons named in the inscription are Vedasiri, Hakusiri and Kumara Satavahana; Vedasiri is identified as the eldest.
49.tq: Use family-list recall and avoid substituting other Satavahana rulers.

49.s: Which of the following groups consists only of Satavahana rulers associated with the performance of yajnas?
o: Satakarni I, Subendran, Gautamiputra and Hala
Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri
Krishna, Pulumavi II, Nagarjuna and Yajna Sri
Satakarni II, Kundakunda, Krishna and Pulumavi II
49.x: The rulers associated with yajnas are Satakarni I, Satakarni II, Gautamiputra and Yajna Sri. The names Vedasri and Yajnasri also reflect Vedic religious affiliation.
49.tq: Identify the complete ruler group and reject names belonging to other religious or literary contexts.

49.s: In the Nasik inscription, Gautamiputra Satakarni is described as:
49.x: The Nasik inscription calls Gautamiputra Satakarni Agama nilaya, meaning an abode of traditional learning.
49.tq: Distinguish the title in the Nasik inscription from the titles in the Naneghat inscription.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about religious patronage under the Satavahanas:
1. Kings generally followed the Vedic religion.
2. Queens are particularly associated with patronage of Buddhism.
3. Royal patronage was the only source of support for Buddhism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Buddhism relied more on public support than on royal support, so statement 3 is false.
49.tq: Watch for the absolute claim ‘only’ when distinguishing royal and public support.

49.s: Gautami Balasri’s Buddhist patronage included which of the following?
o: A cave vihara at Nasik for the Bhadrayaniya sect
A village at Karle for Mahasanghika monks
A vihara at Sriparvata for Nagarjuna
Toranas at Sanchi for the Chaityaka sect
49.x: Gautami Balasri donated a cave vihara at Nasik for the Bhadrayaniya sect, reportedly for the recovery of her son.
49.tq: Start from the sure patron–gift pair and distinguish it from the other royal donations.

49.s: Which Satavahana ruler is associated with the donation of a village to Mahasanghika monks at Karle?
49.x: Pulumavi II donated a village to Mahasanghika monks at Karle.
49.tq: Use the donor–site association rather than confusing Karle with Nasik or Sriparvata.

49.s: Krishna, the second Satavahana king, is associated with which of the following acts?
o: Donating a village at Karle to Mahasanghika monks
Building the Sriparvata Mahachaitya for Nagarjuna
Donating a Nasik cave for shramanas and appointing a Dharma Mahamatra
Recording two Ashvamedhas and a Rajasuya
49.x: Krishna donated a Nasik cave for shramanas and appointed a Dharma Mahamatra. The other acts are associated with different rulers.
49.tq: Apply the who-did-what method to distinguish royal religious patronage.

49.s: Which one of the following statements about Buddhist cave sites is correct?
o: Kanheri is the only rock-cut Buddhist cave site in Andhra Pradesh.
Guntupalli, Karle and Kanheri are all located in Andhra Pradesh.
Nasik is the only rock-cut Buddhist cave site in Andhra, while Guntupalli is in Maharashtra.
Guntupalli is the only rock-cut Buddhist cave site in Andhra, while Nasik, Karle and Kanheri are in Maharashtra.
49.x: Guntupalli is identified as the only rock-cut Buddhist cave site in Andhra. Nasik, Karle and Kanheri are located in Maharashtra.
49.tq: Use location contrast to eliminate swapped regional associations.

49.s: Who founded the Chaityaka or Chaityakavada sect in Andhra?
49.x: The Chaityaka sect was founded by Mahadeva Bhikshu, regarded as the first Buddhist acharya in Andhra.
49.tq: Identify the founder from a list containing figures associated with other religious traditions.

49.s: The Chaityaka sect was primarily centred on the worship of:
49.x: Chaityaka or Chaityakavada was centred on the worship of chaityas.
49.tq: Match the sect name with its defining religious practice.

49.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
49.x: Dhanyakataka was the main centre of the Mahasanghika sect. Rajagirika was associated with Sriparvatam and Bhadrayaniya with Nasik.
49.tq: Begin with the known sect–centre pair and test the geographical distractors.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Purvasaila and Aparasaila were associated with the hills around Dhanyakataka.
2. Rajagirika was centred at Sriparvatam.
3. Bhadrayaniya was associated with Nasik.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. These sects were associated respectively with the Dhanyakataka hills, Sriparvatam and Nasik.
49.tq: Test several sect–centre relationships together and identify the complete correct combination.

49.s: Which of the following statements regarding Buddhism in Andhra is correct?
o: Buddhism in Andhra was confined exclusively to royal families.
Buddhism reached Andhra in the sixth century BC, and its local form was called Andhra Buddhism.
Buddhism reached Andhra only during the Gupta period and was called Bhagavata Buddhism.
Buddhism reached Andhra in the first century AD and rejected Pratitya Samutpada.
49.x: Buddhism reached Andhra in the sixth century BC, and its local form came to be called Andhra Buddhism. The Pratitya Samutpada doctrine was followed.
49.tq: Use the date and distinctive regional label together to identify the correct statement.

49.s: According to Tibetan tradition, the Buddha preached at Amaravati at the request of which king?
49.x: Tibetan tradition states that the Buddha preached at Amaravati at the request of King Subendran.
49.tq: Distinguish the traditional patron of the Buddha’s visit from later Satavahana rulers.

49.s: Which doctrine was followed by the Buddhist tradition in Andhra?
o: Sunyavada alone as a Jain doctrine
49.x: The Buddhist tradition in Andhra followed the doctrine of Pratitya Samutpada. Syadvada is associated with Jainism, while Bhagavata is a Vaishnava tradition.
49.tq: Separate similar-sounding doctrines belonging to Buddhism, Jainism and Bhagavatism.

49.s: The Naneghat inscription invokes which of the following combinations of deities?
o: Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Nagarjuna, Kundakunda and Yama
Indra, Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Surya, Chandra, Yama and Varuna
Shiva, Gauri, Buddha, Mahavira, Surya and Chandra
Buddha, Mahavira, Indra, Ganesha, Krishna and Skanda
49.x: The inscription invokes Indra, Vasudeva, Sankarshana, Surya, Chandra, Yama and Varuna, combining Vedic and Bhagavata elements.
49.tq: Recall the complete deity list and reject names not present in the inscription.

49.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the distinction in the Naneghat inscription?
o: Indra and Varuna — Bhagavata deities; Vasudeva and Sankarshana — Vedic deities
Indra, Yama and Varuna — Vedic deities; Vasudeva and Sankarshana — Bhagavata deities
Vasudeva and Sankarshana — Jain deities; Yama and Varuna — Buddhist deities
All the invoked deities — exclusively Buddhist deities
49.x: The inscription combines Vedic deities such as Indra, Yama and Varuna with Bhagavata deities Vasudeva and Sankarshana.
49.tq: Classify the deities rather than merely recalling their names.

49.s: Which of the following statements about Bhagavata religion is correct?
o: It was founded by Nagarjuna and centred at Sriparvata.
It was founded by Kundakundacharya and centred at Konakondla.
It was founded by Vasudeva-Krishna and was centred at Mathura.
It was founded by Mahadeva Bhikshu and centred at Dhanyakataka.
49.x: Bhagavata religion was founded by Vasudeva-Krishna and centred at Mathura.
49.tq: Use the founder–centre combination to distinguish Bhagavatism from Buddhist and Jain traditions.

49.s:
Arrange the following developments in the correct chronological order as indicated by the material:
A. Bhagavata religion became known as the Vasudeva religion by the time of Hala.
B. Bhagavata religion reached Andhra under Krishna, the second Satavahana king.
C. Gautamiputra’s inscriptions carried Bhagavata symbols.
Choose the correct sequence.
49.x: Bhagavata religion reached Andhra under Krishna, became the Vasudeva religion by Hala’s time, and Bhagavata symbols are noted in Gautamiputra’s inscriptions.
49.tq: Arrange the developments by the rulers and period markers associated with them.

49.s: Which of the following groups includes all the categories of donors to the Buddhist sangha mentioned in the material?
o: Landlords, soldiers and temple priests only
Only foreign rulers and Buddhist monks
Kings, queens, officials, merchants, guilds, artisans and independent women
49.x: Donors included kings, queens, officials, merchants, guilds such as ivory workers and coral dealers, artisans and independent women.
49.tq: Recall the broad social composition of donors and avoid the royal-only trap.

49.s: Guilds at Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri supported monks by:
o: Issuing gold coins exclusively for Buddhist rituals
Compulsorily collecting taxes from villages for monasteries
Replacing monasteries with Vedic sacrificial centres
Holding money on deposit and giving the interest to monks
49.x: Guilds held money on deposit and gave the interest to monks. Ushavadata’s deposit with the Govardhana weavers is an example.
49.tq: Apply the institutional deposit-and-interest mechanism to the stated historical context.

49.s: Ushavadata’s deposit with the Govardhana weavers illustrates which form of Buddhist support?
o: Guild-based financial support through interest on deposits
A Vedic donation of cows to Brahmins
A Jain endowment made by Kundakunda
49.x: The deposit with the Govardhana weavers illustrates how guilds placed money on deposit and transferred the interest to Buddhist monks.
49.tq: Identify the example that represents guild finance rather than royal or sectarian patronage.

49.s: The Alluru inscription is associated with donations made by:
49.x: The Alluru inscription of the Ikshvaku Virapurushadatta records donations to many communities and institutions.
49.tq: Use the inscription–ruler association and avoid substituting a Satavahana donor.

49.s: Kundakundacharya, associated with Konakondla in Anantapur, is known for preaching:
49.x: Kundakundacharya was a Jain teacher associated with Konakondla and preached Syadvada.
49.tq: Distinguish the Jain doctrine Syadvada from the Buddhist doctrines Sunyavada and Pratitya Samutpada.

49.s: Which work is associated with Kundakundacharya?
49.x: Samayasara is associated with the Jain teacher Kundakundacharya. The other works are associated with Acharya Nagarjuna.
49.tq: Separate Jain author–work pairs from Nagarjuna’s Buddhist works.

49.s: Which statement best reflects the religious patronage of royal women in Satavahana Andhra?
o: They were excluded from all forms of religious patronage.
They patronised Buddhism but could also patronise Jainism.
They supported only Bhagavata religion and opposed Buddhism.
They patronised only Vedic sacrifices and never supported heterodox religions.
49.x: Royal women patronised Buddhism and, according to the stated account, also patronised Jainism. This indicates a wider pattern of religious pluralism.
49.tq: Reject exclusive formulations and apply the broader pattern of royal women’s patronage.

49.s: Which of the following correctly expresses the religious significance of the Satavahana period in Andhra?
o: It reflects the complete replacement of Brahmanism by Buddhism.
It reflects religious pluralism, with patronage of both Brahmanism and Buddhism.
It reflects exclusive royal support for Jainism.
It reflects the absence of public participation in religion.
49.x: The period is characterised by religious pluralism, including Brahmanical practices such as the Ashvamedha and Buddhist centres such as Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
49.tq: Select the balanced interpretation instead of an exclusive religious conclusion.

49.s: Which of the following is the correct set of major Andhra anchors associated with Satavahana religious history?
49.x: The principal Andhra anchors are Amaravati/Dhanyakataka, Sriparvata and Gudimallam. Karle, Bhaja and Kanheri are western Indian cave sites, while Naneghat is an inscriptional site.
49.tq: Use the regional anchor approach to distinguish Andhra sites from Maharashtra and wider Indian sites.

49.s: Why did Prakrit contribute to the spread of Buddhism as a mass movement in the Satavahana region?
o: It replaced all local languages through royal compulsion.
It was restricted to royal inscriptions and excluded ordinary people.
It was the language of the people and therefore improved popular communication.
It was used only for Vedic sacrifices conducted by Brahmins.
49.x: Prakrit, described as the people’s language, helped Buddhism communicate beyond elite circles and become a mass movement.
49.tq: Link the linguistic characteristic directly with its social and religious consequence.

49.s: According to the stated current-affairs linkage, Yavana merchants funded caves at which of the following places?
o: Karle, Bhaja, Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri
Naneghat, Sriparvata, Alluru and Guntupalli only
49.x: Yavana merchants are associated with funding caves at Karle, Bhaja, Nasik, Junnar and Kanheri.
49.tq: Recall the complete donor–cave-site list and avoid mixing it with Andhra religious centres.

50.s: The Ikshvakus ruled approximately during which period?
50.x: The Ikshvaku rule lasted approximately 75 years, from about AD 225 to 300.
50.tq: Use the approximate chronological range and distinguish it from the broader century description.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about the number of Ikshvaku rulers:
1. The Puranas list seven Ikshvaku kings.
2. Inscriptions confirm four Ikshvaku rulers.
3. APP Part 2 mentions eight kings and five rulers confirmed by inscriptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: The Puranic tradition lists seven kings, while inscriptions confirm four. APP Part 2 gives the alternative figures of eight kings and five inscriptionally confirmed rulers.
50.tq: Split the options by checking each numerical statement independently.

50.s: Who among the following was the founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty at Vijayapuri?
50.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Chamtamula, also called Santamula, founded the Ikshvaku kingdom at Vijayapuri.
50.tq: Use the founder–dynasty association and eliminate later rulers.

50.s: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula is particularly associated with which of the following measures for agricultural development?
o: Gifts of land, ploughs, bullocks and cows
Granting ports exclusively to Buddhist monasteries
Distribution of salt, iron and horses
Construction of irrigation dams by Roman engineers
50.x: Chamtamula attempted to make the intelligentsia partners in agricultural development by giving land, ploughs, bullocks and cows.
50.tq: Identify the concrete instruments linked with the stated policy objective.

50.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler is associated with the golden age of Buddhism and the large-scale donations of royal queens?
50.x: The reign of Virapurushadatta is regarded as the golden age of Buddhism under the Ikshvakus, and his queens were important donors.
50.tq: Match the ruler with the distinctive contribution rather than with the dynasty generally.

50.s: Ehuvala Chamtamula was the son of:
50.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula was the son of Virapurushadatta and Bhatti Mahadevi.
50.tq: Apply the parentage trap by distinguishing successive rulers and their queens.

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Chamtamula — last ruler defeated by Simhavarman
Ehuvala Chamtamula — ruled for about 24 years
50.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula, son of Virapurushadatta, ruled for approximately 24 years.
50.tq: Find the correctly matched ruler–career detail among swapped dynastic associations.

50.s: Which development is attributed to the reign of Ehuvala Chamtamula?
o: The first issue of Roman coins in Andhra
The first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands
The transfer of the capital to Amaravati
The conquest of Vijayapuri by the Pallavas
50.x: The first Sanskrit inscriptions in the Telugu lands are associated with Ehuvala Chamtamula.
50.tq: Use the ‘first’ associated with a specific ruler, not with the dynasty as a whole.

50.s: The Gummadidurru inscription belongs to the reign of:
50.x: The Gummadidurru inscription is associated with Ehuvala Chamtamula.
50.tq: Link the inscription to its issuer or ruling period rather than to the dynasty generally.

50.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
50.x: Sri Parvatadhipati was a title of Virapurushadatta, while Gosatasahasra and Halasatasahasra were titles of Chamtamula. Andhrabhrityas was a Puranic name for the Ikshvakus, not a specific title of Ehuvala Chamtamula.
50.tq: Check whether each title is attached to the correct ruler rather than to the dynasty.

50.s: The terms ‘Sri Parvatiyas’ and ‘Andhrabhrityas’ in the Puranic tradition refer to the:
50.x: The Puranas refer to the Ikshvakus as Sri Parvatiyas or Sri Parvatiya Andhras and as Andhrabhrityas.
50.tq: Discriminate between similar dynastic names by identifying the Puranic designation.

50.s: The name ‘Ikshvaku’ has been connected by B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao with which word?
50.x: B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao connected the name Ikshvaku with ikshu, meaning sugarcane.
50.tq: Test the exact etymological association rather than a similar-looking word.

50.s: Which combination correctly represents the symbol and royal language of the Ikshvakus?
50.x: The lion was the Ikshvaku symbol and Prakrit was their royal language.
50.tq: Start from the sure symbol–language pair and reject swapped cultural attributes.

50.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Inscription)
A. Nagarjunakonda
B. Alluru
C. Manchikallu
D. Mayidavolu

List-II (Association)
1. Pallava rule over Andhrapatha after the Ikshvakus
2. Santamula founded the kingdom at Vijayapuri
3. Pallava conquest of Vijayapuri
4. Donations to many communities and Satavahana feudatory status

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: The Nagarjunakonda inscription records Santamula’s foundation of the kingdom; Alluru records donations and feudatory status; Manchikallu records the Pallava conquest; Mayidavolu records Pallava rule over Andhrapatha.
50.tq: Start from the distinctive conquest and post-Ikshvaku rule associations, then complete the code.

50.s: Which inscription records that Santamula founded the kingdom at Vijayapuri?
50.x: The Nagarjunakonda inscription of Virapurushadatta records that Santamula founded the kingdom at Vijayapuri.
50.tq: Identify the inscription from the specific historical event recorded in it.

50.s: Which inscription indicates that the Ikshvakus had been feudatories of the Satavahanas?
50.x: The Alluru inscription records donations to several communities and states the Satavahana feudatory connection of the Ikshvakus.
50.tq: Associate the political relationship with the inscription that records it.

50.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Jaggayyapeta inscription is associated with Buddhist donations.
2. The Gurazala inscription belongs to the last phase of the Ikshvaku dynasty.
3. The Manchikallu inscription records the conquest of Vijayapuri by Pallava Simhavarman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. Jaggayyapeta records Buddhist donations, Gurazala belongs to the dynasty’s last phase, and Manchikallu records Simhavarman’s conquest of Vijayapuri.
50.tq: Verify each inscription–content association before selecting the combined code.

50.s: The Mayidavolu inscription was issued by Pallava Sivaskandavarman in approximately:
50.x: The Mayidavolu inscription was issued by Pallava Sivaskandavarman in Prakrit around AD 300 and refers to Pallava rule over Andhrapatha after the Ikshvakus.
50.tq: Use the inscription’s approximate date to distinguish the end of Ikshvaku rule from later Andhra dynasties.

50.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the fall of the Ikshvakus:
1. Rudrapurushadatta was defeated by Pallava Simhavarman.
2. The land south of the Krishna went to the Pallavas.
3. The land north of the Krishna went to the Brihatpalayanas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: All three statements are correct. Simhavarman defeated Rudrapurushadatta; after the fall, the Pallavas controlled the territory south of the Krishna and the Brihatpalayanas the territory to its north.
50.tq: Combine the military event with the geographically divided succession of territories.

50.s: Which of the following statements about the capital of the Ikshvakus is correct?
o: Vijayapuri was located north of the Krishna and was excavated by Rapson.
Vijayapuri was situated at Amaravati and was excavated by B.S.L. Hanumantha Rao.
Vijayapuri was situated in the Nagarjuna Sagar valley and was excavated by R. Subrahmanyam.
Vijayapuri was situated on the coast and was excavated by Pallava Sivaskandavarman.
50.x: Vijayapuri, identified with modern Nagarjunakonda, lies in the Nagarjuna Sagar valley and was excavated by R. Subrahmanyam.
50.tq: Use the location–archaeologist combination to avoid confusing the capital with other Andhra sites.

50.s: Which of the following archaeological features was found at Vijayapuri?
o: A Roman-style amphitheatre and an Ashvamedha platform
A Pallava fort and a Jain cave complex
A Gupta iron pillar and a Buddhist chaitya only
A Chola dockyard and a Vedic altar only
50.x: Excavations at Vijayapuri revealed an amphitheatre, possibly built with Roman help, and an Ashvamedha platform.
50.tq: Identify the archaeological pair that belongs to the same site.

50.s: Which scholar is associated with the view that the Ikshvakus were Telugu or Andhra people?
50.x: Gopalachari is associated with the view that the Ikshvakus were Telugu or Andhra people, though the APP material also records a differing attribution to Caldwell.
50.tq: Distinguish the proponent of the Andhra-origin theory from scholars supporting other origin theories.

50.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Theory)
A. North Indian origin
B. Kannada origin
C. Kshatriya or mixed Kshatriya-Brahmin origin
D. Telugu/Andhra origin

List-II (Proponent)
1. Vogel
2. D.R. Bhandarkar
3. Rapson and Buhler
4. Gopalachari

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: Rapson and Buhler supported a North Indian origin; Vogel a Kannada origin; D.R. Bhandarkar a Kshatriya or mixed Kshatriya-Brahmin origin; and Gopalachari a Telugu/Andhra origin.
50.tq: Start with the distinctive scholar–theory pairs and check all four mappings.

50.s: Which evidence supports the Andhra origin of the Ikshvakus?
o: Their exclusive dependence on Roman administrators
Their use of only northern royal titles
Southern names and the practice of marrying a maternal uncle’s daughter
Their inscriptions being written only in Sanskrit
50.x: Southern names and the southern custom of cross-cousin marriage are cited as evidence supporting the Andhra origin of the Ikshvakus.
50.tq: Apply the cultural-evidence approach rather than relying on a dynastic name alone.

50.s: The Ikshvakus claimed descent in their inscriptions from which traditional lineages?
o: Agni lineage of Rajasthan and the Chalukyas
Lunar lineage of Hastinapura and the Nandas
Mauryan lineage of Pataliputra and the Guptas
Solar or Rama lineage of Ayodhya and, later, the Shakyas
50.x: The Nagarjunakonda inscription is described as claiming Solar or Rama lineage from Ayodhya, with later claims of Shakya descent.
50.tq: Separate dynastic self-claims from modern theories about geographical origin.

50.s:
Arrange the following Andhra dynasties in chronological order:
A. Salankayanas
B. Satavahanas
C. Vishnukundins
D. Ikshvakus

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: The sequence is Satavahanas, Ikshvakus, Salankayanas and Vishnukundins.
50.tq: Fix the earliest dynasty first and then place the post-Ikshvaku successors.

50.s: Which of the following represents the correct sequence after the Ikshvakus in the Andhra dynastic order?
50.x: After the Ikshvakus came the Brihatpalayanas or Pallavas in the relevant territories, followed by the Salankayanas, Vishnukundins and Eastern Chalukyas.
50.tq: Anchor the sequence at the Ikshvaku–Brihatpalayana transition and proceed forward.

50.s: Which of the following sacrifices was NOT performed by Chamtamula according to the recorded lists?
50.x: Chamtamula performed Ashvamedha, Vajapeya, Agnishtoma, Agnihotra and Rajasuya sacrifices. Buddhist Vajrayana sacrifice is not part of this list.
50.tq: Find the outsider by separating Vedic sacrifices from a later Buddhist term.

50.s: Which archaeological discovery corroborates the performance of an Ashvamedha by the Ikshvakus?
50.x: An Ashvamedha platform was found at Nagarjunakonda, supporting the record of Chamtamula’s sacrifice.
50.tq: Connect the ritual with its direct archaeological evidence and location.

50.s: Which statement correctly describes the religious practices associated with Chamtamula and the Ikshvaku family?
o: Chamtamula expelled Brahmins, while the family worshipped only the Buddha.
Chamtamula invited Roman priests, while the family worshipped Vishnu alone.
Chamtamula abolished Vedic rituals, while the family worshipped Jain Tirthankaras.
Chamtamula invited Brahmins from the north, while the family worshipped Virupakshapati and Mahasena.
50.x: Chamtamula invited Brahmins from northern regions, and the family worshipped Virupakshapati, identified with Shiva, and Mahasena, identified with Kartikeya.
50.tq: Test the combined ruler-policy and family-religion association without confusing religious patronage with exclusivity.

50.s: Virapurushadatta’s marriage with Rudrabhattarika was politically significant because she was a princess of:
o: Kanchi and linked the Ikshvakus with the Pallavas
Ujjain and linked the Ikshvakus with the Sakas or Western Kshatrapas
Vengi and linked the Ikshvakus with the Eastern Chalukyas
Pataliputra and linked the Ikshvakus with the Mauryas
50.x: Rudrabhattarika was a princess of Ujjain, and the marriage connected the Ikshvakus with the Sakas or Western Kshatrapas.
50.tq: Use the marriage alliance to identify both the bride’s origin and its political connection.

50.s: Which of the following was NOT mentioned as another wife of Virapurushadatta?
50.x: Virapurushadatta’s other wives included Bhattidevi and Bapisri, while Rudrabhattarika was the princess of Ujjain. Bhatti Mahadevi was the mother of Ehuvala Chamtamula, not listed here as another wife of Virapurushadatta.
50.tq: Distinguish similarly named queens by checking their specific relationship to the ruler.

50.s: The marriage of a man with his maternal uncle’s daughter, practised among the Ikshvakus, is known as:
50.x: Marriage with the maternal uncle’s daughter is a form of cross-cousin marriage and is cited as a southern custom among the Ikshvakus.
50.tq: Translate the relationship described in the question into the precise kinship term.

50.s: Which of the following best describes the broader historical significance of the Ikshvaku dynasty?
o: It established the first Islamic administration in the Krishna valley.
It confined political activity to northern India and avoided temple construction.
It acted as a bridge dynasty, helped the Amaravati school reach its peak, built early temples and promoted an agrarian Puranic order.
It replaced Buddhism entirely with Jainism and ended maritime trade in Andhra.
50.x: The Ikshvakus are regarded as a bridge dynasty that brought the Amaravati school to its peak, built the first temples and moved Andhra towards an agrarian, Puranic order.
50.tq: Select the option that combines the major cultural, religious and economic transitions associated with the dynasty.

50.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Ikshvaku period?
o: Ghantasala — site of the Manchikallu inscription
Machilipatnam — location of the Ashvamedha platform
Nagarjunakonda — Ikshvaku heritage site in Palnadu
50.x: Nagarjunakonda in Palnadu is an important Ikshvaku heritage site. Motupalli and Ghantasala were ports, while the Ashvamedha platform was found at Nagarjunakonda.
50.tq: Separate heritage site, port and inscription locations instead of treating all Andhra sites as interchangeable.

50.s: Which of the following places were ports associated with the Ikshvakus?
50.x: Motupalli and Ghantasala are identified as ports associated with the Ikshvaku period.
50.tq: Identify the pair of commercial locations rather than inscriptional or capital sites.

50.s: Many Roman coins connected with the Ikshvaku period have been found at:
50.x: Many Roman coins have been found at Nagarjunakonda, indicating long-distance commercial connections.
50.tq: Use the archaeological find–site association and distinguish it from nearby inscription sites.

50.s:
Which of the following statements about early temple and inscriptional developments under the Ikshvakus is correct?
1. Pushpabhadraswami and Ashtabhuja Narayana are identified as the first Hindu temples in India.
2. Some inscriptions give the dates and names of sculptors.
3. The practice of naming a child after the grandfather is recorded among their distinctive firsts.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
50.x: All three statements are included among the notable firsts associated with the Ikshvakus: early Hindu temples, dated inscriptions naming sculptors, and the recorded naming practice.
50.tq: Check each distinct ‘first’ before selecting the comprehensive option.

50.s: The first Sanskrit inscription in the Telugu lands is associated with which Ikshvaku ruler?
50.x: Ehuvala Chamtamula is associated with the first Sanskrit inscription in the Telugu lands.
50.tq: Distinguish the dynasty’s general Prakrit usage from the specific ruler linked to the first Sanskrit inscription.

50.s: Which one of the following is the correct identification of the port referred to in the 16th–17th century handloom context?
50.x: Machilipatnam is the 16th–17th century handloom port; it should not be confused with the Ikshvaku-period ports Motupalli and Ghantasala.
50.tq: Separate the later handloom-port reference from the earlier Ikshvaku archaeological locations.

51.s: Who is regarded as the first woman donor at Nagarjunakonda?
51.x: Chamtisri is identified as the first woman donor at Nagarjunakonda.
51.tq: Use direct identification of the donor associated with the distinctive title.

51.s:
With reference to Chamtisri, consider the following statements:
1. She was the sister of Sri Santamula.
2. She was the paternal aunt of Virapurushadatta.
3. She built or restored the Maha Chaitya in the sixth regnal year of Virapurushadatta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: Chamtisri was Sri Santamula's sister and Virapurushadatta's paternal aunt. She built or restored the Maha Chaitya in his sixth regnal year.
51.tq: Combine relationship and date clues, checking each statement separately.

51.s: How many Ayaka pillars were associated with Chamtisri's construction or restoration of the Maha Chaitya?
51.x: Chamtisri's work at the Maha Chaitya included nine Ayaka pillars.
51.tq: Test the exact numerical detail against nearby plausible counts.

51.s: Chamtisri is recorded as having given how many dinari-masakas?
51.x: Chamtisri donated 170 dinari-masakas.
51.tq: Use the exact figure and distinguish it from altered hundreds.

51.s: Which of the following monuments is associated with Chamtisri at Ghantasala?
51.x: Chamtisri is associated with the donation of a stone mandapa at Ghantasala.
51.tq: Distinguish the donor's specific gift from monuments linked to other places.

51.s: For which monk is Chamtisri said to have built a Mahavihara?
51.x: The Mahavihara associated with Chamtisri was built for the monk Bhadanta, or Bhagata, Ananda.
51.tq: Match the donor with the individual connected to her gift.

51.s: Adavi Chamtisri, who installed an Ayaka pillar at the Maha Chaitya, was the:
o: Daughter of Sri Santamula and sister of Virapurushadatta
51.x: Adavi Chamtisri was the daughter of Sri Santamula and sister of Virapurushadatta. Her pillar commemorated both her birth and marital families.
51.tq: Apply the relation-based identity trap among royal women donors.

51.s: Harmyasri's pillar at the Maha Chaitya was dedicated for her:
51.x: Harmyasri, a sister of Sri Santamula, set up a pillar at the Maha Chaitya of the Aparamahavinaseliya sect for her mother. Her daughter Chathasri also set up a pillar.
51.tq: Use the purpose of a dedication to separate closely related donors.

51.s: Bapisri and Chatisri were associated with which of the following donations?
o: Independent pillar dedications at the Mahachaitya
51.x: Bapisri and Chatisri, queens of Virapurushadatta, made independent pillar dedications at the Mahachaitya.
51.tq: Match the pair of queens with their recorded donation.

51.s: Rudradhara Bhattarika was the daughter of:
51.x: Rudradhara Bhattarika, a queen of Virapurushadatta, was the daughter of Kshatrapa Rudrasena of Ujjain.
51.tq: Avoid the swapped-parentage trap in dynastic questions.

51.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bhatti Mahadevi — Maha Vihara and Maha Chaitya for the Bahushrutiya sect
Upasika Bodhisri — Vihara for the Aparamahavinaseliya sect
Rudradhara Bhattarika — Ayaka pillar for the Maha Chaitya
51.x: Bodhisri is associated with the Sinhala Vihara and viharas for foreign monks, not with a vihara for the Aparamahavinaseliya sect.
51.tq: Find the wrongly paired donor and sect by comparing the distinctive gifts.

51.s: Kodabalisri, a daughter of Virapurushadatta, is associated with the construction of a vihara at Nagarjunakonda for the:
51.x: Kodabalisri built a vihara for Mahishasaka monks; the record also associates her with a great stupa and vihara.
51.tq: Link the royal donor to the sect named in the dedication.

51.s: Bhatti Mahadevi was the chief queen of Virapurushadatta and the mother of:
51.x: Bhatti Mahadevi was the chief queen of Virapurushadatta and the mother of Ehuvala Santamula.
51.tq: Test royal relationship without reversing parent and spouse identities.

51.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Upasika Bodhisri?
o: She was a non-royal donor connected with Revanta of Amaravati and treasurer Bodhisarma.
She was a queen of Virapurushadatta and daughter of Rudrasena.
She was the sister of Sri Santamula and builder of the Maha Chaitya.
She was the daughter of Virapurushadatta and founder of a Mahishasaka vihara.
51.x: Bodhisri was a non-royal donor, the daughter of Revanta of Amaravati and kin of the treasurer Bodhisarma. She was ranked first among women donors.
51.tq: Separate royal and non-royal patronage through status and kinship clues.

51.s: Which woman is ranked first among women donors in the Nagarjunakonda records?
51.x: Upasika Bodhisri is ranked first among women donors and represents non-royal patronage.
51.tq: Use the superlative clue to identify the donor most associated with the distinction.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding royal women and Buddhism under the Ikshvakus:
1. The kings were Vedic in orientation.
2. Queens and royal women were major patrons of Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.
3. Their inscriptions indicate that donations were made without male intervention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: The Ikshvaku kings were Vedic, while queens and other royal women prominently patronised Buddhism. Their inscriptions record independent donations without male intervention.
51.tq: Test the contrast between royal religious identity and women's Buddhist patronage.

51.s: Most donative inscriptions at Nagarjunakonda are:
o: Sanskrit royal edicts dated by regnal decades
Tamil merchant records dated to the reign of Sri Santamula
Greek inscriptions issued by Roman officials
Prakrit Ayaka-pillar records dated to the sixth regnal year of Virapurushadatta
51.x: Most records are Prakrit Ayaka-pillar inscriptions dated in Virapurushadatta's sixth regnal year.
51.tq: Combine language, record type and regnal-date clues.

51.s: The Nagarjunakonda inscriptions are particularly significant because the Ikshvakus were the first to date inscriptions by:
51.x: The Ikshvakus were the first to date inscriptions by year, month and day.
51.tq: Identify the exact components of the dating innovation.

51.s: Chamtisri's inscription prays for Virapurushadatta's:
o: Trade monopoly, tax exemption and land grants
51.x: Chamtisri's inscription invokes long life, victory and prosperity for Virapurushadatta.
51.tq: Select the precise triad contained in the royal prayer.

51.s: Which of the following titles was held by Chamtisri?
51.x: Chamtisri held the titles Mahatalavari and Mahadanapatni, the latter referring to her position as wife of Pugiya chief Skandasri.
51.tq: Use exact title recognition and avoid substituting common royal titles.

51.s: The relationship of Bodhisri to Bodhisarma is described differently in the records as:
51.x: Different sources describe Bodhisri as Bodhisarma's daughter-in-law, niece-in-law or niece. Her record is important evidence of non-royal patronage.
51.tq: Handle variant source descriptions without collapsing closely related kinship terms.

51.s: In the Ikshvaku economy, Bhaga represented:
51.x: Bhaga was the land tax and amounted to one-sixth of the produce.
51.tq: Distinguish the exact tax fraction from standard-looking alternatives.

51.s: The farmers in Ikshvaku records were known as:
51.x: Farmers were called Halikas. Telikas, Sale and Kammarus were occupational groups connected with oil pressing, weaving and blacksmithing respectively.
51.tq: Separate the agrarian term from the occupational guild names.

51.s: Which statement best describes Roman trade during the Ikshvaku period?
o: It was lower than under the Satavahanas; after Rome's fall, maritime trade virtually collapsed according to one account.
It was entirely absent because Roman coins were not found.
It was greater than under the Satavahanas and expanded continuously.
It was controlled exclusively by Buddhist monasteries.
51.x: Roman trade was lower than under the Satavahanas. One account further states that maritime trade virtually collapsed after the fall of Rome and villages became self-sufficient.
51.tq: Test the direction of comparison and the stated consequence of Rome's fall.

51.s: Which of the following provides evidence of Roman contact with the Ikshvaku region?
o: Roman gold and silver coins at Nagarjunakonda and a Roman-style amphitheatre at Vijayapuri
Roman ships engraved at Amaravati and Persian coins at Ujjain
Latin manuscripts at Guntur and Roman pillars at Sopara
Roman inscriptions at Motupalli and Greek temples at Ghantasala
51.x: Roman gold and silver coins found at Nagarjunakonda and a Roman-style amphitheatre at Vijayapuri indicate foreign contact. Romans were said to have built a stadium under Sri Santamula.
51.tq: Combine two independent archaeological indicators of foreign contact.

51.s: Which pair of ports is specifically associated with the Ikshvaku records?
51.x: Motupalli and Ghantasala are identified as ports in the relevant records. Other listed ports include Maisolia, Bharukachcha, Kalyan and Sopara.
51.tq: Identify the directly associated port pair rather than a broader comparison list.

51.s: Which of the following was an export from the Ikshvaku region?
51.x: Exports included spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles. Gold, silver, wine and glassware were imported.
51.tq: Separate export items from the paired import list.

51.s: Which one of the following was imported during the Ikshvaku period?
51.x: Wine was an import. Spices, iron, coconuts and cotton textiles were listed among exports.
51.tq: Discriminate between the closely paired export and import categories.

51.s: Ikshvaku coins were mainly made of:
51.x: Ikshvaku coins were made of lead and copper. They carried the Ujjain symbol, elephant and lion motifs.
51.tq: Use material composition to distinguish the coinage from foreign currency.

51.s: Which set of symbols is associated with Ikshvaku coins?
51.x: Ikshvaku coins carried the Ujjain symbol, elephant and lion; the lion was the royal emblem.
51.tq: Match the coin series with its complete motif set.

51.s: Ikshvaku coins have been found in which group of districts?
51.x: The recorded findspots of Ikshvaku coins include Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts.
51.tq: Test the geographical distribution as a complete district group.

51.s: In the Ikshvaku inscriptions, guilds were called:
51.x: Guilds were called Nigamalu; the spelling Negimalu also occurs. They continued the Satavahana sreni tradition.
51.tq: Distinguish the institutional term from occupational and social terms.

51.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the guild with its trade?

a. Parnika Sreni
b. Poosika Sreni
c. Sale

d. Telika

i. Weavers
ii. Betel-leaf traders
iii. Oil pressers
iv. Sweetmeat traders
51.x: Parnika Sreni consisted of betel-leaf traders, Poosika Sreni of sweetmeat traders, Sale of weavers and Telika of oil pressers.
51.tq: Start from the sure pair and complete the occupational matching.

51.s: Which guild was regarded as the most prominent among the listed Ikshvaku guilds?
51.x: Parnika Sreni, the guild of betel-leaf traders, was the most prominent among the listed guilds.
51.tq: Use the prominence qualifier to distinguish one guild from the others.

51.s: Rathavasya, the daughter of a merchant, made a donation to the:
51.x: Rathavasya donated to the Nodageshwara temple.
51.tq: Match the named donor with the specific religious institution.

51.s: Nagarjunakonda is described as a place where merchants and artisans were:
o: Exempt from all forms of trade
Employed only by the royal household
51.x: Nagarjunakonda was home to merchants and artisans organised into guilds.
51.tq: Apply the institutional description to the urban economic setting.

51.s:
Which of the following statements about society under the Ikshvakus is correct?
1. Preventing Varnasankara was regarded as a duty of the king.
2. Brahmins benefited from Brahmadeya grants.
3. Shudras constituted the majority.
4. A new landlord class emerged.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
51.x: All four statements are correct. Varna rules became stricter, Brahmadeya grants supported Brahmins, Shudras were the majority and a new landlord class emerged.
51.tq: Check whether the social, agrarian and administrative statements form one complete set.

51.s: Brahmadeya grants made to Brahmins were exempt from how many taxes?
51.x: Brahmadeya grants were exempt from eighteen taxes.
51.tq: Test the exact exemption number using nearby numerical distractors.

51.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a local clan in the Ikshvaku inscriptions?
51.x: Pugiya, Hiranyaka and Munda were among the local clans listed. Maurya was not included in that list.
51.tq: Find the outsider in a group of locally recorded clan names.

51.s: The cross-cousin marriage associated with the Ikshvakus involved marriage with one's:
51.x: The custom referred to marriage with a maternal uncle's daughter. Virapurushadatta married his aunts' daughters.
51.tq: Carefully distinguish maternal from paternal kinship in the marriage rule.

51.s: Virapurushadatta's marriage alliances linked the Ikshvaku dynasty with the:
o: Guptas of Pataliputra and the Pallavas
Kushanas of Mathura and the Cheras
Satavahanas of Pratishthana and the Cholas
Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the Chutus
51.x: The alliances linked the Ikshvakus with the Kshatrapas of Ujjain and the Chutus. One such connection involved Kodabalisri's marriage to Vishnurudra Sivalananda Satakarni.
51.tq: Identify the two allied political groups without substituting neighbouring dynasties.

51.s: Kodabalisri's marriage to Vishnurudra Sivalananda Satakarni connected the Ikshvakus with the:
51.x: Kodabalisri's marriage to Vishnurudra Sivalananda Satakarni represented the Ikshvaku connection with the Chutus.
51.tq: Use the marriage partner to identify the dynasty involved in the alliance.

51.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects social practices recorded in Ikshvaku inscriptions?
1. Sati, or sahagamana, was practised.
2. Kings used matronymics such as Vasishthiputra.
3. Children could be named after their grandfather, as in Ehuvala Santamula.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: The inscriptions record the practice of sati, the use of matronymics such as Vasishthiputra and names derived from the grandfather, such as Ehuvala Santamula.
51.tq: Combine three independent social-custom clues and test the complete set.

51.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the gifts attributed to Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula:

List-I (Gift)
a. Gold
b. Cows
c. Ploughs

List-II (Quantity)
i. Thousands
ii. Lakhs
iii. Crores of coins

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
51.x: Santamula gave gold in crores of coins, cows in thousands and ploughs in lakhs to support agriculture.
51.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with a reversed quantity.

51.s: Which of the following titles of Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula literally refers to the giver of hundreds of thousands of cows and ploughs?
51.x: The title Goshatasahasra Halashatasahasra denotes the giver of hundreds of thousands of cows and ploughs.
51.tq: Use the exact-title and meaning association rather than relying on a familiar royal epithet.

51.s: Which one of the following sets contains the titles associated with Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula?
51.x: The titles recorded for Santamula are Mahadanapati, Goshatasahasra Halashatasahasra and Satasahasrahalaka.
51.tq: Test the complete title-list and reject options containing unrelated offices or ritual descriptions.

51.s: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula brought Brahmins from which region and granted them what kind of land grants?
51.x: Santamula brought Brahmins from the north and granted them agraharas.
51.tq: Pair the person with both the direction and the specific grant to avoid location–institution swaps.

51.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious activities of Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula:
1. He performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice.
2. He performed the Vajapeya sacrifice.
3. He performed the Agnistoma sacrifice.
4. An Ashvamedha altar associated with this tradition has been found at Nagarjunakonda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements are correct. Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices, and an Ashvamedha altar has been found at Nagarjunakonda.
51.tq: Check whether the site detail is included along with the three named sacrifices before selecting the complete combination.

51.s: According to the recorded four-way division of state revenue, which one of the following was NOT one of the specified major allocations?
51.x: The four specified allocations were administration and army, temples and festivals, poets and scholars, and gifts to religious bodies. Expansion of overseas colonies was not listed; some revenue also went to tanks and canals.
51.tq: Find the option outside the four stated revenue heads rather than choosing a merely less familiar allocation.

51.s:
Consider the following statements about the use of state revenue during the Ikshvaku period:
1. Revenue was divided into four major sectors.
2. One sector supported administration and the army.
3. One sector was assigned to poets and scholars.
4. A portion was also used for tanks and canals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
51.x: All four statements are correct. The four sectors included administration and army, temples and festivals, poets and scholars, and gifts to religious bodies; some funds supported tanks and canals.
51.tq: Verify the broad division first, then include the infrastructure exception-like detail about tanks and canals.

51.s: The Ikshvaku period is significant in Andhra history primarily because it marks the transition from:
o: A Buddhist society to a purely Vedic society
An agrarian economy to a maritime empire
A Satavahana trade economy to an agrarian, agrahara-based early medieval order
A feudal economy to an industrial economy
51.x: The Ikshvaku period marks Andhra's movement from the Satavahana trade economy towards an agrarian, agrahara-based early medieval order.
51.tq: Identify both ends of the historical transition and reject options that alter either the starting or ending phase.

51.s: Under the AP 'Discover Andhra' campaign launched by APPCA in February 2026, which heritage circuit is placed first, with Nagarjunakonda as a key site?
51.x: The Buddhist heritage circuit is placed first in the AP 'Discover Andhra' campaign, and Nagarjunakonda is identified as a key site.
51.tq: Use the campaign–circuit–site chain to distinguish the current-affairs detail from historical religious themes.

51.s: Which one of the following best describes the position of women during the Ikshvaku period as reflected in the historical debate?
o: Royal women alone controlled the entire state revenue system.
Women's general status declined, but royal women retained religious and economic agency.
Women's general status improved, while royal women lost economic agency.
Both women's general status and royal women's agency declined completely.
51.x: The debate holds that women's general status declined, even though royal women continued to exercise religious and economic agency, including through patronage and donations.
51.tq: Separate the general social trend from the specific agency retained by royal women.

52.s: Which of the following sets of Vedic sacrifices is associated with Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula, the founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty?
52.x: Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya and Agnistoma sacrifices.
52.tq: Use the distinctive cluster of sacrifices to identify the correct ruler.

52.s:
Vasishthiputra Sri Santamula is associated with which of the following religious and social policies?
1. Worship of Virupakshapati and Mahasena
2. Grant of agraharas to northern Brahmins
3. Construction of a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Sri Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati and Mahasena and granted agraharas to northern Brahmins. The vihara for the Bahushrutiyas was associated with Ehuvala Santamula.
52.tq: Separate the founder's Vedic policy from the later Bahushrutiya patronage.

52.s: Which Ikshvaku ruler was described by the titles ‘Ashoka of the South’ and ‘Sri Parvatadhipati’?
52.x: Virapurushadatta bore the titles ‘Ashoka of the South’ and ‘Sri Parvatadhipati’.
52.tq: Match the ruler with the distinctive titles rather than with a religious act.

52.s: Which one of the following statements about Virapurushadatta is NOT correct?
o: His reign was regarded as the golden age of Buddhism.
He was the only Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism.
He rebuilt the Maha Chaitya under Acharya Bhadanta Ananda.
He completely abandoned all association with Brahmanical religious traditions.
52.x: Virapurushadatta adopted Buddhism and greatly patronised it, but the statement that he completely abandoned all Brahmanical association is not supported. The other three statements describe his reign.
52.tq: Find the extreme statement that goes beyond the recorded religious policy.

52.s: The sculptures at Nagarjunakonda associated with Virapurushadatta's reign depict which of the following scenes?
o: A Buddhist wheel being worshipped by Brahmins
A Mahachaitya being dismantled by Jain monks
A stupa being built by foreign monks
52.x: The sculptures at Nagarjunakonda show a Shivalinga trampled underfoot, reflecting the strong Buddhist orientation associated with Virapurushadatta's reign.
52.tq: Test a visual-cultural detail through direct identification.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about Ehuvala Santamula:
1. He revived Brahmanism.
2. He was the first Ikshvaku ruler to build Hindu temples.
3. He issued the first Sanskrit inscriptions among the Ikshvakus.
4. He built a vihara for the Bahushrutiyas in his mother's name.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements are associated with Ehuvala Santamula. His reign combined a revival of Brahmanism and Hindu temple construction with continued Buddhist patronage.
52.tq: Check whether the apparent contrast between Brahmanical revival and Buddhist patronage is deliberately retained.

52.s: Which religious feature is specifically associated with the reign of Rudrapurushadatta?
o: The beginning of the custom of erecting chhaya-stambhas near graves
The rebuilding of the Maha Chaitya
The first construction of Hindu temples
The issue of the first Sanskrit inscriptions
52.x: The custom of erecting chhaya-stambhas, or shadow pillars, near graves began during the reign of Rudrapurushadatta.
52.tq: Identify the ruler by a distinctive custom rather than by a broad religious label.

52.s: Which of the following best describes the pattern of religious patronage in the Ikshvaku kingdom?
o: Kings generally performed Vedic sacrifices, while queens, princesses and wealthy lay women funded stupas and viharas.
Queens alone performed Vedic sacrifices and kings funded only Jain establishments.
Buddhist patronage was prohibited by the kings and undertaken secretly by merchants.
All Ikshvaku kings and queens exclusively supported Buddhism.
52.x: The Ikshvaku pattern was one of dual patronage: most kings performed Vedic sacrifices, while royal women and wealthy lay women supported Buddhist stupas and viharas. The kings did not oppose this patronage.
52.tq: Use the contrast between male royal policy and female lay patronage.

52.s: Which one of the following statements regarding religious traditions under the Ikshvakus is correct?
o: Buddhism alone received royal and popular support.
Vaishnavism was absent from the religious landscape of Nagarjunakonda.
Only Shaivism flourished, while Vaishnavism and Shakti worship declined.
Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship all flourished.
52.x: Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship all flourished under the Ikshvakus.
52.tq: Reject the exclusive claim and select the inclusive religious description.

52.s: Hariti, besides being regarded as a goddess who protected children, was associated with which practice?
o: Kings offering horses before undertaking Ashvamedha
Monks offering manuscripts at her shrine for protection from famine
Women offering bangles at her shrine to pray for children
Merchants offering coins for safe sea voyages
52.x: Women offered bangles at Hariti's shrine while praying for children. She was regarded as the tutelary deity of the Ikshvakus.
52.tq: Test the ritual practice linked with a familiar tutelary deity.

52.s: The installation of the image of Hariti is associated with the beginning of which form of worship?
52.x: The installation of Hariti's image is associated with the beginning of Shakti worship in the Ikshvaku context.
52.tq: Distinguish the deity's iconographic association from the other listed cults.

52.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Deity or representation)
A. Skanda
B. Vishnu
C. Hariti
D. Ganapati

List-II (Associated form or identification)
1. Narasimha
2. Kartikeya
3. Protector of children
4. Elephant-headed deity

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
52.x: Skanda was identified with Kartikeya; Vishnu was worshipped as Narasimha; Hariti protected children; and Ganapati was the elephant-headed deity.
52.tq: Start with the sure deity-form pairs and eliminate the crossed combinations.

52.s: The Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda was associated with which Buddhist sect?
52.x: The Maha Chaitya, associated with Chamtisri and Harmyasri, belonged to the Aparamahavinaseliya, also called Aparasaila, tradition. Nagarjunakonda was its main centre.
52.tq: Discriminate among the closely related sect names by linking the sect to its monastery.

52.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Monastery or donor)
A. Maha Chaitya
B. Vihara of Bhatti Mahadevi or Ehuvala Santamula
C. Kodabalisri's vihara
D. Sinhala Vihara of Bodhisri

List-II (Sect)
1. Mahishasaka
2. Mahaviharavasin
3. Bahushrutiya
4. Aparamahavinaseliya

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
52.x: The Maha Chaitya belonged to the Aparamahavinaseliya tradition; Bhatti Mahadevi or Ehuvala Santamula's vihara to the Bahushrutiyas; Kodabalisri's vihara to the Mahishasakas; and Bodhisri's Sinhala Vihara to the Mahaviharavasins.
52.tq: Start from the Sinhala Vihara–Mahaviharavasin pair and complete the remaining matches.

52.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as a Mahasanghika branch or related sect in the Nagarjunakonda religious context?
52.x: Purvasailiya, Rajagirika and Siddharthika were among the Mahasanghika branches or related sects named. Mahaviharavasin was the Theravada tradition associated with the Sinhala Vihara.
52.tq: Separate the Mahasanghika-related names from the Sri Lankan Theravada designation.

52.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the centre associated with the sect?

1. Purvasailiya — Amaravati
2. Aparasailiya — Nagarjunakonda
3. Rajagirika — Guntupalli

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
52.x: Purvasailiya was centred at Amaravati, Aparasailiya at Nagarjunakonda, and Rajagirika at Guntupalli. Therefore, all three pairs are correct.
52.tq: Match each sect with its regional centre before choosing the coded combination.

52.s: Acharya Bhadanta Ananda, associated with the Aparamahavinaseliya tradition, was said to know by heart which Buddhist texts?
52.x: Acharya Bhadanta Ananda was said to know the Digha and Majjhima Nikayas by heart. A Nikaya sect also chanted the Nikayas as mantras.
52.tq: Use the exact pair of texts rather than a broader canonical category.

52.s: The Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda was primarily a:
o: Dhatugarbha stupa containing the Buddha's bodily relics
Memorial pillar erected near a grave
52.x: The Maha Chaitya was a Dhatugarbha, or relic stupa, built over the Buddha's bodily relics.
52.tq: Identify the monument by its defining function rather than by its location alone.

52.s: Which expression in the Prakrit inscription of the Maha Chaitya refers to the enshrining of the excellent relics of the Buddha?
52.x: The expression ‘Samma Sambudhasa dhatuvara parigahita’ means that the excellent relics of the Buddha were enshrined.
52.tq: Test the exact epigraphic phrase through direct recall.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about the construction and rebuilding of the Maha Chaitya:
1. Chamtisri built it in the sixth year of Virapurushadatta.
2. It had nine Ayaka pillars.
3. It was a rebuilding of the ruined Paravata Mahachaitya.
4. The earlier Paravata Mahachaitya had been built by Yajnasri Satakarni for Acharya Nagarjuna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All four statements are correct. Chamtisri rebuilt the Paravata Mahachaitya in Virapurushadatta's sixth year, and the structure had nine Ayaka pillars; the earlier monument was associated with Yajnasri Satakarni and Acharya Nagarjuna.
52.tq: Track the builder, date, structural number and earlier foundation together.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the donors or persons named in the pillar inscriptions of the Maha Chaitya?
52.x: The pillar inscriptions named Chamtisri, Adavi Chamtisri, Harmyasri, Chathasri, Bapisri, Chatisri and Rudrabhattarika. Bodhisri was associated with mandapas at the gateways, but was not included in this listed set of pillar-inscription names.
52.tq: Distinguish the pillar-inscription list from the separate architectural works of Bodhisri.

52.s: Bodhisri built a stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya at Kantakasala, identified with:
52.x: Kantakasala is identified with Ghantasala. Bodhisri built a stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya there and another opposite the Paravata Vihara.
52.tq: Resolve the ancient-place and modern-place identification pair.

52.s: Which of the following groups correctly lists the regions for whose foreign monks Bodhisri built viharas?
o: Sri Lanka, Kashmir, China and Gandhara
52.x: Bodhisri built viharas for monks from Tamravarna or Sinhala, Kashmir, China and Gandhara.
52.tq: Use the four-location cluster associated with foreign-monks' viharas.

52.s: Apart from building viharas for foreign monks, Bodhisri is specifically associated with which of the following activities?
o: Founding a Brahmanical college at Papili and inviting monks from Kashmir
Establishing nine Ayaka pillars and sending monks to Gandhara
Building seven Hindu temples at Papili and sending priests to Sri Lanka
Building seven viharas at Papili and sending missionaries to China and Tibet
52.x: Bodhisri built seven viharas at Papili and sent missionaries to China and Tibet.
52.tq: Combine the two distinctive actions attributed to the same patron.

52.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the countries or peoples named in Bodhisri's inscription as having received the Dhamma?
52.x: The inscription named Kashmir, Gandhara, China, Chila(ta), Tosali, Aparanta, Vanga, Vanavasi, Yavana, Damila and Palura. Magadha was not included in that listed group.
52.tq: Find the geographical name absent from the recorded inscription list.

52.s: According to the Mahavamsa tradition, who took Buddhism from the Pallava-bhoga region to Sri Lanka?
52.x: The Mahavamsa states that Mahadeva Bhikshu took Buddhism from the Pallava-bhoga region to Sri Lanka.
52.tq: Match the missionary figure with the region-to-destination link.

52.s: The Ceylonese monks who came to Nagarjunakonda are associated with which description?
o: They established the first Brahmanical temple at Nagarjunakonda.
They made Nagarjunakonda a base for Mahayana only.
They introduced Vedic sacrifices into the Ikshvaku court.
They made Nagarjunakonda their base for Hinayana.
52.x: Ceylonese monks made Nagarjunakonda their base for Hinayana, strengthening the Sri Lankan Buddhist connection.
52.tq: Distinguish the Buddhist doctrinal affiliation from the site-based association.

52.s:
Which chronological sequence is correct regarding the following developments?
A. Rebuilding of the Maha Chaitya by Chamtisri
B. Construction of the earlier Paravata Mahachaitya by Yajnasri Satakarni
C. Visit of Itsing to India
D. Transmission of Buddhism from Pallava-bhoga to Sri Lanka by Mahadeva Bhikshu
52.x: The earlier Paravata Mahachaitya associated with Yajnasri Satakarni preceded its rebuilding by Chamtisri; the Mahadeva Bhikshu tradition belongs to the Sri Lankan link, and Itsing visited around 700 CE later.
52.tq: Fix the earlier monument first and place the much later Chinese pilgrim last.

52.s: Which deity was worshipped in the Sarvadeva shrine, also known as Kumaraswami Sarvadevadivasa, at Nagarjunakonda?
52.x: The Sarvadeva shrine, also called Kumaraswami Sarvadevadivasa, was dedicated to Kartikeya.
52.tq: Direct deity–shrine recall.

52.s: Who built the Sarvadeva shrine at Nagarjunakonda?
52.x: The Sarvadeva shrine was built by Elisri, who served as the commander of Ehuvala.
52.tq: Who-built-what trap using closely related rulers and commanders.

52.s: The inscription associated with the Sarvadeva shrine at Nagarjunakonda is written in:
52.x: The inscription of the Sarvadeva shrine is in Sanskrit.
52.tq: Direct language identification.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pushpabhadraswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda:
1. It was dedicated to Shiva.
2. It followed a Gajaprishtha or elephant-back plan.
3. It was begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: All three statements are correct. The Pushpabhadraswami shrine was a Shaiva shrine with an elephant-back plan, begun by Virapurushadatta and completed by Ehuvala.
52.tq: Statement checking with builder succession and architectural-plan details.

52.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami — Shiva — built by Elisri
52.x: Sarvadeva was dedicated to Kartikeya and was built by Elisri. The other pairs wrongly interchange deities or builders.
52.tq: Start from the sure deity–builder pair and eliminate swapped combinations.

52.s: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine at Nagarjunakonda was built by:
o: Shivasena, commander of Abhira king Vasusena
52.x: The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine was built by Shivasena, the commander of the Abhira king Vasusena.
52.tq: Builder and patron identification with a swapped-authority trap.

52.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami shrine is correct?
o: It was dedicated to Kartikeya and its inscription was in Sanskrit.
It was dedicated to Vishnu and is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.
It was a Saptamatrika shrine dedicated to Hariti.
It was dedicated to Shiva and had a Gajaprishtha plan.
52.x: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was a Vishnu temple and is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra.
52.tq: First-in-region question using precise temple identification.

52.s: Hariti at Nagarjunakonda was associated with which of the following?
o: A Saptamatrika shrine and the mother goddess of children
A shrine dedicated to Kubera alone
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra
52.x: Hariti was regarded as the mother goddess of children and was associated with a Saptamatrika shrine.
52.tq: Confusable shrine-function discrimination.

52.s: Which of the following groups consists of minor shrines at Nagarjunakonda?
o: Sri Parvataswamy, Sarvadeva, Nandikeshwara and Shiva
Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, Kartikeya, Hariti and Navagraha
52.x: Nodageshwara, Nandikeshwara, Navagraha and Kubera are listed as minor shrines at Nagarjunakonda.
52.tq: List-based group recognition.

52.s:
Consider the following statements about the Brahmanical temples at Nagarjunakonda:
1. Nine Shaiva temples and one Vaishnava temple stood there.
2. The Ikshvakus built the first structural Hindu temples in India.
3. The Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was counted among the Shaiva temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
52.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami was the Vaishnava temple among the ten temples.
52.tq: Split the numerical composition from the wrongly classified temple.

52.s: Sriparvata is identified with which place and is also known by which traditional name?
52.x: Sriparvata is identified with Nagarjunakonda, or Vijayapuri, and is traditionally called Dakshina Gaya.
52.tq: Place–alternative name–title linkage.

52.s: Sriparvata was named after which philosopher?
52.x: Sriparvata was named after Acharya Nagarjuna, the Madhyamika philosopher.
52.tq: Name and contribution association.

52.s: Which school of Buddhism regarded Sriparvata as a sacred place?
52.x: Sriparvata was sacred to Mahayana Buddhism.
52.tq: Confusable Buddhist-school discrimination.

52.s: Who built viharas and chaityas at Sri Parvatam for Nagarjuna?
52.x: Yajnasri Satakarni built viharas and chaityas at Sri Parvatam for Nagarjuna.
52.tq: Patron–construction association.

52.s: Who is associated with the establishment of the Sriparvata University?
52.x: Virapurushadatta is associated with establishing the Sriparvata University.
52.tq: Institution-founder identification.

52.s: Hiuen Tsang, who travelled in the seventh century, found the Sriparvata vihara in which condition?
52.x: Hiuen Tsang found the Sriparvata vihara neglected during his seventh-century visit.
52.tq: Traveller’s observation and condition recall.

52.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the two similarly named religious traditions?
o: Sriparvata was the family deity of the Vishnukundins, while Sriparvataswami was sacred to Mahayana Buddhism.
Sriparvata refers to Srisaila Mallikarjuna, whereas Sriparvataswami refers to Vijayapuri.
Sriparvataswami was the family deity of the Vishnukundins and is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna, whereas Sriparvata refers to Nagarjunakonda.
Both Sriparvata and Sriparvataswami refer exclusively to Nagarjunakonda.
52.x: Sriparvata refers to Nagarjunakonda or Vijayapuri, while Sriparvataswami was the family deity of the Vishnukundins and is identified with Srisaila Mallikarjuna.
52.tq: Separate look-alike names by their associated place and dynasty.

52.s: Bodh Gaya and Sriparvata are respectively associated with which Buddhist traditions?
52.x: Bodh Gaya is associated with Hinayana, while Sriparvata is associated with Mahayana.
52.tq: Reversed-comparison trap between two Buddhist centres.

52.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent tourism-related proposal connected with Nagarjunakonda?
o: The Archaeological Survey of India proposed a Nagarjunakonda–Bodh Gaya air corridor in May 2026.
A Palnadu Collector proposed an Amaravati–Nagarjunakonda rail service under the Integrated Buddhist Circuit in April 2025.
The Ministry of Culture proposed a Srisailam–Amaravati boat service under the Harappan Circuit in April 2026.
A Palnadu Collector proposed a Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam boat service and promoted Swadesh Darshan works in April 2026.
52.x: In April 2026, the Palnadu Collector visited the Nagarjunakonda Museum, proposed a Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam boat service and pushed Swadesh Darshan works.
52.tq: Current-affairs precision using date, office-holder role and scheme-name traps.

52.s: In May 2025, Miss World contestants visited Buddhavanam, which is being developed under the:
52.x: Buddhavanam, located next to Nagarjunakonda, is being developed under the Integrated Buddhist Circuit and was visited by Miss World contestants in May 2025.
52.tq: Scheme and event matching with a famous-word trap.

52.s: Which statement correctly represents the FIRST/LAST distinction associated with Andhra’s religious history?
o: The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami, and the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra was under the Ikshvakus.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Sarvadeva, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Vishnukundins.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Pushpabhadraswami, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Satavahanas.
The first Vaishnava temple in Andhra was Hariti, and the last royal Buddhist zenith was under the Mauryas.
52.x: Ashtabhuja Narayanaswami is regarded as the first Vaishnava temple in Andhra, while the Ikshvakus represented the last royal Buddhist zenith in Andhra.
52.tq: First-and-last comparison using paired historical distinctions.

53.s: Nagarjunakonda is regarded as a main centre of which school of Buddhist art?
