78.tq: Use the ruler–relative–office relationship to avoid swapping the Chalukya rulers.

78.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared his independence and founded the Eastern Chalukya line in:
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana became viceroy in 617 CE and declared independence in 624 CE.
78.tq: Separate the appointment year from the later year of independence.

78.s: Which one of the following was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
78.x: The boar, or Varaha, was the royal emblem of the Eastern Chalukyas.
78.tq: Discriminate among dynastic emblems rather than titles or capitals.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Pulakeshin II conquered the Krishna–Godavari region.
2. Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
3. Sanskrit was their official language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: Pulakeshin II conquered the Krishna–Godavari region, Kubja Vishnuvardhana was his brother, and Sanskrit was the official language of the Eastern Chalukyas.
78.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.

78.s: Which ruler is associated with the title “Yuvaraja” in the Kopparam plates?
78.x: The Kopparam plates refer to Kubja Vishnuvardhana by the title “Yuvaraja.”
78.tq: Match the inscription with the ruler named in it.

78.s: Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram is associated with which ruler?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana is credited with the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.
78.tq: Use the temple–builder pair rather than confusing it with later Vengi temples.

78.s: The title “Samastha Bhuvanashraya” was borne by:
78.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I bore the title “Samastha Bhuvanashraya.”
78.tq: Match the exact royal title with its ruler.

78.s: Which of the following correctly describes the contribution of Vishnuvardhana III?
o: He founded the Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu.
He gave Mushikonda village to the Jains.
He defeated Satyasraya with Chola assistance.
78.x: Vishnuvardhana III patronised Vedic and Jain faiths and granted Mushikonda village to the Jains.
78.tq: Avoid the ruler–achievement swap by linking the grant to Vishnuvardhana III.

78.s: Kokkili, who briefly occupied the Eastern Chalukya throne, subsequently established the kingdom of:
78.x: Vishnuvardhana III recovered the throne from Kokkili, who then established the Yalamanchili kingdom.
78.tq: Trace the consequence of a succession dispute instead of confusing a kingdom with a capital.

78.s: Vijayaditya II is associated with which of the following claims?
78.x: Vijayaditya II is described as having fought 108 battles; he is also associated with the construction of 108 Shiva temples.
78.tq: Distinguish similar numerical traditions attached to different Eastern Chalukya rulers.

78.s:
With reference to Chalukya Bhima I, consider the following statements:
1. He is credited with 360 battles in the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva.
2. He ruled for 30 years.
3. He built the Pancharamas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are associated with Chalukya Bhima I: the 360 battles, a 30-year reign and the construction of the Pancharamas.
78.tq: Combine the numerical, duration and architectural clues belonging to one ruler.

78.s: Which inscription records that Chalukya Bhima I fought 360 battles?
78.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva records the tradition of Chalukya Bhima I fighting 360 battles.
78.tq: Match the inscription with the specific numerical information it records.

78.s: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, the commander of:
78.x: Panduranga, the commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, issued the Addanki inscription.
78.tq: Identify the subordinate–ruler relationship instead of attributing the inscription directly to a king.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Tripura Martya Maheshwara was the title of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, not Amma I. Saktivarman I, Rajaraja Narendra and Vimaladitya are correctly matched as shown.
78.tq: Find the single title–ruler mismatch among otherwise familiar pairs.

78.s: Saktivarman I regained the Vengi throne with the help of Rajaraja Chola and defeated the army of:
78.x: Saktivarman I, with Rajaraja Chola’s assistance, defeated the Kalyani army led by Satyasraya in 1006.
78.tq: Match the political ally and opponent in the Chalukya–Chola conflict.

78.s: The discovery of Eastern Chalukya coins in Arakan is associated with:
78.x: Coins of Saktivarman I have been found in Arakan, present-day Burma.
78.tq: Link the ruler to the geographical evidence associated with his coinage.

78.s: Vimaladitya strengthened the Chola connection of the Eastern Chalukyas by marrying:
o: Ayyana Mahadevi, daughter of Pulakeshin II
Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
78.x: Vimaladitya married Kundavai, the daughter of Rajaraja Chola I.
78.tq: Use the marriage alliance to distinguish Vimaladitya from other Eastern Chalukya rulers.

78.s: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned on:
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned on 16 August 1022.
78.tq: Retain the exact day, month and year rather than only the approximate reign period.

78.s: Which of the following titles was associated with Rajaraja Narendra?
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra bore the title “Kavyageetha Priyudu”; Rajarajanarayana and Baraganda Bhairava were also associated with him.
78.tq: Separate the titles of Rajaraja Narendra from those of earlier rulers.

78.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared independence
B. Saktivarman I defeated Satyasraya
C. Rajaraja Narendra was crowned
D. Vijayaditya VII was ousted by Rajendra Chalukya
78.x: The events occurred in 624 CE, 1006 CE, 1022 CE and 1070 CE respectively.
78.tq: Place the events by their dates before comparing the middle positions.

78.s: Vijayaditya VII, the last ruler of the Eastern Chalukyas, was ousted in 1070 CE by:
o: Rajendra Chalukya, later known as Kulottunga I
78.x: Rajendra Chalukya ousted Vijayaditya VII in 1070 CE and later became known as Kulottunga I.
78.tq: Identify the successor’s alternate name to avoid a person–title confusion.

78.s: Who seized Vengi after killing Danarnava during the interlude in Eastern Chalukya history?
78.x: The Telugu Choda ruler Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and seized Vengi until Danarnava’s sons recovered it with Chola assistance.
78.tq: Track the succession interruption through the killer and the displaced ruler.

78.s: The Kopparam inscription of Pulakeshin II refers to present-day Mangalagiri as:
78.x: The Kopparam inscription calls Mangalagiri “Mangalapura.”
78.tq: Match the historical place-name with its present-day identification.

78.s: Which of the following best describes the architectural style associated with the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: A purely Buddhist style without a Dravidian element
A monolithic rock-cut style derived exclusively from Jain architecture
A Vesara or Chalukya style blending a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence
A purely Nagara style with no local features
78.x: The Eastern Chalukya style is described as Vesara or Chalukya style, combining a Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence.
78.tq: Use the defining architectural features to eliminate absolute descriptions such as “purely” and “exclusively.”

78.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Vengi school of temple architecture?
o: Buddhist style, brick stupas and a wooden vimana
Vesara style, granite domes and a circular jagati
Dravida style, local sandstone and a raised jagati
Nagara style, marble construction and an underground sanctum
78.x: The Vengi school is described as Dravida in style, using local sandstone and a raised jagati.
78.tq: Select the option containing the complete architectural combination rather than one isolated feature.

78.s: Which group of temples at Bikkavolu is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III?
78.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temples of Mukteshwara, Vijayeshwara and Chandrashekhara are attributed to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
78.tq: Start from the sure temple group and match it to its builder.

78.s: The Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu and the Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry are associated with:
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra is associated with both the Rajaraja temple at Bikkavolu and the Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry.
78.tq: Pair two monuments with their common patron to avoid a builder swap.

78.s: Why were the three Shiva temples at Kalidindi constructed according to the tradition associated with Rajaraja Narendra?
o: They marked the conquest of the Vishnukundins.
They were built for Jain monks from Mushikonda.
They served as royal coronation temples.
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra constructed the three Shiva temples at Kalidindi in memory of fallen Chola soldiers.
78.tq: Connect the monument with its stated commemorative purpose.

78.s: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot are attributed to:
78.x: The Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot, also called Chalukya Bhimavaram, are associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
78.tq: Distinguish the Bhimeswara temples from the separate 108-temple tradition.

78.s: Which temple contains carved figures of the Ganga and Yamuna?
78.x: The Vijayeshwara temple is noted for its carved figures of the river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna.
78.tq: Use the distinctive sculptural detail to identify the temple.

78.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
78.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
78.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.

78.s: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu literature primarily because he
o: composed the first Telugu literary work, Andhra Mahabharatamu
founded the first Telugu literary academy at Vengi
translated the complete Ramayana into Telugu
introduced the prose style into Sanskrit literature
78.x: Nannaya Bhattaraka is regarded as Adi Kavi because Andhra Mahabharatamu is considered the first major Telugu literary work.
78.tq: Use the exact title and achievement associated with the poet.

78.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the portion of the Mahabharata rendered by Nannaya in Telugu?
o: The Adi, Sabha and part of the Aranya parvas
Only the Udyoga and Bhishma parvas
The Sabha, Virata and Drona parvas
78.x: Nannaya rendered approximately two and a half parvas: Adi, Sabha and a portion of Aranya.
78.tq: Test the extent of a literary work through a precise list-based option.

78.s: Andhra Mahabharatamu of Nannaya is written in which literary style?
o: Champu style combining verse and prose
78.x: Nannaya's Andhra Mahabharatamu follows the Champu style, which combines verse and prose.
78.tq: Discriminate between closely related literary forms by identifying the defining feature.

78.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Nannaya Bhattaraka?
78.x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was the title of Narayana Bhattu. Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.
78.tq: Find the title belonging to the collaborator rather than the principal poet.

78.s: Andhra Shabda Chintamani, associated with Nannaya, is best described as a work on
78.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani is a Sanskrit grammatical work dealing with Telugu grammar.
78.tq: Match the work with its subject and language rather than with the author's better-known epic.

78.s: Narayana Bhattu, the collaborator of Nannaya, was known by which title?
78.x: Narayana Bhattu bore the title Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara. The other titles are associated with Nannaya or Eastern Chalukya rulers.
78.tq: Use a person–title association and avoid the famous-word substitution trap.

78.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
78.x: Ugradityacharya authored Kalyanakaraka, a medical treatise. Kavijanasrayam was associated with Vemulavada Bhimakavi, while Pavuluri Ganitamu was by Pavuluri Mallana.
78.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors.

78.s: The earliest Telugu inscription mentioned in connection with the pre-Nannaya period is the
78.x: The Kalamalla inscription, dated approximately to 575 CE and associated with Renati Choda Dhananjaya, predates Nannaya.
78.tq: Use the earliest-date clue to distinguish inscriptions from different periods.

78.s: Who among the following is associated with the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple?
78.x: Chamekamba, a courtesan during the reign of Ammaraja II, secured the Kaluchumbarru grant for a Jain temple.
78.tq: Test an unusual person–grant association, a common source of identity traps.

78.s: Potla Cheruvu was known during the Eastern Chalukya period as a centre of
78.x: Potla Cheruvu was a popular Jain centre during this period.
78.tq: Identify the religious association of a place rather than its location alone.

78.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have granted Mushikonda to the Jains?
78.x: Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda to the Jains, illustrating the dynasty's religious tolerance.
78.tq: Apply the ruler–religious patronage association without confusing it with temple construction.

78.s: Kundavva, who became the queen of Vimaladitya, was the mother of
78.x: Kundavva was a Chola princess and the queen of Vimaladitya; she was the mother of Rajaraja Narendra.
78.tq: Trace the family relationship instead of confusing a queen with a ruler.

78.s: The use of the matronymic ‘Hariti-putra’ by the Eastern Chalukyas is comparable to its use by the
78.x: The matronymic Hariti-putra was also used by the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas, indicating a southern cultural connection.
78.tq: Use the comparison group stated with the distinctive title or matronymic.

78.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
78.x: Kushmandini was the mother goddess worshipped by the early Chalukyas. Hariti-putra is a matronymic, while the other two pairs confuse unrelated terms.
78.tq: Separate a deity name from a dynastic title, text and place name.

78.s: Who among the following developed Kandukuru as another ‘Bejawada’?
o: Vijayaditya III, also known as Gunaga Vijayaditya
78.x: Vijayaditya III, or Gunaga Vijayaditya, developed Kandukuru as another Bejawada.
78.tq: Distinguish the ruler associated with town development from rulers linked with capitals.

78.s: Which one of the following statements about the early capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas is correct?
o: Pithapuram was the first capital under Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
Rajamahendravaram was the first capital under Jayasimha Vallabha I.
Vijayawada was the first capital under Amma I.
Vengi was the first capital under Rajaraja Narendra.
78.x: Pithapuram, or Pishtapura, was the first capital under Kubja Vishnuvardhana. Vengi was adopted later, and Rajamahendravaram was subsequently important as a capital.
78.tq: Use the ‘first capital’ clue to distinguish initial and later seats of power.

78.s: The capital of the Eastern Chalukyas was shifted to Vengi by
78.x: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital from Pithapuram to Vengi, identified with Pedavegi.
78.tq: Match a capital change with the ruler responsible for it.

78.s: The Magallu inscription is significant in Andhra history because it is regarded as the first inscription to mention the
78.x: The Magallu inscription is noted as the first inscription mentioning the Kakatiyas.
78.tq: Identify the dynasty connected with a landmark inscription rather than the dynasty ruling at the time.

78.s: Which of the following chronological periods is correctly matched with the dynasty or political phase?
78.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled approximately from 624 to 1075 CE. The other periods belong respectively to the Chalukya-Chola phase, Kakatiyas and Vijayanagara.
78.tq: Check the date range against the dynasty before accepting the sequence-related option.

78.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Vishnuvardhana IV:
1. He backed Govinda III in the Rashtrakuta succession war.
2. He was defeated by Dhruva.
3. Dhruva married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. Vishnuvardhana IV supported Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, and strengthened the relationship through Dhruva's marriage to Sheela Mahadevi.
78.tq: Combine the ruler, opponent and marriage-alliance facts before selecting the coded combination.

78.s: Vijayaditya II is traditionally associated with which of the following achievements?
o: Winning 18 battles in one regnal year
78.x: Vijayaditya II is traditionally said to have fought 108 battles in 12 years. The 108 temples were commemorative constructions associated with these victories.
78.tq: Match the distinctive number with the correct activity rather than with a related monument or inscription.

78.s: The 108 temples traditionally associated with Vijayaditya II were intended to commemorate his
78.x: The 108 temples commemorated Vijayaditya II's victories, traditionally connected with his 108 battles fought over 12 years.
78.tq: Separate the purpose of the temples from the numerical tradition of the battles.

78.s: At which places did Chalukya Bhima I repel the forces of Krishna II?
78.x: Chalukya Bhima I repelled Krishna II's forces at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru.
78.tq: Use place-pair discrimination to avoid confusing Rashtrakuta battles with later Chola–Kalyani conflicts.

78.s: After 973 CE, the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas was the
78.x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.
78.tq: Identify the change in the rival dynasty by using the chronological marker.

78.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Chalukya Bhima I fought Krishna II, not Dhruva. Vijayaditya II fought the Rashtrakutas under Amoghavarsha, while Gunaga Vijayaditya defeated Krishna II and the Kalinga king Devendravarma.
78.tq: Find the swapped opponent, a standard ruler-with-deed trap.

78.s: Jatachoda Bhima, a Telugu Choda of Pedakallu, is associated with which event?
o: Merging Vengi into the Chola Empire
Defeating Dantidurga and founding the Rashtrakuta line
Building three Shiva temples at Kalidindi
78.x: Jatachoda Bhima killed Danarnava and occupied Vengi. Danarnava's sons, Saktivarma I and Vimaladitya, fled to Rajaraja Chola.
78.tq: Link the regional ruler to his specific political action and location.

78.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
78.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
78.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.

78.s: Coins of Saktivarma I have been found in
78.x: Coins of Saktivarma I have been found in Arakan, in present-day Burma.
78.tq: Test the unusual archaeological location directly, using nearby political centres as distractors.

78.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimaladitya — Kundavva, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I
2. Vimaladitya — Melama, daughter of Jatachoda Bhima
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
78.x: All three pairs are correct. Vimaladitya married both Kundavva and Melama, while Rajaraja Narendra married Ammanga Devi, the daughter of Rajendra Chola.
78.tq: Check each marriage independently because the same ruler is linked with two different marital alliances.

78.s: Who supported Rajaraja Narendra in his succession war against Vijayaditya VII?
78.x: Rajaraja Narendra, the son of Kundavva, was supported by Rajendra I. Vijayaditya VII, the son of Melama, was supported by Kalyani Jayasimha II.
78.tq: Distinguish the two rival claimants by matching each with his external supporter.

78.s: Which statement regarding the battle of Kalidindi is correct?
o: The Chola army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army.
Rajaraja Narendra defeated Rajadhiraja I and captured Koppam.
The Rashtrakuta army defeated Rajaraja Narendra and the Chola army.
Jatachoda Bhima defeated Danarnava and occupied Kalidindi.
78.x: At Kalidindi, the Chola army defeated Vijayaditya VII and the Kalyani army. Rajaraja Narendra subsequently built three Shiva temples there for the fallen Chola commanders.
78.tq: Use the battle-location association and reject reversals of the victorious and defeated sides.

78.s: Rajaraja Narendra built three Shiva temples at Kalidindi in memory of the
78.x: The three Shiva temples at Kalidindi were built by Rajaraja Narendra for the fallen Chola commanders.
78.tq: Identify the commemorated group rather than the dynasty that constructed the temples.

78.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Coronation of Rajaraja Narendra
B. Vimaladitya's coronation
C. Battle of Kalidindi
D. Battle of Koppam
78.x: Vimaladitya was crowned in May 1011, Rajaraja Narendra in 1022, the Kalidindi conflict followed, and the battle of Koppam occurred in 1053.
78.tq: Place the securely dated events first and use the sequence of the succession conflict to order the remainder.

78.s: At Koppam in 1053, who killed Rajadhiraja I?
78.x: Ahavamalla Someshwara killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam in 1053. Rajadhiraja had earlier won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka.
78.tq: Match the battlefield casualty with the ruler responsible for the decisive reversal.

78.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas in the order stated for their early and later rulers?
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana used Pithapuram as the first capital, Jayasimha Vallabha I used Vengi, and Rajamahendravaram was associated with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra.
78.tq: Order capitals by ruler association rather than by present-day prominence.

78.s: Vengi, identified with Pedavegi near Eluru, was the capital under
78.x: Vengi, corresponding to Pedavegi near Eluru, was the capital under Jayasimha Vallabha I.
78.tq: Distinguish the capital-place association from the first and last capitals in the sequence.

78.s: Which rulers are associated with Rajamahendravaram as a capital?
o: Saktivarma I and Chalukya Bhima I
Kubja Vishnuvardhana and Jayasimha Vallabha I
78.x: Rajamahendravaram was associated with Amma I and Rajaraja Narendra. Pithapuram was the first capital, while Vengi was associated with Jayasimha Vallabha I.
78.tq: Pair the capital with both rulers listed for it and avoid substituting rulers from adjacent phases.

78.s: What was the consequence of Vijayaditya VII's death in 1075?
o: Jatachoda Bhima restored the Badami Chalukya line.
Kulottunga I merged Vengi into the Chola Empire.
Saktivarma I founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
Rajadhiraja I shifted the capital to Pithapuram.
78.x: Vijayaditya VII died in 1075, after which Kulottunga I, the son of Rajaraja Narendra, merged Vengi into the Chola Empire, creating the Chalukya-Chola line.
78.tq: Connect the end-of-dynasty event with its direct political consequence.

78.s: The Cheepurupalli inscription is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana's
78.x: The Cheepurupalli inscription of Vizianagaram is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana's 18th regnal year.
78.tq: Attach the number to the inscription's regnal-year detail, not to a military or dynastic claim.

78.s: The Kopparam copper plates of 631 CE describe Kubja Vishnuvardhana as
78.x: The Kopparam copper plates dated to 631 CE describe Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Yuvaraja.
78.tq: Match the dated record with the exact status or title mentioned in it.

78.s: Which inscription is associated with Jayasimha Vallabha?
78.x: The Vipparla inscription is associated with Jayasimha Vallabha. Kakumanu is associated with Chalukya Bhima I, Nandampudi with Rajaraja Narendra, and Sataluru with Vijayaditya II's temples.
78.tq: Use inscription–ruler matching and eliminate records belonging to neighbouring rulers.

78.s: Which inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with 108 temples?
78.x: The Sataluru inscription records Vijayaditya II's association with the 108 temples. Addanki is associated with Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription.
78.tq: Separate two inscription records by matching their distinctive content.

78.s: The Addanki inscription is notable because it is associated with
o: Pandaranga and the first Telugu verse inscription
Chalukya Bhima I's military victory at Peruvanguru
Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu
78.x: The Addanki inscription is associated with Pandaranga, the general of Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and is regarded as the first Telugu verse inscription.
78.tq: Identify the record through its unique person-and-content combination.

78.s:
Which of the following inscription–ruler pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kakumanu — Chalukya Bhima I
2. Nandampudi — Rajaraja Narendra
3. Korumelli plates — Rajaraja Narendra
4. Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: All four pairs are correct. The Nandampudi inscription records Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu, written by Nannaya, and the Korumelli plates are also associated with Rajaraja Narendra.
78.tq: Confirm the sure inscription pairs first and then test the remaining records individually.

78.s: Which one of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
78.x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.
78.tq: Find the swapped ruler in a title table, especially where two rulers belong to the same dynastic phase.

78.s: The titles Tribhuvanankusa and Samasta Bhuvanashraya are associated with
o: Vijayaditya II and Gunaga Vijayaditya III
78.x: The titles Tribhuvanankusa and Samasta Bhuvanashraya are associated with Jayasimha I and Vishnuvardhana III.
78.tq: Match the shared title group with the two rulers instead of assigning each title to a single later king.

78.s: Who bore the title Narendramrigaraja?
78.x: Vijayaditya II bore the title Narendramrigaraja. Rajaraja Narendra bore the titles Kavyageetha Priyudu and Rajarajanarayana.
78.tq: Discriminate between similar royal names and the titles attached to them.

78.s: According to the APPSC key, the victories commemorated by the title Tripura-martya-Maheswara were over
78.x: The APPSC key identifies Kiranapuram, Achalapuram and Kandukur as the three cities. This triplet is associated with Gunaga Vijayaditya III's title Tripura-martya-Maheswara.
78.tq: Use the officially keyed triplet and distinguish it from the commonly confused alternative list.

78.s: Which ruler is associated with the title Rajamahendra?
78.x: Ammaraja I bore the title Rajamahendra. Rajaraja Narendra bore the titles Kavyageetha Priyudu and Rajarajanarayana.
78.tq: Separate similar-looking names such as Amma, Ammaraja and Rajaraja before matching the title.

78.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Chalukya Bhima — Kollabhiganda
2. Saktivarma I — Chalukya Chandra
3. Vimaladitya — Rajamartanda
4. Rajaraja Narendra — Rajarajanarayana
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: All four pairs are correct. Chalukya Bhima was associated with Kollabhiganda, Saktivarma I with Chalukya Chandra, Vimaladitya with Rajamartanda, and Rajaraja Narendra with Rajarajanarayana.
78.tq: Verify each title pair independently and watch for the common Kollabhiganda attribution trap.

78.s: The title Rajamartanda, along with Mummadi Bhima, was borne by
78.x: Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima. Chalukya Bhima is associated with the title Kollabhiganda.
78.tq: Distinguish titles of similarly named rulers by grouping the paired epithets.

78.s: Which title–ruler association is correctly stated?
78.x: Kavyageetha Priyudu was a title of Rajaraja Narendra. Vishamasiddhi belonged to Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Narendramrigaraja to Vijayaditya II, and Rajamahendra to Ammaraja I.
78.tq: Use elimination among neighbouring title associations and reject swapped ruler names.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Inscription or grant)
a. Kopparam
b. Vipparla
c. Chekurru

d. Chipurupalli

List-II (Associated ruler or person)
i. Ammaraja I
ii. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
iii. Jayasimha I
iv. Madhavasharma

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78.x: Kopparam is associated with Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Vipparla with Jayasimha I, Chekurru with Ammaraja I, and Chipurupalli names the scholar Madhavasharma.
78.tq: Start with the sure inscription–ruler pair and then complete the one-to-one matching.

78.s: The Chekurru copper-plate grant is associated with
78.x: The Chekurru copper-plate grant is associated with Ammaraja I. Vipparla is associated with Jayasimha I and Kopparam with Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
78.tq: Test a single grant–ruler association directly while using nearby grants as distractors.

78.s: The Kopparam copper plates are associated with which ruler in the copper-plate grant tradition?
78.x: In the copper-plate grant association, the Kopparam plates are attributed to Pulakesin II. The separate Kopparam record dated 631 CE describes Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Yuvaraja.
78.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named or located records instead of merging their attributions.

78.s: Which scholar is named in the Chipurupalli inscription?
78.x: The Chipurupalli inscription names the scholar Madhavasharma. Narayana Bhattu and Nannaya are associated with the Nandampudi record, while Pandaranga is associated with Addanki.
78.tq: Separate the named scholar from other literary and military figures in the inscription list.

78.s: Kulothunga I became the Chola king in which year?
78.x: Kulothunga I became the Chola king in 1070 CE. He subsequently inherited the Chalukya kingdom in 1075 CE.
78.tq: Use the numerical distinction between accession to the Chola throne and inheritance of the Chalukya kingdom.

78.s: Kulothunga I was the son of whom?
78.x: Kulothunga I was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi.
78.tq: Discriminate between a ruler's parentage and other prominent names associated with the dynasty.

78.s: The campaign of Kulothunga I against Kalinga was recorded in which work?
78.x: Kulothunga I's campaign against Kalinga was recorded in Kalingattupparani, composed by Jayangondar.
78.tq: Match the military campaign with its literary record rather than with another work associated with the period.

78.s: Who composed Kalingattupparani?
78.x: Jayangondar composed Kalingattupparani, which records Kulothunga I's campaign against Kalinga.
78.tq: Use the author–work association and distinguish it from poets and scholars connected with Telugu literature.

78.s: Kulothunga I sent how many merchants to China?
78.x: Kulothunga I sent 72 merchants to China.
78.tq: Check the exact numerical figure instead of relying on the surrounding dates of the dynasty.

78.s: Which one of the following was built by Kulothunga I at Visakhapatnam?
78.x: Kulothunga I built Kulothunga Cholapuram at Visakhapatnam. Rajamahendri and Pedavegi were capitals associated with the Eastern Chalukya territory, while Venginadu denotes the core region.
78.tq: Apply the location clue and reject nearby capital and territorial names.

78.s: Which of the following best expresses the major cultural significance of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They confined literary activity exclusively to Sanskrit.
They ended the use of Telugu in the Vengi region.
They turned Telugu into a literary language.
They replaced Telugu with Tamil as the court language.
78.x: A major significance of the Eastern Chalukyas was that they helped turn Telugu into a literary language and laid the foundation for Telugu literature.
78.tq: Identify the positive cultural consequence and reject absolute or reversed statements.

78.s:
With reference to the chronology of the Eastern Chalukya and Chalukya-Chola traditions, arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Beginning of Eastern Chalukya rule
B. Kulothunga I becomes Chola king
C. Kulothunga I inherits the Chalukya kingdom
D. Extended end date under the Chalukya-Chola interpretation
78.x: The sequence is 624 CE, 1070 CE, 1075 CE and 1189 CE. Thus, the correct order is A, B, C, D.
78.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two closely related events of 1070 and 1075.

78.s: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled Andhra for approximately how long according to the conventional 624–1075 CE chronology?
o: About four and a half centuries
78.x: The Eastern Chalukyas ruled Andhra for about four and a half centuries, from 624 to 1075 CE.
78.tq: Convert the stated chronological range into its approximate duration.

78.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the core territory and capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: The Pennar-Tungabhadra doab; Kalyana, Warangal and Devagiri
The Godavari-Narmada region; Pataliputra, Ujjain and Kannauj
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry
The Krishna-Godavari doab; Kanchi, Madurai and Tanjavur
78.x: The core territory was the Krishna-Godavari doab, known as Venginadu. The capitals included Pithapuram, Pedavegi and Rajahmundry.
78.tq: Separate the correct territorial region from similarly named South Indian political centres.

78.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the differing interpretations regarding the end of the Eastern Chalukya line?
1. The conventional date for the end of the proper Eastern Chalukya dynasty is 1075 CE.
2. Some interpretations extend the line to 1189 CE by including the Chalukya-Chola phase.
3. The difference results from whether the Chalukya-Chola phase is included in the dynastic reckoning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
78.x: All three statements are correct. The 1075 CE date excludes the later Chalukya-Chola phase, whereas the 1189 CE interpretation includes that phase in the dynastic reckoning.
78.tq: Read the date question as a classification issue and connect each date with the basis of the interpretation.

78.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Person/Event)
A. Kubja Vishnuvardhana
B. Kulothunga I
C. Jayangondar
D. Eastern Chalukya court

List-II (Association)
I. Laid the base for Telugu literature
II. First king of the Eastern Chalukya line
III. Recorded the Kalinga campaign
IV. Inherited the Chalukya kingdom in 1075 CE

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
78.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the first king of the Eastern Chalukya line; Kulothunga I inherited the Chalukya kingdom in 1075 CE; Jayangondar recorded the Kalinga campaign; and the Vengi court laid the base for Telugu literature.
78.tq: Start with the sure person–event pairs and eliminate codes that misplace the ruler, author or cultural institution.

79.s: Who among the following was honoured with the title “Gandharva-vidya-visarada” and was known as a court singer and dancer in the Eastern Chalukya period?
79.x: Chellavva, also called Challavva, held the title “Gandharva-vidya-visarada” and served as a court singer and dancer.
79.tq: Directly identify the holder of a distinctive title from the court culture list.

79.s: Chellavva received which of the following from Chalukya Bhima I?
o: Attili village and two kandikas of land
79.x: Chalukya Bhima I granted Chellavva Attili village and two kandikas of land.
79.tq: Use the grant-receiver association to distinguish a court artist from scholars and religious donors.

79.s: Mallappa, the father of Chellavva, was compared to whom in the Attili inscription?
79.x: Mallappa was Chellavva’s father and was compared to Tumburu in the Attili inscription.
79.tq: Test a precise inscriptional association rather than the better-known patronage fact.

79.s: Who composed the medical treatise Kalyanakaraka?
79.x: Ugradityacharya composed Kalyanakaraka, a medical treatise of the Eastern Chalukya period.
79.tq: Directly match an author with a specialised work while avoiding the previously tested item wording.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
79.x: Bhattavamana wrote Kavyalankara Sutras and held the title Kavi Vrishabha.
79.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped authors and titles.

79.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vishnuvardhana III — Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu
2. Ammaraja II — Kavigayaka Kalpataru
3. Rajaraja Narendra — Kavyageetha Priyudu
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
79.x: All three pairs are correct: the respective royal titles were Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu, Kavigayaka Kalpataru and Kavyageetha Priyudu.
79.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

79.s: Which statement regarding Chellavva’s patronage is correct?
o: She was patronised by Vimaladitya, who granted her Mushikonda.
She was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who granted her Attili.
She was patronised by Danarnava, who granted her Pithapuram.
She was patronised by Rajaraja Narendra, who granted her Ramatirtham.
79.x: Chellavva was patronised by Chalukya Bhima I, who gave her Attili village and two kandikas of land.
79.tq: Discriminate among nearby royal patrons by linking the artist, patron and grant.

79.s: Which of the following was NOT a title used by Eastern Chalukya kings in the context of Vedic Hinduism?
79.x: Parama Maheshwara, Parama Brahmanya and Parama Bhagavata were royal religious titles. Kavi Vrishabha was the title of Bhattavamana.
79.tq: Find the term belonging to court literary culture rather than royal religious titulature.

79.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is stated to have performed the Ashvamedha?
79.x: Jayasimha I performed the Ashvamedha, while royal prashastis also boast of several Ashvamedhas.
79.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a specific Vedic ritual.

79.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shaivism was the dominant religious sect in the Eastern Chalukya realm.
2. The Kapalika, Kalamukha and Pasupata sects were associated with Shaivism.
3. Andhra was called Trilinga desa after Draksharama, Srisailam and Kaleshwaram.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. Shaivism was dominant, included the three named sects, and the three sacred centres gave Andhra the name Trilinga desa.
79.tq: Check a religious classification, its sub-sects and the associated geographical designation together.

79.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding temple construction by the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: Kings customarily built a temple for each battle fought; Vijayaditya II built 108 temples.
Kings built temples only at the three centres of Trilinga desa; Vijayaditya II built 18 temples.
Temple construction was confined to Jain basadis; Vijayaditya II built 100 temples.
Only Vaishnava kings built temples after battles; Vijayaditya II built 72 temples.
79.x: It was customary for kings to build a temple for each battle fought, and Vijayaditya II built 108 temples.
79.tq: Combine the institutional practice with the exact numerical figure instead of relying on a familiar-looking number.

79.s: The Pancharamas are associated with the temple-building activity of which ruler?
79.x: Chalukya Bhima I is credited with building the Pancharamas.
79.tq: Match a famous religious group of temples with its stated royal patron.

79.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kubja Vishnuvardhana — Kunti Madhava temple, Pithapuram
2. Danarnava — Mandavya Narayana temple, Samalkot
3. Vimaladitya — Ramakonda cave temple
Select the correct answer using the code below.
79.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram and Danarnava built the Mandavya Narayana temple at Samalkot. Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru, but it is not a Vaishnava temple association.
79.tq: Separate Vaishnava temple associations from the Jain temple built by Vimaladitya.

79.s: Which of the following is NOT a Vaishnava shrine mentioned in connection with the Eastern Chalukya period?
79.x: Andhra Mahavishnu at Srikakulam, Ahobilam and Bhavanarayana at Narsavaram were Vaishnava shrines. Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre.
79.tq: Use religious affiliation to separate a Jain centre from Vaishnava shrines.

79.s: Which statement about Jainism under the Eastern Chalukyas is correct?
o: Vimaladitya was the only Vengi Chalukya king stated to have become a Jain.
Potlacheruvu was primarily a Buddhist centre.
Jainism was confined exclusively to Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
No Jains migrated from Andhra to Karnataka under Brahmanical pressure.
79.x: Vimaladitya became a Jain and is identified as the only Vengi Chalukya king to do so. Potlacheruvu was a Jain centre, and some Jains migrated to Karnataka under Brahmanical pressure.
79.tq: Distinguish the sole Jain Vengi ruler from centres and migration-related facts.

79.s: The family of Basaveshwara is mentioned in connection with which development?
o: Formation of the merchant guild at Penugonda
Migration of Jains to Karnataka under Brahmanical pressure
Establishment of Buddhist centres at Amaravati
79.x: Among the Jains who migrated to Karnataka under Brahmanical pressure was the family of Basaveshwara.
79.tq: Identify the historical context linked to a named family rather than confusing it with a religious centre.

79.s: Which statement best describes Buddhism during the Eastern Chalukya period?
o: It survived only at Pithapuram and Samalkot.
It was declining but continued to survive at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
It became the dominant religion and displaced Shaivism throughout Andhra.
It disappeared completely from the region.
79.x: Buddhism was declining, but it continued to survive at Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda.
79.tq: Reject absolute claims by retaining both parts of the stated trend and surviving centres.

79.s: Who is associated with the donation of Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada?
79.x: Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada was donated by Queen Ayyana Mahadevi, wife of Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
79.tq: Directly match a Jain basadi with its royal female donor.

79.s: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham for whom?
o: His Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva
79.x: Vimaladitya built the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru Trikala Yogi Siddhanta Deva, as recorded in the Ramateertham inscription.
79.tq: Link the donor, monument and religious teacher rather than confusing the site with another grant.

79.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mushikonda village — Vishnuvardhana III; Kaluchumbarru grant — Ammaraja II
Mushikonda village — Ammaraja II; Kaluchumbarru grant — Vimaladitya
Mushikonda village — Ayyana Mahadevi; Kaluchumbarru grant — Kubja Vishnuvardhana
Mushikonda village — Danarnava; Kaluchumbarru grant — Chalukya Bhima I
79.x: Vishnuvardhana III granted Mushikonda village to Jains, while Ammaraja II made the Kaluchumbarru grant at the request of Chamekamba.
79.tq: Start from the sure donor–grant pair and check that the two royal donors are not interchanged.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya administration:
1. The king was regarded as autocratic.
2. The throne normally passed to the eldest son.
3. A Yuvaraja assisted the king.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: The administration was modelled on the Badami Chalukya system. The king was autocratic, succession passed to the eldest son, and a Yuvaraja assisted him.
79.tq: Test three connected features of monarchy without confusing succession with ministerial administration.

79.s: The Ashtadasa Tirthas in Eastern Chalukya administration referred to:
79.x: The kingdom followed the Saptanga idea and had Ashtadasa Tirthas, meaning eighteen offices.
79.tq: Discriminate between an administrative number and similarly structured territorial or religious lists.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Eastern Chalukya council of ministers is correct?
o: It was called Agraharas, and the Grameyaka was its chief member.
It was called Basadis, and the Vishayapati was its chief member.
It was called Ghatikas, and the Mandaleswara was its chief member.
It was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.
79.x: The council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was the chief among its members.
79.tq: Match the body and its leading officer, using nearby administrative terms as distractors.

79.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vishaya or Mandala — Vishayapati or Mandaleswara
79.x: The state was organised into Vishayas or Mandalas under a Vishayapati or Mandaleswara.
79.tq: Match the territorial level with its officer while rejecting officers belonging to other institutions.

79.s: Which of the following Nadus was associated with the Nellore region?
79.x: Pakanadu was associated with Nellore. Venginadu covered parts of Krishna and Godavari, while Kammanadu included Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet.
79.tq: Use the geographical association to distinguish the named territorial units.

79.s:
Consider the following territorial associations:
1. Venginadu — Krishna and Godavari
2. Kammanadu — Bapatla, Ongole and Narasaraopet
3. Pakanadu — Nellore
Which of the associations given above are correct?
79.x: All three associations are correct. Palnadu was another important Nadu mentioned in the administrative organisation.
79.tq: Check each regional boundary association before selecting the complete combination.

79.s: Who among the following was a village head or village officer in the Eastern Chalukya administration?
79.x: The village head was known as Grameyaka, Gramani or Urgavunda. Vanneyus were toll collectors.
79.tq: Identify the village-level officer by separating him from state and ministerial officials.

79.s: Vanneyus in the Eastern Chalukya administrative system were associated with:
79.x: Vanneyus were toll collectors, whereas the Sthanadhipati managed temple affairs.
79.tq: Distinguish two specialised officers by the function each performed.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding Eastern Chalukya society is correct?
o: Agraharas were taxable military camps rather than villages.
It followed a varna-based order in which Brahmins enjoyed privilege.
Brahmins were excluded from royal land grants.
It was organised without caste distinctions or Brahmanical influence.
79.x: Eastern Chalukya society followed a varna-based order with Brahmin privilege, and kings often granted tax-free villages called agraharas to Brahmins.
79.tq: Test the central social feature and reject absolute reversals of the stated arrangement.

79.s: Brahmins who received agraharas are stated to have performed which rituals?
79.x: Brahmins receiving tax-free agraharas performed Hiranyagarbha and Bahusuvarna rituals.
79.tq: Match the social beneficiaries with the rituals associated with their privilege.

79.s: Which development is associated with Jayasimha II?
o: The Boyas founded the merchant headquarters at Penugonda.
The Koya Kottalu were drawn into the Brahmanical fold.
The Venginadu was divided into eighteen offices.
79.x: Under Jayasimha II, groups such as the Koya Kottalu were assimilated into the Brahmanical fold.
79.tq: Identify the ruler associated with tribal assimilation rather than with religious construction or administration.

79.s: Who subdued the Boyas?
79.x: Panduranga subdued the Boyas, while Jayasimha II is associated with the assimilation of the Koya Kottalu.
79.tq: Separate two related social developments by matching each group with its stated agent.

79.s: Which of the following was the principal source of income for the Eastern Chalukya state?
79.x: Land revenue was the main income and was collected in cash, kind and services.
79.tq: Identify the principal fiscal source and retain all three forms of collection.

79.s: The practice of granting Brahmadeya and agrahara lands to Brahmins came to Andhra from which model?
79.x: Brahmadeya and agrahara grants came to Andhra from the Badami Chalukya model.
79.tq: Trace an institutional practice to its stated earlier model rather than to a later dynasty.

79.s: Which of the following statements regarding overseas trade is correct?
o: Rajaraja Narendra sent 72 merchants to China, while Saktivarma prohibited overseas trade.
Overseas trade was confined to Karnataka and did not reach Burma or China.
Saktivarma’s coins have been found in Arakan, and trade with the eastern islands continued under Rajaraja Narendra.
Saktivarma’s coins have been found only at Penugonda, and eastern-island trade ended under Rajaraja Narendra.
79.x: Saktivarma’s coins have been found in Arakan, Burma, and trade with the eastern islands continued under Rajaraja Narendra. The dispatch of 72 merchants to China is associated with Kulothunga I.
79.tq: Separate the rulers and regions associated with different overseas trade facts.

79.s: Ghatikas in the Eastern Chalukya period were:
o: Military cantonments attached to royal forts
Jain cave temples used for royal burials
Advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples
Merchant guilds situated at coastal ports
79.x: Ghatikas were advanced Sanskrit schools attached to agraharas or temples.
79.tq: Apply the institutional definition while rejecting misleading associations with military, commercial and temple structures.

79.s: The heads of Ghatikas were known as:
79.x: The heads of Ghatikas were called Ghatika Samanyulu.
79.tq: Match the educational institution with its specialised headship title.

79.s: Mandasharma is associated with which educational centre?
79.x: Mandasharma was the head of the Asanapura Ghatika in Kammanadu.
79.tq: Link the scholar, institution and territorial unit precisely.

79.s: Which of the following subjects was NOT included among the subjects taught in Ghatikas?
79.x: Ghatikas taught subjects such as Vedas, Vedangas, Dharmashastras, Tarka, Vyakarana, Arthashastra, Dhanurveda and Ayurveda. Hallisaka was a popular dance, not an academic subject.
79.tq: Separate the educational curriculum from a performing-art term.

79.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Peddameddali inscription — Guptasharma
2. Nidamarru inscription — Katikasharma
3. Chipurupalli inscription — Madhavasharma
Select the correct answer using the code below.
79.x: Guptasharma is associated with Peddameddali, Katikasharma with Nidamarru, and Madhavasharma with Chipurupalli.
79.tq: Match each inscription with its scholar and use the repeated sure pairs to verify the complete code.

79.s: Guptasharma, associated with the Peddameddali inscription, was known as a logician who knew how many commentaries?
79.x: Guptasharma was a logician who knew 70 commentaries.
79.tq: Test the exact numerical detail attached to a named scholar.

79.s: Katikasharma, associated with the Nidamarru inscription, was the son of:
79.x: Katikasharma, the scholar associated with Nidamarru, was the son of Mandasharma.
79.tq: Use the family relationship to distinguish closely named scholars.

79.s: Jain pupils are stated to have begun their studies with which expression?
79.x: Jain pupils began their studies with the expression “Om Namah Siddham”.
79.tq: Identify the exact introductory formula associated with Jain education.

79.s: Who was responsible for managing temple affairs in the Eastern Chalukya period?
79.x: The Sthanadhipati was the officer who managed temple affairs.
79.tq: Match the institutional function with the correct officer rather than a similarly named administrator.

79.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temples:
1. Temples received land endowments from kings and vassals.
2. Musicians and dancers could be attached to temples and courts.
3. Chellavva is an example of such a court-linked singer and dancer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: All three statements are correct. Kings and vassals made land endowments, while musicians and dancers such as Chellavva were attached to temples and courts.
79.tq: Combine temple finance with its personnel and test whether the illustrative example fits both institutions.

79.s: Hallisaka, identified with Kolatam, was regarded as:
79.x: Hallisaka, or Kolatam, was a popular dance associated with the cultural life of the period.
79.tq: Distinguish a performing art from administrative and fiscal terminology.

79.s: Sculptures of which musical instruments survive at Bhairavakona in Nellore?
79.x: Bhairavakona in Nellore preserves sculptures of the veena, mridangam and cymbals.
79.tq: Identify the exact archaeological combination rather than selecting a partly familiar instrument list.

79.s: The Sri Uma Dharmalingeswara shrine, associated with the Panchadarla temple, is located at which place and district?
79.x: The Panchadarla temple, housing the Sri Uma Dharmalingeswara shrine, is located at Dharapalem in Anakapalli district.
79.tq: Use the location trap by separating the temple name, village and district.

79.s: How many inscriptions were recorded by the Archaeological Survey of India at the Panchadarla temple in 1899?
79.x: The Archaeological Survey of India recorded 17 inscriptions at the Panchadarla temple in 1899.
79.tq: Fix the exact numerical value by distinguishing it from the associated date and publication details.

79.s: The inscriptions of the Panchadarla temple were published in which of the following?
79.x: The 17 inscriptions recorded at Panchadarla in 1899 were published in South Indian Inscriptions, Volume VI.
79.tq: Match the publication title with its correct volume number.

79.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious and cultural conditions under the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Sanskrit served as the official language.
2. Patronage was extended to Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.
3. The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred during the Eastern Chalukya period.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
79.x: Sanskrit was the official language, and patronage of Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism indicates religious tolerance. The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred later in the Kakatiya age, not during the Eastern Chalukya period.
79.tq: Find the chronological mismatch in the statement linking Potlacheruvu with the Eastern Chalukyas.

79.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the later persecution of Jains referred to in the context of South Indian religious history?
o: The Cholas persecuted Jains during the Kakatiya age, and Panchadarla was among the sites attacked.
The Kalamukhas and Virashaivas persecuted Jains during the Kakatiya age, and Potlacheruvu was among the sites attacked.
The Eastern Chalukyas persecuted Jains during their period, and Panchadarla was among the sites attacked.
The Kalamukhas and Virashaivas persecuted Buddhists during the Eastern Chalukya age, and Potlacheruvu was among the sites attacked.
79.x: The persecution was later associated with the Kalamukha and Virashaiva traditions in the Kakatiya age; Potlacheruvu was among the sites attacked. This contrasts with the religious tolerance reflected in Eastern Chalukya patronage.
79.tq: Separate the tolerant Eastern Chalukya context from the later Kakatiya-era persecution by checking the groups, period and site.

80.s: The Eastern Chalukya temples are primarily associated with which architectural style, as identified by the Vengi School tradition?
o: Vesara style developed exclusively under the Rashtrakutas
Nagara style with exclusively Buddhist features
Dravida style enriched by Pallava, Badami Chalukya and local Andhra features
80.x: The Eastern Chalukyas mainly followed the Dravida style, combining Pallava and Badami Chalukya influences with local Andhra features. This regional tradition is also called the Vengi School.
80.tq: Identify the defining combination of architectural influences rather than a single dynasty.

80.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the architectural terminology of the Eastern Chalukya period is correct?
o: The Vengi School is described only as a Nagara tradition.
The Vengi style completely rejected Buddhist artistic elements.
The Eastern Chalukyas used only the pure Pallava style of Kanchi.
The style is called Vesara or Chalukya style in some accounts and is treated as a blend of Dravidian vimana form with Buddhist art.
80.x: Some accounts describe the style as Vesara or Chalukya style and explain it as a blend of the Dravidian vimana form with Buddhist art.
80.tq: Discriminate between the Vengi, Dravida and Vesara descriptions used for the same regional tradition.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about Eastern Chalukya temple construction:
1. Local laterite and limestone were important building materials.
2. Temple-building activity was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta.
3. The temples were constructed exclusively with imported granite.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: Local laterite and limestone were used, and construction was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta. Exclusive use of imported granite is incorrect.
80.tq: Find the geographically and materially supported statements while rejecting the absolute claim.

80.s: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple is regarded as a model of which architectural development?
o: The Vijayanagara style represented by Lepakshi
The Imperial Chola style represented by Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur
The independent Chalukya-Chola style combining Pallava and early Chalukya features
The Kakatiya style represented by Padmakshi temple
80.x: Draksharama Bhimeswara combines Pallava and early Chalukya features in an independent regional Chalukya-Chola style.
80.tq: Use the temple-style association directly and distinguish it from nearby dynastic examples.

80.s: Who is credited with constructing 108 Shiva temples known as Narendresvaralayas or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas?
o: Vijayaditya II, also known as Narendramrigaraja
80.x: Vijayaditya II, known as Narendramrigaraja, is credited with constructing 108 Shiva temples, reportedly at his 108 battle sites.
80.tq: Match the temple-building claim with the correct ruler, avoiding similarly named Chalukya kings.

80.s: The Sataluru inscription is associated with which historical claim?
o: Construction of the Rajahmundry temples by Rajaraja Narendra
Construction of 108 temples by Vijayaditya II
Construction of the Bikkavolu temples by Gunaga Vijayaditya
Construction of the Pancharama temples by Chalukya Bhima I
80.x: The Sataluru inscription is identified as the source for the claim that Vijayaditya II constructed 108 temples.
80.tq: Link an inscription to the specific historical claim it records.

80.s: Who is associated with building the Pancharamas or making them Shaiva kshetras?
80.x: Chalukya Bhima I is associated with building the Pancharamas or establishing them as Shaiva kshetras.
80.tq: Use the builder–religious foundation association rather than the place-based clues.

80.s: Which ruler is associated with the Bikkavolu Shiva temples?
80.x: The Bikkavolu Shiva temple group is attributed to the time of Gunaga Vijayaditya.
80.tq: Avoid the ruler-name swap among the Eastern Chalukya temple builders.

80.s: Who built the Mandavya Narayana, also called Raja Narayana, temple at Samalkot?
80.x: The Mandavya Narayana or Raja Narayana temple at Samalkot is attributed to Danarnava.
80.tq: Distinguish the Samalkot temple attribution from the nearby Kumararama tradition.

80.s:
Which of the following statements about the temples at Rajahmundry is correct?
1. Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu temples are associated with Rajaraja Narendra.
2. The Vishnu temple later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs.
3. All three temples were built by Danarnava.
80.x: Rajaraja Narendra is associated with the Kotilingala, Markandeya and Vishnu temples at Rajahmundry, and the Vishnu temple later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs. The attribution to Danarnava is false.
80.tq: Separate the correct builder and later historical transformation from the swapped attribution.

80.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Temple)
a. Bhimeswara
b. Kumararama
c. Kumaraswamy
d. Someswara

List-II (Place)
i. Chebrolu
ii. Gunupudi near Bhimavaram
iii. Draksharama
iv. Samalkot

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
80.x: Bhimeswara is at Draksharama, Kumararama at Samalkot, Kumaraswamy at Chebrolu and Someswara at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram.
80.tq: Start from the sure temple–place pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.

80.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
80.x: Someswara or Somarama is at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram, not Pithapuram. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
80.tq: Find the single wrong temple–location pair among closely related Eastern Chalukya shrines.

80.s: The Parvateswara temple at Indrakeeladri, Bezawada, is associated with which builder?
o: Bhattupu, the commander of Chalukya Bhima I
80.x: The Parvateswara temple at Indrakeeladri is attributed to Bhattupu, a commander of Chalukya Bhima I.
80.tq: Test the subordinate–builder association rather than attributing every temple directly to a king.

80.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
80.x: Ksheerarama is located at Palakollu. Kumararama is at Samalkot, Somarama at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram and Amararama at Amaravati.
80.tq: Distinguish the similarly named Pancharama shrines by their locations.

80.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the Pancharama shrine, place and district?
1. Draksharama — Draksharama — East Godavari
2. Kumararama — Samalkot — East Godavari
3. Ksheerarama — Palakollu — West Godavari
4. Amararama — Amaravati — Guntur
80.x: All four listed associations are correct according to the traditional undivided-district designations: Draksharama and Kumararama in East Godavari, Ksheerarama in West Godavari and Amararama in Guntur.
80.tq: Check each place–district pair independently before selecting the complete combination.

80.s: Which Pancharama shrine is located at Gunupudi in Bhimavaram?
80.x: Somarama is located at Gunupudi, near Bhimavaram, in West Godavari.
80.tq: Use the specific locality to separate Somarama from the other Pancharamas.

80.s:
Consider the following statements about the Pancharama temples:
1. All except Ksheerarama are two-storeyed temples.
2. The Skanda Purana is one of the literary sources associated with them.
3. Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam is another literary source associated with them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
80.x: All three statements are correct. Ksheerarama is the exception to the two-storeyed form, and the Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are associated literary sources.
80.tq: Combine an architectural exception with the two literary-source associations.

80.s:
The Bikkavolu temple group includes which of the following temples?
1. Mukteswara
2. Vijayeswara
3. Chandrasekhara
4. Golingeswara

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
80.x: Mukteswara, Vijayeswara, Chandrasekhara and Golingeswara are all members of the Bikkavolu temple group. The group also includes the Raja Raja temple.
80.tq: Test membership in a named temple group by checking every listed item.

80.s: The Bikkavolu temple group was built mainly during the period of which ruler?
80.x: The Bikkavolu temple group belongs to the ninth-century period of Gunaga Vijayaditya.
80.tq: Use the period–ruler association to distinguish the Bikkavolu group from later constructions.

80.s: Which temple is described as the only surviving temple of the Bikkavolu group?
80.x: Golingeswara is identified as the only temple of the Bikkavolu group still standing.
80.tq: Identify the exceptional surviving member of a temple group.

80.s: Carvings of which river goddesses are found on the Vijayeswara temple at Bikkavolu?
80.x: The Vijayeswara temple contains carvings of the river goddesses Ganga and Yamuna.
80.tq: Recall the specific iconographic pair associated with the temple.

80.s: Bikkavolu is described in one architectural interpretation as a group representing which transition?
80.x: Bikkavolu is treated as a Chalukya-Reddi transition group because of later Reddi additions.
80.tq: Identify the transition label and connect it with the reason of later additions.

80.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly identifies a Jain religious centre and its associated patron or site?
1. Potlacheruvu — leading Jain centre of the period
2. Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham — Vimaladitya
3. Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada — Queen Ayyana Mahadevi

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
80.x: Potlacheruvu was a leading Jain centre; the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham is associated with Vimaladitya; and Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada is associated with Queen Ayyana Mahadevi in the stated attribution.
80.tq: Combine site, religious function and patron associations without confusing Jain establishments with Shaiva temples.

80.s: For whom was the Ramakonda cave temple at Ramatirtham constructed by Vimaladitya?
80.x: Vimaladitya constructed the Ramakonda cave temple for his Jain guru.
80.tq: Match the patron's act with its stated religious beneficiary.

80.s:
Which of the following statements correctly compares Draksharama and Samalkot?
1. Both are two-storeyed Bhimeswara shrines associated with Chalukya Bhima I.
2. Draksharama has a massive lingam, a huge Nandi mandapa and intricate carving.
3. The towering gopuram at Samalkot was added later than its original core sanctum.
4. The Reddis later renovated both temples.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
80.x: All four statements are correct. Draksharama and Samalkot share a closely similar two-storeyed plan, while Samalkot's gopuram is a later addition and both were later renovated by the Reddis.
80.tq: Compare the two shrines row by row, separating shared features from site-specific details.

80.s: Which of the following features is specifically associated with Draksharama rather than with the original core description of Samalkot?
o: A massive lingam and huge Nandi mandapa with intricate carving
80.x: Draksharama is noted for its massive lingam, huge Nandi mandapa and intricate carving. The other features are shared or apply to both temples.
80.tq: Separate common features from the distinctive structural and sculptural features of one shrine.

80.s: The Samalkot shrine is also known as which of the following?
80.x: The Samalkot shrine is known as Bheemarama or Kumararama. Its original core sanctum and black-granite lingam date to Chalukya Bhima's period.
80.tq: Distinguish alternative names of the Samalkot shrine from names of other Pancharamas and temples.

80.s: Draksharama is counted among which group of sacred places?
80.x: Draksharama is one of the Trilinga kshetras.
80.tq: Recall the specific sacred classification associated with Draksharama.

80.s: At Panchadarla temple in Dharapalem, which historical evidence is recorded?
o: 108 Jain inscriptions recorded in the tenth century
Seventeen Eastern Chalukya inscriptions recorded in 1899
80.x: The pillars at Panchadarla temple carry Eastern Chalukya inscriptions, and the Archaeological Survey of India recorded 17 inscriptions there in 1899.
80.tq: Combine the site, dynasty, number and year instead of relying on the number alone.

80.s: The Panchadarla temple, noted for Eastern Chalukya inscriptions, is located at which place?
80.x: Panchadarla temple is at Dharapalem in Anakapalli, and its pillars carry Eastern Chalukya inscriptions.
80.tq: Use the location clue to identify the inscription-bearing temple.

80.s: Which statement correctly compares the Badami Chalukya and Vengi architectural developments?
o: The Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka, while the Vengi line carried a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase.
The Badami Chalukyas developed Dravida in the Krishna-Godavari delta, while the Vengi line introduced Nagara into Karnataka.
The Vengi line rejected all Badami Chalukya influence in its temple architecture.
Both dynasties developed an exclusively Buddhist style without regional variations.
80.x: The Badami Chalukyas developed Vesara in Karnataka, while the Vengi line transmitted a Dravida-based regional style into the Chalukya-Chola phase.
80.tq: Read the comparison in two directions and avoid reversing the dynasty–region association.

80.s: Which city is known as the cultural capital of the Andhras?
80.x: Rajahmundry is called the cultural capital of the Andhras.
80.tq: Recall the direct cultural-geographical epithet associated with the city.

81.s: The Kalamalla inscription is associated with which ruler and date?
81.x: The Kalamalla inscription belongs to Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, also known as Dhanunjaya Varma, and is dated to 575 CE.
81.tq: Use the ruler–inscription–date association.

81.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kalamalla inscription?
o: A fully available Telugu inscription written in geya style
A Telugu prose inscription that is not fully available today
A Sanskrit inscription in Dviradagati ragada style
A donation record issued by Satyaditya in poetic metre
81.x: The Kalamalla inscription of Dhanunjaya is in Telugu prose, but it is not fully available today.
81.tq: Distinguish the inscription by language, form and state of preservation.

81.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Erragudipadu — Punyakumara — geya style
2. Malepadu — Punyakumara — Dviradagati ragada style
3. Potladurthi — Dhanunjaya — first fully available Telugu inscription

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
81.x: Erragudipadu is associated with Punyakumara and the geya style, while Malepadu is associated with Punyakumara and Dviradagati ragada. Potladurthi is also associated with Punyakumara, not Dhanunjaya, and the description of the first fully available inscription belongs to Erragudipadu.
81.tq: Start with the sure inscription–ruler pairs and eliminate the swapped pair.

81.s: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara is described as being written in which style?
81.x: The Erragudipadu inscription is described as being in geya, or song, style.
81.tq: Identify the distinctive literary form associated with the inscription.

81.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Renati Chola inscriptions is correct?
o: The inscriptions were written exclusively in Sanskrit until the eighth century.
Thirty-three Telugu inscriptions, mostly donation records, are listed in CDX.
All the inscriptions were royal genealogies and none recorded donations.
The inscriptions were found only in the coastal districts of Andhra.
81.x: CDX lists 33 Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions, most of which are donation records or dana sasanalu.
81.tq: Reject absolute wording and recall the number and character of the records.

81.s: The 33 Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions listed in CDX were found mainly in which areas?
81.x: The records were found mainly in the Jammalamadugu and Proddatur taluks.
81.tq: Test the location rather than the inscription names.

81.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of Telugu under the Renati Cholas:

1. They made Telugu a royal and legislative language.
2. Their records replaced the earlier use of Prakrit and Sanskrit.
3. From 575 to 848 CE, Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: All three statements are correct. The Renati Cholas gave Telugu official and legislative status, and the period from 575 to 848 CE saw Telugu used in complete prose sentences.
81.tq: Check whether all three statements describe the same linguistic transition.

81.s: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared in the available records mainly in the form of:
81.x: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared mainly in names; complete prose sentences became characteristic from 575 to 848 CE.
81.tq: Use the chronological contrast between names and prose sentences.

81.s: Who among the following was regarded as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line?
81.x: Nandivarma is identified as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line.
81.tq: Separate the progenitor from the founder and the last ruler.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dhanunjaya Varma — founder and capital at Chimbapuram
Nandivarma — last ruler and capital at Peddachapalli
Punyakumara — progenitor and title Chola Maharaja
Elachola Maharaja — founder and Kalamalla inscription
81.x: Dhanunjaya Varma was the founder, son of Nandivarma, and ruled from Chimbapuram. The other pairs confuse different rulers and roles.
81.tq: Apply the founder–capital association and eliminate swapped roles.

81.s: Mahendra Vikramavarman, a Renati Chola ruler, was the:
o: Grandson of Nandivarma bearing the title Muditha Silakshara Navarama
Son of Punyakumara and author of the Kalamalla inscription
Last ruler of the dynasty bearing the title Chola Mahadhiraju
81.x: Mahendra Vikramavarman was the grandson of Nandivarma and bore the title Muditha Silakshara Navarama.
81.tq: Match the ruler with his genealogical position and title.

81.s: Punyakumara ruled approximately during which period?
81.x: Punyakumara's period of rule is given as 625–650 CE.
81.tq: Use the middle chronological option after identifying the ruler’s period.

81.s:
Which of the following inscriptions were associated with Punyakumara?

1. Potladurthi
2. Malepadu
3. Erragudipadu
4. Kalamalla

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
81.x: Potladurthi, Malepadu and Erragudipadu are associated with Punyakumara. Kalamalla belongs to Dhanunjaya Varma.
81.tq: Find the ruler–inscription mismatch in the list.

81.s: The decline of the Renati Chola power began after the reign of:
81.x: Satyaditya bore the titles Chola Maharaja and Chola Mahadhiraju, and the decline began after his reign.
81.tq: Distinguish the ruler after whom decline began from the last ruler.

81.s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Punyakumara?
81.x: Pormukharama, Purushashardula and Uttamottama were titles of Punyakumara. Chola Sthapanacharya was the title taken by Tikkana Choda.
81.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.

81.s: The Renati Cholas claimed descent from:
81.x: The Renati Cholas claimed Suryavamsa Kshatriya descent from Karikala Chola, although their culture and administration were Telugu.
81.tq: Separate claimed ancestry from cultural and administrative identity.

81.s: Renadu Saptasahasra was so called because it consisted of approximately:
81.x: Renadu was also called Renadu Saptasahasra, referring to 7,000 villages.
81.tq: Recognise the numerical meaning embedded in the regional name.

81.s: Renadu lay principally in the area where which present districts meet?
81.x: Renadu lay where Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor meet, in the upper Pennar basin.
81.tq: Use the three-district location clue.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
81.x: Renadu was situated in the upper Pennar basin and was also known as Renati Cholanadi.
81.tq: Distinguish the basin location from neighbouring regional areas.

81.s: The capital of the Renati Cholas was:
o: Peddachapalli, in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa
81.x: The principal capital was Peddachapalli in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa. Chimbapuram was specifically Dhanunjaya's capital.
81.tq: Distinguish the dynasty’s capital from the founder’s capital.

81.s: The Renati Cholas ruled approximately from the:
o: Third to the sixth centuries CE
Fourth to the seventh centuries CE
Fifth to the eighth centuries CE
Seventh to the tenth centuries CE
81.x: The Renati Cholas ruled from the fifth to the eighth centuries CE.
81.tq: Place the dynasty within the correct broad chronological range.

81.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Pottapi Chodas — Pottapi, Kadapa
2. Konidena Chodas — Kammanadu
3. Nellore Chodas — Vikrama Simhapuri
4. Renati Chodas — Velanadu

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
81.x: Pottapi Chodas were associated with Pottapi in Kadapa, Konidena Chodas with Kammanadu, and Nellore Chodas with Vikrama Simhapuri. Renati Chodas belonged to Renadu, not Velanadu.
81.tq: Identify the swapped regional association in the family list.

81.s: The Konidena Choda family was associated with which region and capital?
81.x: The Konidena Chodas ruled in Kammanadu, comprising parts of Guntur, Ongole and Bapatla, with Konidena near Narasaraopet as their capital.
81.tq: Combine the family, region and capital rather than recalling only one item.

81.s: Which of the following statements about the Konidena Chodas is correct?
o: They emerged only after the Kakatiya period and had no known ruler.
Their inscriptions belonged exclusively to the fifth century.
They were a branch of the Nellore Chodas founded by Tikkana Choda.
They began from the mid-tenth century and included Tribhuvana Mallachoda, also called Tenkanaditya.
81.x: The Konidena branch dates from the mid-tenth century and included King Tribhuvana Mallachoda, also known as Tenkanaditya.
81.tq: Use the period and ruler together to reject dynasty confusion.

81.s: Which Telugu Choda family was regarded as the foremost Telugu Choda clan?
81.x: The Nellore Chodas, associated with Vikrama Simhapuri, were regarded as the foremost Telugu Choda clan.
81.tq: Identify the superlative description in the family comparison.

81.s: The Velanati Chodas came to an end when:
o: Dhanunjaya Varma shifted the capital to Peddachapalli
Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola
81.x: The Velanati Choda line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
81.tq: Use the ruler–event trap to distinguish the end of a branch.

81.s: Who was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas?
81.x: Bijjana was the progenitor of the Nellore Choda family, while Manumasiddhi I was its first king.
81.tq: Distinguish progenitor from first king and later famous members.

81.s: Which one of the following statements about Tikkana Choda is correct?
o: He was the court poet of Manumasiddhi II and wrote Purushartha Saramu.
He ended the Velanati Choda line by killing Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
He was the founder of the Renati Chola line and ruled from Chimbapuram.
He was the son of Manumasiddhi I, helped Rajendra Chola ascend the throne and assumed the title Chola Sthapanacharya.
81.x: Tikkana Choda, also called Tikkabhupati, was the son of Manumasiddhi I and took the title Chola Sthapanacharya after helping Rajendra Chola ascend the throne.
81.tq: Reject the swapped deed and title of a related historical figure.

81.s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana served as minister and court poet to:
81.x: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana served as minister and court poet to Manumasiddhi II.
81.tq: Distinguish the two Manumasiddhis in the court association.

81.s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana went to Kakatiya Ganapati seeking help against:
81.x: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana approached Kakatiya Ganapati for assistance against Vijayaganda Gopala.
81.tq: Match the petitioner, the ally and the opponent.

81.s:
Arrange the following stages in the political position of the Renati Cholas in chronological order:

A. Feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas
B. Emergence of Renati Choda, Bana and Vaidumba states in Rayalaseema
C. Feudatories of the Pallavas
D. Rule of the Banas and Vaidumbas after the Renati Cholas

Select the correct sequence.
81.x: The Renati Cholas were first feudatories of the Pallavas, later of the Badami Chalukyas; the Pallava–Chalukya conflict produced the three Rayalaseema states, after which the Banas and Vaidumbas ruled the area.
81.tq: Fix the first and last stages, then place the change of overlord in the middle.

81.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the relations of the Renati Cholas with other powers?
o: They were feudatories only of the Rashtrakutas.
