88.x: The Chudamani Vihara was built by Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman of Srivijaya, belonging to the Sailendra line.
88.tq: Avoid the ruler–builder swap by distinguishing the Srivijaya king from the Chola patrons.

88.s: Which statement correctly describes the grant associated with the Chudamani Vihara?
o: Rajendra I granted Kaveripattinam village, which was engraved under Kulottunga I.
Rajaraja I ordered the grant of Anaimangalam village, which was engraved under Rajendra I.
Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman granted Anaimangalam, which was engraved under Rajaraja I.
Kulottunga I granted Nagapattinam village before the construction of the vihara.
88.x: Rajaraja I ordered the grant of Anaimangalam village, and the grant was engraved under Rajendra I.
88.tq: Separate the ruler who ordered a grant from the ruler under whom it was engraved.

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the larger Leiden plates:
1. They consist of 21 sheets.
2. They have a bronze ring bearing the Chola tiger, Pandya fish and Chera bow.
3. They are written in Tamil and Sanskrit.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: The larger Leiden plates contain 21 sheets, are attached by a bronze ring bearing the three dynastic emblems, and contain Tamil and Sanskrit text.
88.tq: Use the complete option after verifying the physical, emblematic and linguistic details.

88.s: The smaller Leiden plates associated with the Chudamani Vihara comprise:
o: 21 sheets and record the construction of the vihara by the Srivijaya king
21 sheets and record Rajaraja I’s original grant only
3 sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after an appeal by two Javanese envoys
3 sheets and record Rajendra I’s expedition to Kadaram
88.x: The smaller plates contain three sheets and record Kulottunga I’s extension of the grant after two Javanese envoys appealed to him.
88.tq: Distinguish the smaller three-sheet record from the larger 21-sheet plates.

88.s: Which recent development is associated with the Anaimangalam or Leiden plates?
o: The plates were transferred from Sri Lanka to Srivijaya during a Chola expedition.
The plates were rewritten exclusively in Tamil by the Ayyavole guild.
The plates were formally returned by the Netherlands during the Prime Minister’s visit to The Hague.
The plates were discovered at Mahabalipuram during the Pallava period.
88.x: The Netherlands formally returned the Anaimangalam or Leiden plates during the Prime Minister’s visit to The Hague.
88.tq: Current-affairs application to a historically significant artefact.

88.s: Which statement regarding the language of the Leiden plates is correct?
o: They contain both Tamil and Sanskrit.
They are written only in Sanskrit.
They are written only in Tamil.
They are written in Tamil and Chinese.
88.x: The Leiden plates contain both Tamil and Sanskrit; they are not Tamil-only records.
88.tq: Identify the precise linguistic description against the look-alike ‘Tamil-only’ claim.

88.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra connection of the merchant guilds:
1. Ayyavole and Manigramam operated in Andhra ports and towns.
2. Penugonda was an important centre in this connection.
3. Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
88.x: Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially around Penugonda, while Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas.
88.tq: Combine regional application with guild terminology and dynastic context.

88.s: The wider historical significance of the Chola merchant-guild networks was that they:
o: replaced all temple institutions with royal agencies
confined trade to inland Tamil markets
ended commercial contacts with China and Southeast Asia
carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal
88.x: The guild networks extended Chola commerce and Dravidian cultural influence across the Bay of Bengal.
88.tq: Direct significance-based recall.

89.s: Who completed the construction of the Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur in 1010 CE?
89.x: The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja I and completed in 1010 CE.
89.tq: Use the builder–monument association and distinguish successive Chola rulers.

89.s: The Brihadeeswara Temple is also known by which of the following names?
89.x: Brihadeeswara Temple is also called Dakshina Meru.
89.tq: Test the alternate-name trap by separating titles of closely related Chola temples.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brihadeeswara Temple:
1. Its vimana is about 216 feet high.
2. Its capstone is monolithic and weighs approximately 80 tonnes.
3. The entire vimana was constructed exclusively of brick and mortar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: The vimana is about 216 feet high and has a monolithic capstone of approximately 80 tonnes. Statement 3 is false because only the rest of the vimana, apart from the capstone, is described as being of brick and mortar.
89.tq: Split the material claim from the height and weight figures to identify the overstatement.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
89.x: Koranganatha, an early Chola structural temple, is located at Srinivasanallur. Airavatesvara is at Darasuram and Kampaharesvara is at Tribhuvanam.
89.tq: Start from the sure site–temple pair and eliminate swapped locations.

89.s: Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was constructed during the reign of which ruler?
89.x: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.
89.tq: Apply the wrong-ruler trap to distinguish the Chola builders of major temples.

89.s: The stone chariot drawn by horses and the ‘Musical Steps’ are notable features of which temple?
89.x: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram is noted for its miniature masterpiece form, stone chariot drawn by horses and Musical Steps.
89.tq: Link distinctive architectural features to the correct monument rather than its builder.

89.s: Gangaikondacholapuram was established by Rajendra I primarily to commemorate his
89.x: Rajendra I established Gangaikondacholapuram as a new capital to mark his Ganga expedition.
89.tq: Match the ruler’s achievement with the purpose behind the foundation of the capital.

89.s: Which of the following correctly describes the vimana of the Gangaikondacholapuram Temple?
o: It is 216 feet high and has a straight, rigid profile.
It is 216 feet high and has a circular plan.
It is 180 feet high and is entirely made of brick and mortar.
It is 180 feet high and has a concave curvilinear profile.
89.x: The vimana of Gangaikondacholapuram is about 180 feet high and has a curvilinear concave profile.
89.tq: Use the height and profile together to distinguish it from Thanjavur’s vimana.

89.s: In the comparison of the Chola temples at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram, the latter’s vimana is traditionally described as having a more
89.x: The concave curvilinear profile of Gangaikondacholapuram is described as having feminine grace, in contrast to the masculine bulk of Thanjavur.
89.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap involving the masculine and feminine descriptions.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gangaikondacholapuram — Bronze well and giant Nandi
Airavatesvara — Stone chariot and Musical Steps
89.x: Brihadeeswara has a vimana of about 216 feet. The approximately 180-foot vimana belongs to Gangaikondacholapuram.
89.tq: Find the reversed numerical comparison among otherwise familiar temple features.

89.s: Kampaharesvara Temple, a late Chola monument, is situated at
89.x: Kampaharesvara Temple was built by Kulottunga III at Tribhuvanam and is regarded as a late Chola monument.
89.tq: Use the site–builder pair to distinguish the later Chola temple from earlier examples.

89.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of the sequence given:
A. Brihadeeswara Temple
B. Shore Temple
C. Gangaikondacholapuram Temple
D. Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram
89.x: The sequence is Seven Pagodas of Mahabalipuram, Shore Temple, Brihadeeswara, and Gangaikondacholapuram.
89.tq: Fix the Pallava pair first, then place the two later Chola monuments.

89.s: Which of the following temples is an early Chola structural temple located at Srinivasanallur?
89.x: Koranganatha Temple at Srinivasanallur is identified as an early Chola structural temple.
89.tq: Combine the architectural classification with the site instead of relying on the temple name alone.

89.s: The Chit Sabha, containing carvings of 108 classical dance poses, is associated with the
89.x: The Chit Sabha of the Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram contains carvings of 108 classical dance poses.
89.tq: Identify the shrine through its distinctive dance-related architectural feature.

89.s: The Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram is dedicated to Shiva in the form of
89.x: The Chidambaram shrine is dedicated to Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance.
89.tq: Use the temple’s presiding form of Shiva to distinguish it from other Chola sculptural themes.

89.s: Which of the following statements about the great Nandi at Thanjavur is correct?
o: It is the original monolithic capstone of the vimana.
It was constructed by Rajendra I to mark the Ganga expedition.
It was added later by the Nayakas.
It was installed by Kulottunga III at Tribhuvanam.
89.x: The great Nandi at Thanjavur was added at a later stage by the Nayakas.
89.tq: Watch for the chronology trap separating the original Chola construction from later additions.

89.s:
Which of the following constitutes the UNESCO group known as the ‘Great Living Chola Temples’?
1. Thanjavur
2. Gangaikondacholapuram
3. Darasuram
4. Chidambaram
89.x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram. Chidambaram is not included in this group.
89.tq: Use the exclusion statement to separate a major Chola shrine from the UNESCO group.

89.s: The lost-wax technique perfected by the Cholas for making bronze icons is known as
89.x: The Cholas perfected the cire perdue, or lost-wax, casting technique for bronze icons.
89.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than a general description of metal casting.

89.s: Which of the following best describes the religious status of Chola bronze images?
o: They were made exclusively as architectural decorations.
They were worshipped icons noted for fine craftsmanship and expressive faces.
They were undecorated images intended for military standards.
They were used only as royal commemorative statues.
89.x: Chola bronzes were worshipped icons, distinguished by fine craftsmanship, intricate jewellery and expressive faces.
89.tq: Apply the description to distinguish ritual icons from merely decorative or commemorative sculpture.

89.s: In the standard iconography of Chola Nataraja bronzes, the upper right hand holds the
89.x: The upper right hand of Nataraja holds the damaru, or drum, symbolising creation.
89.tq: Map each hand to its object before considering the associated philosophical meaning.

89.s: The agni held in the upper left hand of Nataraja symbolises
89.x: The fire, or agni, in Nataraja’s upper left hand represents destruction.
89.tq: Discriminate between the paired meanings of the drum and fire.

89.s: The lower right hand of the Nataraja image is generally shown in the abhaya mudra, signifying
89.x: The abhaya mudra means ‘fear not’ and signifies protection or reassurance.
89.tq: Match the gesture with its meaning while avoiding confusion with the foot symbolism.

89.s: The lower left hand of Nataraja points towards the raised left foot, which signifies
89.x: The lower left hand directs attention to the raised foot, symbolising liberation or refuge.
89.tq: Use the hand–foot relationship to identify the meaning of the gesture.

89.s: In the Nataraja icon, the right foot placed on the dwarf Apasmara represents the
o: fusion of male and female principles
89.x: Apasmara represents ignorance, and Nataraja’s right foot placed upon him signifies its conquest.
89.tq: Identify the symbolic meaning by linking the named figure Apasmara with ignorance.

89.s:
Consider the following statements about the earrings of the Chola Nataraja image:
1. The right ear bears a man’s earring.
2. The left ear bears a woman’s earring.
3. They symbolise the fusion of male and female principles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. The different earrings represent the fusion of male and female principles in the Nataraja image.
89.tq: Check the paired left–right details first, then connect them to the symbolic interpretation.

89.s: The ring of flames surrounding the dancing Nataraja is called the
89.x: The ring of flames is called the prabhamandala and represents the cosmic cycle.
89.tq: Separate names of architectural spaces, hand gestures and iconographic elements.

89.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a Nataraja element with its meaning?
o: Right foot on Apasmara — conquest of ignorance
89.x: The right foot placed on Apasmara symbolises the conquest of ignorance. The upper right hand with the drum signifies creation, the upper left hand with fire signifies destruction, and the prabhamandala represents the cosmic cycle.
89.tq: Eliminate reversed symbolic meanings and retain the correctly matched iconographic detail.

89.s: Which of the following statements regarding the number of arms in the standard dancing Shiva image of Nataraja is correct?
o: It is shown with two arms.
It is shown with three arms.
It is shown with four arms.
It is shown with eight arms.
89.x: The standard Nataraja image represents dancing Shiva with four arms.
89.tq: Test the fixed numerical feature directly while separating it from other multi-armed forms.

89.s: The Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram are particularly noted for their
89.x: The Dakshinamurthy panels at these two temples are regarded as among the finest examples of deep-relief stone sculpture in South India.
89.tq: Distinguish the medium and sculptural method from the bronze tradition of the Cholas.

89.s: The Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram are regarded as among the finest examples of this form in
89.x: These panels are rated among the finest deep-relief stone sculptures in South India.
89.tq: Use the regional comparison carefully; the geographical qualifier is the key detail.

89.s:
Which of the following statements about the Nataraja image are correct?
1. The damaru in the upper right hand symbolises creation.
2. The agni in the upper left hand symbolises destruction.
3. The prabhamandala symbolises the cosmic cycle.
4. Apasmara symbolises liberation.
89.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Apasmara represents ignorance; the right foot placed upon it symbolises the conquest of ignorance.
89.tq: Find the single reversed meaning among several correctly paired symbols.

89.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the term ‘Garbhagriha’ in Dravida temple architecture?
o: The womb-house containing the principal icon
The pillared hall used for gatherings
The raised platform of the temple
89.x: Garbhagriha literally denotes the womb-house and houses the principal deity or icon of the temple.
89.tq: Use the exact architectural meaning rather than confusing the sanctum with the hall or gateway.

89.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mandapa — Pillared hall or portico
2. Antarala — Vestibule between the sanctum and the mandapa
3. Jagati — Raised platform
4. Gopuram — Main icon of the temple
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
89.x: Mandapa is a pillared hall, antarala is the intervening vestibule and jagati is a raised platform. Gopuram is the entrance gateway, not the main icon.
89.tq: Find the one swapped architectural meaning before selecting the coded combination.

89.s: In a South Indian temple, the principal entrance gateway is generally known as the
89.x: Gopuram refers to the imposing entrance gateway tower characteristic of South Indian temples.
89.tq: Test the precise function of a familiar architectural term.

89.s: Which one of the following is the correct characteristic of the Dravida temple tower?
o: A flat roof surrounded by corner turrets
A curvilinear shikhara over the sanctum
A pyramidal, multi-storeyed vimana over the sanctum
89.x: The dominant Dravida tower is the vimana, which is pyramidal and multi-storeyed and rises over the garbhagriha.
89.tq: Separate the southern pyramidal vimana from the northern curvilinear shikhara.

89.s:
With reference to Dravida and Nagara temple architecture, consider the following statements:
1. The Dravida temple is associated with a pyramidal vimana.
2. The Nagara temple is associated with a curvilinear shikhara.
3. Elaborate prakara walls and gateways are a usual feature of Nagara temples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Elaborate prakara walls and gateways are characteristic of Dravida temples, whereas Nagara temples usually lack such elaborate enclosures.
89.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap in the statement about temple enclosures.

89.s: The topmost, dome-like crowning part of the vimana is called the
89.x: Shikhara denotes the topmost, dome-like crowning portion of the vimana; the monolithic shikhara of the Thanjavur temple is especially noted.
89.tq: Distinguish the crowning element from the entire tower and its surrounding structures.

89.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Chola temple architecture is NOT correct?
o: Chola temples represented the zenith of the Dravida style.
The Cholas developed massive free-standing structural temples.
The Cholas remained confined to rock-cut cave architecture.
Nandi mandapas and enclosure walls were important features of major Chola temples.
89.x: The Cholas moved from rock-cut caves to massive free-standing structural temples. Their architecture is associated with large vimanas, Nandi mandapas and enclosure walls.
89.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the architectural transition from caves to structural temples.

89.s: In the axial arrangement of a major Dravida temple, which of the following are placed before the sanctum?
89.x: The vehicle or vahana of the deity and the dhvaja pillar are placed axially before the sanctum.
89.tq: Apply the spatial relationship between the sanctum and the axial temple elements.

89.s: Which of the following statements about the continuity of Chola-style architecture is correct?
o: It continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and the Hoysalas.
It ended with the Cholas and was not adopted by later dynasties.
It was replaced by rock-cut architecture under the Hoysalas.
It was continued only by the Nagara temples of northern India.
89.x: Chola-style building continued under both the Kalyani Chalukyas and the Hoysalas.
89.tq: Test the dynasty-to-dynasty continuity rather than the origin of the style.

89.s: Who composed the Kamba Ramayanam, also known as Ramavataram?
89.x: Kamba Ramayanam or Ramavataram was composed by Kamban and is a Tamil adaptation of the Ramayana, not merely a translation of Valmiki.
89.tq: Use author-work matching with closely associated Tamil literary names as distractors.

89.s: Periyapuranam, which describes the lives of the 63 Nayanars, was written by
89.x: Sekkilar authored Periyapuranam, also called Tiruttondarpuranam, dealing with the lives of the 63 Nayanars.
89.tq: Match the religious subject of the work with its correct author.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)
 a. Kalingattupparani
 b. Moovar Ula
 c. Nalavenba
 d. Nannul
List-II (Author)
 i. Pugalendi
 ii. Pavanandhi
 iii. Jayamkondar
 iv. Ottakuthar
89.x: Kalingattupparani was written by Jayamkondar, Moovar Ula by Ottakuthar, Nalavenba by Pugalendi and Nannul by Pavanandhi.
89.tq: Start with the distinctive war poem and then eliminate codes using the sure author pairs.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
89.x: Nannul was authored by Pavanandhi and is a standard Tamil grammar. Sekkilar authored Periyapuranam.
89.tq: Find the swapped author in an otherwise familiar work-author list.

89.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham consists of devotional hymns associated with the
o: Nayanars and was compiled by Sekkilar
Alvars and was compiled by Nathamuni
Chola court poets and was compiled by Jayamkondar
Jains and was compiled by Amirthasagarar
89.x: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham contains 4,000 hymns of the Alvars and was compiled by Nathamuni.
89.tq: Separate the Vaishnava Alvar canon from the Shaiva Nayanar canon.

89.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Tirumurai?
o: A war poem describing Kulottunga I’s Kalinga campaign
A Vaishnava canon of Alvar hymns compiled by Nathamuni
A Shaiva canon of Nayanar hymns, compiled by Nambi Andar Nambi
A Jain work on Tamil prosody compiled by Amirthasagarar
89.x: The Tirumurai is the Shaiva canon containing hymns of the Nayanars, including the Tevaram, and was compiled by Nambi Andar Nambi during the time of Rajaraja I.
89.tq: Use the Shaiva–Vaishnava distinction to avoid confusing the two devotional canons.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tirumurai:
1. It is also called the Tamil Veda or the Fifth Veda.
2. It contains twelve books, with Periya Puranam added as the twelfth book.
3. Its hymns belong to the Shaiva tradition of the Nayanars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. The Tirumurai is the Shaiva Tamil canon, known as the Tamil or Fifth Veda, and its twelfth book is Periya Puranam.
89.tq: When all three statements describe different aspects of the same canon, verify each independently before choosing the complete combination.

89.s: The Alvars and the Nayanars are respectively associated with devotional hymns dedicated to
89.x: The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu, while the Nayanars were devotees of Shiva and composed Shaiva devotional hymns.
89.tq: Test the paired religious identities in their correct order.

89.s: Which of the following is the correct set of components of the UNESCO World Heritage property known as the Great Living Chola Temples?
89.x: The three components are Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur, the temple at Gangaikondacholapuram and Airavatesvara at Darasuram.
89.tq: Recall the complete three-member UNESCO set rather than selecting an individual temple.

89.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the UNESCO listing of the Great Living Chola Temples in chronological order:
A. Extension of the listing to Gangaikondacholapuram and Airavatesvara
B. Listing of the Thanjavur temple
C. Construction or recognition of the three-component heritage grouping
89.x: Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur was listed in 1987, and the listing was extended to the other two temples in 2004. The grouping therefore places the original listing before the extension.
89.tq: Fix the dated milestones first: the original listing preceded the 2004 extension.

89.s: The UNESCO listing of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur took place in
89.x: The Thanjavur temple was listed in 1987; the UNESCO property was extended to the other two Great Living Chola Temples in 2004.
89.tq: Use the paired date distinction between the initial listing and the later extension.

89.s: Which of the following temples is located at Darasuram and forms one of the three components of the Great Living Chola Temples?
89.x: Airavatesvara Temple is located at Darasuram and is one of the three components of the UNESCO property.
89.tq: Link the temple with its location before considering the UNESCO grouping.

89.s: The dark ambulatory passage of the Brihadeeswara temple contains paintings depicting
o: The Alvars composing the Divya Prabandham
Shiva as Tripurantaka and portraits of Rajaraja I with Karuvur Thevar
Only scenes from the Kalinga war
The coronation of Kulottunga II by Ottakuthar
89.x: The Brihadeeswara frescoes show Shiva as Tripurantaka and royal portraits of Rajaraja I together with his guru Karuvur Thevar.
89.tq: Combine the deity image and the royal portrait clues to identify the correct fresco tradition.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola-period paintings and carvings:
1. Murals are also known from Gangaikondacholapuram.
2. Narthamalai cave paintings depict Shiva and Parvati.
3. The finest stone carvings include Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. Murals are known at Gangaikondacholapuram, Narthamalai paintings show Shiva and Parvati, and notable Dakshinamurthy panels occur at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram.
89.tq: Check whether each statement refers to paintings or stone panels without transferring one site’s feature to another.

89.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Brihadeeswara — Shiva as Tripurantaka in the dark ambulatory paintings
89.x: The Thanjavur temple is known for Brihadeeswara frescoes and Dakshinamurthy panels, not exclusively for Jain manuscript illustrations.
89.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘only’ when it contradicts the documented range of temple art.

89.s: Rajaraja I’s inscriptions at the Thanjavur temple are significant because they record
o: The election of village assemblies through the Kudavolai system
Only the names of foreign merchants visiting the Chola ports
About 400 temple dancing women, musicians and temple staff supported by grants
The complete list of Nayanar hymns in the Tirumurai
89.x: The inscriptions mention about 400 temple dancing women and also refer to musicians and other staff who were paid through grants. The Kudavolai election system is recorded in Uttiramerur inscriptions.
89.tq: Distinguish the social records of Thanjavur inscriptions from the administrative record at Uttiramerur.

89.s: The mandapas of Chola temples served as centres for
o: Ceremonial dances, rituals and other social and cultural activities
Only military training and royal taxation
89.x: Temples were centres of social and cultural life, and their mandapas hosted ceremonial dances and rituals.
89.tq: Apply the functional meaning of the mandapa to the social role of the temple.

89.s: The Uttiramerur inscriptions of the time of Parantaka I are especially important for their reference to the
o: Kudavolai system of village assembly elections
89.x: The Uttiramerur inscriptions, associated with Parantaka I, record the Kudavolai or pot-ballot system used in village assembly elections.
89.tq: Associate the inscription site and ruler with the specific administrative institution recorded there.

89.s:
Assertion (A): Chola temples functioned as important centres of social and cultural life.
Reason (R): Their mandapas hosted ceremonial dances and rituals.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
89.x: Both statements are true, and the use of mandapas for ceremonial dances and rituals explains the social and cultural role of Chola temples.
89.tq: Check whether the reason directly accounts for the broader institutional role stated in the assertion.

89.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola embassies to China:
1. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission to China.
2. Rajaraja I sent embassies to China.
3. Rajendra I sent embassies to China.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
89.x: All three statements are correct. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission, while Rajaraja I and Rajendra I also sent embassies to China.
89.tq: Check each ruler separately before selecting the coded combination.

89.s: The principal motive mentioned for the Srivijaya expedition of 1025 was
o: to secure control over the Arabian horse trade
to establish Chola rule in Sri Lanka
to protect the Kaveri delta from floods
89.x: Freeing trade with China was a motive for the Chola expedition against Srivijaya in 1025.
89.tq: Distinguish the stated economic motive from military and territorial objectives.

89.s: The additional grant associated with Kulottunga I and the Chulamanivarma-vihara consisted of
89.x: Kulottunga I added 4,500 kalam of paddy to the grant of the Chulamanivarma-vihara.
89.tq: Focus on the precise quantity and unit rather than the associated ruler alone.

89.s: Arab merchants trading on the Coromandel coast mainly imported
89.x: Horses were a major import brought by Arab merchants trading on the Coromandel coast.
89.tq: Match the trading community with its specifically mentioned major import.

89.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kaveripattinam — Port at the mouth of the Kaveri
89.x: Kaveripattinam, not Nagapattinam, was the early Chola capital and a port at the mouth of the Kaveri.
89.tq: Find the swapped capital description among otherwise familiar port associations.

89.s: Which of the following was the chief Chola port associated with the Srivijaya-built Buddhist vihara?
89.x: Nagapattinam was the chief Chola port and was associated with the Srivijaya-built Chulamanivarma-vihara.
89.tq: Identify the port from its distinctive religious and overseas-trade association.

89.s:
Arrange the following places in the order in which they are associated with the Chola maritime network as described below:
A. Kaveripattinam — trade with Rome
B. Nagapattinam — Chulamanivarma-vihara
C. China — merchant mission of Kulottunga I
D. Coromandel coast — Arab horse trade
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: The sequence follows the stated associations: Kaveripattinam with Roman trade, Nagapattinam with the vihara, China with Kulottunga I's mission, and the Coromandel coast with Arab horse trade.
89.tq: Use the sequence of the maritime-trade associations presented in the question rather than introducing outside chronology.

89.s: Which of the following internal economic institutions was a market centre?
89.x: Nagarams were market centres in the Chola internal economy.
89.tq: Distinguish a local market institution from merchant guilds and protected mercantile towns.

89.s: Erivirappattanas were
o: gold coins used in overseas trade
89.x: Erivirappattanas were protected mercantile towns.
89.tq: Directly identify the institutional meaning of the specialised term.

89.s: In the Chola internal economy, the term ‘Kasu’ referred to a
89.x: Kasu was a gold coin in the Chola internal economy.
89.tq: Separate the monetary term from the names of economic institutions.

89.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
89.x: Kasu was a gold coin. Nagarams were market centres, Erivirappattanas were protected mercantile towns, and Kaveripattinam was a port and early Chola capital.
89.tq: Test precise institutional meanings by identifying the single correctly matched pair.

89.s: Which guild was primarily associated with foreign or long-distance trade?
89.x: Manigramam was a guild engaged in foreign or long-distance trade.
89.tq: Discriminate between long-distance trading guilds and local merchant assemblies.

89.s: The Ainnurruvar, known as the ‘Five Hundred’ of Ayyavole, was a
o: royal council concerned with temple architecture
powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body
guild of Arab horse traders alone
89.x: The Ainnurruvar was a powerful inter-regional and overseas merchant body.
89.tq: Use the scale of activity—inter-regional and overseas—to identify the guild.

89.s: The name ‘Nanadesis’ most closely indicates merchants ‘of’
89.x: Nanadesis means merchants ‘of many countries’ and was associated with foreign trade.
89.tq: Use the literal qualification in the guild name to distinguish foreign traders from local assemblies.

89.s: What was the principal activity of the Nagaram?
o: Local merchant assembly and domestic trade in market towns
89.x: Nagaram was a local merchant assembly in market towns and was associated with domestic trade.
89.tq: Separate the local domestic role of Nagaram from the overseas role of other guilds.

89.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Guild or body)
a. Manigramam
b. Ainnurruvar
c. Nanadesis
 d. Nagaram

List-II (Activity)
i. Local merchant assembly and domestic trade
 ii. Foreign or long-distance trade
 iii. Inter-regional and overseas trade
 iv. Foreign trade, meaning ‘of many countries’

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: Manigramam handled foreign or long-distance trade; Ainnurruvar was inter-regional and overseas; Nanadesis represented merchants of many countries; Nagaram was local and domestic.
89.tq: Build the answer from the distinctive sure pair Nagaram–local domestic trade, then verify the remaining guilds.

89.s: As Chola power declined, the merchant guilds
o: became independent and adopted their own codes and collective decisions
were abolished by the royal administration
restricted themselves exclusively to temple donations
lost all role in foreign trade
89.x: With the waning of Chola power, the guilds grew independent and developed their own codes of conduct and collective decision-making.
89.tq: Identify the institutional change associated with the decline of central power.

89.s: In Andhra, the Nanadesi Pekkundru and the Nakaram were respectively associated with
89.x: The Nanadesi Pekkundru was the foreign-trade guild in Andhra, while the Nakaram was associated with domestic trade.
89.tq: Test the reversed roles of the two Andhra merchant bodies.

89.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nakaram — Overseas merchant body in Andhra
Nanadesi Pekkundru — Foreign trade in Andhra
Ainnurruvar — Inter-regional and overseas merchant body
89.x: Nakaram was the domestic-trade body in Andhra, whereas Nanadesi Pekkundru was associated with foreign trade.
89.tq: Look for the reversed foreign–domestic distinction in the Andhra guild pair.

89.s: The Anaimangalam copper plates are presently associated with which institution?
89.x: The Chola-era Anaimangalam copper plates were held by Leiden University for almost two centuries.
89.tq: Identify the present institutional custodian in a current-affairs heritage question.

89.s: The Anaimangalam copper plates were returned to India by the Netherlands in
89.x: The Anaimangalam copper plates were returned by the Netherlands in May 2026, specifically on 16 May 2026.
89.tq: Distinguish the precise return year from nearby current-affairs dates.

89.s: The Anaimangalam copper plates document Chola links with Srivijaya in the spheres of
89.x: The plates document Chola–Srivijaya religious and trade links.
89.tq: Match the inscriptional source with the two domains explicitly documented by it.

89.s: The Kudavolai system was cited as evidence of
o: the beginning of Roman trade in India
89.x: The Chola Kudavolai ballot-pot system was cited as proof of early Indian democracy.
89.tq: Recognise the institutional function of a historical voting method in a contemporary reference.

89.s: Rajendra I was highlighted as the builder of
89.x: Rajendra I, whose reign is given as 1012–1044, was highlighted as the builder of Gangaikondacholapuram.
89.tq: Match the ruler and regnal period with the city associated with his architectural legacy.

89.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to architectural styles in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Draksharama Bhimeswara — exclusively Imperial Chola style
89.x: Draksharama Bhimeswara represents the independent Chalukya-Chola style. Brihadeeswara is Imperial Chola, while Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.
89.tq: Use the regional architectural comparisons to reject swapped dynastic styles.

89.s: The independent Chalukya-Chola style of the Draksharama Bhimeswara temple reflects the combination of
89.x: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple shows an independent Chalukya-Chola style combining Pallava and early Chalukya elements.
89.tq: Identify the component traditions behind a named regional architectural style.

89.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the comparative development of Dravidian art?
o: The Pallavas laid its foundation and the Cholas developed it on a monumental scale.
The Cholas laid its foundation and the Pallavas built its monumental culmination.
The Rashtrakutas alone created the Dravidian tradition.
The Hoysalas laid its foundation and the Kakatiyas completed it.
89.x: The comparison states that the Pallavas laid the foundation of Dravidian art, while the Cholas built its monumental culmination.
89.tq: Preserve the direction of the comparison instead of reversing the contributions of the Pallavas and Cholas.

89.s: The third phase of underwater exploration mentioned in connection with Poompuhar was begun by
89.x: Tamil Nadu began the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar or Kaveripattinam.
89.tq: Identify the state undertaking the current archaeological exploration.

89.s:
Earlier underwater finds at Poompuhar included which of the following?
1. Wharves
2. Fourth-century BCE pottery
3. A lighthouse
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
89.x: Earlier finds at Poompuhar included wharves, fourth-century BCE pottery and a lighthouse.
89.tq: Check all three archaeological discoveries before selecting the complete combination.

89.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Angkor Wat — a monument of the Imperial Chola style in Tamil Nadu
89.x: Angkor Wat is an example of South-East Asian architecture influenced by the wider transmission of Dravidian art; it is not a monument of Imperial Chola style located in Tamil Nadu.
89.tq: Reject the option that turns cultural influence into an incorrect location and dynastic attribution.

90.s: Which one of the following was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas?
90.x: Belur was the earlier capital of the Hoysalas, before Dwarasamudra became their capital.
90.tq: Use the capital-sequence distinction rather than confusing a capital with a temple site.

90.s: Halebidu acquired the meaning “old city” after which event?
o: Dwarasamudra was sacked by the Delhi armies
90.x: Halebidu means “old city”; the name was adopted after Dwarasamudra was sacked by the Delhi armies.
90.tq: Test the cause behind a historical place-name instead of merely recalling the name.

90.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chennakeshava Temple — Belur
2. Hoysaleswara Temple — Halebid
3. Keshava Temple — Somanathapura
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
90.x: Chennakeshava is at Belur, Hoysaleswara at Halebid, and Keshava at Somanathapura. Therefore, all three pairs are correctly matched.
90.tq: Split the options by verifying the temple-site pairs one by one.

90.s: Who built the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur?
90.x: The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur was built by Vishnuvardhana in 1117.
90.tq: Use the builder–monument association and avoid swapping patrons among Hoysala temples.

90.s: The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur was constructed in 1117 after Vishnuvardhana’s victory over the Cholas at:
90.x: Vishnuvardhana built the temple in 1117 after defeating the Cholas at Talakad.
90.tq: Link the date, builder and victory site instead of treating the year as an isolated fact.

90.s: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebid is dedicated to:
90.x: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebid is dedicated to Shiva.
90.tq: Apply the deity–temple distinction to separate Hoysaleswara from the Vishnu temples.

90.s: Who was responsible for building the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebid?
90.x: Hoysaleswara was built around 1121 by Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana.
90.tq: Use the wrong-person trap by distinguishing the builder, general and sculptor.

90.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura?
o: It is dedicated to Shiva and was built by Ketamalla.
It is dedicated to Vishnu and was built by Somanatha.
It is dedicated to Vishnu and was built by Vishnuvardhana.
It is dedicated to Shiva and was built by Narasimha III.
90.x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura is dedicated to Vishnu and was built in 1268 by Somanatha, the general of Narasimha III.
90.tq: Check the deity and builder together to defeat a swapped-pair option.

90.s: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 during the reign of:
90.x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 during the reign of Narasimha III.
90.tq: Use the reign–monument association rather than relying only on the temple’s location.

90.s: Which one of the following temples is noted for having the best-preserved star-shaped plan?
90.x: The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura is regarded as having the best-preserved star-shaped plan.
90.tq: Use the distinctive architectural superlative to distinguish the three major temples.

90.s: In the classification used in examination references, Hoysala temple architecture belongs to which style family?
90.x: Hoysala architecture is generally classified as Vesara in examination keys, although it is also described as an evolution of the Dravida style.
90.tq: Test the examination classification while distinguishing it from a broader architectural description.

90.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hoysala architecture:
1. Its ground plan is generally stellate or star-shaped.
2. The temples were built on a raised jagati platform of about one metre.
3. The stellate plan reached its peak under the Hoysalas in the twelfth century.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Hoysala temples commonly have stellate plans on raised jagati platforms, and the form reached its peak under the Hoysalas in the twelfth century.
90.tq: Combine architectural form, platform and chronology in a statement set.

90.s: The stellate temple plan originated under the Chalukyas and reached its peak under the Hoysalas in which centuries respectively?
90.x: The stellate plan originated under the Chalukyas in the sixth century and reached its peak under the Hoysalas in the twelfth century.
90.tq: Remember the sequence of origin and culmination through the century pair.

90.s: Which material was particularly used in Hoysala temples because it permitted jewel-like carving?
90.x: Hoysala temples used chloritic schist, commonly called soapstone, which allowed intricate, jewel-like carving.
90.tq: Match the architectural material with its functional advantage.

90.s: Hoysala temples are especially known for pillars that are:
90.x: Hoysala pillars are characteristically lathe-turned and finely polished.
90.tq: Identify the precise architectural feature rather than a general description of temple pillars.

90.s: Which of the following features is associated with Hoysala temple halls?
o: Open mantapas with several shrines around a central pillared hall
90.x: Hoysala temple complexes include open mantapas and several shrines arranged around a central pillared hall.
90.tq: Apply the architectural description to identify the correct plan of the temple hall.

90.s: Horizontal friezes in Hoysala temples commonly depict:
o: Elephants, lions, horses and episodes from epics
90.x: Hoysala horizontal friezes include representations of elephants, lions, horses and epic themes.
90.tq: Use the composition of the friezes to distinguish Hoysala sculptural decoration.

90.s: Madanikas or Salabhanjikas are associated especially with which feature of Hoysala architecture?
90.x: Madanikas or Salabhanjikas are bracket figures prominently associated with the temple at Belur.
90.tq: Distinguish a sculptural feature from a site’s political or defensive history.

90.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
90.x: Mallitamma is associated with the sculptures of Somanathapura. Jakanachari is the legendary sculptor traditionally credited with Belur.
90.tq: Separate historical builders and generals from sculptors’ traditional signatures.

90.s: Which statement about Hoysala pillars is NOT correct?
o: They could include leaping lion or horse heads.
They could be carved into three or four sections on a single base.
They were generally left unpolished to preserve the rough texture of soapstone.
90.x: Hoysala pillars were finely polished, not generally left rough. They could have three or four sections on one base, leaping animal heads, and influenced Vijayanagara architecture.
90.tq: Find the one reversed material-and-finish statement.

90.s: Who among the following was an early chief under the Western Chalukyas?
90.x: Nripa Kama II was an early Hoysala chief under the Western Chalukyas.
90.tq: Use the ruler–achievement association without confusing an early chief with later independent rulers.

90.s: Which Hoysala ruler made the Hoysalas independent after defeating Yadava Bhillama?
90.x: Veera Ballala II defeated Yadava Bhillama and made the Hoysalas independent; his reign is given as 1170–1220.
90.tq: Link the victory and political consequence to the correct ruler.

90.s: Narasimha II is associated with which achievement?
o: Building the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura in 1268
Defeating Yadava Bhillama and founding Hoysala independence
Fighting the Yadavas during his reign
90.x: Narasimha II, who ruled from 1220 to 1254, fought the Yadavas.
90.tq: Distinguish closely related Hoysala rulers by assigning each one a separate achievement.

90.s: Which event is associated with Narasimha III?
o: Victory over the Cholas at Talakad
Defeat of Yadava Ramachandra’s forces in 1305
90.x: Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandya ruler Maravarman Kulasekhara. The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura was also built during his reign.
90.tq: Use the swapped-ruler trap by matching the achievement to the correct reign.

90.s:
Consider the following statements about Ballala III:
1. He defeated the forces of Yadava Ramachandra in 1305.
2. He was defeated by the Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316.
3. He ruled from 1295 to 1342.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
90.x: Ballala III ruled from 1295 to 1342, defeated Ramachandra’s forces in 1305, and was later defeated by the Kakatiya commander Pedarudru after 1316.
90.tq: Verify the ruler through a combination of dates, victories and defeat.

90.s: What was the original name of Vishnuvardhana?
90.x: Vishnuvardhana was originally known as Bittideva, also called Bittiga.
90.tq: Test a ruler’s original name directly, a common history recall pattern.

90.s: Vishnuvardhana, originally a Jain, became a Vaishnava under the influence of:
90.x: Bittideva became a Vaishnava under Ramanuja, who had taken refuge in Hoysala territory from Chola persecution.
90.tq: Use the teacher–conversion association and avoid confusing a religious teacher with a political ally.

90.s: Which statement correctly describes the religious policy of Vishnuvardhana’s court?
o: Queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain, and Jain basadis continued to receive court patronage.
Queen Shantala Devi became a Vaishnava, and Jain basadis were abolished.
Ramanuja remained a Jain, and Vaishnava temples were not patronised.
The court patronised only one religious tradition.
90.x: Although Vishnuvardhana became a Vaishnava, Queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain and the court continued to patronise Jain basadis.
90.tq: Distinguish the ruler’s conversion from the continued religious identity and patronage of the court.

90.s: Vishnuvardhana assumed the title ‘Talakadugonda’ after his victory over the:
90.x: Vishnuvardhana defeated the Cholas at Talakad and assumed the title Talakadugonda.
90.tq: Connect the victory site with the title derived from it.

90.s: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in:
90.x: The Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage property in 2023.
90.tq: Use the year-based current-affairs pattern while distinguishing inscription from construction dates.

90.s: Which of the following correctly lists the components of the UNESCO Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas?
o: Chennakeshava at Belur, Hoysaleswara at Halebid and Keshava at Somanathapura
Chennakeshava at Talakad, Hoysaleswara at Devagiri and Keshava at Belur
Hoysaleswara at Belur, Chennakeshava at Somanathapura and Keshava at Halebid
Keshava at Belur, Chennakeshava at Halebid and Hoysaleswara at Somanathapura
90.x: The three components are Chennakeshava Temple at Belur, Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebid and Keshava Temple at Somanathapura.
90.tq: Start from the sure temple-site pairs and eliminate options that rearrange them.

90.s: Which one of the following statements about Hoysala decline is correct?
o: The Hoysalas faced constant wars with the Yadavas of Devagiri and the Pandyas.
The Hoysalas maintained uninterrupted peace with both the Yadavas and the Pandyas.
The Pandyas were defeated by Narasimha III and became permanent Hoysala allies.
The Yadavas of Devagiri never attacked the Hoysala kingdom.
90.x: The Hoysalas were involved in constant wars with the Yadavas of Devagiri and the Pandyas. Singhana defeated the Hoysalas, while Mahadeva Yadava was defeated by them; Narasimha III was defeated by the Pandyas.
90.tq: Reject absolute peace claims and identify the accurate cause of political decline.

90.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Malik Kafur’s southern campaign?
o: Dwarasamudra was one of the southern capitals attacked by Malik Kafur.
Malik Kafur attacked Dwarasamudra only after the kingdom had passed to Vijayanagara.
The four affected powers included the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.
90.x: Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra in 1311, before the Hoysala kingdom’s space passed to Vijayanagara. The Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas were among the four southern powers affected by his campaign.
90.tq: Use chronology to identify the statement that places an event after the wrong political transition.

90.s: Ballala III died in which year, after which the space of the Hoysala kingdom passed to Vijayanagara?
90.x: Ballala III died in 1342, and the political space of the Hoysala kingdom subsequently passed to Vijayanagara.
90.tq: Distinguish the dates of the Yadava conflict, Malik Kafur’s attack and Ballala III’s death.

90.s: A veeragallu with a Kannada inscription found at Neeragunda in Arsikere taluk may help settle which historical question?
o: The date of the construction of the Keshava Temple
The date of Malik Kafur’s death
90.x: The hero stone, unearthed on 28 June 2026, may help settle the long-disputed date of Vishnuvardhana’s death.
90.tq: Apply the archaeological discovery to the specific historical problem it may resolve.

90.s: The veeragallu mentioned in connection with a disputed Hoysala date was found at:
90.x: The Kannada-inscribed veeragallu was found at Neeragunda in Arsikere taluk.
90.tq: Test the precise archaeological location rather than the broader Hoysala region.

90.s: Which architectural traditions influenced Vijayanagara architecture according to the comparative account of Hoysala art?
90.x: Vijayanagara architecture followed the Hoysala and Pandya styles according to the comparative assessment.
90.tq: Use the comparison pair directly and avoid substituting other South Indian traditions.

91.s: Who among the following founded Devagiri as the capital of the Yadavas after throwing off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship?
91.x: Bhillama V threw off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship and founded Devagiri as the Yadava capital around 1187.
91.tq: Match the ruler with his distinctive achievement.

91.s:
Consider the following statements about Jaitugi:
1. He killed Kakatiya Rudradeva.
2. He held Ganapatideva captive and later released him in 1199.
3. He married his daughter Somaladevi to Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva, held Ganapatideva captive, released him in 1199, and married Somaladevi to him.
91.tq: Check the complete sequence of actions attributed to one ruler.

91.s: The Paithan copper plate of Ramachandra is significant because it confirms that Jaitugi
o: defeated Veera Ballala II and annexed Hoysala territory
captured Delhi and deposed Jalaluddin Khalji
founded Devagiri and renamed it Daulatabad
91.x: The Paithan copper plate confirms Jaitugi’s killing of Rudradeva and imprisonment of Ganapatideva.
91.tq: Identify the inscriptional evidence associated with the event.

91.s: Which Yadava ruler was known as the greatest of the Yadava rulers and assumed the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’?
91.x: Singhana II, who ruled from 1200 to 1247, was regarded as the greatest Yadava ruler and bore the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’.
91.tq: Link the title with the ruler who held it.

91.s: The title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’ means
91.x: The title means ‘installer of the Telugu king’.
91.tq: Discriminate between closely related meanings of a royal title.

91.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ramachandra — Defeated by Delhi forces in 1295
Shankaradeva — Founded Devagiri as the Yadava capital
91.x: Devagiri was founded as the Yadava capital by Bhillama V, not Shankaradeva. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
91.tq: Find the wrong ruler–achievement association.

91.s:
Arrange the following Yadava rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Mahadeva
B. Singhana II
C. Ramachandra
D. Krishna
91.x: Singhana II ruled from 1200, followed by Krishna, Mahadeva and Ramachandra.
91.tq: Place rulers in sequence using the given reign periods.

91.s: Which Yadava ruler’s attack on the Kakatiyas was repulsed by Rudramadevi?
91.x: Rudramadevi repulsed the attack launched by Yadava ruler Mahadeva against the Kakatiyas.
91.tq: Identify the ruler involved in the specific military encounter.

91.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ramachandra was defeated by Delhi forces in 1295.
2. Ramachandra subsequently became a feudatory.
3. Harapaladeva’s death marked the end of the Yadava kingdom.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Ramachandra was defeated in 1295 and became a feudatory, while Harapaladeva’s death during Mubarak Khalji’s invasion marked the end of the Yadava kingdom.
91.tq: Combine ruler, political status and dynastic-end facts.

91.s: Which of the following correctly represents the final Yadava rulers and the circumstances of their deaths?
o: Shankaradeva — Malik Kafur’s invasion; Harapaladeva — Mubarak Khalji’s invasion
Shankaradeva — Alauddin Khalji’s first raid; Harapaladeva — Veera Ballala II’s attack
Shankaradeva — Rudramadevi’s attack; Harapaladeva — Jaitugi’s invasion
Shankaradeva — Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s invasion; Harapaladeva — Malik Kafur’s campaign
91.x: Shankaradeva died during Malik Kafur’s invasion in 1313, and Harapaladeva was killed during Mubarak Khalji’s invasion in 1317–18.
91.tq: Match each ruler with the invading commander responsible for his death.

91.s: The Yadavas of Devagiri were also known as the
91.x: The dynasty is also referred to as the Seuna Yadavas.
91.tq: Recall the alternate dynastic name.

91.s: Which one of the following statements about the linguistic profile of the Yadavas is correct?
o: Their mother tongue was Marathi, while Sanskrit remained the language of scholarship.
Their mother tongue was Kannada, while Prakrit remained the language of scholarship.
Their mother tongue was Telugu, while Kannada remained the language of scholarship.
Their mother tongue was Sanskrit, while Marathi was used only in inscriptions.
91.x: The mother tongue of the Yadavas was Marathi, whereas Sanskrit continued as the language of scholarship.
91.tq: Separate the popular language from the scholarly language.

91.s: Devagiri, the capital of the Yadavas, is identified with present-day
91.x: Devagiri was located in Maharashtra and is presently known as Daulatabad.
91.tq: Link the historical and modern names of the capital.

91.s: Who renamed Devagiri as Daulatabad?
91.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed Devagiri as Daulatabad and shifted his capital there.
91.tq: Use the ruler–administrative action association.

91.s: Singhana II released Ganapatideva primarily because he intended to
o: make him the successor to the Yadava throne
secure control over the Delhi Sultanate
appoint him as the governor of Devagiri
use him as a counterweight to Hoysala Veera Ballala’s advance
91.x: Singhana released Ganapatideva to use him as a counterweight to Veera Ballala’s push into the Krishna–Tungabhadra region.
91.tq: Infer the political purpose behind the release of a captive.

91.s: Who was Sarangapanideva in relation to the Yadava–Kakatiya political context?
o: Hemadri’s teacher who composed the Dnyaneshwari
Singhana II’s son who later served at Rudramadevi’s court
Ganapatideva’s son who defeated Singhana II
91.x: Sarangapanideva, the son of Singhana II, later served at the court of Rudramadevi.
91.tq: Identify the person through a family and court association.

91.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sarngadeva — Music
2. Changadeva — Astronomy
3. Changadeva — Grandson of Bhaskaracharya
4. Sarngadeva — Founder of the school at Patan for teaching Bhaskara’s works
91.x: Sarngadeva was associated with music. Changadeva was an astronomer, grandson of Bhaskaracharya, and established the school at Patan; statement 4 wrongly assigns that act to Sarngadeva.
91.tq: Separate closely associated scholars by their disciplines and deeds.

91.s: Who set up a school at Patan to teach the works of Bhaskaracharya?
91.x: Changadeva, the astronomer and grandson of Bhaskaracharya, established the school at Patan.
91.tq: Match the scholar with the institution founded by him.

91.s: Hemadri served as Shrikaranadhipa under which Yadava rulers?
91.x: Hemadri served Mahadeva and Ramachandra as Shrikaranadhipa, the head of the secretariat or records.
91.tq: Associate an office-holder with the rulers under whom he served.

91.s: The office of Shrikaranadhipa held by Hemadri was concerned chiefly with
91.x: Shrikaranadhipa was the head of the secretariat and records administration.
91.tq: Identify the function of the official designation.

91.s: Hemadri’s Chaturvarga Chintamani is best described as a Sanskrit work dealing with
o: dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas
91.x: Chaturvarga Chintamani is a Sanskrit encyclopaedia dealing with dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas.
91.tq: Identify the subject coverage of the named work.

91.s: Which architectural style is traditionally credited to Hemadri?
91.x: Hemadri is credited with the Hemadpanti style of temple architecture.
91.tq: Match the architect-scholar with the architectural style.

91.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Hemadpanti architecture:
1. It used local black basalt.
2. Its dressed stones were interlocked without mortar.
3. Its masonry is therefore described as dry masonry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
91.x: Hemadpanti construction used local black basalt and interlocked dressed stones without mortar, a technique known as dry masonry.
91.tq: Test material, construction method and technical description as one chain.

91.s: Which statement about Hemadri’s account of Kakatiya Rudra is correct?
o: He claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra.
He stated that Rudra founded the Hemadpanti style.
He recorded that Rudra served as Shrikaranadhipa.
He claimed that Rudra captured and sacrificed Jaitugi.
91.x: The Yadava court poet Hemadri claimed that Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Kakatiya Rudra.
91.tq: Watch for the swapped subject and object in a historical claim.

91.s: Who wrote the Sangita Ratnakara?
91.x: Sangita Ratnakara was written by Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana II.
91.tq: Match the classical work with its author.

91.s: Sarngadeva wrote the Sangita Ratnakara while serving as the court musician of
91.x: Sarngadeva was the court musician of Singhana II.
91.tq: Use the author–patron relationship rather than the work title alone.

91.s: The Sangita Ratnakara is regarded as a basic text for
91.x: The Sangita Ratnakara is considered a basic text for both Hindustani and Carnatic music.
91.tq: Distinguish a shared foundational text from an exclusive tradition.

91.s: The Dnyaneshwari, composed by the saint-poet Dnyaneshwar, is a
o: Marathi prose biography of Chakradhar Swami
91.x: Dnyaneshwari is Dnyaneshwar’s Marathi commentary on the Bhagavad Gita.
91.tq: Identify the language and subject of the literary work.

91.s: In which year and at which place was the Dnyaneshwari written?
91.x: The Dnyaneshwari was written in 1290 at Nevasa during the reign of Ramachandra.
91.tq: Combine the year, place and reigning ruler associated with a work.

91.s: The Dnyaneshwari was composed during the reign of
91.x: Dnyaneshwar composed the Dnyaneshwari in 1290 during Ramachandra’s reign.
91.tq: Match a literary work with its patron’s reign.

91.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chakradhar Swami — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
Dnyaneshwar — Founder of the Mahanubhava sect
91.x: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by Chakradhar Swami. Dnyaneshwar composed the Dnyaneshwari; he did not found the Mahanubhava sect.
91.tq: Separate the founder, author and literary work in a cultural movement.

91.s: Which group of saints took Upanishadic and Gita ideas into Marathi?
91.x: Dnyaneshwar, Namdev, and later Tukaram and Ramdas carried Upanishadic and Gita ideas into Marathi.
91.tq: Identify the complete group belonging to the Bhakti-literary tradition.

91.s: Who led the first Muslim invasion of the South on Devagiri in 1295?
o: Alauddin Khalji on behalf of Sultan Jalaluddin
Muhammad bin Tughlaq on behalf of Alauddin Khalji
Malik Kafur on behalf of Alauddin Khalji
Mubarak Khalji on behalf of Ramachandra
91.x: In 1295, Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin, defeated Ramachandra at Devagiri and took Ellichpur.
91.tq: Distinguish the commander, nominal sovereign and year of the first raid.

91.s: What was the immediate political result of Alauddin Khalji’s 1295 expedition against Devagiri?
o: Harapaladeva ended the Delhi Sultanate’s rule.
Devagiri became the capital of the Kakatiyas.
The Yadavas annexed the Hoysala kingdom.
The Yadavas became vassals of Delhi after Ramachandra’s defeat.
91.x: Alauddin Khalji defeated Ramachandra, took Ellichpur, and reduced the Yadavas to the status of Delhi vassals.
91.tq: Infer the political consequence of a military defeat.

91.s: Which sequence correctly represents the major Delhi Sultanate interventions in the Yadava kingdom?
o: 1295 first invasion; 1307–08 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Harapaladeva killed
1307–08 first invasion; 1295 Shankaradeva killed; 1317–18 Malik Kafur’s campaign; 1313 kingdom founded
1313 first invasion; 1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1307–08 kingdom restored; 1317–18 Ramachandra crowned
1295 Harapaladeva killed; 1313 Malik Kafur appointed vizier; 1307–08 Devagiri founded; 1317–18 Ramachandra submits
91.x: The sequence was the 1295 first invasion, Malik Kafur’s 1307–08 campaign, Shankaradeva’s death in 1313, and Harapaladeva’s death in 1317–18.
91.tq: Use the dated invasion sequence from first defeat to dynastic extinction.

91.s: During Malik Kafur’s campaign of 1307–08, which of the following occurred?
o: Ramachandra submitted and was taken to Delhi.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital to Devagiri.
Bhillama founded Devagiri and defeated Veera Ballala II.
91.x: During the 1307–08 campaign, Ramachandra submitted to Malik Kafur and was taken to Delhi.
91.tq: Match the campaign year with its immediate event.

91.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the year with the event?
1. 1295 — Alauddin Khalji’s first invasion of Devagiri
2. 1307–08 — Malik Kafur’s campaign
3. 1313 — Death of Shankaradeva
4. 1317–18 — Death of Harapaladeva
91.x: All four year–event associations are correct. The 1295 raid is also dated as 1296 in some texts, but the specified chronology places it in 1295.
91.tq: Check every date against its corresponding event, including the final dynastic phase.

91.s: After 1323, who was given charge of the conquered Andhra region?
o: Malik Burhanuddin, the vizier of Devagiri
Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana
91.x: After 1323, Devagiri’s vizier Malik Burhanuddin was placed in charge of conquered Andhra.
91.tq: Identify the administrator appointed over the conquered region.

91.s: The importance of Devagiri in the expansion of the Delhi Sultanate lay in the fact that it
o: was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi and opened routes towards major southern kingdoms
prevented all further Delhi campaigns into the Deccan
was the first capital established by the Hoysalas in northern India
served as the original capital of the Kakatiyas
91.x: Devagiri was the first southern kingdom to fall to Delhi, opening the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
91.tq: Apply the historical significance of a strategic conquest.

91.s: Which of the following places were made accessible to Delhi forces after the fall of Devagiri?
91.x: The fall of Devagiri opened the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
91.tq: Recall the geographical consequences of the first southern conquest.

91.s: Which set correctly represents the Yadava–Kakatiya rivalry?
o: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva; Singhana used the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’; Rudramadevi defeated Mahadeva
Rudradeva killed Jaitugi; Mahadeva installed Singhana; Ganapatideva defeated Rudramadevi
Singhana founded Devagiri; Rudramadevi defeated Bhillama; Jaitugi served under Ramachandra
Mahadeva killed Ganapatideva; Rudradeva founded the Yadava kingdom; Singhana defeated Rudramadevi
91.x: The rivalry included Jaitugi’s killing of Rudradeva, Singhana’s claim to be the installer of the Telugu king, and Rudramadevi’s repulse of Mahadeva’s attack.
91.tq: Start from the sure ruler–event pairs in an inter-dynastic rivalry.

92.s: The ancient name ‘Orugallu’, associated with the later Kakatiya capital, literally means:
92.x: Orugallu is the ancient name of Warangal and means ‘single rock’.
92.tq: Use the exact meaning of the place-name rather than its later political association.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the names associated with the Kakatiya capital:
1. Andhranagari was a name used for Orugallu under Ganapatideva.
2. Sultanpur was the name given to Orugallu after the conquest of 1323.
3. Orugallu was the early capital made by Prola I.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: Andhranagari was used under Ganapatideva, and Sultanpur was the name given after the conquest of 1323. The early capital was Anumakonda or Hanamkonda, not Orugallu.
92.tq: Split the statements by distinguishing the successive names and stages of the capital.

92.s: With reference to the development of the Kakatiya capital, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Prola I — made Orugallu the capital
Rudradeva — gave Orugallu the name Sultanpur
92.x: Prola II developed Hanamkonda. Prola I made Anumakonda the capital, Rudradeva shifted the capital to Orugallu, and Sultanpur was the post-1323 name.
92.tq: Match each ruler with the correct stage in the evolution of the capital.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the respective roles of Rudradeva and Ganapatideva in relation to Orugallu?
o: Rudradeva began fortifying Orugallu, while Ganapatideva completed it and fully moved the court there.
Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Orugallu, while Rudradeva renamed it Sultanpur.
Rudradeva abandoned Orugallu, while Ganapatideva restored Hanamkonda as the capital.
Rudradeva completed the city and Ganapatideva began its fortification.
92.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu. Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.
92.tq: Separate the initiating ruler from the ruler who completed the work.

92.s: Who is identified as the first person named in the Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava dated 956 CE?
92.x: Kakartya Gundana is the first Kakatiya name in the Magallu grant of Danarnava dated 956 CE.
92.tq: Test the earliest named figure through the inscription-date association.

92.s: Which of the following statements about Beta I is correct?
o: He was known as Garuda Beta and obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva.
He was known as Arigajakesari and built Kesamudram tank.
He founded Orugallu and composed Nitisara.
92.x: Beta I, also called Garuda Beta, obtained Anumakonda Vishaya through his aunt Viriyala Kamasani. The other achievements belong to Prola I, Rudradeva and Mahadeva respectively.
92.tq: Use the ruler-achievement association and reject deeds belonging to neighbouring rulers.

92.s: Beta I attacked Kanchi in 1051 in support of which ruler?
92.x: Beta I attacked Kanchi in 1051 in support of Someshwara I.
92.tq: Link the military action to its stated political patron.

92.s: Who built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram?
92.x: Naranayya, the minister of Beta I, built the Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram.
92.tq: Apply the ‘minister–construction’ association without swapping ministers between rulers.

92.s: Prola I is associated with which combination of titles and achievement?
o: Arigajakesari; Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; construction of Kesamudram tank
Cholachamu Vari Pramathana; Vidyabhushana; construction of the Thousand Pillar Temple
Vidyabhushana; Kanchi Churakara; construction of Arikesari Samudram
Samadhigata Panchamahasabda; Rayagaja Kesari; construction of Ramappa temple
92.x: Prola I bore the titles Arigajakesari and Samadhigata Panchamahasabda and built Kesamudram tank.
92.tq: Start from the sure title and verify the achievement attached to the same ruler.

92.s: Which change is associated with Prola I during the development of the Kakatiya polity?
o: The capital changed from Orugallu to Anumakonda.
The emblem changed from Varaha to Garuda.
The capital changed from Hanamkonda to Kanchi.
The emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.x: During Prola I’s period, the Kakatiya emblem changed from Garuda to Varaha.
92.tq: Discriminate between the two directions of an emblem change.

92.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Beta II — Shivapura and Betesvaralayam
2. Durgaraja — donations to the Betesvara temple
3. Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
4. Mahadeva — construction of Ramappa temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: Beta II built Shivapura and Betesvaralayam, Durgaraja made donations to the Betesvara temple, and Prola II erected a victory pillar at Srisailam. Ramappa temple belongs to the reign of Ganapatideva, not Mahadeva.
92.tq: Find the swapped ruler–achievement statement before selecting the coded combination.

92.s: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of which institution?
92.x: Beta II was initiated into Saivism by Rameswara Pandita of the Srisailam Mallikarjuna matha.
92.tq: Identify the religious teacher through the institution associated with him.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Prola II — victory pillar at Srisailam
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 belongs to Ganapatideva. Prola II is associated with Arikesari Samudram, the Swayambhu temple and the victory pillar at Srisailam.
92.tq: Find the achievement belonging to a different ruler.

92.s: Prola II was killed while fighting against which group?
92.x: Prola II was killed while fighting the Velanati kings.
92.tq: Distinguish the opponent in a ruler’s final military engagement.

92.s: Who, along with his wife Mailama, built the Jain Kadalalaya Jainavasadi at Anumakonda?
92.x: Chetanamatya, minister of Prola II, and his wife Mailama built the Jain Kadalalaya Jainavasadi at Anumakonda.
92.tq: Use the minister–spouse–monument linkage to avoid a ministerial name swap.

92.s: Rudradeva’s description as ‘Vidyabhushana’ is associated with which of the following?
o: His donations to the Betesvara temple
His independence from the Kalyani Chalukyas in 1163
His invasion of the Yadavas after the death of Mahadeva
92.x: Rudradeva was described as ‘Vidyabhushana’, and he declared independence in 1163, as recorded in the Thousand Pillar inscription.
92.tq: Connect the ruler’s title with the major political achievement of his reign.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about Rudradeva:
1. He began the Thousand Pillar Temple tradition associated with Rudreshwara at Hanamkonda.
2. He founded Orugallu as the Kakatiya capital.
3. He was killed by the Yadava ruler Jaitugi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements are correct. Rudradeva is associated with the Thousand Pillar Temple, the foundation of Orugallu as capital, and his death at the hands of Yadava Jaitugi.
92.tq: Check each achievement and the ruler responsible before choosing the inclusive code.

92.s: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158, attributed to minister Inangala Brahma Reddi, is important for its description of:
92.x: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 describes the accession of Rudradeva and is attributed to minister Inangala Brahma Reddi.
92.tq: Pair the inscription date with the event it records.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding Mahadeva is correct?
o: He built the Jain Kadalalaya at Anumakonda.
He invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle while crossing a river on an elephant.
He issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244.
He founded Orugallu and completed its fortifications.
92.x: Mahadeva invaded the Yadavas to avenge Rudradeva and died in battle, reportedly on an elephant while crossing a river.
92.tq: Use the unusual detail of the ruler’s death to identify the correct statement.

92.s: Who was the guru of Mahadeva?
92.x: Dhruveshwara Pandita was the guru of Mahadeva.
92.tq: Distinguish Mahadeva’s guru from the religious teacher associated with Beta II.

92.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Ganapatideva is correctly matched?
o: 63-year reign; Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244; Ramappa temple built during his reign
44-year reign; Draksharamam inscription of 1158; Thousand Pillar Temple built during his reign
19-year reign; Bayyaram inscription; Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya at Sanigaram
8-year reign; Kazipet Dargah inscription; Swayambhu temple built during his reign
92.x: Ganapatideva ruled for 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244, and Ramappa temple was built during his reign by Recherla Rudra.
92.tq: Match the ruler with the period length, charter and monumental achievement.

92.s: Ramappa temple was built during the reign of Ganapatideva by:
92.x: Ramappa temple was built during Ganapatideva’s reign by Recherla Rudra in 1213.
92.tq: Separate the builder of the monument from ministers and inscription authors.

92.s: Which of the following set contains only works or grants associated with Ganapatideva’s reign?
o: Ramappa temple, Lakkavaram tank, Ghanapur tank and Ganapavaram villages
Arikesari Samudram, victory pillar at Srisailam and Betesvaralayam
Thousand Pillar Temple, Kadalalaya Jainavasadi and Kesamudram tank
Kesamudram tank, Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya and Swayambhu temple
92.x: Ramappa temple, the Lakkavaram and Ghanapur tanks, and the grant of Ganapavaram villages are associated with Ganapatideva’s reign.
92.tq: Eliminate sets containing achievements of different Kakatiya rulers.

92.s:
Arrange the following Kakatiya rulers in chronological order of their reigns:
A. Prola II
B. Beta II
C. Rudradeva
D. Mahadeva
92.x: The order is Beta II (1076–1108), Prola II (1116–1157), Rudradeva (1158–1195), and Mahadeva (1195–1199).
92.tq: Fix the sequence using the beginning and end of each ruler’s reign.

92.s: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
92.x: Ganapatideva ruled from 1199 to 1262. The periods given for Kakartya Gundana, Beta I and Prola I are correctly matched.
92.tq: Check the numerical reign periods against the ruler sequence.

92.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the ruler who united the Telugu lands and is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler?
92.x: Ganapatideva is regarded as the greatest Kakatiya ruler and is credited with uniting the Telugu lands.
92.tq: Identify the ruler from the broad political achievement rather than a single monument.

92.s: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in which year?
92.x: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1199.
92.tq: Use the date as the direct discriminator among closely related reign events.

92.s: The first inscription of Ganapatideva was issued at Manthena on:
92.x: Ganapatideva's first inscription was the Manthena inscription dated 26 December 1199.
92.tq: Distinguish the exact date and place of an inscription.

92.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ganapatideva and the Velanati Chodas:
1. Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore jointly killed Prithviswara in 1210.
2. Both rulers assumed the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
3. The Velanati kingdom came to an end in 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All three statements are correct. Prithviswara was killed in 1210, the joint title was adopted by Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka, and the Velanati kingdom ended in that year.
92.tq: Check the linked event, title and consequence as one chronological cluster.

92.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions which geographical feature?
92.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions Kolleru Lake.
92.tq: Match the inscription with its distinctive geographical reference.

92.s: Who among the following was Ganapatideva's general in the coastal campaign that began in 1201?
92.x: Mutyalachaundaraya served as Ganapatideva's general and took Divi during the coastal campaign beginning in 1201.
92.tq: Apply the who-did-what trap to distinguish a general from allied nobles.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political arrangements made by Ganapatideva after the coastal campaign?
o: He married the daughters of Prithviswara and appointed Akkana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Pinnachodi and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Mummadi Rajendra Chola and appointed Bayyana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Manumasiddhi and appointed Tikkana as Gajasahani.
92.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama, and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, the chief of the elephant forces.
92.tq: Test a multi-person relationship by separating family ties from political office.

92.s: The title Gajasahani, conferred by Ganapatideva on Jayapa, denoted the chief of the:
92.x: Gajasahani referred to the chief of the elephant force.
92.tq: Discriminate between similar military offices by their functional meaning.

92.s: In 1257, Ganapatideva allied with Akkana and Bayyana against the enemies of Manumasiddhi and killed:
92.x: Ganapatideva, along with Akkana and Bayyana, killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola in 1257, bringing the final end of the Velanati Chodas.
92.tq: Combine the year, alliance and defeated ruler rather than relying on the battle alone.

92.s: Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to:
92.x: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi.
92.tq: Use the author–work–patron relationship to avoid ruler-name substitution.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the consequence of the Battle of Muttukur?
o: Nellore fell to the Pandyas in 1263.
The Kakatiyas captured Divi from the Pandyas in 1263.
The Velanati kingdom was founded in 1263.
Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1263.
92.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva in 1263, and Nellore fell to them after the Battle of Muttukur.
92.tq: Link the battle with its immediate territorial consequence.
