92.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
92.x: Prola I bore the title Arigajakesari. Vikrama Chakri belonged to Beta II, Vidyabhushana to Rudradeva, and Andhra Deshadhiswara to Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pair and eliminate swapped holders.

92.s: The title ‘Samadhigata Panchamahashabda’ was held by:
92.x: Prola I bore the title Samadhigata Panchamahashabda, along with Arigajakesari.
92.tq: Test an exact royal title against nearby Kakatiya rulers.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chola Chamuvardhi — Beta I
2. Vikrama Chakri — Beta II
3. Vinaya Vibhushanudu — Rudradeva
4. Andhra Deshadhiswara — Ganapatideva
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These titles belonged respectively to Beta I, Beta II, Rudradeva and Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair before selecting the coded combination.

92.s: Which of the following statements regarding the title Kumara Rudradeva is correct?
o: It was the feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas.
It was held by Rudradeva during his accession.
It was the title of Ganapatideva after his victory over the Pandyas.
It was held by Prataparudra II at the time of his accession.
92.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.
92.tq: Separate a personal accession title from titles of earlier Kakatiya rulers.

92.s: Mahamandaleswara, in the Kakatiya context, was primarily:
o: A feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas
A title given to generals of the Nellore Chodas
A title of the sovereign Kakatiya emperor only
A religious title of Jain teachers
92.x: Mahamandaleswara was a feudatory title used by the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
92.tq: Distinguish a feudatory designation from a sovereign royal title.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly states the two principal views regarding the progenitor of the Kakatiyas?
o: Prola I of Hanamkonda and Beta I of Orugallu
Kakara Gundana of Magallu and Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram
Rudradeva of Anumakonda and Ganapatideva of Motupalli
Danarnava of Vengi and Durjaya of Pithapuram
92.x: The progenitor is identified in different traditions as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.
92.tq: Compare competing origin traditions without treating one disputed view as exclusive.

92.s:
Arrange the following phases of Kakatiya political history in chronological order:
A. Sovereign phase
B. Samanta phase
C. Kalyani Chalukya overlordship
D. Rashtrakuta overlordship
92.x: The Kakatiyas were first under the Rashtrakutas, then the Kalyani Chalukyas; the Samanta phase lasted from 956 to 1162, followed by the sovereign phase from 1163 to 1323.
92.tq: Fix the first overlord and then place the feudatory and sovereign phases.

92.s: The Samanta and sovereign phases of Kakatiya history are conventionally dated respectively as:
92.x: The Samanta phase extended from 956 to 1162, while the sovereign phase extended from 1163 to 1323.
92.tq: Distinguish adjacent chronological ranges by their boundary years.

92.s: Which sequence correctly represents the principal overlordship of the early Kakatiyas?
o: Rashtrakutas followed by Eastern Chalukyas only
92.x: The early Kakatiyas were first feudatories of the Rashtrakutas and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukya association occurs in the context of the Magallu grant and may appear as an alternative in some questions.
92.tq: Separate the general sequence of overlordship from the issuer of the first inscription.

92.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Kakatiyas:
1. They belonged to the Shudra social category.
2. Sanskrit was their official language.
3. Their early emblem under Rashtrakuta overlordship was Garuda.
4. The emblem changed to Varaha under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
92.x: All four statements are correct: the Kakatiyas are described as Shudras, used Sanskrit officially, used Garuda during the Rashtrakuta phase and Varaha during the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
92.tq: Use the change in emblem to test the broader social and administrative description.

92.s: Which of the following correctly describes the religious development associated with the early Kakatiyas?
o: They were initially Shaivas and later became Jains.
They remained exclusively Buddhist throughout their history.
They were initially Vaishnavas and later became Buddhists.
They were initially Jains and later became Shaivas.
92.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains and later adopted Shaivism. Their clan deity Kakatamma was identified with the Jain Kushmandini and was absorbed into Hinduism as Kakati Devi.
92.tq: Use the direction of religious change to reject reversed alternatives.

92.s: ‘Kakati’ in the explanation of the Kakatiya clan deity is associated with which meaning?
92.x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
92.tq: Discriminate the exact etymological meaning from emblem and deity associations.

92.s: The Bayyaram inscription traces the Kakatiya line to:
92.x: The Bayyaram inscription traces the Kakatiya lineage to Durjaya.
92.tq: Match the genealogy with the inscription that preserves it.

92.s: The early territorial base of the Kakatiyas was known as:
92.x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya, corresponding broadly to modern Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam areas.
92.tq: Distinguish the early territorial base from later campaign regions.

92.s: Which inscription is correctly matched with its issuer and historical significance?
o: Magallu grant — Eastern Chalukya Danarnava — first mention of the Kakatiya family
Bayyaram inscription — Rudradeva — protection to foreign traders
Motupalli inscription — Mailamba — best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Thousand Pillar inscription — Ganapatideva — first mention of Gundyana
92.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava, dated 956, contains the first mention of the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
92.tq: Start from the distinctive first-mention fact and eliminate exchanged issuers.

92.s: The Magallu grant, dated 956, was issued by:
92.x: The Magallu grant of 956 was issued by Eastern Chalukya Danarnava.
92.tq: Pair the date, issuer and first-mention inscription as a single unit.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bayyaram tank inscription — 1219 — genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Palampet inscription — 1213 — Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam — 1244 — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 concerns protection for foreign traders. Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya is associated with the Sanigaram inscription.
92.tq: Find the one exchanged fact in an inscription–date–content set.

92.s: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by:
92.x: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by Minister Inangala Brahma Reddi and records Rudradeva's accession.
92.tq: Distinguish an inscription issued by a minister from those issued by rulers.

92.s:
Which of the following statements about the Thousand Pillar inscription is correct?
1. It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
2. It is dated 1163.
3. It is associated with Rudradeva.
4. It records the declaration of independence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four statements are correct. The Anumakonda or Thousand Pillar inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva and records Kakatiya independence.
92.tq: Combine alternative names, date, ruler and political significance before selecting the code.

92.s: The Anumakonda inscription was found by J. S. Fleet and composed by:
92.x: J. S. Fleet discovered the Anumakonda inscription, and Achitendru composed it.
92.tq: Separate the discoverer from the composer of an inscription.

92.s: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by:
92.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister, and provides the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
92.tq: Test kinship relations together with the inscription issuer.

92.s: Which inscription is associated with Recherla Rudra and the Ramappa temple?
92.x: The Palampet inscription of 1213 is associated with Recherla Rudra and records the Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign.
92.tq: Identify the monument inscription by pairing its place, date and patron.

92.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 primarily provided:
o: A record of the first mention of Gundyana
A genealogy of the Kakatiya family
A declaration of independence from the Chalukyas
92.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam issued by Ganapatideva in 1244 provided protection for foreign traders.
92.tq: Infer the purpose of a charter from its distinctive administrative provision.

92.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sanigaram — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
2. Palampet — Ramappa temple
3. Dharmasagara — Jalakaranda
4. Pithapuram — Kolleru Lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
92.x: All four pairs are correct. These inscriptions respectively refer to Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, the Ramappa temple, Jalakaranda and Kolleru Lake.
92.tq: Use distinctive cultural and geographical references to secure the inscription pairs.

92.s: Who killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva?
92.x: Yadava ruler Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva during the Kakatiya-Yadava conflict.
92.tq: Use the ruler–event association and eliminate opponents belonging to other conflicts.

92.s: Which development contributed to Yadava Jaitugi releasing Ganapatideva?
o: The invasion of the Krishna-Tungabhadra region by Veera Ballala II
The revolt of the Nellore Chodas
The defeat of the Pandyas at Muttukur
The capture of Kanchi by Rudramadevi
92.x: Hoysala Veera Ballala II pushed into the Krishna-Tungabhadra region, compelling Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
92.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link rather than merely recalling the names of the rulers.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the later Kakatiya conflicts?
o: Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
Rudramadevi was defeated by Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru supported Hoysala Ballala III.
Mahadeva defeated Rudramadevi and captured the Kakatiya capital after 1316.
Pedarudru defeated Yadava Jaitugi and installed Rudramadevi on the throne.
92.x: Rudramadevi repulsed Yadava Mahadeva, and Prataparudra’s commander Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
92.tq: Split the paired ruler–opponent relationships before selecting the precisely matched statement.

92.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Recherla Rudra — Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
2. Prasadaditya — Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya
3. Malyala Chauda Senani — Chouda Samudram
4. Kamasani — Gudur inscription
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
92.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Recherla Rudra bore the title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Sthapanacharya; Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram; and Kamasani’s role is recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Verify each family–member–title or achievement pair independently before using the coded options.

92.s: Who among the following was associated with the titles ‘Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya’ and ‘Raya Pitamahanka’?
92.x: Prasadaditya of the Kayastha family bore the titles Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya and Raya Pitamahanka.
92.tq: Distinguish similar feudatory titles by linking the title to the correct family member.

92.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kamasani — Made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Malyala Chauda Senani — Built Ramappa temple
92.x: Malyala Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram. The Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet are associated with Recherla Rudra.
92.tq: Find the swapped achievement among closely related Kakatiya feudatories.

92.s: Which family of Kakatiya feudatories is associated with Kamasani?
92.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
92.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.

92.s: Recherla Rudra is associated with which combination?
o: Saving the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and constructing the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet
Restoring Manumasiddhi II and serving as an envoy to the Pandyas
Building Chouda Samudram and making Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Defeating Hoysala Ballala III and ruling the Nellore region
92.x: Recherla Rudra saved the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and is associated with the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet.
92.tq: Start from the sure achievement and reject combinations assembled from different feudatories.

92.s: Who was the father of Harihara and Bukka, the founders of the Vijayanagara ruling house?
92.x: Sangama, the father of Harihara and Bukka, was a Kakatiya chief. The brothers had served the Kakatiyas before founding Vijayanagara in 1336.
92.tq: Use the dynastic legacy link rather than confusing the Kakatiya chief with a later ruler.

92.s: The brothers Harihara and Bukka are associated with which sequence?
o: Serving the Kakatiyas, followed by the foundation of Vijayanagara in 1336
Founding Vijayanagara, followed by service under the Kakatiyas in 1336
Serving the Pandyas, followed by the foundation of Warangal in 1263
Serving the Hoysalas, followed by the restoration of Nellore in 1159
92.x: Harihara and Bukka served the Kakatiyas before founding Vijayanagara in 1336.
92.tq: Arrange the two linked stages by identifying the earlier service and the later foundation.

92.s: Who restored Manumasiddhi II of Nellore to his throne?
92.x: Ganapatideva intervened in Nellore affairs and restored Manumasiddhi II to the throne. The poet Tikkana went as envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help.
92.tq: Match the political intervention with the ruler who carried it out.

92.s: Who went as an envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help for Manumasiddhi II?
92.x: The poet Tikkana went as an envoy to request Ganapatideva’s intervention on behalf of Manumasiddhi II.
92.tq: Distinguish the literary figure acting as envoy from military commanders and feudatories.

92.s: Which one of the following statements is correct about Ganapatideva?
o: After the Muttukur defeat, he nevertheless retained firm control over coastal Andhra.
After the Muttukur defeat, he abandoned all control over coastal Andhra.
He ruled only the Nellore region after restoring Manumasiddhi II.
He transferred coastal Andhra to the Yadavas after his release.
92.x: Although Ganapatideva was defeated at Muttukur, he continued to hold coastal Andhra firmly.
92.tq: Watch for the extreme reversal in statements claiming complete loss of territory.

92.s: Which title was borne by Ganapatideva in recognition of his authority over the Telugu country?
92.x: Ganapatideva bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara and is associated with the unification of Telugudesam.
92.tq: Separate a ruler’s sovereign title from the titles of his feudatories.

92.s: As a boy, Ganapatideva was held captive by which ruler?
92.x: Ganapatideva was held captive as a boy by Yadava ruler Jaitugi. Recherla Rudra later crushed revolts and installed him.
92.tq: Differentiate the captor from the later Yadava ruler involved in the revenge war.

92.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Velanati Chodas — Defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263
Pandyas — Made Vellanki Gangadhara viceroy of Sabbinadu
92.x: The Yadavas captured Ganapatideva. The Pandyas defeated him at Muttukur; Velanati Chodas killed Prola II; and Rudradeva appointed Vellanki Gangadhara viceroy of Sabbinadu.
92.tq: Identify the correctly paired opponent and episode while rejecting cross-linked events.

92.s: The conflict with which opponent began during the reign of Prola II?
92.x: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas, also called the Sevunas of Devagiri, began during the reign of Prola II.
92.tq: Link the beginning of the conflict to the correct opponent and period.

92.s: Who killed Prola II?
92.x: The Velanati Chodas killed Prola II. Rudradeva later avenged him and appointed Vellanki Gangadhara as viceroy of Sabbinadu.
92.tq: Apply the strongest history trap: match the ruler with the correct opponent responsible for his death.

92.s: In 1159, Rudradeva defeated which group of opponents?
92.x: In 1159, Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy leaders Mailagi, Medaraja of Polavasa and Dommaraja of Nagumuru.
92.tq: Anchor the year to the specific group of opponents rather than to the better-known later wars.

92.s: Which of the following was defeated by Rudradeva?
92.x: Rudradeva defeated the Telugu Chodas and Tailapa III. The Muttukur victory over Ganapatideva belonged to the Pandyas, while Ballala III was defeated later by Pedarudru.
92.tq: Find the option assigning a later or different ruler’s victory to Rudradeva.

92.s: Which statement regarding the succession after Ganapatideva is correct?
o: Ganapatideva had no son, and Rudrama Devi succeeded him after being raised as a son or putrika.
Ganapatideva’s son succeeded him, while Rudrama Devi remained outside the succession.
Ganapatideva was succeeded by his sister Mailamba after appointing Rudrama Devi as a feudatory.
Rudrama Devi succeeded only after the Kakatiya kingdom was annexed by the Yadavas.
92.x: Ganapatideva had no son. Rudrama Devi was raised as a son, or putrika, and succeeded him.
92.tq: Use the succession exception—daughter raised as a son—to reject the conventional son-successor trap.

92.s: Rudrama Devi ruled during which period?
92.x: Rudrama Devi succeeded Ganapatideva and ruled from 1262 to 1289.
92.tq: Compare the closely spaced reign periods and select the one belonging to Rudrama Devi.

92.s: Who guided Rudrama Devi’s training?
92.x: Kupama Devi, Rudrama Devi’s mother, guided her training when she was being raised as a son.
92.tq: Distinguish the mother who guided training from the sisters and daughter mentioned in the succession account.

92.s: Ganapatideva’s sisters Mailamba and Kundamamba were married to whom?
o: The princes of the Yadava house
92.x: Mailamba and Kundamamba married the sons of Natavadi Buddharaja, namely Rudra and his brother.
92.tq: Use the family-relationship clue to distinguish the sisters’ marriages from Ganapatideva’s daughters’ marriages.

92.s: Which statement best describes the political significance of the Kakatiyas?
o: They were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unify all Telugu-speaking regions and the first to rule all Telugu-speakers.
They were the first dynasty after the Satavahanas to rule only the coastal Telugu region.
They were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to establish a purely Sanskrit-speaking administration.
They ruled the Andhra region only after the foundation of Vijayanagara.
92.x: The Kakatiyas are described as the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unite the Andhra region and the first to rule all Telugu-speaking regions.
92.tq: Separate the scope of territorial unification from language and chronological distractors.

92.s: From which ruler’s reign did Telugu replace Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions?
92.x: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from the reign of Ganapatideva. More than 1,000 Kakatiya inscriptions are known.
92.tq: Match the language change with the correct reign rather than with the beginning or end of the dynasty.

92.s: The Archaeological Survey of India’s June 2026 Nallamala survey copied Kakatiya inscriptions among how many records dating from the second to the sixteenth century?
92.x: The survey copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records dating from the second to the sixteenth century.
92.tq: Identify the exact current-affairs figure and reject nearby numerical distractors.

92.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Ramappa Temple at Palampet?
o: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2016 and is noted for a circular platform and granite bricks.
It was built at Nellore and is noted for its rectangular platform and wooden roof.
It was constructed by the Pandyas at Muttukur and is noted for its floating stones.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
92.x: The Ramappa Temple at Palampet became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
92.tq: Combine the location, recognition year and distinctive architectural features before selecting the complete description.

92.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First mention of the Kakatiyas at Magallu
B. Accession of Rudradeva as the first sovereign Kakatiya
C. Defeat of Ganapatideva at Muttukur
D. Rule of Rudrama Devi
92.x: The first mention at Magallu was in 956, Rudradeva became the first sovereign in 1163, Ganapatideva was defeated at Muttukur in 1263, and Rudrama Devi ruled from 1262 to 1289; in the stated sequence, the intended chronological order is A, B, C, D.
92.tq: Start with the earliest dated reference and place the reign and battle dates in ascending order.

92.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Magallu — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
Ganapatideva — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
92.x: The first mention of the Kakatiyas is associated with Magallu in 956. Rudradeva was the first sovereign in 1163, while Prataparudra II was the last ruler.
92.tq: Use the first–last distinction and attach each date to the correct historical milestone.

92.s: Who is regarded as the last ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty?
92.x: Prataparudra II is identified as the last ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty.
92.tq: Distinguish the last ruler from the major earlier sovereigns and the female successor.

93.s: Rudrama Devi was the daughter of which Kakatiya ruler?
93.x: Rudrama Devi was the daughter of Ganapatideva. She was groomed from childhood as a son for kingship and military responsibilities.
93.tq: Use direct succession-based recall and distinguish the ruler from the other members of the dynasty.

93.s: Rudrama Devi was trained from childhood as a son, a practice referred to by which term?
93.x: Rudrama Devi was groomed as a son under the putrika tradition and trained in war and administration.
93.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than its broad meaning.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the accession of Rudrama Devi:
1. She began ruling as Rudradeva Maharaja in 1258 under a system of co-regency.
2. The Tripurantakam inscription of 1266 still refers to her as a vassal of Ganapati.
3. She received full coronation only after the death of Ganapatideva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All three statements are correct. Rudrama began co-regency in 1258, the 1266 inscription retained the vassal description, and her full coronation followed Ganapatideva’s death in 1262.
93.tq: Split the chronology into co-regency, inscriptional evidence and full coronation.

93.s: Rudrama Devi’s full coronation took place after the death of:
93.x: Rudrama Devi was fully crowned after the death of her father, Ganapatideva, in 1262.
93.tq: Apply the succession sequence to identify the immediate predecessor.

93.s: Rudrama Devi was married to:
93.x: Rudrama Devi married Veerabhadra, who belonged to the Chalukya royal family.
93.tq: Use the ruler–spouse association while separating it from later political opponents and officials.

93.s: Rudrama Devi is regarded as the second great woman ruler of medieval India after:
93.x: Rudrama Devi is regarded as the second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana.
93.tq: Directly test the comparative historical designation attached to the ruler.

93.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the principal figures associated with the suppression of the revolt of Rudrama Devi’s half-brothers Harihara and Murari?
o: Prasadaditya Kayastha, Gona Gannareddy and Jannigadeva
Ganga Narasimhadeva, Virabhanudeva and Poti Nayaka
93.x: The revolt of Harihara and Murari was suppressed with the assistance of Prasadaditya Kayastha, Gona Gannareddy, Jannigadeva and other commanders. The other groups relate to different episodes.
93.tq: Start from the sure association between a rebellion and the commanders who suppressed it.

93.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the suppression of the internal revolt against Rudrama Devi?
93.x: Malik Burhanuddin was appointed to administer Andhra after the Tughlaq conquest. Tripurari, Malyala Gundiya and Induluri Annayya were among the figures associated with suppressing the internal revolt.
93.tq: Find the person belonging to a different episode rather than the rebellion against Rudrama Devi.

93.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Ganga Narasimhadeva occupied Vengi
B. Rudrama Devi’s full coronation
C. Recovery of Vengi by the Kakatiyas
D. Death of Rudrama Devi
93.x: Ganga Narasimhadeva occupied Vengi in 1262; Rudrama’s full coronation followed in 1262 after Ganapatideva’s death; Vengi was recovered in 1278; Rudrama died in 1289.
93.tq: Fix the opening and closing dates first, then place the two middle events.

93.s:
With reference to Kalinga and Vengi during Rudrama Devi’s reign, consider the following statements:
1. Ganga Narasimhadeva occupied Vengi in 1262.
2. Vengi was recovered in 1278.
3. Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka defeated Virabhanudeva in the recovery of Vengi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All three statements are correct. Vengi was occupied in 1262 and recovered in 1278 after Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka defeated Virabhanudeva.
93.tq: Combine date, location and commanders in a single regional campaign.

93.s: The Yadava ruler who invaded Rudrama Devi’s kingdom was:
93.x: Yadava Mahadeva attacked Rudrama Devi, but she repulsed the invasion.
93.tq: Distinguish the named invader from other rulers of the Yadava line.

93.s: Which of the following statements about the political opposition faced by Rudrama Devi is correct?
o: Nellore remained permanently under Kakatiya control after Muttukur.
The Pandyas supported Rudrama Devi against Kayastha Ambadeva.
She faced only internal opposition and no external attacks.
Her opponents included the Yadavas and Pandyas, while after Muttukur in 1263 Nellore came under the Pandyas.
93.x: Rudrama Devi faced internal rebellions and attacks by the Yadavas and Pandyas. After Muttukur in 1263, Nellore was under Pandya control.
93.tq: Check the direction of political support and the change in territorial control.

93.s: Rudrama Devi was killed in 1289 while fighting:
93.x: Rudrama Devi died in 1289 while fighting the rebel Kayastha Ambadeva, who had Pandya support.
93.tq: Use the ruler–rebel relationship to avoid confusing internal and external enemies.

93.s: Rudrama Devi’s death in 1289 was recorded in an inscription set up by her servant Puvvula Mummadi. Which inscription was it?
93.x: The Chandupatla inscription of Nalgonda district, set up by Puvvula Mummadi, records Rudrama Devi’s death in 1289 while fighting Ambadeva.
93.tq: Match the event, inscription and associated person rather than relying on the date alone.

93.s: Who was the general associated with Rudrama Devi in her final fight against Ambadeva?
93.x: Mallikarjuna Nayaka was the general associated with Rudrama Devi in her final fight against Ambadeva.
93.tq: Separate the commander in the final battle from the earlier revolt commanders.

93.s: Which of the following statements about Rudrama Devi’s family is correct?
o: Ruyyamma married the Yadava prince Ellanadeva.
Mummadamma was the mother of Prataparudra II.
All the daughters were married to Chalukya princes.
93.x: Rudrama Devi’s daughters were Mummadamma, Rudramma and Ruyyamma. Mummadamma was the mother of Prataparudra II; Rudramma married Ellanadeva and Ruyyamma married Induluri Annayya.
93.tq: Use the family relationships individually and reject the reversed marriages.

93.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rudrama Devi — daughter of Prataparudra II
93.x: Mummadamma was the mother of Prataparudra II. Rudramma married Ellanadeva, Ruyyamma married Induluri Annayya, and Rudrama Devi was the daughter of Ganapatideva.
93.tq: Use reversed family relationships as the principal trap in a matching question.

93.s: Which of the following statements regarding Rudrama Devi’s administrative and military measures is correct?
o: Her royal guru was Malik Maqbul.
She repaired and strengthened the Orugallu fort by adding abutments and bastions.
She abandoned the fort of Orugallu and shifted the capital permanently.
She introduced the Nayankara system only after the Tughlaq conquest.
93.x: Rudrama Devi repaired and strengthened the Orugallu fort, including its abutments and bastions. The Nayankara system is said to have been introduced in her father’s time, and her royal guru was Visveshwara Shivacharya.
93.tq: Identify the true administrative measure while rejecting reversed timing and wrong-person traps.

93.s: Rudrama Devi’s royal guru was:
93.x: Visveshwara Shivacharya was Rudrama Devi’s royal guru and was associated with the Mandaram agrahara.
93.tq: Test the ruler–guru association directly.

93.s: Rudrama Devi was the ______ sovereign of the Kakatiya dynasty, following Rudradeva, Mahadeva and Ganapatideva.
93.x: In the stated succession list, Rudrama Devi was the fourth sovereign after Rudradeva, Mahadeva and Ganapatideva.
93.tq: Count the named predecessors before selecting the ordinal position.

93.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Event)
a. First Tughlaq invasion of Orugallu
b. Second Tughlaq invasion of Orugallu
c. Renaming of Orugallu

d. Administration after the conquest

List-II (Description)
i. Sultanpur
 ii. Malik Burhanuddin placed in charge of Andhra
 iii. 1321–22 under Ulugh Khan
 iv. 1323 under Juna Khan with reinforcements

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
93.x: The first invasion occurred in 1321–22 under Ulugh Khan; the second occurred in 1323 under Juna Khan; Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur; and Malik Burhanuddin was placed in charge of Andhra.
93.tq: Start with the distinctive invasion dates, then complete the place-name and administration pairs.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tughlaq invasions of Orugallu:
1. The fourth invasion took place in 1321–22.
2. Ulugh Khan was also known as Juna Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
3. A false rumour of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq’s death caused the Kakatiyas to chase the army back to Devagiri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All three statements describe the unsuccessful 1321–22 invasion. Ulugh Khan, also called Juna Khan, withdrew after a false rumour about the Sultan’s death spread among the army.
93.tq: Combine aliases, date and cause of failure in the first invasion.

93.s: The successful Tughlaq siege of Orugallu in 1323 lasted for approximately:
93.x: The 1323 invasion involved a five-month siege, after which Prataparudra surrendered.
93.tq: Use the exact duration as the decisive numerical clue.

93.s: Which event directly weakened the Kakatiya resistance during the 1323 siege of Orugallu?
o: The revolt of Harihara and Murari
The occupation of Vengi by Ganga Narasimhadeva
93.x: Bobbareddi’s desertion or withdrawal of forces during the battle weakened the Kakatiya defence and contributed to the surrender of Prataparudra.
93.tq: Identify the immediate military cause from among events belonging to different periods.

93.s: After the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom, Orugallu was renamed:
93.x: The Tughlaqs renamed Orugallu as Sultanpur, also rendered as Sultanpurti.
93.tq: Test the exact official renaming and distinguish it from other medieval city names.

93.s: Who was placed in charge of Andhra after the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom?
o: Malik Burhanuddin, the vizier of Devagiri
Malik Maqbul, the governor of Delhi
Ulugh Khan, the governor of Vengi
93.x: Andhra was placed under Malik Burhanuddin, who was the vizier of Devagiri. Malik Maqbul was stationed at Warangal.
93.tq: Distinguish the provincial administrator from the officer stationed at the former capital.

93.s: Which of the following statements about Malik Maqbul is correct?
o: He was a captured Brahmin named Jagannatha Pandit who was converted and stationed at Warangal.
He was the royal guru of Rudrama Devi at Mandaram agrahara.
He was the Yadava ruler who attacked Rudrama Devi.
He was the Kakatiya general who fought Ambadeva.
93.x: Malik Maqbul is described as a captured Brahmin, Jagannatha Pandit, who was converted and stationed at Warangal after the conquest.
93.tq: Separate the post-conquest official from the Kakatiya ruler, general and guru.

93.s:
With reference to the fate of Prataparudra, consider the following statements:
1. He surrendered after the five-month siege of Orugallu in 1323.
2. He was taken towards Delhi after being captured.
3. The Vilasa copper plate records that he drowned himself in the Narmada.
4. Another account places the drowning in the Kaveri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All four statements are supported by the accounts described. Prataparudra surrendered in 1323 and, while being taken towards Delhi, drowned himself; the Vilasa record names the Narmada, while another account names the Kaveri.
93.tq: Handle a source variation carefully without confusing the common event with the differing river names.

93.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as a cause of the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom?
o: A prolonged maritime blockade by European powers
93.x: The stated causes were disunity among southern kingdoms, weak cavalry, betrayal by chiefs and exhaustion caused by repeated raids. A maritime blockade by European powers was not a cause.
93.tq: Find the anachronistic option while retaining the causes that directly weakened the kingdom.

93.s: Which of the following pairs of post-Kakatiya literary sources and their subject is correctly matched?
o: Gangadevi’s Madhura Vijayam — hardships after the fall of the Kakatiyas
Vilasa grant — the coronation of Rudrama Devi in 1258
Tripurantakam inscription — the five-month Tughlaq siege of 1323
Chandupatla inscription — the invasion of Yadava Mahadeva
93.x: Gangadevi’s Madhura Vijayam and the Vilasa grant describe the hardships following the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom. The other inscriptions are associated with different events.
93.tq: Match each source with its historical context and reject the swapped-event options.

93.s: Who commanded the first Khalji expedition against Warangal in 1303?
93.x: Malik Fakhruddin Juna commanded Alauddin Khalji’s first expedition against Orugallu in 1303.
93.tq: Use the commander–year association to distinguish the successive invasions.

93.s: The first attack on Orugallu in 1303 was repulsed at Upparapalli by:
93.x: The 1303 expedition was defeated at Upparapalli by Pothuganti Aili and Recherla Venna.
93.tq: Match the military outcome with the correct local commanders.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the second Khalji invasion of Warangal:
1. It was led by Malik Kafur.
2. Prataparudra submitted after the fort was besieged.
3. Prataparudra paid a large tribute and accepted Delhi overlordship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: The second invasion of 1309–10 was led by Malik Kafur; Prataparudra submitted, paid a large tribute and accepted Delhi’s overlordship.
93.tq: Check the complete sequence of commander, siege and political outcome.

93.s: Khusrau Khan’s expedition against Warangal, associated with the Mubarak Khalji reign, resulted in:
o: The annexation of Warangal by the Yadavas
The immediate end of the Kakatiya dynasty
The permanent restoration of Kakatiya independence without tribute
A defeat of the invading army followed by a fresh treaty and tribute
93.x: The 1318 expedition led by Khusrau Khan was defeated, after which a fresh treaty was concluded and tribute was paid.
93.tq: Identify the specific outcome rather than confusing it with the final conquest.

93.s:
Arrange the following invasions of Warangal in chronological order:
A. Expedition of Khusrau Khan
B. Expedition of Juna Khan under Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq which failed after false news of the Sultan’s death
C. Expedition of Malik Kafur
D. Final expedition of Juna Khan, after which Warangal fell
93.x: The order is Malik Kafur’s expedition in 1309–10, Khusrau Khan’s in 1318, Juna Khan’s failed expedition in 1321, and the final conquest in 1323.
93.tq: Fix the first and final invasions, then place the two intervening expeditions.

93.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1309–10 — Malik Kafur — Large tribute paid by Prataparudra
1321 — Juna Khan — Expedition failed after false news of the Sultan’s death
1323 — Khusrau Khan — Warangal fell and the Kakatiya dynasty ended
1303 — Malik Fakhruddin Juna — Repulsed at Upparapalli
93.x: The 1323 final expedition was led by Juna Khan, also known as Ulugh Khan, under Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq; it was not led by Khusrau Khan.
93.tq: Find the swapped commander in an otherwise familiar invasion–outcome pair.

93.s: In 1311, the forces of Prataparudra joined Malik Kafur’s march on Madurai under the command of:
93.x: Prataparudra’s forces joined Malik Kafur’s march on Madurai in 1311 under Muppidi Nayaka.
93.tq: Separate the commander of the Madurai contingent from commanders in the Tripurantakam campaign.

93.s: What was the immediate consequence of Alauddin Khalji’s death in 1316 for Prataparudra’s relations with Delhi?
o: He transferred his capital to Devagiri
He accepted direct annexation of Warangal
93.x: After Alauddin Khalji died in 1316, Prataparudra stopped paying tribute to Delhi.
93.tq: Connect the change in imperial authority with the dependent ruler’s response.

93.s: Alauddin Khalji’s raid of 1294/1295 in the Deccan was directed against the Yadavas of:
93.x: Alauddin Khalji’s first Deccan raid targeted the Yadavas of Devagiri, not Andhra or Warangal.
93.tq: Discriminate between the Yadava target and the later Kakatiya target.

93.s: Marco Polo was a traveller belonging to which country or region?
93.x: Marco Polo was a Venetian traveller who visited the eastern coast during Rudramadevi’s reign.
93.tq: Use the traveller’s identity as a direct name–origin association.

93.s: Marco Polo’s journey is generally placed between:
93.x: Marco Polo travelled during 1271–1295 and reached the Coromandel Coast in 1292.
93.tq: Distinguish the broad travel period from the specific year of his coastal visit.

93.s: Marco Polo reached the Coromandel Coast in:
93.x: Marco Polo reached the Coromandel Coast in 1292, toward the end of Rudramadevi’s reign.
93.tq: Choose the specific arrival year rather than the limits of the wider travel period.

93.s: Marco Polo’s Motupalli is identified with:
93.x: Motupalli, also written as Mutfili, was the port visited by Marco Polo on the Coromandel Coast.
93.tq: Resolve the alternate-name pair for the port.

93.s: Which of the following observations is NOT attributed to Marco Polo’s account of the Kakatiya realm?
o: Oppressive taxes imposed on all merchants
93.x: Marco Polo reported that merchants were not subjected to oppressive taxes; he also noted sea trade, textiles, diamonds and rice.
93.tq: Locate the reversed economic observation in a list of genuine descriptions.

93.s:
Consider the following statements about Marco Polo’s account:
1. He referred to the prosperity and efficient administration of the kingdom.
2. He described a woman ruler possessing martial ability.
3. His account is regarded as the first foreign reference to a female ruler in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: Marco Polo described prosperity, efficient administration and a woman ruler of martial ability; his account is regarded as the first foreign reference to a female ruler in India.
93.tq: Verify whether all related observations belong to the same travel account.

93.s: The work associated with Marco Polo is:
o: Il Milione, also known as The Travels
93.x: Marco Polo’s travel account is known as Il Milione or The Travels.
93.tq: Distinguish the traveller’s work from contemporary historical chronicles.

93.s: The description of Ramappa as “the brightest star in the galaxy of temples” is attributed in some accounts to:
93.x: The phrase is attributed in some accounts to Marco Polo in connection with the Ramappa temple.
93.tq: Match the distinctive quotation with its attributed observer.

93.s: Prataparudra was the grandson of:
93.x: Prataparudra was the grandson of Rudramadevi and the son of Mummadamma and Mahadeva.
93.tq: Use the family relationship to distinguish the Kakatiya succession line.

93.s: Which title was associated with Prataparudra before or in connection with his accession?
93.x: Prataparudra was associated with the title ‘Kumara Rudradeva’.
93.tq: Separate the ruler’s title from titles and names used by other figures in the period.

93.s: Prataparudra ruled approximately during which period?
93.x: Prataparudra’s reign is placed between 1289 and 1323.
93.tq: Identify the correct reign span among closely placed medieval dates.

93.s: Under the Nayankara system, the kingdom was organised into principalities held by:
93.x: The Nayankara system assigned principalities and forts to military officers known as Nayakas, who maintained troops and paid fixed tribute.
93.tq: Infer the institutional role from the system’s military and administrative structure.

93.s: Which one of the following was NOT an economic measure associated with Prataparudra?
93.x: Prataparudra’s economic measures included land reclamation, waterworks and founding villages; oppressive merchant taxation was contrary to the account of the period.
93.tq: Identify the measure inconsistent with the recorded developmental activities.

93.s: Prataparudra defeated Ambadeva at:
93.x: Prataparudra defeated Ambadeva at Tripurantakam in 1291.
93.tq: Match the campaign opponent with the battlefield location.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Prataparudra’s campaigns:
1. Ambadeva’s principality was annexed after the Tripurantakam campaign.
2. Ranganatha of Nellore, a Pandya ally, was replaced by Manuma Gandapalu.
3. Gonavithala pushed Kakatiya control towards Devagiri on the Yadava frontier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All three statements are correct. The campaigns dealt with Ambadeva, Ranganatha of Nellore and the Yadava southern frontier respectively.
93.tq: Check each campaign against its opponent, result and commander.

93.s: Who served as Prataparudra’s prime minister?
93.x: Muppidi Nayudu served as the prime minister of Prataparudra.
93.tq: Distinguish a political office-holder from court poets and scholars.

93.s:
Which of the following works were associated with Agastya?
1. Nalakirtikaumudi
2. Balabharata
3. Krishnacharita
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
93.x: Agastya is associated with all three works: Nalakirtikaumudi, Balabharata and Krishnacharita.
93.tq: Test the complete scholar–works list without confusing it with Vidyanatha’s work.

The Kafur siege of Warangal in 1310
The foundation of the Vijayanagara Empire
The marriage of Jaitugi and Ganapati

93.s: Which source is associated with the Kakatiya traditions concerning the marriage of Jaitugi and Ganapati?

o: Socio-economic and religious life of the period
Kafur’s military route to Madurai alone
93.x: Siddheswara Charitra by Kase Siddhappa provides information on socio-economic and religious life.

93.s: Which author is associated with Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi?

93.s: Futuh-us-Salatin is associated with the account of:
o: The diamond mines described by Marco Polo
The social life of Kakatiya villages
93.x: Isami’s Futuh-us-Salatin is a source for the Tughlaq victory over the Kakatiyas.
93.tq: Match the source’s historical use with the correct military event.

93.s:
Which works describe the hardship following the conquest of the Kakatiya kingdom?
1. Gangadevi’s Madhura Vijayam
2. The Vilasa grant of Prolaya Nayaka
3. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

93.tq: Separate post-conquest evidence from a general Delhi campaign chronicle.

93.s: Rudrama Devi ruled under which of the following male regnal names?
93.x: Rudradeva Maharaja was the male regnal name under which Rudrama Devi ruled as a monarch in her own right.
93.tq: Use the exact title–ruler association and distinguish a regnal name from an honorific title.

93.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Title or name)
a. Ravaddar Dev
b. Andhra Deshadhiswara
c. Rudradeva Maharaja

a List-II (Associated ruler or identity)
i. Ganapatideva
ii. Prataparudra II
iii. Rudrama Devi

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
93.x: Amir Khusrau used Ravaddar Dev for Prataparudra II; Ganapatideva was known as Andhra Deshadhiswara; and Rudradeva Maharaja was Rudrama Devi’s male regnal name.

93.s:
The Kakatiya rulers commonly styled themselves as which of the following?

1. Maharaja
2. Parameshwara
3. Tirthakrit

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
93.x: Kakatiya kings used all three styles—Maharaja, Parameshwara and Tirthakrit.
93.tq: Check each formal title independently before selecting the inclusive combination.

93.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the succession from Rudrama Devi to Prataparudra II:

1. Prataparudra II was Rudrama Devi’s grandson through her daughter Mummadamma.
2. Rudrama Devi trained Prataparudra II for succession.
3. Prataparudra II was crowned in 1289.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
93.x: All three statements are correct: Prataparudra was Rudrama’s grandson through Mummadamma, was trained by her, and was crowned in 1289.
93.tq: Verify the relationship, preparation for succession and date separately; the complete combination is supported.

93.s:
From the beginning of his reign, Prataparudra II faced revolts from which of the following groups or leaders?

1. Kayasthas
2. Velamas
3. Reddy factions
4. Tripurari II, son of Ambadeva

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
93.x: Prataparudra II faced opposition from Kayastha, Velama and Reddy factions, as well as Tripurari II, the son of Ambadeva.
93.tq: Treat the named factions and individual rebel as separate statement units before choosing the complete list.

93.s:
The fall of Warangal in 1323 had which of the following consequences?

1. It ended Kakatiya rule.
2. It opened the way for a liberation movement led by the Musunuris.
3. It directly produced the Musunuri and Reddi states.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
93.x: The fall of Warangal in 1323 ended Kakatiya rule and was followed by the Musunuri-led liberation movement, which produced the Musunuri and Reddi states.
93.tq: Link the event with its immediate political consequence and the states that emerged afterward.

93.s: Which of the following was NOT cited as a reason for the fall of the Kakatiyas?
o: A prolonged famine caused by failure of the monsoon
93.x: The cited reasons were southern disunity, weak cavalry and internal betrayal associated with Bobbareddi. A prolonged monsoon failure was not identified as a cause.
93.tq: Find the one option outside the stated group of political and military causes.

93.s: Rudrama Devi is regarded as a leading example of which historical phenomenon?
o: The first ruler to establish the Delhi Sultanate
A woman monarch in medieval South India
A queen who founded the Reddi state
A military governor appointed by the Vijayanagara rulers
93.x: Rudrama Devi is a leading example of a woman monarch in medieval South India.
93.tq: Match the ruler with the broad historical significance specifically associated with her reign.

93.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the institutional succession mentioned in relation to the Nayankara system?
o: Nayankara system → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas → later Poligars
Later Poligars → Nayankara system → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas
Vijayanagara Amaranayakas → later Poligars → Nayankara system
Nayankara system → later Poligars → Vijayanagara Amaranayakas
93.x: The comparative sequence is the Nayankara system, followed by the Vijayanagara Amaranayakas and later the Poligars.
93.tq: Identify the initial institutional form and follow the stated progression to its later forms.

94.s: Which one of the following guilds was primarily associated with domestic trade during the Kakatiya period?
94.x: Nakaram was the guild associated with domestic trade. Nanadesi Pekkandru specialised in foreign trade, while Ubhaya Nanadesi operated in both markets.
94.tq: Use the scope of each guild to distinguish closely related trade organisations.

94.s: The Nanadesi Pekkandru guild was mainly connected with
94.x: Nanadesi Pekkandru was a foreign-trade guild. Nakaram was associated with domestic trade, whereas Ubhaya Nanadesi dealt in both domestic and foreign markets.
94.tq: Test the exact meaning of a similar-sounding guild name.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Nakaram — Domestic trade
2. Nanadesi Pekkandru — Foreign trade
3. Ubhaya Nanadesi Pekkandru — Domestic and foreign trade
4. Ayyavali Ainuraru — Guild of 500

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Nakaram handled domestic trade, Nanadesi foreign trade, Ubhaya Nanadesi both types of trade, and Ayyavali Ainuraru was the guild of 500.
94.tq: Check every pair against the guild’s specialised scope or numerical identity.

94.s: Virabanajam was licensed to operate in which of the following regions?
94.x: The Virabanajam guild was licensed for Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda, as recorded in the Tripurantakam inscription of 1282.
94.tq: Recall the specific licensed regions rather than confusing them with ports or foreign trading partners.

94.s: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 is associated with the licensing of
o: Virabanajam in Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda
94.x: The Tripurantakam inscription of 1282 records the areas in which Virabanajam was licensed to operate: Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda.
94.tq: Link the inscription, date and guild through the distinctive licensing detail.

94.s: Ayyavali Ainuraru is best described as
o: An official body collecting port duties
A guild restricted to domestic trade
94.x: Ayyavali Ainuraru was the great trans-regional merchant guild known as the guild of 500.
94.tq: Use the numerical identity in the guild’s name to identify the organisation.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT a function or characteristic of the Kakatiya merchant guilds?
o: Exercising an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade
Maintaining their own seal or emblem
94.x: Guilds maintained seals or emblems, settled disputes and kept private military forces, but they did not possess an exclusive royal monopoly over all trade.
94.tq: Find the overbroad and exclusive statement that goes beyond the guild functions.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding merchant guilds:

1. A merchant was called a Behari.
2. Trade was referred to as Vyavaharam.
3. The head of a guild was called Setti or Sreshthi.
4. Guild members were drawn exclusively from Vaishyas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Guild members came from several communities, including Settis, Reddis, Nayakulu, Boyas, Dasaris and Vaishyas, so statement 4 is false.
94.tq: Reject the exclusive-membership statement and retain the precise occupational terms.

94.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the economic and administrative functions of merchant guilds?
o: Temple priests, military commanders and village headmen
Bankers, local administrators and negotiators for tax concessions
Coin minters, irrigation engineers and royal ambassadors
Judges, royal tax collectors and hereditary governors only
94.x: Merchant guilds acted as bankers and local administrators and negotiated with the king for tax concessions. The Motupalli charter illustrates this interaction.
94.tq: Identify the option that combines the guild’s economic, administrative and negotiating roles.

94.s: Which of the following was included among the exports of the Kakatiya period?
o: Iron tools, salt and timber only
Perfumes, horses, porcelain and silk alone
Grain, copper and medicinal herbs alone
94.x: The listed exports were textiles, spices, diamonds and gold. Perfumes and spices were mentioned among the imports.
94.tq: Distinguish the export list from the shorter list of imports.

94.s: Which of the following was mentioned as an import in Kakatiya overseas trade?
94.x: Perfumes were among the imports. Textiles, diamonds and gold were listed among the exports.
94.tq: Use the export-import reversal trap with commodities appearing in both trade contexts.

94.s:
The Kakatiya trade network had commercial links with which of the following regions or countries?

1. China
2. Persia
3. Arabia
4. Ceylon
5. East Indies

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: The recorded trading partners included China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies.
94.tq: Verify the complete list instead of stopping after identifying the first few familiar partners.

94.s: Ports collecting import and export duties were known as
94.x: Ports that collected import and export duties were called Kara Pattanam.
94.tq: Distinguish the technical term for duty-collecting ports from names of actual ports and guilds.

94.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam was issued by Ganapatideva in
94.x: Ganapatideva issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244 CE at Motupalli.
94.tq: Place the inscription date among the nearby dates associated with other inscriptions and periods.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam:

1. It guaranteed safety to foreign merchants.
2. It remitted arbitrary taxes.
3. It promised compensation for losses caused by shipwreck or theft.
4. It authorised harassment of merchants by local officials.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes and promised compensation for losses from shipwreck or theft. It stopped, rather than authorised, harassment by officials.
94.tq: Identify the reversed negative statement concerning official harassment.

94.s: Who was appointed at Motupalli under the Abhaya Sasanam of Ganapatideva?
94.x: Siddayya Devudu was the official posted at Motupalli under Ganapatideva’s charter.
94.tq: Match the official with the charter and port, avoiding confusion with later rulers and builders.

94.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two Motupalli protection charters?

1. Ganapatideva’s Abhaya Sasanam was issued in 1244 CE.
2. A later bilingual Telugu-Tamil charter was issued by Anavota Reddi.
3. The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 was associated with Deva Raya I.
4. The 1416 Dharma Sasanam belonged to the reign of Ganapatideva.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I, not Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Separate similar charters by issuer, date and dynasty.

94.s: In the expression ‘Abhaya Sasanam’, the word ‘Abhaya’ conveys the idea of
94.x: ‘Abhaya’ means assurance of safety. The charter used this principle to protect foreign and seafaring traders.
94.tq: Use the literal meaning of the key term to identify the charter’s purpose.

94.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

2. Ramappa tank — Recherla Rudra
3. Pakhala tank — Mummadi Nayaka
4. Laknavaram — Ganapatideva

94.tq: Start with the sure builder-tank pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped ruler or tank.

94.s: Who constructed the Ghanapuram tank?
94.x: Ghanapuram tank was constructed by Ganapatideva.

o: Surambika, wife of Peda Komati Vema
Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka

94.s: Kunda Samudram, also called Chouda Samudram, was associated with
94.x: Kunda Samudram or Chouda Samudram was associated with Kundamamba and Malyala Chauda respectively.

94.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
94.x: Pakhala tank was built by Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka, not by Mailamba. Mailamba was associated with Bayyaram tank.
94.tq: Find the swapped builder by comparing patrons of neighbouring tanks.

94.s:
Which one of the following statements about tank irrigation is correct?

2. Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks.

4. Dashabandhamu referred to tax-free land assigned for tank maintenance.

94.x: All four statements are correct. Samudrams were large tanks, Golusukattu cheruvulu formed linked chains, surplus flowed to lower tanks, and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for upkeep.
94.tq: Confirm the complete irrigation-system description, including the maintenance arrangement.

94.s: Tank-building was counted among the Sapta Santanalu, which refers to
94.x: Sapta Santanalu means seven meritorious works. The list included a son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the Sapta Santanalu?
94.x: The Sapta Santanalu included son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure. A merchant guild was not one of the seven meritorious works.
94.tq: Eliminate the item belonging to trade rather than the list of meritorious works.

94.s: The Porumamilla tank inscription is associated with which combination?
o: 1369, Bhaskara, son of Bukka I, Vijayanagara period
1416, Deva Raya I, Motupalli, Reddi period
94.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription dates to 1369 and was issued by Bhaskara, son of Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I. It belongs to the Vijayanagara period and lists twelve requisites of a good tank.
94.tq: Combine date, person, dynasty and inscription subject to separate similar records.

94.s: The Porumamilla inscription is particularly important in the study of irrigation because it
o: records the twelve requisites of a good tank
defines the five classes of merchant guilds
records the tax rates on imported perfumes
lists the foreign merchants protected at Motupalli
94.x: The Porumamilla inscription of 1369 lists twelve requisites of a good tank. It is from the Vijayanagara period, though it is often studied alongside Kakatiya irrigation works.
94.tq: Identify the inscription from its distinctive technical subject rather than its dynasty alone.

94.s: Which one of the following places was noted for the production of iron during the Kakatiya period?
94.x: Guthikonda and Palnadu were known for iron production. Nirmal was associated with knives, while Warangal was known for carpets and textiles.
94.tq: Use the industry–centre association and eliminate nearby but different craft centres.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Ratna kambalu — Warangal
2. Knives — Nirmal
3. Diamonds — Golconda region
4. Iron — Warangal

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: Ratna kambalu was associated with Warangal, knives with Nirmal and diamonds with the Golconda region. Iron was associated with Guthikonda and Palnadu, not Warangal.
94.tq: Start from the sure industry–centre pairs and identify the reversed association.

94.s: Marco Polo is said to have remarked that the fineness of which Kakatiya textile was such that a seven-yard saree could fit into a matchbox?
94.x: Marco Polo is said to have described the extremely fine cloth of the region in this manner; the material is identified as fine muslin.
94.tq: Test the distinctive traveller–observation association directly.

94.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding painting in Orugallu during the Kakatiya period?
o: Machaladevi was a male court painter of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Painting was confined to the Golconda region and had no association with Orugallu.
Orugallu had about 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi was a woman painter.
Orugallu had about 150 painters' houses, led by Machaladevi.
94.x: Orugallu is described as having 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi is identified as a woman painter.
