Arrange the following stages in the evolution of Telugu script in chronological order:
A. Separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs
B. Bhattiprolu variant of Brahmi
C. Common Old Kannada–Telugu script
D. Beginning of differentiation between Telugu and Kannada
101.x: The sequence is Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant, common Old Kannada–Telugu script, differentiation during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age, and separate Telugu script in the 11th–14th centuries.
101.tq: Fix the earliest script stage first and then place the transition stages.

101.s: Which statement correctly reflects the chronology of the emergence of the distinct Telugu script?
o: It emerged only after the 14th century.
It developed directly from the Tamil script during the 4th century BCE.
It was fully distinct during the Satavahana period.
It had emerged by the 11th century, with full separation placed broadly in the 11th–14th centuries.
101.x: One account places the emergence of distinct Telugu script by the 11th century, while another describes full separation over the 11th–14th centuries.
101.tq: Reconcile close chronological formulations instead of treating them as contradictory.

101.s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian language family?
101.x: Telugu belongs to the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Test the exact linguistic sub-classification rather than the broader family name.

101.s: Which of the following are identified as sister languages of Telugu within the South-Central Dravidian group?
101.x: Gondi and Kui are identified among the sister languages of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Distinguish sister languages from other Dravidian languages outside the stated sub-branch.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Telugu:
1. It is the official language of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It is included among the 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule.
3. It belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh and one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages. It belongs to the Dravidian, not Indo-Aryan, family.
101.tq: Reject the broad-family trap while retaining the constitutional and state-language facts.

101.s: The theory that Telugu grew out of the Desi bhasha, identified with Paisachi of Prakrit, is associated with the view that:
o: Telugu was created by the Kakatiya court
Desi words show close resemblance to Telugu
101.x: The stated theory connects Telugu with the Desi bhasha or Paisachi of Prakrit, and D.C. Sircar observed that Desi words were very close to Telugu.
101.tq: Connect the etymological theory with the linguistic evidence cited for it.

101.s: The Trilinga theory derives the name Andhra from the three Shaiva centres of:
101.x: The Trilinga theory refers to Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama as the three Shaiva centres of Trilinga desa.
101.tq: Use a three-place association to distinguish the Trilinga theory from other regional lists.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Telugu — derived by all scholars exclusively from Tamil
Trilinga — associated with three Shaiva centres
Andhrika — an alternative name of the language
Tenugu — derived by some from tene, meaning honey
101.x: The material presents Telugu, Andhra, Andhrika and Tenugu as names or theories of origin; it does not support an exclusive Tamil derivation accepted by all scholars.
101.tq: Identify the overgeneralised attribution using the extreme word ‘all’.

101.s: Telugu was declared a Classical Language by the Government of India in:
101.x: Telugu was granted Classical Language status by the Union Government in 2008, together with Kannada.
101.tq: Use the year options to distinguish Telugu’s status from Tamil’s earlier recognition.

101.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recognition of Classical Languages is correct?
o: The Government of Uttar Pradesh granted Classical Language status to Telugu.
Tamil was recognised in 2008, after Telugu.
Telugu and Kannada were recognised in 2008, while Tamil was the first in 2004.
Malayalam and Odia were recognised in 2008 along with Telugu.
101.x: Tamil was the first, receiving recognition in 2004. Telugu and Kannada received it in 2008; the granting authority was the Union Government, not Uttar Pradesh.
101.tq: Trap the swapped year and wrong authority in a recognition-related statement.

101.s: Which of the following correctly states the years in which Malayalam and Odia received Classical Language status?
101.x: Malayalam received Classical Language status in 2013 and Odia in 2014.
101.tq: Separate nearby recognition years instead of grouping all languages under 2008.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Author)
a. Vidyanatha
b. Jayapa Senani
c. Sakalya Mallabhattu
List-II (Association)
i. Named among Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court
ii. Prataparudra Yashobhushanam
iii. Nritta Ratnavali, Geeta Ratnavali and Vadya Ratnavali
101.x: Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam; Jayapa Senani wrote the three Ratnavali works; Sakalya Mallabhattu is named among the Sanskrit authors.
101.tq: Start with the distinctive group of three works associated with Jayapa Senani.

101.s: Jayapa Senani held the office of Gajasahini under Ganapatideva. The office refers to his role as:
101.x: Gajasahini means commander of the elephant corps. Jayapa Senani’s military office should not be confused with the subjects of his Ratnavali works.
101.tq: Use the occupational meaning of the title to avoid the profession trap.

101.s: Which attribution is specifically identified as requiring caution because of differing evidence?
101.x: Ravipati Tripurantakudu is credited with the Sanskrit Niroshthya Ramayanam, but an APP fragment attributes Niroshtya Ramayana and Udara Raghavam to Takavelli Mallikarju Bhattu.
101.tq: Recognise the source-attribution dispute rather than treating similar author claims as identical.

101.s: Tikkana’s title ‘Ubhayakavimitrudu’ is associated with his position as a poet in the court of:
101.x: Tikkana was associated with the court of Manumasiddhi II of Nellore and bore the title Ubhayakavimitrudu.
101.tq: Distinguish Tikkana’s patron from the Kakatiya rulers connected with his period.

101.s: Which of the following is an independent work of Tikkana rather than a portion of his Mahabharata translation?
101.x: Krishna Satakam is listed as an independent work of Tikkana. The other works are associated with different authors or literary contexts.
101.tq: Separate a poet’s independent work from works of nearby authors and traditions.

101.s: Tikkana’s Harihara philosophy was intended principally to:
o: Separate religious literature from royal patronage
Replace Telugu with Sanskrit in court literature
101.x: Tikkana propounded Harihara philosophy, described as Harihara Dvaitam, to reconcile Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions.
101.tq: Infer the practical religious purpose from the philosophical label.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Siva Kavi)
a. Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya
b. Nannechoda
c. Palkuriki Somanatha
List-II (Work or contribution)
i. Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra
ii. Sivatattvasaram
iii. Kumarasambhavam
101.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is associated with Sivatattvasaram, Nannechoda with Kumarasambhavam, and Palkuriki Somanatha with Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra.
101.tq: Match the poets through their distinctive Shaiva works.

101.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the claims regarding the first Satakam?
o: Sivatattvasaram is identified in one source, while Vrushadhipa Satakam is identified in another.
Only Vrushadhipa Satakam is ever identified as the first Satakam.
Basava Puranam is identified by both sources as the first Satakam.
Only Sivatattvasaram is ever identified as the first Satakam.
101.x: The sources differ: one identifies Sivatattvasaram as the first Satakam, while another identifies Vrushadhipa Satakam.
101.tq: Handle a documented source variation without converting it into a false single-answer claim.

101.s: Nannechoda is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Vrushadhipa Satakam and the title Gajasahini
Basava Puranam and the title Prabandha Parameswara
101.x: Nannechoda wrote Kumarasambhavam and bore the title Kavirajasekhara. He is also associated with eight descriptions characteristic of the prabandha tradition.
101.tq: Combine the work and title that belong to the same poet.

101.s: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, also known as:
101.x: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, who was also known as Vallabhamatya.
101.tq: Test the alternate name of the attributed author.

101.s: The authorship debate concerning Kreedabhiramam arises partly because it is a Telugu rendering of which Sanskrit play?
101.x: Kreedabhiramam is regarded as a Telugu rendering of Ravipati Tripurantakudu’s Sanskrit play Premabhiramam, creating an attribution issue alongside its credit to Vallabharaya.
101.tq: Separate the Telugu rendering, its Sanskrit source and the credited author.

101.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Orugallu described in Kreedabhiramam?
o: The maritime trade of Motupalli alone
Markets, nightlife and the Kakati Devi temple
Only the military fortifications of the city
101.x: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu, or Warangal, through its markets, nightlife and Kakati Devi temple, and calls it ‘Andhra Nagari’.
101.tq: Select the cluster of urban features actually described in the work.

101.s: Kreedabhiramam belongs to the post-Kakatiya period associated with the:
101.x: Kreedabhiramam was written in the post-Kakatiya period associated with the Reddi era.
101.tq: Use the dynastic-period clue rather than the city’s earlier Kakatiya association.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is attributed to Palkuriki Somanatha. Sumati Satakam was composed by Baddena, while Sivatattvasaram belongs to Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya.
101.tq: Use author–Satakam pairings to distinguish closely related early Telugu works.

101.s: Baddena, the author of Sumati Satakam, is also associated with the title or work:
101.x: Baddena is associated with Sumati Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali.
101.tq: Link the author with the second work listed alongside the better-known Satakam.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Work)
a. Manucharitra
b. Parijatapaharanam
c. Panduranga Mahatmyam
d. Vasucharitra

List-II (Author)
i. Tenali Ramakrishna
ii. Nandi Timmana
iii. Ramaraja Bhushana
iv. Allasani Peddana
101.x: Manucharitra was written by Allasani Peddana, Parijatapaharanam by Nandi Timmana, Panduranga Mahatmyam by Tenali Ramakrishna and Vasucharitra by Ramaraja Bhushana.
101.tq: Start from the sure work–author pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining literary associations.

101.s: Vasucharitra, composed by Ramaraja Bhushana, was dedicated to which ruler?
101.x: Ramaraja Bhushana dedicated Vasucharitra to Tirumala Raya.
101.tq: Distinguish the author of a work from its patron or dedicatee.

101.s: Who among the following wrote both Kalapurnodayam and Raghavapandaviyam?
101.x: Pingali Surana was the author of both Kalapurnodayam and Raghavapandaviyam.
101.tq: Use the paired-work method to identify the author associated with both titles.

101.s: Varadambika Parinayam, a Sanskrit work, was written by
101.x: Tirumalamba wrote the Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam.
101.tq: Apply language discrimination when similar court-literature names appear together.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Madhura Vijayam was written in Sanskrit by Gangadevi, not by Pingali Surana. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
101.tq: Find the swapped author by checking the work–author association rather than the literary genre alone.

101.s: Madhura Vijayam, a Sanskrit work, was composed by
101.x: Gangadevi composed Madhura Vijayam in Sanskrit.
101.tq: Separate Sanskrit court works from Telugu works with similar historical settings.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Title)
a. Kavibrahma
b. Sambhudasa
c. Andhra Kavita Pitamaha
d. Kavisarvabhauma

List-II (Holder)
i. Allasani Peddana
ii. Srinatha
iii. Tikkana
iv. Errana
101.x: Tikkana was Kavibrahma, Errana was Sambhudasa, Allasani Peddana was Andhra Kavita Pitamaha and Srinatha was Kavisarvabhauma.
101.tq: Begin with the distinctive title–poet pair and use code elimination for the rest.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Potana held the title Sahaja Panditya. Kaviraja Sikhamani belonged to Nannechoda, Kavisarvabhauma to Srinatha and Andhra Kavita Pitamaha to Allasani Peddana.
101.tq: Use title–holder discrimination to avoid swapping famous Telugu poets.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the transition to the Prabandha form is correct?
1. The epic kavya gave way to the prabandha.
2. The prabandha generally treats a single episode rather than an entire epic.
3. The prabandha is marked by elaborate descriptions and a strong shringara element.
4. The prabandha dispenses with strict metrical rules.
101.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the prabandha follows strict metrical rules.
101.tq: Reject the statement that reverses a defining feature of the literary form.

101.s: Who introduced the set descriptions that became characteristic of the Prabandha tradition through Kumarasambhava?
101.x: Nannechoda's Kumarasambhava introduced the set descriptions associated with the Prabandha tradition.
101.tq: Link the literary innovation directly to the poet and work rather than to the later peak period.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the emergence of the Prabandha style:
1. Errana is credited in one classification with being the first Prabandha writer.
2. Srinatha is described as a pioneer of the style.
3. Sringara Naishadham and Haravilasam are associated with Srinatha's pioneering role.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Errana is credited as the first Prabandha writer in one classification, while Srinatha is identified as a pioneer through works such as Sringara Naishadham and Haravilasam.
101.tq: Retain both closely related literary attributions instead of treating them as mutually exclusive.

101.s: The Prabandha style reached its peak in the court of
o: Devaraya II, through the Reddi poets
101.x: The Prabandha style reached its peak with the Ashtadiggajas at the court of Krishnadevaraya.
101.tq: Match a literary movement with its principal court and associated group.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding patronage of the Prabandha tradition is correct?
1. The Reddi courts supported Srinatha and Errana.
2. The Vijayanagara Nayaka courts helped spread the style.
3. The style was confined exclusively to the court of Krishnadevaraya.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Reddi courts and Vijayanagara Nayaka courts also supported or spread the Prabandha style.
101.tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘exclusively’ in a statement about literary patronage.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Sanskrit work and Telugu rendering)
a. Harivamsa
b. Markandeya Puranam
c. Naishadham
d. Dasakumara Charitra

List-II (Translator or Telugu author)
i. Ketana
ii. Srinatha
iii. Errana
iv. Marana
101.x: Errana translated Harivamsa, Marana translated Markandeya Puranam, Srinatha rendered Naishadham as Sringara Naishadham and Ketana translated Dasakumara Charitra.
101.tq: Start with the distinctive translation pair and eliminate codes containing swapped translators.

101.s: Who translated Harivamsa into Telugu and dedicated it to Prolaya Vema?
101.x: Errana translated Harivamsa and dedicated it to Prolaya Vema.
101.tq: Separate the translator of a main text from the author of its Uttara section.

101.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
101.x: Uttara Harivamsa was written by Nachana Somana. Markandeya Puranam is associated with Marana, Naishadham with Srinatha and Dasakumara Charitra with Ketana.
101.tq: Discriminate between closely related texts belonging to the same translation tradition.

101.s: Marana, who translated Markandeya Puranam into Telugu, was a disciple of
101.x: Marana was a disciple of Tikkana.
101.tq: Connect a translator with his literary teacher instead of confusing him with the translator's subject text.

101.s: Ketana's Telugu Dasakumara Charitra was based on which Sanskrit work?
101.x: Ketana translated the Sanskrit Dasakumara Charita as Dasakumara Charitra in Telugu.
101.tq: Distinguish near-identical Sanskrit and Telugu titles rather than treating them as separate works.

101.s: Manchena's Keyurabahu Charitra is associated with the Telugu rendering of
101.x: Manchena rendered Viddhasalabhanjika as Keyurabahu Charitra in Telugu.
101.tq: Use the source-work to target-work association to distinguish similar classical titles.

101.s:
Arrange the following periods of Telugu literature in chronological order:
A. Nannaya age
B. Tikkana age
C. Srinatha age
D. Prabandha or Rayala age
101.x: The Nannaya age belongs to the 11th century, followed by the Tikkana age in the 13th century, the Srinatha age in the 15th century and the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century.
101.tq: Place the periods by their century markers, then verify the sequence from earliest to latest.

101.s: The Shiva Kavi Yugam in Telugu literary periodisation is generally assigned to
101.x: The Shiva Kavi Yugam is assigned to the period from 1060 to 1260.
101.tq: Use the stated range directly and reject adjacent-looking chronological intervals.

101.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its period of Telugu literature?
1. Nannaya age — 11th century
2. Tikkana age — 13th century
3. Errana age — 14th century
4. Srinatha age — 15th century
101.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Nannaya belongs to the 11th century, Tikkana to the 13th, Errana to the 14th and Srinatha to the 15th century.
101.tq: Check each century independently before selecting the coded combination.

101.s: Which one of the following represents the correct sequence after the Srinatha age in Telugu literary periodisation?
o: Prabandha age, Dakshinatya age, Modern age
Dakshinatya age, Prabandha age, Modern age
Modern age, Prabandha age, Dakshinatya age
Prabandha age, Modern age, Dakshinatya age
101.x: The Srinatha age is followed by the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century, the Dakshinatya or southern Nayaka age in the 17th–18th centuries and the Modern age from the 19th century onward.
101.tq: Follow the period labels and their century ranges from early modern to modern literature.

101.s:
Which of the following statements about the periodisation of Telugu literature is correct?
1. The Pre-Nannaya period extends approximately up to 1000.
2. The Modern age begins in the 19th century and continues thereafter.
3. All the boundaries of the periods are precise and uniformly fixed.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because boundaries other than the specifically marked ones are approximate.
101.tq: Identify the qualification that limits an otherwise broad periodisation scheme.

101.s: Which of the following is the correct association of a title, its holder and the literary basis of the title?
101.x: Ketana was called Abhinava Dandi for his Telugu Dasakumara Charitra. The other options swap the holders of the titles.
101.tq: Verify all three elements of a composite association instead of relying on the title alone.

101.s: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over which of the following three historical eras?
o: Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi eras
Vijayanagara, Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi eras
101.x: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over three successive eras: the Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi periods.
101.tq: Use the dynasty sequence to identify the correct historical span.

101.s: Which one of the following best explains the significance of Nannaya's contribution to Telugu literature?
o: He established the desi-metre tradition during the Vijayanagara period.
He introduced Persian vocabulary into Telugu court literature.
He fixed the grammar and literary register of classical Telugu and initiated the Kavitrayam tradition.
He was the first poet to compose a Telugu satakam.
101.x: Nannaya's Bharatam helped fix the grammar and literary register of classical Telugu and began the tradition of the Kavitrayam.
101.tq: Select the option that combines the stated literary contributions without adding an unrelated claim.

101.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Andhra Mahabharatamu — First Telugu book
2. Andhra Shabda Chintamani — First Telugu grammar, written in Sanskrit
3. Ganita Sara Sangraha — First Telugu mathematics book

Which of the pairs given above are correct?
101.x: All three pairs are correct. Andhra Mahabharatamu is identified as the first Telugu book, Andhra Shabda Chintamani as the first Telugu grammar in Sanskrit, and Ganita Sara Sangraha as the first Telugu mathematics book.
101.tq: Check each first independently before selecting the coded combination.

101.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August because it commemorates the birth anniversary of whom?
101.x: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.
101.tq: Match the commemorative date with the associated personality.

101.s:
With reference to the Telugu Language Day observances, consider the following statements:

1. Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August.
2. Telugu Language Awards are also associated with 29 August.
3. The date is connected with the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu Language Day and the Telugu Language Awards are associated with 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.
101.tq: When all statements describe closely linked aspects of one observance, verify the date, event and person together.

101.s: From 2026, the annual Telugu Mahotsavam in Andhra Pradesh is intended to be held:
o: Once every decade under the Archaeological Survey of India
Only on Telugu Language Day in alternate years
Once every five years during the World Telugu Conference
Every year as an annual Telugu cultural event
101.x: Andhra Pradesh announced that Telugu Mahotsavam would be held every year from 2026.
101.tq: Distinguish an annual recurring programme from periodic conferences and commemorative events.

101.s: Who announced the annual Telugu Mahotsavam at the valedictory programme held at the Undavalli Caves?
o: The Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India
101.x: Culture Minister Kandula Durgesh announced the annual Telugu Mahotsavam at the valedictory programme at the Undavalli Caves.
101.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the announcement rather than the venue or implementing agency.

101.s: An Archaeological Survey of India survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve during 11–13 June 2026 copied how many inscriptions?
101.x: The ASI survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve copied 25 inscriptions dating from the 2nd to the 16th century CE.
101.tq: For numerical current-affairs questions, separate the exact count from the associated date and range.

101.s: The Telugu records identified during the ASI survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve date from which period?
101.x: The Telugu records found in the survey date from the 7th to the 16th centuries CE.
101.tq: Compare the competing chronological ranges carefully; the broader survey range and the Telugu-record range are different.

101.s: An eighth-century Telugu inscription was reported at which place?
101.x: An eighth-century Telugu inscription was reported at Pitikayagulla.
101.tq: Use location-based recall for an inscriptional discovery.

101.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the early history of Telugu:

1. Nagabu — First Telugu word
2. Kalamalla — First Telugu inscription
3. Addanki — First poetic inscription

Which of the pairs given above are correct?
101.x: All the pairs are correctly matched: Nagabu is associated with the first Telugu word, Kalamalla with the first Telugu inscription, and Addanki with the first poetic inscription.
101.tq: Start from the sure location–fact pairs and verify all three early Telugu milestones.

101.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic and literary situation during the Kakatiya period?
o: Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed, although Sanskrit remained the inscriptional language.
Persian became the principal language of Kakatiya inscriptions.
Only Tamil was used for literary composition and inscriptions.
Telugu literature declined, while Sanskrit disappeared from inscriptions.
101.x: The Kakatiya era saw the development of Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition. Telugu literature flourished, while Sanskrit continued as the inscriptional language.
101.tq: Separate the language of literary development from the language retained in inscriptions.

101.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam — First Telugu Ramayana
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is identified as the first Telugu Ramayana. Bhaskara Ramayanam is associated with the first Telugu champu, while Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is associated with grammar.
101.tq: Discriminate among closely related literary firsts by matching each work with its genre or status.

101.s: Which one of the following represents the source-wise variation regarding the first Telugu Purana?
o: Andhra Mahabharatamu or Ganita Sara Sangraha
Andhra Shabda Chintamani or Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam
101.x: Different sources identify either Markandeya Puranam or Basava Puranam as the first Telugu Purana. The variation reflects differing criteria and traditions concerning literary 'firsts'.
101.tq: Read the wording closely where alternative traditions are expressly recognised instead of forcing a single answer.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya and Telugu literary culture:

1. The line “Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa” is associated with Krishnadevaraya.
2. The Ashtadiggajas are associated with the peak of Telugu literary culture during this period.
3. The Kakatiya period alone is identified with the Ashtadiggajas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Ashtadiggajas are associated with the peak of Telugu literature during the Vijayanagara period, particularly under Krishnadevaraya.
101.tq: Reject the statement that transfers a famous literary group to the wrong historical period.

101.s: Tikkana Somayaji was the first Telugu poet to have a work dedicated to him. Which work was dedicated to him?
o: Ranganatha Ramayanam by Gona Budda Reddy
101.x: Ketana dedicated Dasakumara Charitra to Tikkana Somayaji, making Tikkana the first Telugu poet to have a work dedicated to him.
101.tq: Use the author–work–dedicatee relationship rather than confusing it with authorship of the major epics.

101.s: Telugu was recognised as a classical language of India in which year?
101.x: Telugu has been recognised as a classical language since 2008.
101.tq: Distinguish the exact recognition year from nearby milestone years.

101.s: The proposal to install a statue of Tikkana Somayaji was associated with which district?
101.x: Andhra Pradesh discussed installing a statue of Tikkana Somayaji in SPSR Nellore district.
101.tq: Match the literary personality with the district linked to the current proposal.

101.s:
Arrange the following Telugu literary and inscriptional milestones in chronological order, beginning with the earliest:

A. Kalamalla inscription
B. Pitikayagulla eighth-century inscription
C. Addanki poetic inscription
D. Telugu records of the Nallamala survey extending to the sixteenth century
101.x: Kalamalla is dated to 575 CE, the Addanki poetic inscription belongs later, the Pitikayagulla inscription is from the eighth century, and the surveyed Telugu records extend up to the sixteenth century. Hence the order is A, C, B, D.
101.tq: Anchor the sequence with the known 575 CE date and the sixteenth-century end point, then place the eighth-century item carefully.

101.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy — Birth anniversary commemorated on Telugu Language Day
Tikkana Somayaji — Birth anniversary commemorated on 29 August
101.x: Tikkana Somayaji is not associated with 29 August. The date marks the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy and is observed as Telugu Language Day.
101.tq: Find the single mismatched personality–observance pair rather than accepting all familiar Telugu literary names.

102.s: Muhammad Ghori entered India through which pass?
102.x: Muhammad Ghori entered India through the Gomal Pass.
102.tq: Use direct route-place recall.

102.s: Which one of the following was the correct sequence of Muhammad Ghori's conquests in India?
o: Multan, Peshawar, Sindh, Punjab and Lahore
Peshawar, Multan, Punjab and Lahore, Sindh
Sindh, Multan, Peshawar, Punjab and Lahore
Punjab and Lahore, Sindh, Multan, Peshawar
102.x: Ghori took Multan in 1175, Peshawar around 1179, Sindh around 1182, and Punjab and Lahore around 1190.
102.tq: Arrange territorial conquests in chronological order.

102.s: Who defeated Muhammad Ghori near Mount Abu at Kayadara in 1178?
102.x: The Chaulukya ruler Bhimdev II defeated Muhammad Ghori near Mount Abu at Kayadara in 1178.
102.tq: Distinguish the ruler from nearby Rajput opponents.

102.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battles of Tarain:
1. The First Battle of Tarain was fought in 1191.
2. The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in 1192.
3. Both battles were fought against Jaichand of Kanauj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: The First and Second Battles of Tarain were fought in 1191 and 1192 respectively, both against Prithviraj Chauhan. Jaichand was the opponent at Chandawar.
102.tq: Split the statements by matching battles with years and opponents.

102.s: The First Battle of Tarain was fought over the control of which place?
102.x: The First Battle of Tarain began over Tabarhinda, identified with Bhatinda.
102.tq: Test the immediate cause and location of a battle.

102.s: Which one of the following statements about the aftermath of the First Battle of Tarain is correct?
o: Prithviraj permanently abandoned Bhatinda after capturing it.
Jaichand was appointed Ghori's representative in India.
Prithviraj captured Bhatinda but left it without a strong garrison.
Ghori established his capital at Kanauj.
102.x: Prithviraj took Bhatinda but failed to leave a strong garrison there, enabling Ghori to regroup.
102.tq: Identify the specific military error behind a later reversal.

102.s: Which battle marked the turning point that opened North India to Muhammad Ghori?
102.x: The Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 was the turning point that opened North India to Ghori.
102.tq: Associate the turning-point description with the correct battle.

102.s: The Battle of Chandawar was fought in 1194 between Muhammad Ghori and:
102.x: At Chandawar in 1194, Muhammad Ghori defeated Jaichand, the Gahadavala ruler of Kanauj.
102.tq: Match the battle with the correct opponent.

102.s: After the death of Muhammad Ghori in 1206, who founded the Delhi Sultanate?
102.x: Qutbuddin Aibak, Ghori's slave and Master of Stables, founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.
102.tq: Use the master-slave and succession relationship as the clue.

102.s: Qutbuddin Aibak served Muhammad Ghori in India as his:
102.x: After the Second Battle of Tarain, Qutbuddin Aibak was made Ghori's representative in India and had been his Master of Stables.
102.tq: Discriminate between an office and unrelated administrative roles.

102.s: In 712 CE, Muhammad bin Qasim defeated which ruler in Sindh?
102.x: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir in Sindh in 712 CE.
102.tq: Directly connect the invader with the ruler defeated.

102.s: Which of the following places was NOT among those captured by Muhammad bin Qasim?
102.x: Muhammad bin Qasim captured Debal, Nirun, Sehwan, Brahmanabad and Multan. Somnath was attacked much later by Mahmud of Ghazni.
102.tq: Find the place belonging to a different invasion.

102.s: The capital of Raja Dahir was:
102.x: Dahir's capital was Alor, also known as Aror.
102.tq: Test the capital associated with the defeated ruler.

102.s: Which of the following was NOT mentioned as a cause of the Arab conquest of Sindh?
o: A desire to establish a permanent capital at Kanauj
102.x: Arab maritime interests, expansion and piracy against Arab ships were stated causes. Establishing a capital at Kanauj was not a cause of the conquest of Sindh.
102.tq: Separate stated causes from an unrelated political objective.

102.s: Which statement best describes the religious effect of the Arab conquest of Sindh?
o: All non-Muslims were expelled from Sindh.
Only Buddhists were permitted to retain their religious institutions.
Hindus and Buddhists were given dhimmi status, and there was no mass Islamisation.
It resulted in immediate mass Islamisation of the whole of India.
102.x: The conquest did not cause mass Islamisation; Hindus and Buddhists were granted dhimmi status.
102.tq: Reject extreme claims and identify the precise social consequence.

102.s:
The Arab rule after the conquest remained largely confined to Sindh primarily because of which combination of factors?
1. The Thar and Aravallis
2. The strength of the Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas and Palas
3. Weak Arab resources
4. Complete political unity in North India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
102.x: The Thar and Aravallis, powerful regional states and weak resources restricted Arab expansion. North India was not completely politically united.
102.tq: Reject the reversed statement while retaining the three connected causes.

102.s: Which of the following was one of the important contributions transmitted from India to the Islamic world and subsequently to Europe?
102.x: Indian mathematics, especially the decimal and place-value systems, along with astronomy and medicine, passed to the Islamic world and later to Europe.
102.tq: Identify the cultural transmission rather than a political institution.

102.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
102.x: Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, also known as Tahqiq-i-Hind. Firdausi wrote Shahnama and Utbi wrote Tarikh-i-Yamini.
102.tq: Start from the sure author-work pair and eliminate swapped pairs.

102.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Firdausi's Shahnama was commissioned by Mahmud.
2. Utbi wrote Tarikh-i-Yamini.
3. Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind was an objective account of eleventh-century India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
102.x: All three statements are correct: Firdausi wrote the commissioned Shahnama, Utbi wrote Tarikh-i-Yamini, and Al-Biruni composed an objective account of eleventh-century India.
102.tq: Verify each author-work-description association independently.

102.s: Who was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar?
102.x: Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji was the real founder of Turk rule in Bihar.
102.tq: Distinguish the regional founder from the larger imperial conquerors.

102.s: Which set of Buddhist centres was sacked by Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1193–1203?
102.x: Bakhtiyar Khalji sacked the Buddhist centres of Nalanda, Vikramashila and Odantapuri during approximately 1193–1203.
102.tq: Test a complete named list without substituting famous centres.

102.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Bakhtiyar Khalji in chronological order:
A. Attack on Nadia
B. Sacking of Buddhist centres
C. Driving out Lakshmana Sena
D. Rule from Lakhnauti
102.x: The Buddhist centres were sacked around 1193–1203; Nadia was attacked in 1204, Lakshmana Sena was driven out, and Bakhtiyar then ruled from Lakhnauti.
102.tq: Use the dated event first and the resulting administrative centre last.

102.s: Which one of the following was a military reason for Turkish success in North India?
o: Reliance on war elephants and slow infantry formations
Complete absence of cavalry in Turkish armies
102.x: Turkish armies used mobile cavalry and mounted archers, whereas Indian armies relied heavily on elephants.
102.tq: Apply the contrast between mobility and elephant-based warfare.

102.s:
Assertion (A): The lack of political unity in North India helped the Turks to establish their power.
Reason (R): After the collapse of the Pratiharas, Rajput states became fragmented and competed with one another.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
102.x: Both statements are true, and the fragmentation and rivalry of Rajput states explain why political disunity aided Turkish success.
102.tq: Test whether the historical condition in the Reason explains the Assertion.

102.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with the social causes of Turkish success identified by R. S. Sharma?
o: Universal military participation across all castes
102.x: R. S. Sharma associated Indian feudalism with feudal levies, sub-infeudation and a closed village economy. Caste restricted fighting to a few groups rather than enabling universal participation.
102.tq: Spot the reversed social condition.

102.s: Historians generally give greater weight to which factor than to religious zeal in explaining Turkish success?
102.x: The historical debate gives greater importance to military organisation and less to religious zeal.
102.tq: Distinguish the dominant analytical explanation from a less-supported motive.

102.s: Which statement correctly describes the foundation of the Ghaznavid line?
o: Mahmud founded the line after the conquest of Somnath.
Alptigin and Sabuktigin were both rulers of the Ghurid dynasty.
Sabuktigin founded the line, while Alptigin was only a later governor.
Alptigin founded the line, while Sabuktigin is regarded as its real founder.
102.x: The Ghaznavid line was founded by Alptigin, while Sabuktigin is considered its real founder.
102.tq: Separate formal foundation from the accepted effective founder.

102.s: Mahmud of Ghazni ruled from:
102.x: Mahmud of Ghazni ruled from 998 to 1030 CE. His major raids occurred between 1000 and 1027.
102.tq: Distinguish the ruler's reign from the period of his raids.

102.s: How many raids did Mahmud of Ghazni undertake between 1000 and 1027?
102.x: Mahmud of Ghazni undertook 17 raids between 1000 and 1027.
102.tq: Use direct numerical recall with nearby competing values.

102.s: Which statement best describes the principal nature of Mahmud of Ghazni's raids?
o: They were undertaken only to spread Buddhism.
They were primarily raids that exposed India's military weakness and opened the north-west frontier.
They were aimed at systematic conquest of the whole of India.
They were defensive campaigns against the Seljuks in India.
102.x: Mahmud's 17 raids were not aimed at systematic conquest; they exposed India's military weakness and opened the north-west frontier.
102.tq: Discriminate between raids and permanent conquest.

102.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of Mahmud's targets?
1. Hindushahis
2. Nagarkot
3. Thanesar, Mathura and Kanauj
4. Somnath
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
102.x: Mahmud first encountered the Hindushahis in 1001–1008, attacked Nagarkot in 1009, Thanesar, Mathura and Kanauj in 1014–1018, and Somnath in 1025.
102.tq: Arrange targets using the dated campaign sequence.

102.s: The first opponents to resist Mahmud of Ghazni were the:
102.x: The Hindushahis, represented by Jayapala and Anandapala, were the first opponents to resist Mahmud.
102.tq: Identify the earliest resistance group and its leaders.

102.s: Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Nagarkot in 1009 mainly for its:
102.x: Nagarkot, identified with Kangra, was attacked in 1009 for its temple treasure.
102.tq: Link the place, date and immediate objective.

102.s: Which one of the following statements about Mahmud's campaigns is correct?
o: The Pratihara ruler of Kanauj resisted him successfully throughout.
Somnath was attacked in 1025 when Bhima I of the Solanki line was ruling Gujarat.
Nagarkot was attacked in 1194 during Ghori's campaign.
Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1009 under the rule of Jaichand.
102.x: Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1025 during the rule of Solanki Bhima I in Gujarat. The other statements wrongly interchange rulers, places or dates.
102.tq: Catch swapped rulers, dates and campaigns in a long historical statement.

102.s: Who resisted Mahmud of Ghazni among the following?
102.x: Chandela ruler Vidyadhara resisted Mahmud of Ghazni.
102.tq: Distinguish Mahmud's contemporary resister from rulers of other invasions.

102.s: Which of the following was NOT a motive attributed to Mahmud of Ghazni?
o: Systematic establishment of democratic institutions in India
Temple wealth to fund the state
Control of Punjab and acquisition of prestige
102.x: Mahmud's motives included political expansion, temple wealth, control of Punjab and prestige. Establishing democratic institutions was not among them.
102.tq: Separate historically stated motives from an anachronistic distractor.

102.s: The Ghaznavids declined after Mahmud chiefly under pressure from the:
102.x: The Ghaznavid power declined after Mahmud under Seljuk pressure.
102.tq: Identify the external power responsible for decline.

102.s: Which pair is NOT correctly matched?
102.x: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni, not Firdausi. The other three source-author pairs are correctly matched.
102.tq: Find the swapped author in a list of medieval sources.

102.s: Which source was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj?
102.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.
102.tq: Use direct source-author recall.

102.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chachnama — Muhammad Ali bin Abu Bakr Kufi
2. Kitab-ul-Hind — Al-Biruni
3. Taj-ul-Maasir — Hasan Nizami
4. Prithviraj Raso — Utbi
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
102.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Prithviraj Raso was written by Chand Bardai, not Utbi.
102.tq: Check each author-work pair and reject the single swapped author.

102.s: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to commemorate which historical event?
o: Muhammad Ghori's victory in the Battle of Chandawar
Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath, a thousand years earlier
The Arab conquest of Sindh by Muhammad bin Qasim
102.x: Somnath Swabhiman Parv was launched in January 2026 to mark 1,000 years since Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath.
102.tq: Use the distinctive event-year association and distinguish the commemoration from other invasions.

102.s: Which event is regarded as the turning point for the establishment of Turkish rule in North India?
o: The Arab conquest of Sindh in 712 CE
Mahmud of Ghazni's attack on Somnath
The Second Battle of Tarain in 1192
102.x: The Second Battle of Tarain, fought in 1192, is regarded as the turning point that enabled the establishment of Turkish rule in North India.
102.tq: Identify the decisive event by separating a turning point from earlier raids and subsequent consolidation.

102.s: The principal historical significance of the Arab contact with India beginning in 712 CE was that it
o: ended all indigenous scientific traditions in India
caused the immediate conversion of all Indian rulers to Islam
established permanent Arab rule over the whole of North India
102.x: The Arab contact beginning with the conquest of Sindh in 712 CE helped Indian scientific knowledge move westward and subsequently reach the Islamic world and Europe.
102.tq: Select the precise consequence and reject extreme claims about political or religious transformation.

102.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the objectives of Mahmud of Ghazni and Muhammad Ghori in India?
o: Mahmud mainly raided for plunder, whereas Ghori aimed at conquest and permanent occupation.
Mahmud sought territorial consolidation, whereas Ghori conducted raids for plunder.
Both Mahmud and Ghori were primarily interested only in religious conversion.
Both Mahmud and Ghori confined their activities to the conquest of Sindh.
102.x: Mahmud of Ghazni is characterised mainly as a plunder-seeking raider, while Muhammad Ghori pursued conquest and established a lasting political presence in North India.
102.tq: Split the options by comparing the motive and long-term objective of the two invaders.

103.s: Who is the author of ‘Prithviraj Raso’?
103.x: ‘Prithviraj Raso’ was authored by Chand Bardai and is associated with Prithviraj Chauhan.
103.tq: Direct author–work recall.

103.s: ‘Alha Khand’, associated with the Chandela ruler Paramardi, was written by
103.x: Jagnik is credited with ‘Alha Khand’, which is associated with Chandela Paramardi.
103.tq: Match the work with its author while separating similar court-literature names.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bisaldeva Raso — Narapati (Nalha)
2. Lalit Vigraharaja — Somadeva
3. Kirtikaumudi — Someshvara
4. Navasahasanka Charita — Padmagupta
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
103.x: All four pairs are correct. ‘Bisaldeva Raso’ was written by Narapati, ‘Lalit Vigraharaja’ by Somadeva, ‘Kirtikaumudi’ by Someshvara and ‘Navasahasanka Charita’ by Padmagupta.
103.tq: Check each author–work pair before selecting the complete combination.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: ‘Navasahasanka Charita’ was written by Padmagupta, not Someshvara. ‘Samarangana Sutradhara’ was written by Bhoja.
103.tq: Find the swapped author in a work–author pair.

103.s: The rise of the Chauhans of Ajmer, Chandelas of Bundelkhand and Paramaras of Malwa is principally associated with the
103.x: These Rajput states rose after the collapse of the Pratihara Empire, which led to political fragmentation in North India.
103.tq: Direct cause-and-effect recall.

103.s: Which of the following was a feature of the feudal structure associated with Rajput society?
o: Village economies were fully open and commercially integrated
Military service was completely absent from land grants
Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights
All land was owned directly by village assemblies
103.x: Rajput feudal arrangements involved land grants carrying revenue, judicial and police rights. Sub-infeudation, vishti and relatively closed village economies were also associated with this structure.
103.tq: Identify the precise institutional feature rather than an exaggerated alternative.

103.s:
R.S. Sharma used the expression ‘Indian feudalism’ in connection with which combination of features?
1. Sub-infeudation
2. Vishti or forced labour
3. Closed village economies
4. Complete absence of hierarchical landholding
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: Indian feudalism was characterised by sub-infeudation, vishti or forced labour, and closed village economies. Complete absence of hierarchical landholding is incorrect.
103.tq: Reject the absolute negative statement and retain the established cluster of features.

103.s: Rajput warfare generally placed emphasis on
103.x: Rajput warfare emphasised direct combat and personal valour, with chivalry and clan honour receiving great importance.
103.tq: Confusable strategy discrimination.

103.s: Which of the following statements regarding women and Rajput customs is correct?
o: Sati was entirely unknown in Rajput society
Rani Padmini performed naval warfare against Alauddin Khalji
Jauhar meant the ritual coronation of a queen after victory
Jauhar involved self-immolation to avoid capture
103.x: Jauhar was self-immolation by women to avoid capture. Rani Padmini of Chittor is cited as an example in the conflict with Alauddin Khalji; sati was also practised.
103.tq: Distinguish closely related social practices through their exact meanings.

103.s: The Vijaya Stambha at Chittor was built by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over
103.x: Rana Kumbha built the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.
103.tq: Separate the builder from the opponent associated with the monument.

103.s: Who constructed the Kirti Stambha at Chittor in the twelfth century?
103.x: The Kirti Stambha at Chittor was constructed in the twelfth century by Jijaji, also known as Jeeja, a Jain merchant.
103.tq: Monument–builder recall with a social-identity clue.

103.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
103.x: Kumbhalgarh Fort was built by Rana Kumbha. Chittorgarh was a Guhila or Gehlot, later Sisodia, stronghold of Mewar, while the Kirti Stambha was built by Jijaji.
103.tq: Use builder–monument pairs and eliminate swapped builders.

103.s: The founder of the Chahamana or Chauhan dynasty was
103.x: Vasudeva is regarded as the founder of the Chahamana or Chauhan dynasty.
103.tq: Direct founder recall.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chahamana — Sakambhari, Ajmer and Delhi
2. Paramara — Malwa, Ujjain and Dhar
3. Chandela — Bundelkhand, Khajuraho and Mahoba
4. Gahadavala — Kanauj and Varanasi
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
103.x: All four regional and capital associations are correct.
103.tq: Verify the region–capital associations systematically.

103.s: Who was the last known ruler of the Paramara dynasty, killed in 1305 by Alauddin Khalji’s forces?
103.x: Mahalakadeva was the last Paramara ruler mentioned here and was killed in 1305 by the forces of Alauddin Khalji.
103.tq: Use the date as an anchor for identifying the ruler.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: The Paramara dynasty was founded by Upendra, also known as Krishnaraja. Anangapala founded the Tomara dynasty.
103.tq: Detect the swapped founder among neighbouring Rajput dynasties.

103.s: The Tomaras were associated with which of the following?
o: Dhillika and coins bearing a horseman-and-bull motif
103.x: The Tomaras were associated with Haryana and Dhillika, identified with Delhi. Their coins carried the horseman-and-bull motif with the legend ‘Shri Samanta-deva’.
103.tq: Combine location and distinctive coin-type clues.

103.s:
Arrange the following dynasties in the order of the founders named in the historical sequence given below, beginning with the earliest listed founder in the dynastic tradition:
A. Gahadavala
B. Chahamana
C. Chandela
D. Kalachuri
103.x: The founders are Vasudeva of the Chahamanas, Nannuka of the Chandelas, Chandradeva of the Gahadavalas and Kokalla I of the Kalachuris, giving the sequence B, C, A, D in the arrangement used here.
103.tq: Use the founder sequence and compare the first two positions carefully.

103.s: The Khajuraho group of temples is located in which State?
103.x: The Khajuraho group of temples, associated with the Chandelas, is located in Madhya Pradesh.
103.tq: Direct monument–state recall without repeating the dynasty question.

103.s: Which deity is associated with the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple at Khajuraho?
103.x: The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is dedicated to Shiva. The Lakshmana Temple at Khajuraho is associated with Vishnu.
103.tq: Discriminate between deities associated with temples in the same group.

103.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vimal Vasahi — Rishabha (Adinatha)
2. Luna Vasahi — Neminatha
3. Modhera Sun Temple — Surya
4. Somnath — Shiva
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
103.x: All four deity associations are correct: Vimal Vasahi with Rishabha, Luna Vasahi with Neminatha, Modhera with Surya and Somnath with Shiva.
103.tq: Check each temple–deity pair before accepting the complete set.

103.s: Who built Vimal Vasahi at Dilwara, and in whose reign was it constructed?
o: Hemachandra during the reign of Mularaja I
Vastupala and Tejapala during Kumarapala’s reign
Udayamati during the reign of Jayasimha Siddharaja
Vimal Shah, minister of Bhima I
103.x: Vimal Vasahi was built around 1031 by Vimal Shah, a minister of Solanki ruler Bhima I. It is dedicated to Jain Tirthankara Rishabha or Adinatha.
103.tq: Separate the builder from the builders of the other Dilwara temple.

103.s: Luna Vasahi at Dilwara was constructed in 1230 by
103.x: Luna Vasahi was constructed in 1230 by the Vaghela ministers Vastupala and Tejapala and is dedicated to Neminatha.
103.tq: Link the date with the correct pair of builders.

103.s: Which one of the following statements about Somnath is correct?
o: It is a Vaishnava temple in Madhya Pradesh
It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era and is dedicated to Shiva as a jyotirlinga
Its present temple was completed in 1299 immediately after Khalji’s attack
The Old Somnath temple was built by Vimal Shah in 1031
103.x: Somnath is a Shiva temple and jyotirlinga in Gujarat. It was rebuilt in the Chalukya era, while the present temple was completed in 1951; Ahilyabai Holkar built the Old Somnath temple in 1783.
103.tq: Reject wrong dates and builders attached to a famous monument.

103.s: Rani-ki-Vav at Patan was built by Udayamati in memory of
103.x: Udayamati, the queen of Bhima I, built Rani-ki-Vav in his memory. The monument is recognised as a UNESCO site.
103.tq: Direct builder–person commemorated recall.

103.s: Which of the following is a work of Paramara Bhoja dealing with architecture?
103.x: ‘Samarangana Sutradhara’ is Bhoja’s work on architecture. ‘Siddha-Hema’ is associated with Hemachandra, while ‘Alha Khand’ and ‘Kirtikaumudi’ have different authors.
103.tq: Work–subject discrimination among similar literary titles.

103.s:
Which of the following works is correctly associated with Paramara Bhoja’s scholarly activity?
1. Saraswati-Kanthabharana
2. Yuktikalpataru
3. Rajamartanda
4. Samarangana Sutradhara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: Bhoja’s works include Saraswati-Kanthabharana, Yuktikalpataru, Rajamartanda and Samarangana Sutradhara.
103.tq: Recognise the complete list rather than selecting a partial combination.

103.s: Bhojshala at Dhar is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: An ASI-protected Sanskrit learning centre linked to Bhoja and associated with Saraswati
A Buddhist monastery dedicated to Tara
A military fort built by Rana Kumbha
A Jain temple dedicated to Neminatha at Mount Abu
103.x: Bhojshala at Dhar is an ASI-protected centre of Sanskrit learning linked with Bhoja and associated with a Saraswati or Vagdevi temple. It was later converted into the Kamal Maula Mosque.
103.tq: Identify an institution from its combined educational, religious and administrative clues.

103.s: Bhojshala was converted into a mosque in the
103.x: Bhojshala was converted into a mosque in the fourteenth century and is known to Muslims as the Kamal Maula Mosque.
103.tq: Year-century recall with closely spaced distractors.

103.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with Bhojpur?
o: An unfinished Shiva temple with a huge linga and the Bhojpur lake
A Jain temple dedicated to Rishabha and the Sahasralinga tank
A Sun temple and the Rani-ki-Vav
A victory tower and a mosque called Kamal Maula
103.x: Bhojpur, near Bhopal, is known for an unfinished Shiva temple containing a huge linga and the Bhojpur lake.
103.tq: Use the distinctive physical features to identify the correct place association.

103.s: The Udaipur Prashasti is important because it
o: records the genealogy of the Paramaras and praises Bhoja
records the construction of the Kirti Stambha by Jijaji
describes the naval victories of the Cholas
103.x: The Udaipur Prashasti gives the Paramara genealogy and praises King Bhoja.
103.tq: Inscription–content recall.

103.s: The original capital of the Solanki rulers of Gujarat was
103.x: Mularaja I founded the Solanki dynasty and established Anahilapataka, identified with Patan, as its capital.
103.tq: Founder–capital association.

103.s: Which ruler is correctly matched with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan and patronage of Hemachandra?
103.x: Jayasimha Siddharaja patronised the Jain scholar Hemachandra and is associated with the Sahasralinga tank at Patan.
103.tq: Separate the contributions of successive Solanki rulers.

103.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumarapala encouraged Jainism under the influence of Hemachandra.
2. Kumarapala rebuilt Somnath.
3. Kumarapala curbed animal slaughter.
4. The Solankis were exclusively Buddhist rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Solankis were Shaivas who also patronised Jainism, not exclusively Buddhist rulers.
103.tq: Identify the extreme and religiously swapped statement.

103.s: During the reign of which Solanki ruler was Somnath sacked by Mahmud in 1025?
103.x: Mahmud attacked Somnath in 1025 during the reign of Bhima I. Bhima I was also associated with the Modhera Sun Temple and Vimal Vasahi through his minister Vimal Shah.
103.tq: Anchor the event to the correct ruler and date.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding theories of Rajput origin and their proponents?
103.x: The foreign-origin theory, which associates the Rajputs with Scythians, Hunas and Gurjaras, was propounded by Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith. G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya supported the Kshatriya-descent theory, while the Agnikula tradition is associated with Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso.
103.tq: Start with the sure author–theory pair and eliminate the swapped proponents.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Agnikula theory of Rajput origin:
1. It traces the origin of certain Rajput clans to a sacrificial fire at Mount Abu.
2. Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso is associated with this tradition.
3. It identifies Chauhans, Paramaras, Chalukyas or Solankis and Pratiharas as the traditional four Agnikula clans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The Agnikula tradition describes the clans as emerging from a sacrificial fire at Mount Abu and is recorded in association with Chand Bardai’s Prithviraj Raso; the four traditional clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki.
103.tq: Test the complete traditional list while checking whether the origin legend and its literary association are both retained.

103.s: The theory that the Rajputs had foreign origins, including Scythian, Huna and Gurjara elements, was advocated by:
o: Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith
103.x: Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith advocated the foreign-origin theory of the Rajputs, associating them with Scythian, Huna and Gurjara elements.
103.tq: Use direct scholar–theory recall, with nearby historians as distractors.

103.s: The Kshatriya or ancient Indian descent theory of Rajput origin was supported by:
o: Col. James Tod and V.A. Smith
103.x: G.H. Ojha and C.V. Vaidya supported the view that the Rajputs descended from ancient Indian Kshatriyas.
103.tq: Discriminate between the two commonly confused scholarly groups associated with Rajput-origin theories.

103.s: Which one of the following descriptions correctly refers to the Latina or Rekha-prasada type of Nagara temple tower?
o: A pyramidal tower with multiple terraces
103.x: Latina, also called Rekha-prasada, is characterised by a single curvilinear tower. Phamsana has a sloping, stepped roof, while Valabhi is barrel-vaulted.
103.tq: Separate the three Nagara tower forms by their distinctive roof profiles.

103.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Nagara tower type)
a. Latina or Rekha-prasada
b. Phamsana
c. Valabhi

a. Single curvilinear tower
ii. Sloping, stepped roof
iii. Barrel-vaulted form

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
103.x: Latina or Rekha-prasada is a single curvilinear tower; Phamsana has a sloping, stepped roof; and Valabhi is barrel-vaulted.
103.tq: Build the answer from the three sure architectural form–description pairs.

103.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
103.x: Valabhi is a Nagara shikhara type characterised by a barrel-vaulted form; it is not the name of the Odisha regional school. Odisha or Kalinga is associated with the Rekha deul, Khajuraho with the Chandelas, and Maru-Gurjara with the Solanki tradition.
103.tq: Find the category error by distinguishing a tower type from a regional school.

103.s:
With reference to the Maru-Gurjara style, consider the following statements:
1. It is associated with the Solanki tradition.
2. It developed in the Gujarat-Rajasthan region.
3. It belongs broadly to the period from the eleventh to the thirteenth century.
4. It represents a fusion of the Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All four statements are correct. Maru-Gurjara is a Solanki-associated Nagara sub-style of Gujarat and Rajasthan, broadly dated to the eleventh–thirteenth centuries, and combines the Maha-Maru and Maha-Gurjara traditions.
103.tq: Check the dynasty, region, period and stylistic derivation as separate components of one architectural identification.

103.s: Which architectural feature is often associated with the Maru-Gurjara sub-style?
103.x: The Maru-Gurjara style, associated with the Solanki tradition of Gujarat and Rajasthan, often includes a Kirti-torana.
103.tq: Identify the specific architectural feature attached to the regional style, not merely its geographical location.

103.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bhojshala:
1. The Madhya Pradesh High Court declared Bhojshala a Hindu temple on the strength of Archaeological Survey of India findings.
2. The ASI survey of Bhojshala was ordered in 2024.
3. Under a 2003 ASI arrangement, members of both communities worshipped there on separate days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
103.x: All three statements are correct. The Madhya Pradesh High Court relied on ASI findings in declaring Bhojshala a Hindu temple; the survey was ordered in 2024, while the 2003 arrangement provided for worship by the two communities on separate days.
103.tq: Combine judicial finding, survey year and administrative arrangement without confusing their sequence.

103.s: The Somnath Swabhiman Parv marks:
o: 500 years since the construction of the Somnath temple
500 years since the completion of the Modhera temple
1,000 years since Mahmud’s attack on Somnath
1,000 years since the founding of the Solanki dynasty
103.x: The Somnath Swabhiman Parv commemorates 1,000 years since Mahmud’s attack on Somnath.
103.tq: Distinguish the commemorated historical event from nearby temple-building milestones.

103.s: With reference to the solarisation of Modhera, which one of the following is correct?
o: A 6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2022 at a cost of ₹76.66 crore.
A 60 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2022 at a cost of ₹766.6 crore.
A 6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage was inaugurated on 18 May 2026 at a cost of ₹76.66 crore.
A 15 MW plant with 6 MWh storage was inaugurated on 9 October 2024 at a cost of ₹67.66 crore.
103.x: Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme through a 6 MW plant and 15 MWh storage system. The project, costing ₹76.66 crore, was inaugurated on 9 October 2022.
103.tq: Check the plant capacity, storage capacity, date and cost as a combined numerical set.

103.s: The debates associated with the study of Rajput states and society include debates over:
o: Rajput origin theories and the Indian feudalism thesis
Only the chronology of Chola naval expeditions
The authorship of Sangam literature alone
Only the classification of Buddhist stupas
103.x: The principal debates identified here concern the competing theories of Rajput origin and the Indian feudalism thesis.
103.tq: Select the option that preserves both elements of the stated historiographical debate.

104.s:
Consider the following statements regarding medieval Persian chronicles:
1. Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami and relates to the early Sultanate.
2. Hasan Nizami was patronised by Qutbuddin Aibak.
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Taj-ul-Maasir is associated with Hasan Nizami and the early Sultanate, while Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
104.tq: Combine author, patron and dedication facts while checking whether all statements belong to the same source cluster.

104.s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri primarily deals with which of the following periods?
o: The Bahmani rulers and the Qutb Shahis
The reigns of the later Mughals
The Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans
The reigns of Akbar and Jahangir
104.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj’s Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers the Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans.
104.tq: Use the period covered as the distinguishing clue when several Sultanate works are listed.

104.s: Who wrote Futuh-us-Salatin, a work covering the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq and written at the Bahmani court around 1350?
104.x: Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami at the Bahmani court around 1350 and covers the period from the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq, including the Tughlaq campaigns against Warangal.
104.tq: Distinguish similar Sultanate historians by matching the work with its author and historical range.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi — Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
104.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni’s own historical work was Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
104.tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing, especially where a neighbouring historian is substituted.

104.s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is primarily a work on which subject?
o: The postal system of the Delhi Sultanate
104.x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, written by Ziauddin Barani, deals with political theory and kingship.
104.tq: Identify the subject of a text rather than confusing it with the author’s historical chronicle.

104.s: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written during the reign of which ruler?
o: Mubarak Shah of the Sayyid dynasty
Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Slave dynasty
104.x: Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi during the reign of Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah.
104.tq: Use the title and reign association to separate similarly named Sultanate chronicles.

104.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the periods they primarily cover:
A. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
B. Taj-ul-Maasir
C. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
D. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
104.x: Taj-ul-Maasir belongs to the early Sultanate, followed by Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and finally Tabaqat-i-Akbari up to Akbar’s reign.
104.tq: Place the earliest and latest works first, then distinguish the two intervening Sultanate chronicles.

104.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Amir Khusrau?
o: He wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini as court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni.
He wrote Rihla in Arabic after visiting Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He wrote Shahnama under the patronage of Akbar.
He wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 invasion of Warangal.
104.x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 expedition to Warangal. Kitab-ul-Yamini was written by Utbi, Shahnama by Firdausi and Rihla by Ibn Battuta.
104.tq: Apply the author–ruler–work trap to distinguish famous medieval writers.

104.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
104.x: Utbi was the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini. Firdausi wrote Shahnama, Ibn Battuta wrote Rihla and Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.
104.tq: Use the famous title as the anchor and reject swapped authors.

104.s: Rihla, the travel account of Ibn Battuta, was written in which language?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s travel account, Rihla, was written in Arabic.
104.tq: Test the exact language of a source rather than its author’s place of origin.

104.s: Marco Polo, who landed at Motupalli, visited the kingdom of which ruler?
104.x: Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya kingdom during the reign of Rudramadevi in 1289–93 and landed at Motupalli.
104.tq: Link the traveller’s landing place with the ruler and kingdom visited.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Abdur Razzaq — Portugal — Deva Raya II
104.x: Ibn Battuta was from Morocco and visited the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Marco Polo was from Venice, Abdur Razzaq from Persia and Duarte Barbosa from Portugal.
104.tq: Begin with the country–traveller pair and verify the ruler visited.

104.s: Which traveller is associated with observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets in the Delhi Sultanate?
104.x: Ibn Battuta’s account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign contains observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.
104.tq: Match the distinctive subject described with the traveller who recorded it.

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nicolo Conti was a traveller from Venice.
2. He described innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara.
3. The APPSC-associated account places him at the court of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct in the stated account. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian traveller associated with Vijayanagara and is noted for describing innumerable oil lamps at Diwali.
104.tq: Combine origin, court and distinctive observation to identify one traveller precisely.

104.s: Who among the following mentioned that Vijayanagara possessed more than 300 port towns?
104.x: Duarte Barbosa, the Portuguese traveller, is associated with the observation that Vijayanagara had more than 300 port towns.
104.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to separate travellers with otherwise similar Vijayanagara accounts.

104.s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443–44 as an envoy sent by which ruler?
104.x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443–44.
104.tq: Distinguish the envoy’s sending ruler from the ruler whose court he visited.

104.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Seydi Ali Reis — Italy — Ottoman admiral
Mahmud Wali Balkhi — Balkh — Qutb Shahi court
Mir Zainul Abidin — Persia — Muhammad Qutb Shah
104.x: Seydi Ali Reis was from Turkey and was an Ottoman admiral, not from Italy. Tavernier was French, Mir Zainul Abidin was Persian and Mahmud Wali Balkhi came from Balkh.
104.tq: Find the incorrect country–traveller association among closely related foreign visitors.

104.s: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire is based principally on the accounts of which group?
o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier
104.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire draws chiefly on the accounts of Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.
104.tq: Recognise the specific cluster of sources associated with a modern historical reconstruction.

104.s: Al-Biruni came to India in approximately which year and century?
o: Around 1030 CE in the eleventh century
Around 1450 CE in the fifteenth century
Around 1300 CE in the fourteenth century
Around 1150 CE in the twelfth century
104.x: Al-Biruni came to India around 1030 CE, during the eleventh century, under Mahmud of Ghazni.
104.tq: Distinguish the century and approximate date using the middle-period historical sequence.

104.s: Which one of the following statements about Al-Biruni is correct?
o: He confined his study of India exclusively to military campaigns.
He wrote in Persian without learning any Indian language.
He was patronised by Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.
He wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit and studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.
104.x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and the caste system. He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Vijayanagara.
104.tq: Use the language, subjects and patron together to identify the correct biographical statement.

104.s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
104.x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.
104.tq: Match the festival and its calendrical occasion with the appropriate chronicler.

104.s: Which one of the following was Al-Biruni’s observation about Indian society?
o: Indians had abandoned Sanskrit learning entirely.
Indian society was free from caste distinctions.
Indians were unwilling to share learning with outsiders.
Indian scholars refused to study astronomy.
104.x: Al-Biruni observed that Indians were unwilling to share their learning with outsiders. He nevertheless studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste through Sanskrit sources.
104.tq: Identify the precise social observation without reversing its meaning.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ramacharitam — Sandhyakara Nandi — Life of Ramapala
Prithviraja Vijaya — Gangadevi — Life of Prithviraj Chauhan
Madhura Vijayam — Jayanaka — Conquest of Madurai
104.x: Ramacharitam was written by Sandhyakara Nandi and deals with the life of Pala king Ramapala. Prithviraja Vijaya was by Jayanaka, Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi and Siddhesvara Charitam by Kase Siddhappa.
104.tq: Start with the author–work pair and check the subject attached to each regional source.

104.s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
104.x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.
104.tq: Associate the regional biography with its protagonist, campaign and political context.

104.s: Siddhesvara Charitam, written in Telugu by Kase Siddhappa, is a source for the study of which subject?
104.x: Siddhesvara Charitam is a Telugu work by Kase Siddhappa that provides information on Kakatiya-era society and religion.
104.tq: Match the language and author with the regional historical theme.

104.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
104.x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
104.tq: Detect the swapped author in a list of regional and Deccan sources.

104.s: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also known as which of the following?
104.x: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi and was written by Muhammad Qasim Firishta.
104.tq: Discriminate between similar Persian titles by identifying the alternate title of the same work.

104.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Muhammad Qasim Firishta is correct?
1. He was born in Astarabad in Iran.
2. He was born in 1552.
3. His work calls Telangana ‘Tilang’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Firishta was born at Astarabad in Iran in 1552, and his Deccan history refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’.
104.tq: Combine biographical numbers with a distinctive terminology clue.

104.s: Tarikh-i-Firishta was dedicated to which ruler?
104.x: Muhammad Qasim Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta, or Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi, to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur.
104.tq: Distinguish the dedicatee from the rulers whose dynasties are described in the work.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a Qutb Shahi source?
o: Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah — Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi
History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty — Anonymous, 1617
104.x: Hadikat-us-Salatin was written by Ali bin Tahir Bustani and deals with the Qutb Shahis. Basatin-us-Salatin was by Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi, Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah is anonymous and dated 1617, while H.K. Sherwani wrote the modern history.
104.tq: Use the author–title pair as the anchor and eliminate shifted authorship and dates.

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
104.x: Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl. Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written by Babur, Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum and Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori.
104.tq: Use author–work matching and reject swapped authors.

104.s: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written by Babur in which language?
104.x: Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Turki. It is one of the important royal memoirs of the Mughal period.
104.tq: Test the exact language associated with a royal memoir.

104.s: Who among the following authored the Humayun-nama?
104.x: Humayun-nama was authored by Gulbadan Begum, the daughter of Babur and sister of Humayun.
104.tq: Discriminate among closely associated Mughal court authors.

104.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri — Jahangir
2. Ain-i-Akbari — Abul Fazl
3. Padshahnama — Abdul Hamid Lahori
4. Humayun-nama — Gulbadan Begum
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
104.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was written by Jahangir, Ain-i-Akbari by Abul Fazl, Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori and Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum.
104.tq: Verify each author–work pair before selecting the complete combination.

104.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Mughal literary works and translations?
o: The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Kalila wa Dimna.
The Panchatantra was translated into Persian as Ain-i-Akbari.
The Ramayana was translated into Persian as Padshahnama.
The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Razmnama.
104.x: The Persian translation of the Mahabharata was known as Razmnama. Kalila wa Dimna was the Persian rendering of the Panchatantra.
104.tq: Separate translated works from the titles of their Persian versions.

104.s: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, contains an early reference to which festival?
104.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, mentions Diwali. This makes it an important early textual reference to the festival.
104.tq: Link the precise date with the cultural fact rather than a nearby festival.

104.s: The Ghazinagar Persian inscription is located in which present-day district, and is associated with which Qutb Shahi ruler?
o: Medak district — Jamsheed Quli Qutb Shah
Warangal district — Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
104.x: The Ghazinagar inscription is in Nalgonda and is associated with Ibrahim Quli. It dates to 1576–77.
104.tq: Combine location, ruler and date in an inscription-based identification.

104.s: Which of the following correctly lists the Qutb Shahi inscriptions and their dates?
104.x: The Daru-Shifa inscription dates to 1595, while the Badshahi Ashurkhana inscription dates to 1592–96. The other dates belong to different records.
104.tq: Match inscriptions with their exact dates and avoid date swapping.

104.s: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda is significant because it dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to:
