123.tq: Separate the works of Krishnadevaraya from those of the Aravidu feudatory Anantaraju.

123.s: The steps to Tirumala and the Govindaraja temple are associated with
123.x: The steps to Tirumala and the Govindaraja temple were associated with Anantaraju, an Aravidu feudatory.
123.tq: Identify the correct donor by distinguishing royal patronage from feudatory patronage.

123.s: Which of the following temples was NOT included among those renovated or endowed by Krishnadevaraya?
123.x: Krishnadevaraya renovated or endowed Srikalahasti, Simhachalam, Amaravati and Kanaka Durga at Bejawada. The Govindaraja temple was associated with Anantaraju.
123.tq: Find the exception by separating Krishnadevaraya’s endowments from Anantaraju’s works.

123.s: Kanaka Durga temple, which was renovated or endowed by Krishnadevaraya, is located at
123.x: Kanaka Durga is identified with Bejawada, and it was among the temples renovated or endowed by Krishnadevaraya.
123.tq: Test the temple–place association within the list of royal endowments.

123.s: The Vijayanagara style is regarded as
o: the last great phase of Dravidian temple building
a purely Indo-Islamic phase of temple architecture
a style confined to the Deccan plateau
the earliest phase of Dravidian temple building
123.x: The Vijayanagara style is regarded as the last great phase of Dravidian temple building.
123.tq: Directly test the historical significance assigned to the style.

123.s: The spread of Vijayanagara temple architecture from Hampi included
o: the Himalayan region and coastal Odisha
only the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh
123.x: The style spread from Hampi across Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra.
123.tq: Test the geographical range rather than the architectural features alone.

123.s: Which one of the following places is located in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh?
123.x: Lepakshi is located in Sri Sathya Sai district. The other listed places are associated with different locations in Andhra Pradesh.
123.tq: Use the district–monument association as the deciding clue.

123.s:
Match the following monuments with their districts or locations:

(a) Lepakshi
(b) Tadipatri
(c) Tirupati
(d) Chandragiri

(i) Anantapur
(ii) Sri Sathya Sai district
(iii) Tirupati region
(iv) Chittoor region

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
123.x: Lepakshi is in Sri Sathya Sai district, Tadipatri is in Anantapur, Tirupati belongs to the Tirupati region, and Chandragiri is associated with the Chittoor region.
123.tq: Start with the distinctive Lepakshi–Sri Sathya Sai pairing and eliminate the remaining codes.

123.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the historical debate regarding certain Vijayanagara monuments?

1. The builder of the Hazara Rama temple is variously identified as Devaraya I, Devaraya II or Krishnadevaraya.
2. The builder of Lepakshi is variously identified as Krishnadevaraya or Achyutaraya.
3. There is complete agreement that both monuments were built exclusively by Krishnadevaraya.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
123.x: The authorship of the Hazara Rama temple is debated among Devaraya I, Devaraya II and Krishnadevaraya, while Lepakshi is variously attributed to Krishnadevaraya or Achyutaraya. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
123.tq: Reject the absolute claim and retain the two statements that accurately describe scholarly disagreement.

123.s: The Government of Andhra Pradesh sought ₹103.05 crore for tourism infrastructure at Lepakshi in
123.x: Andhra Pradesh sought ₹103.05 crore for tourism infrastructure at Lepakshi in April 2026.
123.tq: Distinguish closely spaced current-affairs dates and retain the exact monetary figure.

123.s: Which organisation approved a new Kalyana mandapam at Lepakshi in May 2026?
123.x: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams approved a new Kalyana mandapam at Lepakshi in May 2026.
123.tq: Identify the responsible institution rather than the location or date.

123.s: The state launch of Yogandhra-2026 was held at the Lepakshi temple in
123.x: The state launch of Yogandhra-2026 was held at the Lepakshi temple in June 2026.
123.tq: Use chronological separation among the three 2026 Lepakshi developments.

123.s: In March 2026, inscriptions dated to 1534 CE were found on the 50-foot monolithic pillar of the
123.x: The inscriptions were found on the 50-foot monolithic pillar of the Somapalayam Chennakesava temple in Annamayya district. They are dated to 1534 CE, during the time of Achyutaraya.
123.tq: Combine the monument, district and inscription date to avoid location-based distractors.

123.s: The inscriptions discovered on the monolithic pillar of the Somapalayam Chennakesava temple are dated to the reign of
123.x: The inscriptions are dated to 1534 CE, the period of Achyutaraya.
123.tq: Match the inscription date with the ruler of the corresponding period.

123.s:
Which one of the following statements about current conservation and heritage listings is correct?

1. The Archaeological Survey of India is conserving Udayagiri Fort.
2. The IYB 2026 lists Hampi, Tadipatri and Lepakshi among the great monuments of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Tadipatri is associated with the period from the 13th to the 16th century.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
123.x: All three statements are correct. The ASI is conserving Udayagiri Fort, and IYB 2026 lists Hampi, Tadipatri and Lepakshi; Tadipatri is identified with the 13th–16th century period.
123.tq: Combine institutional, heritage-listing and chronological facts in one statement set.

124.s:
Which of the following is associated with Burrakatha?
1. Jamukula Kathalu
2. Thandana Katha in Rayalaseema
3. Harikathalu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
124.x: Burrakatha is also known as Jamukula Kathalu and, in Rayalaseema, as Thandana Katha. Harikathalu is the other name of Harikatha.
124.tq: Separate closely related alternative names before selecting the combination.

124.s: A traditional Burrakatha troupe generally consists of:
o: Two narrators and one actor playing a king
A main narrator and two Vantalu
A single narrator accompanied by a chorus
Three dancers accompanied by two drummers
124.x: The standard Burrakatha group has three members: the main narrator in the middle and two Vantalu who respond and comment.
124.tq: Use troupe composition to distinguish similar folk performance forms.

124.s: Which one of the following sets contains instruments associated with Burrakatha?
124.x: Burrakatha uses the Gummata, Burra, Tambura and Ukki, along with the characteristic chorus phrase ‘Thandana Taana’.
124.tq: Identify the instrument set belonging to one specific form.

124.s: The chorus phrase characteristically associated with Burrakatha is:
124.x: The Burrakatha performance includes the chorus phrase ‘Thandana Taana’.
124.tq: Test the distinctive verbal marker rather than the performer or instrument.

124.s: With reference to Harikatha, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It consists exclusively of puppet theatre.
It combines singing, acting and dancing by a single artist.
It is performed only by the Asadi sub-caste.
It is normally performed by a group of three narrators.
124.x: Harikatha is generally a solo performance in which one artist sings, acts and dances, usually for about three hours.
124.tq: Distinguish solo performance from group-based folk forms.

124.s: The principal musical instrument specifically mentioned in connection with Harikatha is:
124.x: Harikatha performances use Chidatalu, or cymbals.
124.tq: Use the instrument-form association to eliminate neighbouring options.

124.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bhagavatulu:
1. They are mostly associated with the Yadava community.
2. Their performances centre on the Krishna Leelas.
3. They are particularly famous in Rayalaseema.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: Bhagavatulu are mostly Yadavas, perform Krishna Leelas and are famous in Rayalaseema.
124.tq: Check whether all three linked identifiers belong to the same form.

124.s: Which of the following best describes a performance of Bhagavatulu?
o: Three Pichukuntla performers sing Palnati Veeracharitra for fifteen nights.
A solo performer narrates for about three hours using only cymbals.
A group of shepherds sings rural ballads to a small drum.
The performers dance around a pillar bearing Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols, using large bells, ankle bells and cymbals.
124.x: Bhagavatulu use Jeganta or large bells, ankle bells and cymbals, and dance around a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols.
124.tq: Match the performance format, instruments and ritual objects together.

124.s: The story of Ellamma is traditionally associated with:
124.x: Asadi Katha is performed by the Asadi sub-caste of Madigas and narrates the story of Ellamma.
124.tq: Link the narrative subject with its performing community.

124.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
124.x: Javiki and Chedika are the instruments of Asadi Katha. The other pairs assign instruments of different forms incorrectly.
124.tq: Start with the sure instrument-community association.

124.s: Pichukuntla Katha is performed by:
o: A troupe of three from the Pichukuntla community
124.x: Pichukuntla Katha is performed by a troupe of three belonging to the Pichukuntla community.
124.tq: Distinguish the performing community from other narrative traditions.

124.s: Which work is sung by the performers of Pichukuntla Katha?
o: Sugreeva Vijayam of Kandukuri Rudra Kavi
124.x: Pichukuntla performers sing Srinatha’s Palnati Veeracharitra, traditionally over fifteen nights.
124.tq: Use the author-work association to identify the folk form.

124.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pichukuntla Katha — turban, sword and shield
Harikatha — dance round a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols
124.x: Dance around a pillar with Sita-Rama-Lakshmana idols is associated with Bhagavatulu, not Harikatha.
124.tq: Find the performance detail transferred from one folk form to another.

124.s: During the Vijayanagara period, the most popular entertainment of rural Andhra was:
124.x: Tholu Bommalata, the leather puppet show, was the most popular entertainment among the rural people of Andhra during the Vijayanagara period.
124.tq: Separate royal-court entertainment from rural popular entertainment.

124.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Yakshaganam and Tholu Bommalata during the Vijayanagara period?
o: Yakshaganam was associated with royal courts and elites, whereas Tholu Bommalata was popular in rural Andhra.
Tholu Bommalata was confined to royal courts, whereas Yakshaganam was performed only in villages.
Both were exclusively temple rituals performed by the Veeramushti community.
Both were solo narrative performances using only cymbals.
124.x: Yakshaganam entertained royal courts and elites, while the leather puppet show was especially popular in rural Andhra.
124.tq: Read the comparison in both directions and reject the reversed relationship.

124.s: Late Vijayanagara patronage contributed to the development of:
o: Oggu Katha and Chindu Bhagavatam only
124.x: Late Vijayanagara patronage encouraged the development of Yakshaganas and Vachana, a prose-drama style.
124.tq: Identify the cultural forms linked to a particular period of patronage.

124.s: The Vipra-Vinodins of the late Vijayanagara period were:
o: Leather puppeteers performing in rural markets
Brahmin jugglers and actors performing for Brahmin households
Temple dancers attached to Shiva shrines
124.x: Vipra-Vinodins were Brahmin jugglers and actors who performed for Brahmin households.
124.tq: Use the occupation and patron group together to identify the term.

124.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Qutb Shahi period?
124.x: Koravanji is described as an ancient precursor of Yakshagana in the context of the Qutb Shahi period.
124.tq: Match the historical-period association with the correct cultural form.

124.s: Who wrote Sugreeva Vijayam, regarded as the first published Yakshaganam in Telugu?
124.x: Sugreeva Vijayam, considered the first published Yakshaganam in Telugu, was written by Kandukuri Rudra Kavi.
124.tq: Apply the author-work trap common in history questions.

124.s: Which of the following were performed across the countryside during the Qutb Shahi period?
124.x: Bhagavata stories and Parijatam were performed across the countryside during the Qutb Shahi period.
124.tq: Identify the pair belonging to the stated historical setting.

124.s: Which work records the staging of Harikathas, Natakams and Purana Kalakshepams at temple festivals during the Eastern Chalukya period?
124.x: Someshwara’s Abhilashitartha Chintamani, also known as Manasollasa, records these performances at temple festivals.
124.tq: Use the text-title and patron-author association carefully.

124.s: Burrakatha is traditionally associated with which place as its birthplace?
124.x: Guntur is identified as the birthplace of Burrakatha. It is a folk form associated with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
124.tq: Distinguish birthplace from the wider geographical area of practice.

124.s: Veedhi Bhagavatam literally refers to:
o: A Shaiva dance in Shiva temples
A form of leather puppet theatre
Bhagavatam performed only in royal courts
124.x: Veedhi Bhagavatam means ‘Bhagavatam in the street’ and denotes street theatre.
124.tq: Use the literal meaning to identify the cultural form.

124.s: Which statement about the Yakshaganam of Andhra is correct?
o: It is performed only in Sanskrit without costumes.
It is a shepherd ballad accompanied by the Oggu drum.
It is a solo performance centred exclusively on philosophy.
It is performed in Telugu with elaborate costumes and epic or Puranic stories.
124.x: Andhra Yakshaganam is performed in Telugu, uses elaborate costumes and presents epic or Puranic stories.
124.tq: Combine language, costume and subject matter to identify the form.

124.s: Which of the following was NOT a component fused by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu into Harikatha?
124.x: Narayana Dasu fused music, story-telling, dance, philosophy and literature into Harikatha. Leather puppetry is associated with Tholu Bommalata.
124.tq: Find the unrelated art form among the components of a composite performance.

124.s: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was a:
o: Brahmin juggler of the Vipra-Vinodin group
124.x: Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was a multilingual scholar who developed Harikatha as a composite performance tradition.
124.tq: Distinguish the performer’s scholarly identity from community-based folk performers.

124.s: Which of the following is a kavya written by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu?
124.x: Jagajyothi and Navarasa Tarangini are among the kavyas of Adibhatla Narayana Dasu. The other works belong to Burrakatha-related literature.
124.tq: Use genre and authorship to separate literary works from political Burrakathas.

124.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu?
o: Navarasa Tarangini — historical ballad on the Bobbili War
124.x: Na Yeruka is the autobiography of Adibhatla Narayana Dasu. Sri Krishna Kathamrutam is his Sanskrit Harikatha, while the other descriptions are incorrect.
124.tq: Separate literary genres—autobiography, Harikatha and political ballad.

124.s: Which statement regarding Harikatha is correct?
o: It has deep roots in Vizianagaram.
It is another name for Veedhi Bhagavatam.
It originated exclusively among the Pichukuntla community.
It is confined to Rayalaseema and absent from Vizianagaram.
124.x: Harikatha has deep roots in Vizianagaram, a region also associated with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
124.tq: Test the regional association without confusing it with the home region of another form.

124.s: In a Burrakatha troupe, the main narrator generally:
o: Dances around a pillar with idols
Stands in the middle and plays the burra
Acts as one of the two Vantalu and never narrates
Plays only the cymbals from outside the performing area
124.x: The main narrator stands in the middle, plays the burra and leads the performance; the two Vantalu respond and comment.
124.tq: Use stage position and role to distinguish the central performer from supporting members.

124.s: The two Vantalu in Burrakatha primarily:
o: Operate leather puppets behind a screen
Respond to and comment on the main narrator’s presentation
Perform the entire narrative without the main narrator
124.x: The two Vantalu support the main narrator by responding and commenting during the performance.
124.tq: Test functional roles within a troupe rather than names of performers.

124.s: Burrakatha traditionally evokes which rasas?
124.x: Burrakatha evokes heroic and tragic rasas through its narrative and performance style.
124.tq: Associate the emotional effect with the correct narrative form.

124.s: Sheikh Nazar, regarded as the Pitamaha of Burrakatha, was born on:
124.x: Sheikh Nazar, the Pitamaha of Burrakatha, was born on 5 February 1920 at Pannekallu in Guntur.
124.tq: Read the exact date rather than relying on a familiar national date.

124.s: Sheikh Nazar was born at:
o: A village in Telangana associated with Oggu Katha
124.x: Sheikh Nazar was born at Pannekallu in Guntur. Ajjada village in Vizianagaram district is associated with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
124.tq: Discriminate between the birthplaces of two major folk-art exponents.

124.s: Which pair of works is associated with Sheikh Nazar?
124.x: Sheikh Nazar’s works include Palnati Yuddham and Bengal Karuvu. The other pairs include works of Sunkara Satyanarayana or Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
124.tq: Use the author-work association and reject mixed-author options.

124.s: Who among the following is identified as a researcher associated with Burrakatha?
124.x: Dr. Tangirala Subbarao is identified as a researcher of Burrakatha. The other persons are associated with Yakshaganam, Manasollasa or Harikatha.
124.tq: Distinguish researcher, performer and author roles.

124.s: Which of the following names is included among the popularisers of Burrakatha?
124.x: Nazar, the Nittala Brothers and Bhadrakali are listed among the popularisers of Burrakatha.
124.tq: Identify the popularising group from among authors of related works.

124.s: Which of the following Burrakathas is associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana?
124.x: Sunkara Satyanarayana wrote or performed Burrakathas such as Kashtajeevi, Raithu Vijayam, Stalin, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Veeresalingam.
124.tq: Match the political Burrakatha title with its associated creator.

124.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana’s Burrakatha repertoire?
124.x: Bengal Karuvu is associated with Sheikh Nazar. Sunkara Satyanarayana’s listed works include Raithu Vijayam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Veeresalingam.
124.tq: Find the work belonging to the neighbouring but different performer.

124.s: The Praja Natya Mandali used folk plays primarily to spread:
124.x: The Praja Natya Mandali used folk plays to communicate socialist and communist ideals.
124.tq: Identify the stated political purpose of a cultural organisation.

124.s: Mabhoomi, a hit folk play of the Praja Natya Mandali, was associated with:
o: Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
Sheikh Nazar and Dr. Tangirala Subbarao
Adibhatla Narayana Dasu and Kandukuri Rudra Kavi
124.x: Mabhoomi was associated with Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.
124.tq: Match a famous political performance with its two associated creators.

124.s: The political and social utility of Burrakatha lay chiefly in the fact that its narrators:
o: Performed only before educated urban elites
Restricted their narratives to temple festivals
Avoided contemporary political and social issues
Carried news, reformist ideas and nationalist messages to unlettered villages
124.x: Burrakatha narrators communicated news, reform and nationalist messages to unlettered rural populations.
124.tq: Apply the communication function of a folk form to a social situation.

124.s: Which pair of books and years is correctly matched?
124.x: Telugulo Burrakathalu was published in 1986, while Burrakathalu was published in 1988.
124.tq: Match each title with its distinct publication year instead of reversing the pair.

124.s: Who is associated with the book Telugulo Burrakathalu?
124.x: K.H. Lakshman Rao is associated with Telugulo Burrakathalu, published in 1986.
124.tq: Use title-author association to distinguish two Burrakatha books.

124.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
124.x: Burrakathalu was associated with Kuvvada Vijayakumar and was published in 1988.
124.tq: Check both the author and year before accepting a bibliographic match.

124.s: The historical ballads of Burrakatha draw upon events such as the:
124.x: Burrakatha historical ballads draw upon events such as the Bobbili War of 1757, in which Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram sought French assistance.
124.tq: Use the event-year pairing and associated political actors together.

124.s: In the context of the Bobbili War of 1757, Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took the help of the:
124.x: Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram took French assistance in the Bobbili War of 1757; Bussy is associated with this French support.
124.tq: Identify the foreign ally rather than the regional ruler involved.

124.s: Oggu Katha is best described as:
o: A solo Andhra performance combining philosophy and literature with cymbals
A Shaiva temple dance performed by the Veeramushti community
A Telangana ballad form voicing rural life and struggle, sung by the Golla/Kuruma community to a small oggu drum
A leather puppet show popular in rural Andhra under Vijayanagara
124.x: Oggu Katha is a Telangana ballad tradition of rural life and struggle, performed by the Golla/Kuruma shepherd community with a small oggu drum.
124.tq: Combine region, community, subject and instrument to identify the form.

124.s: Chindu Bhagavatam is associated with:
o: The Veeramushti community in Shiva temples
Chindu performers, a sub-group of Madigas, in Telangana
Brahmin jugglers of the Vijayanagara period
124.x: Chindu Bhagavatam is a Telangana dance-drama performed by Chindus, a Madiga sub-group.
124.tq: Distinguish the performer community and region from similar traditions.

124.s: Veeranatyam is a Shaiva ritual dance associated with:
o: The Asadi sub-caste of Madigas narrating Ellamma’s story
The Veeramushti community in Shiva temples
The Golla/Kuruma community with the oggu drum
The Pichukuntla community in village streets
124.x: Veeranatyam is the Shaiva ritual dance of Veerabhadra, performed in Shiva temples by the Veeramushti community.
124.tq: Use deity, ritual setting and community as a three-part identifier.

124.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the material and technique used in Tolu Bommalata?
o: Cloth figures painted on both sides and projected by electric light
Opaque wooden figures painted on one side and moved before a fire
Metal figures suspended above a coloured screen and moved by strings
Thin, translucent leather figures painted on both sides and moved behind a white screen illuminated by an oil lamp
124.x: Tolu Bommalata uses thin, translucent leather figures painted on both sides. The figures are moved behind a white screen lit by an oil lamp.
124.tq: Use material, light source and performance position together to eliminate closely related puppet forms.

124.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Tolu Bommalata:
1. The puppeteer sings verses and delivers dialogue from behind the screen.
2. Moving the heads of the puppets is a distinctive feature of the performance.
3. Its themes include the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: All three statements are correct. Tolu Bommalata combines leather shadow figures, sung verses and dialogue, movable puppet heads, and themes drawn from major Hindu epics and Puranic traditions.
124.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined option.

124.s: The performance tradition of Tolu Bommalata is associated with which combination of themes and musical treatment?
o: Persian court narratives accompanied by military music
Romantic ballads presented without instrumental or vocal music
Themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas presented with classical music
Historical chronicles accompanied only by percussion music
124.x: Tolu Bommalata presents stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas, and its performances include classical music.
124.tq: Match the art form with its characteristic themes and musical tradition.

124.s: The term ‘Rupojjevanam’, associated with the tradition of shadow puppetry, appears in the:
124.x: The term ‘Rupojjevanam’ appears in the Mahabharata.
124.tq: Test the exact textual association of a distinctive technical term.

124.s:
Shadow puppetry, in addition to Andhra Pradesh, is found in which of the following States?
1. Odisha
2. Kerala
3. Karnataka
4. Maharashtra
5. Tamil Nadu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
124.x: Shadow puppetry is also found in Odisha, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. Therefore, all five statements are correct.
124.tq: Track every member of the geographical list before choosing the inclusive combination.

124.s:
With reference to Surabhi theatre, consider the following statements:
1. Vanarasa Govinda Rao belonged to a leather-puppet family.
2. He replaced puppets with live actors in Keechaka Vadham.
3. The performance was staged at a wedding in Sorugu village near Jammalamadugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: All three statements are correct. Vanarasa Govinda Rao came from a leather-puppet family and introduced live actors in Keechaka Vadham at a wedding in Sorugu village near Jammalamadugu.
124.tq: Verify the person, innovation and place as separate components of the statement set.

124.s: Which one of the following statements about the origin of the name ‘Surabhi’ is correct?
o: The name was adopted from the title of Keechaka Vadham.
Sorugu village came to be called Surabhi after the live-actor theatre experiment there.
Kuchipudi village was renamed Surabhi by the Qutb Shahi ruler.
Surabhi was the original name of the leather-puppet family of Kerala.
124.x: The live-actor performance by Vanarasa Govinda Rao’s family took place at Sorugu, and the village subsequently came to be called Surabhi.
124.tq: Use the place-name transformation to distinguish origin from later association.

124.s: The family theatre tradition associated with Surabhi is approximately:
124.x: The Surabhi family theatre tradition is approximately 140 years old.
124.tq: Identify the exact quantitative value rather than relying on the broad historical association.

124.s: Sheikh Nazar is correctly associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Burrakatha — Best Artist, Andhra Nataka Akademi in 1981 and Padma Shri in 1986 — biography Pinjari
Tolu Bommalata — Padma Vibhushan in 1981 — biography Rupojjevanam
124.x: Sheikh Nazar was a Burrakatha artist, received the Best Artist honour of the Andhra Nataka Akademi in 1981 and the Padma Shri in 1986, and is associated with the biography Pinjari.
124.tq: Start with the sure artist-form pair and then verify the honours and associated work.

124.s:
With reference to the awards and recognition of folk artists in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Sheikh Nazar was a Burrakatha artist.
2. Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was associated with Harikatha.
3. Sheikh Nazar received the Padma Shri in 1986.
4. The biography associated with Sheikh Nazar is Pinjari.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: All four statements are correct. Sheikh Nazar was a Burrakatha artist associated with Pinjari and received the Padma Shri in 1986, while Adibhatla Narayana Dasu was associated with Harikatha.
124.tq: Combine form, artist, award year and literary association without confusing the two artists.

124.s: Kuchipudi derives its name from a village located in which district?
124.x: Kuchipudi is named after Kuchipudi village in Krishna district.
124.tq: Use the place-based name carefully and distinguish the district from other Andhra cultural centres.

124.s:
Consider the following statements about the origin of Kuchipudi:
1. It grew out of the Bhagavata Mela dance-drama tradition.
2. It was associated with hereditary Brahmin families.
3. Its origin represents a village-theatre foundation for a classical form.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: Kuchipudi grew from the Bhagavata Mela dance-drama of hereditary Brahmin families, illustrating how a village-theatre tradition developed into a classical form.
124.tq: Read the origin statements as a connected tradition rather than as unrelated descriptions.

124.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the traditional association of Kuchipudi?
o: Founded by Sheikh Nazar and developed from Burrakatha
Founded by Siddhendra Yogi and developed from Bhagavata Mela
Founded by Adibhatla Narayana Dasu and developed from Harikatha
Founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao and developed from Tolu Bommalata
124.x: Kuchipudi is traditionally associated with Siddhendra Yogi and grew out of the Bhagavata Mela dance-drama tradition.
124.tq: Separate the founder of the classical form from artists associated with other folk traditions.

124.s: During whose rule was the village of Kuchipudi gifted to the performers?
124.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah, the last Qutb Shahi ruler, gifted the village of Kuchipudi to the performers.
124.tq: Apply the ruler–grant association and avoid swapping the ruler with the tradition’s founder.

124.s:
Arrange the following associations in the correct conceptual sequence relating to Kuchipudi:
A. Gift of Kuchipudi village to performers
B. Bhagavata Mela dance-drama tradition
C. Development of Kuchipudi as a classical form
D. Siddhendra Yogi’s founding role
124.x: The tradition emerged from Bhagavata Mela, Siddhendra Yogi is associated with its founding, the village was later gifted to the performers by Tana Shah, and Kuchipudi developed as a classical form.
124.tq: Build the sequence from origin, founder, patronage and subsequent classical development.

124.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
124.x: Sheikh Nazar was a Burrakatha artist; the title ‘Harikatha Pitamaha’ is associated with Adibhatla Narayana Dasu.
124.tq: Find the swapped artist-title pair among otherwise valid art-form associations.

124.s: The annual Telugu Mahotsavam announced by Andhra Pradesh is intended primarily to:
o: Replace classical dance traditions with modern theatre
Promote only Kuchipudi performances outside Andhra Pradesh
Revive Tolu Bommalata, Harikatha, Burrakatha and Padya Natakam
Provide exclusive awards to veteran artists
124.x: The Telugu Mahotsavam was announced to revive Tolu Bommalata, Harikatha, Burrakatha and Padya Natakam.
124.tq: Identify the purpose of the initiative rather than confusing it with an award or single-art promotion.

124.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recent cultural initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Nandi Natakotsavams are proposed to be revived along with an annual Telugu Mahotsavam.
The initiatives concern only Kuchipudi and exclude folk forms.
Nandi Natakotsavams are proposed to be discontinued permanently.
The Telugu Mahotsavam is intended only for urban theatre groups.
124.x: Andhra Pradesh announced an annual Telugu Mahotsavam to revive several folk and theatre forms, and Nandi Natakotsavams are also proposed to be revived.
124.tq: Distinguish revival measures from discontinuation and identify the scope of the cultural programme.

124.s: The announcements concerning Telugu Mahotsavam and the revival of Nandi Natakotsavams were associated with which Minister and location?
o: Abul Hasan Tana Shah at Kuchipudi village
124.x: The announcements were associated with Minister Kandula Durgesh and the Undavalli Caves location.
124.tq: Match the contemporary initiative with the responsible minister and reported location.

124.s: Applications for the Andhra Pradesh Ugadi awards in 2026 were invited on:
124.x: Applications for the 2026 Ugadi awards were invited on 19 March 2026.
124.tq: Separate the award-application date from the date associated with the cultural revival announcement.

124.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the condition of folk performance traditions:
1. Lack of patronage contributes to their decline.
2. Some traditions receive only three or four shows a year.
3. Youth disinterest is identified as a challenge.
4. Welfare support for veteran artists is considered weak.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
124.x: All four statements describe identified challenges: inadequate patronage, only three or four performances annually in some cases, youth disinterest and weak welfare support for veteran artists.
124.tq: Treat social, economic and institutional causes as separate statements before selecting the full combination.

124.s: Which scheme of the Union Government supports folk festivals?
124.x: The Centre’s Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana supports folk festivals.
124.tq: Identify the exact scheme name and reject similarly worded but unsupported programmes.

124.s: Folk performance traditions played which role in the Andhra Movement?
o: They replaced all written forms of Telugu literature during the movement.
They were restricted to Qutb Shahi courts and had no village reach.
They served as living proof of a distinct Telugu culture and carried that cultural consciousness to villages.
They functioned only as religious ceremonies for hereditary performers.
124.x: Folk performance was a living expression of distinct Telugu culture behind the Andhra Movement and helped carry that cultural identity to villages.
124.tq: Connect the cultural form with its broader social and political significance.

125.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Hand-knotted carpets — Eluru
2. Wooden cutlery — Udayagiri
3. Crochet lace — Narasapur
4. Lacquerware toys — Etikoppaka
125.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Eluru is known for hand-knotted carpets, Udayagiri for wooden cutlery, Narasapur for crochet lace and Etikoppaka for lacquerware toys.
125.tq: Use a complete matching cluster and verify each place–craft association.

125.s: The designs ‘Farishkhani’ and ‘Ashunkhani’, associated with Andhra Pradesh, attracted attention at which event?
125.x: Farishkhani and Ashunkhani were designs of Eluru carpets that attracted attention at the London Exhibition of 1851.
125.tq: Link the distinctive names with the precise historical year and event.

125.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with its place of production?
1. Budithi bell metal — Srikakulam
2. Dharmavaram sarees — Dharmavaram
3. Kondapalli toys — NTR district
4. Lacquerware toys — Anakapalli district
125.x: All four associations are correct. Budithi is in Srikakulam, Kondapalli is in NTR district, Etikoppaka lacquerware is in Anakapalli district and Dharmavaram is known for its sarees.
125.tq: Check whether each item retains its exact district or town rather than a neighbouring location.

125.s:
Consider the following statements regarding selected Andhra Pradesh handicrafts:
1. Kondapalli toys are made from light Tella Poniki wood.
2. Etikoppaka lacquerware toys have GI-tag status.
3. Dharmavaram sarees have GI-tag status.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct. Kondapalli toys use light Tella Poniki wood, while Etikoppaka toys and Dharmavaram sarees have GI-tag status.
125.tq: Identify the option containing all the precise GI and material attributes.

125.s: Which of the following statements about Kalamkari traditions in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Srikalahasti is associated with pen or freehand Kalamkari, whereas Machilipatnam-Pedana is associated with block printing.
Kalamkari in Andhra Pradesh is confined to Kondapalli.
Srikalahasti is associated only with block printing, whereas Pedana is associated with freehand painting.
Both Srikalahasti and Pedana are known exclusively for lacquerware painting.
125.x: Srikalahasti is known for pen or freehand Kalamkari, while the Machilipatnam-Pedana tradition is block-printed.
125.tq: Separate two closely related traditions by their technique and location.

125.s: Lepakshi, the state handicrafts nodal agency, is identified by which of the following names?
125.x: Lepakshi is the Andhra Pradesh Handicrafts Development Corporation, or APHDC, and functions as the state handicrafts nodal agency.
125.tq: Expand the institutional abbreviation from the agency’s stated function.

125.s: Which of the following products was specifically associated with Lepakshi’s global e-commerce portal for exporting GI products?
o: Banjara needle craft and dokra metal craft
125.x: Lepakshi launched a global e-commerce portal to export GI products such as Kondapalli toys and Dharmavaram sarees.
125.tq: Match the agency initiative with the products explicitly linked to it.

125.s: A 90-foot installation made of GI-tagged toys was reported at which location?
o: The new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram
125.x: A 90-foot installation of GI-tagged Etikoppaka toys stands at the new Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram.
125.tq: Use the distinctive measurement to identify the exact location and object.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about Kuchipudi:
1. The village of Kuchipudi is associated with Krishna district.
2. Kuchipudi is one of India’s eight classical dance forms.
3. It has been described as a global ambassador of Indian culture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct. Kuchipudi village is associated with Krishna district, and the dance is among India’s eight classical forms and is regarded as a global ambassador of Indian culture.
125.tq: Combine geographical, classificatory and cultural-status statements without confusing the village with the wider region.

125.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Kuchipudi from Bharatanatyam?
o: Bharatanatyam originated in Andhra, whereas Kuchipudi belongs to Tamil Nadu.
Kuchipudi is a strictly geometric solo repertoire without dialogue, whereas Bharatanatyam uses spoken dialogue.
Kuchipudi is a dance-drama tradition from Andhra, whereas Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu and a solo temple-dance tradition.
Both are exclusively group dance-dramas performed by male troupes.
125.x: Kuchipudi is an Andhra dance-drama tradition, while Bharatanatyam is associated with Tamil Nadu and a solo temple-dance tradition.
125.tq: Split the comparison into region, performance format and tradition before selecting the precise pair.

125.s: In Kuchipudi performance, ‘Tarangam’ refers to:
o: A sequence performed only with geometric movements
Dancing on the rim of a brass plate
125.x: Tarangam is a distinctive Kuchipudi feature in which the dancer performs while dancing on the rim of a brass plate.
125.tq: Recognise the technical performance term through its distinctive physical action.

125.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a Telangana craft or art tradition?
125.x: Dharmavaram sarees are an Andhra Pradesh tradition. Bidri, Cherial scroll paintings and Nirmal paintings are associated with Telangana.
125.tq: Find the out-of-state item by separating Andhra and Telangana traditions.

125.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of crafts associated with Telangana?
o: Bidri, Banjara needle craft, dokra metal craft and Nirmal art
Crochet lace, wooden cutlery, carpets and Etikoppaka toys
Lepakshi textiles, Srikalahasti Kalamkari, Cherial paintings and Dharmavaram sarees
Kondapalli toys, Kalamkari, Dharmavaram sarees and Budithi bell metal
125.x: Bidri, Banjara needle craft, dokra metal craft and Nirmal art are listed as Telangana crafts. The other sets contain Andhra Pradesh traditions or mixed associations.
125.tq: Check whether every item belongs to the same state rather than accepting a partly correct list.

125.s: Bidri work in Hyderabad is historically associated with Bidar, which is in:
125.x: Hyderabad’s Bidri tradition is derived from Bidar, which is in Karnataka.
125.tq: Distinguish the present production centre from the historical place of origin.

125.s: Which of the following statements regarding Kolattam is correct?
o: It is also called Dandalasyam and may be performed as a stick dance of eight or twelve participants.
It is a tiger dance performed during Vizianagaram Dasara.
It is a solo dance from Namala village in Anantapur.
It is a dummy-horse dance popular in Guntur.
125.x: Kolattam is also known as Dandalasyam and is a stick dance involving eight or twelve participants. The other descriptions refer to Puli Veshalu, Keelugurram and Namala Singadu Nrutyam.
125.tq: Use elimination through the distinctive alternate name and participant number.

125.s:
Consider the following statements about Kolattam:
1. Pennadi is the leader in the dance.
2. It was a main dance during the Eastern Chalukya era.
3. Annamacharya wrote Kolatam kirtanas.
4. The Karnataka version is known as Jadakollu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All four statements are correct. Pennadi leads Kolattam; it was prominent in the Eastern Chalukya era, Annamacharya composed Kolatam kirtanas, and its Karnataka version is Jadakollu.
125.tq: Retain all four linked attributes of one dance instead of confusing them with other folk forms.

125.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Puli Veshalu — Namala village solo dance
125.x: Tappeta Gullu is associated with the north coastal districts. Dhimsa is associated with tribal women of Araku, Keelugurram is popular in Guntur and Puli Veshalu is the Vizianagaram tiger dance.
125.tq: Start with the sure regional association and reject swapped dance descriptions.

125.s: Tappeta Gullu is traditionally performed by shepherd communities mainly to:
o: Celebrate the arrival of spring alone
125.x: Shepherd communities perform Tappeta Gullu to invoke rain and appease Gangamma. Drums are strapped to the chest and ankle bells are also used.
125.tq: Infer the ritual purpose from the community, deity and performance setting.

125.s:
Which of the following statements about selected Andhra folk dances is correct?
1. Butta Bommalu performers wear large hollow figures or masks.
2. Dappu is percussion-led.
3. Garagalu involves decorated pots carried on the head for the village goddess.
4. Gangireddulu features a decorated bull and is associated with Sankranti.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All four statements are correct. These features distinguish Butta Bommalu, Dappu, Garagalu and Gangireddulu respectively.
125.tq: Group the characteristic costume, instrument, prop and festival associations accurately.

125.s: Dhimsa, performed by tribal women of the Araku or Alluri Sitarama Raju district, is traced to which place?
125.x: The origin of Dhimsa is traced to Koraput in Odisha, although it is strongly associated with the tribal women of the Araku and ASR region.
125.tq: Separate the present performance region from the stated origin place.

125.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Namala Singadu Nrutyam — solo dance from Namala village
Keelugurram — dummy-horse dance popular in Guntur
Puli Veshalu — tiger dance of Vizianagaram Dasara
125.x: Dommarata is associated with acrobatics. Lambadi is the dance associated with the Banjara community; the other three pairs are correctly matched.
125.tq: Find the swapped feature by comparing the dance with its defining performance style.

125.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a folk dance with its characteristic feature?
125.x: Chekka Bhajana is performed with wooden clappers. Lambadi is associated with the Banjara community, Gangireddulu features a decorated bull, and Dappu is percussion-led.
125.tq: Match the instrument or object to the dance before considering the community association.

125.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Vasantotsavam under the Reddi kings is correct?
1. Kumaragiri Reddy styled himself Karpura Vasantarayalu.
2. Avachi Tippayashetti headed the Sugandhabhandagara.
3. The Sugandhabhandagara supplied materials for the festival.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
125.x: All three statements are correct. Kumaragiri Reddy used the title Karpura Vasantarayalu, and merchant Avachi Tippayashetti headed the Sugandhabhandagara that supplied the festival.
125.tq: Connect title, official and institutional function within the same historical context.

125.s: Which of the following festivals and associated features is correctly matched?
o: Sankranti — January; Gangireddulaata, Kolla Pandalu and Pottella Pandalu
Atla Taddi — Chaitra month; exclusively a harvest festival
Vasantotsavam — January; festival of Telangana identity
125.x: Sankranti occurs in January and is associated with Gangireddulaata, cockfights called Kolla Pandalu and ram fights called Pottella Pandalu.
125.tq: Use the month and the cluster of associated rural practices to identify the festival.

125.s: Atla Taddi is a women’s festival observed in which month?
125.x: Atla Taddi is a women’s festival observed during the Ashwayuja month.
125.tq: Distinguish the festival month from the January association of Sankranti.

125.s: Which of the following statements about Ugadi in 2026 is correct?
o: It marked Sri Parabhava samvatsara on 19 March 2026.
It marked Bhogali samvatsara on 14 January 2026.
It marked Rongali samvatsara on 19 October 2026.
It marked Karpura samvatsara on 1 April 2026.
125.x: Ugadi, the Telugu New Year, fell on 19 March 2026 and marked the Sri Parabhava samvatsara.
125.tq: Pair the exact date with the correct Telugu year name.

125.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Bathukamma — symbol of Telangana identity
2. Bonalu — symbol of Telangana identity
3. Bihu — Assam
4. Rongali Bihu — April
125.x: All four pairs are correct. Bathukamma and Bonalu represent Telangana identity, while Bihu belongs to Assam and Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April.
125.tq: Combine state identity with the correct state and seasonal form of Bihu.

125.s: Which sequence correctly represents the three forms of Bihu with their months?
o: Rongali — April; Kongali — October; Bhogali — January
Rongali — January; Kongali — April; Bhogali — October
Rongali — October; Kongali — January; Bhogali — April
Rongali — March; Kongali — June; Bhogali — December
125.x: Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April, Kongali Bihu in October and Bhogali Bihu in January.
125.tq: Arrange the seasonal forms using their months rather than their similar names.

125.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Lepakshi Utsav — Lepakshi
2. Visakha Utsav — Visakhapatnam
3. Lepakshi Utsav — Vijayanagara heritage
4. Kondapalli Toys Festival — annual festival
125.x: All four statements are correct. Lepakshi Utsav is held at Lepakshi and reflects Vijayanagara heritage; Visakha Utsav is held in Visakhapatnam, and the Kondapalli Toys Festival is to be held annually.
125.tq: Verify both venue and theme before accepting the festival association.

125.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the current Andhra Pradesh tourism festivals?
125.x: AVAKAI Festival, Vijayawada Utsav and Visakha-Anakapalli Utsav are listed among the current Andhra Pradesh tourism festivals. Bathukamma is a symbol of Telangana identity and is not in that list.
125.tq: Separate the stated Andhra tourism list from a prominent Telangana festival.

125.s: Telugu Mahotsavam was proposed to become an annual event at:
125.x: Telugu Mahotsavam at Undavalli Caves was proposed to become an annual event.
125.tq: Identify the venue associated with the festival’s proposed annual status.

125.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
125.x: Dwaraka Tirumala is known as Dakshina Dwaraka. Draksharamam is Dakshina Kasi and Srikalahasti is Dakshina Kailasam.
125.tq: Use the three epithets as a confusable-pair matching exercise.

125.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the epithets of Draksharamam and Srikalahasti respectively?
125.x: Draksharamam is called Dakshina Kasi, while Srikalahasti is called Dakshina Kailasam.
125.tq: Read the order of the towns carefully and avoid reversing the paired epithets.

125.s: Gangamma Jatara is associated with which place in Andhra Pradesh?
125.x: Gangamma Jatara is held at Tirupati.
125.tq: Use direct place-based recall for a fair and its venue.

125.s: Which one of the following features is associated with the Gangamma Jatara of Tirupati?
o: Men appearing in women's attire as Perantalu Vesham
Ancient tirunallu at a hill shrine
125.x: During the Gangamma Jatara, men appear in women's attire known as Perantalu Vesham.
125.tq: Discriminate between distinctive ritual features of different fairs.

125.s: The bamboo structures known as ‘Chapparalu’ are associated with which fair?
125.x: Chapparalu are bamboo structures associated with the Gangamma Jatara at Tirupati.
125.tq: Identify the exact ritual term linked with a particular fair.

125.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gangamma Jatara — Tirupati
2. Paidithalli Ammavaru — Vizianagaram
3. Mahanandi fair — Nandyal district
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
125.x: All three pairs are correctly matched: Gangamma Jatara is held at Tirupati, Paidithalli Ammavaru is associated with Vizianagaram, and the Mahanandi fair is in Nandyal district.
125.tq: Check each place association before selecting the coded combination.

125.s: Sirimanu utsavam is associated with which of the following festivals?
125.x: Sirimanu utsavam is the distinctive feature associated with Paidithalli Ammavaru at Vizianagaram.
125.tq: Match a distinctive observance with its associated festival.

125.s: Kotappakonda Jatra is located in the Guntur region, which is now included in which district?
125.x: Kotappakonda lies in the former Guntur region and is now in Palnadu district.
125.tq: Use the current administrative location rather than the older regional reference.

125.s: Which one of the following is described as an ancient tirunallu?
125.x: Kotappakonda Jatra is described as an ancient tirunallu.
125.tq: Associate the descriptive historical label with the correct jatra.

125.s: Mahanandi fair is particularly associated with which occasion?
125.x: The fair at Mahanandi, in Nandyal district, is associated with Shivaratri.
125.tq: Distinguish the religious occasion of one fair from the rituals of others.

125.s:
Which of the following statements regarding medieval Tirunallu or Jataralu is correct?
1. They were generally held at holy sites.
2. Kotappakonda was one such site.
3. Srikakulam in Krishna district was also cited as such a site.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
125.x: Medieval Tirunallu or Jataralu were held at holy sites, with Kotappakonda and Srikakulam in Krishna district cited as examples.
125.tq: Combine the general feature with both examples before choosing the code.

125.s: ‘Jola patalu’ belong to which category of folk songs?
125.x: Jola patalu are lullabies.
125.tq: Test the occasion-based meaning of a regional folk-song term.

125.s: Kolatam kirtanas are associated with which occasion or activity?
125.x: Kolatam kirtanas are sung for group dance and are associated with Annamacharya.
125.tq: Separate folk songs by their performance occasion.

125.s: Which of the following statements about the Gathasaptasati is correct?
o: It is a book on the theory of folk knowledge written by Biruduraju Ramaraju.
It describes only lullabies sung by women.
It records only court dances performed by professional artists.
It records couple and choir dances of rural folk.
125.x: The Gathasaptasati records couple and choir dances of rural folk.
125.tq: Reject over-specific descriptions and identify the precise literary-cultural reference.

125.s: The term ‘Janapada Kalalu’ refers to which of the following?
o: Arts of the village or Janapadam
Court music of the medieval sultanates
Classical dance forms performed exclusively on stage
125.x: Janapada Kalalu means the arts of the Janapadam, or village folk.
125.tq: Test the exact meaning of a culturally similar-looking term.

125.s: Who wrote the first book on the theory of folk knowledge?
125.x: Biruduraju Ramaraju wrote the first folk-knowledge theory book.
125.tq: Use the author-work association rather than a broad cultural description.

125.s: World Folk Day is observed on which date?
125.x: World Folk Day is observed on 22 August.
125.tq: Recall the exact date from the set of cultural observances.

125.s: The period from 1857 to 1956 is described as the ‘golden era’ of which field?
125.x: The period 1857–1956 is described as the golden era of dance.
125.tq: Link a date range with its associated cultural field.

125.s:
Which of the following statements about the Kondapalli Toys Festival is correct?
1. It has been made an annual festival.
2. Its annual status was reported in April 2026.
3. It is a marker of Telangana culture.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
125.x: The Kondapalli Toys Festival was made annual, with this development reported in April 2026. It is an Andhra Pradesh cultural reference, not a Telangana marker.
125.tq: Separate current Andhra cultural developments from neighbouring-state markers.

125.s: Etikoppaka received a current institutional connection with which place?
125.x: An Etikoppaka installation was reported at Bhogapuram airport in August 2026.
125.tq: Match the craft-related development with its exact location.

125.s: Which initiative is associated with Lepakshi in the context of current cultural promotion?
125.x: Lepakshi has an e-commerce export portal for promoting crafts, reported in March 2026.
125.tq: Identify the specific digital initiative linked with a state cultural platform.

125.s: Under which theme are Andhra Pradesh GI crafts marketed through Lepakshi by APHDC?
125.x: APHDC markets Andhra Pradesh GI crafts through Lepakshi under the theme ‘Vocal for Local’.
125.tq: Test the exact official slogan associated with the institutional initiative.

125.s: Which one of the following is NOT a marker of Telangana culture?
125.x: Bathukamma, Oggu Katha and Cherial are listed as Telangana markers. Kolatam kirtanas are associated with group dance in the Andhra folk-song context.
125.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring cultural context rather than the listed group.

125.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bathukamma — Telangana marker
2. Bonalu — Telangana marker
3. Bidri — Telangana marker
4. Nirmal — Telangana marker
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
125.x: Bathukamma, Bonalu, Bidri and Nirmal are all listed as Telangana cultural markers.
125.tq: Verify every member of a regional cultural list before selecting the complete combination.

125.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Cultural item)
 a. Gangamma Jatara
 b. Paidithalli Ammavaru
 c. Mahanandi fair
 d. Jola patalu

List-II (Association)
 i. Lullabies
 ii. Vizianagaram
 iii. Shivaratri
 iv. Tirupati
125.x: Gangamma Jatara is associated with Tirupati, Paidithalli Ammavaru with Vizianagaram, Mahanandi fair with Shivaratri, and Jola patalu with lullabies.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought between which two villages, according to local historical tradition?
126.x: Local histories place the battle between the villages of Rakshasi and Tangadi, on the north bank of the Krishna.
126.tq: Use the location clue to identify the correct pair of villages.

126.s: The Battle of Talikota was fought on which side of the Krishna River?
126.x: The battle was fought north of the Krishna, between Rakshasi and Tangadi.
126.tq: Test a precise geographical detail rather than the broader event name.

126.s: Who was the de facto ruler of Vijayanagara during the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Aliya Rama Raya was the de facto ruler and acted as regent for the Tuluva king Sadasiva Raya.
126.tq: Separate the nominal monarch from the effective ruler.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara side in the Battle of Talikota:
1. Sadasiva Raya was the Tuluva king.
2. Aliya Rama Raya acted as his regent.
3. Tirumala and Venkatadri fought alongside Rama Raya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Sadasiva Raya was the nominal Tuluva king, while Rama Raya was his regent; Rama Raya's brothers Tirumala and Venkatadri fought with him.
126.tq: Combine the nominal ruler, regent and military associates in one statement set.

126.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Sultanate)
A. Bijapur
B. Ahmadnagar
C. Golconda
D. Bidar

List-II (Ruler)
1. Ali Barid Shah
2. Ibrahim Qutb Shah
3. Ali Adil Shah
4. Hussain Nizam Shah

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
126.x: Bijapur was ruled by Ali Adil Shah, Ahmadnagar by Hussain Nizam Shah, Golconda by Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Bidar by Ali Barid Shah.
126.tq: Start from the sure ruler–Sultanate pairs and eliminate the codes.

126.s: Who is associated with the organisation of the Deccan Sultanates' coalition against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda is identified as the key organiser or leader of the coalition.
126.tq: Match the political role with the correct Sultan rather than merely identifying an ally.

126.s: Who beheaded Aliya Rama Raya after his capture in the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Hussain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar is stated to have beheaded the captured Rama Raya.
126.tq: Use the deed–person association trap common in medieval history questions.

126.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principal cause contributing to the formation of the Deccan coalition against Vijayanagara?
o: Rama Raya's policy of playing the Sultans against one another
Rama Raya's interference in the affairs of the Sultanates
Rama Raya's sheltering of Jagadeva Rao, a rebel from Golconda
The permanent military union created by the Bahmani emperor
126.x: The notes attribute the coalition to Rama Raya's diplomacy, interference, earlier attacks and sheltering of Jagadeva Rao; no Bahmani emperor created the coalition.
126.tq: Find the historically unrelated cause among closely connected political factors.

126.s: Rama Raya's policy of sacking Ahmadnagar during which period contributed to the hostility of the Deccan Sultanates?
126.x: Rama Raya sacked Ahmadnagar during 1557–63, contributing to the eventual unity of the Sultanates against him.
126.tq: Test the chronological range attached to a specific political action.

126.s: Which of the following pairs of matrimonial alliances is correctly stated in relation to the Deccan Sultanates?
o: Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim and Chand Bibi married Ali Adil
Bibi Jamal married Ali Adil and Chand Bibi married Ibrahim
Bibi Jamal married Ali Barid and Chand Bibi married Ibrahim
Bibi Jamal married Hussain Nizam Shah and Chand Bibi married Ali Barid
126.x: The Sultanates were linked by marriages: Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim and Chand Bibi married Ali Adil.
126.tq: Discriminate between closely similar personal names and matrimonial pairings.

126.s: Which sequence best represents the principal course of the Battle of Talikota?
o: Surprise attack, Vijayanagara success, peace talks, capture of Rama Raya
Vijayanagara successes, deceptive peace talks, surprise attack, withdrawal of Muslim contingents
Peace treaty, Vijayanagara retreat, Sultanate division, capture of Rama Raya
Withdrawal of Muslim contingents, Vijayanagara successes, peace talks, Sultanate attack
126.x: The battle initially saw Vijayanagara successes, followed by deceptive peace talks, a surprise attack and the withdrawal of Muslim contingents from the Vijayanagara army.
126.tq: Arrange the stages of the battle by identifying the first and final developments.

126.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes an immediate military development during the Battle of Talikota?
o: The Sultanates abandoned the field after the initial Vijayanagara success.
Rama Raya escaped to Penukonda before being captured.
The Muslim contingent in the Vijayanagara army withdrew during the battle.
The entire Vijayanagara army joined the Sultanates before the battle began.
126.x: The Muslim contingents serving in the Vijayanagara army deserted or withdrew during the battle, weakening Rama Raya's forces.
126.tq: Identify the precise battlefield development rather than the final consequence.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Battle of Talikota:
1. Hampi was looted for about six months.
2. The damage to the capital was severe but not total.
3. The Nayakas became autonomous and later developed into zamindars and poligars.
4. The Deccan Sultanates permanently stopped fighting one another after their victory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Hampi was looted for about six months, the destruction was severe but not total, and the Nayakas became autonomous. The Sultanates resumed fighting among themselves after the victory.
126.tq: Reject the extreme claim that a temporary alliance became permanent.

126.s: Which territories were gained by Golconda as a consequence of the Battle of Talikota?
126.x: Golconda gained Kondavidu, Machilipatnam and adjoining coastal tracts after the battle.
126.tq: Match the territorial consequence with the correct Sultanate.

126.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the post-battle movement of Vijayanagara leaders?
o: Sadasiva and Tirumala — fled to Penukonda
Rama Raya and Venkatadri — fled to Hampi
Sadasiva and Venkatadri — fled to Madurai
Tirumala and Rama Raya — fled to Chandragiri
126.x: After the defeat, Sadasiva and Tirumala fled to Penukonda. Rama Raya and Venkatadri were killed.
126.tq: Separate the leaders who escaped from those who were killed.

126.s: According to the account attributed to Ferishta, which additional factor aggravated relations between Rama Raya and the Deccan Sultans?
o: A refusal to trade at Pulicat
A dispute over the Portuguese succession
126.x: Ferishta additionally alleged that religious insults contributed to the hostility between Rama Raya and the Sultans.
126.tq: Identify the attributed explanation without confusing it with the main political causes.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Venkatapati Raya II:
1. He allowed Jesuit churches to be built at Nellore and Chandragiri.
2. He permitted the Dutch to trade at Pulicat.
3. He allied with Spain and Portugal.
4. He accepted Akbar's suzerainty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II permitted Jesuit churches and Dutch trade, and allied with Spain and Portugal. He rejected, rather than accepted, Akbar's suzerainty.
126.tq: Use the reversed-meaning trap in the statement about accepting suzerainty.

126.s: Madras, also referred to as Chennapatnam, was acquired by the English during the reign of which ruler?
126.x: The English acquired Madras during the reign of Venkatapati Raya III.
126.tq: Associate the territorial grant with the correct similarly named ruler.

126.s: In 1639, the grant of Madras was made by Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka to whom?
o: Robert Sewell of the English Company
Francis Day of the English East India Company
Francis Xavier of the Jesuit Order
126.x: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka granted Madras in 1639 to Francis Day of the English East India Company.
126.tq: Test the grantor–grantee relationship directly.

126.s: The Madras grant was issued through Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka to Francis Day of which body?
o: The Portuguese Estado da Índia at Goa
The English East India Company's Machilipatnam council
The Dutch East India Company at Pulicat
126.x: The grant was issued through Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka to Francis Day of the English East India Company's Machilipatnam council.
126.tq: Identify the correct company and its local administrative connection.

126.s: The name Chennapattanam was derived from the name of Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka's father. What was his name?
126.x: The site was named Chennapattanam after Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka's father, Chennappa.
126.tq: Trace a place-name to the person after whom it was named.

126.s: Which fort followed the English acquisition of Madras?
126.x: Fort St George followed the acquisition of Madras; the cited account places it in 1641.
126.tq: Link the settlement with its associated colonial fort.

126.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Nayaka kingdom)
A. Madurai
B. Tanjore
C. Gingee
D. Mysore

List-II (Founder)
1. Raja Wodeyar
2. Vishwanatha Nayaka
3. Krishnappa Nayaka
4. Sevappa Nayaka

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
126.x: Madurai was founded by Vishwanatha Nayaka, Tanjore by Sevappa Nayaka, Gingee by Krishnappa Nayaka and Mysore by Raja Wodeyar.
126.tq: Start from the distinctive founder–kingdom pairs and verify the remaining matches.

126.s: Who captured the rebel Nagama, his own father, and was consequently associated with the foundation of the Madurai Nayaka kingdom?
126.x: Vishwanatha Nayaka captured his rebel father Nagama and was granted Madurai.
126.tq: Use the unusual family relationship to identify the correct founder.

126.s: Which Nayaka ruler made Madurai independent around 1565?
126.x: Vishwanatha Nayaka's son Krishnappa Nayaka made Madurai independent around 1565.
126.tq: Associate the approximate date with the ruler who secured independence.

126.s: Which of the following pairs of a Nayaka kingdom and its contemporary Vijayanagara ruler is correctly matched?
126.x: Sevappa Nayaka of Tanjore was contemporary with Achyutaraya. Mysore was associated with Venkata II, while Madurai was associated with Krishnadevaraya and Achyutaraya.
126.tq: Compare founder–kingdom pairs with their contemporary Vijayanagara rulers.

126.s: Raja Wodeyar, associated with Mysore, took Srirangapatna in which year?
126.x: Raja Wodeyar took Srirangapatna in 1610.
126.tq: Identify the middle chronological value attached to the Mysore expansion.

126.s: Which of the following statements about Tirumala Nayaka is correct?
o: He led the Deccan coalition at Talikota.
He founded Gingee and took Srirangapatna in 1610.
He ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659 and allied with Golconda against Vijayanagara.
He granted Madras to Francis Day in 1639.
126.x: Tirumala Nayaka ruled Madurai from 1623 to 1659 and allied with Golconda against Vijayanagara.
126.tq: Match the ruler with his period and major political alliance.

126.s: Which architectural work is associated with Tirumala Nayaka of Madurai?
126.x: Tirumala Nayaka built the Tirumala Rayala Mahal.
126.tq: Identify the monument associated with the correct ruler.

126.s: Madurai came under the control of Chanda Sahib in which year?
126.x: Madurai fell to Chanda Sahib in 1739.
126.tq: Test the later chronological endpoint of Madurai's Nayaka history.

126.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
126.x: Chowdappa Nayaka is identified as the founder or key ruler of Ikkeri (Keladi), founded around 1500.
126.tq: Distinguish the founders of the less commonly tested successor kingdoms.

126.s: Which one of the following Deccan Sultanates did NOT participate in the alliance against Vijayanagara at Talikota?
126.x: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar formed the alliance; Berar, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty, stayed out.
126.tq: Find the excluded member by separating the four participating Sultanates from Berar.

126.s: The Sultanate that stayed out of the Talikota alliance was ruled by which dynasty?
126.x: Berar stayed out of the alliance and was ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty.
126.tq: Connect the excluded state with its ruling dynasty.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deccan alliance at Talikota:
1. Bijapur participated in the alliance.
2. Ahmadnagar participated in the alliance.
3. Golconda participated in the alliance.
4. Berar participated in the alliance in the standard four-member account.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda participated in the alliance, along with Bidar. Berar stayed out in the standard four-member account.
126.tq: Use the membership-composition trap to exclude the non-participating Sultanate.

126.s: The Aravidu dynasty of Vijayanagara derived its name from which place?
126.x: The dynasty was named after Araviti, also called Aravidu, a village in Kurnool district.
126.tq: Use the place-name clue to distinguish the dynasty from similarly named ruling houses.

126.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Aravidu dynasty:
1. It ruled the Vijayanagara Empire from 1570 to 1680.
2. It had seven rulers.
3. It was the first dynasty to rule Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: The Aravidu dynasty ruled from 1570 to 1680 and had seven rulers. Statement 3 is false because it was the fourth ruling dynasty of Vijayanagara.
126.tq: Split the statements and reject the extreme historical claim about being the first dynasty.

126.s: Who founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570?
126.x: Tirumala Raya founded the Aravidu dynasty and was crowned at Penukonda in 1570.
126.tq: Match the founder with his accession place and year.

126.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
126.x: Ramadeva ruled from 1616 to 1630, not from 1600 to 1616. The other pairs correctly give the reign periods stated for those rulers.
126.tq: Check the reign-period range rather than relying only on the ruler’s name.

126.s: Venkatapati Raya II is known in Vijayanagara history by which title?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II, the greatest and longest-ruling Aravidu ruler, was called the Second Krishnadevaraya.
126.tq: Use the title-based identification of a ruler.

126.s: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 is important primarily because it provides information about the genealogy of which dynasties?
126.x: The Vilapakam inscription of 1601 gives the genealogy of the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties.
126.tq: Identify the inscription through its specific genealogical content.

126.s: The Battle of Toppur, regarded as the ‘second Talikota’, was fought in which year?
126.x: The Battle of Toppur was fought in 1616 and is described as the second Talikota. Jagga Raya was killed in this battle.
126.tq: Use the distinctive epithet to anchor the associated year.

126.s: Who was killed in the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
126.x: Jagga Raya was killed in the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
126.tq: Link the named casualty to the battle rather than confusing him with a later commander.

126.s:
Arrange the following capitals of the Vijayanagara Empire under the Aravidu rulers in chronological order of their use:
A. Vellore
B. Penukonda
C. Chandragiri

Select the correct sequence.
126.x: Penukonda was the capital from 1570, followed by Chandragiri, and then Vellore in 1600.
126.tq: Fix the first and last capitals, then place the intermediate capital.

126.s: Which of the following correctly represents the capital–ruler association after the Battle of Talikota?
o: Penukonda — Tirumala; Chandragiri — Venkatapati II; Vellore — Venkatapati II
Penukonda — Venkatapati II; Chandragiri — Tirumala; Vellore — Sriranga III
Penukonda — Sriranga I; Chandragiri — Ramadeva; Vellore — Tirumala
Penukonda — Ramadeva; Chandragiri — Sriranga II; Vellore — Venkatapati III
126.x: Tirumala used Penukonda, while Venkatapati II shifted the capital first to Chandragiri and then to Vellore in 1600.
126.tq: Start from the sure capital–ruler pair and verify the remaining sequence.

126.s: Which of the following architectural features spread across Andhra through the Nayaka courts of places such as Kondavidu, Udayagiri, Chandragiri and Vinukonda?
o: Raya gopurams, kalyana mandapas and pillared corridors
126.x: Nayaka courts helped spread raya gopurams, kalyana mandapas and pillared corridors across Andhra.
126.tq: Distinguish the listed architectural vocabulary from features of other traditions.

126.s: Who wrote the work Vasucharitra during the Aravidu era?
126.x: Ramaraja Bhushanudu authored Vasucharitra, which was dedicated to Tirumala.
126.tq: Apply the author–work association without swapping the court figures.

126.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Classical Telugu literature reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya.
2. Shaivarka Mani Dipika was written by Appayya Dikshita.
3. Vasucharitra was associated with Ramaraja Bhushanudu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements are correct. Krishnadevaraya’s reign marked the zenith of classical Telugu, while Appayya Dikshita and Ramaraja Bhushanudu are linked with the two named works.
126.tq: Verify each author–work and period association before selecting the combined option.

126.s: The Nayankara or Amaranayaka system is chiefly associated with which aspect of Vijayanagara administration?
o: Land and military assignments to local chiefs
Election of provincial governors by temple assemblies
Appointment of village priests by the emperor
126.x: The Nayankara or Amaranayaka system involved the assignment of territories and responsibilities to military-local chiefs. After 1565, many nayakas became hereditary local rulers.
126.tq: Identify the administrative institution from its practical role in governance.

126.s: After the weakening of the Vijayanagara Empire, the amara-nayakas developed into which group?
o: Hereditary Palegars and the forerunners of zamindars
126.x: The amara-nayakas became hereditary Palegars, who were forerunners of the zamindars.
126.tq: Trace the institutional transformation after imperial decline.

126.s: Who surveyed and mapped the ruins of Hampi in 1800?
126.x: Colin Mackenzie surveyed and mapped the Hampi ruins in 1800 and later became the first Surveyor General of India.
126.tq: Associate the survey date with the correct investigator.

126.s: Which work brought the history of Vijayanagara to wide notice in 1900?
o: The History of the Bahmani Kingdom
126.x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire, published in 1900, brought Vijayanagara history to wide notice.
126.tq: Use the title–author–year combination to avoid confusing later historical works.

126.s: Venkatapati Raya II ruled the Aravidu dynasty during which period?
126.x: Venkatapati Raya II ruled from 1585 to 1614, a period of 29 years.
126.tq: Use the middle reign-period option and verify the start and end years.

126.s: Which one of the following was a feature of Venkatapati Raya II’s foreign policy?
o: He accepted Akbar’s demand for submission and severed relations with Europe.
He rejected Akbar’s demand, maintained ties with Portugal and Philip II of Spain, and allowed the Dutch to establish a factory at Pulicat.
He expelled all European traders from the east coast.
He transferred Pulicat to the Golconda Sultanate.
126.x: Venkatapati II rejected Akbar’s demand for submission, maintained relations with the Portuguese and Philip II of Spain, and permitted the Dutch factory at Pulicat.
126.tq: Separate the ruler’s multiple diplomatic actions from absolute reversal statements.

126.s: At which places did Venkatapati Raya II permit the Jesuits to build churches?
126.x: Venkatapati II allowed the Jesuits to build churches at Chandragiri and Nellore.
126.tq: Pair the ruler with the precise locations connected to missionary activity.

126.s:
Which of the following statements about Venkatapati Raya II is correct?
1. He was called the Second Andhra Bhoja.
2. Appayya Dikshita was associated with his court.
3. His coins bore the inscription ‘Om Venkateshwaraya Namah’.
4. He defeated Veerappa Nayaka of Madurai at Vallankota.
126.x: All four statements correctly describe Venkatapati Raya II, his court, coinage and military success at Vallankota.
126.tq: Check each closely connected biographical detail before choosing the complete combination.

126.s: The villages granted by Venkatapati Raya II were associated with which Muslim saint?
126.x: Venkatapati II gave villages to the Muslim saint Babanathu, as recorded in the Penukonda inscription.
126.tq: Use the specific inscriptional association to identify the correct saint.

126.s: Rama Raya was the de facto ruler of Vijayanagara while serving as regent for which nominal king?
126.x: Aliya Rama Raya ruled as regent for the nominal king Sadasiva Raya from 1543 onward.
126.tq: Distinguish the nominal sovereign from the actual power-holder.

126.s: Which policy best describes Rama Raya’s approach towards the Deccan Sultans?
o: He formed a permanent confederacy with all the Sultans against Golconda.
He accepted the supremacy of Ahmadnagar in all Deccan affairs.
He played the Sultans against one another to advance Vijayanagara interests.
He maintained permanent neutrality and avoided all alliances.
126.x: Rama Raya exploited rivalries among the Deccan Sultans, supporting different states at different times for Vijayanagara’s advantage.
126.tq: Identify the governing strategy from the sequence of changing alliances.

126.s:
Consider the following statements about Rama Raya’s Deccan policy:
1. In 1546–47, he supported Ahmadnagar against Bijapur and Bidar.
2. He acquired the Raichur doab during that phase.
3. From 1557 to 1563, he supported Bijapur and razed Ahmadnagar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
126.x: All three statements correctly describe Rama Raya’s shifting alliances and territorial policy in the Deccan.
126.tq: Track the dates and changing allies carefully; the reversal of alliances is the key trap.

126.s: What was the Turka Vada established by Rama Raya?
126.x: Rama Raya established a Muslim quarter known as the Turka Vada.
126.tq: Discriminate between a place-name and administrative or military terminology.

126.s: Who was the guru of Rama Raya?
126.x: Tatacharya was the guru of Rama Raya.
126.tq: Match the ruler with the associated religious teacher.

126.s: Who arranged the grant associated with Madras during the post-Talikota period?
126.x: Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka, the Kalahasti-Wandiwash chief, arranged the Madras grant.
126.tq: Use the office and place association to identify the responsible Nayaka.

126.s: Which pair of leaders won the Battle of Toppur in 1616?
o: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore
Mir Jumla and Sriranga Raya III
Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka and Veerappa Nayaka
126.x: Velugoti Yachama Nayaka and Raghunatha of Tanjore won the Battle of Toppur in 1616.
126.tq: Start with the battle year and match the associated victorious commanders.

126.s: At Gandikota in 1657, who is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon?
126.x: Mir Jumla of Golconda is recorded as having melted temple idols into cannon at Gandikota in 1657.
126.tq: Link the place and year with the named military commander.

126.s: A 1605 inscription at Siddhavatam fort in Kadapa records which event?
o: Mir Jumla melting temple idols into cannon
Tirumala Raya being crowned as founder of the dynasty
Matli Ananta building the fort walls under Venkatapati II
Rama Raya establishing the Turka Vada
126.x: The 1605 Siddhavatam inscription records that Matli Ananta built the fort walls during the reign of Venkatapati II.
126.tq: Use the inscription’s date and location to identify the recorded construction activity.

126.s: Who was the last ruler of the Aravidu dynasty?
126.x: Sriranga Raya III was the last Aravidu ruler. He was defeated at Vandavasi in 1642 and died in 1680, marking the end of the empire.
126.tq: Identify the final ruler through the succession sequence and terminal date.

126.s: Sriranga Raya III was defeated at Vandavasi in 1642 by whom?
