137.tq: Identify the broad architectural classification rather than a monument-specific feature.

137.s:
Which of the following features is associated with Mughal architecture?
1. Use of red sandstone and white marble
2. Charbagh planning
3. Double domes
4. Pietra dura and calligraphy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: Mughal architecture is marked by red sandstone and white marble, charbagh layouts, double domes, pietra dura and calligraphic decoration.
137.tq: Recognise the complete cluster of characteristic architectural features.

137.s: The architectural synthesis represented by Mughal monuments primarily blended which traditions?
137.x: Mughal architecture blended Persian, Timurid and Indian architectural elements.
137.tq: Test the exact components of a cultural synthesis without confusing them with general influences.

137.s: Pietra dura first appeared in Mughal architecture during the reign of which ruler?
137.x: Pietra dura first appeared under Jahangir, although it became especially prominent in later Mughal monuments.
137.tq: Use the first-appearance clue rather than the monument most popularly associated with the feature.

137.s: Which of the following is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition?
137.x: Bibi ka Maqbara is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition.
137.tq: Distinguish the terminal example from the first example in an architectural sequence.

137.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga from Mughal open-court mosques?
o: It follows a charbagh garden plan, unlike Mughal tombs
It is built entirely of white marble, unlike all Mughal mosques
It has no domes, unlike every Mughal mosque
It has a fully covered courtyard, unlike the open-court pattern of Mughal mosques
137.x: The Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga is notable for its fully covered courtyard, whereas Mughal mosques generally followed an open-court arrangement.
137.tq: Focus on the precise structural contrast rather than broad stylistic similarities.

137.s: Charminar, constructed in 1591, is associated with which dynasty and ruler?
o: Qutb Shahi dynasty and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Bahmani dynasty and Ahmad Shah Wali
137.x: Charminar was constructed in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
137.tq: Avoid the dynasty-swapping trap by linking the monument, date and ruler.

137.s:
Which of the following statements about Qutb Shahi monuments is correct?
1. Charminar displays Persian arches with Deccani stucco.
2. Golconda Fort is associated with an acoustic warning system and piped water.
3. Qutb Shahi tombs at Ibrahim Bagh have onion domes on square bases and are set in gardens.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
137.x: All three statements are correct. These features illustrate the distinctive architectural and engineering achievements of the Qutb Shahi period.
137.tq: Group related regional examples and test whether each feature is accurately assigned.

137.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutb Shahi tombs — onion domes on square bases in gardens
Golconda Fort — acoustic warning system and piped water
Charminar — Persian arches with Deccani stucco
137.x: Charminar is not a fully covered courtyard mosque; that feature is associated with the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga. The other pairs are correctly matched.
137.tq: Reject the option that imports a distinctive feature from a different monument.

137.s: Which of the following monuments is a common distractor when identifying Mughal architectural monuments but is actually a Qutb Shahi work?
137.x: Charminar is a Qutb Shahi monument of Hyderabad, not a Mughal monument. Humayun's Tomb, the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort belong to the Mughal architectural tradition.
137.tq: Separate Mughal monuments from the nearby Deccan Qutb Shahi example.

137.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a current legal development:
1. The Allahabad High Court issued notices to the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India.
2. The notices related to a petition challenging an Agra court's refusal to permit a survey of the Taj Mahal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
137.x: Both statements are correct. The Allahabad High Court issued notices in connection with the petition challenging the Agra court's refusal to allow a survey of the Taj Mahal.
137.tq: Link the authority, legal action and subject of the petition without reversing the procedural sequence.

137.s:
Which of the following correctly presents the chronological order of the specified architectural developments?
A. Ram Bagh
B. Charminar
C. First appearance of pietra dura under Jahangir
D. Inclusion of the Taj Mahal among the New Seven Wonders
137.x: Ram Bagh belongs to Babur's period, followed by Charminar in 1591, the first appearance of pietra dura under Jahangir, and the Taj Mahal's inclusion among the New Seven Wonders in 2007.
137.tq: Place the dated event first, then arrange the dynastic and modern milestones.

138.s:
Who among the following Persian masters was brought to India by Humayun and helped lay the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
1. Mir Sayyid Ali
2. Abdus Samad
3. Ustad Mansur
4. Basawan
138.x: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad were the two Persian masters brought by Humayun. Ustad Mansur and Basawan belonged to the later Mughal painting tradition.
138.tq: Identify the two associated names before eliminating painters from later reigns.

138.s: The Mughal school of painting gradually developed from Persian miniature painting into which type of style?
o: A geometric style based exclusively on Central Asian art
A symbolic style without human figures
A purely religious and monochromatic style
138.x: The style gradually moved from Persian miniature painting towards a realistic and colourful Indian style.
138.tq: Choose the precise description of the artistic transition rather than an extreme or exclusive alternative.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Emperor)
a. Humayun
b. Akbar
c. Jahangir
d. Shah Jahan

List-II (Emphasis)
i. Formal court scenes, albums and floral borders
ii. Foundation through Persian masters
iii. Illustrated manuscripts and a large painting atelier
iv. Portraits, albums, flora, fauna and naturalism

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
138.x: Humayun is associated with the Persian masters; Akbar with illustrated manuscripts; Jahangir with naturalism; and Shah Jahan with formal court scenes and floral decoration.
138.tq: Start from the sure pair and match the distinctive artistic emphasis of each emperor.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's painting atelier:
1. It was known as the Tasvir Khana.
2. It had more than 100 painters.
3. It produced illustrated versions of the Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama and Razmnama.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Akbar's Tasvir Khana was a large atelier of more than 100 painters and worked on the listed illustrated manuscripts.
138.tq: Check whether all the components of the atelier description belong to the same reign.

138.s: The Hamzanama, depicting the tales of Amir Hamza, was a major illustrated project of the atelier of which Mughal emperor?
138.x: The Hamzanama was a huge illustrated project undertaken in Akbar's atelier.
138.tq: Use the emperor–project association to distinguish Akbar's manuscript programme from later court painting.

138.s: Which one of the following features is most characteristic of Jahangir's painting tradition?
o: Portraits, albums, flora and fauna, and refined naturalism
Exclusive use of floral borders with heavy gold decoration
Large-scale manuscript illustration as the principal emphasis
Withdrawal of imperial patronage and dispersal of painters
138.x: Jahangir's period represented the zenith of Mughal painting, especially in portraiture, albums, flora, fauna and naturalistic representation.
138.tq: Match the most distinctive cluster of features with Jahangir's reign.

138.s: The introduction of the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head in Mughal painting is associated with the reign of:
138.x: Jahangir's painters introduced the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head, reflecting the period's refined and naturalistic style.
138.tq: Test a distinctive visual innovation against neighbouring emperors.

138.s:
With reference to Shah Jahan's painting tradition, consider the following statements:
1. Formal court scenes were prominent.
2. Albums called muraqqas received attention.
3. Floral borders and extensive use of gold were characteristic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three features are associated with Shah Jahan's formal and richly decorative painting tradition.
138.tq: Verify each element of a reign-wise art profile before selecting the coded combination.

138.s:
The withdrawal of imperial patronage to painters during the reign of Aurangzeb contributed to the growth of painting centres in which of the following regions?
1. Rajasthan
2. Punjab Hills
3. Bihar
4. Bengal
138.x: Painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar after Aurangzeb withdrew patronage. Bengal is not included in this association.
138.tq: Find the one geographically added region that does not belong to the stated dispersal pattern.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basawan — Jahangir's specialist in flora and fauna
Ustad Mansur — Akbar's leading manuscript illustrator
138.x: Abdus Samad was a Persian master associated with Humayun and Akbar and was given the title Shirin Qalam. Ustad Mansur was associated with Jahangir and Basawan with Akbar.
138.tq: Use the title–painter association while rejecting swapped reigns and specialities.

138.s: Ustad Mansur is particularly associated with which aspect of Mughal painting?
138.x: Ustad Mansur, a painter of Jahangir's court, was renowned for depicting flora and fauna.
138.tq: Separate a painter's artistic speciality from literary and architectural activities.

138.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manohar was the son of Basawan.
2. Manohar was associated with portrait painting in the Akbar–Jahangir period.
3. Basawan was one of the leading masters of Akbar's court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Manohar, the son of Basawan, worked in the Akbar–Jahangir period and was known for portraits, while Basawan was a leading Akbar-era master.
138.tq: Link family relationship, artistic speciality and reign without confusing the two painters.

138.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Akbarnama is correct?
o: It was written by Khafi Khan during Aurangzeb's reign.
It consists of three volumes, the third being the Ain-i-Akbari.
It is a critical account of Akbar's religious policy by Badauni.
It was written by Jahangir as his autobiography.
138.x: The Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in three volumes, with the third volume known as the Ain-i-Akbari.
138.tq: Use the volume relationship to distinguish closely related Mughal works and authors.

138.s: The Ain-i-Akbari is best described as:
o: A biography of Aurangzeb's first ten years
A detailed administrative report of Akbar's empire
138.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, the third volume of the Akbarnama, provides a detailed account of Akbar's administration and empire.
138.tq: Identify the work by its function rather than by the emperor associated with its subject.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)
a. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
b. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
c. Padshahnama
d. Alamgirnama

List-II (Author)
i. Abdul Hamid Lahori
ii. Mirza Muhammad Kazim
iii. Nizamuddin Ahmad
iv. Abdul Qadir Badauni

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
138.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad; Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh by Badauni; Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori; and Alamgirnama by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.
138.tq: Start with the sure chronicle–author pair and eliminate codes with swapped Mughal writers.

138.s: Which one of the following authors wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, a work critical of Akbar's religious policy?
138.x: Abdul Qadir Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, which was critical of Akbar's religious policy.
138.tq: Apply the author–work association while distinguishing Badauni from Abul Fazl.

138.s: The attribution of Tabaqat-i-Akbari to which of the following writers is correct?
138.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Abdul Qadir Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
138.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused Mughal historical works and their authors.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
138.x: Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote the Padshahnama. Alamgirnama was written by Mirza Muhammad Kazim, Futuhat-i-Alamgiri by Ishwardas Nagar, and Muntakhab-ul-Lubab by Khafi Khan.
138.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among several author substitutions.

138.s: Alamgirnama, dealing with the first ten years of Aurangzeb's reign, was written by:
138.x: Mirza Muhammad Kazim wrote the Alamgirnama, which covers the first ten years of Aurangzeb's reign.
138.tq: Use the chronological coverage of the work to identify its author among neighbouring chroniclers.

138.s: Who wrote Futuhat-i-Alamgiri?
138.x: Futuhat-i-Alamgiri was written by Ishwardas Nagar and deals with Aurangzeb's reign.
138.tq: Test the exact author of a less frequently recalled Mughal chronicle.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal literary works:
1. The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is an autobiography.
2. Jahangir patronised the dictionary Farhang-i-Jahangiri.
3. The Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, patronised Farhang-i-Jahangiri, and Khafi Khan wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab.
138.tq: Combine related literary facts while checking that each author and work belongs to the correct period.

138.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Tuzuk-i-Baburi from the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
o: The former is Akbar's administrative report, whereas the latter is Badauni's chronicle.
The former is Babur's memoir, whereas the latter is Jahangir's autobiography.
Both are administrative reports written by Abul Fazl.
Both are Persian translations of the Mahabharata.
138.x: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, or Baburnama, is Babur's memoir, while the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is Jahangir's autobiography.
138.tq: Separate two similar titles by identifying their respective imperial authors and genres.

138.s: Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, mentions Diwali and compares it with which festival?
138.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated 1590, mentions Diwali and compares it with Shab-e-baraat.
138.tq: Link the date and the specific comparative cultural reference instead of choosing a generally associated festival.

138.s: The term 'Rekhta', in the context of the rise of Urdu, refers to a linguistic development involving the combination of:
138.x: Rekhta developed through the combination of Persian, Hindi and regional dialects, contributing to the rise of Urdu.
138.tq: Identify the constituent languages of a composite linguistic tradition without adding unrelated classical languages.

138.s: Tansen, who became one of the Navaratnas of Akbar, was originally known as
138.x: Tansen's original name was Ramtanu Pande. He first served at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court.
138.tq: Use the exact-name distinction to reject the look-alike personal name.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baiju Bawra — Court of Raja Man Singh Tomar
Baz Bahadur — Court musician of Akbar from the beginning of his career
138.x: Baz Bahadur was the Sultan of Malwa, famed for his association with Rupmati. He was defeated by Akbar's forces in 1561 and served Akbar later.
138.tq: Find the swapped role and sequence in the incorrectly matched pair.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Tansen:
1. He first served in the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa.
2. He was given the title ‘Mian’.
3. He was one of Akbar’s Navaratnas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Tansen moved from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa's court to Akbar's court and was honoured with the title ‘Mian’.
138.tq: Test the whole biographical chain rather than relying on a single association.

138.s: Baiju Bawra was associated with which of the following courts as a Dhrupad singer?
o: The court of Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
The court of Muhammad Shah at Delhi
The court of Abdullah Qutb Shah at Golconda
The court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa
138.x: Baiju Bawra was a Dhrupad singer at the court of Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior.
138.tq: Match the musician with the specific patron and court.

138.s: Which one of the following musical forms is correctly matched with its Mughal-era patronage?
o: Tappa — Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
138.x: Khayal flourished at the court of Muhammad Shah ‘Rangeela’, particularly through Sadarang and Adarang. Dhrupad was associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar, while Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan.
138.tq: Start from the sure form–court association and eliminate the swapped pairs.

138.s: Who among the following refined Tappa in the late eighteenth-century Awadh–Lucknow milieu?
138.x: Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan in the late eighteenth-century Awadh–Lucknow milieu.
138.tq: Distinguish the composer associated with Tappa from those associated with Khayal.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about music under Aurangzeb:
1. Aurangzeb ended court music.
2. His reign witnessed the production of several Persian works on classical music.
3. Aurangzeb himself played the veena.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Although Aurangzeb ended court music, Persian treatises on classical music were produced during his reign, and he played the veena.
138.tq: Recognise the apparent contradiction between royal policy and developments during the same reign.

138.s: Akbar’s Maktab Khana was located at
138.x: The Maktab Khana was a translation bureau established by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri.
138.tq: Test the institution–location pair directly.

138.s: The principal purpose of Akbar’s Maktab Khana was to
o: train cavalry officers in Persian military terminology
promote cross-cultural understanding among the nobility
prepare revenue records in regional languages
teach only Islamic jurisprudence to court officials
138.x: The Maktab Khana was created as a translation bureau to promote cross-cultural understanding among the nobility.
138.tq: Identify the institutional objective from the function described.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
138.x: Badauni translated the Valmiki Ramayana into Persian during Akbar's reign. Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda, Faizi translated Lilavati, and Nizamuddin Panipati translated Jog Bashisht.
138.tq: Start from the sure translator–work pair and reject the swapped names.

138.s: Lilavati, translated into Persian during Akbar’s reign, was originally a work on
138.x: Lilavati was Bhaskaracharya's mathematical work, translated into Persian by Faizi during Akbar's reign.
138.tq: Use the original-text subject to distinguish translated works with similar religious associations.

138.s: Who translated the Yoga Vasistha into Persian for Prince Salim during Akbar’s reign?
138.x: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yoga Vasistha, known as Jog Bashisht, for Prince Salim during Akbar's reign.
138.tq: Link the translator to both the Persian title and the intended royal recipient.

138.s: Which of the following was translated into Persian by Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi during Akbar’s reign?
138.x: Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda into Persian during Akbar's reign.
138.tq: Discriminate among closely grouped translation projects by translator.

138.s: The earlier Persian rendering of the Panchatantra was known as
138.x: The Panchatantra was earlier rendered into Persian under the title Kalila wa Dimna.
138.tq: Distinguish an earlier translation precedent from Akbar-period translation projects.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
138.x: Keshavdas wrote Ramchandrika, Kavipriya, Rasikpriya and Ratan Bavani; Ram Rasayan is not listed among his works here.
138.tq: Use the single false title among a cluster of genuine poet–work pairs.

138.s: Keshavdas was associated with the
o: court of Shah Jahan at Agra
court of Muhammad Shah at Delhi
court of Abdullah Qutb Shah at Golconda
138.x: Keshavdas was associated with the Bundela court of Orchha and wrote works including Ramchandrika, Kavipriya and Rasikpriya.
138.tq: Match the Hindi poet with his regional court rather than a Mughal emperor.

138.s: Kavindracharya Saraswati is associated with which one of the following achievements?
o: Persuading Shah Jahan to remit the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag
Writing the Persian translation of the Baburnama
138.x: Kavindracharya Saraswati obtained Shah Jahan's remission of the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag and wrote Kavindra-kalpalata in Hindi.
138.tq: Identify the patronage-related achievement rather than confusing it with translation work.

138.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Hindi literary figures of the Mughal age is correct?
1. Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas.
2. Tulsidas was a court poet of Akbar.
3. Surdas wrote Sur Sagar.
4. Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana composed Hindi dohas.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Tulsidas belonged to Akbar's age but was not a court poet of Akbar.
138.tq: Separate a poet’s period from formal court membership.

138.s: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana is correctly associated with
o: Hindi dohas and a Persian translation of the Baburnama
Kavindra-kalpalata and the remission of pilgrim tax
138.x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana composed Hindi dohas and translated the Baburnama into Persian. He was a Navaratna of Akbar.
138.tq: Combine the author’s two literary contributions to avoid a single-clue guess.

138.s: Majma-ul-Bahrain, written by Dara Shikoh, deals primarily with the
o: development of Urdu in Mughal cantonments
common ground between Sufism and Vedanta
military campaigns of Shah Jahan in Central Asia
administrative systems of the Mughals and Safavids
138.x: Majma-ul-Bahrain, meaning ‘Mingling of the Two Oceans’, explores the common ground between Sufism and Vedanta.
138.tq: Use the title’s conceptual meaning to identify the subject of the work.

138.s: The Latin version of Dara Shikoh’s Sirr-i-Akbar was prepared by
138.x: Anquetil-Duperron prepared a Latin version of Sirr-i-Akbar, helping take the Upanishads to Europe.
138.tq: Distinguish the European transmitter from Mughal translators and chroniclers.

138.s: Niccolao Manucci is associated with which of the following?
o: Refining Tappa at the court of Muhammad Shah
Writing Tuti Nama in the court of Abdullah Qutb Shah
Translating the Mahabharata in Akbar’s Maktab Khana
Serving in Dara Shikoh’s artillery before writing Storia do Mogor
138.x: Niccolao Manucci served in Dara Shikoh's artillery and later wrote Storia do Mogor.
138.tq: Match the foreign chronicler with his service and literary work.

138.s: Which language did Babur use for his writings?
138.x: Babur wrote in Turki, whereas Persian served as the Mughal court and administrative language.
138.tq: Separate the emperor’s literary language from the empire’s administrative language.

138.s: Urdu developed historically through the stages represented by which sequence?
138.x: The development is described as Hindavi followed by Rekhta, Lashkari and Urdu. Urdu grew in military camps and bazaars.
138.tq: Arrange the successive names of the language in the stated historical sequence.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Urdu as characterised in the Mughal-period linguistic context?
o: It uses the Devanagari script and excludes local Prakrit influence.
It consists exclusively of Persian vocabulary and Persian grammar.
It developed only in royal courts and not in military camps or bazaars.
It uses the Perso-Arabic script and retains an indigenous grammar.
138.x: Urdu mixes Persian, Arabic, Turkic, local Prakrits and Braj, uses the Perso-Arabic script, and retains an indigenous grammar.
138.tq: Choose the precise composite description and reject exclusive claims.

138.s:
Which of the following languages or linguistic sources contributed to the formation of Urdu?
1. Persian
2. Arabic
3. Turkic
4. Local Prakrits and Braj
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Urdu developed through the interaction of Persian, Arabic, Turkic, local Prakrits and Braj, while retaining an indigenous grammatical base.
138.tq: Treat a composite linguistic-origin list as inclusive unless an element is expressly excluded.

138.s: Deccani Urdu received important patronage from the
138.x: The Qutb Shahis patronised Deccani Urdu in the Deccan.
138.tq: Match the regional language tradition with its ruling patronage.

138.s: Who was the first writer of Deccani poetry in Telangana?
138.x: Mulla Khiali was the first to write Deccani poetry in Telangana.
138.tq: Identify the pioneer rather than the later court poet associated with the same tradition.

138.s: The Golden Age of Urdu is associated with the reign of
138.x: The era of Abdullah Qutb Shah is described as the Golden Age of Urdu.
138.tq: Distinguish Deccani Urdu’s regional golden age from North Indian Mughal patronage.

138.s: Ghavvasi, the court poet associated with Deccani Urdu, wrote
138.x: Ghavvasi wrote Tuti Nama in 1657, rendering the Sanskrit Shuka Saptati.
138.tq: Link the regional court poet to his specific work and date.

138.s: Tuti Nama, written by Ghavvasi, is a rendering of the Sanskrit work
138.x: Ghavvasi's Tuti Nama, written in 1657, rendered the Sanskrit Shuka Saptati.
138.tq: Distinguish among Sanskrit source texts associated with different Persian translations.

138.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Khayal — Sadarang and Adarang
2. Tappa — Shori Miyan
3. Dhrupad — Tansen and Baiju Bawra
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: All three pairs are correct. Khayal flourished through Sadarang and Adarang, Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan, and Tansen and Baiju Bawra were masters of Dhrupad.
138.tq: Confirm each form–artist association before selecting the complete combination.

138.s: The Rajput school of painting primarily developed in which region?
o: Mughal provinces of Bengal and Bihar
Sub-Himalayan belt of Himachal and Jammu
138.x: The Rajput school emerged in the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan.
138.tq: Use the region-school association directly.

138.s: Which one of the following features is most closely associated with Rajput painting?
o: Bold colours, flat two-dimensional treatment and Hindu themes
Muted colours, deep perspective and European naturalism
Heavy use of gold and Persian court imagery
Exclusive depiction of battles fought in the Deccan
138.x: Rajput paintings are known for bold colours, a flat two-dimensional style, and subjects such as Hindu epics, love legends and daily life.
138.tq: Separate the indigenous and vivid Rajput style from Mughal naturalism.

138.s: The Pahari school of painting is associated with which of the following regions?
138.x: The Pahari school developed in the Sub-Himalayan belt, including Himachal, Jammu, Almora and Garhwal.
138.tq: Match the school with its geographical belt.

138.s:
With reference to the Pahari school of painting, consider the following statements:
1. It flourished mainly between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.
2. It was associated with the Sub-Himalayan region.
3. It originated in the Bahmani court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: The Pahari school flourished in the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries in the Sub-Himalayan region. Its association with the Bahmani court belongs to Deccani painting, not Pahari painting.
138.tq: Find the statement carrying the wrong school-origin association.

138.s: The Deccani school of painting began in the court of the
138.x: Deccani painting began in the Bahmani court and continued in the successor states of the Bahmani kingdom.
138.tq: Identify the institutional origin of the school.

138.s: Who is associated with the founding of the Deccani painting tradition at Golconda?
138.x: At Golconda, Mir Hashim is identified as the founder of the Deccani painting tradition; he was later invited to the Mughal court.
138.tq: Use the artist-founder association rather than the later Mughal connection.

138.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes Mughal painting from Rajput painting?
o: Mughal painting was indigenous and decorative, whereas Rajput painting was cosmopolitan and naturalistic.
Rajput painting alone reflected European influence and a cosmopolitan outlook.
Mughal painting generally used muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading, whereas Rajput painting was vivid and decorative.
Both schools used identical styles and differed only in the language of captions.
138.x: Mughal painting generally displayed muted naturalistic colours, perspective, shading and a cosmopolitan outlook, while Rajput painting was indigenous, vivid and decorative.
138.tq: Read both sides of the reversed comparison carefully.

138.s: Sherwani regarded the miniatures including the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi as the
o: first coloured miniatures of the Deccan
138.x: Historian Sherwani called the fourteen miniatures, including the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi, the Deccan's first coloured miniatures.
138.tq: Link the historian's assessment with the distinctive miniature group.

138.s:
Arrange the following Later Mughal rulers in chronological order of accession:
A. Farrukhsiyar
B. Bahadur Shah I
C. Shah Alam II
D. Jahandar Shah
138.x: The correct order is Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar and Shah Alam II.
138.tq: Fix the first and last rulers before arranging the middle reigns.

138.s: Which Later Mughal ruler released Shahu?
138.x: Bahadur Shah I, who reigned from 1707 to 1712, released Shahu.
138.tq: Associate the ruler with the specific administrative event.

138.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Farrukhsiyar is correct?
o: He ruled from 1719 to 1748 and faced Nadir Shah's invasion.
He was a puppet of the Sayyid brothers and gave the English duty-free trade in Bengal.
He was the last Mughal emperor and ruled from 1837 to 1857.
He released Shahu immediately after Aurangzeb's death.
138.x: Farrukhsiyar ruled from 1713 to 1719, was controlled by the Sayyid brothers, executed Banda Singh Bahadur in 1716, and granted the English duty-free trade in Bengal.
138.tq: Reject options that attach another Later Mughal's event to Farrukhsiyar.

138.s: Who among the following was known by the epithet 'Rangeela'?
138.x: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, was popularly known as Rangeela.
138.tq: Use the ruler-epithet pair directly.

138.s: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah was the founder of the independent state of
138.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah, also known as Chin Qilich Khan or Mir Qamar-ud-din Siddiqi, founded the Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad.
138.tq: Match the founder with the successor state.

138.s: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah held which Mughal offices before establishing the Asaf Jahi state?
o: Subedar of the Deccan and Wazir
Nawab of Carnatic and Mir Bakshi
Subedar of Bengal and Diwan of Awadh
Diwan of Bengal and Subedar of Gujarat
138.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk was Subedar of the Deccan and also served as Wazir in the Mughal administration.
138.tq: Distinguish the founder's Mughal offices from those of other successor-state founders.

138.s: Murshid Quli Khan first served in Bengal as its
o: Nawab under the Nizam and later Diwan
Subedar and later Nawab of Awadh
138.x: Murshid Quli Khan held the office of Diwan of Bengal and subsequently became its Subedar.
138.tq: Test the sequence of offices rather than only the state association.

138.s: The founder of the Carnatic state of Arcot was
138.x: Saadatullah Khan, also rendered as Saadullah Khan, founded the Carnatic state of Arcot and named his nephew Dost Ali as successor.
138.tq: Use the founder-name and regional-state association.

138.s: Hyderabad was first envisaged as a separate political entity by
138.x: The idea of Hyderabad was first envisaged by the Deccan viceroy Zulfiqar Khan, with Daud Khan, from 1708.
138.tq: Distinguish the original conception from the later founder.

138.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Nizam-ul-Mulk's role in the decline of Mughal central authority?
o: He helped the Sayyid brothers retain power and appointed Murshid Quli Khan as Diwan.
He helped overthrow the Sayyid brothers and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.
He founded Awadh after defeating Saadat Khan.
He was appointed Diwan of Bengal by Farrukhsiyar.
138.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk helped overthrow the Sayyid brothers and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.
138.tq: Identify the correct political alliance and appointment.

138.s: Nadir Shah invaded the Mughal Empire in
138.x: Nadir Shah of Persia invaded the Mughal Empire in 1739 and plundered Delhi.
138.tq: Separate the invasion years of Nadir Shah and Abdali.

138.s: Which one of the following was carried away by Nadir Shah from Delhi?
o: The Koh-i-Noor and the Jantar Mantar
The Red Fort and the Buland Darwaza
The Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne
The Taj Mahal and the Peacock Throne
138.x: After defeating Muhammad Shah at Karnal and plundering Delhi, Nadir Shah carried away the Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne.
138.tq: Group the two objects associated with the same invasion.

138.s: Nadir Shah defeated Muhammad Shah in the Battle of
138.x: Nadir Shah defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah at Karnal in 1739.
138.tq: Match the invader with the battle location.

138.s: Who wrote *India at the Death of Akbar*?
138.x: *India at the Death of Akbar* was written by W. H. Moreland.
138.tq: Match the title with its historian-author.

138.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fall of the Mughal Empire — M. Athar Ali
Early Travels in India, 1583-1619 — William Foster
Travels in the Mogul Empire, 1656-1668 — Francois Bernier
The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556-1707 — Irfan Habib
138.x: *Fall of the Mughal Empire* was written by Jadunath Sarkar. M. Athar Ali wrote *The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb*.
138.tq: Find the swapped author-title pair.

138.s: Who wrote *The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb*?
138.x: *The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb* was written by M. Athar Ali.
138.tq: Use direct book-author recall after separating the two similar Mughal studies.

138.s: *Travels in the Mogul Empire, 1656-1668* is associated with
138.x: Francois Bernier wrote the traveller's account *Travels in the Mogul Empire, 1656-1668*.
138.tq: Distinguish the traveller's account from modern historical studies.

138.s: Which of the following was a major consequence of Aurangzeb's Deccan wars?
o: They ended all Maratha resistance by 1689.
They drained the treasury because Aurangzeb spent about his last twenty-seven years campaigning in the Deccan.
They strengthened the Mughal treasury through uninterrupted revenue collection.
They led to the immediate abolition of the jagirdari system.
138.x: Aurangzeb spent approximately the last twenty-seven years of his reign campaigning in the Deccan against the Marathas, which drained the Mughal treasury.
138.tq: Connect prolonged military expenditure with financial decline.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Aurangzeb's Deccan policy:
1. Sambhaji was executed in 1689.
2. Rajaram operated from Jinji.
3. Tarabai continued resistance to the Mughals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Sambhaji was executed in 1689, Rajaram continued resistance from Jinji, and Tarabai also played an important role in continuing Maratha resistance.
138.tq: Accept the cluster of related Maratha resistance facts.

138.s: Aurangzeb's reimposition of jizya in 1679 particularly alienated the
138.x: The religious policy, including the reimposition of jizya in 1679, alienated important groups such as the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.
138.tq: Link the dated policy with the affected social and political groups.

138.s: The term 'be-jagiri' in the context of the Mughal decline refers to
o: The assignment of jagirs exclusively to Rajput nobles
The abolition of all mansabs by Aurangzeb
The conversion of jagirs into hereditary zamindaris
A situation in which too many mansabdars competed for too few revenue-yielding jagirs
138.x: The jagirdari crisis involved too many mansabdars and too few revenue-yielding jagirs, a condition described as be-jagiri, which weakened the mansabdari system.
138.tq: Interpret the administrative term through its structural cause.

138.s: Who among the following constituted the Sayyid Brothers?
o: Murshid Quli Khan and Puran Chand
Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan
138.x: The Sayyid Brothers were Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan.
138.tq: Recall the two-member composition of the kingmakers' group.

138.s: The Sayyid Brothers are known in Mughal history as kingmakers mainly because they
o: founded Hyderabad and Bengal as independent states during Aurangzeb's reign
abolished the mansabdari system and introduced the jagirdari system
controlled Jahandar Shah and Farrukhsiyar and installed puppet successors after deposing Farrukhsiyar in 1719
defeated Nadir Shah at Karnal and restored Muhammad Shah
138.x: The Sayyid Brothers controlled Jahandar Shah and Farrukhsiyar, deposed Farrukhsiyar in 1719 and installed puppet successors.
138.tq: Identify the power relationship rather than merely the names.

138.s: Which Mughal noble helped overthrow the Sayyid Brothers?
138.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk helped overthrow the Sayyid Brothers and subsequently became a major figure in the formation of the Hyderabad state.
138.tq: Match the political opponent with the kingmakers' downfall.

138.s: Which of the following sets correctly identifies the broader factors contributing to the decline of the Mughal Empire?
o: Weak successors, noble factions, regional powers, Marathas and foreign invasions
Strong successors, united nobles, decline of regional powers and absence of invasions
Only European trade and the growth of Rajput painting
Only the abolition of jizya and the expansion of Mughal jagirs
138.x: The decline was also accelerated by weak successors, Turani, Irani and Hindustani noble factions, the rise of regional powers and the Marathas, and invasions by Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
138.tq: Select the option that combines the multiple structural causes without an extreme restriction.

138.s: The translation movement, Persian-Indian painting and the development of Hindavi and Urdu together contributed to the growth of which cultural formation?
138.x: The interaction of translation, painting and Hindavi-Urdu literature helped create a composite Indo-Persian culture.
138.tq: Identify the broad cultural consequence of several connected developments.

138.s:
With reference to the Qutb Shahi kingdom, consider the following statements:
1. Persian was the official language.
2. Telugu was the language of the people.
3. Deccani painting and Deccani Urdu flourished under the Qutb Shahis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Persian served as the official language, Telugu was widely used by the people, and Deccani painting and Deccani Urdu developed under Qutb Shahi patronage.
138.tq: Combine language, society and art statements and check whether all belong to the same regional polity.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the development of culture under the Qutb Shahis?
o: Kuchipudi — growth associated with Siddhendra Yogi
Deccani Urdu — language prohibited in the Qutb Shahi court
Telugu — official language of the Qutb Shahi kingdom
Persian — language used only by village communities
138.x: The growth of Kuchipudi is associated with Siddhendra Yogi. Persian was the official language, Telugu was the people's language, and Deccani Urdu flourished rather than being prohibited.
138.tq: Use the correctly matched person and cultural development to eliminate reversed language claims.

138.s: Who granted the village of Kuchipudi to its dancers?
138.x: Abul Hasan Tana Shah granted the village of Kuchipudi to its dancers. Siddhendra Yogi is associated with the growth of Kuchipudi.
138.tq: Distinguish the patron from the cultural figure associated with the art form.

138.s: Who was the first Mughal ruler to bring Persian painters to India?
138.x: Humayun was the first Mughal ruler to bring Persian painters to India.
138.tq: Test a FIRST association directly and distinguish the initiating ruler from later patrons.

138.s: The halo motif first appeared prominently in Mughal painting during the reign of which ruler?
138.x: The halo motif first appeared in Mughal painting under Jahangir.
138.tq: Use the FIRST/LAST clue to distinguish successive Mughal phases of painting.

138.s:
Assertion (A): Aurangzeb's reign witnessed a withdrawal of imperial patronage from Mughal painting and music.
Reason (R): Aurangzeb withdrew patronage from both painting and music.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
138.x: Both statements are true, and the withdrawal of patronage from painting and music directly explains the assertion about Aurangzeb's reign.
138.tq: Check whether the reason directly restates and explains the asserted historical relationship.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
138.x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj, whereas Tabaqat-i-Akbari is associated with Nizamuddin Ahmad.
138.tq: Separate two similarly titled historical works by matching each with its correct author.

138.s: A Public Interest Litigation in the Bombay High Court was associated with which issue?
o: The withdrawal of Persian as the official language of the Qutb Shahi kingdom
The transfer of Kuchipudi village to the Mughal administration
The prohibition of Deccani painting in Mughal India
The removal of a map of the Maratha Empire from a revised NCERT textbook
138.x: The PIL followed the removal of a Maratha Empire map from a revised NCERT textbook.
138.tq: Link a current legal development with the precise historical-textbook issue involved.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Marathas after 1707:
1. They held sway from Attock to Cuttack.
2. Their control over Rajputana involved tribute in the form of chauth rather than complete annexation.
3. Their expansion after 1707 was confined exclusively to the Deccan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Maratha influence after 1707 extended far beyond the Deccan, from Attock to Cuttack.
138.tq: Reject the geographically restrictive statement by contrasting the stated extent of expansion.

138.s: Aurangzeb annexed Golconda on which date, when it became the twenty-first Suba?
138.x: Golconda was annexed by Aurangzeb on 3 October 1687 and was incorporated as the twenty-first Suba.
138.tq: Use the exact date and distinguish adjacent-year distractors.

138.s: Who among the following took part in Aurangzeb's siege of Golconda?
138.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk took part in the siege of Golconda. The other figures are associated with Kuchipudi or Persian historical writing.
138.tq: Identify the military participant while separating him from literary and cultural personalities.

138.s: Which one of the following statements about Qutb Shahi painting is correct?
o: It formed an independent Deccani school associated with Mir Hashim.
It began only after the decline of the Qutb Shahi kingdom.
It was confined exclusively to Sanskrit manuscripts.
It was merely a direct copy of the Mughal style and had no independent character.
138.x: Qutb Shahi Deccani painting, associated with Mir Hashim, developed as an independent school rather than as a mere copy of Mughal painting.
138.tq: Spot the precise school-and-artist association and reject absolute words such as “merely” and “exclusively”.

138.s: The dispersal of Mughal painters contributed significantly to the rise of which schools of painting?
138.x: The dispersal of Mughal painters helped in the emergence and growth of the Rajput and Pahari schools of painting.
138.tq: Identify the cultural consequence of the dispersal of artists rather than the original imperial school.

139.s: Bahadur Shah I, who succeeded Aurangzeb, is also known by which epithet?
139.x: Bahadur Shah I, also known as Muazzam, was given the epithet Shah-i-Bekhabar.
139.tq: Use direct epithet recall and distinguish it from the epithets of later Mughal rulers.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Jahandar Shah:
1. He was known by the epithet ‘Lampat’.
2. He was supported by Wazir Zulfiqar Khan.
3. He ruled under the influence of Lal Kunwar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Jahandar Shah was called Lampat, was backed by Zulfiqar Khan and remained under the sway of his mistress Lal Kunwar.
139.tq: Combine three closely related facts about one ruler and identify the complete set.

139.s: Jahandar Shah met which fate after his brief reign?
o: He was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyids.
He was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857.
He was blinded and pensioned by the Company.
He died in office after appointing a successor.
139.x: Jahandar Shah was deposed and killed by Farrukh Siyar and the Sayyid brothers.
139.tq: Test the fate of a ruler through a person-and-event association.

139.s: Farrukh Siyar issued the farman favourable to the English East India Company in which year?
139.x: Farrukh Siyar issued the important farman granting favourable trading privileges to the Company in 1717.
139.tq: Use numerical discrimination among closely spaced years in the Later Mughal period.

139.s: Which of the following correctly describes the fate of Farrukh Siyar?
o: He was murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk in 1759.
He was blinded, deposed and killed by the Sayyids in 1719.
He died in office after releasing Shahu.
He was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla in 1788.
139.x: Farrukh Siyar was blinded, deposed and killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719.
139.tq: Distinguish similar violent ends of different Later Mughal emperors.

139.s: Who among the following was popularly known as ‘Rangeela’?
139.x: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, was known as Rangeela.
139.tq: Directly identify the ruler associated with a well-known epithet.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Shah:
1. He got rid of the Sayyid brothers with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk.
2. Nizam-ul-Mulk, Saadat Khan and Murshid Quli Khan became autonomous during his reign.
3. Nadir Shah invaded India during his reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Muhammad Shah eliminated the Sayyid influence with Nizam-ul-Mulk’s help, witnessed the autonomy of major provincial rulers and faced Nadir Shah’s invasion in 1739.
139.tq: Check a ruler’s reign through political, provincial and invasion-related facts.

139.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Shah Alam II — Murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk
Alamgir II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Ahmad Shah — Blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk
Akbar II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
139.x: Ahmad Shah was blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk. The other fates belong respectively to Bahadur Shah II, Alamgir II and Shah Alam II.
139.tq: Find the correctly matched ruler and fate among closely related Later Mughal events.

139.s: Udham Bai, who exercised control during the reign of Ahmad Shah, bore which honorific title?
139.x: Udham Bai, who controlled affairs during Ahmad Shah’s reign, was honoured with the title Qibla-i-Alam.
139.tq: Test an official title associated with a specific court personality.

139.s: Which of the following developments took place during the reign of Alamgir II?
o: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 and Abdali invasions continued.
Ram Mohan Roy received the title Raja.
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought and Buxar was won.
The Company granted pension to the first Mughal pensioner.
139.x: Repeated invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Battle of Plassey in 1757 occurred during Alamgir II’s reign.
139.tq: Associate events with the correct reign instead of relying only on chronology.

139.s: With reference to Shah Alam II, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: He was the first Mughal ruler to release Shahu.
He became the first Mughal pensioner of the Company.
He was killed by the Sayyid brothers in 1719.
He gave Raja title to Ram Mohan Roy.
139.x: Shah Alam II became the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company. He witnessed the Third Battle of Panipat and the Battle of Buxar during his reign.
139.tq: Separate the defining political position of Shah Alam II from facts belonging to other rulers.

139.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bahadur Shah II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Shah Alam II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
Akbar II — Gave Ram Mohan Roy the title ‘Raja’
Muhammad Shah — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
139.x: Muhammad Shah was not exiled to Rangoon. Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857; Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla.
139.tq: Find the mismatched ruler and fate by eliminating well-known correct associations.

139.s: Bahadur Shah II, also called Zafar, died in which year after his exile to Rangoon?
139.x: Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after 1857 and died there in 1862.
139.tq: Distinguish the year of exile-related events from the year of death.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II returned to Delhi under the protection of Mahadji Scindia.
2. He returned to Delhi in 1771–72.
3. Before returning, he lived at Allahabad under Company protection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Alam II lived at Allahabad under Company protection and returned to Delhi in 1771–72 under Mahadji Scindia’s protection.
139.tq: Test a sequence of political circumstances rather than a single isolated date.

139.s: Murshid Quli Khan held which offices in Bengal?
139.x: Murshid Quli Khan first served as Diwan and later became Nazim of Bengal. He ruled Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
139.tq: Test the exact office held by a regional founder rather than merely the state associated with him.

139.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Muhammad Khan Bangash — Founder of Hyderabad
Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk — Subedar of Awadh
Ali Muhammad Khan — Nawab of Carnatic under the Nizam
139.x: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk became Subedar of Awadh in 1722 and founded the autonomous state of Awadh.
139.tq: Use founder-position matching and reject swaps among successor states.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Carnatic state:
1. Saadatullah Khan is associated with its foundation.
2. The Carnatic was also known as Arcot.
3. Saadatullah Khan named his nephew Dost Ali as successor without the Nizam’s approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Saadatullah Khan founded the Carnatic or Arcot state and named Dost Ali, his nephew, as successor without the Nizam’s approval.
139.tq: Combine name, alternate designation and succession details in one coded question.

139.s: Who among the following carved out Rohilkhand during the invasion of Nadir Shah?
139.x: Ali Muhammad Khan, an Afghan chief, carved out the state of Rohilkhand during Nadir Shah’s invasion.
139.tq: Identify the founder of a regional state through the circumstance of its emergence.

139.s: Muhammad Khan Bangash is associated with the foundation of which regional state?
139.x: Muhammad Khan Bangash, described as an Afghan adventurer, founded Farrukhabad.
139.tq: Direct state-founder recall using nearby regional successor states as distractors.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Person)
a. Husain Ali Khan
a. Murshid Quli Khan
c. Chin Qilich Khan
d. Safdar Jung

List-II (Association)
i. Awadh
ii. Bengal
iii. Sayyid brother
iv. Nizam of Hyderabad

Which of the following is the correct code?
139.x: Husain Ali Khan was a Sayyid brother, Murshid Quli Khan was associated with Bengal, Chin Qilich Khan was the Nizam of Hyderabad and Safdar Jung was associated with Awadh.
139.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that repeat the wrong regional association.

139.s: The Sayyid brothers who acted as king-makers during the period 1713–1720 were:
o: Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan
Murshid Quli Khan and Ali Muhammad Khan
139.x: The Sayyid brothers were Abdullah Khan, who served as Wazir, and Husain Ali Khan, who served as Mir Bakhshi.
139.tq: Distinguish the Sayyid king-makers from other powerful nobles of the period.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Sayyid brothers is NOT correct?
o: Husain Ali Khan was the Mir Bakhshi.
They were eliminated during the reign of Farrukh Siyar in 1713.
They dominated Mughal politics from 1713 to 1720.
139.x: The Sayyid brothers were eliminated under Muhammad Shah; Husain Ali Khan was killed in 1720. They did not meet this fate during Farrukh Siyar’s reign in 1713.
139.tq: Use the NOT format to separate the period of their dominance from the period of their elimination.

139.s: Which of the following statements about the regional successor states is correct?
o: Nizam-ul-Mulk was initially the Subedar of the Deccan and later became Wazir.
Murshid Quli Khan founded Rohilkhand as an Afghan chief.
Muhammad Khan Bangash served as Subedar of Awadh in 1722.
Saadat Khan founded Bengal as its Diwan.
139.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk held the position of Subedar of the Deccan and later became Wazir. The other statements interchange the founders and offices of Bengal, Rohilkhand and Awadh.
139.tq: Test the position held by the founder and trap office-state reversals.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Awadh succession:
1. Safdar Jung was the nephew and son-in-law of Saadat Khan.
2. Safdar Jung became Nawab of Awadh and Wazir.
3. Shuja-ud-Daula, who came later, fought at the Battle of Buxar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Safdar Jung succeeded Saadat Khan in the specified family relationship and offices, and Shuja-ud-Daula later fought at Buxar.
139.tq: Test succession through relationship, office and a later military event.

139.s: Which of the following correctly describes the early development of Hyderabad?
o: It was first envisaged by Zulfiqar Khan, who governed through Daud Khan from 1708.
It was created by Ali Muhammad Khan during Abdali’s first raid.
It was founded by Murshid Quli Khan after the Battle of Buxar.
It was first envisaged by Saadat Khan as a province of Awadh.
139.x: Hyderabad was first envisaged by the Deccan viceroy Zulfiqar Khan, who governed through Daud Khan from 1708.
139.tq: Distinguish the initial conception of a state from the later founder traditionally associated with it.

139.s: Which one of the following statements about Nizam-ul-Mulk’s administration is correct?
o: He made Puran Chand his Diwan and followed a Mughal-type jagirdari administration.
He made Dost Ali his successor without the Nizam’s approval.
He governed Bengal through Murshid Quli Khan.
He abolished the jagirdari system and appointed Saadat Khan as Diwan.
139.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk was tolerant, appointed Puran Chand as his Diwan and administered Hyderabad through a Mughal-type jagirdari system.
139.tq: Apply administrative clues to identify the correct regional ruler.

139.s: Nadir Shah defeated the Mughal forces under Muhammad Shah at which place?
139.x: Nadir Shah defeated Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal in 1739 before sacking Delhi.
139.tq: Match the invader with the decisive battlefield and avoid swapping it with later battles.

139.s: Which one of the following correctly states the consequence of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s invasions?
o: Bengal and Bihar were ceded to him after the Battle of Karnal.
Punjab and Multan were ceded to him, and he repeatedly invaded during Alamgir II’s reign.
He established the autonomous state of Hyderabad with Puran Chand as Diwan.
He carried away the Peacock Throne after defeating Muhammad Shah at Karnal.
139.x: Punjab and Multan were ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali, and his repeated invasions occurred during the reign of Alamgir II. The other options describe Nadir Shah’s actions or Hyderabad’s administration.
139.tq: Distinguish the consequences and identities of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali.

139.s:
Assertion (A): The invasions of Ahmad Shah Abdali exposed the military weakness of the Mughal Empire.
Reason (R): They repeatedly challenged Mughal authority and drained the imperial treasury.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
139.x: Both statements are true, and the repeated invasions, military challenges and financial drain explain why Mughal weakness was exposed.
139.tq: Test whether the stated consequence logically explains the political impact of repeated invasions.

139.s: Who founded the Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad in 1724?
139.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi founded the Asaf Jahi state and became its first Nizam.
139.tq: Identify the founder directly and distinguish him from the early successors.

139.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
139.x: Aurangzeb conferred the title Chin Qilich Khan, Farrukh Siyar conferred Nizam-ul-Mulk, and Muhammad Shah conferred Asaf Jah in 1725.
139.tq: Start from the sure title-giver pair and eliminate the swapped authorities.

139.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the establishment of the Asaf Jahi state:
1. Farrukh Siyar appointed Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan as Mughal Governor of the Deccan.
2. He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda.
3. The independent Asaf Jahi state was established in 1748.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The state was established in 1724, not 1748; 1748 was the year of the founder's death.
139.tq: Find the changed date in the statement set.

139.s: The Battle of Shakar Kheda, which enabled the establishment of the virtually independent Hyderabad state, was fought in:
139.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda in 1724, the founding year of the Asaf Jahi state.
139.tq: Use the close-date discrimination method for founding year, title year and death year.

139.s: Which one of the following statements about the first Nizam is correct?
o: He accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
He kept the Marathas out of Hyderabad during his lifetime.
He was defeated at Shakar Kheda by Mubariz Khan.
139.x: The first Nizam kept the Marathas out during his lifetime. He died in 1748; the Subsidiary Alliance was accepted much later by Nizam Ali Khan.
139.tq: Separate the founder's achievements from those of the later Nizam Ali Khan.

139.s:
Arrange the following rulers of Hyderabad in chronological order of their accession:
A. Salabat Jung
B. Nasir Jung
C. Muzaffar Jung
D. Asaf Jah I
E. Nizam Ali Khan
Select the correct answer.
139.x: The order is Asaf Jah I (1724), Nasir Jung (1748), Muzaffar Jung (1750), Salabat Jung (1751), and Nizam Ali Khan (1762).
139.tq: Fix the first and last rulers, then arrange the closely spaced middle accessions.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
139.x: Nizam Ali Khan ruled from 1762 to 1803. The period 1751–1762 belonged to Salabat Jung.
139.tq: Check the ruler-period pair for a shifted succession date.

139.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Ruler)
a. Sikandar Jah
b. Nasir-ud-Daula
c. Afzal-ud-Daula
d. Mir Mahbub Ali Khan

List-II (Period of rule)
i. 1857–1869
ii. 1803–1829
iii. 1869–1911
iv. 1829–1857

Select the correct answer.
139.x: Sikandar Jah ruled from 1803–1829, Nasir-ud-Daula from 1829–1857, Afzal-ud-Daula from 1857–1869, and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan from 1869–1911.
139.tq: Start from the distinctive period of Mir Mahbub Ali Khan and complete the sequence.

139.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Asaf Jahi dynasty is correct?
o: Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union through Operation Polo in 1948.
Mir Osman Ali Khan ruled from 1869 to 1911.
The dynasty continued as the ruling power after 1948.
Nizam Ali Khan was the last Nizam of Hyderabad.
139.x: Operation Polo integrated Hyderabad State into the Indian Union in 1948. Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam.
139.tq: Distinguish the end of the dynasty from the end of individual rulers.

139.s: Who wrote both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire?
139.x: Jadunath Sarkar authored both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire.
139.tq: Match the historian with the distinctive pair of works.

139.s: The agrarian-crisis interpretation of Mughal decline, emphasising the over-exploitation of peasants and the resulting revolts, is associated with:
139.x: Irfan Habib explained the decline through an agrarian crisis in The Agrarian System of Mughal India (1963), arguing that over-exploitation of peasants provoked revolts.
139.tq: Link the interpretation to the historian rather than merely recalling the book title.

139.s: Which work is associated with Satish Chandra's explanation of the Mughal decline?
o: Parties and Politics at the Mughal Court, 1707–1740
139.x: Satish Chandra wrote Parties and Politics at the Mughal Court, 1707–1740 and associated decline with the jagirdari crisis.
139.tq: Use author–work discrimination among closely related historiographical titles.

139.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. M. Athar Ali — The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb
2. W. H. Moreland — India at the Death of Akbar
3. François Bernier — Travels in the Mogul Empire
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
139.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Athar Ali examined the Mughal nobility, Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar, and Bernier wrote Travels in the Mogul Empire.
139.tq: Verify each author–work pair before selecting the combined code.

139.s: M. Athar Ali attributed the worsening of the jagir shortage primarily to:
o: The transfer of all jagirs to European companies
The enlargement of the nobility through the inclusion of Deccanis and Marathas
The abolition of the mansabdari system by Farrukh Siyar
The decline of agriculture caused by Nadir Shah's raid
139.x: Athar Ali argued that the enlarged nobility, including Deccanis and Marathas, intensified the shortage of jagirs.
139.tq: Apply the historian's specific causal argument rather than choosing a general cause of decline.

139.s: François Bernier's explanation of Mughal decline emphasised that:
o: The empire collapsed mainly because of the Maratha naval power.
The jagirdari crisis resulted from too few nobles in the imperial service.
The absence of private property in land reduced the incentive for improvement and led towards ruin.
Aurangzeb's religious policy alone caused the complete collapse of agriculture.
139.x: Bernier associated the absence of private property in land with a lack of incentive to improve it and predicted ruin.
139.tq: Identify the precise argument attached to the named historian.

139.s: The revisionist interpretation of the eighteenth century views it chiefly as a period of:
o: Exclusive European control over the peasant surplus
Regional growth, with successor states controlling economic and law-and-order systems
Uninterrupted Mughal centralisation under weak successors
139.x: The revisionist view treats the eighteenth century as a period of regional growth. The new states managed their own economic and law-and-order systems and controlled peasant surplus.
139.tq: Contrast the revisionist regional-growth interpretation with the older collapse narrative.

139.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major cause of the decline of the Mughal Empire?
o: The invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali
The long Deccan wars and the resulting drain on the treasury
The strengthening of central authority by independent nobles
139.x: Independent nobles weakened, rather than strengthened, central authority. The Deccan wars, Maratha rise and invasions were among the major causes of decline.
139.tq: Find the reversed effect in a cause-of-decline option.

139.s: At its greatest extent under Aurangzeb, the Mughal Empire extended approximately from:
o: Kashmir to Jinji and the Hindukush to Chittagong
Kabul to Bijapur and Sindh to Assam
Punjab to Madurai and the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal
Delhi to the Narmada and Gujarat to Bengal
139.x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached from Kashmir to Jinji and from the Hindukush to Chittagong.
139.tq: Recall both geographical limits together instead of relying on one directional clue.

139.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Mughal decline:
1. Aurangzeb's long Deccan wars weakened the foundations of the empire and drained the treasury.
2. The Sayyids' control contributed to corruption and mismanagement.
3. Peasant and zamindar revolts followed the jagirdari and agrarian crises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Religious policies, prolonged warfare, factional noble politics, fiscal crisis and agrarian unrest combined to weaken the empire.
139.tq: Test cumulative causation by checking each internal cause separately.

139.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a cause of Mughal decline?
o: European companies — a factor contributing to the decline
Noble rivalries — weakening of central authority
Maratha rise — restoration of Mughal authority
Agrarian crisis — shrinkage of the fiscal base
139.x: The Maratha rise weakened Mughal authority; it did not restore it. Noble rivalries, agrarian crisis and European companies were associated with the decline.
139.tq: Watch for the reversed consequence in a cause-and-effect pair.

139.s: The Farman of 1717 issued by Farrukh Siyar is significant because it:
o: Granted chauth and sardeshmukhi to Shahu's agent
Exempted the English Company from customs duties in Bengal
Granted the Company Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
Transferred Kora and Allahabad to the Company
139.x: The Farman of 1717 exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal and was called the Company's Magna Carta.
139.tq: Distinguish the 1717 Farman from the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad.

139.s: The Mughal grant of 1719, issued through the Sayyids, granted to Balaji Vishwanath, as Shahu's agent:
o: Diwani rights in Bengal and Bihar
Kora and Allahabad with an annual payment
Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
139.x: The 1719 grant recognised Shahu's claim to chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Deccan subas through his agent Balaji Vishwanath.
139.tq: Separate the content of the 1719 grant from the later Company concessions.

139.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Treaty of Allahabad of 1765?
o: The Sayyids granted the Company chauth of the Deccan subas.
Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Farrukh Siyar exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal.
Akbar II granted the Company the title of Raja.
139.x: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The emperor received Kora and Allahabad and an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
139.tq: Identify the correct grantor and the precise territorial content of the treaty.

139.s:
With reference to the Treaty of Allahabad, consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II received Kora and Allahabad.
2. The emperor was entitled to an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
3. Warren Hastings continued this annual payment without interruption after 1772.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. From 1772 Warren Hastings stopped the annual grant and sold Kora and Allahabad to the Nawab of Awadh.
139.tq: Use the date-based exception to identify the false continuation claim.

139.s: The decline of the Mughal Empire created a power vacuum that was successively filled by:
o: Regional states, the Marathas and finally the East India Company
The Rajputs, the Sikhs and the Portuguese
The Mughals, the Marathas and the Ottoman Empire
The Sayyids, the Afghans and the French alone
139.x: The decline opened space for regional successor states, the Marathas and ultimately the East India Company.
139.tq: Recall the broad political sequence following imperial decline.

139.s: The Diwani granted in 1765 is regarded as the East India Company's:
o: First exemption from customs duties in Bengal
139.x: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, obtained in 1765, provided the Company's legal foothold for territorial and fiscal power in India.
139.tq: Link the constitutional-financial concession with its wider historical significance.

139.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Golconda became the 21st Mughal suba after its fall in 1687.
2. The Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad grew out of the Mughal Deccan.
3. The Nizam accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
139.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda was incorporated as the 21st Mughal suba in 1687, Hyderabad emerged from the Mughal Deccan, and the Nizam accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
139.tq: Combine the Andhra-specific administrative, regional and treaty facts in one coded set.

139.s: Who was the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company?
139.x: Shah Alam II became the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company.
139.tq: Distinguish the first pensioner from the last emperor and the later titular ruler.

139.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the last rulers in the stated categories?
o: Bahadur Shah Zafar — last Mughal emperor; Asaf Jah I — last Nizam
Bahadur Shah Zafar — last Mughal emperor; Mir Osman Ali Khan — last Nizam
Akbar II — last Mughal emperor; Mir Mahbub Ali Khan — last Nizam
Shah Alam II — last Mughal emperor; Nizam Ali Khan — last Nizam
139.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor, while Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam of Hyderabad.
139.tq: Compare parallel 'last' designations and avoid substituting an earlier ruler.

139.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the raids of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali?
o: Nadir Shah took Punjab, whereas Abdali took the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne.
Nadir Shah's raid occurred in 1739, while Abdali's raids began from 1748.
Nadir Shah's raids began in 1748, while Abdali invaded in 1739.
Both raids began in 1761 and ended with the Battle of Panipat.
139.x: Nadir Shah raided India in 1739, taking the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne. Abdali's raids began from 1748, took Punjab and culminated in Panipat in 1761.
139.tq: Separate the two invaders by starting date and the distinctive result of each raid.

139.s: Nadir Shah's raid of 1739 resulted in the removal of which of the following from India?
o: The Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne
The Diwani and the Farman of 1717
139.x: Nadir Shah carried away the Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne during his raid of 1739.
139.tq: Match the invader with the distinctive objects taken during the raid.

139.s: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 is associated with the raids of:
139.x: Ahmad Shah Abdali's raids, which began from 1748, culminated in the Battle of Panipat in 1761.
139.tq: Identify the invader from the terminal event in the sequence.

140.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Minister — Function
o: Amatya — Treasury, accounts audit and revenue
Mantri — Religious affairs and charitable grants
140.x: Amatya, also known as Majumdar, was responsible for the treasury, accounts audit and revenue. Military command belonged to the Senapati, religious affairs to the Panditrao and foreign affairs to the Sumant.
140.tq: Start from the sure portfolio and eliminate swapped ministerial functions.

140.s: The Persian or alternative title of the Peshwa in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan was
140.x: The Peshwa was also called Mukhya Pradhan and functioned as the Prime Minister with responsibility for general administration.
140.tq: Test the exact official title rather than the minister's function.

140.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Amatya — Majumdar
2. Sachiv — Shurnavis
3. Mantri — Waqia-navis
4. Panditrao — Danadhyaksha

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
140.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Amatya was Majumdar, Sachiv was Shurnavis, Mantri was Waqia-navis and Panditrao was Danadhyaksha.
140.tq: Use title-to-title matching and check every pair before selecting the complete combination.

140.s: Who among the following was responsible for religious affairs and charitable grants in Shivaji's administration?
140.x: The Panditrao, also known as Danadhyaksha, handled religious affairs and charitable grants.
140.tq: Distinguish the religious portfolio from justice, records and finance.

140.s: The Nyayadhish in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan was associated with
140.x: Nyayadhish was the minister responsible for justice and functioned as the chief justice.
140.tq: Match the office with its direct functional responsibility.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Shivaji's Ashtapradhan is correct?
o: Every minister reported directly to the Chhatrapati.
All posts were hereditary and could not be transferred.
The council was modelled on the Mughal mansabdari system.
The ministers were appointed for life and could not be dismissed.
140.x: Each minister reported directly to the Chhatrapati. The posts were not hereditary, and ministers could be transferred or dismissed at the king's will.
140.tq: Identify the precise administrative feature while rejecting absolute claims.

140.s:
With reference to the military responsibilities of the Ashtapradhan, consider the following statements:

1. The Panditrao and Nyayadhish were exempt from leading military campaigns.
2. All the other ministers had to lead military campaigns.
3. The exemption of the Panditrao and Nyayadhish made the remaining posts hereditary.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
140.x: The Panditrao and Nyayadhish did not have to lead military campaigns, while all other ministers did. This arrangement did not make the posts hereditary.
140.tq: Find the false extension added to otherwise correct administrative statements.

140.s: The Ashtapradhan council of Shivaji was modelled broadly on the administrative system of the
140.x: The Ashtapradhan model was influenced by the administrative arrangements of the Deccan Sultanates.
140.tq: Use the institutional origin as the key distinguishing fact.

140.s: Which one of the following statements about the Peshwa post is NOT correct?
o: The post was hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan.
The post was associated with general administration.
The post became hereditary and supreme under the later Peshwas.
Initially, the Peshwa was the Prime Minister of Shivaji.
140.x: The Peshwa post became hereditary and supreme only later, under the Peshwas; it was not hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's administration.
140.tq: Reject the statement that extends a later development back to the original system.

140.s: Shivaji captured Torna from Bijapur in
140.x: Shivaji seized Torna from Bijapur in 1646, and it was his first fort.
140.tq: Separate the first-fort date from the birth, battle and treaty dates.

140.s:
Arrange the following events in the chronological order in which they occurred:

A. Capture of Torna
B. Killing of Afzal Khan
C. Night attack on Shaista Khan
D. Treaty of Purandar
140.x: Torna was captured in 1646, Afzal Khan was killed in 1659, Shaista Khan was attacked in 1663 and the Treaty of Purandar was concluded in 1665.
140.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intervening military actions.

140.s: Afzal Khan was killed by Shivaji at
140.x: Shivaji killed the Bijapur general Afzal Khan at Pratapgad in 1659.
140.tq: Match the opponent, location and year without confusing separate encounters.

140.s: The night attack on Shaista Khan by Shivaji took place at Pune in
140.x: Shivaji launched the night attack on Shaista Khan at Pune in 1663.
140.tq: Discriminate between closely placed military-event years.

140.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Treaty of Purandar is correct?
o: It was concluded in 1666 with Shaista Khan, and Shivaji surrendered all his forts.
It was concluded in 1665 with Raja Jai Singh, and Shivaji surrendered 23 of 35 forts.
It was concluded in 1659 with Afzal Khan, and Torna was surrendered.
It was concluded in 1674 with Aurangzeb, and Sambhaji was sent to Golconda.
140.x: The Treaty of Purandar was concluded in 1665 with Raja Jai Singh, also known as Mirza Raja of Amber. Shivaji surrendered 23 of his 35 forts and sent Sambhaji to the Mughal court.
140.tq: Use the treaty's year, negotiator and terms together to reject swapped details.

140.s: At Agra in 1666, Shivaji was placed under house arrest after he was
o: appointed commander of the Mughal army
140.x: At Agra, Shivaji was seated behind lesser nobles and was subsequently placed under house arrest.
140.tq: Identify the immediate cause associated with the Agra episode.

140.s: Shivaji escaped from Agra with Sambhaji by concealing themselves in baskets of
140.x: Shivaji and Sambhaji escaped from Agra in baskets of sweets and fruit.
140.tq: Test the distinctive detail of a famous escape rather than the broader event.

140.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. 1674 — Coronation at Raigad
2. 1680 — Death of Shivaji
3. 1670 — Raid on Surat
4. 1677 — Treaty with Abul Hasan Tana Shah

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
140.x: The coronation at Raigad occurred in 1674, the second raid on Surat occurred in 1670, the treaty with Abul Hasan Tana Shah was made in 1677 and Shivaji died in 1680.
140.tq: Check the year-event pairs individually, especially the adjacent campaign and death dates.

140.s: Ganimi Kava, associated with Shivaji's military tactics, refers to
o: A treaty-based system of revenue collection
Guerrilla hit-and-run warfare in the Sahyadri terrain
A system of permanent fortified cantonments in the Deccan
A naval blockade of Mughal ports
140.x: Ganimi Kava was the guerrilla hit-and-run method used by Shivaji in the difficult Sahyadri terrain.
140.tq: Translate the named tactic into its practical military application.

140.s: In 1677, Shivaji made a treaty for assistance in his southern campaign with
o: Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda
Diler Khan of the Mughal Empire
140.x: In 1677 Shivaji made a treaty with Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Golconda, through Akkanna and Madanna, to obtain assistance in his southern campaign.
140.tq: Distinguish the diplomatic ally from the generals and opponents associated with other events.
