168.x: The plea invoked Article 14 and argued that officers without legal training should not adjudicate land-title disputes. The Supreme Court issued notice on the plea.
168.tq: Identify the constitutional article directly linked to the stated legal argument.

168.s: Who was identified as the Chief Justice of India when the Supreme Court issued notice on the plea for a separate revenue judicial service cadre?
168.x: The notice was issued by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice Surya Kant. The plea concerned the adjudication of land-title disputes by revenue officers.
168.tq: Test the current-affairs office-holder directly rather than confusing it with earlier office-holders.

169.s: The proposal for constructing an anicut near Rajahmundry was urged by Arthur Cotton before the Board of Revenue in which year?
169.x: Arthur Cotton reported to the Board of Revenue in 1844, urging the construction of an anicut near Rajahmundry.
169.tq: Test the precise year associated with the administrative proposal.

169.s: The immediate trigger for Arthur Cotton's proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry was the:
169.x: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 prompted the proposal for an anicut near Rajahmundry.
169.tq: Link a public-works proposal with its immediate historical cause.

169.s: The Dowleswaram anicut was sanctioned in:
169.x: The Dowleswaram anicut was sanctioned in late 1846; its construction began in 1847.
169.tq: Distinguish the sanction year from the commencement and completion years.

169.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dowleswaram anicut:
1. Its main work was completed in April 1852.
2. Its reported cost was Rs 1.5 lakh.
3. Veenam Veeranna served as an Indian assistant in the project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
169.x: All three statements are correct. The main work was completed in April 1852 at a cost of Rs 1.5 lakh, with Veenam Veeranna serving as Indian assistant.
169.tq: Combine completion date, cost and personnel facts in a statement set.

169.s: Veenam Veeranna, associated with the construction of the Dowleswaram anicut, was made:
169.x: Veenam Veeranna was made Rao Bahadur and served as an Assistant Engineer in connection with the project.
169.tq: Test the exact designation and honour attached to a named individual.

169.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Anicut or work)
a. Krishna anicut, Bezwada
b. Penna anicut, Nellore
c. K.C. Canal
d. Sangam anicut
List-II (River or location)
i. Penna, Nellore district
ii. Tungabhadra at Sunkesula
iii. Krishna
iv. Penna
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
169.x: The Krishna anicut was on the Krishna, the Penna anicut was at Nellore, the K.C. Canal was associated with the Tungabhadra at Sunkesula, and the Sangam anicut was on the Penna.
169.tq: Start from the sure river-location pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.

169.s: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada, now associated with the Prakasam Barrage, was built by Charles Orr on the plan of:
169.x: Charles Orr built the Krishna anicut on Arthur Cotton's plan. Col. Henry Atlock (Lake) had proposed it.
169.tq: Use the builder–plan–proposal distinction to avoid a swapped-person trap.

169.s: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was constructed during:
169.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was constructed during 1852–55.
169.tq: Identify the correct construction range from closely placed dates.

169.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
169.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was constructed during 1852–55, not in 1872. The K.C. Canal dates to 1872, while Dowleswaram was begun in 1847 and the Penna anicut dates to 1860.
169.tq: Find the single wrong date among closely related irrigation works.

169.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Godavari irrigation system mentioned in connection with the anicuts?
o: It consisted of two canals and initially irrigated 1.5 lakh acres.
It consisted of three main canals and initially irrigated 6.62 lakh acres.
It consisted of three canals and initially irrigated 10 lakh acres only.
It consisted of six canals and initially irrigated 3.26 lakh acres.
169.x: The Godavari system had three main canals and covered 6.62 lakh acres initially; the area later rose to 10 lakh acres.
169.tq: Separate the initial figure from the later expanded figure.

169.s: The revenue from the Godavari irrigation system increased from Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to approximately:
169.x: The revenue increased from Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to Rs 55.18 lakh in 1894–95.
169.tq: Match both endpoints of a quantitative trend rather than one isolated number.

169.s: Arthur Cotton was knighted in:
169.x: Arthur Cotton was knighted in 1861.
169.tq: Test a biographical date directly with nearby administrative dates as distractors.

169.s: Arthur Cotton was popularly known as:
169.x: Arthur Cotton was popularly called Apara Bhagiratha and Cotton Dora.
169.tq: Discriminate between the exact popular titles of historical personalities.

169.s: On Arthur Cotton's suggestion, which two districts were renamed Godavari and Krishna?
169.x: Arthur Cotton suggested renaming Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam districts as Godavari and Krishna respectively.
169.tq: Test a place-renaming relationship involving original and renamed districts.

169.s: Ramapada Sagaram, proposed near Polavaram, is identified with the present-day:
169.x: Ramapada Sagaram is the earlier name associated with today's Polavaram Project.
169.tq: Test the historical name–modern project correspondence.

169.s: Which one of the following was a major feature of the economic impact of British rule on handicrafts in Andhra?
o: Handicrafts were protected by complete prohibition of imported goods.
Artisans received increased traditional patronage from local courts.
British manufactured goods entered the market duty-free and artisans lost patronage.
Artisans were shifted exclusively to government employment.
169.x: Deindustrialisation occurred because artisans lost traditional patronage and British goods entered duty-free.
169.tq: Identify the correct cause-effect explanation for deindustrialisation.

169.s: Why did the cash revenue demand encourage farmers to shift towards commercial crops?
o: Food crops were exempt from revenue, so farmers abandoned all commercial crops.
Farmers received fixed cash subsidies for growing only cotton.
Revenue had to be paid in cash, encouraging cultivation of tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
The government prohibited the cultivation of rice throughout Andhra.
169.x: Since land revenue had to be paid in cash, farmers increasingly cultivated commercial crops such as tobacco, indigo, cotton and oilseeds.
169.tq: Apply the cash-revenue mechanism to the observed change in cropping pattern.

169.s: The reduction of land under food crops made the region more:
169.x: The shift from food crops to commercial crops reduced food availability and made the region more vulnerable to famines.
169.tq: Follow the chain from commercialisation to food insecurity and famine vulnerability.

169.s:
Consider the following statements about agriculture in Andhra under British rule:
1. Most people depended on agriculture.
2. Rice was the main crop.
3. Commercial crops completely replaced food crops in all districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
169.x: Most people depended on agriculture and rice was the main crop. Commercial crops did not completely replace food crops in all districts.
169.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the two supported agricultural facts.

169.s: The principal role of the railways that reached Andhra in the late nineteenth century was to:
o: Link the interior with the Madras port
Link Andhra exclusively with Bombay port
Connect only the Agency tracts with Calcutta
169.x: The railways linked the interior of Andhra with the port of Madras, facilitating movement and trade.
169.tq: Test the direction and commercial purpose of an early transport link.

169.s: During the British period, Vizagapatnam port began developing particularly for the export of:
169.x: Vizagapatnam port developed for the movement of iron ore and agricultural exports.
169.tq: Match a port with its stated export commodities.

169.s: The Buckingham Canal is best described as a:
o: Feeder canal exclusively for the K.C. Canal
Freshwater irrigation canal linking the Krishna and Godavari
Mountain canal connecting Andhra with Mysore
Salt-water navigation canal running along the coast through Pulicat Lake
169.x: The Buckingham Canal was a salt-water navigation canal along the coast, passing through Pulicat Lake.
169.tq: Distinguish a navigation canal from irrigation and feeder canals.

169.s: The Buckingham Canal forms part of which National Waterway, along with the Eluru and Kakinada canals?
169.x: The Buckingham Canal is now part of NW-4, the Kakinada–Puducherry waterway, along with the Eluru and Kakinada canals.
169.tq: Test the canal–national waterway association directly.

169.s: The Buckingham Canal was extended as a famine-relief measure during:
169.x: The Buckingham Canal was extended as famine relief during 1876–78.
169.tq: Connect a public-works extension with the famine-relief period.

169.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Administrator)
a. Arthur Cotton
b. C.P. Brown
c. Colin Mackenzie
d. Thomas Munro
List-II (Contribution)
i. Ryotwari and suppression of the palegars
ii. Godavari and Krishna anicuts
iii. Telugu revival and manuscript-library work
iv. Surveyor General and preservation of records
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
169.x: Arthur Cotton built the major anicuts; C.P. Brown contributed to Telugu revival and manuscript work; Colin Mackenzie preserved records; and Thomas Munro introduced ryotwari and suppressed the palegars.
169.tq: Start with the distinctive anicuts–Cotton pair and complete the administrative matches.

169.s: C.P. Brown served as Collector of:
169.x: C.P. Brown served as the Collector of Kadapa.
169.tq: Test the administrator–district association without confusing it with other postings.

169.s: Which of the following was associated with C.P. Brown?
o: Serving as the first Surveyor General in 1815
Introducing ryotwari and suppressing the palegars
Editing the Madras Literary Journal and serving as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library
169.x: C.P. Brown contributed to Telugu revival, edited the Madras Literary Journal and served as Curator of the Madras Manuscript Library.
169.tq: Use a contribution cluster to distinguish one administrator from neighbouring personalities.

169.s: Colin Mackenzie became the first Surveyor General in:
169.x: Colin Mackenzie was the first Surveyor General in 1815 and also preserved manuscripts and records.
169.tq: Separate the appointment year from the administrator’s lifespan and other dates.

169.s: Thomas Munro was Governor during:
169.x: Thomas Munro served as Governor from 1820 to 1827.
169.tq: Test the exact tenure using adjacent administrative periods as distractors.

169.s: G.N. Taylor is associated with which of the following contributions?
169.x: G.N. Taylor, Rajahmundry Sub-Collector, started Anglo-Vernacular schools across Andhra.
169.tq: Avoid the swapped-contribution trap among British administrators.

169.s: Which famine affected the Northern Circars during 1790–92, with the Ganjam famine occurring in 1791–92?
169.x: The Northern Circars famine occurred during 1790–92, and the Ganjam famine formed part of the 1791–92 crisis.
169.tq: Match a famine label with its period and regional setting.

169.s: The famine affecting all Andhra districts during 1805–07 was followed by a famine in 1823 affecting several districts, including:
o: Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Guntur, Vizag and Nellore
169.x: The 1823 famine affected Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Guntur, Vizag and Nellore; the 1805–07 famine affected all Andhra districts.
169.tq: Use the complete regional list to distinguish the 1823 famine from other entries.

169.s: Which statement regarding the Guntur famine of 1832–33 is correct?
o: It was confined to Kurnool and caused 40 per cent deaths.
It affected only the Northern Circars and caused no migration.
It occurred after the American Civil War and centred on cotton.
It was the worst famine in the south and caused about two lakh deaths.
169.x: The Guntur famine of 1832–33 was regarded as the worst in the south and caused about two lakh deaths, though one account gives the death share as 40 per cent.
169.tq: Identify the famine with its severity, deaths and regional description.

169.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
169.x: The Kurnool famine occurred in 1866. The other pairs assign incorrect dates to the named famines.
169.tq: Check famine names against their exact years rather than relying on regional familiarity.

169.s: Budda Vengala Reddy is associated with relief during the Kurnool famine of 1866. He was awarded a gold medal on:
169.x: Budda Vengala Reddy fed people during the 1866 Kurnool famine and received a gold medal on 1 January 1877.
169.tq: Link a relief figure, famine and award date in one precise recall question.

169.s: The Ganjam famine after 1865 was closely connected with:
o: The end of American Civil War cotton demand and migration to Mauritius and Sri Lanka
The opening of the Madras port and migration to Burma only
The construction of the K.C. Canal and migration to Mysore
The introduction of ryotwari and migration to Bengal
169.x: The decline in cotton demand after the American Civil War contributed to the Ganjam famine, after which people migrated to Mauritius and Sri Lanka.
169.tq: Connect an international economic change with regional famine and migration.

169.s: The Great Famine of 1876–78 particularly affected the:
169.x: The Great Famine of 1876–78 affected the Madras Presidency.
169.tq: Match a major famine with its presidency-level region.

169.s: Which statement about famines in the late nineteenth century is correct?
o: There were no major famines after 1852.
There were eleven famines, all confined to Ganjam.
There were eleven famines, and 1865–66 was the most severe.
There were three famines, and 1832–33 was the only severe one.
169.x: The late nineteenth century witnessed eleven famines, with 1865–66 described as the most severe.
169.tq: Test both the count and the comparative severity of famines.

169.s: The Rajahmundry and Kakinada collectorates were united as Rajahmundry district in:
169.x: The Rajahmundry and Kakinada collectorates were united as Rajahmundry district in 1802.
169.tq: Distinguish the early district formation date from later reorganisation dates.

169.s: After Crown rule, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts in:
169.x: In 1859, Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam were reorganised into Godavari and Krishna districts respectively.
169.tq: Test the chronology of district renaming and reorganisation.

169.s:
Arrange the following district developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of West Godavari district
B. Union of Rajahmundry and Kakinada collectorates
C. Reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna districts
D. Formation of Guntur and East Godavari districts
169.x: The correct order is 1802, 1859, 1904 and 1925: union of collectorates, reorganisation into Godavari and Krishna, formation of Guntur and East Godavari, and formation of West Godavari.
169.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two middle reorganisation stages.

169.s: Guntur and East Godavari became districts in 1904, while West Godavari became a district in:
169.x: Guntur and East Godavari became districts in 1904, and West Godavari was formed in 1925.
169.tq: Compare two related district-formation dates.

169.s: The Collector in the Madras Presidency combined which set of powers?
o: Legislative, judicial and diplomatic powers only
169.x: The Collector combined revenue, magisterial and police powers.
169.tq: Recall the combined authority of the district Collector without adding unrelated departments.

169.s: In Ganjam, the Collector also acted as Agent to the Governor for the Agency tracts from:
169.x: From 1819, the Collector in Ganjam also acted as Agent to the Governor for the Agency tracts.
169.tq: Test the exceptional regional role and its starting year.

169.s: The foundation for replacing the gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage was laid on which date?
169.x: The foundation for replacing the gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage was laid on 13 July 2026.
169.tq: Use precise date discrimination among closely related alternatives.

169.s: How many gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage are proposed to be replaced?
169.x: The project involves replacing 117 gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage.
169.tq: Check the exact numerical figure rather than relying on approximate similarity.

169.s: The estimated cost of replacing the gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage is:
169.x: The estimated cost of the gate-replacement project is ₹152.95 crore.
169.tq: Distinguish the exact project cost from nearby numerical distractors.

169.s: By which time is the replacement of the 117 gates of the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage scheduled to be completed?
169.x: The gate-replacement work is scheduled for completion by July 2028.
169.tq: Separate the completion deadline from alternative years and months.

169.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage:
1. Its length is 5.837 kilometres.
2. It was rebuilt in 1969.
3. It irrigates approximately 10 lakh acres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
169.x: All three statements are correct: the barrage is 5.837 kilometres long, was rebuilt in 1969, and irrigates about 10 lakh acres.
169.tq: Verify each numerical statement independently before selecting the combined option.

169.s: What was the discharge recorded from the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage during the floods of July 2026?
169.x: During the July 2026 floods, the barrage discharged over 5.2 lakh cusecs.
169.tq: Identify the exact discharge figure and retain the stated unit of cusecs.

169.s: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at which barrage in February 2026?
169.x: Automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at the Prakasam Barrage in February 2026.
169.tq: Apply the location-and-year pair to distinguish similar irrigation structures.

169.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of the Godavari and Krishna deltas in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They are known as the Cotton Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Mineral Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra.
They are known as the Industrial Bowl of Andhra.
169.x: The Godavari and Krishna deltas are collectively known as the “Rice Bowl of Andhra” because of their importance for rice cultivation.
169.tq: Match the distinctive regional title with the correct geographical area.

170.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Punjab — Conquest in the Second Anglo-Sikh War
170.x: Punjab was annexed in 1849 after its conquest in the Second Anglo-Sikh War. Sindh was conquered, Awadh was annexed for maladministration, and Satara under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Use the ground of annexation to eliminate swapped causes.

170.s: Punjab was annexed to British India in which year?
170.x: Punjab was annexed in 1849 following the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
170.tq: Distinguish closely spaced annexation years by linking the year with the event.

170.s: Which of the following states was annexed on the ground of maladministration, rather than under the Doctrine of Lapse?
170.x: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration, based on Outram's reports. Nagpur, Jhansi and Sambalpur were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Find the exception by separating policy-based annexations from administrative grounds.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sindh was annexed after conquest under Ellenborough.
2. Punjab was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
3. Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, not under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Test each statement against the specific ground of annexation.

170.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
170.x: Jhansi was annexed in 1853, not 1854. Nagpur was annexed in 1854; the Udaipur mentioned here was Udaipur in Chhattisgarh, not Mewar.
170.tq: Check the numerical sequence carefully and watch for a one-year shift.

170.s: The Udaipur annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1852 was located in:
170.x: The Udaipur referred to in the annexation list was Udaipur in Chhattisgarh, not the larger princely state of Udaipur in Mewar.
170.tq: Discriminate between identically named places by using the precise regional qualifier.

170.s:
Arrange the following annexations in chronological order:
A. Nagpur
B. Baghat
C. Satara
D. Jhansi
170.x: The correct order is Satara (1848), Baghat (1850), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).
170.tq: Place the earliest and latest years first, then resolve the middle sequence.

170.s: Which of the following was annexed by Lord Dalhousie on the ground of misgovernance rather than by the Doctrine of Lapse?
170.x: Dalhousie annexed Burma and Awadh on grounds of misgovernance. Satara, Jaitpur and Baghat were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Identify the policy exception among a group of lapse annexations.

170.s: Wajid Ali Shah was deposed when the British annexed:
170.x: Wajid Ali Shah was deposed when Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of maladministration.
170.tq: Match the deposed ruler with the annexed territory.

170.s: The Doctrine of Lapse was principally associated with the tenure of which Governor-General?
170.x: The Doctrine of Lapse was the policy of Lord Dalhousie, who served as Governor-General from 1848 to 1856.
170.tq: Match the distinctive policy with its principal Governor-General.

170.s: Under the Doctrine of Lapse, when the ruler of a dependent state died without a natural heir, the state:
o: lapsed to the East India Company
became an independent monarchy under the adopted heir
was placed under the direct rule of the Governor-General without annexation
was transferred automatically to the Mughal emperor
170.x: A dependent state without a natural heir lapsed to the East India Company under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Apply the definition to the legal consequence of the ruler's death.

170.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Doctrine of Lapse:
1. It was associated with Lord Dalhousie.
2. An adopted son could inherit the ruler's private property.
3. An adopted son could automatically inherit the throne of the dependent state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under the policy, an adopted son could inherit private property but not the throne.
170.tq: Separate private-property succession from succession to political sovereignty.

170.s: A ruler of a dependent princely state dies without a natural heir but leaves an adopted son. According to the Doctrine of Lapse, which consequence follows?
o: The adopted son succeeds to both property and throne.
The adopted son succeeds to the throne but not private property.
The state remains independent because adoption is legally sufficient.
The adopted son may inherit private property, but the state lapses to the Company.
170.x: Adoption protected the right to private property but did not confer the right to inherit the throne under the Doctrine of Lapse.
170.tq: Use the paired distinction between personal inheritance and political succession.

170.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War was fought during the tenure of:
170.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War, generally dated 1775–1782, occurred during the tenure of Warren Hastings.
170.tq: Link each war with the Governor-General in office.

170.s: Which treaty ended the First Anglo-Maratha War?
170.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai in 1782.
170.tq: Match the war with its final settlement, not an intermediate treaty.

170.s: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded between the British and the Marathas through:
170.x: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded in 1782 between the British and the Marathas through Mahadji Scindia.
170.tq: Identify the intermediary associated with the final treaty.

170.s: Which of the following was a consequence of the Treaty of Salbai?
o: The Marathas ceded Delhi to the British.
The British retained Salsette and peace was maintained for about twenty years.
The British surrendered Salsette to the Marathas.
170.x: The Treaty of Salbai established the status quo, allowed the British to retain Salsette and ushered in about twenty years of peace.
170.tq: Distinguish the settlement's actual outcome from results of later wars.

170.s: The British supported Raghunath Rao against the Barabhai Council in the:
170.x: The British backed Raghunath Rao against the Barabhai Council during the First Anglo-Maratha War.
170.tq: Match the political alignment with the correct war.

170.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the early treaties of the First Anglo-Maratha War?
170.x: The sequence was the Treaty of Surat in 1775, Treaty of Purandar in 1776, Convention of Wadgaon in 1779 and Treaty of Salbai in 1782.
170.tq: Arrange intermediate agreements before the final settlement.

170.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Treaty of Purandar is correct?
o: It abolished the office of the Peshwa.
It was concluded by the Calcutta Council with the Barabhai Council and set aside the Treaty of Surat.
It was concluded between the British and Holkar in 1805.
It gave the British control over the Mughal emperor.
170.x: The Treaty of Purandar of 1776 was concluded by the Calcutta Council with the Barabhai Council and set aside the Treaty of Surat.
170.tq: Use the negotiating parties and treaty relationship to reject swapped events.

170.s: The Convention of Wadgaon followed the British defeat at:
170.x: The Convention of Wadgaon followed the British defeat at Talegaon in 1779, after which the British had to give up their gains.
170.tq: Match the battlefield event with the immediate treaty consequence.

170.s: The Second Anglo-Maratha War was fought during the tenure of:
170.x: The Second Anglo-Maratha War, generally dated 1803–1805, occurred during the tenure of Lord Wellesley.
170.tq: Pair the war with the Governor-General rather than with a later settlement.

170.s: Which of the following was NOT a term associated with the Treaty of Bassein?
o: The Peshwa ceded lands yielding Rs 26 lakh.
The Peshwa surrendered Surat to the British.
The Peshwa obtained additional chauth claims on the Nizam.
A subsidiary force was to be maintained in Maratha territory.
170.x: Under the Treaty of Bassein, the Peshwa gave up his chauth claims on the Nizam; he did not obtain additional claims. The other three were terms of the treaty.
170.tq: Find the reversed provision in a list of treaty terms.

170.s: Which treaty was concluded with the Bhonsle of Nagpur during the Second Anglo-Maratha War?
170.x: The Treaty of Deogaon was concluded with the Bhonsle of Nagpur in 1803.
170.tq: Match the treaty with the specific Maratha house involved.

170.s: The Treaty of Surji-Arjangaon was concluded with Scindia and enabled the British to gain:
o: Delhi and control over the Mughal emperor
170.x: The Treaty of Surji-Arjangaon was concluded with Scindia in 1803 and gave the British Delhi and control over the Mughal emperor.
170.tq: Connect the treaty partner with its distinctive territorial and political outcome.

170.s: The Treaty of Rajpurghat was concluded with:
170.x: The Treaty of Rajpurghat was concluded with Holkar in 1805.
170.tq: Use the treaty-party association to separate the three Maratha settlements.

170.s: Which one of the following was a major consequence of the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
o: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded.
The British restored the office of Peshwa under a subsidiary alliance.
The Marathas gained control over Delhi.
The office of Peshwa was abolished and Baji Rao II was pensioned.
170.x: After the Third Anglo-Maratha War, Peshwa Baji Rao II was deposed and pensioned, and the office of Peshwa was abolished.
170.tq: Identify the institutional outcome rather than a treaty from an earlier war.

170.s: The Third Anglo-Maratha War was associated with the campaigns against the:
170.x: The Third Anglo-Maratha War was set off by Lord Hastings' campaign against the Pindaris, followed by the rising of the Peshwa, Bhonsle and Holkar.
170.tq: Identify the immediate trigger of the conflict.

170.s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Anglo-Maratha War:
1. It occurred during the tenure of Lord Hastings.
2. The Peshwa attacked the Poona Residency.
3. The office of Peshwa continued after the war under Baji Rao II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the office of Peshwa was abolished and Baji Rao II was deposed and pensioned.
170.tq: Use the final constitutional consequence to identify the false statement.

170.s: Which one of the following statements about the First Anglo-Maratha War is correct?
o: It ended with the abolition of the Peshwa-ship.
The British retained Salsette under the Treaty of Salbai.
It was fought during the tenure of Lord Wellesley.
The British gained control over the Mughal emperor through the Treaty of Purandar.
170.x: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai, under which the British retained Salsette. The other statements refer to later developments or wrong Governor-General associations.
170.tq: Combine the war's final treaty with its specific territorial outcome.

170.s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46)?
170.x: Lord Hardinge was the Governor-General during the First Anglo-Sikh War, fought in 1845–46.
170.tq: Use the ruler-period association and distinguish Hardinge from Dalhousie.

170.s: Which one of the following was the immediate cause of the First Anglo-Sikh War?
o: The murder of Vans Agnew and Anderson at Multan
The refusal of the Nizam to assign Berar
The Sikh army crossing the Sutlej
The detention of two British doctors in Sikkim
170.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War began when the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej, whose boundary had been fixed by the Treaty of Amritsar of 1809.
170.tq: Identify the immediate cause rather than a later Anglo-Sikh event.

170.s: Which of the following sets contains only battles of the First Anglo-Sikh War?
170.x: Mudki, Ferozeshah, Aliwal and Sobraon were the principal battles of the First Anglo-Sikh War.
170.tq: Group the battles by war and eliminate those belonging to the Second Anglo-Sikh War or Sindh.

170.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the First Anglo-Sikh War:
1. The Battle of Sobraon was fought in 1846.
2. Lal Singh and Tej Singh betrayed the Sikh side.
3. The Treaty of Bhairowal made the British Resident the virtual ruler.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the British Resident became the virtual ruler under the Treaty of Bhairowal, not as a result of the First War's battles themselves; Bhairowal was a subsequent treaty of December 1846.
170.tq: Separate battlefield facts from the later treaty arrangement before selecting the coded combination.

170.s:
The Treaty of Lahore of 1846 resulted in which of the following?
1. Cession of territory south of the Sutlej
2. Payment of an indemnity by the Sikh state
3. Transfer of Kashmir to Gulab Singh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: The Treaty of Lahore provided for territory south of the Sutlej and an indemnity. Kashmir was handed over to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar in March 1846.
170.tq: Watch for the treaty-name trap involving Kashmir and distinguish Lahore from Amritsar.

170.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists.
List-I (Battle)
A. Mudki
B. Chillianwala
C. Gujrat
D. Sobraon
List-II (War)
1. First Anglo-Sikh War
2. Second Anglo-Sikh War

Codes:
170.x: Mudki and Sobraon belonged to the First Anglo-Sikh War, while Chillianwala and Gujrat belonged to the Second.
170.tq: Start from the sure battle-war pairs and use them to eliminate the mixed codes.

170.s: The Battle of Chillianwala was fought in:
170.x: The Battle of Chillianwala was fought in January 1849 during the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
170.tq: Use the year within the Second Anglo-Sikh War and distinguish it from the 1846 battles.

170.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Second Anglo-Sikh War?
o: Kashmir was annexed directly by the British in 1846.
Punjab was annexed by the British in 1849.
Punjab accepted a subsidiary alliance but retained complete sovereignty.
The Sikh army occupied territory south of the Sutlej.
170.x: The Second Anglo-Sikh War ended with the annexation of Punjab by the British in 1849.
170.tq: Match the war with its final political result and reject reversed outcomes.

170.s:
Which of the following events occurred after the First Anglo-Sikh War?
1. Treaty of Bhairowal
2. Transfer of Kashmir to Gulab Singh under a separate Treaty of Amritsar
3. Annexation of Punjab
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: The Treaties of Bhairowal and Amritsar followed the First Anglo-Sikh War. Punjab was annexed only after the Second Anglo-Sikh War in 1849.
170.tq: Use the sequence of treaties and annexation to reject the later event.

170.s: After the death of Ranjit Singh, Punjab fell into chaos in:
170.x: Ranjit Singh died in 1839, after which Punjab entered a period of political chaos.
170.tq: Distinguish the correct date from the tempting but incorrect 1836 reference.

170.s:
With reference to the political status of Indian states under British paramountcy, consider the following statements:
1. Indian states retained their internal administration.
2. They possessed complete international freedom.
3. The British interfered in internal matters to fulfil their international commitments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Indian states generally retained internal administration but had no independent international life. British intervention in internal matters was justified partly by their international commitments.
170.tq: Spot the reversed meaning of the phrase ‘no international life’.

170.s: The British intervened in the internal administration of Indian states on the ground of misgovernance in the case of:
170.x: Misgovernance was cited as a ground for intervention and annexation in Coorg and Awadh.
170.tq: Pair the stated ground of intervention with the two associated territories.

170.s: Who converted the policy of subsidiary alliances into a wider system of paramountcy?
170.x: Lord Hastings developed subsidiary alliances into the system of British paramountcy and imposed humiliating treaties on the Peshwa and Scindia.
170.tq: Distinguish the architect of paramountcy from the Governor-General associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.

170.s: Under the subordinate alliances accepted by Rajputana states in 1818, the states:
o: surrendered their internal administration but retained foreign relations
were exempted from all British political control
gave up their external relations in return for British protection
became directly administered provinces of the Company
170.x: The Rajputana states accepted British protection and surrendered control over their external relations under subordinate alliances in 1818.
170.tq: Apply the protection-for-external-control structure of a subordinate alliance.

170.s: Which of the following states was NOT specifically included among the Rajputana states accepting subordinate alliances in 1818?
170.x: Udaipur, Jaipur and Jodhpur were among the Rajputana states that accepted subordinate alliances in 1818. Awadh was not a Rajputana state in this arrangement.
170.tq: Find the outsider in a regional political grouping.

170.s: Sindh was annexed by the British in 1843 during the Governor-Generalship of:
170.x: The conquest and annexation of Sindh took place in 1843 under Lord Ellenborough.
170.tq: Link the annexation year with the correct Governor-General rather than with Dalhousie’s later expansion.

170.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the British conquest of Sindh?
o: Recovering prestige lost in the First Afghan War
Securing the trade of the Indus
Introducing the Doctrine of Lapse in Sindh
170.x: The stated objectives were recovery of prestige after the First Afghan War, countering Russia and securing Indus trade. The Doctrine of Lapse was not an objective of the conquest of Sindh.
170.tq: Eliminate the policy that belongs to Dalhousie’s annexations rather than Sindh.

170.s: Who adopted a bullying policy towards the Amirs of Sindh and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo?
170.x: Sir Charles Napier used coercive diplomacy against the Amirs and annexed Sindh after the battles of Miani and Dabo.
170.tq: Use the commander-deed association and avoid confusing Napier with the Governors-General.

170.s: The annexation of Sindh was described as the:
170.x: The British annexation of Sindh was called the ‘Tail of the Afghan Storm’.
170.tq: Test the exact historical expression rather than a plausible geographical description.

170.s: Which one of the following series of wars covered the period 1746–1763?
170.x: The Carnatic Wars were fought during the period 1746–1763.
170.tq: Match the war series with its span and distinguish overlapping conflicts.

170.s: The Anglo-Nepal War was fought during:
170.x: The Anglo-Nepal War took place from 1814 to 1816.
170.tq: Use the chronological position of the Nepal conflict between the Maratha and Burmese wars.

170.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
170.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War was fought from 1824 to 1826. The other periods belong respectively to the Anglo-Nepal War, First Anglo-Afghan War and Anglo-Sikh Wars.
170.tq: Check each war against its distinctive time span and reject shifted periods.

170.s: Which statement best explains the historical significance of the Anglo-Maratha Wars?
o: The wars ended before the Mysore Wars began.
The British effectively acquired India from the Marathas rather than from the Mughals.
The Marathas were defeated by the Sikhs in these wars.
The Marathas established British rule over Bengal.
170.x: The British effectively took control of India from the Marathas; the Mughal emperor no longer represented the main political power being conquered.
170.tq: Identify the broader political conclusion instead of confusing successive regional wars.

170.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad order of the three major series of wars?
o: Anglo-Maratha Wars, Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars
Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Maratha Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars
Anglo-Sikh Wars, Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Maratha Wars
Anglo-Mysore Wars, Anglo-Sikh Wars, Anglo-Maratha Wars
170.x: The Anglo-Mysore Wars (1767–1799) preceded the Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775–1818), which in turn preceded the Anglo-Sikh Wars (1845–1849).
170.tq: Arrange the series by their starting periods and verify the final sequence.

170.s: Coorg was annexed in 1834 during the administration of:
170.x: Coorg was taken in 1834 by Lord William Bentinck on the plea of misgovernance, along with Central Cachar.
170.tq: Pair the annexed territory and year with the correct Governor-General.

170.s: Coorg was annexed along with:
170.x: Coorg was taken by Bentinck together with Central Cachar, with misgovernance cited as the justification.
170.tq: Use the territorial pair rather than confusing nearby annexations of Burma or Berar.

170.s: Parts of Sikkim were annexed in 1850 after:
o: the Amirs refused to sign a commercial treaty
the Nizam failed to pay an indemnity
the Sikh army crossed the Sutlej
170.x: Dalhousie annexed parts of Sikkim in 1850 after two British doctors had been detained.
170.tq: Link the annexation to its immediate incident and reject causes from other campaigns.

170.s: In 1855, the titles and pensions of the rulers of which territories were abolished?
170.x: The titles and pensions of the rulers of Karnataka, or Carnatic, and Tanjore were abolished in 1855.
170.tq: Test the exact territories associated with abolition of titles and pensions.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pension of Nana Sahib was stopped after the death of Baji Rao II.
2. Baji Rao II died in 1851.
3. Nana Sahib was the adopted son of Baji Rao II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: All three statements are correct. Nana Sahib, the adopted son of Baji Rao II, was denied continuation of the Peshwa pension after Baji Rao II died in 1851.
170.tq: Combine relationship, date and policy consequence before choosing the complete code.

170.s: Berar was assigned to the British by the Nizam under the:
170.x: Berar was assigned by the Nizam under the Berar Treaty in 1853.
170.tq: Identify the treaty by its direct territorial association and avoid Anglo-Sikh treaty names.

170.s:
Which of the following developments contributed to resentment against the East India Company before the Revolt of 1857?
1. Annexation of Awadh
2. Withdrawal of titles and pensions
3. Fear of further annexations among princes and taluqdars
4. Discontent among many Awadh sepoys
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All four developments contributed to the growth of resentment. Awadh’s annexation, loss of privileges, fear of annexation and sepoy discontent helped create conditions for the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Recognize the cumulative nature of several connected causes rather than selecting a single grievance.

170.s: Awadh was annexed by the British primarily because of its:
o: adoption of a foreign policy hostile to Russia
cotton market and agrarian wealth, with misgovernance also invoked
refusal to accept the Treaty of Amritsar
strategic control over the Indus trade alone
170.x: Awadh’s cotton market and agrarian wealth were important motives, while misgovernance was used as the formal justification. Its annexation generated immense resentment and contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Distinguish the economic motive from the formal administrative justification.

170.s: By 1856, British India extended geographically from the:
170.x: By 1856, British India stretched from the Hindukush to Burma. This created geographical unity as well as a basis for common resistance.
170.tq: Recall the two geographical limits and reject narrower or altered boundaries.

170.s:
The territorial expansion of British India by 1856 had a dual consequence. It:
1. Created geographical unity in India.
2. Provided a basis for common resistance.
3. Eliminated all political resentment among Indian rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
170.x: Expansion created geographical unity and a basis for common resistance. It did not eliminate resentment; annexations and the loss of titles and pensions intensified it.
170.tq: Separate the stated positive structural consequence from an absolute and unsupported claim.

170.s: The capital of Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan's kingdom was
170.x: Srirangapatnam, also known as Seringapatam, was the capital of Mysore under Haidar Ali and Tipu Sultan.
170.tq: Use the direct capital–state association.

170.s:
The British conflicts with Mysore were connected with which of the following factors?
1. Mysore's control over Malabar pepper and cardamom
2. The perceived threat to Madras
3. Mysore's alliances with France
4. Mysore's control over the Sutlej frontier
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: The British were concerned about Mysore's control of Malabar spices, its threat to Madras and its French connections. The Sutlej frontier was associated with Sikh affairs, not the Mysore struggle.
170.tq: Separate the three relevant causes from the unrelated frontier reference.

170.s: Tipu Sultan sent ambassadors to France mainly to
o: secure the transfer of the capital to Paris
recruit troops for the Anglo-Sikh War
170.x: Tipu Sultan sent ambassadors to France in an effort to obtain European technology and modernise his state.
170.tq: Match the diplomatic mission with its stated objective.

170.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Tipu Sultan is correct?
o: He founded the Dal Khalsa at Lahore.
He established the British Subsidiary Alliance in Hyderabad.
He signed the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809.
He joined the Jacobin Club and planted a Tree of Liberty at Srirangapatnam.
170.x: Tipu Sultan is said to have joined the Jacobin Club and planted a Tree of Liberty at Srirangapatnam.
170.tq: Use the distinctive person–event association.

170.s: Wellesley's fear of which proposed alliance became the pretext for the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
170.x: Wellesley feared that Tipu Sultan might form an alliance with Napoleon. This fear was used as the pretext for the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
170.tq: Discriminate the feared alliance from other regional combinations.

170.s: Haidar Ali established a modern arsenal at Dindigul in
170.x: Haidar Ali set up a modern arsenal at Dindigul in 1755 with French assistance.
170.tq: Place the arsenal date among the nearby Mysore-war dates.

170.s: Who among the following was associated with the Rohilla War of 1774, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War?
170.x: Warren Hastings was Governor-General from 1772 to 1785 and his tenure included the Rohilla War, the First Anglo-Maratha War and the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
170.tq: Match the Governor-General with the cluster of wars fought during his tenure.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cornwallis was Governor-General from 1786 to 1793.
2. The Third Anglo-Mysore War was fought during his tenure.
3. The Treaty of Seringapatam was concluded in 1792.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All three statements are correct. Cornwallis's tenure covered the Third Anglo-Mysore War, which ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
170.tq: Check the tenure, war and treaty as one connected sequence.

170.s: At the Battle of Kharda in 1795, the Marathas defeated the Nizam while the Governor-General was
170.x: Sir John Shore, Governor-General from 1793 to 1798, followed a policy of neutrality at Kharda, where the Marathas defeated the Nizam.
170.tq: Use the neutral-policy clue to identify the Governor-General.

170.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Wellesley — Fourth Anglo-Mysore War and Second Anglo-Maratha War
2. Lord Hastings — Anglo-Nepalese War and Third Anglo-Maratha War
3. Ellenborough — Annexation of Sindh and war with Gwalior
4. Dalhousie — First Anglo-Sikh War and annexation of Lower Burma
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. The First Anglo-Sikh War belonged to Hardinge; Dalhousie was associated with the Second Anglo-Sikh War and the annexation of Lower Burma.
170.tq: Detect the swapped war in the final Governor-General pairing.

170.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
170.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War was fought during Hardinge's tenure, not Cornwallis's. Cornwallis was associated with the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
170.tq: Find the Governor-General placed in the wrong period.

170.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists.
List-I (Battle)
a. Porto Novo
a. Assaye
c. Mudki
d. Chillianwala
List-II (British commander)
i. Arthur Wellesley
ii. Sir Hugh Gough
iii. Eyre Coote
iv. Sir Hugh Gough
170.x: Porto Novo was commanded by Eyre Coote, Assaye by Arthur Wellesley, and both Mudki and Chillianwala by Sir Hugh Gough.
170.tq: Start from the sure battle–commander pair and eliminate the codes.

170.s: The Battle of Porto Novo, fought in 1781, belonged to the
170.x: Porto Novo was fought in 1781 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War. Eyre Coote defeated Haidar Ali in this battle.
170.tq: Match the battle year and war rather than the commander alone.

170.s: The battles of Assaye, Delhi and Laswari were associated with the
170.x: Assaye, Delhi and Laswari were important battles of the Second Anglo-Maratha War in 1803.
170.tq: Group battles by the war to which they belong.

170.s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
1. Arthur Wellesley commanded the British forces at Assaye.
2. Lord Lake commanded the British forces at Delhi and Laswari.
3. Sir Hugh Gough commanded at Mudki and Chillianwala.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All three statements are correct. Arthur Wellesley commanded at Assaye, Lord Lake at Delhi and Laswari, and Sir Hugh Gough at Mudki and Chillianwala.
170.tq: Verify repeated commander associations across different battles.

170.s: Chillianwala was a battle of the
o: Second Anglo-Maratha War and was fought under Lord Lake
First Anglo-Sikh War and was decisive for the British
Second Anglo-Sikh War and was costly and indecisive
Anglo-Nepalese War and was fought under Lord Hastings
170.x: Chillianwala was fought in 1849 during the Second Anglo-Sikh War. The battle under Sir Hugh Gough was costly and indecisive.
170.tq: Reject the wrong war and the reversed assessment of the battle.

170.s: Who among the following was known as the 'Lion of Punjab'?
170.x: Maharaja Ranjit Singh was popularly known as the 'Lion of Punjab'.
170.tq: Use the title–person association.

170.s: Ranjit Singh's capital was
170.x: Lahore was the capital of Ranjit Singh's kingdom.
170.tq: Identify the capital of the ruler rather than the treaty location.

170.s: The combined force of the Sikh misls was known as the
170.x: The combined force of the Sikh misls was called the Dal Khalsa. Ranjit Singh united the Sikh misls.
170.tq: Distinguish the collective force of the misls from the later modernised army.

170.s: Ranjit Singh signed a treaty of perpetual friendship with Bentinck in
170.x: Ranjit Singh signed a treaty of perpetual friendship with Bentinck in 1831.
170.tq: Separate the friendship treaty date from the Treaty of Amritsar and Ranjit Singh's death.

170.s: Which of the following statements about Ranjit Singh's Khalsa army is correct?
o: It was modernised with the assistance of European officers.
It was dissolved after the Treaty of Amritsar.
It was commanded by Lord Lake.
It was formed exclusively by the Nizam's French battalions.
170.x: Ranjit Singh modernised the Khalsa army with the assistance of European officers.
170.tq: Identify the correct modernisation feature of the army.

170.s:
Arrange the following successors of Ranjit Singh in chronological order of succession:
A. Sher Singh
B. Kharak Singh
C. Dalip Singh
D. Nau Nihal Singh
170.x: The order was Kharak Singh, Nau Nihal Singh, Sher Singh and finally the minor Dalip Singh, with Rani Jindan as regent.
170.tq: Fix the first and last successors, then arrange the middle sequence.

170.s: Who was the regent of the minor Dalip Singh?
170.x: Rani Jindan acted as regent for the minor Dalip Singh, who was the last ruler of Punjab before its annexation.
170.tq: Match the minor ruler with the correct regent.

170.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ranjit Singh died in 1839.
2. Chaos and indiscipline followed his death.
3. Dalip Singh was the last ruler when Punjab was annexed.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: All three statements are correct. Ranjit Singh died in 1839, disorder followed, and Dalip Singh was the last ruler of Punjab at annexation.
170.tq: Combine the ruler's death, its consequence and the final succession fact.

170.s: During the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam, the Marathas and the British were allied against
170.x: In the First Anglo-Mysore War, the Nizam, the Marathas and the British formed an alliance against Haidar Ali.
170.tq: Identify the opponent from the alliance configuration.

170.s:
Which of the following territories were recovered by Nizam Ali under the Treaty of Seringapatam of 1792?
1. Bellary
2. Gurramkonda
3. Gandikota
4. Kambham
5. Kadapa
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
170.x: The territories listed—Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham and Kadapa—were included among the Rayalaseema lands recovered by Nizam Ali under the 1792 settlement.
170.tq: Test completeness of the territorial list rather than one isolated district.

170.s: After the Nizam's defeat at Kharda in 1795, which development led to his acceptance of the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798?
o: He accepted the Treaty of Amritsar.
He ceded Punjab to Lord Dalhousie.
He joined Ranjit Singh against the British.
He blamed Shore's neutrality and hired French battalions under Raymond.
170.x: The Nizam blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality at Kharda and hired French battalions under Raymond. Resident Kirkpatrick reported the development, and the Nizam accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
170.tq: Follow the cause-and-effect chain from Kharda to the Subsidiary Alliance.

170.s: In 1800, the Nizam ceded which group of territories to meet the cost of the subsidiary force?
170.x: In 1800, the Nizam ceded Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary. These territories became known as the Ceded Districts or Dattamandalalu.
170.tq: Match the Ceded Districts with the complete territorial group.

170.s: The Ceded Districts were also known as
170.x: The territories ceded by the Nizam in 1800 were known as the Ceded Districts or Dattamandalalu.
170.tq: Distinguish the regional administrative term from unrelated territorial names.

170.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the major grounds of British territorial expansion?
o: Sindh and Punjab—misgovernance; Satara to Nagpur—abolition of titles; Awadh and Coorg—lapse; Carnatic and Tanjore—conquest
Sindh and Punjab—lapse; Satara to Nagpur—conquest; Awadh and Coorg—abolition of titles; Carnatic and Tanjore—misgovernance
Sindh and Punjab—conquest; Satara to Nagpur—lapse; Awadh and Coorg—misgovernance; Carnatic and Tanjore—abolition of titles
Sindh and Punjab—abolition of titles; Satara to Nagpur—misgovernance; Awadh and Coorg—conquest; Carnatic and Tanjore—lapse
170.x: The classification is: conquest for Sindh and Punjab, Doctrine of Lapse for Satara to Nagpur, misgovernance for Awadh and Coorg, and abolition of titles for Carnatic and Tanjore.
170.tq: Keep the four legal and political grounds separate instead of swapping them.

170.s: The lapse annexations of 1848–1854 and the annexation of Awadh in 1856 contributed to the grievances that fed the
170.x: The annexations carried out between 1848 and 1854 and the annexation of Awadh in 1856 were among the princely grievances that contributed to the Revolt of 1857.
170.tq: Link the annexation policy with its stated political consequence.

170.s: The lands of the Carnatic Nawab in Nellore and Chittoor were annexed in 1801 on the charge of
170.x: Nellore and Chittoor were taken from the Carnatic Nawab in 1801 on the charge of collusion with Tipu Sultan, an early pretext annexation.
170.tq: Match the Andhra territories with the specific annexation pretext.

170.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Nellore and Chittoor taken from the Carnatic Nawab
B. Ceded Districts obtained from the Nizam
C. British paramountcy became unchallenged after the defeat of the Marathas
D. Treaty of Amritsar
170.x: The sequence is Treaty of Amritsar in 1809, acquisition of the Ceded Districts in 1800, Nellore and Chittoor in 1801, and the unchallenged position after 1818. Therefore, the chronological order among the labelled items is B, A, D, C; however, because the options place D first, the correct chronological order is B, A, D, C.
170.tq: Anchor the dated territorial acquisitions before the later consolidation of paramountcy.

170.s: The Mysore wars and the Subsidiary Alliance brought Rayalaseema under the control of the Company in
170.x: The Mysore wars and the Subsidiary Alliance resulted in Rayalaseema coming under Company control in 1800 through the territories ceded by the Nizam.
170.tq: Distinguish the Rayalaseema date from the immediately following Carnatic annexation.

170.s: After the acquisition of Rayalaseema and the annexation of Nellore and Chittoor, Wellesley merged the Andhra region into the
170.x: Wellesley merged the Andhra region into the Madras Presidency after the Company obtained Rayalaseema in 1800 and Nellore and Chittoor in 1801.
170.tq: Match the Andhra territorial change with the correct Presidency.

170.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding British paramountcy in India?
o: It became unchallenged after 1818 following the removal of the last strong Indian powers.
It became unchallenged immediately after the Treaty of Amritsar in 1809.
It ended after the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
It was established only after the annexation of Punjab in 1849.
170.x: The Anglo-Mysore, Anglo-Maratha and other conflicts removed the last strong Indian powers; after 1818, British paramountcy was unchallenged.
170.tq: Use the broader consequence of the wars rather than one individual treaty or annexation.

171.s: Which one of the following measures is associated with Warren Hastings?
171.x: Warren Hastings abolished the Dual Government in 1772. The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis, the Subsidiary Alliance by Wellesley and Sindh was annexed during Ellenborough’s tenure.
171.tq: Use the ruler–measure association and reject measures belonging to neighbouring administrations.

171.s:
With reference to Warren Hastings, consider the following statements:
1. He shifted the treasury to Calcutta.
2. He stopped the payment of ₹26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam.
3. He established Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Warren Hastings shifted the treasury to Calcutta, stopped the ₹26 lakh tribute to Shah Alam and established Diwani and Fauzdari Adalats.
171.tq: Combine three measures of the same Governor-General and identify the complete code.

171.s: Which of the following institutions was founded by Warren Hastings?
171.x: The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded during Warren Hastings’s tenure. College of Fort William is associated with Wellesley and the Public Works Department with Dalhousie.
171.tq: Apply the founder–institution trap by distinguishing institutions of successive administrations.

171.s: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 is chiefly associated with which of the following measures?
o: Separation of revenue administration from justice
171.x: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 separated revenue administration from judicial administration. The other measures belong to Wellesley, Bentinck and Dalhousie respectively.
171.tq: Identify the precise administrative reform linked with the named code.

171.s: Which one of the following posts was created during the tenure of Lord Cornwallis?
171.x: Lord Cornwallis created the post of District Judge as part of his judicial and administrative reforms.
171.tq: Use the post–reformer association rather than confusing it with a later office.

171.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
171.x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William in 1800. The Anti-Slavery Act was associated with Ellenborough, while the Permanent Settlement and Cornwallis Code belonged to Cornwallis.
171.tq: Start with the sure institution–Governor-General pair and eliminate swapped measures.

171.s: The Treaty of Amritsar of 1809 was concluded during the tenure of:
171.x: Minto I concluded the Treaty of Amritsar with Ranjit Singh in 1809.
171.tq: Discriminate between similarly named or successive Governors-General through the treaty year.

171.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Marquess Hastings is correct?
o: He introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal.
He founded the College of Fort William.
He introduced the Mahalwari system in 1822 through Holt Mackenzie.
171.x: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 through Holt Mackenzie during the tenure of Marquess Hastings. The other measures are associated with Cornwallis, Wellesley and William Bentinck.
171.tq: Find the single correct measure among reforms belonging to different administrations.

171.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of William Bentinck?
o: Treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh
Introduction of the Mahalwari system in 1822
171.x: The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 during the tenure of Marquess Hastings. Bentinck abolished Sati, suppressed female infanticide and concluded a treaty of perpetual friendship with Ranjit Singh in 1831.
171.tq: Find the measure belonging to the preceding administration rather than the named Governor-General.

171.s:
Consider the following statements about William Bentinck:
1. He took Coorg in 1834.
2. He took over the administration of Mysore.
3. He established universities for the first time in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Bentinck took Coorg in 1834 and took over Mysore’s administration. The first universities were established in 1857 during Canning’s tenure, not during Bentinck’s tenure.
171.tq: Reject the later institutional development inserted into a list of genuine Bentinck measures.

171.s: Which Governor-General is associated with both the end of the Afghan War and the annexation of Sindh?
171.x: Ellenborough ended the Afghan War and annexed Sindh in 1843.
171.tq: Link two contemporaneous measures to their common Governor-General.

171.s: The Anti-Slavery Act of 1843 was enacted during the tenure of:
171.x: The Anti-Slavery Act was enacted in 1843 during Lord Ellenborough’s tenure.
171.tq: Use the year as an anchor to distinguish adjacent Governor-Generalships.

171.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
171.x: The Treaty of Lahore of 1846 was concluded during Hardinge I’s tenure. Auckland started famine relief, Hardinge I was associated with the Anti-Human-Sacrifice Act and Dalhousie with the Widow Remarriage Act.
171.tq: Identify the swapped Governor-General in a group of closely dated administrative measures.

171.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Lord Dalhousie?
171.x: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793. Dalhousie was associated with the Doctrine of Lapse, the Caste Disabilities Removal Act and railway, post and telegraph development.
171.tq: Locate the historical outlier among measures of a single Governor-General.

171.s: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Governor-Generals?
o: Warren Hastings, Cornwallis, Wellesley, Minto I
Cornwallis, Warren Hastings, Wellesley, Minto I
Warren Hastings, Wellesley, Cornwallis, Minto I
Minto I, Wellesley, Cornwallis, Warren Hastings
171.x: Warren Hastings served first, followed by Cornwallis, Wellesley and Minto I.
171.tq: Use the first and last positions to eliminate reversed and partially swapped sequences.

171.s: Who among the following served as Governor-General immediately after Sir John Shore?
171.x: Sir John Shore served from 1793 to 1798, and Wellesley succeeded him in 1798.
171.tq: Test succession through the boundary years of adjoining tenures.

171.s:
Arrange the following Governor-Generals in chronological order:
A. Sir George Barlow
B. Minto I
C. Cornwallis, second term
D. Wellesley
171.x: Wellesley served before Cornwallis’s second term; Cornwallis’s second term was followed by Sir George Barlow and then Minto I.
171.tq: Fix Wellesley as the earliest and Minto I as the latest, then arrange the middle pair.

171.s: Which Governor-General died at Ghazipur during his second term in office?
171.x: Cornwallis returned for a second term in 1805 and died at Ghazipur during that term.
171.tq: Use the exceptional second tenure to distinguish Cornwallis from the regular succession.

171.s: Which one of the following is the correct tenure of Marquess Hastings as Governor-General?
171.x: Marquess Hastings served as Governor-General from 1813 to 1823. The other periods correspond to Sir George Barlow, Minto I and Amherst respectively.
171.tq: Match the exact tenure with nearby consecutive administrations.

171.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding William Bentinck’s tenure?
o: He served from 1823 to 1828 and was followed by Amherst.
He served from 1835 to 1836 and was followed by Auckland.
He served as Governor-General from 1828 to 1835 and became Governor-General of India from 1833.
He served as Governor-General only from 1833 to 1835.
171.x: Bentinck served from 1828 to 1835; after the Charter Act of 1833, he held the title Governor-General of India from 1833 onward.
171.tq: Separate the full tenure from the shorter period after the title changed.

171.s: The Vellore Mutiny of 1806 occurred during the tenure of:
171.x: The Vellore Mutiny occurred in 1806 during the tenure of Sir George Barlow.
171.tq: Use the event year to identify the Governor-General in office.

171.s: The Code of Gentoo Laws was compiled during the tenure of:
171.x: The Code of Gentoo Laws was prepared in 1776 during Warren Hastings’s tenure.
171.tq: Match the distinctive legal compilation with the correct early Governor-General.

171.s: The Ring Fence policy of Warren Hastings was intended primarily to:
o: Introduce direct British rule in Punjab
Create Awadh as a buffer state
171.x: The Ring Fence policy treated Awadh as a buffer state to protect British territories from external threats.
171.tq: Infer the purpose of a policy from its strategic description rather than its name alone.

171.s: Thuggee suppression with the assistance of Sleeman is associated with:
171.x: The suppression of Thuggee, with Sleeman’s assistance, took place during William Bentinck’s tenure.
171.tq: Apply the official–associate pairing without confusing it with military campaigns of later Governors-General.

171.s: The Public Works Department was established during the tenure of:
171.x: The Public Works Department was established during Lord Dalhousie’s tenure.
171.tq: Match the department with the Governor-General known for infrastructure expansion.

171.s: The liberation of the press in British India is associated with:
171.x: Sir Charles Metcalfe is associated with the liberation of the press during his brief tenure in 1835–36.
171.tq: Distinguish a press reform from the Charter Act and other administrative measures of nearby periods.

171.s: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed during the tenure of:
171.x: The Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the transition between Minto I and Marquess Hastings, whose tenure began in 1813.
171.tq: Handle an event falling at the boundary between two consecutive tenures.

171.s: The Treaty of Bassein of 1802 was concluded during the tenure of:
171.x: The Treaty of Bassein was concluded in 1802 during Lord Wellesley’s tenure, in the context of the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
171.tq: Match the treaty year with the Governor-General serving at that time.

171.s: The Anglo-Nepal War of 1814–1816 and the Treaty of Sugauli were associated with:
171.x: The Anglo-Nepal War took place during the tenure of Marquess Hastings, and the Treaty of Sugauli was concluded in 1816.
171.tq: Use the war period and treaty year together to identify the correct tenure.

171.s: The Treaty of Yandabo, which ended the First Anglo-Burmese War, was concluded during the tenure of:
171.x: The First Anglo-Burmese War occurred from 1824 to 1826 during Amherst’s tenure, and the Treaty of Yandabo transferred Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim to the British sphere.
171.tq: Match the treaty with the war and the Governor-General in office.

171.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
171.x: The Second Anglo-Burmese War was fought during Dalhousie’s tenure. Auckland was associated with the First Anglo-Afghan War, Ellenborough with the war with Gwalior and Dalhousie with the Second Anglo-Sikh War.
171.tq: Find the campaign assigned to the wrong Governor-General among otherwise correct pairings.

171.s: The First Anglo-Sikh War and the Treaty of Lahore of 1846 occurred during the tenure of:
171.x: The First Anglo-Sikh War and the Treaty of Lahore occurred during Lord Hardinge I’s tenure.
171.tq: Distinguish the first Anglo-Sikh conflict from the later conflict under Dalhousie.

171.s: The office of Governor-General of Bengal was created by the:
171.x: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as its first holder.
171.tq: Match the constitutional title with the Act that created it.

171.s: Which Act changed the title to Governor-General of India?
171.x: The Charter Act of 1833 changed the title to Governor-General of India, and William Bentinck was the first holder of that title.
171.tq: Distinguish the Act changing the territorial scope of the title from the later Act creating the Viceroyship.

171.s: The title ‘Viceroy and Governor-General’ was created by the:
171.x: The Government of India Act of 1858 created the title Viceroy and Governor-General. Lord Canning was its first holder.
171.tq: Match the constitutional title with the statutory change that followed the transfer of power.

171.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal.
2. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.
3. Lord Canning was the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Robert Clive was the first Governor of Bengal, Warren Hastings the first Governor-General of Bengal and Lord Canning the first Viceroy and Governor-General.
171.tq: Distinguish the first holders of three successive constitutional titles.

171.s: William Bentinck was the:
o: First Governor-General of Bengal and first Viceroy
First Governor-General of India and last Governor-General of Bengal
First Governor of Bengal and first Governor-General of Bengal
First Viceroy and Governor-General and last Governor-General of India
171.x: William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India and also the last Governor-General of Bengal after the title changed in 1833.
171.tq: Use the changeover between titles to identify the person occupying both transitional positions.

171.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Popular title — Person
o: Father of Civil Services in India — Lord Cornwallis
Father of Modern Western Education in India — Lord Dalhousie
Father of Civil Services in India — Lord Wellesley
171.x: Lord Cornwallis is known as the Father of Civil Services in India. William Bentinck is associated with modern Western education, while Wellesley was described as the Bengal Tiger.
171.tq: Start from the sure title–person pair and reject swapped names.

171.s: Who among the following was popularly described as the "Bengal Tiger" in his own description?
171.x: Lord Wellesley described himself as the "Bengal Tiger".
171.tq: Use the exact title rather than associating the description with a neighbouring Governor-General.

171.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Richard Colley Wellesley — Earl of Mornington
2. Francis Rawdon-Hastings — Lord Moira
3. Gilbert Elliot — Minto I
4. James Andrew Broun-Ramsay — Dalhousie

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
171.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Wellesley was Richard Colley Wellesley, Hastings was Francis Rawdon-Hastings, Minto I was Gilbert Elliot, and Dalhousie was James Andrew Broun-Ramsay.
171.tq: Check each real-name and title pairing independently before selecting the complete combination.

171.s:
With reference to the impeachment of Warren Hastings, consider the following statements:
1. Edmund Burke and the Whigs impeached Warren Hastings in the British Parliament in 1787.
2. The impeachment was connected with alleged administrative excesses.
3. The trial ended in his conviction in 1795.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The trial ran from 1788 to 1795 and ended in Hastings's acquittal, so statement 3 is false.
171.tq: Find the outcome trap: acquittal has been changed to conviction.

171.s: The impeachment proceedings against Warren Hastings were initiated in which year?
171.x: Warren Hastings was impeached in 1787 by Edmund Burke and the Whigs in the British Parliament. The trial itself began in 1788.
171.tq: Separate the year of impeachment from the year in which the trial commenced.

171.s: The trial of Warren Hastings on impeachment charges continued from 1788 until:
171.x: The impeachment trial of Warren Hastings ran from 1788 to 1795 and ended in his acquittal.
171.tq: Distinguish the duration of the trial from the earlier year of impeachment.

171.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the charges associated with the impeachment of Warren Hastings?
o: Treatment of Chait Singh of Benares
Plunder of the Begums of Awadh
Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam
171.x: The charges included the Rohilla War, the treatment of Chait Singh, the plunder of the Begums of Awadh and the judicial murder of Nand Kumar. The Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was associated with Wellesley, not with the impeachment charges against Hastings.
171.tq: Find the item belonging to a different Governor-General and policy context.

171.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the successive changes in the title of the head of British administration in India?
o: Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Viceroy
Governor-General of Bengal → Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of India
Governor of Bengal → Governor-General of India → Governor-General of Bengal → Viceroy
Governor of Bengal → Viceroy → Governor-General of Bengal → Governor-General of India
171.x: The sequence was Governor of Bengal, Governor-General of Bengal from 1773, Governor-General of India from 1833, and Viceroy from 1858.
171.tq: Fix the first and last titles, then place the two intermediate constitutional changes in order.

171.s: The title of Governor-General of India replaced the title of Governor-General of Bengal in:
171.x: The title changed to Governor-General of India in 1833. The title of Viceroy came later in 1858.
171.tq: Distinguish the constitutional year of a title change from the years of earlier and later changes.

171.s: Which of the following sets of measures is correctly associated with Lord Wellesley in the Andhra-related context?
o: Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1798, Ceded Districts in 1800 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1801
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1801, Ceded Districts in 1798 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1800
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1829, Ceded Districts in 1833 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1858
Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam in 1843, Ceded Districts in 1845 and merger of Andhra into Madras in 1856
171.x: Under Wellesley, the Subsidiary Alliance with the Nizam was concluded in 1798, the Ceded Districts followed in 1800, and Andhra was merged into Madras in 1801.
171.tq: Use the sequence of the three dated measures to eliminate the shifted-year alternatives.

171.s:
Arrange the following social measures in chronological order:
A. Infanticide-related measure under Wellesley
B. Abolition of Sati under Bentinck
C. Abolition of slavery under Ellenborough
D. Prohibition of human sacrifice under Hardinge I
171.x: The measures are dated 1802, 1829, 1843 and 1845 respectively. Therefore, the correct order is A, B, C, D.
171.tq: Arrange the events by their stated years, beginning with the earliest reform.

171.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

Governor-General — Social measure
171.x: The prohibition of human sacrifice in 1845 is associated with Hardinge I. Dalhousie is associated with caste disabilities legislation in 1850 and widow remarriage in 1856.
171.tq: Watch for the swapped Governor-General in a ruler–measure pairing.

171.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social measures associated with the Governor-Generals:
1. Lord Wellesley is associated with an infanticide-related measure in 1802.
2. Lord Bentinck is associated with the abolition of Sati in 1829.
3. Lord Dalhousie is associated with caste disabilities legislation in 1850 and widow remarriage in 1856.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
171.x: All three statements are correct. The listed measures are associated respectively with Wellesley, Bentinck and Dalhousie in the stated years.
171.tq: Verify each ruler–reform–year combination before choosing the complete set.

172.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Durbar — Occasion

(a) 1877 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
(b) 1903 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
(c) 1911 — Coronation of King Edward VII
(d) 1877 — Coronation of King George V
o: 1877 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
1903 — Proclamation of Queen Victoria as Empress of India
172.x: The 1877 Delhi Durbar, held during Lord Lytton's tenure, proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India, or Kaiser-i-Hind.
172.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate the options with swapped monarchs.

172.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Delhi Durbars:
1. The 1877 Durbar was held during the tenure of Lord Lytton.
2. The 1903 Durbar was associated with the coronation of King Edward VII.
3. The 1911 Durbar was the only Durbar attended by the reigning monarch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
172.x: All three statements are correct. The 1877, 1903 and 1911 Durbars were respectively associated with Victoria, Edward VII and George V, and the 1911 Durbar was the only one attended by the monarch.
172.tq: Check each statement against the Durbar–Viceroy–occasion sequence.

172.s: The 1911 Delhi Durbar was held during the viceroyalty of
172.x: The 1911 Delhi Durbar was held during the tenure of Lord Hardinge II and was associated with the coronation of King George V.
172.tq: Use the viceroy–event association rather than relying only on the year.

172.s:
Which of the following was NOT announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911?

(a) Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
(b) Creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province
(c) Transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
(d) Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
o: Annulment of the Partition of Bengal
Creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province
Transfer of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi
Introduction of the Indian Councils Act, 1909
172.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 was enacted during the tenure of Minto II and was not an announcement of the 1911 Durbar. The other three measures were announced on 12 December 1911.
172.tq: Find the item belonging to a different viceroy and event cluster.

172.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Partition of Bengal
B. Delhi Durbar associated with the coronation of Edward VII
C. Delhi Durbar associated with the coronation of George V
D. Annulment of the Partition of Bengal

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
172.x: The correct sequence is 1903 Durbar, 1905 Partition of Bengal, 1911 Durbar, and the 1911 annulment of the Partition of Bengal.
172.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1905 event between the two Durbars.

172.s: The Delhi Conspiracy Case of 1912 was associated with an attempt to assassinate
o: Lord Lytton during the 1877 Delhi Durbar
Lord Curzon during the 1905 Partition announcement
