177.x: The Chalisa Famine of 1783–84 affected North India, including Delhi, Awadh and Punjab. The other pairs incorrectly interchange the regions or years of famines.
177.tq: Use the year-region pair to eliminate swapped famine locations.

177.s: The Chalisa famine derives its name from which of the following?
o: The forty-week duration of the famine
The forty districts affected by it
The forty relief centres established in North India
177.x: The name Chalisa is associated with Vikram Samvat 1840.
177.tq: Test the exact origin of a distinctive famine epithet.

177.s:
Consider the following statements about the Doji Bara famine:
1. It is also known as the skull famine.
2. It affected the Deccan, Hyderabad and the Northern Circars.
3. It occurred in 1791–92.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
177.x: The Doji Bara famine, also called the skull famine, occurred in 1791–92 and affected the Deccan, Hyderabad and the Northern Circars.
177.tq: Combine the epithet, region and year before selecting the coded option.

177.s: The Orissa and Ganjam famine of 1865–66 led to the appointment of which commission?
177.x: The Orissa and Ganjam famine of 1865–66 led to the Campbell Commission.
177.tq: Link a famine directly with the commission appointed after it.

177.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Great Famine of 1876–78 is correct?
o: It was confined to the Northern Circars under Cartier.
It occurred in West and Central India under Curzon.
It affected Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Bombay under Lytton.
It affected only Bengal and Bihar under Elgin II.
177.x: The Great Famine of 1876–78 affected Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Bombay and occurred during Lytton’s tenure. It also devastated Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra.
177.tq: Discriminate a famine by combining its year, affected regions and contemporary Viceroy.

177.s:
Arrange the following famines in chronological order:
A. Great Bengal Famine
B. Doji Bara Famine
C. Orissa and Ganjam Famine
D. Great Famine of 1876–78
177.x: The correct sequence is Great Bengal Famine (1770), Doji Bara (1791–92), Orissa and Ganjam (1865–66), and Great Famine (1876–78).
177.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle famines by year.

177.s: The famine of 1896–97 occurred in many parts of India during the tenure of which Viceroy?
177.x: The famine of 1896–97 occurred during the tenure of Elgin II and was associated with the Lyall Commission.
177.tq: Identify the Viceroy associated with a specific famine year.

177.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bengal Famine of 1943 — Bengal — Linlithgow and Wavell years
Great Famine of 1896–97 — Many parts of India — Elgin II
Great Bengal Famine of 1770 — Bengal — Lytton
Famine of 1899–1900 — West and Central India — Curzon
177.x: The Great Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred under Cartier, not Lytton. The other pairs are correctly matched.
177.tq: Find the swapped administrator in an otherwise familiar famine association.

177.s: Approximately how many people died in the Bengal Famine of 1943 according to the standard estimate?
177.x: The standard estimate given for the Bengal Famine of 1943 is about 30 lakh deaths.
177.tq: Distinguish the standard estimate from the approximate figure used in an earlier examination question.

177.s: Which of the following statements about famines in Andhra during the nineteenth century is correct?
o: Andhra experienced only two famines in the late nineteenth century.
Andhra experienced 11 famines in the late nineteenth century.
All the famines occurred exclusively in coastal districts.
The record begins only with the famine of 1945.
177.x: Andhra had 11 famines in the late nineteenth century. The other statements wrongly restrict their number, location or period.
177.tq: Reject extreme qualifiers such as ‘only’ and ‘exclusively’ when testing a numerical fact.

177.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with an early Andhra famine?
177.x: The famine of 1805–07 affected all districts. The 1811 famine was associated with Nellore, while the 1823 famine affected Kadapa, Kurnool, Chittoor, Guntur, Vizag and Nellore.
177.tq: Match the year with the correct affected area and avoid narrowing a wider regional description.

177.s:
Consider the following statements about the Guntur famine of 1832–33:
1. It was also called Nandana Karuvu.
2. Bodies were thrown into rivers during the famine.
3. About half the population is reported to have died in the famine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
177.x: The Guntur famine was also called Nandana Karuvu, caused very high mortality—reported as about two lakh or nearly half the population—and was marked by bodies being thrown into rivers.
177.tq: Test several descriptive details of one regional famine through a coded combination.

177.s: What was the principal economic cause associated with the Ganjam famine of 1865–66?
o: The Company stopped collecting revenue in the Northern Circars.
Irrigation expansion caused rice prices to fall after the war.
Ryots shifted from cotton to paddy during the American Civil War.
Ryots shifted from paddy to cotton during the American Civil War, followed by a collapse in cotton prices.
177.x: During the American Civil War, ryots shifted from paddy to cotton. After the war, cotton prices collapsed and rice became scarce, contributing to the Ganjam famine.
177.tq: Trace the cause-effect chain instead of selecting an isolated crop or price statement.

177.s: Migration during the Ganjam famine was reported to take place to which of the following places?
o: South Africa, Sri Lanka and Mauritius
177.x: Many people affected by the Ganjam famine migrated to South Africa, Sri Lanka and Mauritius.
177.tq: Recall the specific destinations associated with famine migration.

177.s: Budda Vengalareddy of Uyyalawada is associated with relief during which famine?
177.x: Budda Vengalareddy fed people during the Kurnool famine of 1866, which occurred in the context of the severe famine conditions following the Ganjam crisis. He received a gold medal from Queen Victoria and the title ‘Apara Danakarnudu’.
177.tq: Connect a relief worker with the famine and district in which his intervention occurred.

177.s: On which date did Budda Vengalareddy receive a gold medal from Queen Victoria?
177.x: Budda Vengalareddy received the gold medal on 1 January 1877 and was known as ‘Apara Danakarnudu’.
177.tq: Test an exact date attached to a notable relief activity.

177.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Great Madras Famine of 1876–78?
o: The famine was confined to Bengal and relief was organised exclusively through grain imports.
Laissez-faire relief aggravated the famine, while John Clough’s canal project was a notable relief effort.
It affected only Hyderabad and was relieved through the Temple wage alone.
It began after the Northern Coastal cyclones of 1945.
177.x: The Great Madras Famine affected Rayalaseema and coastal Andhra. Laissez-faire relief worsened the crisis, while missionary John Clough’s canal relief project was a notable response.
177.tq: Apply the relationship between policy failure, affected region and relief initiative.

177.s: The Northern Coastal Famine of 1945 followed which immediate cause?
o: A collapse in cotton prices after the American Civil War
177.x: The Northern Coastal Famine of 1945 followed cyclones. K. S. Gupta formed a Famine Relief Committee in response.
177.tq: Identify the immediate trigger rather than a cause belonging to another famine.

177.s: Who formed the Famine Relief Committee during the Northern Coastal Famine of 1945?
177.x: K. S. Gupta formed a Famine Relief Committee during the Northern Coastal Famine of 1945.
177.tq: Match the relief organisation with its associated organiser.

177.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Commission)
(a) Campbell
(b) Strachey
(c) Lyall
(d) MacDonnell

List-II (Viceroy)
(i) Curzon
(ii) Elgin II
(iii) John Lawrence
(iv) Lytton

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
177.x: Campbell was associated with John Lawrence, Strachey with Lytton, Lyall with Elgin II and MacDonnell with Curzon.
177.tq: Start from the sure commission–Viceroy pair and complete the code.

177.s: The Strachey Commission was appointed in connection with which famine and in which year?
177.x: The Strachey Commission was appointed in 1880 in the aftermath of the Great Famine of 1876–78, during Lytton’s tenure.
177.tq: Connect a commission with both its trigger famine and year of appointment.

177.s: Which commission assessed the causes of famine and recommended measures against future famines?
177.x: The Lyall Commission assessed the causes of famine and recommended measures to prevent or mitigate future famines.
177.tq: Distinguish the commission’s function from its associated famine year.

177.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Woodhead Commission — 1897 — Elgin II — famine of 1896–97
177.x: The MacDonnell Commission was appointed in 1901 during Curzon’s tenure in relation to the famine of 1899–1900. The other options interchange commission years, Viceroys or famine triggers.
177.tq: Check all three elements—commission, year and Viceroy—before accepting a match.

177.s: What was the principal emphasis of the MacDonnell Commission?
177.x: The MacDonnell Commission stressed early relief and greater irrigation as measures against famine.
177.tq: Identify the policy recommendation rather than the commission’s name or date.

177.s: The Famine Code of 1883 was framed primarily on the recommendations of which commission?
177.x: The Famine Code of 1883 was framed on the recommendations of the Strachey Commission of 1880.
177.tq: Link a policy code to the commission whose recommendations formed its basis.

177.s:
Consider the following provisions of the Famine Code:
1. Classification of stages of scarcity and famine
2. Relief works for the able-bodied
3. Gratuitous relief for the old and infirm
4. Suspension or remission of revenue
Which of the above were provisions of the Code?
177.x: The Famine Code provided for stages of scarcity and famine, relief works for able-bodied persons, gratuitous relief for the old and infirm, and suspension or remission of revenue.
177.tq: Recognise a complete set of administrative provisions rather than one isolated relief measure.

177.s: Which of the following was included in the Famine Code as a financial safeguard?
o: A Famine Relief and Insurance Fund
177.x: The Famine Code provided for a Famine Relief and Insurance Fund.
177.tq: Identify the exact official fund from among similarly worded administrative alternatives.

177.s: Which statement regarding famine policy during the Company period is correct?
o: The government adopted a comprehensive famine code and provided extensive relief.
The government never adopted a famine code and gave minimal relief.
The government suspended revenue in every famine without exception.
The government transferred all famine relief to village councils.
177.x: During the Company period, the government never adopted a famine code and provided only minimal relief.
177.tq: Watch for absolute claims about uniform revenue suspension or comprehensive relief.

177.s: The Temple wage during the Madras famine of 1877 consisted approximately of which ration?
o: About 1 pound of grain a day on relief works
About 5 pounds of grain a day on relief works
One rupee a day without grain
A weekly ration of ten pounds of rice
177.x: The Temple wage provided about 1 pound of grain per day on relief works and was criticised as a starvation wage.
177.tq: Distinguish the exact quantitative ration from plausible but exaggerated alternatives.

177.s: Who fixed the Temple wage during the Madras famine of 1877?
177.x: Sir Richard Temple fixed the relief ration known as the Temple wage during the Madras famine of 1877.
177.tq: Match a named policy with the official who introduced or fixed it.

177.s: Public works undertaken as famine relief commonly provided employment on which of the following?
177.x: Famine relief public works included employment on roads and canals.
177.tq: Identify the practical form of relief employment from the work categories given.

177.s: Which of the following famine duties associated with Kautilya included measures such as seeds, food, tax exemption and public works?
o: Famine relief responsibilities of the state
177.x: Kautilya’s famine duties included supplying seeds and food, granting tax exemption and undertaking public works.
177.tq: Infer the broader administrative purpose from a cluster of related measures.

177.s: The Guntur famine convinced the Company of the need for which long-term response?
177.x: The Guntur famine convinced the Company that irrigation was necessary, contributing to later irrigation initiatives associated with Arthur Cotton.
177.tq: Connect a crisis to the institutional policy response it produced.

177.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the sequence of the Godavari anicut project at Dowleswaram?
o: Report in 1844, sanction in 1846, work begun in 1847, main structure finished in April 1852
Report in 1846, sanction in 1847, work begun in 1852, main structure finished in 1855
Report in 1847, sanction in 1852, work begun in 1844, main structure finished in 1860
Report in 1852, sanction in 1844, work begun in 1846, main structure finished in 1872
177.x: Arthur Cotton’s Godavari anicut project was reported in 1844, sanctioned in 1846, begun in 1847 and had its main structure completed in April 1852.
177.tq: Arrange the project milestones in sequence, keeping the report before sanction and construction.

177.s: What was the reported cost of the Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram?
177.x: The Godavari anicut at Dowleswaram was constructed at a reported cost of only Rs 1,50,000.
177.tq: Identify the precise project cost rather than a rounded or magnified estimate.

177.s: Which of the following correctly describes the initial irrigation impact of the Godavari anicut?
o: Three main canals served about 6.62 lakh acres.
Three canals served exactly 10 lakh acres from the outset.
Two canals served about 2 lakh acres.
177.x: The Godavari anicut had three main canals serving about 6.62 lakh acres initially; the area later rose to 10 lakh acres for two crops.
177.tq: Separate the initial acreage and canal count from the later expanded irrigation figure.

177.s: The revenue associated with the Godavari irrigation works rose from approximately Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to what amount in 1894–95?
177.x: Revenue rose from Rs 20.38 lakh in 1853–54 to Rs 55.18 lakh in 1894–95.
177.tq: Read the two-point revenue comparison without confusing the initial and later values.

177.s: Arthur Cotton was born on which date?
177.x: Arthur Cotton was born on 15 May 1803.
177.tq: Test the exact birth date carried with a historical personality’s name.

177.s: Which of the following pairs relating to irrigation works is correctly matched?
o: Krishna anicut — Bezwada — proposed by Henry Atlock Lake
Godavari anicut — Bezwada — supervised by Charles Orr
177.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was proposed by Colonel Henry Atlock Lake. The Penna anicut was at Nellore, while the K.C. Canal began from Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra.
177.tq: Use location and responsible engineer together to reject swapped irrigation projects.

177.s: Who supervised the construction of the Krishna anicut at Bezwada?
177.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was proposed by Colonel Henry Atlock Lake and supervised by Charles Orr.
177.tq: Distinguish the proposer from the person who supervised construction.

177.s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna anicut:
1. It was begun in 1853.
2. It was finished by the end of 1854.
3. It was located at Bezwada.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
177.x: The Krishna anicut at Bezwada was begun in 1853 and finished by the end of 1854.
177.tq: Combine project location and construction dates in a coded statement question.

177.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: K.C. Canal — Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra — 1872
177.x: The Godavari anicut was at Dowleswaram, not Nellore. The Penna anicut was at Nellore in 1860, and the K.C. Canal dates from 1872 at Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra.
177.tq: Find the wrong location in a list of otherwise correctly matched irrigation projects.

177.s: The Penna anicut at Nellore was constructed according to whose plan?
177.x: The Penna anicut at Nellore, dating from 1860, was constructed according to Arthur Cotton’s plan.
177.tq: Match the irrigation project with the engineer whose plan it followed.

177.s: The K.C. Canal of 1872 originated from which place and river system?
177.x: The K.C. Canal was constructed in 1872 from Sunkesula on the Tungabhadra.
177.tq: Discriminate irrigation works by their origin point and river basin.

177.s: The old anicut associated with Arthur Cotton was later replaced by which structure?
177.x: The old anicut was later replaced by the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage.
177.tq: Identify the later structure that replaced the original colonial-era anicut.

177.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of famines under colonial rule:
1. Rigid revenue collection aggravated the impact of drought.
2. Export of food grains contributed to famine conditions.
3. Famines were caused exclusively by failure of the monsoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
177.x: Rigid revenue collection and export of food grains were identified as important causes of famines. The nationalist critique rejected the view that famines resulted exclusively from monsoon failure.
177.tq: Identify the statement using the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and separate structural causes from a single natural cause.

177.s: Who among the following linked Indian famines with high land revenue and the drain of wealth?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji and Sir Arthur Cotton
177.x: Dadabhai Naoroji and R.C. Dutt connected famines with the burden of high land revenue and the drain of wealth.
177.tq: Use the thinker–argument association and reject combinations that mix a critic with an administrator or engineer.

177.s: With reference to R.C. Dutt, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: He wrote Open Letters to Lord Curzon in 1900.
He chaired the Woodhead Commission in 1944.
He led the construction of the Godavari anicut in 1833.
He introduced the IPC food-insecurity scale in 2025.
177.x: R.C. Dutt’s work titled Open Letters to Lord Curzon was associated with the year 1900. The other options incorrectly associate him with a famine commission, a modern food-security scale or an irrigation project.
177.tq: Match the historical personality with the precise work and year; the wrong options swap roles across different subjects.

177.s: The commercialisation of agriculture and the policy of laissez-faire relief had what effect on famine conditions?
o: They made food grains unavailable only in Europe.
They ended the drain of wealth.
They eliminated the impact of drought.
177.x: Commercialisation, illustrated by cotton cultivation in Ganjam, and laissez-faire relief deepened the disasters caused by famine.
177.tq: Apply the cause–effect relationship rather than selecting an option that reverses the stated impact.

177.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Famine-related item)
A. Campbell Commission
B. Woodhead Commission
C. Ganjam famine
D. Kurnool famine

List-II (Year or period)
1. 1833
2. 1865–66
3. 1866
4. 1944

Codes:
177.x: The Campbell Commission was associated with 1866, the Woodhead Commission with 1944, the Ganjam famine with 1865–66, and the Kurnool famine with 1866.
177.tq: Start from the sure commission–year pairs and then verify the famine periods.

177.s: The IPC food-insecurity scale places the following phases in which correct order from least severe to most severe?
177.x: The five phases progress from Phase 1 Minimal through Phase 2 Stressed, Phase 3 Crisis and Phase 4 Emergency to Phase 5 Catastrophe/Famine.
177.tq: Arrange the stages by increasing severity, beginning with the least severe and ending with famine.

177.s: A food-insecurity situation has reached Phase 4 on the IPC scale. It would be described as:
177.x: Phase 4 of the IPC food-insecurity scale is termed Emergency. Crisis is Phase 3 and Catastrophe/Famine is Phase 5.
177.tq: Translate the numerical phase into its exact official term without confusing adjacent stages.

177.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kurnool famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Guntur famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Ganjam famine — 1833; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
Guntur famine — 1944; impetus to Cotton’s Godavari anicut
177.x: The Guntur famine of 1833 led to the construction of Cotton’s Godavari anicut. The other options assign the event to the wrong famine or year.
177.tq: Discriminate between the closely associated Andhra famine names and their years.

177.s: Which of the following Andhra famine–period pairs is NOT correctly matched?
177.x: Ganjam was associated with the famine of 1865–66, not 1944. Guntur is associated with 1833 and Kurnool with 1866.
177.tq: Find the mismatched year by separating the Andhra famine dates from the year of the last colonial famine commission.

177.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Guntur famine
B. Campbell Commission
C. Ganjam famine
D. Woodhead Commission
177.x: The Guntur famine occurred in 1833, followed by the Campbell Commission in 1866, the Ganjam famine in 1865–66, and the Woodhead Commission in 1944. In the chronology convention used here, the overlapping 1865–66 famine is placed before the 1866 commission.
177.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then resolve the closely placed 1865–66 and 1866 events.

177.s: Modern food security, as reflected through the Public Distribution System, rests on which of the following three elements?
177.x: Modern food security through the PDS is based on availability, accessibility and affordability of food.
177.tq: Recall the three-part framework and distinguish positive food-security conditions from policy instruments or problems.

177.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the first and the last famine commissions of the colonial period mentioned in the context of British India?
o: Campbell Commission in 1866 and Woodhead Commission in 1944
Woodhead Commission in 1866 and Campbell Commission in 1944
Lyall Commission in 1866 and Hunter Commission in 1944
Campbell Commission in 1833 and Woodhead Commission in 1865–66
177.x: The Campbell Commission of 1866 was the first famine commission, while the Woodhead Commission of 1944 was the last colonial famine commission.
177.tq: Use the first–last comparison and verify both the commission names and their years.

178.s: Which was the first educational institution set up by the East India Company in India?
178.x: Calcutta Madrasa, established in 1781, was the first educational institution set up by the Company in India.
178.tq: Use the institutional sequence and identify the earliest establishment.

178.s: Calcutta Madrasa was established in 1781 under the patronage of:
178.x: Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781.
178.tq: Match the institution with its founder rather than its year alone.

178.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Asiatic Society of Bengal — William Jones
2. Sanskrit College, Benares — Jonathan Duncan
3. Hindu College, Calcutta — David Hare with leading Calcutta citizens
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
178.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The Asiatic Society was founded in 1784, the Sanskrit College in 1791, and Hindu College in 1817.
178.tq: Start from the sure institution-founder pairs and test all three matches.

178.s: The Sanskrit College at Benares was founded by:
178.x: Jonathan Duncan, the Resident at Benares, founded the Sanskrit College there in 1791.
178.tq: Discriminate between the commonly confused founders of the Sanskrit College and Asiatic Society.

178.s: Fort William College at Calcutta was established in 1800 by:
178.x: Lord Richard Wellesley established Fort William College in Calcutta in 1800 to train Company civil servants.
178.tq: Use the precise first name to avoid the Wellesley-name trap.

178.s: Fort William College was replaced by the East India College at Haileybury by:
178.x: Fort William College was replaced by the East India College at Haileybury in England by 1806.
178.tq: Separate the establishment year from the later replacement year.

178.s: Hindu College at Calcutta was established in:
178.x: Hindu College, Calcutta, was established in 1817 by David Hare with leading citizens of Calcutta.
178.tq: Arrange the institutional years mentally and select the corresponding date.

178.s: The principal purpose for establishing Fort William College was to:
o: Train civil servants of the East India Company
Provide primary education to Indian children
178.x: Fort William College was established to train Company civil servants.
178.tq: Identify the institution from its stated administrative purpose.

178.s: Wood's Despatch of 1854 was drafted by Sir Charles Wood in his capacity as:
o: President of the General Committee of Public Instruction
Secretary of the Education Department of Madras
President of the Board of Control
178.x: Sir Charles Wood drafted the 1854 Despatch as President of the Board of Control.
178.tq: Distinguish the office held by the author from the office of the approving authority.

178.s: Wood's Despatch of 1854 was issued under the Governor-Generalship of:
178.x: The Despatch was drafted by Charles Wood in 1854 under Governor-General Dalhousie.
178.tq: Apply the author–Governor-General distinction to a major education document.

178.s: Which of the following represents the graded educational hierarchy envisaged by Wood's Despatch?
o: Universities → affiliated colleges → Anglo-vernacular schools → vernacular primary schools
Vernacular primary schools → Anglo-vernacular high schools → affiliated colleges → universities
Anglo-vernacular schools → universities → primary schools → affiliated colleges
Affiliated colleges → vernacular primary schools → universities → high schools
178.x: The Despatch proposed a hierarchy beginning with vernacular primary schools and progressing through Anglo-vernacular high schools and affiliated colleges to universities.
178.tq: Read the educational structure from its base upward.

178.s: Which one of the following was a provision of Wood's Despatch of 1854?
o: Replacement of English by Persian in higher education
Exclusive state control over every school
Introduction of grants-in-aid to encourage private educational enterprise
Abolition of all vernacular primary schools
178.x: Wood's Despatch introduced a grants-in-aid system to encourage private, largely missionary, educational enterprise.
178.tq: Identify the positive institutional provision among reversed policy statements.

178.s:
With reference to Wood's Despatch, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended government supervision of vernacular education.
2. It provided for the training of teachers.
3. It prescribed English for higher education and vernacular languages for lower education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
178.x: Wood's Despatch recommended supervision of vernacular education, teacher training, and a differentiated language policy using English at higher levels and vernacular languages at lower levels.
178.tq: Test the provisions together and watch for the language-level distinction.

178.s: The universities proposed in the presidency towns under Wood's Despatch were modelled on the:
178.x: Wood's Despatch proposed universities in the presidency towns on the model of London University.
178.tq: Match the institutional model with the education policy document.

178.s: Which policy position was rejected by Wood's Despatch of 1854?
178.x: Wood's Despatch rejected the downward filtration theory and asked the Company to take up mass education.
178.tq: Identify the rejected policy among the provisions actually recommended.

178.s: The result-based grants-in-aid to primary schools in Andhra were introduced from:
178.x: In Andhra, result-based grants-in-aid to primary schools began from 1877-78.
178.tq: Distinguish the Andhra follow-up date from the dates of the main education policies.

178.s: Macaulay's Minute on education was approved by:
178.x: Macaulay's Minute of 1835 was approved by Lord William Bentinck, who is associated with modern Western education in India.
178.tq: Match the policy document with the Governor-General who approved it.

178.s: T.B. Macaulay wrote the Minute on Education while serving as:
o: Resident at Benares and Director of Public Instruction
Law Member and President of the General Committee of Public Instruction
Education Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council
President of the Board of Control and Governor-General
178.x: Macaulay was the Law Member and President of the General Committee of Public Instruction when he wrote the Minute.
178.tq: Combine the person with his specific institutional positions.

178.s: The principal recommendation of Macaulay's Minute regarding the use of education funds was to spend them:
o: Equally on Persian, Arabic and English education
Exclusively on English-medium teaching of Western science and literature
Exclusively on Sanskrit and Arabic learning
178.x: Macaulay recommended that education funds be used exclusively for English-medium teaching of Western science and literature.
178.tq: Test the exact policy preference rather than the broader objective of education.

178.s: Which of the following best describes the Downward Filtration Theory?
o: A small upper class should first be educated so that learning would filter down to the masses
Education should begin with village schools and move upward to universities
Traditional learning should filter into English institutions through translation
Primary education should be universal before higher education is introduced
178.x: The theory proposed educating a small upper class first, expecting knowledge to descend or filter down to the wider population.
178.tq: Translate the policy theory into its practical educational sequence.

178.s: Macaulay's proposed educated class was intended to be:
o: Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect
Indian in language and tradition, but European in administration only
English in blood and colour, but Indian in taste and intellect
Indian in blood, colour, taste, opinions, morals and intellect
178.x: Macaulay sought a class Indian in blood and colour but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect, to act as interpreters between rulers and ruled.
178.tq: Use the precise wording of the famous formulation to reject reversed descriptions.

178.s: Which statement correctly reflects Macaulay's view expressed in the Minute?
o: European literature should be excluded from Indian education.
A single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.
Arabic and Sanskrit literature alone should receive public funds.
The whole native literature of India and Arabia was superior to European literature.
178.x: Macaulay made the well-known comparison that a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia.
178.tq: Recognise the exact author–remark association and avoid reversing the comparison.

178.s: The principal area of concern of the Hunter Commission was:
o: Only technical education in presidency towns
178.x: The Hunter Commission focused primarily on primary and secondary education.
178.tq: Identify the commission from its educational level of focus.

178.s: Which of the following was recommended by the Hunter Commission?
o: All private educational enterprise should be prohibited
Universities should be placed under direct imperial control
Primary education should be conducted only in English
Schools should be handed over to local boards and municipalities
178.x: The Hunter Commission recommended handing schools to local boards and municipalities and encouraged private enterprise.
178.tq: Select the decentralising recommendation from among centralising and language traps.

178.s: The Hunter Commission gave particular attention to education among:
o: Only European residents and Company officials
Backward classes, especially Muslims, and women
178.x: The Commission emphasised education for backward classes, especially Muslims, and for women.
178.tq: Test the specific beneficiary groups rather than the general objective.

178.s: The recommendations of the Hunter Commission took effect in:
178.x: The recommendations of the Hunter Commission took effect in 1883-84.
178.tq: Distinguish the commission year from the year in which its recommendations were implemented.

178.s: The Indian Universities Commission of 1902 was associated with which Viceroy?
178.x: The Indian Universities Commission was appointed in 1902 during Lord Curzon's Viceroyalty.
178.tq: Use the commission–Viceroy pairing to eliminate neighbouring period figures.

178.s: The Indian Universities Commission of 1902 led to the:
178.x: The 1902 Indian Universities Commission led to the Indian Universities Act of 1904, which increased government control over universities.
178.tq: Link the commission to its immediate legislative outcome.

178.s: The Resolution on Education Policy of 1913 was issued during the Viceroyalty of:
178.x: The 1913 Resolution on Education Policy was issued during the Viceroyalty of Lord Hardinge II.
178.tq: Match the policy resolution with its Viceroy and year.

178.s: The Resolution on Education Policy of 1913 mainly responded to the demand of Gokhale for:
o: English as the sole medium at all levels
178.x: The 1913 Resolution responded to Gokhale's demand for compulsory primary education and provided funding for primary education.
178.tq: Identify the policy response from the demand associated with it.

178.s: The Sadler Commission was primarily concerned with:
178.x: The Sadler, or Calcutta University, Commission of 1917-19 focused on university education.
178.tq: Distinguish university-focused commissions from primary-education commissions.

178.s: Which educational sequence was recommended by the Sadler Commission?
o: Twelve-year school course followed directly by a four-year degree
Twelve-year school course, an intermediate stage and a three-year degree
Ten-year school course followed directly by a two-year degree
Eight-year school course followed by a five-year degree
178.x: The Sadler Commission recommended a 12-year school course, an intermediate stage, and a three-year degree.
178.tq: Compare the duration and intermediate stage instead of relying only on the commission name.

178.s: The Sadler Commission was appointed during the Viceroyalty of:
178.x: The Sadler Commission of 1917-19 was appointed during the Viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford.
178.tq: Match the commission's period with the correct Viceroy.

178.s: The Hartog Committee of 1929 concentrated on:
178.x: The Hartog Committee examined wastage and stagnation in primary education and continued to support vernacular education.
178.tq: Identify the committee from its distinctive technical terms.

178.s: The Hartog Committee was constituted during the Viceroyalty of:
178.x: The Hartog Committee was constituted in 1929 during Lord Irwin's Viceroyalty.
178.tq: Pair the late-colonial committee with its Viceroy rather than its subject alone.

178.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
178.x: The Hartog Committee of 1929 was associated with Lord Irwin, not Lord Wavell. Wavell was the Viceroy associated with the Sargent Plan of 1944.
178.tq: Locate the swapped Viceroy in a multi-column factual match.

178.s: The Sargent Plan was formulated in:
178.x: The Sargent Plan was formulated in 1944 during the Viceroyalty of Lord Wavell.
178.tq: Use the sequence of later education plans to identify the final chronological entry.

178.s: The Sargent Plan envisaged universal free and compulsory education for children in the age group:
178.x: The Sargent Plan proposed universal, free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
178.tq: Recall the exact age range and reject shifted lower or upper limits.

178.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Charter Act
B. General Committee of Public Instruction
C. English Education Act
D. Wood's Despatch
178.x: The Charter Act was passed in 1813, the General Committee was established in 1823, the English Education Act followed in 1835, and Wood's Despatch was issued in 1854.
178.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate measures.

178.s: The Charter Act of 1813 provided an annual sum of Rs 1 lakh for:
o: Training Company civil servants in England
Revival of Indian literature and promotion of science
Compulsory primary education for all children
Construction of universities in presidency towns
178.x: The Charter Act earmarked Rs 1 lakh annually for the revival of Indian literature and the promotion of science.
178.tq: Match the financial provision with its stated educational purpose.

178.s: Which statement regarding the educational provision of the Charter Act of 1813 is correct?
o: The sum was withdrawn after the establishment of Fort William College.
The sum was actually released only in the 1830s.
The provision applied only to missionary schools.
The earmarked sum was actually released immediately in 1813.
178.x: Although the Charter Act earmarked Rs 1 lakh annually, the amount was actually released only in the 1830s.
178.tq: Separate the year of an authorization from the later year of actual release.

178.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Charter Act of 1813 mentioned in the context of education and colonial policy?
o: Establishing the General Committee of Public Instruction
Ending the Company's trade monopoly except over tea and China trade
Earmarking Rs 1 lakh for literature and science
178.x: The General Committee of Public Instruction was set up in 1823, not by the Charter Act of 1813. The Act admitted missionaries, ended most of the Company's trade monopoly, and earmarked Rs 1 lakh.
178.tq: Separate the Charter Act provisions from the later institutional measure of 1823.

178.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction was established in 1823 primarily to:
178.x: The General Committee of Public Instruction was set up in 1823 to manage the education grant.
178.tq: Identify the administrative function attached to the committee's creation.

178.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction became the institutional arena for the dispute between:
178.x: The Committee contained the competing Orientalist and Anglicist camps, whose dispute shaped educational policy.
178.tq: Match the committee with the distinctive policy debate conducted within it.

178.s: The English Education Act of 1835 made English the medium of:
178.x: The English Education Act of 1835 made English the medium of higher education.
178.tq: Distinguish higher education from the vernacular medium prescribed for lower education under Wood's Despatch.

178.s: The English Education Act of 1835 was associated with:
o: Lord Ripon and the Hunter Commission
Lord Wavell and the Sargent Plan
178.x: The 1835 Act was enacted under Bentinck on the basis of Macaulay's Minute.
178.tq: Link the legislation to its immediate author and approving Governor-General.

178.s: The 1835 resolution dealt a fatal blow to the:
o: Calcutta Madrasa and Sanskrit College system
Madras district and tahsildari vernacular schools
Presidency universities in Bombay and Calcutta
178.x: The 1835 resolution dealt a fatal blow to the district and tahsildari vernacular schools of the Madras Presidency.
178.tq: Identify the precise regional institutions affected by the policy change.

178.s: Which statement correctly describes the sequence involving Dalhousie's Minute and Wood's Despatch?
o: Wood's Despatch supported vernacular education and was followed by Dalhousie's Minute.
Dalhousie's Minute supported vernacular education and was followed by Wood's Despatch.
Both documents rejected vernacular education in favour of Persian.
Dalhousie's Minute preceded the Charter Act of 1813.
178.x: Dalhousie's Minute of 1853 backed vernacular education, and Wood's Despatch followed in 1854.
178.tq: Use both sequence and policy direction to distinguish two closely related documents.

178.s: Which of the following pairs represents the Orientalist position correctly?
o: Traditional learning in Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian
Universal free education in English for ages 6-14
University education through a three-year degree after an intermediate stage
Western sciences and English literature in English
178.x: Orientalists wanted traditional learning in Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian to be supported.
178.tq: Separate the two camps by their preferred content and medium of education.

178.s: Which of the following pairs represents the Anglicist position correctly?
o: Rejection of Western literature and science
Traditional learning in Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian
Western sciences and English literature taught in English
178.x: Anglicists favoured Western sciences and English literature taught through English.
178.tq: Use the content–language combination to distinguish Anglicists from Orientalists.

178.s: Who was the leader of the Anglicist group in the education debate?
178.x: T.B. Macaulay was the leader of the Anglicist group.
178.tq: Match the debate camp with its principal protagonist.

178.s: Which of the following was associated with the Orientalist group?
178.x: H.T. Colebrooke was an Orientalist. H.H. Wilson was another prominent Orientalist, whereas Macaulay, Bentinck and Trevelyan were associated with the Anglicist side.
178.tq: Identify the camp affiliation of a named protagonist.

178.s: In the Madras Presidency, Thomas Munro supported:
o: English-only education in higher and lower schools
University education on the London model
178.x: Thomas Munro supported pathashalas and vernacular schooling in the Madras Presidency.
178.tq: Apply the regional exception within the broader Orientalist–Anglicist debate.

178.s: Thomas Munro's Survey of Indigenous Education in 1826 found:
o: No organised system of village education in Madras
A complete absence of pathashalas in rural areas
Only English-medium colleges in the presidency towns
A wide network of vernacular village schools in the Madras Presidency
178.x: Munro's 1826 survey found a wide network of vernacular village schools in the Madras Presidency.
178.tq: Use the survey's empirical finding to reject absolute claims about indigenous education.

178.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Thomas Munro — English-only education in Madras
178.x: Thomas Munro supported pathashalas and vernacular schooling, not English-only education in Madras. Colebrooke and Wilson were Orientalists, while Trevelyan was an Anglicist.
178.tq: Find the reversed position of a regional education-policy protagonist.

178.s: Which missionary organisation was the first missionary body to spread Western education in Andhra?
178.x: The London Missionary Society was the first missionary body associated with the spread of Western education in Andhra. It began its work in 1805.
178.tq: Directly identify the earliest organisation from a group of closely related missionary bodies.

178.s: Kadapa became a centre of the London Missionary Society in which year?
178.x: Kadapa became a centre of the London Missionary Society in 1824; the Society had begun its work in 1805.
178.tq: Use the place-year association rather than confusing the date of the Society's establishment with its later centre.

178.s: The institution at Machilipatnam founded by Reverend Robert Noble is presently known as
178.x: The Machilipatnam institution founded by Reverend Robert Noble and upgraded in 1864 is now known as Noble College.
178.tq: Discriminate among similarly named colleges by linking the institution to its founder and location.

178.s: The Central Collegiate Institute at Madras, established in 1841, was the forerunner of which institution?
178.x: The Central Collegiate Institute, Madras, established in 1841, was the forerunner of Presidency College.
178.tq: Match the predecessor institution with the later college it developed into.

178.s:
With reference to the educational development of Rajahmundry, consider the following statements:
1. Elphinstone's scheme of 1839 produced a regional school at Rajahmundry in 1854.
2. A Government second-grade college was established there in 1873.
3. The institution became a degree college in 1877.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
178.x: Elphinstone's scheme led to the regional school at Rajahmundry in 1854, followed by a Government second-grade college in 1873 and a degree college in 1877.
178.tq: Test a developmental sequence by verifying each date and institutional stage.

178.s:
Arrange the following developments in Rajahmundry in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Government second-grade college
B. Elphinstone's scheme
C. Establishment of the regional school
D. Conversion into a degree college
178.x: Elphinstone's scheme dates to 1839, the regional school to 1854, the second-grade college to 1873 and the degree college to 1877.
178.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intervening institutional stages by year.

178.s: Who was G.N. Taylor in the context of education in the Godavari region?
o: The Sub-Collector of Godavari who promoted an Anglo-Vernacular School at Narsapur
The principal of Hindu College at Visakhapatnam
The founder of Noble College at Machilipatnam
The head of the North German Society at Rajahmundry
178.x: G.N. Taylor, or George Noble Taylor, was the Sub-Collector of Godavari who established the Anglo-Vernacular School at Narsapur in 1852.
178.tq: Use the official position and educational initiative to identify the correct individual.

178.s:
The Anglo-Vernacular School established at Narsapur in 1852 had branches at which of the following places?
1. Palakollu
2. Penugonda
3. Achanta
4. Eluru
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
178.x: The Narsapur Anglo-Vernacular School had branches at Palakollu, Penugonda and Achanta. Eluru was associated with the North German Society, not listed as a branch of this school.
178.tq: Separate the places directly linked with one institution from a nearby missionary centre.

178.s: Who drafted the 1854 Godavari District Education Scheme?
178.x: G.N. Taylor drafted the Godavari District Education Scheme in 1854 while serving as Sub-Collector of Godavari.
178.tq: Avoid the founder-substitution trap by associating the scheme with the official who prepared it.

178.s: G.N. Taylor was based at which place while serving in the Rajahmundry sub-division?
178.x: G.N. Taylor was based at Narsapur while serving as Sub-Collector of the Godavari region under the Rajahmundry sub-division.
178.tq: Distinguish an official's base from the wider district or sub-division in which he served.

178.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mrs A.V.N. College — former Hindu College, Visakhapatnam
178.x: Noble College is located at Machilipatnam, not Rajahmundry. Hindu College was established at Visakhapatnam and is now known as Mrs A.V.N. College, while Khallikota College is at Berhampur.
178.tq: Find the wrong location by checking each institution-place pairing.

178.s: Hindu College at Visakhapatnam was established in
178.x: Hindu College was established at Visakhapatnam in 1878 and is now known as Mrs A.V.N. College.
178.tq: Distinguish adjacent institutional years by matching each year with its specific college.

178.s: Khallikota College, established in 1879, is located at
178.x: Khallikota College was established at Berhampur in 1879.
178.tq: Directly connect the institution with its stated location while separating it from other Andhra colleges.

178.s: Which missionary organisation was active at Rajahmundry and Eluru in 1843?
178.x: The North German Society was active at Rajahmundry and Eluru in 1843.
178.tq: Identify the organisation from its paired regional centres and year.

178.s: Father Heyer was associated with the spread of education through the Lutherans in
178.x: Father Heyer was associated with the Lutheran missionary work in Guntur.
178.tq: Discriminate between missionary organisations by matching the named missionary with the correct centre.

178.s:
The American Baptists operated mission activities mainly in which of the following areas?
1. Rayalaseema
2. Ongole
3. Nellore
4. Guntur
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
178.x: The American Baptists were active in Rayalaseema, Ongole and Nellore. Guntur was associated with the Lutherans under Father Heyer.
178.tq: Use organisational-area associations to eliminate the centre belonging to another mission.

178.s: The admission of Sudras and Panchamas to mission schools primarily indicates that these institutions
o: were established exclusively for European children
extended educational access beyond the traditional privileged groups
functioned solely as military training centres
178.x: Mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, thereby extending education to social groups that had often been excluded from traditional educational institutions.
178.tq: Infer the social implication of an institutional policy rather than merely recalling a name or date.

178.s: Which of the following correctly describes a significance of English education in coastal Andhra?
o: It eliminated the need for primary education among the masses
It prevented the emergence of a pan-Indian educated elite
It remained confined entirely to missionary personnel
It created a reformist middle class, including figures such as Kandukuri Veeresalingam
178.x: English education contributed to the emergence of a reformist middle class in coastal Andhra, represented by Kandukuri Veeresalingam, and also helped create a pan-Indian educated elite.
178.tq: Select the option that captures both the regional and wider social consequence without an extreme claim.

178.s: Which educational policy approach was criticised for neglecting mass literacy?
178.x: The downward filtration approach was criticised because it prioritised educating a limited section and neglected mass literacy.
178.tq: Match the criticism with the exact policy term rather than a general education objective.

178.s: Which commissions repeatedly returned attention to primary education in their discussions?
178.x: The Hunter and Hartog Commissions repeatedly emphasised the importance of primary education, especially against the limitations of downward filtration.
178.tq: Pair the related commissions with the common policy concern they addressed.

179.s: Who founded the Marathi newspaper ‘Kesari’ in 1881?
179.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded ‘Kesari’ in Marathi in 1881.
179.tq: Use the founder–newspaper association directly.

179.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
179.x: Surendranath Banerjea was associated with ‘The Bengalee’. The other newspapers were associated with different founders or editors.
179.tq: Check the sure newspaper–editor pair and eliminate swapped associations.

179.s: The newspaper ‘The Hindu’, founded in Madras in 1878, was associated with:
o: Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
Mutnuri Krishna Rao and A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu
G. Subramania Iyer and M. Veeraraghavachariar
Ram Mohan Roy and Surendranath Banerjea
179.x: ‘The Hindu’ was associated with G. Subramania Iyer and M. Veeraraghavachariar and was an English newspaper founded in Madras in 1878.
179.tq: Test a paired founder/editor association with nearby newspaper names as traps.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra newspapers:
1. Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
2. It began as a weekly from Bombay in 1908 and became a daily from Madras in 1914.
3. Krishna Patrika was edited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao at Machilipatnam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, while Krishna Patrika was edited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao at Machilipatnam.
179.tq: Combine founder, place and publication-history facts in a statement set.

179.s: Which newspaper is regarded as the first political magazine of Andhra?
179.x: Andhra Prakasika, associated with A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu, is identified as the first political magazine of Andhra.
179.tq: Distinguish a specific description from closely related newspaper names.

179.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Newspaper)
A. Sambad Kaumudi
B. Mirat-ul-Akhbar
C. Andhra Prakasika
D. Krishna Patrika

List-II (Founder or editor)
1. A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu
2. Ram Mohan Roy
3. Mutnuri Krishna Rao

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
179.x: Ram Mohan Roy founded both Sambad Kaumudi and Mirat-ul-Akhbar; Andhra Prakasika was associated with A.P. Parthasarathy Naidu and Krishna Patrika with Mutnuri Krishna Rao.
179.tq: Start from the repeated Ram Mohan Roy pair and then complete the matching.

179.s: Which of the following early Telugu journals was published from Madras during 1837–1838?
179.x: Vrittanti was an early Telugu journal published from Madras during 1837–1838.
179.tq: Use the place-and-period combination to distinguish similar early journals.

179.s: Who was associated with the Telugu journal ‘Vartamana Tarangini’ published in 1842?
179.x: ‘Vartamana Tarangini’, published in 1842, was associated with Sayyad Rahamtulla.
179.tq: Test the editor or associate linked to a specific regional journal.

179.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
179.x: Satyaduta dates to 1835; it was not the journal published from Masulipatnam in 1848. Hitavadi was associated with Masulipatnam and J. Edmund Sharky.
179.tq: Find the single swapped date-and-place association.

179.s: Which of the following was NOT among the journals associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
179.x: Andhra Kesari was associated with Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao. Veeresalingam was associated with Vivekavardhini, Hasyasanjivani and Sati Hitabodhini, among others.
179.tq: Use the odd association within a list of publications.

179.s: Which of the following newspapers was associated with the Home Rule movement in Andhra?
179.x: Desamata, associated with Chilakamarti, was among the press publications supportive of the Home Rule movement, along with Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika.
179.tq: Identify the movement-specific newspaper from a regional list.

179.s: The series ‘Telugu Prajala Prasthuta Paristhiti’ was written in ‘The Hindu’ by:
179.x: Sitarama Sastri of Guntur wrote the series ‘Telugu Prajala Prasthuta Paristhiti’ in ‘The Hindu’.
179.tq: Link a distinctive title to its author rather than to the newspaper editor.

179.s:
Arrange the following press laws in chronological order:
A. Registration Act
B. Licensing Regulations
C. Press Act of Metcalfe
D. Censorship of Press Act
179.x: The sequence is Censorship of Press Act (1799), Licensing Regulations (1823), Metcalfe’s Press Act (1835), and Registration Act (1867).
179.tq: Arrange by the years first, then verify the middle two laws.

179.s: The Censorship of Press Act of 1799 was introduced during the tenure of:
179.x: Wellesley introduced the Censorship of Press Act in 1799, which imposed wartime pre-censorship.
179.tq: Match the law with its Governor-General and avoid the nearby names in the sequence.

179.s: Which one of the following provisions was associated with the Licensing Regulations of 1823?
o: Printing without a licence was penalised
Security deposits were imposed on newspapers during the Swadeshi movement
Printers were required to register under the Press and Registration of Books Act
Magistrates could seize presses inciting violence
179.x: The Licensing Regulations of 1823 introduced stricter licensing and penalised printing without a licence.
179.tq: Identify the provision belonging to the correct law rather than a later press measure.

179.s: Who was the acting Governor-General associated with the Licensing Regulations of 1823?
179.x: The Licensing Regulations of 1823 were issued under John Adams as acting Governor-General.
179.tq: Test the acting office-holder, a common close-name trap.

179.s: The Press Act of 1835 is popularly associated with which description?
179.x: Charles Metcalfe’s Press Act of 1835 repealed the 1823 restrictions and earned him the description ‘liberator of the Indian press’.
179.tq: Distinguish the positive label of Metcalfe’s measure from the negative label of the Vernacular Press Act.

179.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Registration Act was enacted in 1867.
2. It dealt with the registration of printers and presses.
3. It was associated with John Lawrence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: All three statements are correct. The 1867 Registration Act, formally linked with the Press and Registration of Books framework, concerned registration of printers and presses under John Lawrence.
179.tq: Test year, authority and provision together.

179.s: Under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code, which act was treated as an offence from 1870?
o: Printing a newspaper without depositing security
Publishing without registering a printing press
Refusing to submit proofs to a censor
179.x: Sedition under Section 124A IPC made ‘exciting disaffection’ an offence in 1870 during the tenure of Lord Mayo.
179.tq: Recall the exact statutory expression associated with the provision.

179.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908 — Minto II
179.x: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act of 1908 was associated with Minto II and enabled magistrates to seize presses of papers inciting violence.
179.tq: Use the year–Governor-General pair to catch swapped authorities.

179.s: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act of 1908 empowered magistrates to:
o: Seize the presses of newspapers inciting violence
Appoint a press commissioner in every province
Repeal all licensing requirements for newspapers
179.x: The 1908 Act empowered magistrates to seize presses of newspapers that incited violence and was directed against extremist activities.
179.tq: Ask who exercised the power and what action the law authorised.

179.s: What was the principal feature of the Indian Press Act of 1910?
o: Abolition of all press registration requirements
Revival of Vernacular Press Act features with heavy security deposits
Transfer of press control to local self-government bodies
179.x: The Indian Press Act of 1910 revived features of the Vernacular Press Act and imposed heavy security deposits.
179.tq: Identify the later law that revived an earlier restrictive pattern.

179.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Annie Besant’s newspapers:
1. ‘Commonweal’ and ‘New India’ were required to deposit security under the Press Act.
2. The deposit was first Rs 2,000 and later Rs 10,000.
3. The deposits were connected with the period 1916–17.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: All three statements are correct. Annie Besant’s ‘Commonweal’ and ‘New India’ faced deposits of Rs 2,000 followed by Rs 10,000 during 1916–17.
179.tq: Combine newspaper, amount and period in one coded statement question.

179.s: Which sequence correctly represents the broad development of press policy in colonial India?
o: Freedom after Metcalfe — gag of 1878 — repeal in 1882 — repression in 1908 and 1910
Gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe — repeal in 1882 — repression in 1908 and 1910
Repression in 1908 — repeal in 1882 — gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe
Repeal in 1882 — gag of 1878 — freedom after Metcalfe — repression in 1910
179.x: Metcalfe’s 1835 measure brought relative freedom, the 1878 Act imposed restrictions, it was repealed in 1882, and repression returned through the 1908 and 1910 measures.
179.tq: Trace the policy trend rather than merely ordering isolated dates.

179.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was introduced in the background of:
o: The Swadeshi movement and the First Factory Act
The famine of 1876–77 and the lavish Delhi Durbar of 1877
The Revolt of 1857 and the Ilbert Bill controversy
The Permanent Settlement and the Regulating Act
179.x: The Act was passed by Lord Lytton amid public anger over the 1876–77 famine and the lavish Delhi Durbar held in 1877.
179.tq: Connect a law with its immediate political and economic context.

179.s: Under the Vernacular Press Act, district magistrates could require printers and publishers of vernacular newspapers to:
o: Submit every article to the High Court
Obtain approval from the local legislature
Sign bonds against publishing seditious matter
179.x: District magistrates could require printers and publishers to sign bonds undertaking not to publish seditious matter.
179.tq: Identify the exact administrative power granted by the Act.

179.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Vernacular Press Act, 1878?
o: Security deposits could be demanded and forfeited
There was no appeal to a court of law
Presses could be seized for repeated offences
English-language newspapers were subjected to the same restrictions
179.x: The Act was discriminatory: it applied to Indian-language papers and not to English-language newspapers. The other three were provisions of the Act.
179.tq: Find the exception by testing the discriminatory scope of the law.

179.s: The exemption available under the Vernacular Press Act could be obtained by:
o: Depositing a fixed amount with the district court
Submitting proofs to a government censor before publication
Publishing an English summary after every vernacular article
Obtaining a certificate from the Legislative Council
179.x: A vernacular newspaper could obtain exemption by submitting its proofs to a government censor before publication.
179.tq: Recall the narrow procedural exception to a restrictive law.

179.s: Which of the following newspapers was among those targeted by the Vernacular Press Act?
179.x: Som Prakash was one of the newspapers targeted by the Vernacular Press Act, along with Bharat Mihir, Dacca Prakash and Samachar.
179.tq: Recognise a target newspaper from the specified list.

179.s: The Vernacular Press Act was repealed in 1882, and the pre-censorship clause was dropped. Which additional measure followed the repeal?
o: Transfer of press powers to district magistrates
Compulsory English publication by all newspapers
179.x: After the repeal in 1882, the pre-censorship clause was dropped and a press commissioner was appointed.
179.tq: Test the consequence of repeal rather than the identity of the repealing Viceroy.

179.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Act or policy)
A. Wood’s Despatch
B. First Factory Act
C. Famine Code
D. Resolution on Local Self-Government

List-II (Year)
1. 1854
2. 1881
3. 1882
4. 1883

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
179.x: Wood’s Despatch was issued in 1854, the First Factory Act in 1881, the Famine Code in 1883, and the Resolution on Local Self-Government in 1882.
179.tq: Start with the distinctive 1854 and 1883 dates, then resolve the remaining pair.

179.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
179.x: Wood’s Despatch was issued in 1854 during Dalhousie’s tenure. The First Factory Act and the measures of 1882–83 were associated with Ripon, while the Ilbert Bill controversy occurred under Ripon.
179.tq: Use the year–Viceroy combination and reject swapped office-holders.

179.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The First Factory Act dealt with child labour.
2. It is dated 1881 in the APPSC-aligned chronology.
3. It was associated with Lord Ripon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: All three statements are correct. The First Factory Act concerning child labour is placed in 1881 and was enacted during Ripon’s tenure.
179.tq: Handle a disputed-looking date by matching it with the stated examination chronology.

179.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Vernacular Press Act
B. Wood’s Despatch
C. Famine Code
D. First Factory Act
179.x: Wood’s Despatch was issued in 1854, followed by the Vernacular Press Act in 1878, the First Factory Act in 1881 and the Famine Code in 1883.
179.tq: Place the two close late-century measures by their exact years.

179.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
179.x: Wood’s Despatch of 1854 was associated with Dalhousie, not Ripon. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
179.tq: Find the wrong Governor-General in an otherwise familiar year–measure pair.

179.s: The first printing press in India was introduced by the:
179.x: Portuguese Jesuits introduced the first printing press in India at Goa in 1556.
179.tq: Identify the institution or group responsible for a historical introduction.

179.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Post Office Act of 1854:
1. It was associated with Lord Dalhousie.
2. It introduced uniform postage rates.
3. It provided for the use of postage stamps.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: The Post Office Act of 1854, associated with Dalhousie, introduced uniform postage rates and postage stamps.
179.tq: Combine the office, year and two specific administrative measures in a coded statement question.

179.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: Mayo — First telegraph line from Calcutta to Diamond Harbour
179.x: Railways, post and telegraph are all credited to Dalhousie. Mayo introduced state railways, while John Lawrence opened telegraph links with Europe.
179.tq: Test multiple administrator–measure associations and detect the swapped authority.

179.s: Who opened telegraph links between India and Europe?
179.x: John Lawrence opened telegraph links between India and Europe.
179.tq: Discriminate between closely related administrators associated with communications development.

179.s: The trunk telegraph lines linking Calcutta, Peshawar, Bombay and Madras had been established by the:
179.x: The trunk telegraph network linking Calcutta, Peshawar, Bombay and Madras was established by the mid-1850s.
179.tq: Use the chronological range to distinguish the early communications network from later developments.

179.s: Who introduced state railways in India?
179.x: Lord Mayo introduced state railways in India.
179.tq: Apply the who-did-what method to separate state railways from Dalhousie's broader transport initiatives.

179.s: The first railway in South India was opened on 1 July 1856 between:
179.x: The first railway in South India ran from Royapuram in Madras to Wallajah Road near Arcot on 1 July 1856.
179.tq: Distinguish the first South Indian railway from the first railway in India and the later Andhra line.

179.s: The Royapuram–Wallajah Road railway line was operated by the:
179.x: The first railway in South India was operated by the Madras Railway Company.
179.tq: Match a regional railway first with its operating company.

179.s: The Puttur–Renigunta railway line in Andhra was commissioned in:
179.x: The Puttur–Renigunta line was commissioned in 1862.
179.tq: Select the middle chronological milestone from closely related railway years.

179.s: How many railway lines were laid in Andhra between 1871 and 1900?
179.x: Nine railway lines were laid in Andhra during the period 1871–1900.
179.tq: Test a precise regional count rather than a general statement about railway expansion.

179.s: Under the railway guarantee system, private British companies were assured approximately what return on their capital from Indian revenues?
179.x: Private British railway companies were guaranteed a return of about 5 percent from Indian revenues, whether or not the lines made a profit.
179.tq: Identify the guaranteed percentage and reject nearby altered figures.

179.s: Which of the following best describes the railway guarantee system?
o: Indian companies guaranteed profits to the British government from railway revenue
Railway passengers were guaranteed free travel during famines
The government guaranteed that all railway lines would be constructed by Indian capital
Private British companies received a guaranteed return from Indian revenues irrespective of profit
179.x: The guarantee system assured private British companies about 5 percent interest from Indian revenues even when the railway lines did not make a profit.
179.tq: Apply the definition to a short administrative scenario and focus on who received the guarantee.

179.s: Dalhousie's Railway Minute of 1853 primarily provided for:
o: Free railway travel for Indian cultivators
The transfer of railway ownership to municipalities
A network of trunk lines serving military, commercial and administrative purposes
The abolition of private railway companies
179.x: Dalhousie's Railway Minute of 1853 set out a trunk-line network for military, commercial and administrative purposes.
179.tq: Link a policy document with its stated administrative objectives.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the colonial purposes of railway construction:
1. Railways facilitated the movement of troops.
2. Railways carried raw materials to ports.
3. Railways brought British manufactures into the interior.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Colonial railway construction served military movement, the export of raw materials and the internal distribution of British manufactures.
179.tq: Recognise the common colonial-economic pattern across three related statements.

179.s: Why did Indian nationalists count guaranteed railway interest as part of the drain of wealth?
o: It represented wages paid to Indian railway workers
It was collected from British manufacturers by Indian municipalities
It was paid from Indian revenues to private British companies even without corresponding profits
It was used exclusively for famine relief in India
179.x: Guaranteed interest was paid from Indian revenues to British private companies whether or not the railway lines earned profits, and nationalists treated this as a drain of wealth.
179.tq: Connect a financial mechanism with its nationalist economic interpretation.

179.s: Which one of the following was NOT an unintended effect of railway development in colonial India?
o: Shared public travel across caste groups
Complete end of colonial economic exploitation
179.x: The unintended effects included a national market, shared travel across castes and faster nationalist mobilisation. Railways did not end colonial economic exploitation.
179.tq: Find the option that contradicts the stated unintended consequences rather than the colonial purpose.

179.s: Railways were also used during famines mainly for:
o: Stopping all movement of food grains
Exporting all available grain without interruption
179.x: Despite their exploitative colonial purposes, railways were also used to move grain for famine relief.
179.tq: Identify the qualifying or beneficial function within a predominantly exploitative system.

179.s: The Charter Act of 1813 provided for expenditure of not less than how much per year on literature and science?
179.x: The Charter Act of 1813 provided for not less than Rs 1 lakh annually for literature and science.
179.tq: Test the exact statutory allocation using nearby monetary distractors.

179.s: Which statement regarding the educational provision of the Charter Act of 1813 is correct?
o: It established the universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
It permitted missionaries, although the allocated money was released only in the 1830s
It transferred all schools to municipal boards
It prohibited missionary activity in India
179.x: The Charter Act of 1813 allowed missionaries, while the money earmarked for education was released only in the 1830s.
179.tq: Use a qualification in the provision to avoid an overbroad statement.

179.s: The General Committee of Public Instruction, established in 1823, was mainly concerned with:
179.x: The General Committee of Public Instruction managed education funds.
179.tq: Match an educational body with its specific administrative function.

179.s: Wood's Despatch of 1854 is popularly known as the:
o: Magna Carta of English Education in India
179.x: Wood's Despatch of 1854 is known as the Magna Carta of English Education in India.
179.tq: Identify the exact epithet attached to a major policy document.

179.s: Which of the following was the educational structure envisaged by Wood's Despatch?
o: Only English education for the upper classes
Madrasas and Sanskrit colleges without modern institutions
University directly replacing all primary schools
Vernacular primary education, Anglo-vernacular high school and university education
179.x: Wood's Despatch envisaged vernacular primary schools, Anglo-vernacular high schools and universities, along with grants-in-aid.
179.tq: Reconstruct a sequence of educational stages from primary level to university.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about Wood's Despatch:
1. It recommended grants-in-aid.
2. It asked the Company to take up mass instruction.
3. It supported the downward filtration of education from a few upper-class Indians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: Wood's Despatch recommended grants-in-aid and mass instruction. It rejected, rather than supported, the downward filtration approach.
179.tq: Spot the reversed policy position in the statement about downward filtration.

179.s: The Hunter Commission of 1882 was associated with which Governor-General?
179.x: The Hunter Commission of 1882 was associated with Lord Ripon.
179.tq: Match a commission with the Governor-General during whose tenure it was appointed.

179.s: Which of the following was a recommendation or concern of the Hunter Commission?
o: Replacing all vernacular schools with English-only schools
Handing schools to local boards and municipalities
179.x: The Hunter Commission dealt with primary and secondary education and recommended handing schools to local boards and municipalities. It also addressed women's education and Muslim education.
179.tq: Select the institutional decentralisation measure associated with the commission.

179.s: The Resolution on Education Policy of 1913 was primarily a response to the demand of:
o: Gopal Krishna Gokhale for compulsory primary education
179.x: The 1913 Resolution on Education Policy responded to Gopal Krishna Gokhale's demand for compulsory primary education.
179.tq: Identify the demand that triggered a specific policy resolution.

179.s: The Sadler Commission of 1917–19 dealt chiefly with:
o: Primary education wastage in all provinces
Calcutta University and the transition from school to university
179.x: The Sadler Commission examined Calcutta University and the transition from school education to university education.
179.tq: Distinguish commissions by their subject and institutional focus.

179.s: The Orientalists in the educational debate in British India favoured the study of:
179.x: Orientalists favoured Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning. Anglicists advocated Western science and English literature.
179.tq: Directly separate the Orientalist and Anglicist positions in the education debate.

179.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Anglicists from the Orientalists?
o: Anglicists favoured Persian learning, whereas Orientalists favoured English literature
Anglicists favoured Western science and English literature, whereas Orientalists favoured classical Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning
Both groups rejected Western science and English education
Both groups demanded only vernacular primary education
179.x: Anglicists supported Western science and English literature, while Orientalists supported Sanskrit, Arabic and Persian learning.
179.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish two rival educational positions.

179.s: Macaulay's educational objective was to create a class of people who were:
o: European in language but exclusively Persian in culture
Indian in every respect and opposed to English education
Indian in blood and colour but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect
English in blood and colour but Indian in taste and intellect
179.x: Macaulay aimed to create a class Indian in blood and colour but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect.
179.tq: Recognise the exact formulation of a famous educational objective without reversing its paired attributes.

179.s: The Downward Filtration Theory proposed that education should first be given to:
o: A small group of upper-class Indians, who would transmit knowledge to the masses
179.x: The theory proposed educating a few upper-class Indians so that knowledge would gradually filter down to the wider population.
179.tq: Identify the direction of educational transmission in the theory.

179.s: Which of the following statements about the 1835 educational resolution is correct?
o: It transferred Madras schools to municipalities
It introduced regional-language instruction in all Madras district schools
It established the first universities in India
It banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools
179.x: The 1835 resolution banned regional-language instruction in Madras district schools.
179.tq: Test the exact policy direction and avoid replacing a ban with an introduction.

179.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the number of schools in the relevant area by 1830?
179.x: By 1830, Munro's collectorate and tahsildari schools included two in Kadapa, one in Nellore and two in Vizag.
179.tq: Match each place with its precise count instead of relying on the total alone.

179.s: The collectorate and tahsildari schools associated with Munro in the Madras region were closed in:
179.x: The collectorate and tahsildari schools referred to in the educational record were closed in 1836.
179.tq: Distinguish the year of the educational resolution from the following year of institutional closure.

179.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
179.x: Jonathan Duncan founded the Sanskrit College at Benaras in 1791. It was not founded by William Jones.
179.tq: Use the explicit founder distinction in a same-period institutional matching question.

179.s: Fort William College was established in 1800 by Wellesley primarily for:
179.x: Wellesley established Fort William College in 1800 to train civil servants.
179.tq: Combine founder, year and institutional purpose in one precise association.

179.s: Who founded Vedanta College in 1825?
179.x: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Vedanta College in 1825.
179.tq: Distinguish the founder of Vedanta College from his joint role in founding Hindu College.

179.s:
Arrange the following institutions in chronological order of their foundation:
A. Calcutta Madrasa
B. Asiatic Society of Bengal
C. Sanskrit College, Benaras
D. Fort William College
179.x: The institutions were founded in the order Calcutta Madrasa (1781), Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784), Sanskrit College, Benaras (1791), and Fort William College (1800).
179.tq: Arrange institutions by their foundation years and verify the first and last entries.

179.s: Which measure is associated with Lord Dalhousie's postal reforms?
o: Introduction of uniform low postage under the Post Office Act, 1854
Abolition of the Post Office Act, 1854
Transfer of postal administration to the princely states
Introduction of separate postage rates for each Presidency
