179.x: Lord Dalhousie’s reforms included the Post Office Act of 1854, which introduced uniform low postage throughout British India.
179.tq: Identify the reform directly associated with the administrator.

179.s: John Lawrence opened telegraph communication with Europe during which period?
179.x: John Lawrence opened telegraph communication with Europe during the period 1864–1869.
179.tq: Use the chronological range to distinguish closely related administrative developments.

179.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the wider effects of the telegraph and postal system:
1. They contributed to the integration of the market.
2. They facilitated travel across caste lines.
3. They assisted the growth of pan-Indian mobilisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: The integrated postal and telegraph network helped integrate markets, eased travel across caste lines and facilitated pan-Indian mobilisation.
179.tq: Test a cluster of related consequences through an all-inclusive option.

179.s: The London Missionary Society began its work in Andhra in 1805 at:
179.x: The London Missionary Society is associated with Jammalamadugu in Cuddapah, where it began work in Andhra in 1805.
179.tq: Apply the place-and-year pair rather than relying on the organisation alone.

179.s: The Machilipatnam National College became notable as a centre of Home Rule protests in:
179.x: The Machilipatnam National College was a centre of Home Rule protests in 1917.
179.tq: Discriminate among close years associated with a political institution.

179.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Year)
a. 1841
b. 1843
c. 1857

a. Central Collegiate Institute, Madras
b. Noble School, Machilipatnam
c. Madras University

List-II (Institution)
i. Madras University
ii. Noble School, Machilipatnam
iii. Central Collegiate Institute, Madras

Codes:
179.x: The Central Collegiate Institute dates to 1841, the Noble School to 1843, and Madras University to 1857.
179.tq: Start from the sure year–institution pair and eliminate incompatible codes.

179.s: Madras University was established on 5 September 1857 under the:
179.x: Madras University was established on 5 September 1857 under Wood’s Despatch.
179.tq: Match the institution with the education policy that shaped its establishment.

179.s: Grants-in-aid linked with educational results began in:
179.x: The system of grants-in-aid tied to results began in 1877–78.
179.tq: Select the precise administrative year range from plausible alternatives.

179.s: Rajahmundry was an important base for the reform journalism of:
179.x: Rajahmundry served as the base of Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s reform journalism.
179.tq: Identify the reformer associated with the place and activity.

179.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023?
o: It replaced the Vernacular Press Act, 1878.
It transferred press registration to the Election Commission of India.
It replaced the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
It repealed the Press Council Act, 1978.
179.x: The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867.
179.tq: Distinguish closely named press laws by their year and legal relationship.

179.s: The Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 was repealed with effect from:
179.x: The Press and Registration of Books Act, 1867 was repealed with effect from 1 March 2024.
179.tq: Test the effective date rather than merely the enactment year.

179.s: The Registrar of Newspapers for India (RNI) is now designated as the:
179.x: The RNI is now designated as the Press Registrar General of India.
179.tq: Choose the exact official title from similar institutional names.

179.s: India’s position in the World Press Freedom Index 2026 was:
179.x: India ranked 157th out of 180 countries in the World Press Freedom Index 2026.
179.tq: Read the rank and denominator together to avoid a nearby-number trap.

179.s:
Consider the following statements about the Press Council:
1. Its statutory basis is the Press Council Act, 1978.
2. It possesses punitive powers over the press.
3. It continues to lack punitive powers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
179.x: The Press Council is based on the Press Council Act, 1978, but it continues to lack punitive powers; therefore, statement 2 is false.
179.tq: Find the contradiction between a statutory role and an alleged power.

179.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
179.x: Puttur-Renigunta is associated with 1862, not 1885. Andhra Prakasika, Krishna Patrika and Andhra Patrika are associated with the Andhra press.
179.tq: Find the single reversed date in an otherwise related set of pairs.

179.s: The railway connection associated with Puttur-Renigunta dates to:
179.x: The Puttur-Renigunta railway connection is associated with the year 1862.
179.tq: Use the exact regional date rather than a more famous railway milestone.

179.s: Which of the following combinations best expresses the significance of English education, the press, railways and the telegraph in colonial India?
o: They restricted communication to European officials alone.
They created an educated middle class and helped form an all-India public sphere for nationalism.
They eliminated regional languages from public life immediately.
They confined political mobilisation to individual princely states.
179.x: English education, the press, railways and the telegraph helped create an educated middle class and an all-India public sphere in which nationalism developed.
179.tq: Apply the combined cause-and-effect relationship to a broader historical outcome.

179.s: Which of the following statements about early education and journalism in Andhra is correct?
o: Telugu journalism began in Andhra only after 1900.
Madras University was established before the Central Collegiate Institute, Madras.
Telugu journalism dates from 1835, while Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry emerged as early centres.
Rajahmundry was unrelated to reform journalism.
179.x: Telugu journalism is traced to 1835, and Machilipatnam and Rajahmundry were important early centres of education and public activity.
179.tq: Select the precise composite statement while rejecting reversed chronology and negation traps.

179.s:
Raja Ram Mohan Roy is associated with which of the following sequence of institutions and years?
1. Atmiya Sabha — 1814
2. Hindu College — 1817
3. English school — 1822
4. Vedanta College — 1825
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
179.x: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is associated with Atmiya Sabha in 1814, Hindu College in 1817, an English school in 1822 and Vedanta College in 1825.
179.tq: Check each year–institution pair before selecting the complete combination.

179.s: Which of the following sequences is in the correct chronological order?
o: Madras University — Central Collegiate Institute — Noble School — grants-in-aid system
Central Collegiate Institute — Noble School — Madras University — grants-in-aid system
Noble School — Central Collegiate Institute — grants-in-aid system — Madras University
Central Collegiate Institute — Madras University — Noble School — grants-in-aid system
179.x: The correct order is Central Collegiate Institute (1841), Noble School (1843), Madras University (1857), and the grants-in-aid system linked to results (1877–78).
179.tq: Place the earliest and latest items first, then resolve the middle dates.

180.s: The first municipal corporation in India was established at which place in 1688?
180.x: The first municipal corporation in India was established at Madras in 1688.
180.tq: Use the place-year association to distinguish the first corporation from the later corporations at Bombay and Calcutta.

180.s: In which year were municipal corporations established at Bombay and Calcutta?
180.x: Municipal corporations were established at Bombay and Calcutta in 1726, after the first corporation at Madras in 1688.
180.tq: Separate the close chronological milestones by matching the year with the two later-established corporations.

180.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870:
1. It marked the first step towards financial decentralisation.
2. It bifurcated central and provincial finances.
3. It gave provinces certain services to administer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: All three statements are correct. Mayo's Resolution of 1870 began financial decentralisation, divided central and provincial finances, and assigned certain services to the provinces.
180.tq: Test the cluster of connected features rather than relying on the year alone.

180.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the services specifically associated with the provincial responsibility under Lord Mayo's financial decentralisation scheme?
180.x: Police, jails and education were among the services assigned to the provinces. Foreign affairs was not one of the locally administered services listed under the scheme.
180.tq: Find the item outside the closely related group of provincial administrative services.

180.s: Under Lord Mayo's financial decentralisation scheme, the provinces were expected to meet their responsibilities primarily by
o: transferring their services to district courts
receiving fixed grants and raising local taxes
180.x: The provinces received fixed grants for administering certain services and were also instructed to raise local taxes.
180.tq: Apply the financial arrangement to identify the combination of grants and local taxation.

180.s:
With reference to Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for an elected non-official majority in local bodies.
2. It emphasised local autonomy.
3. It envisaged the participation of non-official members in local boards, district boards, municipal councils and village panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Ripon's Resolution included an elected non-official majority, local autonomy and wider participation of non-official members in the principal local institutions.
180.tq: Check whether each statement captures a separate institutional feature of the 1882 Resolution.

180.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Government of India Act, 1935 made local self-government a provincial subject
B. Lord Ripon's Resolution on local self-government
C. Government of India Act, 1919 treated local self-government as a transferred subject
D. Lord Mayo's Resolution on financial decentralisation
180.x: The correct sequence is Mayo's Resolution of 1870, Ripon's Resolution of 1882, the Government of India Act of 1919, and the Government of India Act of 1935.
180.tq: Fix the sequence by first placing the dated Mayo and Ripon resolutions, then the two constitutional Acts.

180.s: The Royal Commission on Decentralisation, constituted during 1907–09, was chaired by
180.x: C.E.H. Hobhouse chaired the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09.
180.tq: Discriminate between the reforming Viceroys and the chairman of the later commission.

180.s: Which of the following recommendations was associated with the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09?
o: Making local self-government an exclusively central subject
Strengthening local institutions and village panchayats
Replacing municipal councils with military boards
180.x: The Commission recommended strengthening local institutions, including village panchayats.
180.tq: Identify the recommendation that directly advances decentralisation instead of reversing it.

180.s: What significant change concerning local self-government was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: It made local self-government a provincial subject.
It placed local self-government under the exclusive control of the Governor-General.
It transferred local self-government to the Central Legislature.
It abolished village panchayats in the provinces.
180.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 made local self-government a provincial subject.
180.tq: Match the constitutional Act with the level of government to which the subject was assigned.

180.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of local self-government:
1. Village panchayats were set up in several provinces after the Government of India Act, 1919.
2. Local bodies after Ripon's Resolution were entirely free from colonial official control.
3. Local bodies were often starved of funds.
4. Non-official members entered village panchayats, municipal councils and district boards after 1882.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is false because local bodies continued to be controlled by colonial officials and were also constrained by inadequate funds.
180.tq: Reject the absolute claim of complete freedom while retaining the institutional changes and criticism.

180.s: Lord Mayo's tenure, during which he introduced financial decentralisation and conducted the first census of India, was
180.x: Lord Mayo served from 1869 to 1872. During this period, the financial decentralisation Resolution of 1870 was introduced and the first census was conducted in 1871.
180.tq: Link the tenure with the two dated developments to avoid confusing adjacent three-year ranges.

180.s: In addition to financial decentralisation, Lord Mayo's administration is associated with
o: the transfer of local self-government to the provinces in 1935
the Royal Commission on Decentralisation of 1907–09
the first municipal corporation at Madras in 1688
a statistical survey of India and the first census in 1871
180.x: Lord Mayo also undertook a statistical survey of India and conducted the first census in 1871.
180.tq: Separate Mayo's statistical and census initiatives from reforms belonging to other years and administrators.

180.s:
Assertion (A): The local self-government institutions introduced during the colonial period did not enjoy complete autonomy.
Reason (R): They were often starved of funds and remained subject to the control of colonial officials.

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
180.x: Both statements are true, and inadequate finances together with continued official control explains why the local bodies did not possess complete autonomy.
180.tq: Test whether the stated institutional limitation is directly explained by the administrative and financial constraints.

180.s: Which one of the following best describes the principal features associated with Lord Cornwallis's civil service reforms in India?
o: A military service based on hereditary succession and private trade
A merit-based covenanted service, prohibition of private trade and gifts, and promotion by seniority
A wholly Indian civil service recruited through provincial elections
A service recruited exclusively through examinations conducted in India
180.x: Cornwallis established a merit-based covenanted civil service, prohibited private trade and acceptance of gifts, and introduced promotion substantially based on seniority.
180.tq: Use the cluster of reforms associated with the correct administrator rather than relying on a single keyword.

180.s: The College of Fort William was established at Calcutta in 1800 primarily for which of the following purposes?
o: Administering the Provincial Public Service Commission
Conducting the first simultaneous ICS examination
Training only Indian judges in customary law
Training recruits of the Company's civil service
180.x: Wellesley established the College of Fort William at Calcutta in 1800 to train recruits of the Company's civil service.
180.tq: Match the institution with its specific administrative function and founder.

180.s: The Charter Act of 1853 is significant in the history of the Indian civil services because it:
o: Established the Indian Civil Service exclusively for Indians
Transferred the ICS examination from London to Allahabad
Created the Federal Public Service Commission
Abolished the patronage system and introduced open competitive examination
180.x: The Charter Act of 1853 abolished appointments by patronage of the Company's Directors and introduced open competitive examination for the civil services.
180.tq: Identify the administrative change directly linked with the named Act, while rejecting later institutional developments.

180.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Macaulay Committee report:
1. It recommended that the civil service examination should be conducted in London.
2. It favoured preference for graduates of Oxford and Cambridge.
3. It recommended continuation of appointments solely through the patronage of Company Directors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Macaulay recommendations were associated with competitive examination, not continuation of the Company's patronage system.
180.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reform by confusing competitive recruitment with patronage.

180.s: The Indian Civil Services Act of 1861 provided for which of the following?
o: Replacement of the ICS by the IAS
Abolition of all civil service examinations in London
Immediate parity between Indians and Europeans in all covenanted posts
Limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, subject to conditions including residence and language examination
180.x: The Indian Civil Services Act of 1861 allowed limited Indian entry, mainly into uncovenanted posts, with conditions including seven years' residence and an examination in the local language.
180.tq: Separate limited statutory entry from the later policy of Indianisation and post-1947 changes.

180.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the reduction in the maximum age limit for the civil service examination?
o: 23 years in 1859, 22 years in 1860, 21 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
23 years in 1859, 21 years in 1860, 22 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
22 years in 1859, 23 years in 1860, 21 years in 1866 and 19 years in 1878
23 years in 1859, 22 years in 1860, 19 years in 1866 and 21 years in 1878
180.x: The maximum age was reduced successively from 23 in 1859 to 22 in 1860, 21 in 1866 and 19 in 1878. The reduction under Lytton became a major Indian grievance.
180.tq: Track both the numerical trend and the corresponding years before comparing the sequences.

180.s: The reduction of the maximum age for the civil service examination to 19 years in 1878 was associated with the tenure of:
180.x: The maximum age was reduced to 19 in 1878 during the tenure of Lord Lytton, and this became an important Indian grievance.
180.tq: Link the numerical change to the Viceroy in office when it occurred.

180.s: The demand for raising the age limit and holding the civil service examination simultaneously in India and England was taken up by the Indian National Congress from:
180.x: The INC began pressing these demands from its first session in 1885.
180.tq: Use the earliest stated organisational milestone rather than the later date of implementation.

180.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
180.x: The Aitchison Public Service Commission was appointed in 1886 during the viceroyalty of Dufferin. Islington belonged to 1912–15 under Hardinge II, while Lee belonged to 1923–24 under Reading.
180.tq: Start with the sure year–commission pair and eliminate options that swap the commissions and Viceroys.

180.s:
The Aitchison Public Service Commission is associated with which of the following recommendations or changes?
1. Dropping the terms 'covenanted' and 'uncovenanted' services.
2. Classification into Imperial, Provincial and Subordinate services.
3. Raising the age limit to 23 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: The Aitchison Commission dropped the covenanted–uncovenanted terminology, proposed the three-level classification of services and raised the age limit to 23 years.
180.tq: Verify each commission feature independently instead of associating all civil service reforms with one Act.

180.s: The principal objective associated with the Islington Commission of 1912–15 was:
o: Abolition of the Provincial and Subordinate services
Indianisation of higher civil service posts
Introduction of patronage appointments by Company Directors
Creation of the IAS after independence
180.x: The Islington Commission, appointed during the tenure of Hardinge II, dealt principally with the Indianisation of higher posts.
180.tq: Identify the commission by its central recommendation, not merely by its date.

180.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lee Commission:
1. It was appointed in 1923–24 during the viceroyalty of Lord Reading.
2. It proposed 50:50 Indian-European parity in the ICS within 15 years.
3. Its recommendations were unrelated to the creation of a Public Service Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Lee Commission was also associated with the establishment of a Public Service Commission, so statement 3 is false.
180.tq: Reject the negative statement that disconnects a commission from an institutional consequence expressly associated with it.

180.s: On which date was the Public Service Commission established in connection with the recommendations of the Lee Commission?
180.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926 in the context of the Lee Commission's recommendations.
180.tq: Distinguish the precise institutional date from the dates of the Lee Commission and later constitutional changes.

180.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relevant civil service provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: It established the Federal Public Service Commission in place of all provincial services.
It abolished the ICS and created the IAS with immediate effect.
It provided for a separate ICS examination in India, enabling simultaneous examinations with England from 1922.
It restored the exclusive patronage of the Company's Directors over civil service appointments.
180.x: The Government of India Act, 1919, provided for a separate ICS examination in India; simultaneous examinations were held from 1922, alongside the London examination.
180.tq: Distinguish the enabling legal provision from the later date of actual examination and from post-independence reforms.

180.s:
With reference to the examination arrangements for the Indian Civil Service, consider the following statements:
1. Examinations were held in India at Allahabad from 1922.
2. Delhi later became the Indian venue.
3. The London examination was discontinued when the Indian examination began.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: The Indian examination began at Allahabad in 1922 and was later held at Delhi, alongside the examination in London. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
180.tq: Watch for the false discontinuity claim in a question about simultaneous arrangements.

180.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1950 — UPSC replaced the Federal Public Service Commission
Government of India Act, 1919 — UPSC replaced the Federal Public Service Commission
Government of India Act, 1935 — Federal Public Service Commission and Provincial Public Service Commissions
180.x: The Government of India Act, 1919, dealt with the provision for a separate ICS examination in India. The Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions were provided for by the 1935 Act, and UPSC replaced the Federal PSC in 1950.
180.tq: Find the option that assigns a later constitutional development to the wrong Act.

180.s: Who described the Indian Civil Service as the 'Steel Frame' of India?
180.x: Sardar Patel described the Indian Civil Service as the 'Steel Frame' of India.
180.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the statesman associated with it.

180.s: Which of the following statements correctly explains the statutory civil service scheme introduced under Lord Lytton in 1878–79?
o: One-half of the ICS posts were reserved for Indians under the Lee Commission.
All covenanted posts were opened equally to Indians and Europeans through local examinations.
One-sixth of the covenanted posts were set aside for Indians of high families, and the scheme was later abolished.
The scheme transferred all civil service appointments to elected provincial governments.
180.x: Lytton's statutory civil service scheme reserved one-sixth of covenanted posts for Indians of high families; it was later abolished. It did not establish complete equality or the later 50:50 parity proposal.
180.tq: Separate the limited statutory concession under Lytton from the later Lee Commission parity proposal.

180.s: Who established the district Diwani and Faujdari Adalats in 1772?
180.x: Warren Hastings established the district Diwani Adalats for civil cases and Faujdari Adalats for criminal cases in 1772.
180.tq: Directly identify the Governor-General associated with a judicial reform.

180.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the judicial reforms of Warren Hastings:
1. District Diwani Adalats dealt with civil cases.
2. District Faujdari Adalats dealt with criminal cases.
3. Sadar Diwani and Sadar Nizamat Adalats were established at Calcutta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: All three statements are correct. Hastings established the district civil and criminal courts and the Sadar Diwani and Sadar Nizamat Adalats at Calcutta.
180.tq: Check each statement against the civil, criminal and appellate structure introduced by Hastings.

180.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the Cornwallis Code of 1793?
o: Separation of commercial, judicial and revenue branches
Establishment of High Courts at the presidency towns
Abolition of all provincial courts of appeal
Replacement of Persian by vernacular languages in courts
180.x: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 separated the commercial, judicial and revenue branches. The other reforms belonged to later administrative developments.
180.tq: Use the reform directly associated with the named code and period.

180.s:
With reference to Cornwallis's judicial administration, consider the following statements:
1. The Collector was deprived of judicial powers.
2. The post of District Judge was created.
3. Provincial courts of appeal were established at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad and Patna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: All three statements correctly describe Cornwallis's judicial arrangements. The creation of the District Judge's post accompanied the removal of judicial powers from the Collector.
180.tq: Test a reform cluster through a coded combination of correct statements.

180.s: The Sadar Diwani and Sadar Nizamat Adalats at Calcutta were presided over by the Governor-General in Council under whose reforms?
180.x: Under Cornwallis, the Sadar Diwani and Sadar Nizamat Adalats at Calcutta were presided over by the Governor-General in Council.
180.tq: Distinguish the appellate arrangements of Cornwallis from those of Hastings and Bentinck.

180.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly associated with Bentinck's judicial reforms?
o: Abolition of Cornwallis's provincial courts of appeal
Creation of provincial courts of appeal at Dacca and Patna
Transfer of circuit courts' work to Commissioners
Establishment of separate Sadar courts at Allahabad
180.x: The creation of provincial courts of appeal at Dacca and Patna was associated with Cornwallis. Bentinck abolished the provincial courts of appeal and circuit courts, transferred their work to Commissioners, and established separate Sadar courts at Allahabad.
180.tq: Find the reform belonging to another Governor-General.

180.s: Which language change was introduced in the courts during Bentinck's administration?
o: English and vernacular languages replaced Persian
Persian replaced English and vernacular languages
Sanskrit replaced Persian in all courts
Only English was permitted in every court
180.x: During Bentinck's administration, vernacular languages and English were introduced in place of Persian in the courts.
180.tq: Discriminate between the language policy of Bentinck and the earlier Persian-based court system.

180.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Code or law)
a. Code of Civil Procedure
b. Indian Penal Code
c. Code of Criminal Procedure

List-II (Year)
i. 1859
ii. 1860
iii. 1861

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
180.x: The Code of Civil Procedure was enacted in 1859, the Indian Penal Code in 1860, and the Code of Criminal Procedure in 1861.
180.tq: Start from the sure date-code pair and complete the matching sequence.

180.s: The codification of laws under the Law Commission headed by T.B. Macaulay was associated with which Act?
180.x: The Law Commission under T.B. Macaulay and the codification of laws were associated with the Charter Act of 1833.
180.tq: Match the law-making milestone with its enabling Act.

180.s: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council was formalised by the:
180.x: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council was formalised by the Judicial Committee Act of 1833.
180.tq: Distinguish the Judicial Committee Act from other judicial statutes of the period.

180.s: The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 provided for High Courts at:
180.x: The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 provided for High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras; they began functioning in 1862. They replaced the Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats.
180.tq: Recall the three presidency locations and avoid substituting later High Court centres.

180.s: Which institutions were replaced by the High Courts established under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861?
o: Provincial courts of appeal and circuit courts only
180.x: The High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras replaced the existing Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats.
180.tq: Test the institutional consequence rather than merely the year of the Act.

180.s:
Arrange the following judicial developments in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta
B. Charter Act providing for the Law Commission
C. Indian High Courts Act
D. Code of Civil Procedure
180.x: The correct sequence is Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774), Charter Act and Law Commission (1833), Code of Civil Procedure (1859), and Indian High Courts Act (1861).
180.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle reforms by year.

180.s: The principal aim of the Ilbert Bill was to empower Indian:
o: Collectors to try all revenue cases involving Europeans
Police officers to investigate cases against European officials
High Court judges to appoint European juries
District magistrates and sessions judges to try European British subjects
180.x: The Ilbert Bill sought to allow Indian district magistrates and sessions judges to try European British subjects, removing the racial judicial privilege enjoyed by Europeans.
180.tq: Identify the authority and jurisdiction targeted by the proposed legal change.

180.s: Who was the Law Member associated with the Ilbert Bill?
180.x: C.P. Ilbert, the Law Member, introduced the Bill that became known as the Ilbert Bill.
180.tq: Use the author or sponsoring official as the distinguishing clue.

180.s: Why did European residents in India strongly oppose the Ilbert Bill?
o: It ended the separate European regiments in the army.
It sought to permit Indian judges to try European British subjects.
It transferred police administration to village panchayats.
It proposed to abolish the High Courts at the presidency towns.
180.x: European residents opposed the Bill because it would permit Indian district magistrates and sessions judges to try European British subjects, who had previously been tried only by European judges.
180.tq: Link the opposition to the specific judicial privilege threatened by the Bill.

180.s: Which of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Ilbert Bill controversy?
o: A compromise required a jury with at least half European members in cases involving Europeans.
The Bill was withdrawn and no compromise was made.
European subjects were placed under village courts.
The Bill was passed without modification.
180.x: The Bill was diluted after European agitation. Europeans tried by an Indian judge could claim a jury containing at least half European members.
180.tq: Distinguish the original objective from the diluted final arrangement.

180.s: The European agitation against the Ilbert Bill is commonly described as the:
180.x: The fierce European agitation against the Ilbert Bill was popularly described as the “white mutiny.”
180.tq: Recall the distinctive contemporary label attached to the agitation.

180.s: Which statement best expresses the wider significance of the Ilbert Bill episode?
o: It proved that racial discrimination had ended in the judiciary.
It demonstrated the value of organised agitation to Indians and exposed continuing racial discrimination.
It established complete judicial equality between Europeans and Indians.
It abolished the office of the Viceroy.
180.x: The episode showed that racial discrimination persisted, while also demonstrating to Indians the effectiveness of organised agitation.
180.tq: Choose the option that captures both the immediate constitutional limitation and the wider political lesson.

180.s: Under Cornwallis's police reorganisation, a district was divided into thanas placed under the charge of a(n):
180.x: Cornwallis divided districts into thanas, each placed under an Indian daroga assisted by constables.
180.tq: Match the administrative unit with its designated police officer.

180.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of Cornwallis's police reorganisation?
o: The Royal Irish Constabulary model was adopted.
Indian darogas were placed in charge of thanas.
Zamindars were relieved of police duties.
180.x: The Royal Irish Constabulary model was adopted for the Police Act of 1861, not for Cornwallis's reorganisation. Cornwallis introduced thanas under darogas and removed police duties from zamindars.
180.tq: Separate the Cornwallis reorganisation from the later Police Act model.

180.s: In the Mughal administrative tradition, the kotwal was the:
o: Head of a district civil court
180.x: The kotwal was the older Mughal chief of town police. The daroga, by contrast, was associated with the later thana-based police arrangement.
180.tq: Discriminate between the older kotwal office and the later daroga system.

180.s: The daroga was described as the local representative of the:
o: Aura and authority of Company Bahadur
180.x: The daroga represented the “aura and authority of Company Bahadur” at the local level. Darogas also became notorious for abuse of power.
180.tq: Recall the distinctive descriptive phrase associated with the office.

180.s: The Police Act of 1861 created a colonial police force modelled on the:
180.x: The colonial police force created under the Police Act of 1861 was modelled on the Royal Irish Constabulary and was intended to suppress dissent.
180.tq: Match the colonial institution with its foreign organisational model.

180.s: The Police Act of 1861 was introduced during the administration of:
180.x: The Police Act of 1861 was introduced during Lord Canning's administration and created a colonial force intended to suppress dissent.
180.tq: Avoid the ruler-swapping trap by matching the Act with its correct administration.

180.s: The Police Commission of 1902 was appointed by Curzon under the chairmanship of:
180.x: The Police Commission of 1902 was appointed by Lord Curzon and functioned under Andrew Frazer.
180.tq: Match the commission with both its chairman and appointing authority.

180.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recommendation of the Peel Commission of 1859?
o: Increase of the European share in the army and retention of artillery for Europeans
Recruitment exclusively from Awadh and Bihar
Abolition of all presidency armies immediately
Reduction of the European share in the army
180.x: The Peel Commission recommended a greater European share in the army and reserved artillery and key positions for Europeans.
180.tq: Identify the post-1857 military measure rather than a later army-merger proposal.

180.s: After the reorganisation recommended by the Peel Commission, the ratio of European to Indian troops was:
o: 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:5 in the Bengal Army and 1:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
2:1 in the Bengal Army and 5:2 in the Madras and Bombay armies
180.x: The ratio of European to Indian troops was fixed at 1:2 in the Bengal Army and 2:5 in the Madras and Bombay armies.
180.tq: Read the ratios in the stated presidency order and watch for reversal of numerator and denominator.

180.s:
Which of the following statements regarding army reorganisation after 1857 is correct?
1. Artillery and key positions were reserved for Europeans.
2. Recruitment shifted towards groups described as martial races.
3. Recruitment was shifted away from Awadh and Bihar towards Punjab, Gorkhas and the NWFP.
4. Regiments were organised without regard to caste or region.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
180.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the policy of “divide and counterpoise” involved mixing regiments by caste and region, not ignoring those identities.
180.tq: Find the reversed statement hidden among correct military-reorganisation features.

180.s: The policy of “divide and counterpoise” in the post-1857 army was reflected in the:
o: Abolition of all regional distinctions in recruitment
Mixing of regiments by caste and region
Replacement of Indian troops by police constables
180.x: The policy involved mixing regiments by caste and region to prevent unified opposition within the army.
180.tq: Apply the phrase to the organisational measure it describes.

180.s: The Eden Commission of 1879 recommended the:
o: Abolition of the separate presidency armies
Restoration of the separate presidency armies
Transfer of army control to zamindars
180.x: The Eden Commission recommended abolishing the separate presidency armies. They were subsequently merged into a single Indian Army with four commands in 1895.
180.tq: Distinguish the Eden Commission's recommendation from the earlier presidency-army structure.

180.s: The three presidency armies of Bengal, Madras and Bombay were merged into a single Indian Army with four commands in:
180.x: Following the recommendation of the Eden Commission, the separate presidency armies were merged into a single Indian Army with four commands in 1895.
180.tq: Link the recommendation year with the later year of implementation.

180.s: Thomas Munro returned in June 1814 as President of the:
180.x: Thomas Munro returned in June 1814 as President of the Judicial Commission, which reviewed judicial and police administration in Bengal and Madras.
180.tq: Identify the commission from the office held by Munro on his return.

180.s: The Judicial Commission presided over by Thomas Munro reviewed judicial and police administration during:
180.x: Munro presided over the Judicial Commission from 1814 to 1818, and its report was submitted in April 1816.
180.tq: Distinguish the commission's tenure from Munro's later governorship of Madras.

180.s:
Which recommendations were made by Thomas Munro's Judicial Commission?
1. Police supervision should be placed under the Collector rather than judges.
2. Village officers should try minor crimes at the village level.
3. All criminal cases should be transferred to the High Courts.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
180.x: Munro recommended police supervision under the Collector and trial of minor crimes by village officers. He did not recommend transferring all criminal cases to High Courts.
180.tq: Separate the two positive recommendations from an extreme and unrelated judicial transfer.

180.s: The village-level officer or institution associated with Munro's recommendation for trying minor crimes was the:
180.x: Munro recommended that minor crimes could be tried at village level by a village munsif or panchayat.
180.tq: Match the village-level judicial function with its appropriate local institution.

180.s: Which administrative measure is associated with Thomas Munro as Governor of Madras?
o: Creation of the Indian High Courts
Introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal
Establishment of the Police Commission of 1902
180.x: As Governor of Madras, Thomas Munro extended the Ryotwari system. The other measures belonged to different administrations and regions.
180.tq: Match the administrator with the land-revenue measure linked to his Madras tenure.

180.s: Who was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination?
180.x: Satyendranath Tagore, the brother of Rabindranath Tagore, was the first Indian to clear the ICS examination.
180.tq: Use the precise individual rather than the more famous related name.

180.s: Satyendranath Tagore was selected for the Indian Civil Service in 1863 and cleared the examination in:
180.x: Satyendranath Tagore was selected in 1863 and is recorded as the first Indian to clear the ICS in 1864.
180.tq: Distinguish the selection year from the year associated with clearing the examination.

180.s: What amount was approved by the Government of Andhra Pradesh for Phase-I of the AP Judicial Academy (APPCA) in June 2026?
180.x: The Government of Andhra Pradesh approved Rs 130.38 crore for Phase-I of the AP Judicial Academy in June 2026.
180.tq: Use precise numerical recall and distinguish closely similar figures.

180.s: According to NJDG data cited in June 2026, the number of pending cases across Indian courts had crossed which threshold?
180.x: NJDG data cited in June 2026 indicated that pending cases across courts had crossed 5 crore.
180.tq: Test the threshold figure directly through numerical discrimination.

180.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the police station model restored in Kerala:
1. The Sub-Inspector-led SHO model was restored.
2. The model was restored in 421 out of 484 police stations.
3. The restoration was reported on 15 August 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: All three statements are correct: Kerala restored the Sub-Inspector-led SHO model in 421 of its 484 stations, as reported on 15 August 2026.
180.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the figure, date and institutional detail.

180.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
 a. Indian Civil Service
 b. Codified laws
 c. Police model of 1861
 d. Ripon's local bodies

List-II
 i. Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies
 ii. Indian Administrative Service
 iii. Police institutions of the modern state
 iv. IPC-era legal codes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
180.x: The ICS is the direct ancestor of the IAS, codified laws of IPC-era codes, the 1861 police model of modern police institutions, and Ripon's local bodies of PRIs and ULBs.
180.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched institutional successors.

180.s:
The petitions submitted in Andhra during the 1850s demanded which of the following?

1. Appointment of trained judges
2. Separation of police from revenue officials
3. Appointment of Indians to higher posts

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
180.x: The Andhra petitions of the 1850s demanded trained judges, separation of the police from revenue officials, and the appointment of Indians to higher posts.
180.tq: Identify the complete set of demands rather than selecting an isolated reform.

180.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Madras — Presidency governing Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema
180.x: Munro is associated with the Madras judicial and police models. Ripon is associated with local self-government, not the Madras judicial model.
180.tq: Find the swapped personality–reform association.

180.s:
With reference to the administrative legacy of British rule in India, consider the following statements:
1. Cornwallis, Wellesley and Macaulay contributed to building the administrative ‘steel frame’.
2. The UPSC, CAG and Election Commission can trace their institutional roots to British-era bodies.
3. The administrative legacy was confined exclusively to the police and did not extend to constitutional institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
180.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the legacy also extended to institutions whose successors include the UPSC, CAG and Election Commission.
180.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ when the institutional legacy spans several branches of administration.

180.s:
Arrange the following in the order in which their modern institutional successors are identified in the administrative legacy described below:
A. Ripon's local bodies
B. Indian Civil Service
C. Police model of 1861
D. Codified laws

Select the correct chronological order.
180.x: The sequence is the Indian Civil Service, codified laws, the police model of 1861, and Ripon's local bodies. The first two are associated with the earlier administrative developments, followed by the 1861 police model and Ripon's later local-government reforms.
180.tq: Use the anchor date 1861 and place Ripon's local-government reforms last.

180.s: Madras was significant in the administrative history of Andhra Pradesh because it was the capital of the presidency that governed which regions?
180.x: Madras was the capital of the presidency that governed Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema.
180.tq: Test the administrative-geographical relationship between a presidency capital and its governed regions.

180.s: In July 2026, which action was taken in relation to the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC)?
o: The KPSC was dissolved by the Supreme Court after a constitutional amendment.
The KPSC Chairperson resigned after the Governor transferred the Commission to Andhra Pradesh.
The KPSC was placed under the direct control of the Union Public Service Commission.
The KPSC Chairperson was suspended by the Karnataka Governor pending inquiry, and a reference was sought from the Supreme Court under Article 317(1).
180.x: The Karnataka Governor suspended the KPSC Chairperson pending inquiry and sought a Supreme Court reference under Article 317(1). This was described as a first for the KPSC.
180.tq: Match the constitutional authority with the action and the relevant Article.

180.s: The action involving the Karnataka Public Service Commission in July 2026 was described as which of the following?
o: The first such action for the KPSC
A routine annual action applicable to all State Public Service Commissions
An action previously undertaken by the KPSC in every inquiry
The second such action for the KPSC after a parliamentary inquiry
180.x: The suspension of the KPSC Chairperson pending inquiry and the request for a Supreme Court reference under Article 317(1) were described as a first for the KPSC.
180.tq: Distinguish a reported first from routine or repeated institutional practice.

180.s: Which of the following best expresses the principal criticism of the colonial police system?
o: It was designed primarily for public service and community participation.
It was intended to replace the judicial system with revenue administration.
It was built mainly for administrative control rather than service to the public.
It was created exclusively to administer local self-government institutions.
180.x: The colonial police system was criticised as having been built primarily for control rather than public service.
180.tq: Identify the central purpose-based criticism rather than a related administrative institution.

180.s: Which of the following criticisms was associated with the colonial justice system and the Ilbert Bill debate?
o: Justice was inexpensive, rapid and racially equal.
Justice was costly, slow and racially unequal.
Justice was transferred entirely to elected local bodies.
Justice was administered only by Indian judges without racial distinctions.
180.x: The colonial justice system was criticised as costly, slow and racially unequal; these inequalities were highlighted in the context of the Ilbert Bill debate.
180.tq: Use the three-part criticism as a precise descriptive combination.

181.s: The annexation of Awadh in 1856 was justified by the British on the ground of
o: Absence of a natural male heir
181.x: Awadh was annexed by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 on the ground of misgovernment, not under the Doctrine of Lapse.
181.tq: Distinguish the stated ground of annexation from the commonly associated Doctrine of Lapse.

181.s: Who among the following was deposed and exiled to Calcutta after the annexation of Awadh?
181.x: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was deposed after Awadh was annexed and was exiled to Calcutta.
181.tq: Use the ruler–territory association to avoid swapping rulers of different annexed states.

181.s:
With reference to the Summary Revenue Settlement introduced in Awadh in 1856, consider the following statements:
1. The settlement was made directly with village proprietors.
2. Taluqdars were dispossessed of their estates.
3. Taluqdars were allowed to retain their arms and forts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
181.x: The settlement was made directly with village proprietors, while taluqdars lost their estates, were disarmed and had their forts demolished. Statement 3 is false.
181.tq: Find the false statement by checking the reversal of a specific administrative consequence.

181.s: Which of the following was NOT an immediate consequence of the annexation of Awadh?
o: The taluqdars received permanent protection for their estates
Officials and retainers of the Nawab were thrown out of work
Awadh became a centre of unrest
The landed aristocracy was deeply alienated
181.x: The taluqdars were dispossessed and disarmed; they did not receive permanent protection for their estates. The other developments followed the annexation.
181.tq: Eliminate the option that reverses the documented political and social effect.

181.s: The annexation of Awadh particularly alienated the Bengal Army sepoys because
o: most Bengal Army sepoys were recruited from Punjab alone
their families in Awadh were affected by the new revenue burden
their own regiments were immediately disbanded
they were denied promotion to the rank of Resident
181.x: The Bengal Army drew heavily from Awadh, and the new revenue burden directly affected the families of its sepoys.
181.tq: Link the social base of recruitment with the direct effect of annexation on soldiers’ families.

181.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Awadh — 1856 — annexation due to absence of a natural heir
Satara — 1848 — first annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Punjab — 1849 — annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse
Berar — 1853 — annexation after the Second Anglo-Sikh War
181.x: Satara was annexed in 1848 and was the first state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse. Punjab was conquered after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, Awadh for misgovernment, and Berar was taken for subsidy arrears.
181.tq: Check both the ground and the year instead of accepting a partially familiar pair.

181.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jaitpur and Sambalpur — 1849
2. Baghat — 1850
3. Udaipur, the small state — 1852
4. Jhansi — 1853
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
181.x: Jaitpur and Sambalpur were annexed in 1849, Baghat in 1850, the small state of Udaipur in 1852, and Jhansi in 1853, all under the Doctrine of Lapse.
181.tq: Verify each year in the compact annexation sequence before choosing the coded combination.

181.s: Which of the following states was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in spite of the presence of an adopted heir whose succession was refused?
181.x: Rani Lakshmibai’s adopted son, Damodar Rao, was not recognised as heir and Jhansi was annexed in 1853.
181.tq: Pair the adopted heir with the correct state rather than with another annexed territory.

181.s: Nagpur was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse after the death of
o: Raghuji III, the Bhonsle Raja, without an heir
Duleep Singh without a natural heir
Raja of Satara after the Second Anglo-Sikh War
Wajid Ali Shah without an adopted son
181.x: Nagpur was annexed in 1854 after Bhonsle ruler Raghuji III died heirless.
181.tq: Use the ruler–state association and reject combinations mixing different annexation grounds.

181.s: Under the Doctrine of Lapse as applied by Lord Dalhousie, an adopted son of a ruler of a dependent state could
o: inherit both the throne and the state automatically
inherit private property but not the throne
inherit the throne but not private property
inherit neither private property nor the throne
181.x: Under Dalhousie’s policy, adoption was recognised for private property but not for succession to the throne of a dependent state.
181.tq: Discriminate between the right to private property and the right to political succession.

181.s: Lord Dalhousie announced the Doctrine of Lapse in
181.x: Lord Dalhousie formulated and applied the Doctrine of Lapse from 1848.
181.tq: Use the earliest date in the sequence of Dalhousie’s annexations and policies.

181.s: Which of the following grievances was associated with Nana Saheb?
o: Denial of the pension of his adoptive father, Baji Rao II
Refusal to recognise his adopted son as ruler of Jhansi
Removal from the Red Fort and loss of the imperial title
181.x: Nana Saheb, the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, was denied the pension of his adoptive father.
181.tq: Match the leader with his personal political grievance, avoiding swapped revolutionary leaders.

181.s: The policy of annexation under the Doctrine of Lapse was formally abandoned after the Revolt of 1857 through
181.x: Queen Victoria’s Proclamation, read by Canning at the Allahabad Durbar on 1 November 1858, abolished the policy and recognised adoption.
181.tq: Connect the policy change with the correct proclamation, date and official occasion.

181.s: Which one of the following was NOT a condition of the Subsidiary Alliance devised by Lord Wellesley?
o: The ruler had to maintain a British subsidiary force at his own cost
The ruler had to accept a British Resident
The ruler had to exclude other Europeans from his service
The ruler could freely conduct an independent foreign policy
181.x: A subsidiary ally had to surrender independent foreign-policy control. The other conditions were part of the system devised by Wellesley.
181.tq: Spot the option that reverses the central consequence of the alliance.

181.s: If a ruler under the Subsidiary Alliance failed to pay the prescribed subsidy, the British could require him to
o: cede territory in lieu of payment
181.x: Unpaid subsidy could result in the cession of territory to the British.
181.tq: Apply the financial condition of the alliance to the consequence of default.

181.s: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in September 1798 and again in
181.x: The Nizam of Hyderabad entered the arrangement in September 1798 and renewed it in 1800.
181.tq: Distinguish the initial agreement from its subsequent renewal by comparing adjacent years.

181.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the year of accepting the Subsidiary Alliance?
1. Mysore — 1799
2. Tanjore — October 1799
3. Awadh — November 1801
4. Peshwa — December 1801
181.x: Mysore accepted the alliance in 1799, Tanjore in October 1799, Awadh in November 1801 and the Peshwa in December 1801.
181.tq: Read the dates as a sequence and check both the year and the month where supplied.

181.s:
Arrange the following Subsidiary Alliance acceptances in chronological order:
A. Bhonsle of Berar
B. Awadh
C. Scindia
D. Peshwa
181.x: Awadh accepted the alliance in November 1801, the Peshwa in December 1801, Bhonsle of Berar in December 1803 and Scindia in February 1804.
181.tq: Place the two 1801 events first, then distinguish the 1803 and 1804 agreements.

181.s: Which one of the following groups entered into the Subsidiary Alliance in 1818?
o: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi
Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa and Scindia
Punjab, Awadh, Holkar, Tanjore and Jaitpur
Hyderabad, Berar, Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur
181.x: Holkar, Bharatpur, Jodhpur, Jaipur and Bundi entered into the arrangement in 1818. Holkar was the last Maratha power to sign it.
181.tq: Recognise the final group in the alliance chronology and avoid mixing it with earlier signatories.

181.s: The 1800 treaty involving the Nizam resulted in the cession of the Rayalaseema districts, which came to be known as the
181.x: The Nizam ceded the Rayalaseema districts in 1800 to meet the cost of the subsidiary force; these became known as the Ceded Districts.
181.tq: Link the treaty, territorial transfer and historical regional name.

181.s: The British pressure that led the Nizam of Hyderabad to accept the Subsidiary Alliance was connected with his raising of French battalions under
181.x: The Nizam raised French battalions under Raymond. Resident Kirkpatrick reported this to Wellesley, who then forced the alliance.
181.tq: Separate the officer who commanded the French battalions from the Resident who reported them.

181.s: Dalhousie announced that the successors of Bahadur Shah would have to leave the
o: Red Fort and move to the Qutub at Mehrauli
Qutub at Mehrauli and move to Calcutta
Agra Fort and move to Delhi
Allahabad Fort and move to Lucknow
181.x: Dalhousie declared that Bahadur Shah’s successors would have to leave the Red Fort and move to the Qutub at Mehrauli.
181.tq: Use the place pair—Red Fort and Qutub, Mehrauli—to avoid confusing Mughal centres.

181.s: What did Canning announce in 1856 regarding the successors of Bahadur Shah Zafar?
o: They would receive pensions equal to those of the Peshwas
They would lose the imperial title and become mere princes
They would be recognised as governors of Awadh
They would inherit the imperial title and the Red Fort
181.x: Canning announced that after Bahadur Shah Zafar, his successors would lose the imperial title and would be treated merely as princes.
181.tq: Distinguish Canning’s announcement about imperial status from Dalhousie’s order about residence.

181.s: Which of the following titles were abolished in 1855?
o: The titles of the Nizam and the Peshwa
The titles of the Raja of Satara and the ruler of Jhansi
The titles of the Mughal emperor and the Nawab of Awadh
The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja
181.x: The titles of the Carnatic Nawab and the Tanjore Raja were abolished in 1855.
181.tq: Match the year with the two specific titles rather than with rulers affected by the Doctrine of Lapse.

181.s: Which of the following developments added to the number of unemployed persons before the Revolt of 1857?
o: Disbanding of Pindaris and irregular troops
181.x: The disbanding of Pindaris and irregular troops increased unemployment and contributed to discontent.
181.tq: Identify the administrative action that produced the stated economic consequence.

181.s: Begum Hazrat Mahal’s political grievance during the Revolt of 1857 was primarily connected with
o: the loss of the Red Fort by Mughal successors
the annexation of Awadh and the proclamation of her son Birjis Qadr as ruler
the confiscation of Kunwar Singh’s estates
the denial of Baji Rao II’s pension
181.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal opposed the annexation of Awadh and had her son Birjis Qadr proclaimed ruler.
181.tq: Match the leader with the specific grievance and associated claimant.

181.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khan Bahadur Khan — proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam
Rani Lakshmibai — adopted son denied the throne
Kunwar Singh — ruined by loss of his estates
Bahadur Shah Zafar — denial of the pension of Baji Rao II
181.x: Denial of Baji Rao II’s pension was Nana Saheb’s grievance. Bahadur Shah Zafar’s grievance concerned the loss of title and the Red Fort for his successors.
181.tq: Find the swapped leader–grievance pair among closely related political grievances.

181.s: Who among the following was a Rohilla chief who proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam at Bareilly?
181.x: Khan Bahadur Khan, a Rohilla chief at Bareilly, proclaimed himself Nawab Nizam.
181.tq: Use the place and political title to identify the correct regional leader.

181.s: The fear of annexation among the princes contributed to the Revolt of 1857 by
o: turning a sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt
preventing the participation of Awadh’s landed aristocracy
making the revolt exclusively a movement of zamindars
181.x: Fear of further annexations encouraged princely and aristocratic participation and helped transform the sepoy mutiny into a wider revolt.
181.tq: Apply the political cause to the broader character and spread of the revolt.

181.s: After 1858, the British Crown guaranteed the princely states in return for their acceptance of
181.x: After 1858, princely states were guaranteed in return for accepting British paramountcy.
181.tq: Distinguish a guarantee under paramountcy from restoration of full sovereignty.

181.s: V.D. Savarkar referred to the Revolt of 1857 as the
o: last war of the Mughal Empire
181.x: V.D. Savarkar called the Revolt of 1857 the ‘first war of India’s independence’.
181.tq: Match the distinctive historical phrase with its associated thinker.

182.s: The Pattern 1853 Enfield rifle was introduced into the army in:
182.x: The new Pattern 1853 Enfield rifle was introduced into the army in December 1856.
182.tq: Use the precise date rather than the better-known date of the uprising.

182.s: Why did the cartridges of the new Enfield rifle offend both Hindu and Muslim sepoys?
o: They were believed to contain cow and pig fat, and had to be bitten open.
They required sepoys to cross the sea before use.
They were made exclusively from animal skin.
They were distributed only to European soldiers.
182.x: The greased-paper cartridges were believed to contain cow fat, offensive to Hindus, and pig fat, offensive to Muslims. Sepoys had to bite them open before loading.
182.tq: Identify the religious implication of the practical loading procedure.

182.s: The cartridge controversy was interpreted by many sepoys as evidence of:
o: A policy to promote Indian officers above Subedars
A colonial-missionary plot to defile religion and force conversion
A plan to reduce the size of the Bengal Army
182.x: The cartridges were viewed as final proof of a colonial-missionary conspiracy to defile Indian religions and compel conversion.
182.tq: Test the interpretation attached to an immediate cause.

182.s: Which one of the following rumours circulated before the Revolt of 1857?
o: Cow blood was being mixed in government wells only.
Bone dust was being mixed in Company flour.
Gunpowder was being mixed with salt in army stores.
Cholera germs were being mixed in postal letters.
182.x: A rumour spread that bone dust was being mixed in the flour supplied by the East India Company.
182.tq: Distinguish the specific rumour from unrelated allegations.

182.s: The mysterious chapatis associated with the events preceding the Revolt of 1857 were passed from village to village across:
182.x: Mysterious chapatis were passed from village to village across North India in early 1857.
182.tq: Test the geographical association of a distinctive event.

182.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early refusals and outbreaks connected with the Revolt of 1857:
1. The 19th Native Infantry refused at Berhampur in February 1857.
2. Mangal Pandey's action occurred at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
3. The Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: All three statements are correct: the 19th Native Infantry acted at Berhampur in February, Mangal Pandey acted at Barrackpore on 29 March, and the Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857.
182.tq: Link the three events through their locations and dates.

182.s: Mangal Pandey, associated with the Barrackpore incident, belonged to the:
182.x: Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
182.tq: Use the person-regiment association to separate closely related incidents.

182.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Barrackpore episode involving Mangal Pandey?
o: He attacked General Canning and was executed on 10 May 1857.
He led the 85 cavalrymen at Meerut and was executed on 9 May 1857.
He attacked Lieutenant Baugh and Sergeant-Major Hewson and was executed on 8 April 1857.
He refused service at Berhampur and was executed in February 1857.
182.x: Mangal Pandey attacked Lieutenant Baugh and Sergeant-Major Hewson at Barrackpore and was executed on 8 April 1857.
182.tq: Match the correct person with the deed and date.

182.s: What was the immediate administrative consequence for Mangal Pandey's regiment after the Barrackpore episode?
o: It was merged with the European regiments.
It was placed under the command of Mangal Pandey.
182.x: The 34th Bengal Native Infantry, Mangal Pandey's regiment, was disbanded after the incident.
182.tq: Test the institutional consequence rather than the event itself.

182.s: At Meerut, the 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were court-martialled on 9 May 1857 and sentenced to:
182.x: The 85 sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry were court-martialled on 9 May 1857 and given ten years' imprisonment, helping precipitate the rising on 10 May.
182.tq: Separate the punishment date from the date of the uprising.

182.s: The General Service Enlistment Act of 1856 was associated with the administration of:
182.x: The General Service Enlistment Act was enacted under Lord Canning in 1856.
182.tq: Apply the ruler-or-authority association trap.

182.s: The General Service Enlistment Act, 1856 required new recruits to:
o: Serve only within their home province
Receive equal pay with European soldiers
182.x: The Act required new recruits to serve anywhere, including overseas. Orthodox Hindus feared that sea travel would cause loss of caste.
182.tq: Infer the military grievance from the service obligation.

182.s: Why did overseas service create anxiety among orthodox Hindu sepoys?
o: Crossing the sea was believed to cause loss of caste.
It suspended their promotion to Subedar.
It involved compulsory conversion to Christianity.
It made them ineligible for bhatta in Punjab.
182.x: Orthodox Hindus believed that crossing the sea resulted in loss of caste, making the overseas-service requirement deeply unpopular.
182.tq: Connect a military rule with its socio-religious consequence.

182.s: Bhatta, whose withdrawal angered the sepoys, was a:
182.x: Bhatta was the foreign service allowance paid to soldiers serving outside their ordinary area.
182.tq: Discriminate between military pay components with similar administrative associations.

182.s: Bhatta was withdrawn for service in:
182.x: Bhatta was withdrawn for service in Sindh and Punjab after these areas became British territory.
182.tq: Pair the allowance grievance with the correct territories.

182.s: Which of the following was NOT a military grievance of the Indian sepoys mentioned in relation to the Revolt of 1857?
o: The ceiling of promotion at the rank of Subedar
182.x: Inefficiency of officers was identified as not being a cause of sepoy anger. Lower pay, racial contempt and the Subedar ceiling were genuine grievances.
182.tq: Find the one item expressly excluded from the list of grievances.

182.s: An Indian sepoy in the pre-1857 army could ordinarily rise no higher than:
182.x: Racial discrimination restricted the highest rank ordinarily attainable by an Indian soldier to Subedar.
182.tq: Test the exact promotion ceiling rather than general discrimination.

182.s: Which Act ended free postage for sepoys?
182.x: Free postage for sepoys was ended by the Post Office Act of 1854.
182.tq: Match a specific grievance with the legislation that caused it.

182.s: On the eve of the Revolt of 1857, the approximate ratio of Indian sepoys to European soldiers in India was:
182.x: There were about 2.3 lakh Indian sepoys and 45,000 European soldiers, giving an approximate ratio of 5:1.
182.tq: Convert the supplied troop figures into the approximate ratio.

182.s: Which pair correctly represents the approximate military strength on the eve of the Revolt of 1857?
o: 3 lakh Indian sepoys and 1 lakh Europeans
182.x: The Indian army consisted of approximately 2.3 lakh sepoys compared with about 45,000 European soldiers.
182.tq: Read both sides of a numerical comparison instead of relying only on the ratio.

182.s: The European troops in India had been reduced in part because they had been drawn off for the:
182.x: European troops had been drawn away for the Crimean and Persian wars, contributing to the imbalance in troop strength.
182.tq: Identify the two wars connected with the troop shortage.

182.s: Awadh was called the “nursery of the Bengal Army” because:
o: It was the only province where European soldiers were recruited.
Many Bengal Army sepoys were high-caste men from Awadh and carried regional grievances into the army.
It housed the headquarters of the Bengal Army exclusively.
It was the birthplace of the Enfield rifle.
182.x: The Bengal Army recruited many high-caste men from Awadh. Its annexation in 1856 therefore angered a large section of the sepoys.
182.tq: Use the institutional metaphor to infer its concrete meaning.

182.s: The expression “peasants in uniform” referred to the fact that the sepoys:
o: Were recruited only from European farming communities
Were trained exclusively in agricultural work
Received land grants instead of salaries
Carried rural and village grievances into the army
182.x: The sepoys were largely drawn from rural communities, so their grievances reflected those of the villages from which they came.
182.tq: Translate a descriptive phrase into its historical implication.

182.s: Who wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* on the causes of the Indian Revolt?
182.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan wrote *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*, meaning “The Causes of the Indian Revolt.”
182.tq: Match the author with the exact title of the work.

182.s: *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* was written in:
182.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan's work was written in Urdu during 1858–59.
182.tq: Test the language of a named historical source.

182.s: Vishnubhat Godse is associated with which of the following works?
o: *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*
182.x: Vishnubhat Godse wrote *Majha Pravas*, a Marathi eyewitness travelogue.
182.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair in a literary match.

182.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: V.D. Savarkar — *The Indian War of Independence*
182.x: V.D. Savarkar wrote *The Indian War of Independence*. *Majha Pravas* was written by Vishnubhat Godse, *Rebellion 1857: A Symposium* by P.C. Joshi, and *Eighteen Fifty-Seven* by S.N. Sen.
182.tq: Use author–work matching to reject swapped literary attributions.

182.s: V.D. Savarkar's *The Indian War of Independence* was published in:
182.x: V.D. Savarkar's work *The Indian War of Independence* was published in 1909.
182.tq: Distinguish the publication year from the revolt and later historical works.

182.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of publication:
A. *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*
B. *The Indian War of Independence*
C. *Eighteen Fifty-Seven*
D. *Majha Pravas*
182.x: *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind* appeared in 1858–59, followed by *Majha Pravas*, then Savarkar's work in 1909, and S.N. Sen's *Eighteen Fifty-Seven* in 1957.
182.tq: Fix the earliest and latest works first, then place the middle entries.

182.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its author?
o: *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857* — S.N. Sen
182.x: P.C. Joshi wrote *Rebellion 1857: A Symposium*. G.B. Malleson wrote *The Indian Mutiny of 1857*, Christopher Hibbert wrote *The Great Mutiny*, and Iqbal Hussain wrote *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857*.
182.tq: Reject swapped authors by checking the exact author–title combination.

182.s: Who wrote *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*?
182.x: R.C. Majumdar wrote *The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857*.
182.tq: Test a single author–title association from a cluster of historical writings.

182.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Iqbal Hussain — *Religion and Ideology of the Rebels of 1857*
Khan Mohammad Sadiq Khan — *Excavation of Truth*
P.E. Roberts — *The Causes of the Indian Revolt*
182.x: P.E. Roberts was associated with the description of the revolt as “just a sepoy mutiny,” not with a work titled *The Causes of the Indian Revolt*. *Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind*, meaning “The Causes of the Indian Revolt,” was written by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
182.tq: Detect the familiar title wrongly assigned to a different author.

182.s: P.E. Roberts described the Revolt of 1857 as:
o: A religious war against the British
The First War of Indian Independence
182.x: P.E. Roberts characterized the revolt as “just a sepoy mutiny,” particularly in connection with the cartridge issue.
182.tq: Separate the British interpretive label from the nationalist interpretation.

182.s:
According to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, which of the following contributed to the outbreak of the Revolt of 1857?
1. Lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council
2. Misunderstanding of Indian customs
3. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers
Which of the statements given above are correct?
182.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan blamed the lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council and the misunderstanding of Indian customs. Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers was not a cause identified by him.
182.tq: Use the contradiction in the third statement to isolate the two supported causes.

182.s: Which one of the following mutinies took place in July 1806?
o: Barrackpore mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry
Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry
182.x: The Vellore mutiny took place in July 1806. It was associated with the controversial military dress regulations and religious apprehensions.
182.tq: Use the direct date–event association.

182.s: The Vellore mutiny of 1806 was chiefly triggered by which of the following measures?
o: Introduction of a new dress code and prohibition of caste marks and earrings
Refusal to cross the sea to Burma
Refusal to use the new rifle cartridges
182.x: The new dress code, including a turban with a leather cockade and restrictions on caste marks and earrings, caused resentment among the sepoys at Vellore.
182.tq: Distinguish the cause attached to a specific mutiny.

182.s: The Barrackpore mutiny of November 1824 was caused by the sepoys’ refusal to—
182.x: The 47th Native Infantry at Barrackpore refused to go to Burma by sea during the First Anglo-Burmese War.
182.tq: Apply the who–cause–event linkage.

182.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Vellore mutiny — July 1806
b. Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry — November 1824
c. Berhampur mutiny of the 19th Native Infantry — February 1857
d. Barrackpore mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry — 29 March 1857
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
182.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Berhampur involved refusal of the new cartridges, while Mangal Pandey’s attack at Barrackpore occurred on 29 March 1857.
182.tq: Start from the sure date–event pairs and eliminate mismatched combinations.

182.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: 38th Native Infantry — Refusal to go to Burma in 1852
19th Native Infantry — Attack on officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857
182.x: The attack at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 was carried out by Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry. The 19th Native Infantry at Berhampur refused the new cartridges in February 1857.
182.tq: Find the wrong person–regiment association.

182.s: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 is distinguished from the mutinies listed in the context of the 1857 uprising because it was—
o: the first mutiny of the 34th Native Infantry
a civil revolt rather than a sepoy revolt
an uprising caused by the new cartridges
a military revolt over sea service
182.x: The Santhal revolt of 1855–56 was a civil revolt and not a sepoy mutiny.
182.tq: Separate a civil revolt from a military mutiny.

182.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Barrackpore mutiny of the 47th Native Infantry
B. Vellore mutiny
C. Berhampur refusal of the new cartridges
D. Mangal Pandey’s attack at Barrackpore
182.x: The correct sequence is Vellore mutiny in July 1806, Barrackpore mutiny in November 1824, Berhampur in February 1857 and Mangal Pandey’s attack on 29 March 1857.
182.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the intervening events.

182.s: Mangal Pandey was hanged and his regiment was disbanded on—
182.x: Mangal Pandey was hanged and the regiment was disbanded on 8 April 1857. His attack had taken place earlier, on 29 March 1857.
182.tq: Distinguish closely spaced dates in a sequence of events.

182.s: What immediately preceded the Meerut rising of 10 May 1857?
o: The proclamation of Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan
The sentencing of 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry to ten years’ imprisonment
The disbandment of Mangal Pandey’s regiment
The refusal of the 19th Native Infantry to use the rifle
182.x: On 9 May 1857, 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry at Meerut were sentenced to ten years. The rising followed on 10 May, when officers were shot and imprisoned comrades were freed.
182.tq: Identify the immediately preceding event rather than the later consequence.

182.s: The rebels who reached Delhi on 11–12 May 1857 proclaimed whom as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan?
182.x: After reaching Delhi, the rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as Shahenshah-e-Hindustan on 11–12 May 1857.
182.tq: Match the political title with the associated leader.

182.s: The abolition of Sati in 1829 was resented by orthodox sections primarily because it was viewed as—
o: an attempt to abolish temple taxation
182.x: The abolition of Sati was perceived by orthodox groups as interference in established custom.
182.tq: Link a social law with the specific form of resentment it generated.

182.s: Which British Governor-General is associated with the abolition of Sati in 1829?
182.x: The abolition of Sati in 1829 was carried out during the tenure of Lord William Bentinck.
182.tq: Use the reformer–reform association while avoiding ruler-swapping traps.

182.s: The Lex Loci Act, also known as the Religious or Caste Disabilities Act, was enacted in—
182.x: The Religious Disabilities Act, also called the Caste Disabilities Removal Act or Lex Loci Act, was enacted in 1850.
182.tq: Discriminate between closely related reform dates.

182.s: What provision of the Religious Disabilities Act of 1850 particularly alarmed orthodox sections?
o: It prohibited the taxation of religious lands
It abolished the zamindari system throughout India
It permitted converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property
It granted sepoys exemption from overseas service
182.x: The Act enabled converts to Christianity to inherit ancestral property, which was viewed as an incentive for conversion.
182.tq: Identify the practical consequence behind a source of religious apprehension.

182.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Christian missionaries preached under police protection.
2. Missionaries criticised Hindu and Islamic practices.
3. Western education, railways and the telegraph generated fears of mass conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
