191.s: The address beginning with ‘Sisters and Brothers of America’ was delivered by Swami Vivekananda on:
191.x: Vivekananda delivered the famous opening address on 11 September 1893 at the Chicago Parliament of Religions.
191.tq: Separate the event date from Vivekananda’s birth, Mission-foundation and death dates.

191.s: The expression “Daridra Narayana” in the teachings of Swami Vivekananda signifies that:
o: Religious institutions should avoid social service
The poor should be regarded as enemies of social progress
Service to the poor is service to God
Poverty is caused exclusively by lack of education
191.x: “Daridra Narayana” means that serving the poor is equivalent to serving God.
191.tq: Directly identify the precise meaning of a distinctive quotation.

191.s: Which of the following was NOT emphasised by Swami Vivekananda for national regeneration?
191.x: Vivekananda emphasised strength, self-confidence, youth and service, while condemning empty ritual.
191.tq: Find the one option that reverses the reformer's stated position.

191.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social ideas of Swami Vivekananda:
1. He condemned caste-based discrimination.
2. He regarded humanitarian relief as a monastic duty.
3. He supported empty ritual as the basis of national regeneration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Vivekananda condemned empty ritual, so statement 3 is false.
191.tq: Split the options by testing the reformer's positive and negative positions separately.

191.s: Who among the following was the Western disciple of Swami Vivekananda known as Sister Nivedita?
191.x: Margaret Noble became the well-known Western disciple of Vivekananda under the name Sister Nivedita.
191.tq: Match the adopted religious name with the original personal name.

191.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two journals associated with the Ramakrishna movement?
o: Prabuddha Bharata was in English and Udbodhan was in Bengali
Prabuddha Bharata was in Bengali and Udbodhan was in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in English
Both Prabuddha Bharata and Udbodhan were in Bengali
191.x: Prabuddha Bharata was an English journal, whereas Udbodhan was published in Bengali.
191.tq: Discriminate between two similar entries by pairing each with its language.

191.s: Belur Math, established in 1898, is significant because it is the:
o: First headquarters of the Arya Samaj
Permanent headquarters of the Ramakrishna Order
191.x: Belur Math became the permanent headquarters of the Ramakrishna Order in 1898.
191.tq: Use the date and institutional function together to identify the correct establishment.

191.s: The architecture of Belur Math symbolically combines which of the following traditions?
191.x: Belur Math blends Hindu, Islamic and Christian architectural motifs to express the unity of religions.
191.tq: Recall a distinctive three-part cultural combination.

191.s: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was associated as a mystic and priest with the:
191.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa served as a mystic and priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Calcutta.
191.tq: Identify the religious figure through his principal place of association.

191.s: What was the original name of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
191.x: Ramakrishna Paramahansa was born as Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya.
191.tq: Separate the original names of closely associated nineteenth-century religious figures.

191.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
191.x: Bhairavi Brahmani instructed Ramakrishna in Tantra, while Totapuri was his teacher in Advaita. Sarada Devi was his wife.
191.tq: Start from the sure teacher–school pair and eliminate the swapped associations.

191.s: Who was the wife of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
191.x: Sarada Devi was the wife of Ramakrishna Paramahansa.
191.tq: Directly identify the associated family relationship.

191.s: The statement “as many faiths, so many paths” expresses Ramakrishna Paramahansa’s belief that:
o: All religions lead to the same truth
Salvation is possible only through renunciation
Only one religion can lead to salvation
Religious rituals are superior to devotion
191.x: The statement expresses the belief that different religions ultimately lead to the same truth.
191.tq: Apply a famous maxim to the underlying religious doctrine.

191.s:
According to Ramakrishna Paramahansa, salvation could be pursued through:
1. Devotion
2. Meditation
3. Renunciation
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Ramakrishna identified devotion, meditation and renunciation as paths through which salvation could be pursued.
191.tq: Recognise the complete list when all listed elements belong to the same teaching.

191.s: The Adyar headquarters of the Theosophical Society was important in Andhra because it:
o: Transferred the Arya Samaj headquarters to Andhra
Excluded Andhra from the Society’s activities
Placed Andhra within the Society’s core area
191.x: The Adyar headquarters placed Andhra within the core area of the Theosophical Society.
191.tq: Identify the institutional effect of a regional headquarters.

191.s: Which of the following publications of Annie Besant reached Andhra and helped spread Home Rule ideas?
191.x: Annie Besant’s New India and Commonweal reached Andhra, along with the activities of her Madras Home Rule League.
191.tq: Discriminate between reform and nationalist journals by their editor and context.

191.s: In which year did the Krishna Divyajnana Lodge establish a public library at Guntur?
191.x: The Krishna Divyajnana Lodge established the public library in Guntur in 1882, the first public library in Guntur district.
191.tq: Use the year attached to a specific regional institutional event.

191.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Mocherla Hanumantha Rao
(b) Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
(c) Veeresalingam
(d) BT College

List-II
(i) Madanapalle
(ii) Organised Besant’s Andhra tour
(iii) Secretary of the Andhra Home Rule branch
(iv) First Theosophical High School in Andhra

Select the correct code:
191.x: Mocherla organised Besant’s tour; Gadicherla was Secretary of the Andhra Home Rule branch; Veeresalingam set up the first Theosophical High School; BT College was at Madanapalle.
191.tq: Start from the sure person–role pairs and complete the institutional matches.

191.s: Besant Theosophical (National) College was established at Madanapalle in:
191.x: Besant Theosophical (National) College was established at Madanapalle in 1916.
191.tq: Match a regional institution with its establishment year.

191.s: Which of the following was the original name of Swami Dayanand Saraswati?
191.x: Swami Dayanand Saraswati was born Mool Shankar.
191.tq: Distinguish the birth names of major reformers.

191.s: Which work of Swami Dayanand Saraswati is known as “Light of Truth”?
o: At the Feet of the Master
191.x: Satyarth Prakash means “Light of Truth” and is the principal text associated with Dayanand Saraswati.
191.tq: Match the translated title with the correct original work.

191.s: The slogan “Back to the Vedas” is associated with the Arya Samaj’s belief that:
o: Only priests may read the Vedas
191.x: The Arya Samaj advocated a return to the Vedas and regarded the Vedas as infallible.
191.tq: Infer the doctrinal principle represented by a reform movement’s slogan.

191.s:
Consider the following statements about the Arya Samaj:
1. It opposed caste based on birth.
2. It supported widow remarriage and women’s education.
3. It held idol worship to be useful and essential.
4. It maintained that all people could read the Vedas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Arya Samaj considered idol worship useless, making statement 3 false.
191.tq: Find the single doctrinal reversal among several reform principles.

191.s: The split in the Arya Samaj between the College or DAV party and the Gurukul party took place in:
191.x: The Arya Samaj split into the College or DAV wing and the Gurukul wing in 1893, after Dayanand’s death.
191.tq: Use the movement’s internal division date rather than the dates of its institutions.

191.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: DAV party — Swami Shraddhanand — Gurukul Kangri
Gurukul party — Mahatma Hansraj — First DAV School, Lahore
DAV party — Mahatma Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai — First DAV School, Lahore
Gurukul party — Lala Lajpat Rai — Gurukul Kangri
191.x: The College or DAV party was led by Mahatma Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai and was associated with the First DAV School at Lahore.
191.tq: Use the leader–wing–institution chain to reject swapped combinations.

191.s: Gurukul Kangri, associated with the Gurukul wing of the Arya Samaj, was established at Haridwar in:
191.x: Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar was established in 1902 and was associated with Swami Shraddhanand, originally Munshi Ram.
191.tq: Link the institution, location and year before selecting the numerical answer.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in:
191.x: Vivekananda established Vedanta Societies in the United States of America and Britain.
191.tq: Recall the two-country institutional association given for the reformer.

191.s: Lectures from Colombo to Almora is associated with speeches delivered by Swami Vivekananda after his return in 1897 through:
191.x: The work is based on speeches delivered after Vivekananda’s 1897 return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras.
191.tq: Identify the correct travel route attached to a published work.

191.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Swami Vivekananda in chronological order:
A. Meditation on the Kanyakumari rock
B. Address at the World’s Parliament of Religions
C. Speech at Mahboob College, Secunderabad
D. Return through Colombo, Ramnad and Madras
191.x: Vivekananda meditated at Kanyakumari in December 1892, spoke at Secunderabad in February 1893, addressed the Chicago Parliament in 1893, and returned through the southern route in 1897.
191.tq: Fix the first and last events, then arrange the two intervening 1893 events.

191.s: Swami Vivekananda meditated on the rock at Kanyakumari in:
191.x: Vivekananda meditated on the Kanyakumari rock in December 1892, before his journey to Chicago.
191.tq: Distinguish two closely connected pre-Chicago dates.

191.s: At which of the following places did Swami Vivekananda speak in February 1893?
191.x: Swami Vivekananda spoke at Mahboob College in Secunderabad in February 1893.
191.tq: Match the speaker with the specific South Indian venue.

191.s: The Shuddhi Movement launched by the Arya Samaj primarily aimed at:
o: Reconversion to Hinduism and admission of outsiders
191.x: The Shuddhi Movement sought the reconversion to Hinduism of those who had adopted Islam or Christianity and also admitted outsiders into Hindu society.
191.tq: Apply the movement’s stated purpose to a concrete religious-community situation.

191.s: Which organisation launched the Shuddhi Movement?
191.x: The Shuddhi Movement was launched by the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Identify the organisation from a movement–organisation association.

191.s: The Andhra Shuddhi Samajam was established at Guntur in January 1934 under the secretaryship of:
191.x: The Andhra Shuddhi Samajam was established at Guntur in January 1934, with Upputuru Venkata Punnarao as secretary.
191.tq: Combine the organisation, place, date and office-holder before choosing the answer.

191.s:
Which of the following regions is associated with the activities of the Shuddhi Movement in Andhra?
1. Guntur
2. West Godavari
3. Krishna
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: The Shuddhi Movement had activities in Guntur, West Godavari and Krishna districts or regions of Andhra.
191.tq: Recognise the complete regional list when all three locations are associated with the movement.

191.s: Which one of the following was NOT a common feature of the nineteenth-century reform movements considered together?
191.x: These reform movements attacked caste and promoted rationalism, education and women’s emancipation; they did not support caste hierarchy uncritically.
191.tq: Find the option that contradicts the shared reform orientation.

191.s: The cultural role of these reform movements in the growth of Indian nationalism was primarily to:
o: Strengthen the colonial claim of Indian inferiority
Create cultural confidence and provide ground for the national movement
End all political activity in India
191.x: By generating cultural confidence against the colonial narrative of Indian inferiority, the reform movements helped prepare the ground for the national movement.
191.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect link between cultural reform and nationalism.

191.s: Which statement best describes the political significance of Theosophy in the Indian context?
o: It supported the colonial narrative of racial superiority
It remained completely separate from political activity
It opposed all forms of education
It led directly into the Home Rule movement
191.x: Theosophy led directly into Home Rule, particularly through Annie Besant’s activities and publications.
191.tq: Identify the direct political consequence of an intellectual movement.

191.s: The Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre of the Ramakrishna Mission is located at which place in Andhra Pradesh?
191.x: The Ramakrishna Mission's Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre is located at Vijayawada.
191.tq: Use the place-name distinction among the Andhra Pradesh locations.

191.s: The Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre at Vijayawada was built at an expenditure of approximately:
191.x: The centre at Vijayawada was built at a cost of ₹8.5 crore.
191.tq: Identify the exact figure from closely spaced numerical options.

191.s: Who inaugurated the Ramakrishna Mission's Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre at Vijayawada on 1 February 2026?
191.x: Ramakrishna Mission President Swami Gautamananda inaugurated the centre on 1 February 2026.
191.tq: Match the office-holder with the event rather than the associated speaker.

191.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vivekananda Human Excellence Centre at Vijayawada was inaugurated on 1 February 2026.
2. It was built at a cost of ₹8.5 crore.
3. It was inaugurated by M. Venkaiah Naidu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
191.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Swami Gautamananda inaugurated the centre; M. Venkaiah Naidu described the Mission as a ‘university of values’.
191.tq: Separate the person who inaugurated an event from the person associated with a quoted description.

191.s: M. Venkaiah Naidu described the Ramakrishna Mission as a:
191.x: M. Venkaiah Naidu called the Ramakrishna Mission a ‘university of values’.
191.tq: Test the exact wording of a notable description.

191.s: National Youth Day 2026 marked which anniversary of Swami Vivekananda's birth?
191.x: National Youth Day 2026 marked Swami Vivekananda's 163rd birth anniversary.
191.tq: Distinguish the precise anniversary from nearby numerical distractors.

191.s: Which one of the following best expresses the historical significance attributed to Theosophy and the Ramakrishna movement?
o: They rejected all forms of Indian cultural revival.
They confined religious reform to political representation.
They restored Indian cultural self-confidence against colonial claims of superiority.
They promoted colonial claims of European cultural superiority.
191.x: Theosophy and the Ramakrishna movement helped restore Indian cultural self-confidence in opposition to colonial claims of superiority.
191.tq: Select the option that captures the stated cause-and-effect relationship.

191.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an Andhra Pradesh association?
1. BT College — Madanapalle
2. Theosophical lodge library — Guntur
3. Ramakrishna Mission — Vijayawada
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: All three associations are correct: BT College is associated with Madanapalle, the Theosophical lodge library with Guntur, and the Ramakrishna Mission with Vijayawada.
191.tq: Verify each place–institution pair before selecting the complete combination.

191.s: The International Aryan Summit 2025, held in New Delhi, marked which of the following occasions?
o: Dayanand's 150th birth anniversary and Arya Samaj's 100th year
Dayanand's 175th birth anniversary and Arya Samaj's 125th year
Dayanand's 200th birth anniversary and Arya Samaj's 150th year
Dayanand's 200th birth anniversary and Arya Samaj's 200th year
191.x: The International Aryan Summit 2025 marked Dayanand's 200th birth anniversary and the 150th year of the Arya Samaj.
191.tq: Match two commemorative figures simultaneously rather than relying on one number.

191.s: By 1920, Arya Samaj branches in Andhra Pradesh were reported at which of the following places?
191.x: By 1920, Arya Samaj branches had been established in Anantapur and Chittoor.
191.tq: Identify the correct geographical pair from nearby Andhra Pradesh locations.

191.s: Madanapalle is associated with which movement or organization in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
191.x: Madanapalle is identified as an Andhra centre of Theosophy.
191.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed reform movements using the associated centre.

191.s:
Which one of the following correctly represents the comparative orientation of the three movements?
1. Arya Samaj — revivalist and associated with ‘Back to the Vedas’
2. Ramakrishna Mission — service and universalism
3. Theosophy — foreign-founded Hindu revival
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
191.x: All three comparisons are correct. Arya Samaj followed a revivalist ‘Back to the Vedas’ approach, the Ramakrishna Mission emphasised service and universalism, and Theosophy represented a foreign-founded Hindu revival.
191.tq: Compare the defining orientation of each movement instead of treating them as identical reform organisations.

191.s:
Arrange the following Andhra Pradesh associations in the order in which they are presented in the comparative regional context:
A. Theosophical centre at Madanapalle
B. Arya Samaj branches at Anantapur and Chittoor by 1920
C. Guntur Theosophical lodge library
D. Ramakrishna Mission centre at Vijayawada
191.x: The regional associations are presented as Madanapalle's Theosophy centre, the Guntur Theosophical lodge library, Arya Samaj branches in Anantapur and Chittoor by 1920, and the Ramakrishna Mission at Vijayawada.
191.tq: Use the sequence of regional references and distinguish it from a purely chronological sequence.

192.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scientific Society associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan:
1. It was founded at Ghazipur in 1864.
2. It translated Western science, history and philosophy into Urdu.
3. It was later shifted to Lucknow.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The Scientific Society was founded at Ghazipur in 1864 and translated Western knowledge into Urdu. It was later shifted to Aligarh, not Lucknow.
192.tq: Split the statements by checking the institution's original and later locations.

192.s:
With reference to the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental institution, consider the following statements:
1. The school stage began at Aligarh in 1875.
2. It was elevated into a college in 1877.
3. It was founded by Theodore Beck.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The MAO institution began as a school in 1875 and became a college in 1877 under Sayyid Ahmad Khan. Theodore Beck later served as its principal, but was not its founder.
192.tq: Distinguish the founder from a later principal and separate the school and college dates.

192.s: The Muhammadan Educational Conference associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan was established in
192.x: The Muhammadan Educational Conference was established in 1886.
192.tq: Use the exact year and reject nearby institutional dates.

192.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: MAO Defence Association — Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck
Muhammadan Literary Society — Nawab Abdul Latif
Muhammadan Educational Conference — Rashid Ahmad Gangohi
192.x: The Muhammadan Educational Conference was associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan, not Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.
192.tq: Find the mismatched founder while keeping the institution-founder pairs distinct.

192.s: The MAO Defence Association, formed in 1893, was primarily associated with which of the following positions?
o: Loyalism and opposition to the Congress
192.x: The MAO Defence Association, associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck, was loyalist and anti-Congress in outlook.
192.tq: Identify the organisation's political stance rather than its educational association.

192.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Aligarh Movement — Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
2. Faraizi Movement — Haji Shariatullah
3. Taiyuni Movement — Karamat Ali Jaunpuri
4. Ahmadiya Movement — Mirza Ghulam Ahmad
192.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Aligarh, Faraizi, Taiyuni and Ahmadiya movements are associated respectively with Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, Haji Shariatullah, Karamat Ali Jaunpuri and Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.
192.tq: Start from the sure founder-pairs and verify all four before selecting the complete combination.

192.s: Haji Shariatullah's Faraizi Movement was mainly associated with
192.x: The Faraizi Movement was founded by Haji Shariatullah in East Bengal, particularly the Faridpur region.
192.tq: Separate the regional locations of closely related Muslim reform movements.

192.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Faraizi Movement is correct?
o: It was founded by Haji Shariatullah in 1818 and was later associated with Dudu Miyan.
It was founded by Syed Ahmad Barelvi at Patna in 1888.
It was founded by Karamat Ali Jaunpuri at Lucknow in 1894.
It was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad at Qadian in 1889.
192.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in 1818, and Dudu Miyan later succeeded him.
192.tq: Match the founder, year and successor instead of relying on a single name.

192.s: Syed Ahmad Barelvi's Wahabi movement in India was inspired by the teachings of
192.x: The Indian Wahabi movement led by Syed Ahmad Barelvi drew inspiration from Shah Waliullah.
192.tq: Distinguish the ideological inspiration from the later organisational centre.

192.s:
Which of the following combinations regarding Muslim reform movements is correct?
1. Wahabi Movement — Patna as a principal centre
2. Ahmadiya Movement — Qadian
3. Nadwatul Ulama — Lucknow
4. Deoband Movement — Saharanpur district
192.x: Patna was a principal centre of the Wahabi movement, Qadian was associated with the Ahmadiya movement, Nadwatul Ulama was located at Lucknow, and Deoband lay in Saharanpur district.
192.tq: Compare locations across movements and check whether each regional association is accurate.

192.s:
Arrange the following movements in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Faraizi Movement
B. Deoband Movement
C. Ahmadiya Movement
D. Nadwatul Ulama
192.x: The Faraizi Movement dates from 1818, Deoband from 1866, Ahmadiya from 1889 and Nadwatul Ulama from 1894.
192.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two nineteenth-century movements between them.

192.s: The Deoband Movement began at Darul Uloom in 1866 under the leadership of
o: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad and Shibli Numani
Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi
Sayyid Ahmad Khan and Theodore Beck
192.x: Qasim Nanotavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi led the establishment of the Deoband movement at Darul Uloom in 1866.
192.tq: Use the paired-founder clue and avoid mixing Deoband leaders with Aligarh or Ahmadiya figures.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deoband Movement:
1. It began in Deoband in Saharanpur district of the United Provinces.
2. It was led by orthodox ulema.
3. Its principal aim was to promote loyalty to British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: The movement began at Deoband in Saharanpur district and was led by orthodox ulema. It opposed foreign rule rather than promoting loyalty to the British.
192.tq: Test the location and leadership separately from the reversed political stance.

192.s: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Deoband Movement?
o: To keep alive the spirit of jihad against foreign rulers
To replace traditional Islamic learning with exclusively Western education
To spread the pure teachings of the Quran and Hadith
192.x: The Deoband Movement aimed at religious revival, training religious leaders and resistance to foreign rule; replacing Islamic learning with exclusively Western education was not its objective.
192.tq: Find the option that reverses the movement's traditionalist educational character.

192.s: The Deoband leadership's position towards the Indian National Congress was that it
o: remained permanently neutral towards all political organisations
welcomed the Congress and issued a fatwa against the anti-Congress associations of Sayyid Ahmad Khan
rejected the Congress and established the United Indian Patriotic Association
supported the MAO Defence Association against the Congress
192.x: The Deoband movement welcomed the Congress. In 1888, it issued a fatwa against Sayyid Ahmad Khan's United Indian Patriotic Association and MAO Association.
192.tq: Contrast the Congress-friendly Deoband position with the anti-Congress Aligarh position.

192.s: The fatwa issued by the Deoband scholars in 1888 was directed against which organisations associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan?
o: Muhammadan Literary Society and Scientific Society
United Indian Patriotic Association and MAO Association
192.x: The 1888 fatwa opposed the United Indian Patriotic Association and the MAO Association associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan.
192.tq: Link the date to the two organisations rather than to the later political bodies.

192.s: Who among the following gave political content to the Deoband Movement and became associated with the Jamiat-ul-Ulema?
192.x: Mahmud-ul-Hasan gave the Deoband movement a political orientation and was associated with the Jamiat-ul-Ulema.
192.tq: Match the later political development with its correct Deobandi leader.

192.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Aligarh and Deoband approaches?
o: Aligarh emphasised Western education and loyalty to the British, whereas Deoband emphasised traditional Islamic learning and opposed foreign rule.
Aligarh opposed Western education, whereas Deoband promoted exclusive Western education.
Both movements opposed the Congress and supported loyalty to the British.
Both movements rejected religious education and concentrated only on political agitation.
192.x: The Aligarh approach promoted Western education and loyalty to the British, while Deoband upheld traditional Islamic learning and adopted an anti-foreign-rule orientation.
192.tq: Compare both columns together, especially education policy and political attitude.

192.s: Shibli Numani is associated with the founding of which institution at Lucknow?
192.x: Shibli Numani founded Nadwat al-Ulama at Lucknow in the 1894–96 period and supported the teaching of English and European science.
192.tq: Distinguish the Lucknow institution from the Aligarh and Deoband organisations.

192.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan's Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind dealt with
o: the history of the Faraizi Movement
the principles of the Ahmadiya faith
the causes of the Indian Revolt of 1857
the foundation of the Indian National Congress
192.x: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind, written by Sayyid Ahmad Khan in 1859, examined the causes of the Indian Revolt of 1857.
192.tq: Identify the subject of the work rather than confusing it with the author's educational writings.

192.s: Which of the following was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist thought?
192.x: Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was the journal associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan's reformist and rational interpretation of Islam.
192.tq: Distinguish a journal from books and publications associated with other reformers.

192.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan promoted Urdu primarily as
o: a language restricted to religious ceremonies
the official language of the Indian National Congress
a replacement for all regional languages
192.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan promoted Urdu as a unifying language among Muslims.
192.tq: Apply the stated purpose of a language policy rather than infer an exaggerated exclusive claim.

192.s: Which of the following best describes Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political position towards the Indian National Congress?
o: He supported the Congress as the sole organisation representing both communities.
He founded the Congress and presided over its first session.
He asked Muslims to stay away from it and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
He joined the Congress through the Deoband fatwa of 1888.
192.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan advised Muslims to remain away from the Congress and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888 to counter it.
192.tq: Use the organisation formed and its date to confirm the political position.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about Sayyid Ahmad Khan:
1. He lived from 1817 to 1898.
2. After 1857, he promoted the modernisation of Muslims through English education.
3. He advocated a rational reading of Islam.
4. He consistently maintained the same political view throughout his life and never spoke of Hindu-Muslim unity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: Sayyid Ahmad Khan lived from 1817 to 1898 and promoted English education and rational religious interpretation after 1857. The fourth statement is false because his earlier thought included advocacy of Hindu-Muslim unity.
192.tq: Reject the absolute word 'never' by separating an earlier view from a later political position.

192.s: The change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook, from an earlier emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity to separate political paths, was associated with the
192.x: The Hindi-Urdu controversy of 1867 contributed to the change in Sayyid Ahmad Khan's political outlook.
192.tq: Link the change in political outlook to the specific earlier controversy, not to later nationalist movements.

192.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Theodore Beck — Principal of MAO College from 1883 to 1899
Theodore Morison — Successor to Theodore Beck as MAO principal
Mahmud-ul-Hasan — Founder of the United Indian Patriotic Association
192.x: The United Indian Patriotic Association was formed by Sayyid Ahmad Khan in 1888. Mahmud-ul-Hasan was associated with giving political content to the Deoband movement.
192.tq: Separate institutional office-holders from founders of political associations.

192.s:
Arrange the following developments associated with Sayyid Ahmad Khan in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Scientific Society at Ghazipur
B. Beginning of the MAO school at Aligarh
C. Establishment of the Muhammadan Educational Conference
D. Formation of the United Indian Patriotic Association
192.x: The Scientific Society began in 1864, the MAO school in 1875, the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886, and the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.
192.tq: Place the dated milestones in ascending order and use the 1886–1888 pair as the final check.

192.s: The Aligarh Movement primarily sought to modernise Muslims through
o: armed resistance against the British from the beginning
English education and a rational interpretation of Islam
exclusive reliance on traditional madrasa education
rejection of all Western science and philosophy
192.x: The Aligarh Movement promoted English education and a rational reading of Islam as instruments of Muslim modernisation after 1857.
192.tq: Identify the central reform principle by distinguishing modernisation from traditional revivalism.

192.s: Which one of the following institutions was later transformed into Aligarh Muslim University in 1920?
192.x: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was transformed into Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
192.tq: Trace the institutional continuity from the college to the university.

192.s: The Faraizi Movement, founded in East Bengal, primarily aimed at:
o: Enforcing the religious duties known as faraiz and purging un-Islamic practices
192.x: The Faraizi Movement sought to enforce religious duties, or faraiz, and remove un-Islamic practices. It was founded by Haji Shariatullah in East Bengal.
192.tq: Identify the movement from its distinctive objective and religious terminology.

192.s: Who founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818?
192.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818. Dudu Miyan, his son, later led the movement.
192.tq: Separate the founder from the later leader while retaining the date.

192.s: Dudu Miyan transformed the Faraizi Movement into a movement primarily directed against:
o: British missionary institutions and Parsi reformers
192.x: Dudu Miyan, the son of Haji Shariatullah, converted the Faraizi Movement into a peasant movement against zamindars and indigo planters.
192.tq: Apply the movement’s social base and immediate opponents to a rural conflict.

192.s: Which sequence correctly represents the institutional development of the Aligarh educational initiative?
o: College classes in 1877 — school in 1875 — AMU in 1920
School in 1875 — college classes in 1877 — AMU in 1920
AMU in 1920 — school in 1875 — college classes in 1877
School in 1877 — college classes in 1920 — AMU in 1875
192.x: The Aligarh institution began as a school in 1875, college classes started in 1877, and it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
192.tq: Arrange the institutional stages by first identifying the earliest year.

192.s: The educational model of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was based on:
o: Khalsa College and Singh Sabha schools
Traditional madrasas of Patna and Deoband
192.x: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was modelled on Oxford and Cambridge. It was intended to provide modern education to Muslims.
192.tq: Distinguish the institutional model from the movement’s broader political orientation.

192.s:
Consider the following statements about the Aligarh Movement:
1. It emerged against the background of the educational backwardness of Muslims after 1857.
2. It encouraged a rational reading of Islam.
3. It was associated with cooperation with the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
192.x: All three statements are correct. The movement sought Muslim social and educational uplift through modern education, rational religious interpretation and cooperation with the British.
192.tq: Check each statement against the movement’s background, intellectual approach and political attitude.

192.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the later leadership of the Aligarh Movement?
192.x: Baba Dayal Das was associated with the Nirankari movement. Chiragh Ali, Altaf Husain Hali and Mohsin-ul-Mulk were later leaders associated with the Aligarh Movement.
192.tq: Find the person belonging to a neighbouring reform movement rather than the named movement.

192.s: Who served as a British principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in addition to Theodore Beck?
192.x: Theodore Morison was another British principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College. The other three were later Muslim leaders associated with the Aligarh Movement.
192.tq: Separate British institutional administrators from later Indian movement leaders.

192.s: The Wahabi Movement in India was named after:
192.x: The movement was named after Abdul Wahab of Arabia, although its Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi.
192.tq: Distinguish the ideological namesake from the Indian founder.

192.s:
Arrange the following events connected with the Wahabi Movement in chronological order:
A. Ambala trial
B. Arrest of Mubariz-ud-Daula
C. Patna trial
D. Suppression of the movement
192.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, followed by the Ambala trial in 1864, the Patna trial in 1865 and suppression of the movement by 1870.
192.tq: Use the dated events as anchors and place the undated suppression after the trials.

192.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Wahabi Movement is correct?
o: It was suppressed by 1857 after remaining confined to Bengal.
It supported British influence in the Deccan and rejected armed resistance.
It was primarily a Parsi educational movement centred in Bombay.
It fought the Sikhs in Punjab and subsequently opposed the British.
192.x: The movement first fought the Sikhs in Punjab and then fought the British. It was suppressed by 1870 and was anti-British in character.
192.tq: Test the movement’s changing military target and overall political character.

192.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with Wahabi activity in Hyderabad, was:
o: A Parsi reformer who edited Rast Goftar
A brother of the Nizam who resisted British influence in the Deccan
A principal of the Aligarh college
A Sikh mahant who controlled gurdwaras in Punjab
192.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was the Nizam’s brother. Influenced by Syed Ahmad Barelvi, he attempted to organise resistance to British influence in the Deccan and died in prison after his arrest.
192.tq: Match the regional leader with his family position and political activity.

192.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: The Indian Musalmans — Sayyid Ahmad Khan
192.x: W.W. Hunter wrote The Indian Musalmans in 1871. Sayyid Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind, while Rast Goftar was associated with Parsi reform.
192.tq: Start with the sure book–author pair and eliminate cross-movement substitutions.

192.s: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by:
192.x: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by Sayyid Ahmad Khan. W.W. Hunter authored The Indian Musalmans.
192.tq: Discriminate between two books dealing with Muslims under British rule.

192.s: The Ahmadiya Movement was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad at Qadian in:
192.x: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian in Punjab in 1889.
192.tq: Use the place–founder–year combination to distinguish the movement from Aligarh and Sikh reform movements.

192.s: Which one of the following is NOT a belief or feature associated with the Ahmadiya Movement?
o: A liberal and universal conception of religion
Unqualified acceptance of orthodox Muslim objections to its founder’s claims
Promotion of Western liberal education among Muslims
192.x: The Ahmadiya Movement promoted liberal and universal religious ideas, opposed jihad and supported Western liberal education. Orthodox Muslims rejected Mirza Ghulam Ahmad’s claim to be a messiah.
192.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the movement’s relationship with orthodox criticism.

192.s: Qadian, associated with the foundation of the Ahmadiya Movement, is located in:
192.x: Qadian is in Gurdaspur district of Punjab. It was the place where Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiya Movement.
192.tq: Use the precise location rather than the broader regional label alone.

192.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Movement)
a. Nirankari
b. Namdhari or Kuka
c. Singh Sabha
d. Akali

List-II (Leader or feature)
i. Removal of corrupt mahants from gurdwaras
ii. Baba Dayal Das and belief in Nirankar
iii. Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini
a. Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature
192.x: Nirankari was associated with Baba Dayal Das and the formless God; Namdhari with Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini; Singh Sabha with Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature; and Akali with removal of corrupt mahants.
192.tq: Start from the distinctive Nirankar and mahant associations to secure the code.

192.s: The Singh Sabha movement was associated with which of the following developments?
o: Opposition to all forms of Sikh education
Promotion of Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature
Establishment of the Faraizi peasant movement
192.x: The Singh Sabha movement promoted Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature. It was associated with Singh Sabha centres at Amritsar and Lahore and with Khalsa College, Amritsar.
192.tq: Link the reform organisation with its specific literary and educational programme.

192.s: Which of the following chronology is correct regarding institutions associated with the Singh Sabha movement?
o: Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1873; Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1879; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1892
Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1873; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1873; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1879; Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1873
192.x: The Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar in 1873 and Lahore in 1879. Khalsa College at Amritsar was established in 1892.
192.tq: Arrange the three dated Sikh reform developments from earliest to latest.

192.s: Which statement best describes the significance of Ram Singh Kuka in the Sikh reform tradition?
o: He was the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods.
He founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian.
He introduced Urdu as the language of Osmania University.
He founded the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha in Bombay.
192.x: Ram Singh Kuka is noted as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods. He was later exiled to Rangoon after the 1872 Malerkotla clash.
192.tq: Identify the distinctive method associated with the correct Sikh leader.

192.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925 placed gurdwaras under the control of the:
192.x: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed gurdwaras under the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, or SGPC. This represented a major success of the Akali Movement.
192.tq: Match the legislation with the institutional authority created or recognised by it.

192.s: Which of the following was NOT a focus of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
192.x: The Sabha focused on girls’ education, reform of marriage customs and opposition to orthodoxy. Gurdwara management belonged to the Sikh reform context, particularly the Akali movement.
192.tq: Find the item belonging to a different religious reform tradition.

192.s: Rast Goftar, the organ of the Parsi reform movement, means:
192.x: Rast Goftar means “Truth-teller.” It was the organ of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha and was edited by Dadabhai Naoroji.
192.tq: Use the exact meaning of the named journal rather than a broad reform slogan.

192.s: Who edited Rast Goftar, the organ associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
192.x: Dadabhai Naoroji edited Rast Goftar. He was also one of the founders of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha.
192.tq: Separate the journal editor from the other founders listed with him.

192.s: Nasaraiah, who was popular among the Madigas, preached:
o: The superiority of zamindars over peasants
The necessity of armed jihad against all Western education
One God and opposition to idol worship
The establishment of Sikh gurdwara committees
192.x: Nasaraiah, a Sayyid Muslim who died in 1825, preached belief in one God and opposed idol worship. He was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet region of Guntur.
192.tq: Connect the regional reformer with his central religious teaching.

192.s: Nasaraiah was associated with which region of present-day Andhra Pradesh?
192.x: Nasaraiah was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet area of Guntur. He was popular among the Madigas and preached monotheism.
192.tq: Use the precise Andhra regional association to distinguish similar reformers.

192.s: Which one of the following statements about Osmania University is correct?
o: It was established at Bombay in 1851 and taught through Gujarati.
It was established at Qadian in 1889 and taught through Punjabi.
It was established at Aligarh in 1920 and taught only through Persian.
It was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught through Urdu.
192.x: Osmania University was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught in Urdu. It conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in 1953.
192.tq: Combine the institution’s place, year and medium of instruction.

192.s: Osmania University conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in:
192.x: Osmania University, established in Hyderabad in 1918, conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in 1953.
192.tq: Distinguish the university’s founding year from the later honorary degree year.

192.s: Which comparison between the Aligarh and Deoband movements is correctly stated?
o: Aligarh emphasised Western education and cooperation with the British, whereas Deoband represented an orthodox and anti-British strand.
Aligarh was orthodox and anti-British, whereas Deoband promoted Western education and cooperation with the British.
Both movements rejected modern education and supported British colonial rule.
Both movements were primarily Sikh and Parsi reform organisations.
192.x: Aligarh promoted Western education and was broadly pro-British and anti-Congress, whereas Deoband preserved an orthodox, anti-British and pro-Congress strand.
192.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap by separating educational orientation from political stance.

192.s: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the broader significance of the Aligarh and Deoband movements?
o: Deoband created the modern educated Muslim middle class, while Aligarh opposed all modern education.
Aligarh helped build a modern educated Muslim middle class, while Deoband kept alive an orthodox and anti-colonial strand.
Aligarh and Deoband were both exclusively movements for Sikh gurdwara reform.
Neither movement had an educational or political significance.
192.x: Aligarh contributed to the growth of a modern educated Muslim middle class. Deoband preserved an orthodox and anti-colonial tendency within Muslim public life.
192.tq: Match each movement with its distinctive historical contribution rather than reversing them.

192.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan’s later political conservatism has been criticised for:
o: Sowing the seeds of communal division
192.x: A criticism of Sayyid Ahmad Khan’s later political conservatism is that it sowed the seeds of communal division. This criticism is distinct from the educational objectives of the Aligarh Movement.
192.tq: Identify the stated historical criticism without confusing it with institutional achievements.

192.s: Which statement reflects the criticism concerning the political position of the Deoband movement?
o: It was founded to promote Parsi marriage reform.
It supported British rule because it rejected all anti-colonial activity.
It supported Congress largely to oppose Sir Syed rather than from a positive political creed.
It sought to replace Gurmukhi with Urdu in Sikh institutions.
192.x: One criticism holds that Deoband supported Congress more as a means of opposing Sir Syed than from an independently developed positive political creed.
192.tq: Distinguish a historiographical criticism from the movement’s general political description.

192.s: Which of the following legal pairings is correctly matched?
192.x: Parsi marriages are governed by the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936. The Sikh Anand Marriage Act dates to 1909 and was amended in 2012 to allow registration.
192.tq: Separate the original enactment year from the later amendment year and the other community’s law.

192.s: The Sikh Anand Marriage Act, 1909 was amended in 2012 to:
o: Abolish the practice of idol worship among Madigas
Introduce Urdu as the medium of higher education
192.x: The Sikh Anand Marriage Act, 1909 was amended in 2012 to allow registration of Sikh marriages. Gurdwara administration was dealt with by the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.
192.tq: Distinguish the purpose of the marriage-law amendment from the separate gurdwara legislation.

192.s: Which movement is identified among the earliest movements to resist British rule in Punjab?
192.x: The Namdharis are identified among the earliest movements that resisted British rule in Punjab. The other options belonged to different regional or religious reform contexts.
192.tq: Use the regional resistance clue to distinguish the Namdhari movement from reform associations elsewhere.

193.s: The Kuka movement was initially begun in the 1840s by whom?
193.x: The Kuka movement was begun in Punjab in the 1840s by Bhagat Jawahar Mal. Baba Ram Singh later organised it as the Namdhari movement.
193.tq: Distinguish the original founder from the later organiser of the movement.

193.s: Baba Ram Singh organised the Kuka movement as the Namdhari movement in 1857 with its centre at:
193.x: Baba Ram Singh organised the movement as the Namdhari movement in 1857, and its centre was at Bhaini in Ludhiana.
193.tq: Use the place-based distinction among related Sikh movements and centres.

193.s: Which one of the following was NOT a characteristic practice of the Kuka or Namdhari followers?
193.x: Kuka followers rejected Brahmin-led rituals. They commonly wore white clothes, abstained from meat and carried a lathi.
193.tq: Find the practice that conflicts with the reform movement's stated principles.

193.s: The Kukas rejected which of the following practices?
o: The use of the Gurmukhi script
Idol worship and worship of tombs, trees and snakes
Khalsa ceremonies associated with Guru Gobind Singh
193.x: The Kukas rejected idol worship, worship of tombs, trees and snakes, and Brahmin-led rituals. They revived the Khalsa ceremonies of Guru Gobind Singh.
193.tq: Test a cluster of distinctive religious practices rather than a general reform objective.

193.s:
Consider the following statements about the methods adopted by the Kuka movement:
1. It boycotted British goods.
2. It boycotted English education.
3. It rejected British law courts and the postal system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
193.x: The Kuka movement advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
193.tq: Combine several connected boycott measures and check whether any item is outside the list.

193.s: Who is regarded as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott as a political weapon against British rule?
193.x: Satguru Ram Singh is regarded as the first to use boycott and non-cooperation against British rule as political weapons.
193.tq: Identify the person associated with a distinctive political method.

193.s: The Kuka movement anticipated which later methods of the Indian national movement?
o: Individual satyagraha and the Cabinet Mission
Home Rule and the Cripps proposals
193.x: The Kuka boycott anticipated the later Swadeshi and non-cooperation methods used in the national movement.
193.tq: Link an early movement's method with the later movements it foreshadowed.

193.s: The suppression of the Kuka movement followed the clash at Malerkotla in:
193.x: The Malerkotla clash took place in 1872 and was followed by severe suppression of the Kukas.
193.tq: Use the date as the decisive discriminator among related movement milestones.

193.s: Which of the following correctly describes the British suppression of the Kukas after the Malerkotla clash?
o: They were executed at Nankana Sahib and Ram Singh retired to Amritsar.
Dozens were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon.
They were sent to the Andaman Islands and Ram Singh remained in Punjab.
They were imprisoned at Lahore and Ram Singh was deported to London.
193.x: After the 1872 Malerkotla clash, dozens of Kukas were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon in Burma.
193.tq: Match the punishment with the correct leader and location.

193.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Reform body)
 a. Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha
 b. Singh Sabha
 c. Deoband
 d. Kuka or Namdhari

List-II (Community)
 i. Muslims
 ii. Parsis
 iii. Sikhs

Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
193.x: Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha reformed the Parsis; Singh Sabha and Kuka/Namdhari were Sikh movements; Deoband was associated with Muslims.
193.tq: Start with the distinctive Parsi pair and eliminate codes with swapped communities.

193.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
193.x: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was a Parsi reform body. Singh Sabha and Nirankari were associated with Sikhs, while Aligarh was associated with Muslims.
193.tq: Discriminate between reform bodies belonging to neighbouring religious communities.

193.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Radhasoami Satsang was founded by Shiv Dayal Singh.
2. Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Narain Agnihotri.
3. Dharma Sabha was founded by Radhakant Deb.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
193.x: Shiv Dayal Singh founded Radhasoami Satsang, Shiv Narain Agnihotri founded Dev Samaj, and Radhakant Deb founded Dharma Sabha.
193.tq: Verify each founder independently before selecting the coded combination.

193.s: Radhasoami Satsang was founded by Shiv Dayal Singh at:
193.x: Shiv Dayal Singh, also known as Soamiji Maharaj, founded Radhasoami Satsang at Agra in 1861.
193.tq: Pair the founder with the correct place and year rather than with another reform body.

193.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dev Samaj — Shiv Narain Agnihotri — Lahore, 1887
Dharma Sabha — Shiv Dayal Singh — Agra, 1861
Bharat Dharma Mahamandal — Naoroji Furdonji — Bombay, 1851
193.x: Dev Samaj was founded by Shiv Narain Agnihotri at Lahore in 1887. The other combinations exchange founders, places or organisations.
193.tq: Use the founder-place-year triple to expose swapped reform bodies.

193.s: The text associated with Dev Samaj was:
193.x: Dev Samaj was associated with the text Deva Shastra. Rast Goftar was a journal of the Parsi reform movement, while hukamnamas were issued by the Nirankaris.
193.tq: Separate a reform text from journals and religious directives of other movements.

193.s: Which of the following was NOT among the principles stressed by Dev Samaj?
193.x: Dev Samaj stressed abstaining from alcohol and meat, along with the eternity of the soul, supremacy of the guru and good deeds.
193.tq: Identify the reversed form of a stated reform principle.

193.s: Radhasoami teaching primarily stressed:
o: Worship of idols through Brahmin-led rituals
193.x: Radhasoami teaching stressed inner realisation through the guru. The other options relate to practices or objectives of different movements.
193.tq: Distinguish the central spiritual teaching from institutional or political objectives.

193.s: Which one of the following statements about the Dharma Sabha is correct?
o: It was founded by Naoroji Furdonji in Bombay in 1851 and promoted girls' education.
It was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1902 and led the Gurdwara Reform Movement.
It was founded by Radhakant Deb at Calcutta in 1830 and opposed abolition of sati.
It was founded by Shiv Narain Agnihotri at Lahore in 1887 and promoted abolition of sati.
193.x: Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha at Calcutta in 1830, and it opposed the abolition of sati.
193.tq: Watch for swapped founders, places and reform objectives in long options.

193.s: The Bharat Dharma Mahamandal was established in 1902 as:
o: A Sikh body for gurdwara administration
193.x: Bharat Dharma Mahamandal was an orthodox all-India Hindu body established in 1902. Madan Mohan Malaviya was a leading figure associated with it.
193.tq: Identify the institutional character of the organisation before considering its associated personality.

193.s: The Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha was founded in Bombay in 1851 by:
o: Kartar Singh Jhabbar, Shiv Narain Agnihotri and Behramji Malabari
Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji and S. S. Bengalee
Baba Dayal Das, Bhagat Jawahar Mal and Ram Singh
Radhakant Deb, Shiv Dayal Singh and Madan Mohan Malaviya
193.x: The Parsi Religious Reform Association was founded in Bombay in 1851 by Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji and S. S. Bengalee.
193.tq: Recall the complete founder group and reject groups assembled from other reform movements.

193.s: Which of the following was a principal focus of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
o: Boycott of postal services and law courts
Gurdwara control and removal of mahants
Girls' education and reform of marriage customs
193.x: The Sabha focused on girls' education and reform of marriage customs while challenging Parsi orthodoxy.
193.tq: Match the organisation with its community-specific reform agenda.

193.s: Which journal was associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
o: Jagat Mithra only as its official title
193.x: Rast Goftar was associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha. Jagat Mithra is also mentioned in connection with the movement, but Rast Goftar is its principal identified journal.
193.tq: Separate the principal journal from texts and publications linked to other organisations.

193.s: Behramji M. Malabari is regarded as the greatest Parsi social reformer of the nineteenth century mainly for his campaign against:
193.x: Behramji M. Malabari campaigned against child marriage, a campaign associated with the Age of Consent Act, 1891.
193.tq: Link a reformer with the specific social evil against which he campaigned.

193.s: The campaign against child marriage associated with Behramji M. Malabari led to the enactment of the:
193.x: Malabari's campaign against child marriage was associated with the Age of Consent Act of 1891.
193.tq: Distinguish the reform law by its exact year from later legislation on a similar subject.

193.s: The Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar and Lahore respectively in:
193.x: The Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar in 1873 and at Lahore in 1879.
193.tq: Preserve the order of the two places while matching them with their respective years.

193.s: Which of the following was NOT an aim of the Singh Sabha movement?
o: Promoting Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature and education
Placing gurdwaras under corrupt Udasi mahants
193.x: The Singh Sabha aimed at Sikh social and educational reform. The movement did not seek to place gurdwaras under corrupt Udasi mahants; the Akali movement sought to free them from such control.
193.tq: Distinguish the aims of Singh Sabha from the grievance addressed by the Akali movement.

193.s: Khalsa College was set up at Amritsar in:
193.x: The Singh Sabha helped establish Khalsa College at Amritsar in 1892.
193.tq: Separate the educational institution's year from the founding years of Singh Sabha branches.

193.s: The Akali movement grew out of the:
193.x: The Akali movement grew out of the Singh Sabha movement and later developed into the Akali Dal as a political party.
193.tq: Trace institutional succession among closely related Sikh movements.

193.s: The principal objective of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement of 1920–25 was to:
o: Establish English education in Punjab courts
Free gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants
Revive worship of trees and snakes
193.x: The Akali movement sought to free Sikh gurdwaras from corrupt Udasi mahants. It was led by figures including Kartar Singh Jhabbar.
193.tq: Identify the institutional grievance that gave rise to the movement.

193.s: Who was a leader of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement?
193.x: Kartar Singh Jhabbar was a leader of the Akali or Gurdwara Reform Movement during 1920–25.
193.tq: Avoid swapping leaders among contemporary religious and social reform bodies.

193.s: The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) was formed in:
193.x: The SGPC was formed in 1920 during the Gurdwara Reform Movement.
193.tq: Distinguish the body's formation year from the later legislation that gave it statutory control.

193.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a flashpoint of the Akali movement?
193.x: The Nankana Sahib massacre of 1921 was one of the flashpoints of the Akali movement. Guru-ka-Bagh was another flashpoint in 1922.
193.tq: Match each event with its exact year before checking the alternatives.

Formation of the Justice Party in the Madras Presidency
