194.x: The symbol of the Justice Party was the Scales.
194.tq: Test a distinctive organisational symbol directly.

194.s: The first general meeting of the South Indian Liberal Federation was held at Coimbatore on:
194.x: The first general meeting was held at Coimbatore on 19 July 1917, with Panagal Raja presiding.
194.tq: Match the meeting with its place, date and presiding leader.

194.s: The principal aim of the Justice Party was to:
o: organise the armed struggle against British rule
secure separate electorates for Muslims בלבד
194.x: The Justice Party was established primarily to protect the interests of non-Brahmins in the Madras Presidency.
194.tq: Identify the stated institutional aim without being distracted by broader movements.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the social base of the Justice Party:
1. Its base included non-Brahmin landed gentry.
2. In Andhra, Reddys, Kammas and Kapus formed part of this social base.
3. Brahmins constituted approximately 90 per cent of the Presidency’s population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Brahmins were approximately 3 per cent of the Presidency’s population, not 90 per cent; the 90 per cent-plus figure referred to their share of government jobs.
194.tq: Catch the reversed population-versus-employment comparison.

194.s: In the Madras Presidency election of 1920, the Justice Party secured:
194.x: In the 1920 election, held after the Congress boycott, the Justice Party won 63 of the 98 seats and formed the first ministry.
194.tq: Match the election year with its exact seat result.

194.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Justice Party’s result in 1926 and the position of other groups?
194.x: In 1926, the Justice Party won 22 seats, while the Swaraj Party won 41 and independents won 36.
194.tq: Compare all three figures in the same election rather than recalling one number in isolation.

194.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First Justice Party ministry
B. Election in which the Justice Party won 44 seats
C. Election in which the Justice Party won 22 seats
D. Congress ministry under Rajaji
194.x: The sequence is 1920 election and first ministry, 1923 election with 44 seats, 1926 election with 22 seats, and 1937 Congress ministry under Rajaji.
194.tq: Use the election years 1920, 1923, 1926 and 1937 as anchors.

194.s: Who was the first Premier of the Madras Presidency under the Justice Party ministry?
194.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar was the first Premier, serving from 17 December 1920 until July 1921 because of ill health.
194.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the longer-serving successor.

194.s: Which Justice Party Premier served from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries?
194.x: Panagal Raja, also known as P. Ramarayaningar, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926 and headed two ministries.
194.tq: Associate the tenure with the correct premier rather than the party founder.

194.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the tenure of a Justice Party Premier?
194.x: B. Munuswamy Naidu served from 1930 to 1932. Bobbili Raja served from 1932 to 1937, Panagal Raja from 1921 to 1926, and Subbarayalu Reddiar from December 1920 to July 1921.
194.tq: Use tenure overlap and sequence to eliminate swapped office-holders.

194.s: Who acted as Premier of Madras from April to August 1936 during the tenure of the Bobbili Raja ministry?
194.x: P.T. Rajan acted as Premier from April to August 1936 during the period of the Bobbili Raja ministry.
194.tq: Test the brief acting tenure hidden within a longer ministry.

194.s: The independent P. Subbarayan ministry of 1926–1930 functioned with the support of the:
194.x: P. Subbarayan headed an independent ministry from 1926 to 1930 with the support of the Justice Party.
194.tq: Identify the supporting party rather than the formal label of the ministry.

194.s:
Panagal Raja was associated with which combination of offices and facts?
1. President of the Justice Party
2. Premier from 1921 to 1926
3. Association with Andhra University in 1926
4. Death on 16 December 1928
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All four statements are correct. Panagal Raja was party president, served as Premier from 1921 to 1926, was associated with Andhra University in 1926 and died on 16 December 1928.
194.tq: Verify a personality through office, institutional association and date.

194.s: Which statement correctly describes K.V. Reddy Naidu in relation to the Justice Party?
o: He was the first Premier in 1920 and resigned due to ill health.
He acted as Premier from April to August 1936.
He founded the South Indian Liberal Federation in 1916.
He was a minister in the first ministry and became Premier in 1937.
194.x: Kurma Venkata Reddy Naidu of Eluru was a minister in the first ministry in 1920 and became Premier in 1937.
194.tq: Match the leader with the two offices held at different times.

194.s: Bobbili Raja, also known as Ramakrishna Ranga Rao, was the:
194.x: Ramakrishna Ranga Rao was the 13th Raja of Bobbili and served as Premier from 1932 to 1937. He was also a delegate to the Second Round Table Conference.
194.tq: Use the hereditary title to identify the correct political personality.

194.s: Who moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, which was later withdrawn at A.P. Patro’s urging?
194.x: M. Suryanarayana moved the separate Andhra resolution in 1922, and it was withdrawn at the urging of A.P. Patro.
194.tq: Separate the mover of a resolution from the person who urged its withdrawal.

194.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: K.V. Reddy Naidu — editor of Justice
194.x: Munukuru Rama Rao was associated with organising the party in Krishna. A.P. Patro was Education Minister, while M. Suryanarayana was associated with Visakhapatnam.
194.tq: Start with the regional and office associations that are least interchangeable.

194.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the language of the newspaper and its editor?
o: Andhra Prakasika — Tamil; P. Thyagaraya Chetty
194.x: Justice was an English newspaper edited by T.M. Nair. Dravidian was in Tamil and Andhra Prakasika was in Telugu.
194.tq: Match both language and editor, not merely the newspaper name.

194.s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of the Justice Party?
o: Its refusal to participate in provincial elections
Its opposition to both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement
Its strong mass base among all sections in Andhra
Its merger with the Congress before 1920
194.x: The party suffered from Andhra–Tamil rivalry, lacked a mass base in Andhra and opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement.
194.tq: Select the historically stated cause while rejecting absolute organisational claims.

194.s: Which development followed the Justice Party’s defeat in 1937?
o: It merged with the Independent Labour Party.
Periyar became dominant and the political stream later ran into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
It formed the first ministry under Rajaji.
C.R. Das became its leader and renamed it the Swaraj Party.
194.x: After the 1937 defeat, Periyar became dominant, and the stream later developed into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
194.tq: Test the later transformation of an organisation after electoral decline.

194.s: Who criticised the neglect of the poor and Harijans within the Justice Party?
194.x: C. Natesa Mudaliar criticised the Justice Party for neglecting the poor and Harijans.
194.tq: Distinguish internal criticism from external political opposition.

194.s: Which of the following pairs relating to deaths of Justice Party leaders is correctly matched?
194.x: P. Thyagaraya Chetty died on 25 April 1925, while Panagal Raja died on 16 December 1928.
194.tq: Discriminate between two close organisational personalities and dates.

194.s: The colonial government used the Justice Party primarily as a counter to:
o: the Swadeshi movement and the Khilafat movement
the Andhra University movement and the Dalit movement
the Round Table Conferences and the Simon Commission
194.x: The government used the Justice Party against the Home Rule movement and Gandhi’s movements.
194.tq: Identify the political movements against which an organisation was deployed.

194.s: Who moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923?
194.x: C.R. Reddy moved the no-confidence motion against Panagal Raja on 26 November 1923.
194.tq: Match the parliamentary action with its mover and date.

194.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 1926, C.V.S. Narasimha Raju declined to form a ministry.
2. Panagal Raja was also unable to form a ministry in that situation.
3. The Swaraj Party was formed within the Congress in 1923.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All three statements are correct. In 1926, C.V.S. Narasimha Raju declined to form a ministry and Panagal Raja could not form one either; the Swaraj Party had been formed within the Congress in 1923.
194.tq: Combine the 1926 ministry episode with the origin and date of the Swaraj Party.

194.s:
The non-Brahmin movement in the Madras Presidency primarily sought to end Brahmin dominance in which of the following spheres?
1. Jobs
2. Education
3. Politics
4. Religion
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The movement aimed to end Brahmin dominance in jobs, education, politics and religion, besides safeguarding the interests of non-Brahmins.
194.tq: Use the complete-list option when every listed sphere belongs to the movement’s stated objective.

194.s:
The principal social base of the non-Brahmin movement in Andhra consisted of which of the following intermediate landed castes?
1. Reddys
2. Kammas
3. Kapus
4. Nairs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
194.x: Reddys, Kammas and Kapus formed the principal intermediate landed-caste base of the movement. Nairs are not included in this Andhra social base.
194.tq: Eliminate the geographically and socially unrelated caste from a region-specific list.

194.s: The Justice Party was established in which year?
194.x: The Justice Party was formed in 1916 to safeguard non-Brahmin interests and challenge Brahmin dominance.
194.tq: Distinguish closely spaced organisational dates by focusing on the formation year.

194.s:
With reference to the Communal G.O. of 1921, consider the following statements:
1. It was secured by the intermediate landed castes associated with the non-Brahmin movement.
2. It is regarded as a root or forerunner of reservation policy in South India.
3. It was intended exclusively for Dalit organisations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The Communal G.O. of 1921 was secured by the intermediate landed castes and became a forerunner of South Indian reservation policy. It was not intended exclusively for Dalit organisations.
194.tq: Find the single over-exclusive statement among otherwise connected historical facts.

194.s: The Andhra Mahasabha session associated with the demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins was held at:
194.x: The Andhra Mahasabha met at Vijayawada in 1917 and sought reserved seats for non-Brahmins.
194.tq: Separate a place-year combination from nearby organisation and session dates.

194.s:
The demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins in the Andhra Mahasabha was echoed by:
1. Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy
2. Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary
3. Gora
4. Periyar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
194.x: Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy and Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary echoed the demand. Gora and Periyar are associated with other strands of rationalist and anti-caste activity.
194.tq: Match individuals to the specific regional demand rather than to the broader reform movement.

194.s: The parallel movement built by Dalits alongside the non-Brahmin movement was known as the:
194.x: Dalits built a parallel movement identified with the prefix ‘Adi’, asserting a distinct social identity.
194.tq: Distinguish the Dalit parallel stream from the broader non-Brahmin and rationalist movements.

194.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was popularly known by which title?
194.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was popularly known as ‘Kavi Raju’.
194.tq: Test the exact honorific associated with a regional literary and reform personality.

194.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary used drama and poetry primarily to:
o: Attack Puranic caste stories from a rationalist perspective
Spread the economic programme of the Justice Party
Defend the exclusive religious authority of Brahmins
Promote Puranic caste stories without criticism
194.x: His rationalist writings and dramas attacked caste stories found in Puranic traditions.
194.tq: Infer the reformer’s ideological method from the stated purpose of his literary work.

194.s: The song ‘Veeragandhamu techinaramu... veerulevvaro telpudi’ was associated with which movement?
194.x: The song was associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement.
194.tq: Link a distinctive cultural expression to the freedom movement with which it was associated.

194.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
194.x: Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Jala Rangaswamy, whereas Boyi Bhimanna wrote works such as Paleru and Gudiselu Kalipotunnai.
194.tq: Use the author-work mismatch to identify the incorrectly matched pair.

194.s: Who among the following is associated with the works Paleru, Gudiselu Kalipotunnai, Pilli Shatakam and Paleru Nundi Padmasri Daka?
194.x: These works are associated with Boyi Bhimanna.
194.tq: Start from a distinctive work-title cluster and identify its author.

194.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Prabhodini — Viswa Brahmana Sangham
2. Panchanana — Viswa Brahmana Sangham
3. Prabhodini — Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham
4. Panchanana — Justice Party
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
194.x: Prabhodini and Panchanana were journals of the Viswa Brahmana Sangham. They were not journals of Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham or the Justice Party.
194.tq: Separate two journals belonging to the same caste association from unrelated organisations.

194.s: Which of the following correctly describes Prabhodini?
o: A 1914 journal edited by K. Ramamurthy at Sompet
A 1917 journal of the Andhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada
A 1907 journal associated with Vaddipati Niranjanasastri of Duggirala
A 1923 journal of Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham at Hyderabad
194.x: Prabhodini was associated with the Viswa Brahmana Sangham in 1907 and with Vaddipati Niranjanasastri of Duggirala.
194.tq: Discriminate between two similar journals by using their year, editor and place.

194.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Prabhodini — 1923 — Hyderabad — Andhra Jana Kendra Sangham
194.x: Panchanana was associated with the Viswa Brahmana Sangham in 1914 at Sompet and with K. Ramamurthy.
194.tq: Use the complete four-part association of journal, year, place and person.

194.s: Goparaju Ramachandra Rao was popularly known as:
194.x: Goparaju Ramachandra Rao was popularly known as Gora.
194.tq: Test the sobriquet of a rationalist leader against nearby reform personalities.

194.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Atheist Centre:
1. It was founded by Gora in 1940.
2. It was founded at Mudunuru.
3. It moved to Vijayawada in 1947.
4. Its associated work included Positive Atheism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: Gora founded the Atheist Centre at Mudunuru in 1940; it moved to Vijayawada in 1947, and Positive Atheism is associated with him.
194.tq: Check all components of an institution’s founder, date, place, later movement and associated idea.

194.s: The Congress-linked temple-entry campaign associated with Gora took place at Siddhantam in which district and in which year?
194.x: The temple-entry campaign took place at Siddhantam in Krishna district in 1933.
194.tq: Combine a specific locality, district and year instead of relying on a broad movement label.

194.s: The two-year nationwide celebration of Jyotiba Phule’s 200th birth anniversary was begun by the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
194.x: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment began the two-year nationwide celebration, marked on 11 April 2026.
194.tq: Identify the responsible ministry in a current-affairs institutional question.

194.s: Jyotiba Phule’s 200th birth anniversary was marked on:
194.x: The 200th birth anniversary celebration of Phule was marked on 11 April 2026.
194.tq: Distinguish a commemorative date from the separate birth-anniversary date of Narayana Guru.

194.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice Party:
1. It formed governments four times from 1920.
2. It had declined by 1937 as the Congress rose.
3. Its reservation policy for non-Brahmins shaped Tamil politics.
4. It was entirely free from criticism regarding its social base and political orientation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: The Justice Party formed governments four times from 1920, declined by 1937, and its reservation policy influenced Tamil politics. It was criticised as pro-British, landlord-led and weak among Andhra masses.
194.tq: Reject the absolute claim that a historically criticised organisation was entirely free from criticism.

194.s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the Justice Party?
o: It was anti-British, peasant-led and dominant among Andhra masses
It opposed all forms of reservation for non-Brahmins
It was pro-British, landlord-led and weak among Andhra masses
It was exclusively led by Dalit organisations
194.x: The Justice Party was criticised for being pro-British and landlord-led, and for having a weak base among the Andhra masses.
194.tq: Select the option containing the historically precise combination of criticisms.

194.s: The Adi Andhra name, adopted in 1917, represented:
o: A religious reform movement led by Narayana Guru
A new name for the Justice Party
The first Brahmin educational association in Andhra
The first Dalit identity assertion in the Telugu country
194.x: The name ‘Adi Andhra’ was the first major Dalit identity assertion in the Telugu country.
194.tq: Distinguish an identity assertion from an organisation, caste association or religious movement.

194.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the two important sessions associated with the Adi-Andhra and non-Brahmin mobilisation in the Krishna region?
194.x: The relevant sessions were held at Vijayawada in 1917 and Machilipatnam in 1919. Krishna district was the hub of this mobilisation.
194.tq: Fix the sequence by identifying the earlier session and then the later session.

194.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the comparative approaches of Gandhi and Ambedkar:
1. Gandhi viewed varna as a division of labour.
2. Gandhi regarded untouchability as a corruption.
3. Ambedkar sought the annihilation of caste and legal rights.
4. Ambedkar’s approach included the demand for separate electorates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
194.x: All four statements accurately describe the contrast: Gandhi defended varna as division of labour while opposing untouchability, whereas Ambedkar sought caste annihilation, legal rights and separate electorates.
194.tq: Compare reform within the varna framework with the demand for annihilation of caste.

194.s: Which one of the following correctly contrasts Periyar’s movement with the Andhra non-Brahmin movement?
o: Periyar’s movement was anti-religious, whereas Andhra’s was largely reformist and education-led
Periyar’s movement was education-led, whereas Andhra’s was exclusively anti-religious
Both movements were exclusively religious reform movements
Both movements rejected education as a means of social change
194.x: Periyar’s movement was strongly anti-religious, while the Andhra movement was mostly reformist and education-led.
194.tq: Identify the reversed comparison by carefully separating the characteristic of each regional movement.

194.s: Periyar’s movement influenced which of the following developments in Andhra?
o: The formation of the Andhra Mahasabha in 1917
The rise of the Adi-Andhra leaders
The establishment of the Viswa Brahmana Sangham in 1907
The founding of the Atheist Centre at Mudunuru in 1940
194.x: Periyar’s movement inspired the Adi-Andhra leaders in Andhra.
194.tq: Connect an ideological movement with its stated regional influence rather than with its date of origin.

194.s: Sree Narayana Guru’s 172nd birth anniversary was observed on:
194.x: Sree Narayana Guru’s 172nd birth anniversary was observed on 28 August 2026.
194.tq: Distinguish a contemporary commemorative date from the historical date of an associated event.

194.s: The Aruvippuram Shiva consecration associated with Sree Narayana Guru took place in:
194.x: Sree Narayana Guru consecrated Shiva at Aruvippuram in 1888.
194.tq: Separate a reformer’s landmark religious act from later organisational and political dates.

194.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Andhra legacy of the Justice Party?
o: It established the Viswa Brahmana Sangham in 1907.
It organised the Aruvippuram consecration in 1888.
Its lasting Andhra legacy was Andhra University, established in 1926.
Its lasting Andhra legacy was the Atheist Centre, established in 1940.
194.x: Andhra University, established in 1926, is identified as the lasting Andhra legacy of the Justice Party.
194.tq: Identify the correct institutional legacy while rejecting achievements belonging to other movements.

195.s: Which of the following was the first Telugu journal, published from Bellary in 1835?
195.x: Satyaduta, published by the Bellary Christian Mission in 1835, is identified as the first Telugu journal and was issued from Bellary.
195.tq: Use the distinctive place-and-year combination to identify the journal.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Telugu journals:
1. Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition.
2. Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani supported women's education.
3. Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Raja Rammohan Roy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition, while Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Raja Rammohan Roy. Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani was orthodox and opposed women's education.
195.tq: Find the statement that reverses the reformist and orthodox positions of two rival journals.

195.s: The journal Satyasamvardhini, associated with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj, was published in which year?
195.x: Satyasamvardhini was a monthly associated with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj and was published in 1891.
195.tq: Distinguish closely spaced journal years by linking the year with the institution.

195.s: Who edited Satyasamvardhini?
195.x: Satyasamvardhini was edited by Rayasam Venkata Siva and included a biography of Raja Rammohan Roy.
195.tq: Separate the editor of a journal from the founders or editors of similarly named journals.

195.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Journal)
(a) Satyaduta
(b) Satyasamvardhini
(c) Janana Patrika
(d) Chintamani

List-II (Association or feature)
(i) First Telugu political journal
(ii) Bellary Christian Mission
(iii) Women's education
(iv) Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
195.x: Satyaduta was issued by the Bellary Christian Mission; Satyasamvardhini was associated with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj; Janana Patrika concerned women's education; and Chintamani was the first Telugu political journal.
195.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that disturb the journal's distinctive association.

195.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the first girls' school in Andhra
B. Establishment of Vivekavardhini
C. Setting up of his own printing press
D. Establishment of Satihitabodhini

Select the correct sequence.
195.x: The first girls' school was established in 1874, Vivekavardhini began in 1874, the printing press was set up in 1876, and Satihitabodhini began in 1883. In the sequence used here, the school and Vivekavardhini precede the press and Satihitabodhini.
195.tq: Place the dated milestones first and then verify the order of the later reform activities.

195.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani — Opposition to women's education
Satyasamvardhini — Opposition to the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj
195.x: Satyasamvardhini was associated with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj; it was not opposed to it. Hasyavardhini was connected with Kokkonda Venkataratnam, Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani was orthodox, and Hasyasanjeevani replied to Hasyavardhini.
195.tq: Check whether the journal's purpose is reversed, especially in the rival-journal pair.

195.s: The first Telugu political journal was:
195.x: Chintamani, associated with Veeresalingam and Nyapati Subbarao, is identified as the first Telugu political journal.
195.tq: Distinguish a journal's historical significance from its founder or editor.

195.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chintamani was jointly associated with Veeresalingam and Nyapati Subbarao.
2. Satyasamvardhini was a monthly of the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj.
3. Janana or Zenana Patrika was connected with women's education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Chintamani was jointly edited by Veeresalingam and Nyapati Subbarao, Satyasamvardhini was linked with the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj, and Janana or Zenana Patrika promoted women's education.
195.tq: When all three statements describe distinct journal associations accurately, select the complete combination.

195.s: Which one of the following journals was started as a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini?
195.x: Veeresalingam's Hasyasanjeevani, started in 1876, was a satirical reply to Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Hasyavardhini.
195.tq: Discriminate between similarly named journals by identifying the direction of the rivalry.

195.s:
Assertion (A): Veeresalingam's journals were used as instruments of social reform.
Reason (R): His reform journalism attacked corruption and superstition and promoted women's education.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
195.x: Both statements are true. Veeresalingam used journals such as Vivekavardhini and Satihitabodhini to oppose corruption and superstition and to support women's education.
195.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the reformer's use of journalism.

195.s: Which of the following statements regarding Kandukuri Veeresalingam is correct?
o: He established the press in 1905 after about twenty Telugu journals had appeared.
He set up his own printing press in 1876.
He set up the press only after the launch of Satyasamvardhini in 1891.
He established his own printing press in 1883.
195.x: Veeresalingam established his own printing press in 1876. By 1905, about twenty Telugu journals were in print, which was much later.
195.tq: Reject options that shift a known event to a nearby but incorrect year.

195.s: By approximately which year were about twenty Telugu journals in print?
195.x: The number of Telugu journals had reached about twenty by 1905.
195.tq: Match the approximate quantity with its stated benchmark year.

195.s: Which of the following works of Veeresalingam is regarded as the first Telugu novel?
195.x: Rajasekhara Charitra is identified as the first Telugu novel. Brahma Vivaham was a satire, while Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu followed the model of Gulliver's Travels.
195.tq: Separate literary genre and distinction from the other works of the same author.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the works of Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
o: Brahma Vivaham — Historical chronicle of the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj
Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu — Based on Gulliver's Travels
195.x: Brahma Vivaham was a satire, not a historical chronicle of the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj. The other three pairs correctly state the significance or inspiration of the works.
195.tq: Identify the option that assigns the wrong genre or description to a known work.

195.s: Which journal was associated with the popularisation of the vyavaharika dialect in Telugu?
195.x: Janavani, associated with Tapi Dharma Rao, was the first magazine to popularise the vyavaharika dialect in Telugu.
195.tq: Link the linguistic objective with the journal specifically associated with it.

195.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The monthly Telugu was associated with Gidugu in 1919.
2. Janavani was associated with Tapi Dharma Rao.
3. The Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine was associated with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu was associated with Gidugu in 1919, Janavani with Tapi Dharma Rao, and the Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.
195.tq: Check each journal-editor association independently before selecting the combined code.

195.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sequence of journals associated with Veeresalingam?
195.x: Vivekavardhini began in 1874, Hasyasanjeevani in 1876, and Satihitabodhini in 1883. Their purposes respectively included social reform, satire, and women's education.
195.tq: Use the three dated journal milestones as a compact chronological chain.

195.s: Which of the following journals was associated with Veeresalingam's reply to Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri's Arya Mata Bodhini?
195.x: Satyavahini, also referred to as Satyavadini, was Veeresalingam's reply to Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri's Arya Mata Bodhini and is associated with 1905.
195.tq: Distinguish journals by the specific rival publication they answered.

195.s: Who among the following was associated with the first widow remarriage in Andhra, involving Sitamma and Gogulapati Sriramulu?
195.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam conducted the first widow remarriage in Andhra involving Sitamma and Gogulapati Sriramulu.
195.tq: Identify the reformer directly associated with the specific social reform first.

195.s: Which one of the following was the first organised social reform body in Andhra?
195.x: The Rajahmundry Social Reform Association was regarded as the first organised reform body in Andhra.
195.tq: Distinguish the earliest organisation from later reform bodies by its specific description.

195.s: The Rajahmundry Social Reform Association was established in which year?
195.x: The Social Reform Society, also known as the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association, was established in 1875 to provide shelter, legal defence and financial assistance to widows.
195.tq: Separate closely related years belonging to different reform organisations.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reform institutions associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam:
1. The Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry was established in 1878.
2. The Widow Remarriage Association was established in 1880.
3. Hitakarini Samajam was established in 1905.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. The Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj dates to 1878, the Widow Remarriage Association to 1880, and Hitakarini Samajam to 1905.
195.tq: Build the answer by checking each institution against its distinct year.

195.s: The Widow Remarriage Association in Andhra was associated with which combination?
o: Veeresalingam, Challapalli Bapayya and Basavaraju Gavarraju
Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and Mrs Manning
Gurajada Apparao, Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu and Basavaraju Gavarraju
195.x: The Widow Remarriage Association was formed in 1880 by Veeresalingam with Challapalli Bapayya and Basavaraju Gavarraju.
195.tq: Start from the sure association between the reform body and its principal collaborators.

195.s:
Which of the following statements about Kandukuri Veeresalingam is correct?
1. He had arranged 20 widow remarriages by 1892.
2. He established widow homes at Madras and Rajahmundry.
3. He was the first person in Andhra to promote co-education.
195.x: All three statements are correct. By 1892 Veeresalingam had arranged 20 widow remarriages, established widow homes at Madras and Rajahmundry, and promoted co-education in Andhra.
195.tq: Treat each biographical reform activity as an independent statement to be verified.

195.s: The widow homes established by Kandukuri Veeresalingam were located at:
195.x: Veeresalingam established a widow home at Madras in 1897 and another at Rajahmundry in 1905. The Rajahmundry home was called Vitantu Saranalayam.
195.tq: Use the paired-place and year sequence to eliminate reversed locations.

195.s: Which institution was managed through the entire property donated by Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
195.x: Veeresalingam donated his entire property, valued at Rs. 50,000, to Hitakarini Samajam, which managed all his institutions.
195.tq: Link the distinctive donation detail with the institution it supported.

195.s: The Ram Mohan Roy School, founded in 1909 for children of backward communities, was established by:
195.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham founded the Ram Mohan Roy School in 1909 to provide education for children from backward communities.
195.tq: Apply the founder–institution association without confusing it with Veeresalingam’s institutions.

195.s: Who among the following was known as the ‘Gadya Tikkana’ and ‘Andhra Vaitalikudu’?
195.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was known by several titles, including Gadya Tikkana and Andhra Vaitalikudu.
195.tq: Discriminate among reformers by matching multiple honorific titles to one person.

195.s: The title ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ was conferred on Kandukuri Veeresalingam by:
195.x: M. G. Ranade called Veeresalingam the ‘Vidyasagar of South India’ in 1898, when Veeresalingam presided over the Indian Social Reform Congress at Madras.
195.tq: Pair the title with the person who bestowed it, not with the reformer’s own title.

195.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
195.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was known as Andhra Ratna. The title Brahma Rishi was associated with Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu.
195.tq: Find the swapped title–person pair among closely related reform personalities.

195.s:
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was known by which of the following titles?
1. Brahma Rishi
2. Abhinava Socrates
3. Kavi Raju
195.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was known as Brahma Rishi and Abhinava Socrates. Kavi Raju was the title of Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
195.tq: Separate similar honorifics by matching each title with its correct reformer.

195.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was knighted in:
195.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was knighted in 1924 and was later known among his students as Brahma Rishi in 1932.
195.tq: Distinguish the year of official honour from the later year associated with a popular title.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu — Father of Andhra Drama
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu — Father of Andhra Drama
195.x: Dharmavaram Krishnamacharyulu was known as the Father of Andhra Drama. Andhra Ratna was the title of Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, while Kavi Raju was associated with Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary.
195.tq: Use title-based elimination, especially where neighbouring personalities have similar reform credentials.

195.s: The play ‘Brahma Vivaham’, described as a satire, was written by:
195.x: Brahma Vivaham was written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam and is identified as a satire.
195.tq: Match a literary work with its author using the author–genre association.

195.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s ‘Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu’ was based on:
195.x: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travels. Rajasekhara Charitramu, by contrast, was based on The Vicar of Wakefield.
195.tq: Discriminate between two works by the same author and their different English sources.

195.s:
Which of the following statements regarding ‘Kanyasulkam’ is correct?
1. It was written by Gurajada Apparao.
2. It deals with bride-price and the plight of widows.
3. It was written in spoken Telugu.
195.x: All three statements are correct. Kanyasulkam was written by Gurajada Apparao, dealt with bride-price and the plight of widows, and used spoken Telugu.
195.tq: Verify author, subject and linguistic style as separate attributes of the same literary work.

195.s: Which one of the following statements about Gurajada Apparao’s ‘Kanyasulkam’ is correct?
o: It was first written in 1905 and revised in 1919.
It was first written in 1892 and revised in 1909.
It was first written in 1878 and revised in 1881.
It was first written in 1909 and revised in 1892.
195.x: Kanyasulkam was first written in 1892 and revised in 1909.
195.tq: Use chronological order to distinguish the original publication year from the revision year.

195.s: ‘Desamante matti kadoyi, desamante manushuloyi’ conveys the idea that:
o: A country is determined by its religious institutions.
A country is its people, not merely its soil.
A country is defined exclusively by its territory.
A country is identified primarily with its rulers.
195.x: The line from Gurajada Apparao’s poem Desamunu Preminchumanna expresses that a nation consists of its people rather than merely its soil.
195.tq: Interpret the central idea of the quoted line rather than relying only on author recall.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: The Vicar of Wakefield — Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu
195.x: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Gulliver’s Travels, not The Vicar of Wakefield. The Vicar of Wakefield was the basis for Veeresalingam’s Rajasekhara Charitramu.
195.tq: Spot the swapped source-work relationship among otherwise familiar literary pairs.

195.s:
Arrange the following institutions associated with Andhra social reform in chronological order of establishment:
A. Hitakarini Samajam
B. Rajahmundry Social Reform Association
C. Widow Remarriage Association
D. Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry
195.x: The correct order is Rajahmundry Social Reform Association (1875), Prarthana Samaj (1878), Widow Remarriage Association (1880), and Hitakarini Samajam (1905).
195.tq: Arrange the organisations by their establishment years, beginning with the earliest reform body.

195.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological sequence in the life and public recognition of Veeresalingam?
A. He was given the title Rao Bahadur.
B. M. G. Ranade called him the Vidyasagar of South India.
C. He died at Madras.
D. Hitakarini Samajam was established.
195.x: The sequence is Hitakarini Samajam (1905), Rao Bahadur title (1893) is actually earlier; therefore the chronological order is A (1893), B (1898), D (1905), C (1919).
195.tq: Check every date carefully rather than accepting the apparent biographical sequence.

195.s: Madras Veda Samajam was renamed as Dakshina Bharata Brahmo Samaj by its secretary, who among the following?
195.x: Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu, the secretary of Madras Veda Samajam, renamed it Dakshina Bharata Brahmo Samaj.
195.tq: Match the office-holder with the institutional change.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Brahmo movement in Andhra:
1. Its period of greatest influence was approximately from 1870 to 1935.
2. Rajahmundry and Kakinada were its principal centres in Andhra.
3. The movement was based on monotheism and opposition to idol worship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. The Brahmo movement in Andhra reached its peak during 1870–1935, with Rajahmundry and Kakinada as its main centres, and upheld monotheism without idol worship.
195.tq: Test the time span, centres and defining principle together.

195.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of establishment of the listed Samajs in Andhra?
o: Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj – Machilipatnam Brahmo Samaj – Kakinada Samaj – Guntur Samaj
Machilipatnam Brahmo Samaj – Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj – Guntur Samaj – Kakinada Samaj
Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj – Kakinada Samaj – Machilipatnam Brahmo Samaj – Guntur Samaj
Kakinada Samaj – Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj – Machilipatnam Brahmo Samaj – Guntur Samaj
195.x: The correct chronological order is Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj (1878), Machilipatnam Brahmo Samaj (1882), Kakinada Samaj (1888) and Guntur Samaj (1898).
195.tq: Arrange institutions by their establishment years.

195.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kakinada Widow Remarriage Association — Paidah Ramakrishnayya
Kakinada Samaj — Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu and Duggirala Surya Prakasarao
195.x: Guntur Samaj was founded by Pillarisetty Sitaramayya in 1898. Desiraju Peda Bapayya was associated with Bapatla and the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
195.tq: Find the swapped founder among closely related Andhra reform institutions.

195.s: The anti-nautch campaign in Andhra was primarily directed against which practice?
o: The use of the grandhika Telugu style
195.x: The anti-nautch campaign opposed the Bhogam or Devadasi custom. Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was its major leader, while Desiraju Peda Bapayya led the boycott of Bhogam melas.
195.tq: Distinguish the target of a reform campaign from unrelated social issues.

195.s:
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Social Purity Association, 1891
2. Principalship of Pithapuram Raja's College, Kakinada
3. First Andhra Vice-Chancellorship of Madras University
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements correctly describe Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu. He led the Social Purity Association, served as principal of Pithapuram Raja's College from 1905 to 1918, and became the first Andhra Vice-Chancellor of Madras University.
195.tq: Combine an organisation, a post and an institutional distinction of one reformer.

195.s: Who among the following was the first practising Brahmo in Andhra and later founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry?
195.x: Desiraju Peda Bapayya of Bapatla was the first practising, or Anushtanika, Brahmo in Andhra. He discarded the sacred thread and founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
195.tq: Identify the reformer through two distinctive institutional and personal clues.

195.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Desiraju Peda Bapayya is correct?
o: He led the boycott of Bhogam melas at Rajahmundry.
He established the first Prarthana Samaj at Rajahmundry.
He founded the Kakinada Samaj in 1888.
He served as principal of Pithapuram Raja's College from 1905 to 1918.
195.x: Desiraju Peda Bapayya led the boycott of Bhogam melas through the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham. The other statements refer to Veeresalingam, Tayi Surya Prakasarao Naidu and Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu respectively.
195.tq: Separate similar reformers by their specific deed rather than by their general reform role.

195.s:
Which of the following statements about the early social reform movement in Andhra is correct?
1. Rajahmundry was regarded as Andhra's first Renaissance centre.
2. Dowlaiswaram had the first girls' school associated with this reform phase.
3. Kakinada was another major centre of the movement.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. Rajahmundry was the first Renaissance centre, Dowlaiswaram had the first girls' school, and Kakinada became another important centre.
195.tq: Check three linked place-based facts without confusing centre and institution.

195.s: The Andhra branch of the Brahmo Samaj was established at Rajahmundry in 1878. In this context, which description is most appropriate?
o: It was founded as a military association for opposing British recruitment.
It was established exclusively for promoting Sanskritised Telugu literature.
It represented the Andhra branch and became part of the wider Brahmo reform network.
It functioned as a political party after the decline of the Justice Party.
195.x: The Rajahmundry institution established in 1878 was regarded as the Andhra branch of the Brahmo movement. Its orientation was religious and social reform, not military, linguistic or party politics.
195.tq: Apply the institutional description to distinguish a reform body from political and literary organisations.

195.s: Which of the following is the correct pair regarding Telugu translations and publications connected with the Brahmo movement?
o: Brahmadharma Sudha — translated by Mannava Buchayya Pantulu
Brahma Dharmam — Telugu translation by Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu
Andhra Brahma Geethanjali — translated by Talla Pragada Prakasarayudu
Brahma Dharmam — authored originally in Telugu by Tarakam
195.x: Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu translated Debendranath Tagore's Brahma Dharmam into Telugu in 1875. Mannava Buchayya Pantulu published it in 1886; Brahmadharma Sudha was associated with Talla Pragada Prakasarayudu and Andhra Brahma Geethanjali with Tarakam.
195.tq: Use author–translator–publisher discrimination in a reform-literature question.

195.s: Who among the following is correctly associated with Andhra Brahmo literature?
o: Mannava Buchayya Pantulu — Andhra Brahma Geethanjali
195.x: Talla Pragada Prakasarayudu was associated with Brahmadharma Sudha. Tarakam was associated with Andhra Brahma Geethanjali, while Mannava Buchayya Pantulu published Brahma Dharmam and Chembeti Sridharulu Naidu translated it.
195.tq: Separate the names of translators, publishers and authors of related works.

195.s:
Arrange the following places in the order in which the Andhra social reform movement spread from its earliest centre to later centres:
A. Guntur
B. Rajahmundry
C. Bapatla
D. Kakinada
195.x: Reform began at Rajahmundry and subsequently developed in Kakinada, Bapatla and Guntur. Therefore, the sequence is B, D, C, A.
195.tq: Identify the first centre and then follow the stated spread to later towns.

195.s: The earliest phase of Andhra social reform was led mainly by which social group?
195.x: The reform movement began in Rajahmundry under the leadership of the English-educated middle class. It was not an exclusive movement of rulers, soldiers or European missionaries.
195.tq: Identify the social base of a movement rather than its geographical location.

195.s: Rajahmundry, the earliest centre of social reform in Andhra, was located in which historical district?
195.x: The reform movement began at Rajahmundry in Godavari district, corresponding broadly to present-day East Godavari. Kakinada was another major centre.
195.tq: Distinguish the pioneering district from other later reform centres.

195.s: Who is identified as the first guru associated with the early social reform movement in Andhra?
195.x: Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham is identified as the first guru of the early Andhra social reform movement.
195.tq: Recall the specific title-holder among several reform-era personalities.

195.s: Which of the following reform associations is correctly matched with its principal association?
o: Rajahmundry Nimna Jati Uddharana Sangham — Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty
Madras Native Association — Madras Mahajana Sabha
195.x: Stree Punarvivaha Sangham was associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam. Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was associated with the Madras Native Association, while the other pairings incorrectly substitute institutions or persons.
195.tq: Match a reform organisation with its associated reformer without swapping neighbouring bodies.

195.s:
Which of the following statements regarding reform bodies in the Madras Presidency is correct?
1. The Madras Native Association was formed in 1852.
2. Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was associated with the Madras Native Association.
3. The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. The Madras Native Association dates to 1852 and was associated with Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty; the Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884.
195.tq: Combine dates and an associated personality in a coded statement question.

195.s: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led a movement against which literary style in Telugu?
195.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led the movement for Vyavaharika Bhasha, opposing the Sanskritised grandhika style. He was allied with Gurajada Apparao.
195.tq: Distinguish the spoken-language movement from unrelated literary and religious styles.

195.s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary's song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with which movement?
195.x: The song 'Veeragandhamu techinaramu' is associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement.
195.tq: Link a literary work with the correct phase of the national movement.

195.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajyalakshmamma, also known as Bapamma, was the wife of Veeresalingam.
2. She married Veeresalingam in 1860.
3. She cared for widows and couples connected with the widow-remarriage movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Rajyalakshmamma, or Bapamma, married Veeresalingam in 1860 and supported widows and couples involved in the remarriage movement.
195.tq: Test a reformer's family association, date and social role together.

195.s: Which social issues were attacked through the literary work of Gurajada Apparao?
o: Land revenue and salt taxation only
195.x: Gurajada Apparao used literature to criticise bride-price and the exploitation of widows. His literary reform was directed at social practices rather than taxation, military or succession issues.
195.tq: Infer the reform objective from the social issues targeted by the writer.

195.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding reform institutions?
1. Hitakarini Samajam — Veeresalingam
2. Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam — Komarraju Lakshmana Rao
3. Kavi Club, Kumudavalli — 1897
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Hitakarini Samajam was founded by Veeresalingam, Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was associated with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, and the Kavi Club at Kumudavalli dates to 1897.
195.tq: Combine founder, institution and year in a three-part matching question.

195.s: Hitakarini Samajam, established in 1906, was intended particularly to support which of the following?
195.x: Veeresalingam established Hitakarini Samajam in 1906 and donated all his property to it for women's homes and schools.
195.tq: Identify an institution's purpose from the reformer's concrete contribution.

195.s: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was established at Hyderabad in 1901 with the association of which group?
o: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao
Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu, Desiraju Peda Bapayya and Tayi Surya Prakasarao
Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, Paidah Ramakrishnayya and Atmuri Lakshmi Narasimham
Veeresalingam, Gurajada Apparao and Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
195.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Hyderabad was established in 1901 with Komarraju Lakshmana Rao, Ravichettu Ranga Rao and Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao.
195.tq: Identify the correct founding group from closely related reform-era names.

195.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the place and year mentioned in the context of Andhra reform activity?
o: Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam — Hyderabad, 1898
195.x: The Kavi Club was located at Kumudavalli in West Godavari and dates to 1897. The other options wrongly interchange the towns or years of the reform institutions.
195.tq: Check both components of a place–year pair instead of accepting a familiar institution name.

195.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Gurajada Appa Rao?

1. Kanyasulkam — Attack on bride-price and child marriage
2. Mutyala Saralu — New metre
3. Desamunu Preminchumanna — Patriotic song

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Kanyasulkam attacked bride-price and child marriage, Mutyala Saralu introduced a new metre, and Desamunu Preminchumanna is a patriotic song associated with Gurajada Appa Rao.
195.tq: Combine closely related literary facts and test whether all the pairings are correctly identified.

195.s: Kanyasulkam is especially significant in the history of Telugu literature because it
o: attacked bride-price and child marriage through spoken Telugu
described the travels of Telugu merchants in Europe
introduced Sanskrit drama into Telugu for the first time
defended orthodox marriage customs through satire
195.x: Kanyasulkam, written in 1892, attacked the social evils of bride-price and child marriage and used spoken Telugu.
195.tq: Identify the precise social theme and literary form associated with a major work.

195.s: Gurajada Appa Rao worked with which reformer in promoting literary and cultural renaissance in Andhra?
195.x: Gurajada Appa Rao worked alongside Kandukuri Veeresalingam's reform activities, contributing to literary and cultural renaissance.
195.tq: Use the associated-person trap by distinguishing collaborators from other reformers.

195.s: Who among the following, along with Gurajada Appa Rao, championed the use of vyavaharika or spoken Telugu?
195.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy and Gurajada Appa Rao were prominent champions of vyavaharika, or spoken, Telugu.
195.tq: Separate leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement from leaders of library and widow-remarriage movements.

195.s:
With reference to women reformers of Andhra, consider the following statements:

1. Bhandaru Acchamamba founded Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram in Machilipatnam in 1902.
2. Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai.
3. Rajyalakshmamma sheltered widows and conducted widow and inter-caste marriages at her home.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Acchamamba founded Stree Samajam in 1902, Hindu Sundari was associated with Ramabai and Shantabai, and Rajyalakshmamma provided shelter and organised marriages.
195.tq: Test several women reformers through a coded combination of organisations and activities.

195.s: The organisation founded by Bhandaru Acchamamba in 1902 was
195.x: Bhandaru Acchamamba founded Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram in Machilipatnam in 1902.
195.tq: Match the reformer directly with the organisation founded by her.

195.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Bhandaru Acchamamba — Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala
2. Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai — Hindu Sundari
3. Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja — Devadasi Bill movement

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Acchamamba wrote Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala, Ramabai and Shantabai were associated with Hindu Sundari, and Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja worked for the Devadasi Bill.
195.tq: Use a three-way association question to test women reformers, writings and legislation.

195.s: Hindu Sundari, associated with the reform activities of Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai, was published from
195.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with Mosalikanti Ramabai and Vempati Shantabai and was published from Kakinada in 1902.
195.tq: Test a journal-place association using nearby Andhra reform centres as distractors.

195.s: The Devadasi Bill associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja was passed in
195.x: The Devadasi Bill campaign was associated with Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy and Chodagam Ammannaraja; the Bill was passed in 1947.
195.tq: Distinguish the year of the reform initiative from the year in which the legislation was passed.

195.s: Who among the following founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914?
195.x: Iyyanki Venkata Ramanaiah founded the Andhra Desa Library Association in 1914.
195.tq: Distinguish the founder of the library movement from leaders of the spoken-Telugu movement.

195.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August in recognition of the contribution of
195.x: 29 August is observed as Telugu Language Day in recognition of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, a major champion of vyavaharika Telugu.
195.tq: Link a commemorative date with the correct movement leader rather than a general reformer.

195.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

A. Establishment of the Andhra Desa Library Association
B. Foundation of Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram
C. Publication of Hindu Sundari
D. First widow remarriage in Andhra

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: The first widow remarriage occurred in 1881, Stree Samajam and Hindu Sundari date to 1902, and the Andhra Desa Library Association was founded in 1914. Thus, D, B, C, A is the correct sequence.
195.tq: Use the first and last events, then arrange the two events from 1902 carefully.

195.s: Which one of the following works of Kandukuri Veeresalingam is correctly matched with its genre or distinction?
o: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu — Translation of a Sanskrit drama
Abhijnana Sakuntalam — Satire on opponents of reform
195.x: Rajasekhara Charitra, published in 1878, is regarded as the first Telugu novel. Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Gulliver's Travels, Brahma Vivaham was a satire, and Abhijnana Sakuntalam was a translation.
195.tq: Find the correctly matched work while rejecting swapped genres and literary forms.

195.s: Which of the following is regarded as the first Telugu autobiography?
195.x: Veeresalingam's Autobiography is regarded as the first Telugu autobiography.
195.tq: Distinguish a literary first from the author's other novels, biographies and travel narratives.

195.s:
Which of the following works were translations through which Veeresalingam became the first to render classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu?

1. Abhijnana Sakuntalam
2. Malavikagnimitram
3. Ratnavali

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: Abhijnana Sakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram and Ratnavali were among the translations through which Veeresalingam rendered classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu for the first time.
195.tq: Test completeness of a named literary list through coded options.

195.s:
Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

A. Satyavati Charitra — Prose narrative
B. Brahma Vivaham — Satire on opponents of reform
C. Rajasekhara Charitra — Travel account based on Gulliver's Travels
D. Victoria Maharani Charitra — Biography
195.x: Rajasekhara Charitra was the first Telugu novel and was modelled on The Vicar of Wakefield. Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu, not Rajasekhara Charitra, was based on Gulliver's Travels.

195.s: Rajasekhara Charitra carried which reform themes and helped establish the template for Telugu social fiction?
195.x: Rajasekhara Charitra carried the reform themes of widow remarriage and education and helped establish the pattern of Telugu social fiction.
195.tq: Infer the social-fiction significance of a work from its reform themes.

195.s: The first girls' school associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam was founded in
195.x: The first girls' school associated with Veeresalingam was founded in 1874 at Rajahmundry. A second school was established at Innispeta, Rajahmundry, in 1881.
195.tq: Distinguish the year of the first school from the year of the later Innispeta school.

195.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Veeresalingam's educational activities is correct?

1. He founded the first girls' school associated with his reform work in 1874.
2. A second girls' school was established at Innispeta, Rajahmundry, in 1881.
3. He was the first in Andhra to promote co-education.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. Veeresalingam's first girls' school dates to 1874, the Innispeta school to 1881, and he was the first in Andhra to promote co-education.
195.tq: Combine dates and a distinction to test the complete educational reform profile.

195.s: On 3 August 1879, Kandukuri Veeresalingam delivered a public lecture at Rajahmundry declaring that widow remarriage was
o: a matter solely for colonial courts
195.x: On 3 August 1879, Veeresalingam publicly argued at Rajahmundry that widow remarriage was sanctioned by Hindu scripture. He was attacked and was protected by his students.

195.s:
Consider the following statements about the first widow remarriage in Andhra:

1. It took place on 11 December 1881.
2. It was held at Ananda Udyana Mandapam behind Veeresalingam's house at Rajahmundry.
3. The groom was Gogulapati Sriramulu and the bride was Seethamma, originally known as Gauramma.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements correctly describe the first widow remarriage in Andhra on 11 December 1881.
195.tq: Test date, venue and participants together, requiring complete identification of the event.

195.s: The second widow remarriage conducted in Andhra in December 1881 involved
195.x: The second widow remarriage took place on 15 December 1881 between Racharla Ramachandrayya and Ratnamma.
195.tq: Distinguish the participants of the first and second remarriages.

195.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

A. Paidah Ramakrishnayya — Kakinada Widow Remarriage Association
B. Vedam Venkataraya Sastri — Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam
C. Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri — Aryananda Brundavani Sabha
D. All of the above
195.x: All three pairs are correct. Paidah Ramakrishnayya supported remarriages at Kakinada, Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote the anti-remarriage work, and Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri was associated with Aryananda Brundavani Sabha.
195.tq: Start from the sure associations and verify all three reform-related pairings.

195.s: The first major anti-widow-remarriage book mentioned in connection with Andhra was
195.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam in 1883, described as the first major anti-remarriage book.
195.tq: Identify the exact title of a polemical work instead of a reformist literary work.

195.s: Which of the following was NOT among the social evils against which reform activities in Andhra were directed?
195.x: Expansion of scientific education was a reform objective, not a social evil. The listed evils included child marriage, nautch or Bhogam and official corruption, among others.
195.tq: Find the item that is a reform measure rather than a social evil.

195.s: Which one of the following was NOT a method used in the social reform campaigns associated with Veeresalingam?
o: Conducting public lectures and establishing schools
Performing remarriages at his own cost and maintaining widow homes
195.x: Veeresalingam's reform methods included journals, satire, public lectures, schools, co-education, remarriages at his own expense and widow homes. Prarthana Samaj worship was conducted without idols.
195.tq: Reject the reversed religious practice while retaining the practical reform methods.

195.s: Which of the following social evils was directly associated with the term 'Bhogam' in reform discussions in Andhra?
195.x: Nautch, or the Bhogam system, was one of the social evils targeted by reformers in Andhra.
195.tq: Discriminate between a named social practice and other evils in the same reform list.

195.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Prarthana Samaj from Arya Samaj?

1. Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang.
2. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar were associated with Prarthana Samaj.
3. Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 and promoted the Shuddhi programme.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: All three statements are correct. Prarthana Samaj originated in Bombay in 1867 under Atmaram Pandurang and was associated with Ranade and Bhandarkar, while Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 and promoted Shuddhi.
195.tq: Compare two similarly named reform movements by founder, date, associates and programme.

195.s: The Arya Samaj worked mainly from which place after its foundation in Bombay in 1875?
195.x: Arya Samaj was founded by Dayananda Saraswati in Bombay in 1875 but worked mainly from Lahore. Its Shuddhi programme was a prominent feature of its activities.
195.tq: Use the movement's operational centre as a location-based discriminator.

195.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:

A. Foundation of Arya Samaj
B. Foundation of Prarthana Samaj
C. Earliest Prarthana Samaj centre in Andhra
D. First widow remarriage in Andhra

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867, Arya Samaj in 1875, the earliest Andhra Prarthana Samaj centre was established in 1878, and the first Andhra widow remarriage took place in 1881.
195.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then distinguish 1867, 1875 and 1878.

195.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was inspired to join the Brahmo Samaj by whom?
195.x: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu joined the Brahmo Samaj under the inspiration of Pandit Sivanath Sastri.
195.tq: Test the reformer–influence association directly.

195.s: Which of the following regions was NOT specifically associated with the extension of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu's reform activities from the Godavari districts?
195.x: His reform activities spread to the North Coastal Andhra districts of Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam, not Anantapur.
195.tq: Find the one location outside the stated reform area.

195.s:
Consider the following statements about Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu:
1. He founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in 1891.
2. He was associated with the anti-nautch movement in Madras.
3. He founded the Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Temperance and Social Purity Sangham at Rajahmundry was associated with Desiraju Peda Bapayya.
195.tq: Separate the reformer's own organisations from those founded by another reformer.

195.s: Which one of the following journals was associated with the anti-Devadasi campaign of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu?
195.x: People's Friend was associated with Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu's anti-Devadasi campaign.
195.tq: Match the reform journal with its distinctive social campaign.

195.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu held the office of Vice-Chancellor of Madras University during which period?
195.x: The stated tenure of Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu as Vice-Chancellor of Madras University was 1925–1928.

195.tq: Test the title–year association.

195.x: He was the first non-official educator to receive a knighthood, in 1924.

The first girls' school in Andhra

Founding the Theosophical Society at New York

o: Written in 1890, first staged in 1892, published in 1897
Written in 1892, first staged in 1897, published in 1909
Written in 1897, first staged in 1890, published in 1892
Written in 1909, first staged in 1892, published in 1897

A social play in vyavaharika Telugu

A poetry work that introduced a new lyrical metre of the same name

A short story regarded as the first modern Telugu short story

Which of the following statements regarding Kanyasulkam is correct?
1. It uses the Srikakulam dialect.

195.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Granthika Telugu from Vyavaharika Telugu?
o: Granthika is spoken Telugu, whereas Vyavaharika is Sanskritised Telugu
Granthika was promoted by Gidugu, whereas Vyavaharika was defended by orthodox pandits
Granthika is a classical and Sanskritised form, whereas Vyavaharika is based on spoken Telugu
Both are identical forms of Telugu used only in administration

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the objectives of the Vyavaharika language movement:
1. Granthika supporters claimed that it was the only pure literary medium.
2. Vyavaharika supporters sought to reduce the gap between written and spoken Telugu.
3. Orthodox pandits generally led the movement for spoken Telugu.

195.s: The meeting associated with the founding of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha was held at which place in 1910?
195.x: Gidugu founded the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha after a meeting held at Visakhapatnam in 1910.

195.x: J. A. Yates inspired the movement for the use of Vyavaharika Telugu.

195.s: Which of the following was the principal role of the Navya Sahitya Parishat in the language movement?
o: Preparing Sanskrit grammars for orthodox pandits
Spreading the cause of Vyavaharika Telugu among the youth
Opposing the use of spoken Telugu in education
Introducing Telugu as a classical language in 2008
195.x: Navya Sahitya Parishat functioned as a youth organisation that spread Gidugu’s cause of spoken Telugu.

1. Literature
2. Education
3. Administration

195.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the earliest Telugu autobiography mentioned in connection with early modern Telugu prose?
o: It was written by C. P. Brown
It was written by Gurajada Apparao
It was written by Enugula Veeraswamayya

195.x: Gidugu Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 at Ponduru in the Srikakulam region.

Arrange the following events relating to Gidugu Ramamurthy in chronological order:
A. Birth of Gidugu Ramamurthy
B. Foundation of the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha
C. Conferment of the title Kaisar-e-Hind
D. Death of Gidugu Ramamurthy
195.x: Gidugu was born in 1863, founded the organisation in 1910, received Kaisar-e-Hind in 1934, and died in 1940.

The Vicar of Wakefield — Gidugu Ramamurthy

2. Abhinava Vaganushasanudu
3. Kaisar-e-Hind

195.s: Who was the patron associated with Gurajada Apparao’s court at Vizianagaram?
195.x: Gurajada was associated with the court of Ananda Gajapati at Vizianagaram, and his play was staged by the Vizianagaram troupe.
195.tq: Apply the ruler-or-patron trap to distinguish literary court associations.

195.s: The metre associated with Gurajada Apparao is
195.x: Gurajada is associated with the metre *Mutyala Saralu*.
195.tq: Match the literary personality with the distinctive metre.

195.s: The line “Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi” conveys which idea?
o: A nation depends primarily on its ancient monuments
A nation is identified with its people
A nation is created only by its rulers
A nation is defined exclusively by its territory
195.x: The line expresses the idea that a nation is its people rather than merely its soil or territory.
195.tq: Infer the central idea from a well-known literary line.

195.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the ‘twin pioneers’ of the modern Telugu language and literary movement?
o: Kandukuri Veeresalingam and C. P. Brown
Tapi Dharma Rao and Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu
195.x: Gurajada Apparao, associated with 1861–1915, and Gidugu Ramamurthy, associated with 1863–1940, are described as twin pioneers.
195.tq: Use paired identification along with the associated period.

195.s:
Which of the following groups consisted of supporters of spoken-Telugu prose?
1. Gidugu Ramamurthy
2. Gurajada Apparao
3. Tapi Dharma Rao
4. Navya Sahitya Parishat
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
195.x: Gidugu, Gurajada, Tapi Dharma Rao and the Navya Sahitya Parishat all supported the movement for spoken-Telugu prose.
195.tq: Recognise the complete supporters’ group rather than selecting only individual reformers.

195.s: Who among the following represented the orthodox opposition to the reform of Telugu prose?
o: Gidugu Ramamurthy, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Gurajada Apparao, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Tapi Dharma Rao, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
Kokkonda Venkataratnam, editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini*
195.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam was an orthodox editor of *Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevini* and opposed the reform towards spoken Telugu.
195.tq: Use the editor–journal association to identify the opponent of reform.

195.s: The classical side in the Telugu language controversy was led through which organisation by Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu?
195.x: Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu led the classical side through the Andhra Sahitya Parishad.
195.tq: Match the leader with the organisation representing his position.

195.s: Telugu Bhasha Dinotsavam is observed on 29 August because it is the birthday of
195.x: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Ramamurthy.
195.tq: Link the commemorative date with the concerned reformer’s birth anniversary.

195.s: In which year did Telugu receive classical language status from the Government of India?
195.x: Telugu was granted classical language status by the Government of India in 2008.
195.tq: Test the exact year using closely spaced numerical distractors.

195.s: Which statement is correct regarding Gidugu Ramamurthy’s wider recognition?
o: He was described by Sri Sri as the patron of the Vizianagaram court.
He was described by Sri Sri as the author of *The Vicar of Wakefield*.
He was described by Sri Sri as the founder of the Andhra Sahitya Parishad.
He was described by Sri Sri as ‘our recent inspiration’.
195.x: Sri Sri referred to Gidugu Ramamurthy as ‘our recent inspiration’.
195.tq: Identify the exact attribution associated with a prominent literary figure.

195.s: Which one of the following places became the centre of Telugu social reform, modern prose, journalism and the novel during the nineteenth century?
195.x: Rajahmundry emerged as the centre of Telugu social reform and the development of modern prose, journalism and the novel.
195.tq: Use the significance-based location clue and distinguish the reform centre from other Andhra places.

195.s: Who described Kandukuri Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitra as a mere translation?
195.x: Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri criticised Rajasekhara Charitra by calling it a mere translation.
195.tq: Apply the author-versus-critic discrimination trap in literary history.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding two major reformers of Andhra:
1. Kandukuri Veeresalingam was associated with the Prarthana Samaj and widow remarriage.
2. Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu was associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
3. Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu advocated anti-nautch and social purity reforms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All three statements are correct. Veeresalingam is linked with the Prarthana Samaj and widow remarriage, while Venkataratnam Naidu was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, anti-nautch and social purity reforms.
195.tq: Check each reformer's institutional association and distinctive reform programme separately.

195.s: Which of the following best explains the principal method adopted by Kandukuri Veeresalingam for advancing social reform?
o: Organising armed resistance against colonial rule
Using the press rather than direct political activity
Rejecting all forms of public education
Working exclusively through princely state administrations
195.x: Veeresalingam primarily used the press as an instrument of social reform rather than pursuing reform through direct political activity.
195.tq: Identify the means of reform from the contrast between press activism and political action.

195.s: Who is associated with being the first Telugu autobiographer?
195.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is credited with being the first Telugu autobiographer.
195.tq: Match the superlative achievement with the correct reformer without confusing him with contemporary literary figures.

195.s: Which of the following statements about the later phase of social reform in the Rajahmundry–Kakinada region is correct?
o: Vizianagaram replaced Rajahmundry as the sole centre of Telugu journalism.
The Pithapuram Raja opposed all institutional reform activity.
The Pithapuram Raja funded later reform work.
Madanapalle became the only centre of widow-remarriage work.
195.x: The Pithapuram Raja supported and funded later reform work in the Rajahmundry–Kakinada belt.
195.tq: Test the patronage relationship by distinguishing a documented supporter from absolute or exclusive claims.

195.s: The social reform movement in Andhra acquired greater continuity because it became institutionalised through:
195.x: The reform movement became institutional through samajs, homes and journals, enabling it to outlive its individual founders.
195.tq: Translate the cause-and-effect relationship into an institutional continuity scenario.

195.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Raja Rammohan Roy in chronological order:
A. Sati abolition
B. Establishment of the Atmiya Sabha
C. Establishment of the Brahmo Sabha
D. Establishment of the Brahmo Samaj
195.x: The sequence is Atmiya Sabha in 1814, Brahmo Sabha in 1828, Brahmo Samaj in 1828 as the developed institutional form, and abolition of sati in 1829.
195.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the related Brahmo institutions between them.

195.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Prarthana Samaj from the Brahmo Samaj?
o: The Prarthana Samaj rejected idol worship and caste more completely than the Brahmo Samaj.
The Brahmo Samaj was chiefly concerned with anti-nautch reform, while the Prarthana Samaj dealt only with education.
The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the Brahmo Samaj.
Both organisations adopted identical positions on idol worship and caste.
195.x: The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, whereas the Brahmo Samaj took a more categorical position against them.
195.tq: Separate the two similarly named reform organisations by testing their doctrinal difference.

195.s: The Andhra connection of the Theosophical movement is particularly associated with:
195.x: Madanapalle is noted for the Andhra link of the Theosophical movement, including Besant's college and its association with Krishnamurti.
195.tq: Use the specific place-association method for organisations and cultural movements.

195.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent Telugu cultural initiatives in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Telugu Mahotsavam is to be held every year.
2. Telugu Language Day and Telugu Language Awards are observed on 29 August.
3. Nandi Natakotsavams have been revived.
4. These initiatives were announced at Undavalli Caves by Minister Kandula Durgesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
195.x: All four statements are correct. The initiatives include annual Telugu Mahotsavam, Telugu Language Day and Awards on 29 August, revival of Nandi Natakotsavams, and the announcement at Undavalli Caves by Minister Kandula Durgesh.
195.tq: Verify each component of a current-affairs cluster instead of selecting an option from one familiar detail.

195.s: The Kandukuri Awards are associated with:
o: Literary awards of the Government of West Bengal
Military decorations of the Union Government
Cultural awards of the Government of Andhra Pradesh
Awards for Theosophical studies at Madanapalle
195.x: The Kandukuri Awards are included among the cultural awards of the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
195.tq: Identify the issuing authority and field rather than relying only on the eponymous name.

195.s: Which one of the following best describes the importance of the vyavaharika prose movement in Telugu?
o: It enabled school books, newspapers and nationalist songs to reach the masses.
