Which of the following persons were identified with the later phase of Moderate activity in Andhra?
1. Konda Venkatappayya
2. B. N. Sharma
3. Nyapathi Subbarao
4. P. Anandacharlu
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
200.x: Konda Venkatappayya and B. N. Sharma were identified as later Andhra Moderate leaders. Nyapathi Subbarao and P. Anandacharlu were separately noted among the earlier Andhra Moderate figures.
200.tq: Separate the specifically described later figures from the other leaders in the same regional grouping.

200.s: Mahatma Gandhi’s return to India is associated with the advice of which Moderate leader?
200.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale advised Gandhi in connection with his return to India. This reflects the continuing influence of Moderate leadership on later national politics.
200.tq: Use the person-and-influence association instead of confusing regional Andhra leaders with the national mentor.

201.s: Who was the first Telugu person to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress?
201.x: P. Anandacharlu was the first Telugu person to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress.
201.tq: Directly identify the person associated with the distinction.

201.s: The 7th session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by P. Anandacharlu, was held at:
201.x: The 7th session of the INC was held at Nagpur in 1891 under the presidency of P. Anandacharlu.
201.tq: Link the session number with its venue rather than its president alone.

201.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. P. Anandacharlu served as Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha.
2. He served as Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884.
3. Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Jaipur session of the INC in 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
201.x: All three statements are correct. Anandacharlu was Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884, while Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the Jaipur session in 1948.
201.tq: Check each statement against the office, year and session details.

201.s: The Coconada Literary Association was mainly associated with public affairs in:
201.x: The Coconada Literary Association was associated with public affairs in the Godavari region.
201.tq: Identify the geographical sphere of a local political association.

201.s: Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty, who founded the Madras Native Association, also started which publication in 1844?
201.x: Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty started The Crescent in 1844.
201.tq: Connect an associated publication with its founder.

201.s: The tour of S. N. Banerjee in 1878 was undertaken for which organisation and helped stir political sentiment?
201.x: S. N. Banerjee toured in 1878 on behalf of the Indian Association, stimulating political sentiment.
201.tq: Match the political leader with the organisation represented during the tour.

201.s: The Krishna District Association was formed broadly on the lines suggested at the:
o: First session of the Indian National Congress
Seventh session of the Indian National Congress
201.x: The Krishna District Association was formed on the lines suggested at the first session of the INC.
201.tq: Link an institutional development with the earlier national event that inspired it.

201.s: Who presided over the conference of the Krishna District Association that attracted approximately 223 delegates?
201.x: Nyapathi Subbarao presided over the Krishna District Association conference, which attracted approximately 223 delegates.
201.tq: Use the presiding officer as the decisive clue in a local association question.

201.s:
Arrange the following district associations in chronological order of their formation:
A. Vizag District Association
B. Nellore District Association
C. Krishna District Association
D. Kurnool District Association
201.x: The order is Krishna (1892), Vizag (1893), Nellore (1908) and Kurnool (1914).
201.tq: Fix the earliest and latest associations first, then place the intermediate years.

201.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the year of formation?
201.x: The Vizag District Association was formed in 1893. Anantapur, Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor–Kadapa were associated with 1907, 1908, 1914 and 1916 respectively.
201.tq: Start with the pair whose year is closest to the first district association.

201.s: The district associations of Chittoor and Kadapa were formed in:
201.x: The Chittoor and Kadapa district associations were formed in 1916.
201.tq: Distinguish the paired districts and their later formation year from the preceding entries.

201.s: Which of the following statements regarding the early district associations of Andhra is NOT correct?
o: The Anantapur District Association was formed in 1907.
The Kurnool District Association was formed in 1914.
The Nellore District Association was formed in 1908.
The Vizag District Association was formed in 1907.
201.x: The Vizag District Association was formed in 1893, not 1907. The other three statements are correct.
201.tq: Find the single altered year in an otherwise familiar chronological list.

201.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Andhra delegate)
a. P. Anandacharlu
a. P. Rangaiah Naidu
c. Nyapathi Subbarao
d. Gutti Kesava Pillai
List-II (Place associated)
i. Chittoor
ii. Rajahmundry
iii. Anantapur
iv. Not specified as a district in the given list

Select the correct answer using the code below:
201.x: P. Anandacharlu was associated with Chittoor, Nyapathi Subbarao with Rajahmundry, and Gutti Kesava Pillai with Anantapur. P. Rangaiah Naidu is the remaining entry without a district specified in the list.
201.tq: Start with the sure regional pairings and eliminate the remaining code.

201.s: Who presided over the 1887 Madras session of the Indian National Congress?
201.x: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the 1887 Madras session of the INC.
201.tq: Use the session year and venue to distinguish the early INC presidents.

201.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to participate as a delegate in the Indian National Congress?
201.x: Ponaka Kanakamma was the first Telugu woman in the Indian National Congress.
201.tq: Identify the person associated with a specific first in regional political participation.

201.s: Andhra Prakasika is correctly associated with which person?
201.x: The pairing of Andhra Prakasika with P. Anandacharyulu is accepted as correct.
201.tq: Discriminate between closely associated newspaper editors and founders.

201.s: Krishna Patrika was published from Machilipatnam in 1902 under the association of:
201.x: Krishna Patrika was associated with Konda Venkatappayya and was published from Machilipatnam in 1902.
201.tq: Combine the newspaper, place and year with its associated person.

201.s: Nyapathi Subbarao was associated as editor with which of the following publications?
201.x: Nyapathi Subbarao was associated as editor with the monthly publications Vyjayanti and People's Magazine.
201.tq: Match the editor with the pair of publications linked to him.

201.s: By 1905, approximately how many Telugu journals were in circulation among the nationalist publications of Andhra?
201.x: By 1905, there were approximately 20 Telugu journals, including Deshabhimani, Sasilekha, Rasikollasini and Gowtami.
201.tq: Identify the approximate count rather than confusing it with a precise enumeration.

201.s: The nationalist journals of Andhra during 1885–1905 primarily:
o: Supported administrative failures and opposed democratic ideas
Criticised administrative failures and spread nationalism and democracy
201.x: These journals criticised administrative failures and helped spread nationalism and democratic ideas.
201.tq: Apply the stated function of the press to its political role.

201.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the early demands of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
o: Simultaneous ICS examination in England and India
201.x: The early demands included simultaneous ICS examinations, elected legislative councils and reduction of military expenditure. Complete independence was not among the listed demands of 1885.
201.tq: Find the later nationalist objective inserted into an early moderate demand list.

201.s: The early Congress opposed the annexation of:
201.x: One of the early Congress demands was opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma.
201.tq: Identify the specific territory in the moderate nationalist demand list.

201.s: Who presented a data-led critique of the economic drain from Madras against Andhra at the 7th Andhra Mahasabha in Guntur in 1919?
201.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao presented the data-led drain critique at the 7th Andhra Mahasabha in Guntur in 1919.
201.tq: Link the economic argument with its speaker, venue and occasion.

201.s: The division between Moderates and Extremists in the nationalist movement became prominent in:
201.x: The Moderate–Extremist divide became prominent in 1905.
201.tq: Separate the year of ideological division from the years of institutional formation.

201.s: The opposition of the Andhras to the transfer of Ganjam to Orissa was regarded as their:
201.x: The Andhra opposition to the transfer of Ganjam to Orissa was regarded as the first victory of the Andhra political movement.
201.tq: Identify the significance attached to a specific regional political action.

201.s: Who served as the municipal president of Kakinada during the early phase of Andhra political activity?
201.x: Paidah Ramakrishnayya served as the municipal president of Kakinada.
201.tq: Match the municipal centre with its local political leader.

201.s: Which of the following correctly represents the significance of the nationalist movement in Andhra before 1905?
o: It rejected both constitutional politics and public associations.
Moderates, district associations and the press helped build Andhra's political base before the Vande Mataram phase.
It began only after the formation of the first district association in 1916.
It was confined entirely to municipal politics and had no press support.
201.x: Moderate leaders, district associations and nationalist newspapers collectively built Andhra's political base before the Vande Mataram phase of 1905.
201.tq: Combine institutional, political and press developments to infer their broader significance.

201.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Krishna Patrika — first Telugu journal, Bellary Mission
Krishna district — first district association in Andhra, 1892
Andhra Prakasika — municipal president of Kakinada
Vande Mataram phase — before the growth of district associations
201.x: Krishna district had the first district association in Andhra in 1892. Krishna Patrika was published from Machilipatnam, while Satyadoota was associated with the Bellary Christian Mission.
201.tq: Compare the firsts and distinguish organisations, publications and political phases.

201.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. First session of the Indian National Congress
B. Formation of the Madras Mahajana Sabha
C. Formation of the Krishna District Association
D. Publication of Krishna Patrika
201.x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded in 1884, the first INC session was held in 1885, the Krishna District Association was formed in 1892, and Krishna Patrika appeared in 1902.
201.tq: Place the dated institutional and press developments from earliest to latest.

202.s: The partition of Bengal in 1905 created which of the following administrative units and population distributions?
o: Eastern Bengal with 18 million people, and Western Bengal and Assam with 36 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 54 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 31 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 36 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 18 million people
Eastern Bengal and Assam with 31 million people, and the rest of Bengal with 54 million people
202.x: The partition created Eastern Bengal and Assam with 31 million people and the remaining Bengal with 54 million people.
202.tq: Use the distinctive population figures to eliminate the reversed and recombined distributions.

202.s:
With reference to the partition of Bengal, consider the following statements:
1. Administrative convenience was given as its official justification.
2. One of its political effects was to make Bengalis a minority in their own province.
3. Its underlying objective was to strengthen Bengali nationalism by uniting Hindus and Muslims.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Administrative convenience was the stated reason, while the actual policy sought to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims. The third statement is therefore false.
202.tq: Separate the stated administrative justification from the political motive behind the measure.

202.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal during 1903–1905?
o: It was led by Lord Curzon and relied mainly on official proclamations and military action.
It was led by Hardinge II and relied mainly on revolutionary violence and secret societies.
It was led by King George V and relied mainly on the boycott of constitutional institutions.
It was led by S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray and relied mainly on petitions and meetings.
202.x: The Moderates’ campaign from 1903 to 1905 was associated with S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray, and used petitions and meetings. The campaign failed to prevent the partition.
202.tq: Match the leaders with the characteristic constitutional methods rather than the later militant methods.

202.s: On 16 October 1905, the day on which the partition of Bengal came into effect, which of the following combinations was associated with the popular protest?
o: Industrial strike, salt march, individual satyagraha and underground revolt
Day of mourning, hartal, bathing in the Ganga and Rakhi-bandhan
National education, constitutional reform, separate electorates and provincial autonomy
Day of celebration, military parade, temple entry and public feasting
202.x: The day was observed as a day of mourning and hartal; people took a bath in the Ganga and observed Rakhi-bandhan as a symbol of unity.
202.tq: Identify the cluster of contemporaneous protest rituals linked to the effective date.

202.s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at which event, and what important administrative change accompanied it?
o: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of King George V in 1911; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
The Simla Conference of 1911; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of Edward VII in 1903; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Bombay.
202.x: The partition was annulled on 12 December 1911 at the Delhi Durbar of King George V. The capital was simultaneously transferred from Calcutta to Delhi.
202.tq: Link the annulment event with its accompanying capital-transfer decision.

202.s: Who described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism” in the context of the partition of Bengal?
202.x: Lord Curzon described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism,” reflecting the political significance he attached to the province.
202.tq: Discriminate between the Viceroy, the Home Secretary and the monarch associated with the episode.

202.s: Which one of the following correctly explains why the partition of Bengal was regarded as a measure against Bengali nationalism?
o: It transferred all Bengali districts to a single enlarged province under one administration.
It divided the Bengali-speaking population and made Bengalis a minority in the remaining province.
It abolished the distinction between Eastern Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
It granted complete provincial autonomy to Bengal and ended official interference.
202.x: The partition separated Bengali-speaking areas and altered the demographic balance so that Bengalis became a minority in their own province, thereby weakening the nationalist centre in Bengal.
202.tq: Apply the demographic and political consequences to identify the measure’s real nationalist impact.

202.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: King George V — Viceroy who announced the partition of Bengal
Lord Hardinge II — Viceroy at the time of annulment
H.H. Risley — “Bengal united is a power”

202.x: Bipin Chandra Pal undertook an Andhra tour in 1907 and was subsequently arrested.
202.tq: Identify the correct leader–activity pair while rejecting swapped biographies.

202.s: Which of the following statements about Aurobindo Ghosh is correct?
o: He was imprisoned for six years at Mandalay and later went to the USA.
He presided over the Calcutta session of 1906.
He founded Kesari and Mahratta in 1881.
He was acquitted in the Alipore case and later retired to Pondicherry.
202.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted in the Alipore case and later retired to Pondicherry.
202.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-deed trap to revolutionary biographies.

202.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Extremist concept of Swaraj:
1. It meant complete freedom.
2. It meant colonial self-government within the British Empire.
3. Boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance were among its associated methods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: Extremist Swaraj meant complete freedom, not colonial self-government. Boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance were its associated methods.
202.tq: Reject the reversed comparison between complete freedom and colonial self-government.

202.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dacca primarily to:
202.x: The Muslim League was founded at Dacca in 1906 to safeguard Muslim political interests.
202.tq: Link an organisation with its stated political objective.

202.s: Who among the following were associated with the founding of the All-India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906?
o: Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca
202.x: The Muslim League was founded at Dacca under the leadership of Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca.
202.tq: Use the founder–organisation association rather than the later reform association.

202.s: The Simla Deputation to Lord Minto, which preceded the formation of the Muslim League, took place in:
202.x: The Simla Deputation to Minto took place in October 1906, before the Muslim League was founded later in 1906.
202.tq: Separate closely related events by their month and year.

202.s: With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It abolished legislative councils and introduced national education.
It enlarged legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
It created the Muslim League at Dacca.
It reunited Bengal and ended the Surat Split.
202.x: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 enlarged the legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
202.tq: Identify the reform measure by its distinctive constitutional provisions.

202.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the offices held by Morley and Minto in connection with the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: Morley was the President of Congress and Minto was the Governor of Bengal.
Morley was the Viceroy and Minto was the Secretary of State.
Morley was the Secretary of State and Minto was the Viceroy.
Both Morley and Minto were Viceroys of India.
202.x: John Morley was the Secretary of State for India, while Lord Minto was the Viceroy.
202.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated authorities by office.

202.s: Which of the following sets of resolutions was associated with the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906?
o: Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, provincial autonomy, adult franchise and federation
Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India and Khilafat
Council entry, constitutional reform, Home Rule and communal award
202.x: The Calcutta session of 1906 passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education as a compromise between Moderates and Extremists.
202.tq: Recognise the distinctive four-resolution combination.

202.s: The immediate cause of the Surat Split of 1907 was chiefly the dispute between Moderates and Extremists over:
o: the annulment of the partition of Bengal
the formation of the Muslim League
the four resolutions adopted at Calcutta
202.x: The Surat conflict centred on the four resolutions adopted at the Calcutta session, especially the Extremists’ approach to them.
202.tq: Identify the specific issue behind an organisational split rather than its later consequences.

202.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Surat Split of 1907?
o: Moderates — Gokhale and Mehta; Extremists — Tilak
Moderates — Aga Khan; Extremists — Nawab Salimullah
202.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta represented the Moderates, while Bal Gangadhar Tilak represented the Extremists in the Surat conflict.
202.tq: Start with the sure leader–group pair and eliminate swapped affiliations.

202.s: The Surat session of the Indian National Congress in 1907 was presided over by:
202.x: Rash Behari Ghosh was the president of the Surat session of 1907.
202.tq: Distinguish the president of Surat from the president of Calcutta.

202.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Calcutta Congress session
B. Surat Split
C. Formation of the All-India Muslim League
D. Indian Councils Act introducing separate electorates
Choose the correct answer.
202.x: The Calcutta session occurred in 1906, followed by the Muslim League’s formation later in 1906, the Surat Split in 1907 and the Indian Councils Act in 1909.
202.tq: Fix the endpoint first and then separate the closely spaced 1906 events.

202.s: Which one of the following was an important consequence of the Surat Split?
o: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 was withdrawn.
Moderates dominated the Congress until the Lucknow reunion of 1916.
The Muslim League was dissolved immediately after the split.
The Swadeshi movement expanded continuously without repression until 1916.
202.x: After the Surat Split, the Moderates dominated the Congress until the reunion at Lucknow in 1916.
202.tq: Distinguish an immediate organisational consequence from unrelated constitutional developments.

202.s:
Which of the following developments formed part of the aftermath of the Surat Split?
1. Repression by the colonial government
2. Newspapers Act of 1908
3. Imprisonment of Tilak
4. Immediate reunion of Moderates and Extremists in 1908
Select the correct answer.
202.x: Repression, the Newspapers Act of 1908 and Tilak’s imprisonment followed the split. The reunion occurred at Lucknow in 1916, not in 1908.
202.tq: Find the false chronology hidden among otherwise related consequences.

202.s: Sumit Sarkar is associated with which of the following works?
202.x: Sumit Sarkar authored The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal, dealing with the 1905 partition and its movement.
202.tq: Match the historian with his work, avoiding author–title swaps.

202.s: According to the historical interpretation associated with Sumit Sarkar’s work, which of the following helped intensify anger against the partition of Bengal?
o: The formation of the Muslim League in 1909
202.x: Japan’s victory over Russia in 1904–05 inspired Asian and Indian nationalist sentiment and contributed to anger against the partition.
202.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in a cause-and-effect statement.

202.s: Which of the following forms of literature and publicity were noted as important in the Swadeshi movement’s mobilisation?
202.x: Plays, novels and pamphlets were used to spread nationalist ideas during the Swadeshi movement.
202.tq: Select the precise cultural instruments associated with mass mobilisation.

202.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Rabindranath Tagore and the national movement is correct?
o: Amar Sonar Bangla is the national anthem of India, while Jana Gana Mana is the national anthem of Bangladesh.
Jana Gana Mana is the national anthem of India, while Amar Sonar Bangla is the national anthem of Bangladesh.
Both songs are the national anthems of India.
Both songs are the national anthems of Bangladesh.
202.x: Jana Gana Mana is India’s national anthem, whereas Amar Sonar Bangla is Bangladesh’s national anthem.
202.tq: Discriminate between two closely associated songs and their national attribution.

202.s: Japan’s victory over Russia inspired nationalist sentiment in Andhra. Which of the following pairs is correctly associated with this influence?
o: Munagala Raja — named his sons Togo and Nogi
Adipudi Somanatha Rao — named his sons Togo and Nogi
Adipudi Somanatha Rao — presided over the Surat session
202.x: Munagala Raja named his sons Togo and Nogi, reflecting the influence of Japan’s victory over Russia. Adipudi Somanatha Rao wrote Japan Charitra.
202.tq: Separate two Andhra personalities linked to the same international inspiration.

202.s: Who wrote the Andhra-related work Japan Charitra?
202.x: Adipudi Somanatha Rao wrote Japan Charitra in the context of the inspiration created by Japan’s victory over Russia.
202.tq: Match the author with the work rather than with a related contemporary.

202.s:
Which of the following statements best describes the historical significance of the Swadeshi movement of 1905?
1. It was regarded as the first mass movement.
2. It marked the birth of mass nationalism.
3. It introduced boycott and Swadeshi as important methods of struggle.
4. It introduced national education as a method of nationalist mobilisation.
Select the correct answer.
202.x: The movement was regarded as the first mass movement, fostered mass nationalism and popularised boycott, Swadeshi and national education as methods of struggle.
202.tq: Use the complete significance cluster rather than selecting only one feature.

202.s: Which one of the following was a major limitation of the Swadeshi movement?
o: It continued unaffected by repression after 1908.
It rejected all forms of national education.
It had no support among intellectuals or urban groups.
It received limited participation from peasants and Muslims.
202.x: Peasant and Muslim participation in the movement was limited. The movement also faded by 1908 under repression and after the Surat Split.
202.tq: Find the accurately stated limitation while rejecting extreme generalisations.

202.s: The Swadeshi movement had largely faded by 1908 mainly because of:
o: Japan’s defeat by Russia and the annulment of Bengal partition
the Lucknow reunion and the Indian Councils Act
colonial repression and the Surat Split
the formation of the Muslim League and the Simla Deputation
202.x: The movement weakened by 1908 because of colonial repression and the organisational division caused by the Surat Split.
202.tq: Identify the paired causes of decline instead of a later event.

202.s: Which of the following newspapers or journals is correctly matched with its Andhra association?
202.x: Krishna Patrika was associated with Andhra journalism from 1902. Swarajya was associated with Gadicherla and Desamata with Chilakamarti.
202.tq: Start with the year-linked newspaper and reject swapped Andhra associations.

202.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra-linked nationalist papers:
1. Krishna Patrika is associated with 1902.
2. Swarajya is associated with Gadicherla.
3. Desamata is associated with Chilakamarti.
4. Andhra Kesari is listed among the Andhra papers connected with nationalist activity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
202.x: All four statements are correct: Krishna Patrika dates from 1902, Swarajya is linked with Gadicherla, Desamata with Chilakamarti, and Andhra Kesari is also listed among the relevant Andhra papers.
202.tq: Check each newspaper–person or newspaper–year association separately.

202.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s birth anniversary is associated with which combination?
202.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 at Ratnagiri.
202.tq: Combine the date and birthplace and reject location swaps.

202.s: Which sequence correctly relates Tilak’s cultural initiatives to their years?
202.x: Tilak’s promotion of Ganesh Utsav is associated with 1893, while Shivaji Jayanti is associated with 1895.
202.tq: Fix the earlier and later dates before comparing the two initiatives.

203.s: In 1906, which two organisations were established in Madras to promote Swadeshi activities?
o: A Swadeshi Store and a National School
A Bala Bharathi Samiti and a Swarajya Samiti
An Industrial Association and a Swadeshi League
A National College and a Young Men's Association
203.x: Madras had an Industrial Association to promote Swadeshi goods and a Swadeshi League in 1906.
203.tq: Identify the paired institutions associated with the same year and place.

203.s: Who toured Andhra to popularise Swadeshi activities in the early phase of the movement?
o: Mutnuri Krishna Rao and T. Prakasam
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and J. Ramachandra Rao
Nyapathi Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao
Karanam Guneswara Rao and Kattiventi Perraju
203.x: Nyapathi Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao toured Andhra to popularise Swadeshi activities.
203.tq: Test the persons associated with propagation, not those associated with later institutions or trials.

203.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala:
1. It was located at Machilipatnam.
2. It was founded in 1910.
3. Its foundation stone was laid by Bipin Chandra Pal in 1907.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
203.x: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala, also called Bandaru National College, was located at Machilipatnam, founded in 1910, and had its foundation stone laid by Bipin Chandra Pal in 1907.
203.tq: Separate the foundation year from the earlier foundation-stone ceremony.

203.s: Who was the president of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala?
203.x: Nyapathi Subbarao was the president of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala.
203.tq: Distinguish the president from the first principal and other education activists.

203.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the first principal of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala is correct?
o: Nyapathi Subbarao introduced weaving as a subject.
Karanam Guneswara Rao founded it at Rajahmundry.
Kattiventi Perraju served as its first principal.
Kompalle Hanumantha Rao introduced weaving as a subject.
203.x: Kompalle Hanumantha Rao, also referred to as Kompelli Hanumantha Rao, was the first principal and made weaving a subject.
203.tq: Use the person–office–achievement relationship to reject swapped roles.

203.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Institution)
a. Godavari Swadeshi Store
b. National School
c. Andhra Jateeya Kalasala

i. Ramachandrapuram
ii. Rajahmundry
iii. Machilipatnam

List-II (Place)
203.x: The Godavari Swadeshi Store was at Rajahmundry, the National School at Ramachandrapuram, and the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam.
203.tq: Start with the sure institution–place pair and eliminate codes containing a repeated or displaced location.

203.s: Which of the following statements about the National School at Ramachandrapuram is correct?
o: It was affiliated to the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala at Machilipatnam.
Kattiventi Perraju donated Rs. 1,000 and Guneswara Rao gave land worth Rs. 40,000.
It was inaugurated by Bipin Chandra Pal as the first national college.
Guneswara Rao donated Rs. 1,000 and Kattiventi Perraju gave land worth Rs. 40,000.
203.x: Guneswara Rao contributed Rs. 1,000, while Kattiventi Perraju provided land valued at Rs. 40,000. Nyapathi Subbarao inaugurated it as a true National School.
203.tq: Match each contributor with the correct amount and distinguish a school from a college.

203.s: Which institution at Rajahmundry was inaugurated by Bipin Chandra Pal?
203.x: Bipin Chandra Pal inaugurated the Godavari Swadeshi Store at Rajahmundry in 1907.
203.tq: Distinguish an inaugurated Swadeshi store from the national education institutions.

203.s: The National School at Rajahmundry was affiliated to which body?
203.x: The Rajahmundry school was affiliated to the Bengal national education body.
203.tq: Identify the institutional affiliation rather than the place where the school was situated.

203.s: Which event was inspired by Japan's victory over Russia in 1905?
o: The growth of interest in industrial training in Japan and works such as Japaniyam and Japan Charitra
The formation of the Young Men's Swarajya Samiti alone
The establishment of the Godavari Swadeshi Store at Rajahmundry
203.x: Japan's victory over Russia inspired many young Andhras to seek industrial training in Japan and influenced Munagala Raja, the play Japaniyam and Adipudi Somanatha Rao's Japan Charitra.
203.tq: Connect a historical cause with the several cultural and educational responses it produced.

203.s: Which subjects formed the themes of Bipin Chandra Pal's two speeches at Kakinada?
203.x: At Kakinada, Pal delivered speeches on Vedanta and on Swadeshi-Swaraj.
203.tq: Discriminate between the actual speech themes and the broader programme associated with Pal.

203.s: Who welcomed Bipin Chandra Pal at Rajahmundry, where he delivered five lectures?
203.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao welcomed Pal at Rajahmundry, where Pal stayed at Madella Sourayya's house and delivered five lectures.
203.tq: Keep the welcoming person distinct from the organiser and the host at another town.

203.s: On which date and at which place did Bipin Chandra Pal deliver a speech specifically on national education during his Andhra tour?
203.x: Pal delivered a speech on national education at Rajahmundry on 23 April 1907.
203.tq: Combine the precise date with the town instead of relying only on the sequence of the tour.

203.s: Which pair of persons hosted Bipin Chandra Pal at Vijayawada?
o: Munagala Raja and Nayani Venkata Rangarao
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Madella Sourayya
Kattiventi Perraju and Karanam Guneswara Rao
Kompalle Hanumantha Rao and Brahmo Ramadasu Naidu
203.x: Munagala Raja and Nayani Venkata Rangarao hosted Pal at Vijayawada on 24 April 1907.
203.tq: Pair the town with its hosts while avoiding the host arrangements of Rajahmundry and Machilipatnam.

203.s: What was the title of Bipin Chandra Pal's final speech at Machilipatnam?
203.x: Pal delivered his final speech, titled Matru Murthi, at Machilipatnam on 27 April 1907.
203.tq: Distinguish the title of a speech from titles of seditious writings and books.

203.s: Which of the following best represents Bipin Chandra Pal's political message during his Andhra tour?
o: National schools were unnecessary if Swadeshi stores were established.
Swaraj was the goal, boycott was the weapon, and organisation had to reach the village level.
Swaraj could be achieved only through government employment and legislative petitions.
The movement should remain confined to major urban centres.
203.x: Pal presented Swaraj as the goal, boycott as the weapon, and stressed village-level organisation and national schools.
203.tq: Apply the stated programme to identify the option containing the complete and accurate set of principles.

203.s: Who started the Telugu weekly Swarajya in 1908?
203.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao started the Telugu weekly Swarajya in 1908.
203.tq: Match the publication with its founder rather than with a political organiser or student leader.

203.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for which period in the case arising from Viparita Buddhi?
203.x: His article Viparita Buddhi led to a sedition charge and a sentence of three years' rigorous imprisonment.
203.tq: Test the exact sentence length using closely spaced numerical alternatives.

203.s: Which of the following statements about the Rajahmundry college incident is correct?
o: The incident occurred at the National College in Machilipatnam in 1910.
The ban was imposed by T. Prakasam at Vijayawada.
Principal Mark Hunter banned Vandemataram badges and the slogan in April 1907.
Principal Mark Hunter encouraged students to wear Vandemataram badges during examinations.
203.x: Mark Hunter, principal of the Rajahmundry Arts and Teachers Training College, banned Vandemataram badges and the slogan in April 1907.
203.tq: Use the authority–institution–action combination to catch swapped persons and places.

203.s: What was the immediate action taken by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao in defiance of the Rajahmundry college authorities?
o: He founded the Godavari Swadeshi Store.
He organised a bomb attack on a railway train.
He delivered the final speech Matru Murthi.
He presented an address to Bipin Chandra Pal.
203.x: Gadicherla defied Principal Mark Hunter by presenting an address to Bipin Chandra Pal. J. Ramachandra Rao co-organised the action.
203.tq: Identify the specific act of defiance rather than a later or unrelated movement activity.

203.s: Which consequence followed the Rajahmundry college Vandemataram incident?
o: The college was affiliated to the Bengal national education body.
All students were transferred to Machilipatnam.
138 students were debarred from examinations for two years.
203.x: A total of 138 students were debarred from examinations for two years after the incident.
203.tq: Distinguish the collective punishment imposed on students from the separate punishment imposed on Gadicherla.

203.s: The Rajahmundry college incident of 1907 is historically significant because it marked:
o: The beginning of the Home Rule Movement in Andhra
The foundation of the Andhra Jateeya Kalasala in 1910
The first use of bombs in the Andhra movement
The active entry of Andhra students into India's freedom struggle
203.x: The incident marked the active entry of Andhra students into the freedom struggle.
203.tq: Identify the broader historical significance of a specific local incident.

203.s: Which statement regarding the Kotappakonda riots is correct?
o: They occurred in February 1909 in Guntur, and 14 persons died.
They occurred in July 1907 in Kakinada, and 138 students were punished.
They occurred in April 1909 in Tenali, and the accused were released by T. Prakasam.
They occurred in April 1907 in Rajahmundry, and Pal presided over the meeting.
203.x: The Kotappakonda riots occurred in February 1909 in Guntur, and 14 persons died.
203.tq: Check the event against both its date and place, since the other options borrow details from neighbouring incidents.

203.s: Who was sentenced to death in connection with the Kotappakonda riots?
203.x: Chinnapa, also known as Chennappa Reddy, was sentenced to death and was described as the only person in India sentenced to death in the Vandemataram movement.
203.tq: Distinguish the person sentenced from the accused and witness in the Tenali case.

203.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tenali bomb case:
1. It took place in April 1909.
2. The bomb was aimed at the Howrah passenger.
3. Y. Jagganna was a witness in the case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
203.x: The Tenali bomb case occurred in April 1909, involved a bomb aimed at the Howrah passenger, and had Y. Jagganna as a witness.
203.tq: Combine date, target and witness details to identify the complete set of correct statements.

203.s: Which set of persons was accused in the Tenali bomb case?
o: Chinnapa Reddy, Y. Jagganna and T. Prakasam
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, J. Ramachandra Rao and Mark Hunter
Munagala Raja, Nayani Venkata Rangarao and Kattiventi Perraju
Chukkapalli Ramaiah, Lakkaraju Basavaiah and K. Venkatarayudu
203.x: The accused were Chukkapalli Ramaiah, Lakkaraju Basavaiah and K. Venkatarayudu.
203.tq: Separate the accused group from the witness and the lawyer associated with the case.

203.s: Who secured the release of the accused in the Tenali bomb case?
203.x: T. Prakasam successfully secured the release of the accused in the Tenali bomb case.
203.tq: Match the legal outcome with the person who acted in that role.

203.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Association)
a. Bala Bharathi Samiti
b. Young Men's Association
c. Young Men's Swarajya Samiti

List-II (Town)
i. Machilipatnam
ii. Rajahmundry
iii. Rajahmundry
203.x: The Bala Bharathi Samiti and Young Men's Association were associated with Rajahmundry, while the Young Men's Swarajya Samiti was formed at Machilipatnam.
203.tq: Use the distinctive Machilipatnam pair first, then distinguish the two Rajahmundry associations.

203.s: Who were among the founders of the Bala Bharathi Samiti at Rajahmundry?
o: Munagala Raja, Nayani Venkata Rangarao and Kattiventi Perraju
Nyapathi Subbarao, K. Venkataramana Rao and Kompalle Hanumantha Rao
Tanguturi Prakasam, Panchumarti Ramachandra Rao and T. Prakasam
Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, Gante Lakshmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu
203.x: The founders were Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, Gante Lakshmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu.
203.tq: Distinguish founders from later members and from people connected with Pal's tour.

203.s: Which pair consisted of members of the Bala Bharathi Samiti?
o: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao and Gante Lakshmanna
Tanguturi Prakasam and Panchumarti Ramachandra Rao
Munagala Raja and Nayani Venkata Rangarao
203.x: Tanguturi Prakasam and Panchumarti Ramachandra Rao were members of the Bala Bharathi Samiti; the other named founders were Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao, Gante Lakshmanna and Unguturi Sriramulu.
203.tq: Separate the founders of an association from its listed members.

203.s: The Young Men's Swarajya Samiti was formed during which event?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal's visit to Machilipatnam
203.x: The Young Men's Swarajya Samiti was formed at Machilipatnam during Bipin Chandra Pal's visit in 1907.
203.tq: Link the association with the event during which it was formed, not merely with its town.

203.s: The second Andhra Students Conference was held in:
203.x: The second Andhra Students Conference was held at Machilipatnam in 1909.
203.tq: Test the exact year–place combination using adjacent movement dates as distractors.

203.s: What name was given in Andhra Pradesh to the movement associated with the Swadeshi upsurge and the use of the Vande Mataram slogan?
203.x: In Andhra, the Swadeshi-related agitation was popularly known as the Vandemataram Movement.
203.tq: Use the exact regional name instead of a broader national movement label.

203.s: Surendranath Banerjee's arrest in 1906 led to protests in which of the following places in Andhra?
203.x: The arrest of Surendranath Banerjee in 1906 triggered protests at Rajahmundry, Kakinada, Vizianagaram and Gooty.
203.tq: Test the complete place-list by distinguishing it from nearby Andhra centres.

203.s: Which slogan was raised during the protests that followed Surendranath Banerjee's arrest in Andhra?
203.x: The protesters raised the slogan “Vandemataram - Manade Rajyam,” meaning that self-rule belonged to them.
203.tq: Discriminate the Andhra-specific slogan from other famous nationalist slogans.

203.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the use of “Vande Mataram” in Andhra:
1. It became a form of greeting among the people.
2. Official restrictions on its use contributed to the Rajahmundry and Kakinada incidents.
3. It was used only as the title of a newspaper and not as a public greeting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
203.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because “Vande Mataram” became a popular greeting as well as a political expression.
203.tq: Find the false exclusive statement and retain the two connected facts about greeting and official curbs.

203.s: Who translated Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches and composed on the spot the poem beginning “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu”?
203.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham translated Pal's speeches and composed the poem beginning “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi yaavu.”
203.tq: Match the literary contribution with the correct nationalist leader.

203.s: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is regarded as the first Telugu national poet. Which work is identified as the first Telugu national song?
203.x: “Hinduvulara ennaall ee gati” is identified as the first Telugu national song, while Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham is regarded as the first Telugu national poet.
203.tq: Distinguish a nationalist song from the titles of newspapers associated with the movement.

203.s: Who was the editor of Krishna Patrika during the Swadeshi period in Andhra?
203.x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao was the editor of Krishna Patrika at Machilipatnam.
203.tq: Use the editor–newspaper association to separate similarly placed nationalist leaders.

203.s: Krishna Patrika was founded at Machilipatnam on 1 February 1902 by which pair?
o: Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao
Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and C.Y. Chintamani
Mutnuri Krishna Rao and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao and Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
203.x: Krishna Patrika was founded on 1 February 1902 by Konda Venkatappaiah and Dasu Narayana Rao at Machilipatnam.
203.tq: Combine the date with the founder pair rather than relying on the later editor’s name.

203.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham during the Swadeshi movement in Andhra?
o: He edited Desamata at Rajahmundry and translated Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches.
He edited Krishna Patrika at Machilipatnam and founded it in 1902.
He edited Swarajya and led the Rajahmundry student protest.
He served as the regional leader of the movement in Vizag and Vizianagaram.
203.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham was the editor of Desamata at Rajahmundry and translated Bipin Chandra Pal's speeches.
203.tq: Check the exact leader–newspaper–activity combination and reject swapped roles.

203.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was associated with which of the following combination of roles?
o: Editor of Swarajya, leader at Bandar, and leader of the Rajahmundry student protest
Editor of Krishna Patrika, leader at Vizianagaram, and translator of Pal's speeches
Editor of Desamata, leader at Guntur, and founder of Krishna Patrika
Editor of Andhra Kesari, leader at Vijayawada, and founder of Desamata
203.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya, was a leader at Bandar, and led the Rajahmundry student protest.
203.tq: Keep the three linked roles together and avoid swapping newspapers or regional centres.

203.s: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao was associated with which publication and place?
203.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao was associated with Andhra Kesari at Rajahmundry.
203.tq: Discriminate between similar newspaper and leader associations.

203.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Region)
 a. Vizag/Vizianagaram
 b. Vijayawada
 c. Guntur

List-II (Leader)
 i. Konda Venkatappaiah
 ii. C.Y. Chintamani
 iii. Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
203.x: C.Y. Chintamani led in Vizag/Vizianagaram, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao in Vijayawada, and Konda Venkatappaiah in Guntur.
203.tq: Start from the sure regional pair and eliminate codes that swap neighbouring Andhra centres.

203.s:
Which of the following statements best expresses the significance of the Vandemataram movement in Andhra?
1. It marked the first mass political awakening in Andhra.
2. National education, Swadeshi stores and student politics began in this context.
3. It remained confined to elite political meetings and had no educational or student dimension.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
203.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the movement was connected with national education, Swadeshi stores and student politics.
203.tq: Reject the limiting statement that contradicts the movement’s wider social and educational impact.

203.s: The Vandemataram movement in Andhra fed directly into which later developments?
o: The Quit India movement and the Cabinet Mission negotiations
The Justice Party era and the separate electorates movement
The Andhra Mahasabha era and the Home Rule branches led by the same leaders
The Khilafat movement and the Non-Cooperation committees led by new leaders
203.x: The movement fed into the Andhra Mahasabha era and the Home Rule branches led by the same men, including Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Konda Venkatappaiah.
203.tq: Trace the institutional continuity from an earlier movement to its later regional political forms.

203.s: Who received the only death sentence recorded in India in connection with the movement, according to the Andhra account?
203.x: Chinnapa Reddy is identified with the only death sentence in India associated with this movement; he was connected with Kotappakonda.
203.tq: Test the exceptional case by separating the person from the better-known movement leaders.

204.s: Who among the following was popularly known as the ‘Lokmanya’?
204.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was popularly known as ‘Lokmanya’, meaning ‘beloved of the people’.
204.tq: Use direct identification of a leader’s popular title.

204.s: Valentine Chirol used the expression ‘Father of Indian Unrest’ in his book titled:
o: The Arctic Home in the Vedas
204.x: Chirol used the phrase in his book Indian Unrest, published in 1910.
204.tq: Distinguish a famous title from the associated book title and year.

204.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai — Punjab Kesari
2. Bipin Chandra Pal — Father of Revolutionary Thoughts
3. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao — Andhra Tilak
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
204.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Lajpat Rai was called Punjab Kesari, Pal was called the Father of Revolutionary Thoughts, and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was known as Andhra Tilak.
204.tq: Match each leader with the exact title rather than a similar-sounding designation.

204.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremists?
204.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremist wing.
204.tq: Separate ideological leadership from organisational or moderate leadership.

204.s: Which one of the following leaders was NOT associated with the Moderate group of the Indian National Congress?
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal belonged to the Extremist group. R.C. Dutt, Pherozeshah Mehta and Gokhale were Moderates.
204.tq: Find the one leader belonging to the opposite ideological group.

204.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
204.x: The Maharashtra extremist group was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak; Bengal was associated with Pal and Aurobindo, and Punjab with Lala Lajpat Rai.
204.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate swapped leaders.

204.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Moderate and Extremist phases of the Congress:
1. The Moderates generally sought self-government within the British Empire.
2. The Extremists regarded British rule as exploitative.
3. The Moderates relied on self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will.
4. The Extremists drew support from students, women, workers and peasants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The three principles of self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will characterised the Extremists, not the Moderates.
204.tq: Identify the reversed methods statement among otherwise correct comparisons.

204.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the methods associated with the Moderates and Extremists respectively?
o: Moderates—prayers, petitions and protests; Extremists—self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will
Moderates—boycott and mass agitation; Extremists—constitutional petitions only
Moderates—complete freedom; Extremists—self-government within the Empire
Moderates—revolutionary violence; Extremists—social reform through legislation
204.x: The Moderates followed the three Ps—prayers, petitions and protests—whereas the Extremists emphasised the three Ss and mass agitation.
204.tq: Use the paired comparison to detect reversed goals and methods.

204.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the social-reform positions of the two groups?
o: The Moderates were generally pro-reform, whereas the Extremists were comparatively orthodox.
The Extremists were uniformly pro-reform, whereas the Moderates opposed social reform.
Both groups rejected all forms of social reform.
Both groups adopted identical positions on the Age of Consent Bill.
204.x: The Moderates were generally pro-reform, while the Extremists were comparatively orthodox; Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill.
204.tq: Test the comparison through a specific social-reform issue.

204.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
204.x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.
204.tq: Place the events by their years before comparing the middle items.

204.s: The Swadeshi Movement was formally launched on 7 August in which year?
204.x: The Swadeshi Movement was launched on 7 August 1905, following the partition of Bengal.
204.tq: Test the year attached to a dated movement rather than its broader phase.

204.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 are particularly associated with the introduction of:
204.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates, especially for Muslims.
204.tq: Link a constitutional reform to its distinctive provision.

204.s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
204.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.
204.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced chronological milestones.

204.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916.
2. Annie Besant's Home Rule League was founded in September 1916.
3. The Congress reunion and Lucknow Pact took place in December 1916.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916, Besant’s in September, and the reunion and Lucknow Pact occurred in December.
204.tq: Check dates within the same year instead of treating all Home Rule events as simultaneous.

204.s: Which one of the following newspapers was published by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Marathi?
204.x: Tilak published Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English; both newspapers began in 1881.
204.tq: Distinguish paired newspapers by language and leader.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — The Arctic Home in the Vedas
204.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with The Punjabee. The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Tilak, Unhappy India by Lajpat Rai and The Soul of India by Pal.
204.tq: Avoid the swapped-author trap among books and newspapers.

204.s: Which of the following statements about extremist newspapers and writings is correct?
o: Annie Besant edited Mahratta and wrote Gita Rahasya.
Aurobindo Ghosh edited Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old.
Lajpat Rai edited Kesari and wrote Bhavani Mandir.
Tilak edited Bande Mataram and wrote Unhappy India.
204.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was the editor of Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old. The other options interchange the works or newspapers of different leaders.
204.tq: Use the author-editor association and reject swapped names.

204.s: New Lamps for Old appeared during 1893–94 in which newspaper?
204.x: Aurobindo Ghosh’s New Lamps for Old appeared during 1893–94 in the Bombay newspaper Indu Prakash.
204.tq: Pair a work with its periodical and publication period.

204.s: Who co-edited Bande Mataram with Aurobindo Ghosh according to the standard association?
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal is commonly identified with Aurobindo Ghosh as a co-editor of Bande Mataram.
204.tq: Test the standard collaborator rather than a leader from the same movement.

204.s: Which one of the following slogans is associated with Lala Lajpat Rai?
o: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
204.x: Lala Lajpat Rai is associated with the slogan ‘Go back Simon’. Tilak’s slogan was ‘Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’.
204.tq: Separate slogans of closely associated Extremist leaders.

204.s: Annie Besant’s New India was originally published under which name?
204.x: Annie Besant’s New India was the renamed Madras Standard. She was also associated with Commonweal, begun in January 1914.
204.tq: Test a renamed newspaper using the original title as the key distinction.

204.s: At the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906, which set of resolutions was passed as part of the compromise?
o: Provincial autonomy, Adult Franchise, Boycott and Home Rule
Non-cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Khilafat and Swaraj
Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, Home Rule, Dyarchy and Swadeshi
204.x: The 1906 Calcutta session passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education, although Swaraj was left undefined.
204.tq: Recall a complete resolution set rather than one isolated item.

204.s: Which issue at the Surat session of 1907 most clearly reflected the difference between the Extremists and Moderates?
o: Whether the Congress should support separate electorates
Whether the boycott should be extended throughout India or restricted to Bengal
Whether the Partition of Bengal should be annulled immediately
Whether the Home Rule League should be founded in 1916
204.x: The Extremists wanted the boycott extended throughout India, while the Moderates wanted the movement restricted to Bengal and sought to drop the 1906 resolutions.
204.tq: Compare the two sides on the precise disputed issue.

204.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the immediate outcome of the Surat session of 1907?
o: The Extremists secured the presidency and adopted a national boycott.
The session adopted the Lucknow Pact unanimously.
The Moderates pushed the Extremists out, and the session was suspended after a scuffle.
The Congress reunited under Tilak’s leadership.
204.x: The Moderates, being in a majority, pushed out the Extremists; a scuffle followed and the session was suspended.
204.tq: Test the actual consequence rather than the causes of a famous split.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly identifies the leadership of the two sides at Surat?
204.x: The Extremists at Surat were led by Tilak, while the Moderates were led by Gokhale.
204.tq: Avoid reversing the leaders of opposing factions.

204.s: The Congress split at Surat was finally healed at which place and in which year?
204.x: The division between the Moderates and Extremists was healed at Lucknow in 1916.
204.tq: Link a political rupture with the later place and year of reconciliation.

204.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on:
204.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 at Ratnagiri.
204.tq: Combine the date and birthplace to defeat close-date distractors.

204.s: Which one of the following pairs of public festivals and years is correctly matched with Tilak?
204.x: Tilak transformed Ganesh Utsav into a public festival in 1893 and Shivaji Jayanti in 1895.
204.tq: Keep the two similar festival dates in their correct sequence.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Tilak’s educational activities:
1. He helped establish the New English School with Agarkar.
2. The Deccan Education Society founded Fergusson College.
3. The standard dates associated with these educational initiatives are 1880 and 1884.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak worked with Agarkar in establishing the New English School, and the Deccan Education Society founded Fergusson College; the standard dates are 1880 and 1884.
204.tq: Combine institutional associations with the dates attached to them.

204.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Tilak’s sedition-trial and imprisonment sequence?
204.x: Tilak received 18 months in the 1897 sedition trial, six years in Mandalay in 1908, and was acquitted in the 1916 case.
204.tq: Match each year with the correct legal consequence and punishment.

204.s: Tilak was released from his imprisonment in Mandalay on:
204.x: Tilak was released from Mandalay prison on 16 June 1914 after his six-year imprisonment beginning in 1908.
204.tq: Distinguish the release date from the later Home Rule date.

204.s: The book The Arctic Home in the Vedas was authored by:
204.x: The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
204.tq: Use the author-work association while rejecting works of neighbouring leaders.

204.s: Which of the following statements about Tilak’s political career is correct?
o: He joined the Indian National Congress in 1890 and founded the Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1905 and founded the Home Rule League in 1914.
He joined the Congress in 1885 and founded the Home Rule League in September 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1897 and founded the Home Rule League in December 1916.
204.x: Tilak joined the Congress in 1890 and founded his Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
204.tq: Pair two dates from the same leader’s political career and reject shifted years.

204.s: Who served as president of Tilak’s Home Rule League, with N.C. Kelkar serving as secretary?
204.x: Joseph Baptista was the president of Tilak’s Home Rule League, while N.C. Kelkar served as secretary.
204.tq: Distinguish office-holders within the same organisation.

204.s: Lajpat Rai, who was associated with the Arya Samaj, was born in which year?
204.x: Lajpat Rai was born in 1865. He was an important Arya Samaj leader and a prominent extremist nationalist.
204.tq: Use the precise year and distinguish it from the birth years of other extremist leaders.

204.s: Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay in:
204.x: Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay in 1907 as part of the government's repression of extremist nationalism.
204.tq: Distinguish the year of deportation from the later deportation of Tilak.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Lajpat Rai:
1. He went to the United States after 1908.
2. He established the Indian Home Rule League of America.
3. The Indian Home Rule League of America was established by him in 1917.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All three statements are correct. Lajpat Rai went to the United States after 1908 and established the Indian Home Rule League of America in 1917.
204.tq: Combine a person, organisation and year; verify each statement independently.

204.s: Which of the following sets contains only biographies written by Lajpat Rai?
204.x: Lajpat Rai wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi and Shivaji.
204.tq: Identify the complete author–works set and eliminate the set containing a nearby but unsupported name.

204.s: Who among the following authored the work entitled Unhappy India?
204.x: Unhappy India was written by Lala Lajpat Rai.
204.tq: Test the author–title association directly.

204.s: Bipin Chandra Pal was associated with which organisation?
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was a member of the Brahmo Samaj, whereas Lajpat Rai was associated with the Arya Samaj.
204.tq: Separate the two leaders by their religious-reform associations.

204.s: Why was Bipin Chandra Pal arrested in 1907?
o: For leading the protest against the Simon Commission
For organising the Indian Home Rule League of America
For refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case.
204.tq: Match the arrest with the specific legal incident rather than with a later nationalist event.

204.s: Bipin Chandra Pal lived in England during which period?
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal lived in England from 1908 to 1911.
204.tq: Distinguish overlapping periods by checking both the starting and ending years.

204.s: Bipin Chandra Pal particularly stressed India's:
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal emphasised India's spiritual and cultural revival.
204.tq: Select the central ideological emphasis associated with the leader.

204.s:
Consider the following statements about Aurobindo:
1. He was acquitted in the Alipore case in 1909.
2. He retired to Pondicherry in 1910.
3. His retirement to Pondicherry preceded the Alipore case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Aurobindo retired to Pondicherry in 1910, after his acquittal in the Alipore case in 1909.
204.tq: Check the sequence of the legal case and subsequent retirement.

204.s: In extremist political thought, Swaraj signified:
o: administrative decentralisation within the colonial state
204.x: For the Extremists, Swaraj meant complete freedom from British control, not merely colonial self-government.
204.tq: Distinguish complete independence from the moderate demand for colonial self-government.

204.s: Which one of the following was NOT a method associated with extremist nationalism?
204.x: The Extremists had no faith in British generosity. Their methods included passive resistance, mass agitation, boycott, Swadeshi, national education and self-sacrifice.
204.tq: Find the option that contradicts the underlying political attitude.

204.s:
Consider the following methods:
1. Passive resistance
2. Mass agitation
3. Boycott and Swadeshi
4. National education
The Extremist programme included:
204.x: All four were part of the Extremist programme, along with self-sacrifice and a rejection of dependence on British generosity.
204.tq: Recognise the inclusive option when all listed methods belong to the same programme.

204.s: The concept of spiritual nationalism viewed the nation primarily as:
204.x: Spiritual nationalism represented the nation as a mother goddess, an idea expressed through symbols such as Bande Mataram and Bhavani Mandir.
204.tq: Identify the defining symbol of an ideological concept.

204.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with spiritual nationalism?
1. Bande Mataram — national symbolism
2. Bhavani Mandir — spiritual-nationalist imagery
3. Pride in India's past — cultural revival
4. Hindu festivals — mass contact
Select the correct answer using the code below.
204.x: All four associations are correct. Spiritual nationalism used national symbolism, pride in India's past and Hindu festivals to create mass contact.
204.tq: Test several linked features of one ideology through a complete coded option.

204.s: Atmashakti, in the context of extremist ideology, referred to:
204.x: Atmashakti meant self-reliance. It was connected with constructive work such as the establishment of cooperatives.
204.tq: Match the indigenous term with its precise ideological meaning.

204.s: Which of the following was an example of constructive work associated with self-reliance?
204.x: Cooperatives were cited as an example of constructive work associated with Atmashakti or self-reliance.
204.tq: Apply the concept to the practical activity that expresses it.

204.s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted in 1908 to deal with incitement to offences through newspapers?
204.x: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act was enacted in 1908. The Indian Press Act followed in 1910.
204.tq: Distinguish similarly named press and security laws by their exact titles and years.

204.s:
Consider the following laws:
1. Seditious Meetings Act — 1907
2. Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act — 1908
3. Criminal Law Amendment Act — 1908
4. Explosive Substances Act — 1908
Which of the statements given above are correct?
204.x: All four pairings are correct. The Seditious Meetings Act was enacted in 1907, while the other three listed Acts were enacted in 1908.
204.tq: Verify each Act–year pair before selecting the complete combination.

204.s: The Indian Press Act mentioned in the context of extremist repression was enacted in:
204.x: The Indian Press Act was enacted in 1910.
204.tq: Separate the later press law from the cluster of repressive Acts enacted in 1908.

204.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — deported to Mandalay in 1907
Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra — Bengal leaders deported in 1908
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — sent to Mandalay in 1908
Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh — deported in 1907
204.x: Bipin Chandra Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case; he was not deported to Mandalay. Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported in 1907, while Tilak and the mentioned Bengal leaders faced repression in 1908.
204.tq: Find the swapped person–punishment association among closely related repression measures.

204.s: Which sequence correctly describes the position of the leading Extremists by 1910?
o: Tilak was in jail; Aurobindo had retired; Pal was arrested; Lajpat Rai had left
Tilak had left; Aurobindo was in jail; Pal had retired; Lajpat Rai led Congress
Tilak was in England; Aurobindo led Congress; Pal was deported; Lajpat Rai was in Mandalay
Tilak was in Pondicherry; Aurobindo was in Mandalay; Pal led Congress; Lajpat Rai was arrested
204.x: By 1910, Tilak was in jail, Aurobindo had retired to Pondicherry, Pal had been arrested and Lajpat Rai had left. This enabled the Moderates to dominate the Congress.
204.tq: Use a multi-person status snapshot and eliminate options with swapped locations or actions.

204.s: The dominance of the Moderates in the Congress by 1910 was primarily facilitated by:
o: the merger of the Arya Samaj and Brahmo Samaj
the complete acceptance of Swaraj by the colonial government
the absence, imprisonment or retirement of leading Extremists
204.x: The Moderates dominated because Tilak was in jail, Aurobindo had retired, Pal was arrested and Lajpat Rai had left by 1910.
204.tq: Infer the political consequence from the combined status of the leaders.

204.s: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was jailed in Andhra in:
204.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was jailed in Andhra in 1908.
204.tq: Test the regional application of the wider repression chronology.

204.s: The Extremists contributed to the national movement by:
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
204.x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.
204.tq: Identify the principal historical significance rather than a method or criticism.

204.s: Which of the following was a criticism of Extremist politics?
o: Its religious symbolism alienated Muslims and its social outlook was orthodox.
It weakened the demand for Swaraj by supporting colonial rule.
It completely rejected all cultural symbols.
It prevented the use of boycott and Swadeshi.
204.x: The Extremists were criticised for using religious symbolism that alienated Muslims and for being socially orthodox. The Surat Split was also regarded as weakening the Congress.
204.tq: Select the option containing the recognised criticisms without reversing the Extremist programme.

204.s: Which statement regarding the Surat Split is correct?
o: It weakened the Congress as an organisation.
It ended the use of Swadeshi permanently.
It led to the retirement of Aurobindo in 1907.
204.x: The Surat Split weakened the Congress by dividing the Moderates and Extremists. The other statements do not describe its consequence.
204.tq: Distinguish the organisational consequence of the split from unrelated extremist developments.

204.s: The Prime Minister paid tribute to Lokmanya Tilak on his birth anniversary observed on:
204.x: Lokmanya Tilak's birth anniversary is observed on 23 July, and the Prime Minister paid tribute to him on that occasion.
204.tq: Use the exact commemorative date and avoid confusing it with other national observances.

204.s: By 1917, the number of Home Rule branches in Andhra was:
204.x: Andhra had 52 Home Rule branches by 1917.
204.tq: Test the precise regional organisational figure.

204.s: What did students of the Machilipatnam National College wear after Annie Besant's arrest on 15 June 1917?
204.x: Students of the Machilipatnam National College wore Besant lockets after Annie Besant was arrested on 15 June 1917.
204.tq: Link the protest action with the person and triggering date.

204.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay
B. Tilak was sent to Mandalay
C. Aurobindo was acquitted in the Alipore case
D. Aurobindo retired to Pondicherry
204.x: The correct order is 1907 deportation of Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh, 1908 deportation of Tilak, Aurobindo's acquittal in 1909 and his retirement to Pondicherry in 1910.
204.tq: Anchor the sequence to the years 1907, 1908, 1909 and 1910.

205.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for bicameralism and direct elections at the Centre.
3. The Government of India Act, 1935 prescribed an All-India Federation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All three statements are correct features of the 1919 and 1935 constitutional reforms.
205.tq: Group the distinctive features of two successive constitutional Acts.

205.s:
The Government of India Act, 1919 extended communal representation to which of the following communities?
1. Sikhs
2. Indian Christians
3. Anglo-Indians
4. Europeans
205.x: The 1919 Act extended communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
205.tq: Check the complete membership of a constitutional category.

205.s:
The Government of India Act, 1935 extended separate electorates to which of the following?
1. Depressed classes
2. Women
3. Labour
4. Europeans
205.x: The 1935 Act extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour. Europeans were among the communities receiving communal representation under the 1919 arrangements.
205.tq: Separate closely related categories before selecting the complete set.

205.s: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 provided for which of the following electoral arrangements?
o: Election by a single national constituency
Universal adult franchise through direct elections
205.x: The 1909 reforms introduced indirect, multi-tier elections rather than direct universal elections.
205.tq: Discriminate between direct, indirect and nominated representation.

205.s:
With reference to the Indian Councils Act, 1909, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Legislative Council was enlarged to 60 additional members.
2. An official majority was retained at the Centre.
3. A non-official majority was provided in the provinces.
4. The Governor's veto made the provincial non-official majority ineffective in practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All four statements describe the composition and practical limitations of the councils under the 1909 reforms.
205.tq: Read constitutional composition and actual executive control together.

205.s: Which of the following powers was NOT granted to members under the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
205.x: Members could discuss the budget, ask supplementary questions and move resolutions, but they could not vote on the budget.
205.tq: Find the one power excluded from an otherwise expanded legislative role.

205.s: Who was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council?
205.x: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council and held the Law portfolio.
205.tq: Link the office with the exact Indian office-holder.

205.s: Satyendra Prasanna Sinha served on the Viceroy's Executive Council as the:
205.x: Sinha was the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council and served as its Law Member.
205.tq: Use the portfolio trap when a person and office are closely associated.

205.s: Who went to England in 1906 and met John Morley to press for self-government for India on the model of other colonies?
205.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale met Morley in England in 1906 and advocated self-government for India.
205.tq: Match the political leader with the specific constitutional initiative.

205.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced mainly to:
o: Rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty
Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic
205.x: Morley and Minto sought to rally the Moderates and reward Muslim loyalty through limited constitutional concessions and separate electorates.
205.tq: Identify the political purpose behind a constitutional measure.

205.s: The Simla Deputation led by Aga Khan III met Lord Minto on:
205.x: The Simla Deputation, led by Aga Khan III, met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.
205.tq: Separate two closely connected 1906 dates by linking each to its event.

205.s:
The Simla Deputation of 1906 demanded:
1. Separate electorates for Muslims
2. Weightage for Muslims
3. Representation based on their contribution to the Empire's defence
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The deputation demanded separate electorates and weightage, justifying the demand by referring to the Muslims' contribution to the defence of the Empire.
205.tq: Combine the demands with the stated justification rather than selecting only the headline demand.

205.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at a session of the:
205.x: The All-India Muslim League was founded at Dacca during the session of the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference.
205.tq: Distinguish the founding conference from the organisation founded there.

205.s: Who proposed the formation of the All-India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906?
205.x: Nawab Salimullah of Dacca proposed the formation of the All-India Muslim League.
205.tq: Separate the proposer, first president and later London organiser.

205.s: Who was the first president of the All-India Muslim League?
205.x: Aga Khan III was the first president of the All-India Muslim League.
205.tq: Use role-based discrimination among closely associated Muslim League figures.

205.s: Which one of the following was NOT an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Keeping Muslims away from the Congress
Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire
205.x: The early League aimed at loyalty to the British Empire, protection of Muslim political interests and separation from the Congress; immediate armed revolt was not one of its stated aims.
205.tq: Reject the extreme revolutionary alternative when testing an organisation's declared aims.

205.s: The Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916 was presided over by:
205.x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.
205.tq: Avoid swapping the session president with the principal brokers of the pact.

205.s:
The Lucknow Congress Session of 1916 was historically significant because it witnessed:
1. Reunion of Moderates and Extremists
2. The Congress-League alliance
3. Tilak's return to the Congress fold
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The 1916 session marked the reunion of Moderates and Extremists, Tilak's return and the Congress-League alliance represented by the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify all historically linked features of a landmark session.

205.s: The Muslim League delegation associated with the Lucknow Pact was led by the:
