216.x: The movement’s short-run success was limited by its restricted spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift.
216.tq: Identify the paired outcome factors rather than confusing them with causes of other movements.

216.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the broad historical transition in Indian peasant movements?
o: From sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders to Gandhian satyagraha and then organised Kisan Sabhas
From organised Kisan Sabhas to sporadic revolts and then to plantation movements
From tribal movements to exclusive urban labour movements
From revolutionary violence directly to constitutional reforms without mass participation
216.x: Before 1917, peasant movements were often sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders; they later developed into Gandhian satyagraha and organised Kisan Sabhas in the 1930s.
216.tq: Recognise the chronological sequence of changing forms of agrarian mobilisation.

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to peasant movements in Gujarat?
o: Bardoli — Baba Ramchandra and Madari Pasi
Kheda — Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Bardoli — Ali Musliyar and Kunjahammad Haji
216.x: Kheda in Gujarat was associated with Patel and Mohanlal Pandya. The other pairs combine leaders from Uttar Pradesh, Bengal and Malabar movements.
216.tq: Use the region first, then verify the associated leaders.

216.s: The Telangana peasant movement of 1946–51 was associated with which combination?
o: Hyderabad, the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha
Bengal, the Indian National Congress and the Agrarian League
Gujarat, the Congress Socialist Party and the All India Trade Union Congress
Mewar, the Muslim League and the Oudh Kisan Sabha
216.x: The Telangana armed struggle occurred in Hyderabad during 1946–51 and was associated with the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha.
216.tq: Combine the region, period and organisations to avoid confusing Telangana with Tebhaga.

216.s: The anti-zamindari struggles in Andhra Pradesh mentioned in connection with land reform included which of the following?
216.x: The Nellore and Munagala anti-zamindari struggles are highlighted as important Andhra-related agrarian movements. Land reform demands also contributed to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill of 1947.
216.tq: Identify the Andhra-specific locations rather than selecting nationally prominent movement centres.

216.s: The Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill was introduced in which year in the context of land reform demands?
216.x: Land reform demands associated with agrarian struggles led to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill in 1947.
216.tq: Distinguish the bill’s year from the years of the Kisan Sabha and Bargadari legislation.

216.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Moplah Movement is correct?
o: It occurred in Maharashtra in 1875 and targeted moneylenders from Gujarat and Marwar.
It occurred in Bengal in 1946 and was led by bargadars demanding two-thirds of the crop.
It occurred in Gujarat in 1928 as a non-violent Congress campaign against revenue enhancement.
It occurred in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants against landlords and the British.
216.x: The Moplah Movement took place in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants in conflict with landlords and the British.
216.tq: Separate Moplah from Tebhaga, Deccan and Bardoli through region, year and target.

216.s: Which of the following pairs of leaders was associated with the Moplah Movement?
o: Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
216.x: Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar were associated with the Moplah Movement in Malabar.
216.tq: Match the movement with its distinctive leadership rather than its general social base.

217.s: The Nellore District Zamindari Rythu Sangham first met on 19 October 1929 at the house of whom?
217.x: The Nellore District Zamindari Rythu Sangham first met on 19 October 1929 at Dodla Ramireddy’s house.
217.tq: Test the exact combination of date, place and associated person.

217.s:
With reference to the Andhra Rashtra Zamindari Rythu Sangham, consider the following statements:
1. It was formed in August 1929.
2. Jagannadhadasu of Ganjam was associated with its founding.
3. Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju served as its President.
4. Mandeswara Sarma served as its General Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: All four statements are correct. The organisation was formed in August 1929, with Jagannadhadasu of Ganjam associated with its formation, Bhupathiraju Venkatapathiraju as President and Mandeswara Sarma as General Secretary.
217.tq: Check each office-bearer and date before selecting the coded combination.

217.s: The First Zamindar Rythu Sabha of North Andhra was held at Vizag on:
217.x: The First Zamindar Rythu Sabha of North Andhra was held at Vizag on 3 November 1929.
217.tq: Distinguish closely spaced organisational dates.

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zamin Ryot — edited by N.G. Ranga
Rythu Bidda — written by Dodla Ramireddy
217.x: The First Zamindar Rythu Sabha in North Andhra started Prajavani, which was edited by Garimella Krishnamurthy.
217.tq: Use the publication-editor association to eliminate swapped names and places.

217.s: The First anti-zamindari conference held at Venkatagiri in September 1931 was presided over by:
217.x: N.G. Ranga presided over the First anti-zamindari conference at Venkatagiri in September 1931.
217.tq: Test the presiding leader of a historically significant conference.

217.s: The principal objective of the First anti-zamindari conference at Venkatagiri was:
o: Introduction of cash rents in all estates
217.x: The stated goal of the conference was the abolition of the zamindari system.
217.tq: Identify the central demand rather than an associated grievance.

217.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Jameen Ryot Mahasabha is correct?
o: It campaigned for the continuation of zamindari with reduced rents.
It demanded the abolition of ryotwari settlements.
It was formed to protect the rights of zamindars over forest produce.
It demanded in 1938 that the government enact a Zamindari Abolition Act.
217.x: The Jameen Ryot Mahasabha campaigned for abolition of zamindari and, in 1938, demanded a Zamindari Abolition Act.
217.tq: Separate an organisation’s abolitionist demand from opposing zamindari-era claims.

217.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Zamin Ryot was associated with Nellore Venkataramana Naidu.
2. It was published from March 1930.
3. The dates 7 March and 17 March 1930 are both associated with its publication in the available records.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: Nellore Venkataramana Naidu was associated with Zamin Ryot, published in March 1930; records cite both 7 March and 17 March 1930.
217.tq: Retain all supported details when a question combines publication, person and date.

217.s: The rent in Gampalagudem estate was collected primarily:
o: In cash after annual auction of grazing lands
In kind, resulting in excessive extraction
Through a fixed payment of 60 seers per acre
As a renewal fee called nazarana
217.x: In Gampalagudem, rent was collected in kind rather than cash, leading to excessive extraction.
217.tq: Distinguish the mode of rent collection from other estate grievances and levies.

217.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kancha paddhati in the Venkatagiri estate?
o: Waste land was seized for lanka cultivation.
Rent was collected only in harvested grain.
Grazing land was auctioned every year.
Forest land was transferred permanently to tenants.
217.x: Under the Kancha paddhati, grazing land in the Venkatagiri estate was auctioned annually.
217.tq: Match the exact local practice with its meaning.

217.s:
Consider the following statements about the Venkatagiri estate agitation:
1. Venkatagiri was the second largest estate in Coastal Andhra.
2. Pullari was collected even during drought.
3. The Palemkota revolt took place on 20 March 1933.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: All three statements are correct. The estate was the second largest in Coastal Andhra, pullari was collected even during drought, and the Palemkota revolt occurred on 20 March 1933.
217.tq: Combine estate status, tax practice and a precise revolt date.

217.s: Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad was the zamindar associated with which estate agitation?
217.x: Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad was the zamindar of Challapalli, where agitation began in June 1930.
217.tq: Use the zamindar–estate pair and avoid swapping neighbouring estate names.

217.s: The principal grievances in the Challapalli estate included:
o: Reduction of harvest wages from 80 to 60 seers per acre
Seizure of lanka and waste lands and imposition of vetti
Annual auction of grazing land and collection of pullari only during drought
Arrests for forest cutting followed by police firing
217.x: The Challapalli agitation concerned the seizure of lanka and waste lands and the imposition of vetti.
217.tq: Compare the distinctive grievance of one estate with those of other agitations.

217.s: In the Munagala estate agitation of 1938–39, the harvest wage was reduced from:
217.x: In Munagala, the harvest wage was reduced from 80 to 60 seers per acre during 1938–39.
217.tq: Test both figures in a paired numerical change.

217.s: Which of the following estate–agitation pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kalipatnam — 4,000 acres grabbed for a project and not returned
Gampalagudem — annual auction of grazing land under Kancha paddhati
Mandasa — forest-cutting arrests followed by police firing
Munagala — harvest wage reduced from 80 to 60 seers per acre
217.x: Annual auction of grazing land under Kancha paddhati was associated with Venkatagiri, not Gampalagudem. Gampalagudem involved rent collection in kind and excessive extraction.
217.tq: Find the swapped estate–grievance pair.

217.s: The Kalipatnam agitation in West Godavari was connected with the taking of land for a project. What was the approximate extent of land grabbed?
217.x: About 4,000 acres were taken for a project and were never returned in the Kalipatnam estate.
217.tq: Recall the distinctive quantitative feature of the agitation.

217.s: Which one of the following statements about the Mandasa agitation is correct?
o: It began in June 1930 under Yarlagadda Sivarama Prasad.
It was led by the annual auction of grazing lands.
It occurred on 1 April 1940 and police firing killed five persons, including Pusumanu Gunnamma.
It concerned a wage cut from 80 to 60 seers per acre.
217.x: The Mandasa agitation occurred on 1 April 1940 after arrests for forest cutting; police firing killed five persons, including Pusumanu Gunnamma.
217.tq: Combine the date, immediate cause and consequence of an agitation.

217.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Area)
A. Kalipatnam
B. Srikakulam
C. Challapalli
D. Munagala

List-II (Leader)
1. Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju
2. Gouthu Latchanna
3. Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya
4. Nanduri Prasada Rao

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
217.x: Kalipatnam was associated with Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju; Srikakulam with Gouthu Latchanna; Challapalli with Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya; and Munagala with Nanduri Prasada Rao.
217.tq: Start with the sure area–leader pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nellore/Venkatagiri — Yakasiri Chellamma, associated with women’s chilli-powder resistance
217.x: Yakasiri Chellamma was associated with the women’s chilli-powder resistance in the Nellore/Venkatagiri area.
217.tq: Discriminate among leaders belonging to different districts and local struggles.

217.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the anti-zamindari movement in the Nellore/Venkatagiri area?
1. Vennelakanti Raghavaiah and Dodla Ramireddy were associated with it.
2. Petturi Govinda Reddy and Baddedi Venkatanarayana Reddy were also associated with the area.
3. Baddedi Venkatanarayana Reddy was a Gudur MLA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
217.x: All three statements are correct. These leaders were associated with the Nellore/Venkatagiri area, and Baddedi Venkatanarayana Reddy was the Gudur MLA.
217.tq: Check a cluster of related names and the accompanying political designation.

217.s: Gandhi visited Venkatagiri on:
217.x: Mahatma Gandhi visited Venkatagiri on 20 December 1933.
217.tq: Distinguish a precise visit date from dates of conferences and legislation.

217.s: Who directed the film Rythu Bidda, released in 1939 and banned by the zamindar?
217.x: Rythu Bidda was directed by Gudavalli Ramabrahmam, released in 1939, and banned by the zamindar.
217.tq: Match a cultural work with its creator and its political context.

217.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Introduction of the Estates Abolition Bill by Kala Venkata Rao
B. Passage of the Act by the Madras Assembly
C. Assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari
D. The Act came into force

Select the correct sequence.
217.x: The Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947, passed in November 1948, received assent on 2 April 1949, and came into force on 7 September 1949.
217.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place passage and assent between them.

217.s: Who introduced the Madras Estates Abolition Bill on 11 November 1947?
217.x: Revenue Minister Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947.
217.tq: Identify the minister associated with introducing legislation rather than giving assent to it.

217.s:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of the Estates Abolition legislation:
1. It abolished zamindari and inamdari estates.
2. Tenants became direct ryots of the state.
3. Zamindars were paid compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: The legislation abolished zamindari and inamdari estates, made tenants direct ryots of the state and provided compensation to zamindars.
217.tq: Test the three principal legal consequences together.

217.s: The assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari to the Estates Abolition law was given on:
217.x: Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari gave assent on 2 April 1949. It was the first law of independent India to receive the Governor-General’s assent.
217.tq: Separate the Bill-introduction, Assembly-passage, assent and commencement dates.

217.s: Which statement regarding the commencement and implementation of the Estates Abolition law is correct?
o: It came into force on 2 April 1949, while estates were taken over from 1951.
It came into force in November 1948, while estates were taken over from 1949.
It came into force on 7 September 1949, while estates were taken over from 1950.
It came into force on 11 November 1947, while estates were taken over from 1948.
217.x: The law came into force on 7 September 1949, and estates were taken over from 1950.
217.tq: Distinguish the commencement date of an Act from the later administrative takeover.

217.s: Which of the following was a major grievance of ryots under the zamindari system?
o: Payment of wages in cash by zamindars
Ryotwari assessment fixed directly by the state
Nazarana, a renewal fee for tenancy
Universal exemption from forest and grazing taxes
217.x: Nazarana was a renewal fee imposed for continuation of tenancy and was among the grievances of ryots.
217.tq: Distinguish a zamindari-era levy from features of the ryotwari system.

217.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gothi — annual renewal fee for tenancy
217.x: Gothi referred to hereditary bonded labour in the Agency. The annual renewal fee for tenancy was nazarana.
217.tq: Identify the swapped meaning among closely related customary exactions.

217.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Forest-produce, water and cattle taxes were among the burdens on the rural population.
2. Gothi referred to hereditary bonded labour in the Agency.
3. Pullari was a tax on grazing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: All three statements are correct. These taxes and forms of bonded labour formed part of the grievances associated with zamindari conditions.
217.tq: Group several related exactions while checking the precise meaning of each term.

217.s: Which development intensified agrarian distress during 1929–35?
o: The abolition of all forest taxes
The conversion of all estates into ryotwari holdings
A sharp rise in crop prices
The crash in crop prices during the Depression
217.x: The Depression of 1929–35 caused crop prices to crash, intensifying agrarian distress.
217.tq: Link the economic event with its direct agrarian consequence.

217.s: At the time of Independence, approximately what proportion of Andhra’s land remained under zamindars?
217.x: About 40 percent of Andhra’s land was still under zamindars at Independence.
217.tq: Recall the quantitative scale of zamindari persistence at Independence.

217.s: Who first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920?
217.x: Pattabhi first called for an anti-zamindari struggle in 1920.
217.tq: Distinguish the earliest call from later organisational leadership.

217.s:
With reference to the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, consider the following statements:
1. Inam ryots fought for abolition of inam estates under this Act.
2. The Vizag Zamindar Rythu Sabha in 1929 demanded that the Act be amended.
3. The Act itself abolished all zamindari and inamdari estates in 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
217.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 1908 Act was the subject of demands for amendment and abolition of inam estates; the later Estates Abolition legislation abolished zamindari and inamdari estates.
217.tq: Separate the 1908 Estates Land Act from the later abolition legislation.

217.s: In which year did the Madras Congress Ministry appoint the committee on the zamindari system, with C. Rajagopalachari as Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam as Revenue Minister?
217.x: The Madras Congress Ministry appointed the committee in 1937. C. Rajagopalachari was the Chief Minister and Tanguturi Prakasam served as the Revenue Minister.
217.tq: Use the ministry-composition clue to identify the correct year and distinguish the Chief Minister from the Revenue Minister.

217.s: The formal constitution of the Prakasam Committee on the zamindari system took place in:
217.x: The committee was formally constituted in September 1938 and consisted of nine members.
217.tq: Pair the month and year with the membership figure instead of relying on the committee’s appointment year.

217.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Completion of the report of the zamindari enquiry committee
B. Appointment of the committee by the Madras Congress Ministry
C. Formal constitution of the committee
D. Passage of the Madras Act that became one of the early abolition laws
217.x: The correct sequence is appointment in 1937, formal constitution in September 1938, completion of the report on 7 November 1938, and the Madras Act of 1948.
217.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1938 committee events in their proper order.

217.s: Which of the following was the principal conclusion of the committee’s report regarding the relationship between land, the tiller and the zamindar?
o: The State alone owned the land and the zamindar had no role in revenue collection.
The zamindar was the absolute owner of the land and the tiller was only a tenant.
Land belonged jointly to the zamindar and the cultivating tenants.
Land belonged to the tiller, while the zamindar was merely a tax collector.
217.x: The report held that land belongs to the tiller and that the zamindar is only a tax collector.
217.tq: Test the precise relationship stated in the report and avoid the swapped-owner and tenant descriptions.

217.s: What did Tanguturi Prakasam regret about the report of the zamindari enquiry committee?
o: That it failed to discuss the position of the tiller
That it did not identify the zamindari areas of the Madras Presidency
That it recommended continuation of zamindari without reforms
That it did not state outright whether zamindari should be abolished
217.x: Prakasam regretted that the report did not say expressly whether the zamindari system should be abolished.
217.tq: Look for the precise limitation of the report rather than assuming that its criticism of zamindari amounted to an explicit abolition recommendation.

217.s: Who led the yatra from Ichchapuram to submit a petition to the committee on the zamindari system?
o: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao
Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and C. Rajagopalachari
217.x: Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao led the yatra from Ichchapuram to petition the committee.
217.tq: Match the specific action and starting place with the correct pair of leaders.

217.s: Which one of the following best expresses the significance of the anti-zamindari agitations in Andhra?
o: They resulted in the establishment of the zamindari system throughout the Madras Presidency in 1948.
They led to the replacement of the Madras Presidency by a separate zamindari administration.
They helped make the Madras Act of 1948 one of the first zamindari abolition laws of independent India.
They postponed all legislation on zamindari abolition until the 1960s.
217.x: The agitations in Andhra helped create the political conditions in which the Madras Act of 1948 became one of the first abolition laws of independent India.
217.tq: Distinguish a historical significance statement from options that reverse the outcome of the movement.

217.s: Which organisation is associated with pioneering the demand for ‘land to the tiller’ and the abolition of zamindari?
217.x: The communists pioneered the demand for land to the tiller and for the abolition of zamindari.
217.tq: Use the distinctive political demand to identify the organisation associated with it.

217.s: Approximately what proportion of zamindari land in the Madras Presidency was concentrated in Vizag, Nellore, the two Godavaris, Krishna and Chittoor?
217.x: About 70 percent of the zamindari land in the Madras Presidency lay in Vizag, Nellore, the two Godavari districts, Krishna and Chittoor.
217.tq: Identify the exact percentage before assessing the geographical grouping associated with it.

218.s: N.G. Ranga is associated with which of the following titles?
218.x: N.G. Ranga was popularly known as Rythu Bandhu. He was also described as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement and as Acharya.
218.tq: Directly identify the popular title associated with a peasant leader.

218.s: Which one of the following statements regarding N.G. Ranga is correct?
o: He founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham alone in 1915.
He was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement.
He led the 1937 Rythu Yatra as a village association organiser.
218.x: N.G. Ranga was known as the Father of the Indian Peasant Movement. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah, while the 1937 Rythu Yatra was led by Kommareddi Satyanarayana.
218.tq: Use the leader–title association and reject swapped deeds.

218.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. N.G. Ranga was also known as Acharya.
2. He received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991.
3. He founded the Andhra Kisan movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: All three statements are correct. N.G. Ranga was known as Acharya, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1991, and founded the Andhra Kisan movement.
218.tq: Check each biographical statement independently before selecting the combined code.

218.s: Who among the following authored the Munagala Award?
218.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah authored the Munagala Award. He was also a pioneer of the zamindari ryot movement and Secretary of the APCC.
218.tq: Match the named document with its author, guarding against swapped deeds.

218.s:
Kommareddi Satyanarayana is associated with which of the following activities?

1. Formation of village peasant associations in 1935
2. Leadership of the 1937 Rythu Yatra
3. Presidency of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936

Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: Kommareddi Satyanarayana formed village peasant associations in 1935 and led the 1937 Rythu Yatra. The 1936 AIKS President was Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
218.tq: Separate a leader’s documented activities from a similar organisational position.

218.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao — Srikakulam kisan leader
2. Gouthu Latchanna — Srikakulam kisan leader
3. Gottipati Brahmaiah — Srikakulam kisan leader

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao and Gouthu Latchanna were Srikakulam kisan leaders. Gottipati Brahmaiah is associated with the zamindari ryot movement and the Munagala Award.
218.tq: Use the regional association to eliminate the swapped leader.

218.s: Which of the following is NOT a book associated with N.G. Ranga?
218.x: Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry and Fight for Freedom are books associated with N.G. Ranga. The Munagala Award was authored by Gottipati Brahmaiah and is not a book of Ranga.
218.tq: Find the item that belongs to the neighbouring leader rather than the named author.

218.s: The First Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha associated with N.G. Ranga was founded at:
218.x: The First Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha was founded at Nidubrolu in 1923.
218.tq: Pair the institution with both its place and year.

218.s: Which one of the following was India’s first Kisan School?
218.x: The Peasant Institute, or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, at Nidubrolu was India’s first Kisan School. It was established in 1933–34 with Bharathi Devi and Ranga’s brothers.
218.tq: Distinguish the first institution from later schools and political centres.

218.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Political summer school — Kothapatnam — 1937
2. Rajakeeya Pathashala — Kankipadu — 1939
3. Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam — Madanapalle — May 1938

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
218.x: All three pairs are correct. The Political Summer School was at Kothapatnam in 1937, Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939, and Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam at Madanapalle in May 1938.
218.tq: Start from the sure place–year pairs and verify the complete set.

218.s: The Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu, also called Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam, was established during:
218.x: The Peasant Institute or Ramanayidu Rythu Vidyalayam was established at Nidubrolu in 1933–34 and was regarded as India’s first Kisan School.
218.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced institutional years.

218.s: The Divi Taluk Resettlement Mahasabha at Mopidevi, which adopted a no-tax resolution, was led by:
218.x: The 1931 Divi Taluk Resettlement Mahasabha at Mopidevi adopted a no-tax resolution under the leadership of Gottipati Brahmaiah.
218.tq: Match the agitation with its leader rather than another ryot organiser.

218.s: The Ryot Agitation of Andhra took place in:
218.x: The Ryot Agitation of Andhra took place in 1933 and was led by Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary.
218.tq: Use the year–agitation association and distinguish it from adjacent movements.

218.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. 1935 anti-resettlement movement in Guntur — N.G. Ranga
2. 1933 Ryot Agitation of Andhra — Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary
3. 1931 Divi Taluk Resettlement Mahasabha — N.G. Ranga

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: The 1935 anti-resettlement movement in Guntur and the Rythu Rakshana Yatra were led by N.G. Ranga, while the 1933 agitation was led by Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary. The 1931 Divi Taluk movement was led by Gottipati Brahmaiah.
218.tq: Catch the swapped leader in a year–movement sequence.

218.s: The cycle rally from Ichchapuram to Madras against the Madras Land Settlement Act was associated with:
218.x: N.G. Ranga led the cycle rally from Ichchapuram to Madras against the Madras Land Settlement Act during 1938–39.
218.tq: Identify the movement by its distinctive route, issue and period.

218.s:
With reference to the All India Kisan Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. It was founded in April 1936 at Lucknow.
2. Its founding took place during an INC session.
3. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was its President and N.G. Ranga was its Secretary.
4. The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham merged into it in 1940.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham merged into the AIKS in 1936, not 1940.
218.tq: Reject the famous-word year trap in an otherwise correct organisational statement.

218.s: The Palasa session of the All India Kisan Sabha was held in:
218.x: The Palasa AIKS session was held in March 1940 and was presided over by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
218.tq: Separate a session date from the organisation’s founding date.

218.s: Which one of the following events occurred immediately after the Palasa AIKS session of March 1940?
o: The founding of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham
The founding of the First Agricultural Labourers’ Mahasabha
218.x: The Mandasa firing followed the Palasa AIKS session and took place on 1 April 1940.
218.tq: Use the immediate chronological link between a conference and its reported consequence.

218.s: Why was N.G. Ranga jailed in connection with the Palasa AIKS session?
o: He occupied the zamindar’s surplus land.
He defied an order while confined to Nidubrolu.
He refused to preside over the session.
218.x: N.G. Ranga was confined to Nidubrolu, defied the order, and was consequently jailed in connection with the Palasa session.
218.tq: Identify the action that explains the stated consequence.

218.s: During the Second World War, the communist-led All India Kisan Sabha supported which policy?
218.x: During the Second World War, the communist-led AIKS supported the policy known as the People’s War.
218.tq: Match the organisation with its wartime political position.

218.s: Which organisation was founded by N.G. Ranga in 1943 after he left the All India Kisan Sabha?
218.x: N.G. Ranga left the AIKS during the wartime period and founded the Andhra Rashtra Kisan Congress in 1943.
218.tq: Use the organisational succession to distinguish similarly named bodies.

218.s: Munagala paragana was situated in which administrative area at the time of the struggle?
218.x: Munagala paragana was located in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district at the time. It is now associated with Suryapet/Nalgonda.
218.tq: Test the historical location rather than the present administrative association.

218.s: Who was the zamindar of Munagala?
218.x: Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao was the zamindar of Munagala. Though a literary patron, he was described as a harsh landlord.
218.tq: Match the estate with its zamindar, avoiding a leader–landlord swap.

218.s: The Munagala Zamindari Rythu Sangham was founded in 1930 by:
o: Nanduri Prasada Rao and Uppala Ramayya
Immadi Papayya and Kodati Venkata Narasimha Rao
Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
218.x: The Munagala Zamindari Rythu Sangham was founded in 1930 by Immadi Papayya, Kodati Venkata Narasimha Rao and others.
218.tq: Identify the founders of a specific local organisation.

218.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalukova Satyagraha:
1. It took place in 1938.
2. It was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao.
3. It concerned a paddy wage of 80 seers per acre.
4. The Sub-Collector made the zamindar pay.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: All four statements are correct. The 1938 Kalukova Satyagraha was led by Nanduri Prasada Rao over the 80-seers-per-acre paddy wage, and the Sub-Collector compelled the zamindar to pay.
218.tq: Verify the date, leader, demand and administrative outcome as one event cluster.

218.s: The Brahmaiah Award in the Munagala struggle was issued on:
218.x: Gottipati Brahmaiah mediated the settlement and issued the Brahmaiah Award on 15 January 1939. It covered 142 villages.
218.tq: Distinguish the award date from the later Munagala Day and withdrawal date.

218.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Munagala struggle?
o: Uppala Ramayya led land occupations, and 350 women were lathi-charged.
The struggle ended with the 1938 Kalukova wage settlement alone.
The Brahmaiah Award was accepted permanently by the zamindar.
The zamindari was abolished on 11 June 1939.
218.x: The Brahmaiah Award was broken, after which Uppala Ramayya led land occupations and 350 women were lathi-charged. The zamindari struggle was later withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after assurances by Prakasam and Ranga.
218.tq: Reject the overstatement and identify the documented consequence of the broken award.

218.s: Munagala Day was observed on:
218.x: Munagala Day was observed on 11 June 1939. The struggle was withdrawn on 19 June 1939 after Prakasam and N.G. Ranga promised action.
218.tq: Separate two closely related dates in the same movement.

218.s: The Challapalli zamindari struggle began with the revolt of farmers in Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva in:
218.x: Farmers in Potharlanka, Ghantasala and Movva revolted in June 1930 under the leadership of Gorrepati Venkata Subbayya.
218.tq: Link the opening event of a struggle with its exact year and leader.

218.s:
Which of the following events is correctly matched with the Challapalli zamindari struggle?

1. 1939 — The zamindar grabbed 600 acres of temple land.
2. 1942 — Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya led the struggle.
3. 1946 — Firing over Kishkindapalem land killed four persons.
4. July 1947 — Farmers occupied the zamindar’s surplus land.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: All four statements are correct. Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya were jailed in 1942, while the 1946 firing killed four persons and farmers occupied surplus land in July 1947.
218.tq: Track the sequence of events and test every year–event pair.

218.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was launched by N.G. Ranga on:
218.x: N.G. Ranga launched the Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra on 3 July 1937. Kommareddi Satyanarayana led the yatra.
218.tq: Distinguish the launch date from the alternative 1938–39 dating of the cycle rally.

218.s: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to which national movement?
218.x: The Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra was compared to the Dandi March. It ended with a memorandum submitted to Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy.
218.tq: Use the stated comparison to identify the model movement.

218.s: Who led the Ichchapuram–Madras Rythu Rakshana Yatra after it was launched by N.G. Ranga?
218.x: The yatra was launched by N.G. Ranga on 3 July 1937 and led by Kommareddi Satyanarayana.
218.tq: Distinguish the person who launched an event from the person who led it.

218.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Nuzella (Gudivada) — first peasant meeting — October 1905
2. Venkatagiri — ryot conference — September 1931
3. Nellore — labourers’ meeting under M.N. Roy — 1937
4. Palasa — AIKS session — 1940

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: All four venue–event–year pairs are correct. Nuzella hosted the first peasant meeting in October 1905, while the Palasa AIKS session took place in 1940.
218.tq: Start with the distinctive early date and verify the remaining conference pairs.

218.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First peasant meeting at Nuzella
B. Formation of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham
C. Founding of the All India Kisan Sabha
D. Palasa AIKS session

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: The first peasant meeting at Nuzella was held in 1905, the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was formed in 1928, the AIKS was founded in 1936, and the Palasa session occurred in 1940.
218.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate organisations.

218.s: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in:
218.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was founded in 1928. It merged into the AIKS in 1936.
218.tq: Distinguish the association’s founding year from the years of predecessor bodies and merger.

218.s:
Who among the following were the founders of the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham?

1. N.G. Ranga
2. Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana
3. Maganti Bapineedu
4. B.V. Ratnam

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: N.G. Ranga, Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana and Maganti Bapineedu founded the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham. B.V. Ratnam was its first General Secretary, not a listed founder.
218.tq: Separate founders from the later office-bearers of the organisation.

218.s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham is correct?
o: It was based at Palasa and merged into the AIKS in 1940.
It was based at Lucknow and was founded by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
It was based at Nidubrolu, with B.V. Ratnam as first President.
It was based at Vijayawada, with N.G. Ranga as first President and B.V. Ratnam as first General Secretary.
218.x: The Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham was based at Vijayawada. N.G. Ranga was its first President and B.V. Ratnam its first General Secretary; it merged into the AIKS in 1936.
218.tq: Test headquarters and office-bearers together, guarding against organisational swaps.

218.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents the predecessor ryot associations and their years?

1. Krishna District Rythu Sangham — 1915
2. Guntur and Godavari sanghams — 1923
3. Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham — 1928

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: The Krishna District Rythu Sangham was formed in 1915, the Guntur and Godavari sanghams in 1923, and the Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham in 1928.
218.tq: Arrange related organisations by their stated formation years.

218.s: Which of the following is a journal associated with N.G. Ranga?
218.x: Praja Bandhu and Navayuga were associated with Ranga, while Zamin Ryot was published from Nellore and Prajavani from Vizag. Thus all three listed journals are associated with the movement, though not all with Ranga personally.
218.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after checking the publication association of each item.

218.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Journal)
a. Praja Bandhu
b. Navayuga
c. Zamin Ryot
d. Prajavani

List-II (Association)
i. Vizag
 ii. Ranga
 iii. Nellore
 iv. Ranga

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
218.x: Praja Bandhu and Navayuga were Ranga’s journals, Zamin Ryot was associated with Nellore, and Prajavani with Vizag.
218.tq: Start from the sure location pairs and complete the repeated Ranga association.

218.s: The Union Cabinet extended the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme up to which financial year?
218.x: The Union Cabinet extended PM-KISAN up to 2030–31.
218.tq: Use the exact terminal year to distinguish closely spaced policy periods.

218.s: What outlay was provided for the extended period of the PM-KISAN scheme?
218.x: The extended PM-KISAN scheme has an outlay of Rs 3.15 lakh crore.
218.tq: Identify the precise financial figure rather than relying on approximate magnitude.

218.s: Under PM-KISAN, eligible farmers continue to receive annually:
218.x: PM-KISAN provides Rs 6,000 per year to eligible farmers in three instalments.
218.tq: Separate the scheme’s central annual benefit from state-level supplementary assistance.

218.s: In May 2026, the first 2026 kharif instalment under Annadata Sukhibhava, in conjunction with PM-KISAN, was paid in Andhra Pradesh at the rate of:
218.x: Andhra Pradesh paid Rs 7,000 per farmer as the first 2026 kharif instalment under Annadata Sukhibhava with PM-KISAN.
218.tq: Distinguish the state-linked payment from the standard PM-KISAN annual amount.

218.s: Approximately how many farmers received the first 2026 kharif instalment under Annadata Sukhibhava with PM-KISAN in Andhra Pradesh?
218.x: The payment was made to 46.85 lakh farmers in Andhra Pradesh.
218.tq: Read the decimal figure carefully when numerical options differ by a constant interval.

218.s: The All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) protested police action at Hansi in:
218.x: AIKS protested police action at Hansi, Haryana, on 16 August 2026.
218.tq: Match the organisation with the specific location of its reported activity.

218.s: On which date did the AIKS protest police action at Hansi, Haryana?
218.x: The protest at Hansi, Haryana, was reported on 16 August 2026.
218.tq: Discriminate between nearby dates associated with different contemporary developments.

218.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the demands associated with peasant movements in Andhra:
1. Demand for Minimum Support Price was included.
2. Demand for minimum wages was included.
3. Abolition of zamindari was demanded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
218.x: The demands included MSP, minimum wages and zamindari abolition; therefore, all three statements are correct.
218.tq: Check whether all items belong to the same demand cluster before selecting the complete combination.

218.s: N. G. Ranga’s memorandum to the Whitley Commission in 1929 primarily reflected the demand for:
218.x: N. G. Ranga’s 1929 memorandum to the Whitley Commission raised the demand for minimum wages.
218.tq: Link the document, year and demand instead of confusing it with other agrarian demands.

218.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Nidubrolu — India’s first peasant training institute
Hansi — First peasant training institute in India
Nidubrolu — Place of the Whitley Commission in 1929
218.x: Nidubrolu was India’s first peasant training institute. The Whitley Commission memorandum was associated with N. G. Ranga in 1929, while Hansi and Mandasa refer to other developments.
218.tq: Start with the sure place–institution pair and eliminate the swapped associations.

218.s: Who died in jail after the Mandasa protest?
o: A leader of the AIKS at Hansi
218.x: Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao died in jail after the Mandasa protest.
218.tq: Match the individual with the specific consequence and event rather than with a similar agrarian association.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revolt)
a. Santhal Hul
b. Munda Ulgulan
c. Kol/Larka rising
d. Khond rising

List-II (Leader)
i. Chakra Bisoi
ii. Birsa Munda
iii. Budhu Bhagat
iv. Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
219.x: Santhal Hul was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, Munda Ulgulan by Birsa Munda, the Kol rising by Budhu Bhagat and the Khond rising by Chakra Bisoi.
219.tq: Start from the sure leader–revolt pairs and eliminate the codes.

219.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
219.x: The Bhil rising occurred in Khandesh, in present-day Maharashtra. Bhumij was associated with Manbhum, Tamar with Tamar in Jharkhand and Paika with Khurda in Odisha.
219.tq: Use the region column to distinguish closely related tribal revolts.

219.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bhumij rising — Ganga Narayan
2. Paika Rebellion — Bakshi Jagabandhu
3. Ramosi uprising — Chittur Singh, Umaji Naik and Bapu Trimbakji Sawant
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
219.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Ganga Narayan led the Bhumij rising, Bakshi Jagabandhu led the Paika Rebellion and the listed leaders were associated with the Ramosi uprisings.
219.tq: Check each leader against the corresponding revolt before selecting the coded combination.

219.s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
219.x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.
219.tq: Test the tribe–region association rather than relying only on the revolt name.

219.s: The British invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the Rajmahal Hills primarily after they had failed to control the:
219.x: The British were unable to control the Paharias of the Rajmahal Hills and therefore invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the area.
219.tq: Identify the immediate colonial administrative response to resistance in the Rajmahal Hills.

219.s: The tract in the Rajmahal Hills demarcated for Santhal settlement was known as:
219.x: The tract demarcated for Santhal settlement and cultivation was called Damin-i-Koh. Kolhan was associated with the administration of the Kol region.
219.tq: Use exact administrative terminology to distinguish neighbouring tribal regions.

219.s: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on:
219.x: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855, observed as Hul Divas.
219.tq: Treat the place and exact date as a paired chronology clue.

219.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Santhal Hul:
1. About 30,000 Santhals proclaimed Santhal Raj.
2. The revolt was crushed in 1856.
3. More than 15,000 Santhals were killed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: All three statements are correct. The movement involved about 30,000 Santhals, was crushed in 1856 and caused more than 15,000 deaths.
219.tq: Verify the numerical and outcome statements together before choosing the coded option.

219.s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing
219.x: Chand and Bhairav, along with the sisters Phulo and Jhano, were associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul.
219.tq: Distinguish members of one revolt’s leadership from leaders of other tribal movements.

219.s: Which one of the following was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
o: Oppression by zamindars, moneylenders and police
The abolition of the Khuntkatti system by the Santhals themselves
The transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
The introduction of bonded labour in Mewar
219.x: The Santhals faced oppression by zamindars, moneylenders, commonly called dikus, and the police. The Khuntkatti issue belonged principally to the Munda movement.
219.tq: Match the cause with the revolt instead of the similarly worded causes of other movements.

219.s: After the Santhal Hul, which one of the following developments took place?
o: Santhal Parganas became a separate district with special laws protecting tribal land.
Upper Assam was restored to the Santhal leaders.
The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was enacted in 1876.
Kolhan was placed under the Munda-Manki system immediately after the Ulgulan.
219.x: After the Hul, Santhal Parganas was created as a separate district and special laws were introduced to protect tribal land. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act came later, in 1908.
219.tq: Find the correct post-revolt administrative consequence among closely related outcomes.

219.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is dated to 1876 in the cited chronology.
2. The current Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is from 1949.
3. Santhal Parganas was created before the Santhal Hul.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: The 1876 date is associated with the Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act and the current Act is from 1949. Santhal Parganas was created after the Hul, so statement 3 is false.
219.tq: Spot the reversed before–after relationship in the third statement.

219.s: Birsa Munda was born in:
219.x: Birsa Munda was born in 1875. He led the Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
219.tq: Separate the leader’s birth year from the years of his movement and its legal consequence.

219.s: Birsa Munda’s religious movement, which blended Munda tradition with Hinduism and Christianity, was known as:
219.x: Birsa Munda founded the monotheist Birsait faith, which blended elements of Munda tradition, Hinduism and Christianity.
219.tq: Use the exact name of the reform movement to distinguish it from later Bhil and Oraon movements.

219.s: Which one of the following was NOT part of Birsa Munda’s social and religious reform programme?
o: Opposition to animal sacrifice and spirit worship
Promotion of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system
219.x: Birsa’s programme opposed liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice and spirit worship and promoted a monotheist faith. Khuntkatti was a landholding system whose destruction helped cause the revolt; it was not a religious reform practice.
219.tq: Find the option that changes a land-rights issue into a reform practice.

219.s: The immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda’s revolt was the destruction of the:
219.x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.
219.tq: Identify the precise institution affected instead of choosing a general tribal-administration term.

219.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ulgulan:
1. It took place during 1899–1900.
2. Its objective included Abua Raj, or self-rule.
3. About 6,000 Mundas participated in it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: The Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, aimed at Abua Raj and involved about 6,000 Mundas.
219.tq: Combine date, objective and participation figures in a single movement profile.

219.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the final phase of Birsa Munda’s life?
o: He was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
He was captured in June 1900 and died in Bhognadih jail in February 1901.
He surrendered in 1899 and died in Khurda jail in 1908.
He was executed in 1905 after the enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act.
219.x: Birsa Munda was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
219.tq: Use the sequence of capture, imprisonment and death to reject swapped dates and places.

219.s: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, associated with the consequences of the Ulgulan, is significant because it:
o: introduced the Eki movement in Mewar
created the Santhal Parganas as a separate district
handed Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights
219.x: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights.
219.tq: Infer the legal purpose from the land-rights grievance behind the movement.

219.s: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is observed on 15 November in connection with the birth anniversary of:
219.x: 15 November, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
219.tq: Link the commemorative date with the correct tribal leader.

219.s: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in:
219.x: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in Khurda in present-day Odisha.
219.tq: Use the revolt–region association to distinguish Paika, Santhal, Bhil and Eki movements.

219.s:
Which of the following was a major grievance of the Paikas in 1817?
1. Loss of rent-free lands after the British conquest of 1803
2. Salt policy and revenue burdens

1948 — Prajasakti was founded as the first Andhra Communist unit
1946 — Chief Minister Prakasam arrested communist leaders
222.x: Chief Minister Prakasam arrested communist leaders in 1946. Prajasakti was banned in 1948, while the All-India ban had already been lifted in 1942.
222.tq: Check the authority and year together, using swapped action-and-date combinations as the trap.

222.s: In 1934, communists met secretly in whose garden at Vijayawada and formed a seven-member committee with P. Sundarayya as secretary?
222.x: The secret meeting took place in Katragadda Narayana Rao's garden at Vijayawada in 1934, where a seven-member committee was formed with P. Sundarayya as secretary.
222.tq: Combine the precise place, organiser and committee detail to identify the correct founding episode.

222.s: Amir Haider Khan's Young Workers League contributed to the communist movement in Andhra by
o: leading the Join Indian Union movement
222.x: Amir Haider Khan's Young Workers League, formed in 1929, recruited P. Sundarayya and provided an early organisational root of the communist movement in Andhra.
222.tq: Link the organisation, year and individual recruited to identify the movement's early roots.

222.s: The first communist unit in Telangana was the Hyderabad State Comrades Association, formed in
222.x: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association, regarded as Telangana's first communist unit, was formed in 1939. Its members included Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Raj Bahadur Gour and Syed Ibrahim.
222.tq: Use the sequence of early communist milestones to distinguish the first Telangana unit from the Andhra party's formation.

222.s: The third Communist conference held at Vijayawada in July 1943 was significant because it was
o: the first open conference, with Chandra Rajeswara Rao as secretary
the conference at which the CPI split occurred
the first secret meeting of communists in Andhra
the meeting at which the Comrades Association was formed
222.x: The third Communist conference at Vijayawada in July 1943 was the first open conference, and Chandra Rajeswara Rao served as secretary.
222.tq: Use the conference number and its distinctive organisational feature to reject neighbouring conference details.

222.s: The Visalandhra Maha Sabha held at Hyderabad in July 1956 resulted in the
o: merger of the Andhra and Telangana communist units
formation of the Hyderabad State Congress
imposition of the All-India CPI ban
formation of the Hyderabad State Comrades Association
222.x: The Visalandhra Maha Sabha at Hyderabad in July 1956 resulted in the merger of the Andhra and Telangana communist units.
222.tq: Identify the organisational merger linked to the 1956 Visalandhra event rather than confusing it with earlier party formation milestones.

222.s:
Consider the following statements about the 1964 split in the communist movement:
1. The CPI side included Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
2. The CPI(M) side included P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah.
3. The CPI side was associated with a pro-Soviet position, while the CPI(M) side was associated with a pro-China position.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: All three statements are correct. Ravi Narayana Reddy and Chandra Rajeswara Rao remained with the CPI, while P. Sundarayya and Basavapunnaiah went with the CPI(M); the two sides were identified respectively with pro-Soviet and pro-China positions.
222.tq: Match both leaders and ideological alignments before selecting the complete set of correct statements.

222.s: Who taught at the Kothapatnam political summer school?
o: Ravi Narayana Reddy and K.V. Ranga Reddy
Swami Ramananda Tirtha and Darsi Chenchaiah
222.x: N.G. Ranga and others taught at the Kothapatnam political summer school in 1937.
222.tq: Identify the organisers or teachers associated with the named educational initiative rather than leaders of unrelated political bodies.

222.s: Which of the following places was NOT listed as another location associated with the political summer-school activity besides Kothapatnam?
222.x: Tulluru, Nidubrolu and Mantena vari Palem were listed along with Kothapatnam in connection with the summer-school activity. Kakinada was associated with the formal establishment of the Andhra Communist Party and a youth league meeting.
222.tq: Separate locations belonging to the summer-school network from places linked to party formation or youth organisations.

222.s: The Kalukova Satyagraha was associated with which of the following places?
222.x: The Kalukova Satyagraha was conducted at Munagala in 1938.
222.tq: Use the place-name association to distinguish the three communist-led peasant struggles.

222.s: Who among the following led the communist mobilisation at Munagala during the Kalukova Satyagraha?
222.x: Nanduri Prasada Rao led the Munagala struggle, which was backed by Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
222.tq: Apply the leader–movement association carefully; nearby leaders belong to other struggles.

222.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the peasant struggle at Kalipatnam:
1. It took place in West Godavari.
2. It occurred during 1938–39.
3. Sundarayya and Kommareddy opposed the requirement that satyagrahas should obtain prior permission from the Congress rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: All three statements are correct. The Kalipatnam struggle in West Godavari occurred in 1938–39 and involved opposition by Sundarayya and Kommareddy to prior-permission requirements.
222.tq: Check the place, period and specific political issue separately before selecting the combined option.

222.s: The Challapalli peasant struggle of 1942 was associated with which pair of communist leaders?
o: Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
222.x: The Challapalli struggle in Krishna district in 1942 was led by Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya, who was jailed.
222.tq: Use the leader–place pairing and avoid swapping leaders between neighbouring struggles.

222.s: Which of the following correctly describes Navasakti?
o: It was the first officially recognised CPI publication in India.
It was a weekly begun in 1942 and edited by Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao.
It was a daily published from Vijayawada from 22 June 1952 and inaugurated by Tapi Dharma Rao.
It was the first Telugu communist paper, published from Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937, with Chandra Rajeswara Rao as editor.
222.x: Navasakti was the first Telugu communist paper. It was published from Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937 and edited by Chandra Rajeswara Rao.
222.tq: Combine the journal’s identity, place, date and editor instead of relying on a single name.

222.s:
With reference to Prajasakti, consider the following statements:
1. It was a weekly in 1942.
2. It became a daily in 1945.
3. It was banned in 1948.
4. Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao was identified as its editor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: Prajasakti was a weekly in 1942, became a daily in 1945, was banned in 1948, and was edited by Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao. Garimella Krishnamurthy is also named in one reference list in connection with its editorship.
222.tq: Track the publication’s changing periodicity, ban year and editor as separate factual clues.

222.s: Which one of the following combinations is correct regarding Visalandhra?
222.x: Visalandhra was a daily published from Vijayawada from 22 June 1952 and was inaugurated by Tapi Dharma Rao.
222.tq: Start with the sure journal–place pair and then verify the date and inauguration detail.

222.s: Who wrote the work *Visalandhralo Prajarajyam* in 1946?
222.x: P. Sundarayya wrote *Visalandhralo Prajarajyam* in 1946.
222.tq: Distinguish the author of the ideological work from editors and inaugurators of communist journals.

222.s: Which of the following statements regarding the communist position on Visalandhra is correct?
o: The communists were the first to demand Visalandhra in 1946 and initiated the movement.
The communists opposed the formation of linguistic states from the beginning.
The demand for Visalandhra was first raised only after 1955.
The communists supported Visalandhra but did not participate in its movement.
222.x: The communists were the first to demand Visalandhra in 1946 and started the movement. They did not oppose linguistic states.
222.tq: Reject reversed or delayed chronology and distinguish support for linguistic states from opposition to them.

222.s: Praja Natya Mandali was primarily established as which of the following?
o: A constitutional body for local self-government
A communist cultural front for propagating ideas through drama, songs and folk forms
A peasant tribunal for settling tenancy disputes
A journal-editing committee of the CPI
222.x: Praja Natya Mandali was a communist cultural front that spread its ideas through drama, songs and folk forms.
222.tq: Identify an organisation from its function and method of mobilisation rather than from its name alone.

222.s: The best-known play associated with Praja Natya Mandali was:
222.x: *Maa Bhoomi* was the best-known play associated with Praja Natya Mandali.
222.tq: Separate the title of a cultural production from the title of a political work or movement.

222.s: Who were associated with the authorship of *Maa Bhoomi*?
o: Maddukuri Chandrasekhara Rao and Tapi Dharma Rao
Chandra Rajeswara Rao and Peta Chapanayya
Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao
222.x: *Maa Bhoomi* was written by Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao.
222.tq: Apply the author–work association and avoid swapping cultural figures with communist leaders or editors.

222.s: Which folk form constituted the main folk medium of Praja Natya Mandali?
222.x: Burrakatha was the main folk form used by Praja Natya Mandali.
222.tq: Use the exact traditional art form rather than a broadly related cultural performance.

222.s: The political significance of communist activity in Andhra is best expressed by which of the following statements?
o: It confined Andhra politics exclusively to cultural questions.
It shifted the main focus of Andhra politics from language to land.
It ended peasant mobilisation in Andhra.
It rejected the demand for Visalandhra.
222.x: The communists shifted Andhra politics from language to land through peasant mobilisation, while their social base also helped drive the Visalandhra movement.
222.tq: Identify the central political transition rather than a consequence that reverses the communist role.

222.s: In the 1952 elections, communist candidates won how many of the 145 seats in the Andhra region?
222.x: The communist base carried the party to 41 of the 145 Andhra-region seats in 1952.
222.tq: Separate the number of seats won from the total number of seats and from the later 1955 result.

222.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. CPI split
B. CPI ban lifted
C. CPI ban imposed
D. Labour Kisan Gazette identified as the first officially recognised CPI publication in India
222.x: The CPI was banned in 1934, the ban was lifted in 1942, the party split in 1964, and the Labour Kisan Gazette is identified in the 2026 current-affairs material as the first officially recognised CPI publication in India.
222.tq: Fix the dated political milestones first and place the later current-affairs reference last.

222.s: The CPI was banned in 1934, and the ban was lifted in:
222.x: The CPI ban imposed in 1934 was lifted in 1942.
222.tq: Distinguish the national CPI ban chronology from the separate bans concerning regional organisations.

222.s: What was one political consequence of the CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and its opposition to the Quit India Movement?
o: It cost the CPI the 1945–46 elections.
It helped the CPI win the 1945–46 elections decisively.
It led immediately to the CPI split in 1964.
It resulted in the formation of Praja Natya Mandali.
222.x: The CPI’s ‘People’s War’ line and opposition to the Quit India Movement cost it the 1945–46 elections.
222.tq: Match the political line and wartime position with their stated electoral consequence.

222.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the first Andhra State ministry under Prakasam:
1. It fell on 15 November 1954.
2. Its fall followed communist-led agitation.
3. The CPI won 41 of 196 seats in the 1955 elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
222.x: The Prakasam ministry fell on 15 November 1954 after communist-led agitation. Statement 3 is false: the CPI won only 15 of 196 seats in 1955, not 41.
222.tq: Use the changed figure as the trap and compare the 1952 and 1955 electoral numbers carefully.

222.s: The CPI won how many seats out of 196 in the 1955 elections referred to in the Andhra political context?
222.x: The CPI won only 15 of the 196 seats in the 1955 elections.
222.tq: Do not transfer the 1952 Andhra-region figure of 41 to the different 1955 total of 196 seats.

223.s: The Communal Award of 1932 was announced by Ramsay MacDonald primarily after the failure of which event to resolve the issue of minority representation?
o: The Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress
223.x: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award in August 1932 after the Second Round Table Conference failed to reach agreement on minority representation.
223.tq: Link the announcement to its immediate political background.

223.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Communal Award of 1932:
1. It divided Indians into 11 groups for purposes of representation.
2. It recognised the Depressed Classes as a minority.
3. It provided separate electorates only for Muslims and Sikhs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: The Award divided Indians into 11 groups and treated the Depressed Classes as a minority. Separate electorates were also provided for Europeans, Indian Christians and Anglo-Indians, among others; therefore statement 3 is false.
223.tq: Find the over-restrictive statement in a list of provisions.

223.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the groups for which separate electorates were provided under the Communal Award?
223.x: The Award provided separate electorates for Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and the Depressed Classes. Labour, landlords, traders and industrialists received representation, but industrial workers were not included among the separate-electorate groups listed here.
223.tq: Separate the groups receiving separate electorates from occupational interests receiving seats.

223.s: Under the Communal Award, what special electoral arrangement was provided to the Depressed Classes?
o: Two votes restricted to the separate electorate
A single vote in the general electorate only
No vote, but nomination to provincial legislatures
A double vote in a separate electorate and the general electorate
223.x: The Depressed Classes were given a double vote: one in a separate electorate and another in the general electorate.
223.tq: Test the exact mechanism rather than merely the existence of separate electorates.

223.s:
With reference to the Communal Award, consider the following statements:
1. Three per cent of the seats in all provinces, except the North-West Frontier Province, were earmarked for women.
2. The Award dealt only with religious communities and made no provision for occupational interests.
3. Seats were also provided for labour, landlords, traders and industrialists.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: Three per cent of seats were reserved for women in all provinces except the North-West Frontier Province. The Award also included occupational interests such as labour, landlords, traders and industrialists, making statement 2 false.
223.tq: Pair a numerical exception with the correct list of beneficiaries.

223.s: Mahatma Gandhi began his fast unto death against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes on:
223.x: Gandhi began the fast on 20 September 1932 in Yerwada Jail, Poona, opposing separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.
223.tq: Distinguish the Award date, Pact date and fast date.

223.s: Why did Gandhi oppose separate electorates for the Depressed Classes under the Communal Award?
o: He believed they would permanently divide Hindu society.
He opposed any form of political representation for the Depressed Classes.
He believed they would abolish all caste distinctions immediately.
He wanted the British Parliament to nominate all their representatives.
223.x: Gandhi argued that separate electorates for Dalits would permanently divide Hindu society. His opposition was not to representation itself but to a separate electorate.
223.tq: Identify the underlying political reasoning behind a historical action.

223.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of the Indian National Congress on the Communal Award?
o: It formally accepted the Award in its entirety.
It formally rejected every provision of the Award.
It neither accepted nor rejected the Award.
It accepted separate electorates but rejected reserved seats.
223.x: The Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Communal Award as a whole.
223.tq: Watch for the middle position between complete acceptance and rejection.

223.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gandhi — Harijan
2. Ambedkar — Dalit/Scheduled Castes
3. Gandhi — Legal and constitutional rights as the principal method
4. Ambedkar — Separate electorates
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
223.x: Gandhi used the term Harijan and emphasised moral persuasion, temple entry and constructive work. Ambedkar used Dalit/Scheduled Castes and advocated legal, constitutional and political rights including separate electorates; pair 3 is therefore false.
223.tq: Match each leader with his terminology and method, not merely his objective.

223.s: Which of the following best represents Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?
o: Political power was necessary to protect their interests.
Political power could be secured only through religious conversion.
Political power should remain exclusively with caste Hindus.
Political power was irrelevant because social reform alone was sufficient.
223.x: Ambedkar held that political power was necessary for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves and secure their rights.
223.tq: Test the central argument associated with a political thinker.

223.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Ambedkar's later assessment of the Poona Pact?
o: It replaced joint electorates with separate electorates.
It made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus.
It abolished all reserved representation for Dalits.
It made Dalits independent of caste Hindus in political matters.
223.x: Ambedkar later felt that the Pact made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus, although he had accepted joint electorates during the negotiations.
223.tq: Distinguish the immediate acceptance of an arrangement from its later evaluation.

223.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the electorates under the Communal Award and the Poona Pact?
o: The Award provided separate electorates with a general vote, while the Pact provided joint electorates with reserved seats.
The Award provided joint electorates, while the Pact provided separate electorates.
Both provided separate electorates with no reserved seats.
Neither made any provision for representation of the Depressed Classes.
223.x: The Communal Award provided a separate electorate along with a general vote, whereas the Poona Pact replaced this with joint electorates and reserved seats.
223.tq: Compare the operative electoral mechanism rather than the political controversy.

223.s: In addition to reserved representation, the Poona Pact promised:
o: Separate electorates for all occupational groups
Fair representation in civil services and a share of educational grants
Complete transfer of education to local bodies
223.x: The Pact promised fair representation for the Depressed Classes in civil services and a share of education grants.
223.tq: Test the less frequently recalled accompanying provisions of an agreement.

223.s: The Poona Pact was signed at Yerwada, Poona, in September 1932. Which date is associated with its signing in the standard account?
223.x: The standard account places the signing of the Poona Pact on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada, Poona.
223.tq: Separate the date of the fast from the date of the agreement that ended it.

223.s: Which sequence correctly represents the development of Ambedkar's major organisations and movement?
o: Scheduled Castes Federation — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Independent Labour Party — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Independent Labour Party — Scheduled Castes Federation
Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Scheduled Castes Federation — Independent Labour Party
Independent Labour Party — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Scheduled Castes Federation
223.x: The sequence is Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924, Kalaram Temple Satyagraha in 1930, Independent Labour Party in 1936 and Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942.
223.tq: Use the dates to fix the first and last events before arranging the middle pair.

223.s: The Independent Labour Party, associated with B.R. Ambedkar, was established in:
223.x: Ambedkar's Independent Labour Party was established in 1936.
223.tq: Reject the nearby movement dates and identify the exact organisational year.

223.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: All India Depressed Classes Association — M.C. Rajah
223.x: M.C. Rajah was associated with the All India Depressed Classes Association. The Scheduled Castes Federation was established in 1942, the Independent Labour Party in 1936, and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded by Ambedkar.
223.tq: Use a sure leader–organisation pair to eliminate swapped dates and founders.

223.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. V.R. Shinde — Depressed Classes Mission
2. Bhagya Reddy Varma — Jagan Mitra Mandali
3. B.R. Ambedkar — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
4. Jyotiba Phule — Harijan Sevak Sangh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
223.x: V.R. Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission, Bhagya Reddy Varma founded Jagan Mitra Mandali, and Ambedkar founded Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha. Harijan Sevak Sangh was the renamed form of the All India Anti-Untouchability League, not an organisation founded by Phule.
223.tq: Detect the founder substituted with a prominent but unrelated reformer.

223.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the year of establishment?
223.x: Jagan Mitra Mandali was established by Bhagya Reddy Varma in 1906. Satyashodhak Samaj dates to 1873, the Depressed Classes Mission to 1906, and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha to 1924.
223.tq: Match the organisation with its exact year while screening nearby dates.

223.s: The Mahad Satyagraha of 20 March 1927 was organised at which place?
223.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha organised the Mahad Satyagraha at the Chawdar Tank on 20 March 1927.
223.tq: Match a movement with its specific site rather than its leader alone.

223.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Gandhi's Andhra tour of 1932–33?
o: It collected Harijana Bhiksha and included a temple-entry initiative at Siddhantam.
It organised the Coolie Sangham exclusively for industrialists.
It established the Scheduled Castes Federation at Siddhantam.
It launched the Civil Disobedience Movement at Vizianagaram.
223.x: During his 1932–33 Andhra tour, Gandhi collected Harijana Bhiksha and launched temple entry at Siddhantam in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
223.tq: Combine the purpose, local campaign and place of a regional tour.

223.s: The Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour was organised by:
223.x: The communists organised the Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour.
223.tq: Identify the organisation by the political group associated with its formation.

223.s:
Consider the following statements about journals associated with the Depressed Classes movement:
1. Mooknayak was associated with Ambedkar.
2. Bahishkrit Bharat was associated with Ambedkar.
3. Harijan was a weekly journal associated with Gandhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: All three statements are correct. Mooknayak was published in 1920, Bahishkrit Bharat in 1927, and Harijan was Gandhi's weekly journal from 1933.
223.tq: Confirm a complete set of leader–journal associations before selecting the inclusive code.

223.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional history of the term 'Scheduled Castes' is correct?
o: It was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list came in 1936.
It was first used in the Communal Award and abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935.
It was first used by Gandhi in 1932 and legally defined in 1942.
It was first used in the Poona Pact and listed in 1950.
223.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.
223.tq: Arrange the institutional stages of a constitutional term in sequence.

223.s: Article 17 of the Constitution is significant in the context of the Depressed Classes movement because it:
o: Provided separate electorates for Scheduled Castes
223.x: Article 17 abolished untouchability and prohibited its practice in any form.
223.tq: Match a constitutional Article with its precise subject.

223.s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
223.x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.
223.tq: Identify the institutional feature that carried forward into the Constitution.

224.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were named after which two officials?
224.x: The reforms were named after Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy of India.
224.tq: Use the name-to-office association to distinguish similarly named constitutional reforms.

224.s: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in which month and year?
224.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report was announced in July 1918; it subsequently formed the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
224.tq: Separate the report date from the declaration date and the Act date.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional status of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
o: They were rules framed exclusively by the Viceroy's Executive Council.
They were recommendations of the Indian National Congress alone.
They were an Act of the UK Parliament.
They were a royal proclamation establishing the Chamber of Princes.
224.x: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals were enacted through the Government of India Act, 1919, an Act of the UK Parliament.
224.tq: Identify the correct constitutional source instead of confusing proposals with executive rules.

224.s:
With reference to dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919, consider the following statements:
1. It was introduced in the provinces.
2. It divided provincial subjects into reserved and transferred subjects.
3. It made the provincial budget independent of the central budget.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces, provincial subjects were divided into reserved and transferred categories, and the provincial budget was separated from the central budget.
224.tq: Check whether each feature belongs to provincial dyarchy rather than to the later provincial autonomy scheme.

224.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Reserved subjects — Governor and Executive Council — not answerable to the legislature
Reserved subjects — elected ministers — answerable to the legislature
Transferred subjects — Governor alone — not answerable to the legislature
Transferred subjects — Secretary of State — answerable to Parliament only
224.x: Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and his Executive Council and were not answerable to the provincial legislature.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair linking reserved subjects with the Governor and Executive Council.

224.s:
