Under the dyarchical arrangement, which of the following were transferred subjects?
1. Education
2. Health
3. Local self-government
4. Law and order
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Education, health and local self-government were transferred subjects administered by ministers responsible to the legislature. Law and order was a reserved subject.
224.tq: Find the one reserved subject and eliminate the option that includes it.

224.s: A provincial minister responsible to the elected legislature was most likely to administer which of the following under the Government of India Act, 1919?
224.x: Education was a transferred subject administered by a Governor's minister drawn from the elected legislature and answerable to it.
224.tq: Apply the institutional relationship to identify a transferred subject.

224.s: The central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919 was:
o: Bicameral, consisting of the Chamber of Princes and the Federal Court
Bicameral, consisting of the Council of State and the Legislative Assembly
Unicameral, consisting only of nominated members
Tricameral, consisting of the Council of State, Legislative Assembly and Provincial Council
224.x: The Act introduced a bicameral central legislature comprising the Council of State as the upper chamber and the Legislative Assembly as the lower chamber.
224.tq: Match the constitutional arrangement with the exact names of its two chambers.

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the central legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Legislative Assembly had 145 members.
2. Of the members of the Legislative Assembly, 104 were elected.
3. The Council of State had 60 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: The Legislative Assembly had 145 members, including 104 elected members, while the Council of State had 60 members.
224.tq: Verify each numerical detail separately before selecting the combined code.

224.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, how many members of the Viceroy's Executive Council, excluding the Commander-in-Chief, were to be Indians?
224.x: Three of the six members of the Viceroy's Executive Council, other than the Commander-in-Chief, were to be Indians.
224.tq: Distinguish the specified six-member group from the separately excluded Commander-in-Chief.

224.s:
Which of the following communities were included when communal representation was extended under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms?
1. Sikhs
2. Indian Christians
3. Anglo-Indians
4. Europeans
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Communal representation was extended beyond Muslims to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
224.tq: Treat the complete community list as a composition question and check every member.

224.s: The franchise under the Government of India Act, 1919 was primarily based on:
o: Religious identity and nomination by the Governor
224.x: The franchise remained limited and was based on qualifications relating to property, taxation and education.
224.tq: Reject the universal-suffrage trap and identify the three stated qualifications.

224.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: Direct elections to the central legislature
Creation of the office of High Commissioner for India in London
Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget
Provincial autonomy in place of dyarchy
224.x: Provincial autonomy was associated with the Government of India Act, 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces, along with the other listed features.
224.tq: Use the later 1935 feature as the chronological trap in a NOT question.

224.s: The gradual introduction of responsible government in India was associated with the declaration of:
224.x: Montagu's August Declaration of 20 August 1917 stated the policy of the gradual introduction of responsible government in India.
224.tq: Separate the August Declaration date from the later report and reform dates.

224.s: The provision for establishing a Public Service Commission in India was contained in which section of the Government of India Act, 1919?
224.x: Section 96(C) of the Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of a Public Service Commission in India.
224.tq: Use exact-section recall, a common constitutional-provision trap.

224.s: The Public Service Commission provided for under the Government of India Act, 1919 was set up on:
224.x: The Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, after the Lee Commission.
224.tq: Distinguish the statutory provision in 1919 from the body's establishment in 1926.

224.s: Which one of the following was created under the Government of India Act, 1919 as a consultative body of Indian rulers?
224.x: The Chamber of Princes, also known as Narendra Mandal, was created as a consultative body of rulers under the 1919 reforms.
224.tq: Match the body's function with its institutional identity rather than its legislative name.

224.s: The Chamber of Princes, or Narendra Mandal, was set up in:
224.x: The Chamber of Princes was set up in 1921 by royal proclamation under the framework of the 1919 reforms.
224.tq: Keep the reform year distinct from the year in which the associated body was established.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Office-holder)
a. Frederick Whyte
a. Sachchidananda Sinha
c. Vithalbhai Patel
List-II (Position)
i. First elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly
ii. First Deputy President
iii. First President

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President, Sachchidananda Sinha the first Deputy President, and Vithalbhai Patel the first elected Indian President.
224.tq: Start from the distinctive pair Vithalbhai Patel–first elected Indian President and complete the matching.

224.s: Who became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925?
224.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the first elected Indian President of the Legislative Assembly in 1925.
224.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the first elected Indian holder of the office.

224.s: Frederick Whyte and Sachchidananda Sinha were respectively associated with which offices?
o: First elected Indian President and first Chief Minister of Madras
First President and first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly
High Commissioner for India and first President of the Legislative Assembly
First Deputy President and first President of the Council of State
224.x: Frederick Whyte was the first President and Sachchidananda Sinha was the first Deputy President of the Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Separate similar office-holder facts by matching each person to the exact office and status.

224.s: In the Madras elections of 1920, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: Congress boycotted the elections and the Justice Party won 63 seats
The Justice Party boycotted the elections and Congress won 63 seats
Both Congress and the Justice Party boycotted the elections
224.x: The Congress boycotted the 1920 Madras elections as part of the Non-Cooperation movement, while the Justice Party won 63 seats.
224.tq: Pair the political action with the correct party and election result.

224.s: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of which period?
224.x: The Justice Party held office in Madras for most of the period from 1920 to 1937.
224.tq: Use the complete period rather than confusing it with the first ministry's starting year.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections on the basis of:
o: Separate nomination by the Secretary of State
224.x: The Act introduced direct elections, but the franchise remained limited by property, tax and educational qualifications.
224.tq: Combine the electoral method with the qualification-based nature of the franchise.

224.s: Which Act introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates?
224.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 introduced elected non-official members, largely through indirect and separate electorates. Direct elections were associated with the 1919 Act.
224.tq: Discriminate between the 1909 indirect electoral innovation and the 1919 direct elections.

224.s: If an examination question asks for the first Act associated with direct elections in India, which answer is most appropriate?
224.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced direct elections. The 1909 Act introduced elected non-official members mainly through indirect and separate electorates.
224.tq: Resolve a close-option ambiguity by distinguishing direct elections from indirect elections.

224.s:
Match the following Acts with their principal features:
List-I (Act)
a. Regulating Act
b. Pitt's India Act
c. Indian Councils Act, 1909
d. Government of India Act, 1919
List-II (Feature)
i. Provincial dyarchy and central bicameralism
ii. Board of Control and dual control
iii. Governor-General of Bengal and Supreme Court at Calcutta
iv. Separate electorate for Muslims

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: The Regulating Act, 1773 provided for the Governor-General of Bengal and the Supreme Court at Calcutta; Pitt's India Act created the Board of Control; the 1909 Act introduced Muslim separate electorates; and the 1919 Act introduced dyarchy and central bicameralism.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair Regulating Act–Supreme Court at Calcutta and eliminate mismatched codes.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pitt's India Act, 1784 — Board of Control
Regulating Act, 1773 — Supreme Court at Calcutta
Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909 — separate electorate for Muslims
224.x: The 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, not provincial autonomy. Provincial autonomy was a feature of the Government of India Act, 1935.
224.tq: Identify the later constitutional feature wrongly brought into the 1919 framework.

224.s: Which Act is correctly associated with the introduction of dyarchy in the provinces, bicameralism at the Centre and direct elections?
224.x: These three features were introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
224.tq: Recognize the characteristic three-feature combination of the 1919 Act.

224.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Councils Act, 1909 is associated with separate electorates for Muslims.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 is associated with dyarchy in the provinces.
3. The Government of India Act, 1935 prescribed a federation and provincial autonomy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: All three statements are correct: the 1909 Act introduced Muslim separate electorates, the 1919 Act introduced provincial dyarchy, and the 1935 Act provided for federation and provincial autonomy.
224.tq: Map each Act to its signature feature and test the sequence across reforms.

224.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the 1909 and 1919 reforms?
o: The 1919 reforms abolished communal representation introduced in 1909.
The 1909 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates.
The 1909 reforms introduced Muslim separate electorates, whereas the 1919 reforms introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
Both reforms introduced provincial autonomy in the provinces.
224.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, while the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced provincial dyarchy and direct elections.
224.tq: Compare the signature feature of each reform instead of swapping their dates and provisions.

224.s: Who is associated with the description 'Father of the Communal Electorate'?
224.x: Lord Minto is associated with the title 'Father of the Communal Electorate' because the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
224.tq: Link the popular epithet to the reform and Viceroy of the same period.

224.s: The office of High Commissioner for India in London was created by the:
224.x: The Government of India Act, 1919 created the office of High Commissioner for India in London.
224.tq: Match the institutional office with the constitutional Act that created it.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the initial location of the simultaneous ICS examination in India?
224.x: From 1922, the ICS examination was held simultaneously in India at Allahabad and was later conducted at Delhi.
224.tq: Test the sequence of locations rather than recalling only the year.

224.s: The first elections to the Central Legislative Assembly under the Government of India Act, 1919, were held in:
224.x: The first elections under the 1919 constitutional arrangements were held in 1920. The Congress boycotted these elections.
224.tq: Use the exact year rather than confusing the first election with the later Swarajist contest.

224.s: The principal objective of the Swaraj Party in contesting the elections of 1923 was to:
o: Obstruct the working of the legislatures from within
Accept the reforms and cooperate with the government
Demand immediate partition of British India
224.x: The Swaraj Party, led by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, entered the legislatures in order to obstruct colonial governance from within.
224.tq: Identify the political purpose behind entering the legislatures instead of merely recalling the party name.

224.s: With reference to the Swarajists in the elections of 1923, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: They won about 10 per cent of the seats and rejected legislative politics.
They won about 25 per cent of the seats and formed the government at the Centre.
They won about 40 per cent of the seats and demanded a review of the 1919 Act.
They won a majority of all provincial seats and abolished dyarchy.
224.x: The Swarajists secured about 40 per cent of the seats in 1923 and demanded a review of the Government of India Act, 1919.
224.tq: Split the option into the seat share and the associated demand; both details must match.

224.s: The Muddiman Committee of 1924 was appointed in response to the demand of the Swarajists for:
o: A review of the Government of India Act, 1919
224.x: The Muddiman Committee was the British response to the Swarajist demand for a review of the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
224.tq: Link the committee to the demand that caused its appointment.

224.s: Who became the President, or Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly after the Swarajist success in 1923?
224.x: Vithalbhai Patel became the President, commonly described as the Speaker, of the Central Legislative Assembly.
224.tq: Use the office-holder trap by distinguishing the legislative leaders from the presiding officer.

224.s: V. Ramadas was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly from Andhra in:
224.x: V. Ramadas was elected to the Central Legislative Assembly in 1923.
224.tq: Recall the regional candidate together with the election year.

224.s: The elections to the provincial legislatures held in 1937 were followed by which of the following developments?
o: The Congress won in the provinces, while the Centre continued under the 1919 structure.
The federation under the 1935 Act came into operation immediately.
The Swaraj Party returned to the legislatures for the first time.
224.x: The Congress won in the 1937 provincial elections. The Centre continued under the 1919 structure because the proposed federation never came into existence.
224.tq: Test the comparison between provincial implementation and the unformed federal Centre.

224.s: The immediate political pressure that prompted the Montagu Declaration of 20 August 1917 was exerted chiefly by the:
224.x: The Home Rule Leagues created political pressure that contributed to the British declaration recognising self-government as an objective.
224.tq: Identify the immediate political force rather than the later constitutional outcome.

224.s: Montagu and Chelmsford toured India in December 1917 primarily to:
o: Consult Indian opinion on constitutional reforms
Conduct elections to the Central Legislative Assembly
224.x: Montagu and Chelmsford toured India in December 1917 as part of the process of consulting Indian opinion on constitutional reforms.
224.tq: Match the tour with its constitutional-reform context, not with later events.

224.s: A 27-member Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao met Montagu at Madras to demand:
o: A separate Muslim province in South India
Abolition of the Madras Legislative Council
224.x: The Andhra delegation led by Nyapati Subbarao sought the creation of a separate Andhra province.
224.tq: Connect the delegation leader and its regional constitutional demand.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Moderates to the constitutional reforms of 1919?
o: They accepted the reforms and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
They boycotted the reforms and formed the Justice Party.
They joined the Home Rule Leagues and demanded complete independence.
They rejected the reforms and formed the Swaraj Party.
224.x: Surendranath Banerjee and other Moderates accepted the reforms, left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation in 1918.
224.tq: Use the founder-group and organisation pairing to avoid confusing Moderates with Swarajists.

224.s: At the Amritsar Congress of 1919, the reforms were described as:
224.x: The Amritsar Congress characterised the reforms as inadequate, unsatisfactory and disappointing.
224.tq: Recall the exact three-part political assessment used by the Congress.

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra reaction to the reforms of 1919:
1. A special Andhra Mahasabha was held at Guntur on 17 August 1918.
2. It was held under the leadership of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
3. Krishna Patrika described the reforms as giving with the right hand and taking with the left.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: All three statements are correct. The Guntur meeting, its leadership and the Krishna Patrika description reflect the critical Andhra response to the reforms.
224.tq: Check the date, regional leader and exact contemporary description together.

224.s: The official name of the Rowlatt Act was the:
o: Indian Security and Public Order Act, 1919
224.x: The official title of the Rowlatt Act was the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919.
224.tq: Distinguish the popular name from the exact statutory title.

224.s: The Rowlatt Act was passed on:
224.x: The Rowlatt Act was passed on 10 March 1919. 6 April was the date of the Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal, while 13 April was the date of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
224.tq: Separate the dates of enactment, hartal and massacre rather than treating them as one event.

224.s:
Which of the following were provisions of the Rowlatt Act?
1. Arrest and detention without warrant or trial
2. In-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel
3. Right of appeal to the Privy Council in every case
4. Suspension of habeas corpus
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: The Act permitted arrest and detention without warrant or trial, in-camera trials by a three-judge High Court panel and suspension of habeas corpus. It did not provide an appeal in every case.
224.tq: Find the wrong procedural safeguard by testing the exceptional powers against the claimed right of appeal.

224.s: The Rowlatt Act came into existence as an extension of the:
224.x: The Rowlatt legislation extended the extraordinary powers earlier provided under the Defence of India Act, 1915.
224.tq: Distinguish the parent wartime legislation from the later Rowlatt enactment.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi's response to the Rowlatt Act?
o: He accepted the Act and entered the Viceroy's Executive Council.
He formed the Indian National Liberal Federation.
He launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1915.
He launched his first all-India campaign through the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
224.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was Gandhi's first all-India campaign. It was organised through a Satyagraha Sabha and included a hartal on 6 April 1919.
224.tq: Identify the movement by its scale and immediate historical context.

224.s: The Rowlatt Act was repealed during the viceroyalty of:
224.x: The Rowlatt Act was repealed under Lord Reading, along with the Press Act of 1910.
224.tq: Distinguish the viceroy associated with repeal from the one in office when the Act was passed.

224.s: The statutory review provision of the Government of India Act, 1919 required the appointment of a commission after:
224.x: The Act required a statutory commission to review its working after ten years. The Simon Commission was appointed two years early under this provision.
224.tq: Recall the statutory interval and distinguish it from the actual early appointment.

224.s: The Simon Commission was appointed two years before the statutory review period because it was constituted in:
224.x: The Government appointed the Simon Commission in 1927, two years before the ten-year review point prescribed by the 1919 Act.
224.tq: Calculate the early appointment against the ten-year review clause.

224.s: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 by the:
o: Liberal Government under David Lloyd George
224.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 by the Conservative Government headed by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin.
224.tq: Match the commission with the government in power at the time of appointment.

224.s:
With reference to the Simon Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It consisted of seven members.
2. All its members were British.
3. Sir John Simon was its chairman.
4. Clement Attlee was one of its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: The commission had seven members, all British, with Sir John Simon as chairman; Clement Attlee was also a member.
224.tq: Verify composition, nationality, chairmanship and membership before selecting the coded option.

224.s: The Simon Commission was also known as the:
o: Indian Statutory Commission or White Commission
224.x: The Simon Commission was officially associated with the name Indian Statutory Commission and was popularly called the White Commission because it had no Indian member.
224.tq: Distinguish the formal designation from the popular descriptive name.

224.s: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on:
224.x: The Simon Commission arrived at Bombay on 3 February 1928.
224.tq: Separate the appointment year from the year of arrival in India.

224.s: Which one of the following was the correct route of the Simon Commission through Andhra?
224.x: The Andhra route of the Simon Commission was Tenali, Guntur, Vijayawada, Ongole and Madras.
224.tq: Arrange the places in geographical travel sequence rather than selecting isolated locations.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Place)
a. Lahore
b. Madras
c. Lucknow
d. Tenali and Guntur
List-II (Protest leader)
i. Tanguturi Prakasam
ii. G.V. Unnayya Sastri
iii. Lala Lajpat Rai
iv. Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant
224.x: Lahore was associated with Lala Lajpat Rai, Madras with Tanguturi Prakasam, Lucknow with Jawaharlal Nehru and G.B. Pant, and Tenali–Guntur with G.V. Unnayya Sastri.
224.tq: Start from the sure place–leader pair and eliminate codes containing incompatible matches.

224.s: Tanguturi Prakasam acquired the title 'Andhra Kesari' in connection with which incident?
o: Baring his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras
Leading the Home Rule League in Andhra
Leading the boycott of the Rowlatt Act in Guntur
224.x: Tanguturi Prakasam bared his chest before the police during the anti-Simon Commission protest at Madras and became known as Andhra Kesari.
224.tq: Link the title to the distinctive action and place associated with it.

224.s: The lathi charge on Lala Lajpat Rai at Lahore on 30 October 1928 was ordered by:
224.x: The lathi charge was ordered by SP James Scott. Saunders, who is sometimes confused with Scott, was later shot by Bhagat Singh and Rajguru in an act of revenge.
224.tq: Discriminate between the officer who ordered the lathi charge and the officer later targeted in revenge.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the anti-Simon Commission organisation in Andhra?
o: G.V. Unnayya Sastri presided over the committee, while M.A. Ansari toured Andhra.
Bulusu Sambamurthy presided over the committee, while S. Satyamurti toured Punjab.
Tanguturi Prakasam presided over the committee, while Lala Lajpat Rai toured Andhra.
S. Satyamurti presided over the Andhra anti-Simon committee, while Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra for the boycott.
224.x: S. Satyamurti was president of the Andhra anti-Simon committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy toured Andhra to promote the boycott.
224.tq: Avoid the swapped-person trap by matching each leader with the correct organisational role.

224.s:
Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission Report?
1. Abolition of provincial dyarchy
2. Introduction of provincial autonomy
3. Retention of separate electorates
4. Immediate establishment of a responsible federal government at the Centre
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
224.x: The report recommended abolition of provincial dyarchy, provincial autonomy and retention of separate electorates. It did not recommend the immediate establishment of a responsible federal government at the Centre.
224.tq: Find the one proposal that does not belong among the report's actual recommendations.

224.s: The Simon Commission Report recommended the separation of:
o: Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India
Bihar from Bengal and Assam from India
Burma from Bengal and Orissa from Bihar
Andhra from Madras and Sindh from Punjab
224.x: The report recommended separating Sindh from Bombay and Burma from India.
224.tq: Use the paired territorial recommendation rather than confusing it with later provincial reorganisation.

224.s: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the:
224.x: The term 'Scheduled Castes' was first used in the Simon Commission Report.
224.tq: Match the exact constitutional term with the report in which it first appeared.

224.s:
Arrange the following constitutional milestones in chronological order:
A. Nehru Report
B. Partition of Bengal
C. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
224.x: The correct order is Partition of Bengal (1905), Nehru Report (1928), Jinnah's Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931).
224.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest milestones first, then place the 1928 and 1929 developments between them.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1919 — Government of India Act and Rowlatt Act
224.x: The Rowlatt Act and the Government of India Act were both associated with 1919. The Partition of Bengal was in 1905, the Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and the Nehru Report in 1928.
224.tq: Check each year against the constitutional milestone instead of relying on a familiar title alone.

224.s: The Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points were issued in, respectively:
224.x: The Nehru Report was issued in 1928, followed by Jinnah's Fourteen Points in 1929.
224.tq: Distinguish two closely spaced constitutional documents by their consecutive years.

224.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was concluded in:
224.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was concluded in March 1931.
224.tq: Use the month and year to distinguish the pact from the Civil Disobedience events surrounding it.

224.s: Who chaired the committee that prepared the Nehru Report in 1928?
224.x: Motilal Nehru chaired the nine-member committee that drafted the Nehru Report in 1928.
224.tq: Use the person-to-role association and distinguish chairman from secretary.

224.s: The Nehru Report was primarily prepared in response to which of the following?
o: Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution
The demand for a separate Muslim homeland
The failure of the Cripps Mission
224.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in reply to Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame their own constitution.
224.tq: Identify the immediate cause behind a constitutional document.

224.s: Which one of the following was NOT a proposal of the Nehru Report?
224.x: The Nehru Report proposed joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates.
224.tq: Find the reversed feature in a closely related constitutional programme.

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nehru Report:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
2. It recommended a Supreme Court.
3. It proposed the continuation of dyarchy in the provinces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary and the report recommended a Supreme Court. It proposed ending dyarchy, so statement 3 is false.
224.tq: Locate the one reversed constitutional recommendation.

224.s: At which session and in which month was the Nehru Report discussed, with a one-year ultimatum to the British?
224.x: The Nehru Report was discussed at the Calcutta session in December 1928, where a one-year ultimatum was given to the British.
224.tq: Combine the event, venue and date rather than recalling the year alone.

224.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were formulated as the Muslim League's response to which document?
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were the Muslim League's answer to the Nehru Report.
224.tq: Discriminate between closely connected constitutional documents.

224.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important features of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
o: Unitary constitution, joint electorates and abolition of provincial autonomy
Federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces and separate electorates
Dominion status, nominated legislatures and universal adult franchise
Presidential government, one-third provincial seats and communal veto at all levels
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces and separate electorates.
224.tq: Split the options by testing the distinctive features of a constitutional demand.

224.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the proposed All-India Federation was to consist of
o: British provinces and directly administered tribal areas only
224.x: The proposed federation was to include both British provinces and princely states.
224.tq: Test the composition of the proposed federal scheme.

224.s:
With reference to the federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. Accession of princely states was optional.
2. The federation actually came into operation.
3. Dyarchy was provided at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Accession of princely states was optional and dyarchy was provided at the Centre. The federation never came into being, making statement 2 false.
224.tq: Separate a proposed provision from one that was actually implemented.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is notable for being the longest British constitutional Act relating to India, containing
224.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; it is also described in some references as having 14 parts and 321 articles.
224.tq: Use the numerical pair rather than relying on the size description alone.

224.s: Which one of the following was a direct consequence of provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Introduction of dyarchy in every province
Transfer of provincial subjects to the Governor-General
224.x: Provincial autonomy abolished dyarchy in the provinces.
224.tq: Match the constitutional reform with its immediate institutional effect.

224.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 began in
224.x: Provincial autonomy began in April 1937.
224.tq: Discriminate between nearby years and months associated with implementation.

224.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: It established bicameral legislatures in some provinces and abolished the India Council.
It abolished all provincial legislatures and retained the India Council.
It abolished bicameral legislatures in the provinces.
It introduced a single legislature for all provinces.
224.x: The Act provided bicameral legislatures in some provinces and abolished the India Council.
224.tq: Combine two institutional changes and reject their reversed versions.

224.s: How many legislative lists were provided under the Government of India Act, 1935?
224.x: The Act provided Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists, making three legislative lists.
224.tq: Recall the constitutional classification by counting its categories.

224.s: The Federal Court established under the Government of India Act, 1935 was located at
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937.
224.tq: Use the institution-to-location association.

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Federal Public Service Commission — 1935 Act — Calcutta, 1937
Provincial Public Service Commissions — 1909 Act — Delhi, 1910
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935. The Act also provided for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs.
224.tq: Start from the sure institution-location-year pair and eliminate swapped authorities.

224.s: The Reserve Bank of India began operations on
224.x: The RBI started functioning on 1 April 1935. It was nationalised later, on 1 January 1949.
224.tq: Distinguish the commencement date from the later nationalisation date.

224.s: The establishment of the Reserve Bank of India was preceded by the recommendations of the
224.x: The Hilton Young Commission of 1926 recommended the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
224.tq: Match a financial institution with the commission that recommended it.

224.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. RBI was nationalised
B. Hilton Young Commission
C. RBI started operations
D. Provincial autonomy began
224.x: The correct sequence is Hilton Young Commission in 1926, RBI operations in 1935, provincial autonomy in April 1937, and RBI nationalisation in 1949.
224.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle dates.

224.s: Who became the premier of Madras after the provincial elections of 1937 when the Congress formed the ministry there?
224.x: C. Rajagopalachari became the premier of Madras in 1937.
224.tq: Distinguish the 1937 Congress ministry from the earlier Justice Party ministry.

224.s: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 mainly because
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
224.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.
224.tq: Identify the political cause behind a major institutional action.

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political response to the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939?
o: The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 26 January 1940, and Rajagopalachari joined it.
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 15 August 1939, and Jinnah resigned.
The Congress observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939, and Ambedkar opposed it.
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939, and B. R. Ambedkar joined it.
224.x: The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939; B. R. Ambedkar also joined the observance.
224.tq: Test a date-person-event combination and reject swapped participants.

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature of the Government of India Act, 1935)
a. Instrument of Instructions
b. Federal Court
c. Emergency powers
d. Federal scheme and Public Service Commissions

List-II (Constitutional counterpart)
i. Supreme Court
ii. Directive Principles of State Policy
iii. Emergency provisions
iv. Union-State structure and UPSC/State PSCs

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
224.x: The Instrument of Instructions corresponds to the Directive Principles, the Federal Court to the Supreme Court, emergency powers to emergency provisions, and the federal scheme and PSCs to the Union-State structure and present PSC system.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair Federal Court–Supreme Court and complete the constitutional parallels.

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is regarded as the largest single source of the
224.x: The 1935 Act is considered the largest single source of the structural provisions of the Constitution of India.
224.tq: Identify the historical document's long-term constitutional significance.

224.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's
o: Power to nationalise the Reserve Bank
Power to appoint the Federal Court judges
Power to dissolve the Constituent Assembly
224.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
224.tq: Match a specific section with its constitutional function.

224.s: The criticism that dyarchy gave ministers transferred subjects without adequate financial control was based on the fact that
o: The Governor-General controlled all transferred subjects directly.
Ministers were denied legislative powers altogether.
Finance was abolished as a provincial subject.
224.x: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers controlled transferred subjects while finance remained among the reserved subjects.
224.tq: Apply the reserved-transferred distinction to an administrative criticism.

224.s: Which one of the following best explains why dyarchy was criticised as an ineffective arrangement?
o: All provincial subjects were transferred to elected ministers with complete financial authority.
The system provided no distinction between executive and legislative functions.
Transferred subjects were placed under ministers, but essential financial control remained reserved.
The arrangement abolished the office of the Governor.
224.x: Ministers were responsible for transferred subjects but lacked control over finance, which remained reserved; this limited responsible government.
224.tq: Choose the precise cause-effect explanation rather than an extreme generalisation.

224.s: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with which pair of leaders?
224.x: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with Subbarayalu Reddiar and Panagal Raja.
224.tq: Distinguish the earlier Justice Party ministry from the later Congress ministry.

224.s: C. Sankaran Nair was recalled in recent public discourse on the 106th anniversary of the
224.x: The Prime Minister recalled C. Sankaran Nair on the 106th anniversary of Jallianwala Bagh.
224.tq: Link a contemporary reference to the historical event it commemorates.

224.s: Which one of the following was associated with the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills?
o: Rajagopalachari described them as the “Day of Deliverance Bills”.
Motilal Nehru described one of them as the “Slavery of India Bill”.
Ambedkar introduced them in the Federal Court.
Jinnah called both bills the “Federal India Acts”.
224.x: In the context of the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills, Motilal Nehru called one the “Slavery of India Bill”.
224.tq: Use the person-quotation association and reject quotations assigned to nearby leaders.

224.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between the Government of India Act, 1935 and the Constitution of India?
1. The Federal Court was a precursor to the Supreme Court.
2. The Instrument of Instructions influenced the Directive Principles.
3. Emergency powers under the Act influenced the emergency provisions of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: All three are recognised constitutional continuities between the 1935 Act and the Constitution of India.
224.tq: Recognise a cluster of borrowed constitutional features rather than an isolated provision.

225.s: The Simon Commission was appointed by the British Government on
225.x: The Simon Commission was appointed on 8 November 1927 by the Conservative Government headed by Stanley Baldwin, two years ahead of schedule.
225.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the later arrival and protest dates.

225.s: The Simon Commission was appointed primarily to
o: settle the question of communal representation
frame a constitution for an independent India
review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919
implement the recommendations of the Nehru Report
225.x: The Commission was appointed to review the working of the Government of India Act, 1919.
225.tq: Identify the statutory purpose rather than the later political consequences.

225.s: The principal reason for the boycott of the Simon Commission by Indian political organisations was that
o: it recommended the continuation of separate electorates
it was appointed after the Nehru Report
225.x: The Commission was boycotted because all its members were British and it contained no Indian member.
225.tq: Separate the immediate cause of boycott from later constitutional disagreements.

225.s: At the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in December 1927, the decision regarding the Simon Commission was to
o: boycott it only at its first meeting
send an Indian delegation to assist it
boycott it at every stage and in every form
225.x: The Madras Congress session under M. A. Ansari resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage and in every form.
225.tq: Recall the precise wording of an organisational resolution.

225.s:
Which of the following groups did NOT join the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Jinnah's faction of the Muslim League
2. Shafi's faction of the Muslim League
3. Hindu Mahasabha
4. Justice Party
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: Shafi's League faction and the Justice Party did not join the boycott. Jinnah's faction and the Hindu Mahasabha participated in it.
225.tq: Use organisational faction differences to identify the exceptions.

225.s: Lala Lajpat Rai led the protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore on
225.x: Lala Lajpat Rai led a peaceful protest at Lahore on 30 October 1928.
225.tq: Link the protest date with the later date of death caused by the injuries.

225.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence of events connected with Lala Lajpat Rai's death?
1. S. P. James Scott ordered a lathi charge.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai led a protest at Lahore.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai died of his injuries.
4. Saunders was killed by Bhagat Singh's group.
Select the correct chronological order.
225.x: Lajpat Rai led the protest on 30 October 1928, Scott ordered the lathi charge, Rai died on 17 November 1928, and Saunders was killed in December 1928.
225.tq: Fix the first protest and last revenge event, then arrange the intervening events.

225.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Lahore protest against the Simon Commission?
o: S. P. James Scott ordered the lathi charge, while Saunders was later killed by Bhagat Singh's group.
Bhagat Singh led the peaceful protest and later died of lathi injuries.
Lala Lajpat Rai was killed immediately at the protest by the Simon Commission members.
Saunders ordered the lathi charge and was later killed by Lajpat Rai's followers.
225.x: S. P. James Scott ordered the lathi charge that injured Lajpat Rai. Bhagat Singh's group later killed Saunders in December 1928 in an act of revenge.
225.tq: Trap the swapped person responsible for the lathi charge and the later assassination.

225.s: In the Madras Presidency, the protest against the Simon Commission in 1928 was led by
225.x: Tanguturi Prakasam led the protest in Madras in 1928.
225.tq: Distinguish the regional protest leader from other Andhra organisers.

225.s: Tanguturi Prakasam earned the title ‘Andhra Kesari’ because he
o: drafted the Nehru Report in Andhra
bared his chest and dared the police to shoot during the Simon protest
organised the first Round Table Conference
led the boycott resolution at the Madras Congress session
225.x: During the Simon protest, Prakasam bared his chest and challenged the police to shoot, earning the title ‘Andhra Kesari’.
225.tq: Connect an honorific with the specific incident that produced it.

225.s: During the Simon Commission protest in Madras, the person killed by police firing was
225.x: Police firing during the Madras protest killed Parthasarathi.
225.tq: Identify the individual associated with a specific regional incident.

225.s: Who was the President of the Andhra Boycott Committee formed in connection with the Simon Commission agitation?
225.x: S. Satyamurthy served as President of the Andhra Boycott Committee.
225.tq: Separate the committee office-holder from the field protest leaders.

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: G. V. Unnayya Sastri — protest at Tenali and Guntur
Bulusu Sambamurti — tour of Andhra for Simon boycott
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Vijayawada boycott initiative
S. Satyamurthy — led the protest at Lahore
225.x: S. P. James Scott, not S. Satyamurthy, was associated with the Lahore lathi charge. The other three pairs correctly describe Andhra-related activities.
225.tq: Find the wrong person-to-event pairing among closely related organisers.

225.s: At Vijayawada, the cover sent by Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao in protest against the Simon Commission contained only the words
225.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao sent a cover bearing only the words ‘Simon Go Back’. The Vijayawada municipality also passed a boycott resolution.
225.tq: Recall the distinctive wording used in a symbolic protest action.

225.s:
Which of the following places passed municipal resolutions supporting the boycott of the Simon Commission?
1. Vijayawada
2. Tirupati
3. Kurnool
4. Eluru
5. Srikakulam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The municipalities of Vijayawada, Tirupati, Kurnool, Eluru and Srikakulam passed resolutions supporting the boycott.
225.tq: Check every item in the regional list before selecting the complete combination.

225.s: Black flags were shown against the Simon Commission at
225.x: Black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole. G. V. Unnayya Sastri led protests at Tenali and Guntur.
225.tq: Distinguish locations of black-flag demonstrations from locations of organised leadership.

225.s: The challenge issued by Birkenhead in 1927, which led to the formation of the committee for the Nehru Report, was that Indians
o: could not organise a boycott of the Simon Commission
could not agree on a constitutional scheme
225.x: Birkenhead challenged Indians to prepare an agreed constitutional scheme, leading to the All Parties Conference and the Nehru Report committee.
225.tq: Identify the cause behind the formation of a constitutional committee.

225.s:
Consider the following statements about the committee that prepared the Nehru Report:
1. It was constituted by an All Parties Conference.
2. Dr M. A. Ansari presided over the All Parties Conference.
3. Motilal Nehru was its chairman.
4. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: All four statements are correct. The seven-member committee was formed by the All Parties Conference presided over by Dr M. A. Ansari, with Motilal Nehru as chairman and Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary.
225.tq: Verify the formation, presiding officer, chairman and secretary separately.

225.s: The Nehru Report was published in
225.x: The Nehru Report was issued in August 1928.
225.tq: Reject the nearby but incorrect years associated with the committee and later reactions.

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Nehru Report?
o: Universal adult suffrage and fundamental rights
Separate electorates as the permanent basis of representation
A federal structure with a bicameral central legislature
225.x: The Nehru Report recommended joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates as a permanent arrangement.
225.tq: Use the central distinction between joint electorates and separate electorates.

225.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents recommendations of the Nehru Report?
1. End of dyarchy
2. Responsible government
3. Establishment of a Supreme Court
4. Linguistic provinces, including Andhra
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The Nehru Report recommended ending dyarchy, establishing responsible government and a Supreme Court, and creating linguistic provinces including Andhra.
225.tq: Recognise the complete set of constitutional and administrative recommendations.

225.s: The Nehru Report recommended which arrangement for minority representation?
o: One-third separate representation for Muslims in every province
Nomination of all minority members by the Governor-General
Joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities
225.x: The Report proposed joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities.
225.tq: Discriminate between the Nehru Report proposal and Jinnah's later demands.

225.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the reaction to the Nehru Report?
1. The Muslim League rejected it.
2. Jinnah's amendments failed at the Calcutta All Parties Convention.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose demanded complete independence.
4. The Congress immediately accepted complete independence without an ultimatum.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Congress gave Britain a one-year ultimatum; complete independence was declared at Lahore in 1929 after the ultimatum expired.
225.tq: Identify the single false statement by distinguishing an ultimatum from its later outcome.

225.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Partition of Bengal
B. Simon Commission
C. Nehru Report
D. Jinnah's Fourteen Points
E. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
225.x: The sequence is Partition of Bengal (1905), Simon Commission (1927–28), Nehru Report (1928), Fourteen Points (1929), and Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931).
225.tq: Anchor the earliest and latest events, then place the closely spaced constitutional developments.

225.s:
Which one of the following correctly describes the First Round Table Conference?
1. The Congress boycotted it.
2. It was held while the Civil Disobedience Movement was continuing.
3. It was followed by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
4. It was conducted under Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four statements are correct. The First Round Table Conference was held during the Civil Disobedience Movement, without Congress participation, under Ramsay MacDonald, and was followed by the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
225.tq: Combine participation, political context and consequence to identify the complete description.

225.s: Which of the following statements about the three Round Table Conferences is correct?
o: Only the Second Conference was held in London to discuss dominion status.
All three were held in Delhi under the Viceroy of India.
The conferences were convened by the Indian National Congress to draft the Nehru Report.
All three were held in London under Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.x: All three Round Table Conferences were held in London under British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald to discuss the Simon Report and a federal constitution.
225.tq: Use venue, convening authority and agenda together to eliminate substituted details.

225.s: The Second Round Table Conference failed mainly because of disagreement over
o: the location of the federal capital
the appointment of the Simon Commission
225.x: The Second Round Table Conference failed chiefly because agreement could not be reached on minority representation.
225.tq: Identify the central issue that caused the conference deadlock.

225.s:
Which of the following statements about the Third Round Table Conference is correct?
1. It was held from 17 November to 24 December 1932.
2. The Congress boycotted it.
3. It had only 46 delegates.
4. It contributed to the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four statements are correct. The Third Conference was held in late 1932, was boycotted by Congress, had 46 delegates and helped shape the plan for the Government of India Act, 1935.
225.tq: Check the date, attendance, size and constitutional outcome as a single cluster.

225.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Round Table Conference — Congress represented by Gandhi
Second Round Table Conference — Gandhi as sole INC representative
Third Round Table Conference — attended by Congress under Jawaharlal Nehru
First Round Table Conference — held after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
225.x: Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress. Congress boycotted the First and Third Conferences.
225.tq: Start with the sure Congress-attendance pair and eliminate reversals.

225.s: Dr B. R. Ambedkar attended the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the
225.x: Ambedkar participated in the Round Table Conferences as a representative of the depressed classes.
225.tq: Match the prominent delegate with the social group he represented.

225.s: After the Second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi
o: joined the Third Round Table Conference as a British delegate
resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was jailed in Yerwada
formed the Muslim League to negotiate minority representation
accepted the Communal Award and retired from public life
225.x: After the Second Conference, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement and was imprisoned in Yerwada. The Communal Award followed in August 1932.
225.tq: Link a conference outcome with its immediate political consequence.

225.s: The Butler Committee was appointed to examine the relationship between
o: the British Parliament and the Indian National Congress
the provinces and the central legislature
the Muslim League and the Hindu Mahasabha
the Indian princely states and the Paramount Power
225.x: The Butler Committee, appointed in 1927 under Harcourt Butler, examined relations between the Indian princely states and the Paramount Power.
225.tq: Identify the exact institutional relationship under examination.

225.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Butler Committee — relations of princely states with the Paramount Power
Simon Commission — review of the Government of India Act, 1919
Butler Committee — chaired by Lord Irwin
225.x: The Butler Committee was associated with Harcourt Butler, not Lord Irwin. Its purpose was to examine relations between princely states and the Paramount Power.
225.tq: Use the swapped-person trap in a commission-to-chairman pairing.

225.s: Under the Delhi Proposals of March 1927, Muslim leaders offered to give up separate electorates in favour of joint electorates subject to, among others, which condition?
o: Removal of all safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Complete separation of Bengal from India
225.x: The Delhi Proposals offered joint electorates in return for safeguards including one-third Muslim representation at the centre, separation of Sindh, reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan, and population-based representation in Punjab and Bengal.
225.tq: Recall the conditional nature of a constitutional compromise.

225.s:
Which of the following was NOT a condition associated with the Delhi Proposals?
1. Separation of Sindh
2. Reforms in the North-West Frontier Province and Baluchistan
3. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
4. Abolition of joint electorates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: The Delhi Proposals supported joint electorates subject to safeguards; they did not seek the abolition of joint electorates. The other three were associated conditions.
225.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the central proposal.

225.s: The All Parties Muslim Conference held at Delhi in January 1929, under the Aga Khan,
o: drafted the Government of India Act, 1935
resolved to boycott the Simon Commission at every stage
accepted the Nehru Report without modification
225.x: The All Parties Muslim Conference at Delhi in January 1929, presided over by the Aga Khan, rejected the Nehru Report.
225.tq: Distinguish the Muslim Conference's reaction from the earlier All Parties Conference.

225.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 at the
o: Indian National Congress session at Lahore
Second Round Table Conference at London
225.x: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 at the Muslim League session in Delhi.
225.tq: Match a constitutional document with its organisation, venue and date.

225.s:
Which of the following demands formed part of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
1. Federal constitution with residuary powers vested in the provinces
2. One-third Muslim representation at the centre
3. Separate electorates
4. Safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
225.x: All four were among the major demands associated with Jinnah's Fourteen Points: provincial residuary powers, one-third central representation, separate electorates and safeguards for Muslim-majority provinces.
225.tq: Distinguish Jinnah's demands from the joint-electorate provisions of the Nehru Report.

225.s: The Deepavali Declaration was issued by which of the following Viceroys of India?
225.x: The Deepavali Declaration was issued by Viceroy Lord Irwin.
225.tq: Use the office-holder association to distinguish the declaration from other constitutional developments.

225.s: The Deepavali Declaration was issued on which date?
225.x: Lord Irwin issued the Deepavali Declaration on 31 October 1929.
225.tq: Separate closely related dates by fixing the exact year attached to the event.

225.s: Which one of the following most accurately states the significance of the Deepavali Declaration?
o: It introduced provincial autonomy and abolished separate electorates.
It accepted the demand for a separate Andhra Province and announced the Government of India Act, 1935.
It declared complete independence as the immediate constitutional objective and cancelled the Simon Commission.
It recognised dominion status as the natural goal of India’s constitutional progress and promised a Round Table Conference after the Simon Commission report.
225.x: The declaration described dominion status as the natural goal of India’s constitutional progress and promised a Round Table Conference after the Simon report.
225.tq: Choose the option that combines the two precise features of the declaration without importing later constitutional measures.

225.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deepavali Declaration:
1. It was issued in 1929.
2. It was issued by Lord Irwin.
3. It promised a Round Table Conference before the Simon Commission report.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the promised Round Table Conference was to be held after the Simon Commission report.
225.tq: Find the reversed sequence in the statement containing ‘before’ and retain the two directly established facts.

225.s: The Simon Commission submitted its report in which month and year?
225.x: The Simon Commission report was issued in May 1930.
225.tq: Distinguish the report date from the dates of the declaration and the Round Table Conferences.

225.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I
 a. Dyarchy
 b. Sindh
 c. Burma
 d. Orissa

List-II
 i. Separation from India
 ii. Creation as a province
 iii. Abolition
 iv. Separation from Bombay

option_a: a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii
option_b: a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
option_c: a–ii, b–i, c–iv, d–iii
option_d: a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii
225.x: The report recommended abolition of dyarchy, separation of Sindh from Bombay, separation of Burma from India, and creation of an Orissa province.
225.tq: Start from the sure pair ‘dyarchy–abolition’ and eliminate codes with incorrect territorial relationships.

225.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation of the Simon Commission report?
o: Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre
225.x: The report recommended abolition of dyarchy, provincial autonomy and continuation of separate communal electorates. Immediate establishment of complete responsible government at the Centre was not listed as its recommendation.
225.tq: Find the option that goes beyond the specific constitutional recommendations rather than merely changing one territorial detail.

225.s:
With reference to the territorial recommendations of the Simon Commission report, consider the following statements:
1. Sindh was to be separated from Bombay.
2. Burma was to be separated from India.
3. Orissa was to be created as a province.
4. Andhra was to be created as a province.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the report ignored Andhra’s demand for a separate province.
225.tq: Identify the one swapped territorial outcome by comparing the treatment of Orissa and Andhra.

225.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the response of the Oriyas and the Andhras to the Simon Commission?
o: The Oriyas boycotted the Commission, whereas the Andhras lobbied it.
The Oriyas lobbied the Commission, whereas the Andhras boycotted it.
Both groups lobbied the Commission for their respective provincial demands.
Both groups boycotted the Commission and rejected provincial reorganisation.
225.x: The Oriyas lobbied the Simon Commission, while the Andhras boycotted it. The report supported the creation of Orissa but ignored Andhra’s demand.
225.tq: Test the paired contrast directly by checking which group lobbied and which group boycotted.

225.s: The report of the Simon Commission, together with the Round Table Conferences, contributed to the enactment of which legislation?
225.x: The Simon Commission report and the Round Table Conferences contributed to the Government of India Act, 1935.
225.tq: Link the constitutional process to its legislative outcome while rejecting earlier and later Acts.

225.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Simon Commission report recommended full provincial autonomy.
2. It recommended retaining separate communal electorates.
3. It accepted Andhra’s demand for a separate province.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Simon Commission report ignored Andhra’s demand.
225.tq: Spot the false acceptance claim by contrasting the report’s recommendation on provinces with its treatment of Andhra.

225.s: Lala Lajpat Rai, who led the anti-Simon Commission protest in Lahore, had earlier presided over the first session of the AITUC in which year?
225.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the first session of the All India Trade Union Congress in 1920.
225.tq: Connect the personality with the distinct organisational milestone and its year.

225.s: Which one of the following statements best explains the historical significance of Lala Lajpat Rai’s role in the anti-Simon Commission movement?
o: He led the Lahore protest and was fatally injured in the anti-Simon agitation.
He chaired the Simon Commission and drafted its report.
He represented the Indian National Congress at all three Round Table Conferences.
He secured the acceptance of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission.
225.x: Lala Lajpat Rai led the anti-Simon protest in Lahore and was fatally injured during the agitation.
225.tq: Use the leader–movement–consequence chain to reject options assigning him unrelated constitutional roles.

225.s: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission, along with Tanguturi Prakasam’s ‘Andhra Kesari’ moment, contributed to which political development?
o: The demand for a separate Andhra Province
The demand for the continuation of Burma within India
The demand for the abolition of provincial autonomy
The demand for the restoration of dyarchy in the provinces
225.x: The neglect of Andhra’s demand by the Simon Commission and Prakasam’s political role fuelled the demand for a separate Andhra Province.
225.tq: Trace the stated regional grievance to the political demand it helped strengthen.

225.s:
Consider the following statements about the Simon Commission and its regional impact:
1. Its report recommended the creation of an Orissa province.
2. It ignored Andhra’s demand for a separate province.
3. The Andhras lobbied the Commission, while the Oriyas boycotted it.
4. Its report and the Round Table Conferences contributed to the Government of India Act, 1935.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
225.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the regional responses: the Oriyas lobbied the Commission, while the Andhras boycotted it.
225.tq: Locate the reversed pair in statement 3 and retain the three statements supported by the constitutional sequence.

226.s: In how many provinces did the Indian National Congress form ministries after the elections held under the Government of India Act, 1935?
226.x: Congress formed ministries in eight of the eleven provinces in 1937. These included Bombay, Madras, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, the United Provinces, the North-West Frontier Province and Assam.
226.tq: Use the total number as the distinguishing numerical fact.

226.s: Which one of the following groups consisted entirely of provinces where the Congress secured a clear majority on its own in the 1937 elections?
o: Bombay, Madras, Bengal, Bihar and Punjab
Madras, Assam, Sindh, Bihar and Orissa
Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa
United Provinces, Bombay, Punjab, Orissa and Bengal
226.x: Congress secured clear majorities in Madras, the United Provinces, the Central Provinces, Bihar and Orissa.
226.tq: Separate clear-majority provinces from provinces where Congress was only the largest party.

226.s: Mahatma Gandhi advised the Congress ministries to hold office:
o: firmly and permanently as a constitutional right
only until the completion of the war
lightly, not tightly, as a crown of thorns
226.x: Gandhi advised the ministers to hold office “lightly, not tightly”, describing office as a “crown of thorns”.
226.tq: Test the exact wording of a famous political expression.

226.s: The Congress ministries formed in 1937 resigned during:
226.x: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939, following the unilateral declaration of India's participation in the Second World War.
226.tq: Distinguish the closely related year and month range.

226.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939:
1. Lord Linlithgow declared India to be a party to the Second World War.
2. Indian leaders were not consulted before the declaration.
3. The Muslim League observed 22 December 1939 as Deliverance Day.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
226.x: All three statements are correct. Linlithgow made the declaration without consulting Indian leaders, and the League observed the Congress resignations as Deliverance Day on 22 December 1939.
226.tq: Check each statement against the cause, authority and consequence of the resignations.

226.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based primarily on the discussions of the:
o: First Round Table Conference and the Simon Commission Report
Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper
Second Round Table Conference and the Nehru Report
Cabinet Mission and the Cripps Proposals
226.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 was based on the Third Round Table Conference and the White Paper.
226.tq: Match the constitutional enactment with its immediate source documents.

226.s:
Consider the following provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. All-India Federation of provinces and princely states
2. Provincial autonomy with abolition of dyarchy in the provinces
3. Dyarchy at the Centre
4. Federal Court at Delhi
Which of the above were actually implemented?
226.x: Provincial autonomy and the Federal Court were implemented. The proposed Federation and dyarchy at the Centre were not implemented because the Federation did not come into operation.
226.tq: Find the implemented provisions by separating operative features from conditional proposals.

226.s: The proposed All-India Federation under the Government of India Act, 1935 did not come into existence because:
o: the Federal Court declared it unconstitutional
the provinces refused to join and the British Parliament rejected it
joining was optional and the princely states refused to join
the Congress refused to participate in the Round Table Conferences
226.x: The Federation was never implemented because joining was optional and the princely states refused to join.
226.tq: Link a constitutional proposal with the specific condition that prevented its operation.

226.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in relation to the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Council of India — Continued without alteration
226.x: The Council of India created under the Government of India Act, 1858 was abolished, and the Secretary of State was provided with advisers.
226.tq: Find the reversed or opposite description among otherwise correct pairs.

226.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 are correct?
1. It provided for bicameral legislatures in six provinces.
2. It provided for Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions.
3. It separated Burma from India.
4. It made Sindh and Orissa provinces.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
226.x: All four statements are correct. The six provinces with bicameral legislatures were Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and the United Provinces.
226.tq: Cover a list of related structural provisions through an all-inclusive combination.

226.s: In which of the following provinces did the Government of India Act, 1935 introduce bicameral legislatures?
o: Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and United Provinces
Assam, Punjab, Sindh, Bihar, Madras and Orissa
Bengal, Bombay, Central Provinces, Madras, Punjab and Sindh
Bombay, Bihar, Orissa, Punjab, United Provinces and Assam
226.x: Bicameral legislatures were introduced in Assam, Bengal, Bombay, Bihar, Madras and the United Provinces.
226.tq: Recall the complete membership of a named constitutional list.

226.s: The Reserve Bank of India was established in 1935 under the:
226.x: The RBI was set up in 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
226.tq: Discriminate between the year of establishment and the year of the enabling Act.

226.s: The elections to the Madras Legislative Assembly in 1937 were held during:
226.x: The Madras elections were held from 15 to 20 February 1937.
226.tq: Distinguish closely placed dates by retaining both the month and range.

226.s: Who led the Congress campaign in the 1937 Madras elections along with Bulusu Sambamurthy?
226.x: The campaign was led by Tanguturi Prakasam, then President of the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, and Bulusu Sambamurthy.
226.tq: Match the political campaign with its leading figures rather than the later ministry.

226.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political outcome in the Madras Presidency after the 1937 elections?
o: The Muslim League formed the ministry under a coalition arrangement.
The Congress formed the ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out.
The Justice Party formed the ministry with the People's Party.
The Hindu Mahasabha formed the ministry with the Congress.
226.x: The Congress formed the Madras ministry, while the Justice Party was almost wiped out. The People's Party of the Pithapuram Zamindar lost all its seats, and the League and Hindu Mahasabha performed poorly.
226.tq: Reject the options that assign office to parties which performed poorly.

226.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. Tanguturi Prakasam
 b. Bezawada Gopala Reddy
 c. V.V. Giri
 d. Bulusu Sambamurthy

List-II (Post)
 i. Speaker
 ii. Labour and Industries
 iii. Revenue
 iv. Local Self-Government

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
226.x: Tanguturi Prakasam held Revenue, Bezawada Gopala Reddy held Local Self-Government, V.V. Giri held Labour and Industries, and Bulusu Sambamurthy was Speaker.
226.tq: Start from the sure leader-post pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.

226.s: The introduction of Hindi in Madras schools by C. Rajagopalachari's ministry led to:
o: the merger of the Justice Party with the Congress
the resignation of the Congress ministry in 1937
Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation and subsequent withdrawal of the policy
the permanent adoption of Hindi as the sole medium of instruction
226.x: Rajaji introduced Hindi in Madras schools, but Periyar's anti-Hindi agitation in 1937 led the government to withdraw the policy.
226.tq: Follow the cause-effect chain from a policy to the political response.

226.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Government of India Act, 1935 as a source of constitutional features?
1. Federal scheme — Government of India Act, 1935
2. Directive Principles — Instrument of Instructions
3. Bicameralism at the Centre — Government of India Act, 1919
4. Separate electorate for Muslims — Indian Councils Act, 1909
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
226.x: All four pairs are correct. The 1935 Act supplied the federal scheme, the Instrument of Instructions influenced the Directive Principles, the 1919 Act provided for central bicameralism, and the 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
226.tq: Match each constitutional feature with its historical source before selecting the combination.

226.s: The provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 that served as a model for the Directive Principles of State Policy was the:
226.x: The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 served as the model for the Directive Principles of State Policy.
226.tq: Test a direct source-feature relationship.

226.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Congress response to the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: Congress accepted the Act without qualification and abandoned the demand for a Constituent Assembly.
Congress accepted the Federation but rejected provincial autonomy.
Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
Congress rejected elections and demanded restoration of dyarchy in the provinces.
226.x: Congress rejected the Act and demanded a Constituent Assembly elected on adult franchise.
226.tq: Identify the precise political demand rather than an extreme reversal of policy.

226.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Roy raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
2. The demand became an official Congress demand in 1935.
3. The Lucknow session of 1936 rejected the Government of India Act.
4. The Faizpur session of 1936 decided to contest the elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
226.x: All four statements are correct. M.N. Roy first raised the Constituent Assembly demand in 1934, Congress adopted it officially in 1935, Lucknow rejected the Act, and Faizpur decided to contest the elections.
226.tq: Arrange related resolutions by person, year and Congress session.

226.s: Who described the Government of India Act, 1935 as “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable”?
226.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah used the description “thoroughly rotten, fundamentally bad and totally unacceptable” for the Act.
226.tq: Discriminate between two well-known but different criticisms of the same Act.

226.s: The provincial elections under the Government of India Act, 1935 were held in:
226.x: The elections were held in the winter of 1936-37 in eleven provinces.
226.tq: Combine the election season, years and number of provinces.

226.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Unionist Party ministry under Sikandar Hayat Khan
Bengal — Coalition led by Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party
226.x: In Bengal, Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party formed a coalition. Punjab was associated with the Unionist Party under Sikandar Hayat Khan, while Sindh had a coalition under Allah Baksh.
226.tq: Use province-leader-party associations to reject swapped outcomes.

226.s: In which province was a coalition formed under Allah Baksh after the 1937 elections?
226.x: A coalition under Allah Baksh was formed in Sindh.
226.tq: Test the exact province associated with a coalition leader.

226.s: Which of the following statements about the Muslim League's performance after the 1937 elections is correct?
o: It performed strongly in all Muslim seats and formed ministries in every Muslim-majority province.
It did poorly even in Muslim seats, after which it alleged Hindu Raj and launched mass-contact campaigns.
It merged with the Congress in the provinces where Congress formed ministries.
It won a clear majority in Bengal and rejected mass-contact campaigns.
226.x: The Muslim League performed poorly even in Muslim seats. It subsequently alleged “Hindu Raj” and launched mass-contact campaigns.
226.tq: Trace the political consequence of an electoral setback.

226.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists contained, respectively, how many subjects?
226.x: The Federal List contained 59 subjects, the Provincial List 54 subjects and the Concurrent List 36 subjects.
226.tq: Use the numerical association between the three lists and eliminate options that interchange their figures.

226.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the distribution of legislative subjects under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Provincial, Municipal and Concurrent Lists were provided
Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists were provided
Union, State and Local Lists were provided
Federal and Provincial Lists alone were provided
226.x: The Act divided subjects among Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists. The terminology Union, State and Local Lists belongs to a later constitutional framework.
226.tq: Discriminate between the exact statutory terminology of the 1935 Act and familiar later constitutional terms.

226.s: In the absence of an entry in the Federal, Provincial or Concurrent List under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the
226.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 assigned residuary powers to the Governor-General.
226.tq: Ask who would exercise the residual power and avoid confusing the Governor-General with provincial Governors.

226.s: Which of the following powers was associated with the Governor-General under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Suspending proceedings relating to a Bill and stopping discussion
Appointing all provincial ministers without legislative responsibility
Transferring all residuary powers to provincial legislatures
Abolishing the Concurrent List by executive order
