Which of the following developments reflects the wider institutional influence of Gandhian thought in India?
1. Directive Principles relating to village panchayats
2. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment's panchayat framework
3. Policy support for cottage industries
Which of the statements given above are correct?
230.x: Gandhian ideas influenced the Directive Principles, the panchayat framework associated with the 73rd Amendment and policies supporting cottage industries.
230.tq: Identify institutional consequences across constitutional and economic fields.

230.s: Who wrote *Sarvodaya Ganam* and translated Gandhi's autobiography into Telugu?
230.x: Tummala Sitaramamurthy wrote *Sarvodaya Ganam*, inspired by Vinoba, and translated Gandhi's autobiography into Telugu.
230.tq: Use the author–work–language combination to identify the Andhra cultural association.

230.s: Which of the following correctly represents the contemporary relevance associated with Gandhian ideas?
o: The Baltic freedom struggle was based exclusively on industrial trade unions rather than civil resistance.
Gandhian ideas are relevant only to village panchayats and have no contemporary application.
Trusteeship has been cited in relation to owners funding fire-safety systems, and Gandhian civil resistance has been credited in the Baltic freedom struggle.
Trusteeship has been cited only in relation to land redistribution, while civil resistance was rejected in the Baltic freedom struggle.
230.x: Gandhian trusteeship has been cited in connection with owners funding fire-safety systems, while Gandhian civil resistance has been credited as an influence in the Baltic freedom struggle.
230.tq: Apply an abstract principle to the contemporary examples associated with it.

231.s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
231.x: G.D. Birla served as the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh, while Amritlal Thakkar was its secretary.
231.tq: Use the office-holder distinction to avoid confusing president with secretary.

231.s: Amritlal Thakkar, popularly known as Thakkar Bapa, was associated with the Harijan Sevak Sangh as its:
231.x: Amritlal Thakkar, popularly known as Thakkar Bapa, was the secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh.
231.tq: Discriminate between closely associated office-bearers.

231.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded in September 1932. A specific record places its establishment on:
231.x: The organisation was founded in September 1932; one record specifically gives 30 October 1932 at Mumbai as the date and place of establishment.
231.tq: Separate the general month from the specifically recorded date and place.

231.s: Which of the following was NOT among the activities associated with the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
o: Introducing separate electorates for the Depressed Classes
Promoting entry into wells and temples
231.x: The Sangh worked for access to wells, schools and temples, and promoted schools, hostels, cooperatives, inter-dining and inter-caste marriage. Separate electorates were a political demand associated with the Poona Pact debate, not its activity.
231.tq: Find the option belonging to the political debate rather than the organisation's constructive work.

231.s: Which pair relating to the Andhra branches of the Harijan Sevak Sangh is correctly matched?
231.x: The Andhra branches were located at Hyderabad and Vijayawada. Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was president and Maganti Bapineedu was secretary of the Vijayawada branch.
231.tq: Start from the sure branch-office bearer pair.

231.s: Nai Talim, or Basic Education, primarily aimed at:
o: Replacing manual work with purely literary education
Providing higher education exclusively in English
Training students only for government employment
Making villages self-sufficient through vocational and craft-centred education
231.x: Gandhi's Basic Education was vocational and craft-centred, sought to make villages self-sufficient and aimed to dignify manual labour.
231.tq: Identify the educational philosophy from its practical social objective.

231.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education:
1. The Wardha Educational Conference adopted the scheme in 1937.
2. The Zakir Hussain Committee drew up the scheme.
3. The scheme prescribed free and compulsory education for seven years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
231.x: All three statements are correct. The scheme was adopted in 1937, drafted by the Zakir Hussain Committee, and envisaged seven years of free and compulsory education.
231.tq: Check the date, drafting committee and duration before selecting the combined option.

231.s: Under Nai Talim, the proposed age group for seven years of free and compulsory education was:
231.x: Nai Talim proposed seven years of free and compulsory education for children in the age group of 7 to 14 years.
231.tq: Test the paired duration and age range precisely.

231.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principle of Nai Talim?
231.x: Nai Talim emphasised the mother tongue, productive craft and dignity of manual labour; it did not prescribe exclusive reliance on classical languages.
231.tq: Find the option that reverses the practical and vernacular character of the scheme.

231.s:
With reference to the temple-entry movements, consider the following pairs:
a. Vaikom — Travancore
b. Guruvayur — Malabar
c. Siddhantam — Krishna district
d. Lakshminarayan Temple — Wardha
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
231.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Vaikom was in Travancore, Guruvayur in Malabar, Siddhantam in Krishna district and the Lakshminarayan Temple was at Wardha.
231.tq: Match each movement with its location before checking the combined code.

231.s: The Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924–25 was associated with which combination?
o: T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon; Gandhi visited and negotiated
Potti Sriramulu and Durgabai; Gandhi organised the procession
Jamnalal Bajaj and Malaviya; Gandhi led the fast
K. Kelappan and A.K. Gopalan; Gandhi ordered the opening of the temple
231.x: The Vaikom Satyagraha in Travancore was led by T.K. Madhavan and K.P. Kesava Menon. Periyar participated, Sree Narayana Guru supported it, and Gandhi visited and negotiated.
231.tq: Use the leader-role distinction: Gandhi negotiated rather than being listed as the principal local leader.

231.s: Who took part in the Vaikom Satyagraha, while Sree Narayana Guru supported it?
231.x: Periyar took part in the Vaikom Satyagraha, and Sree Narayana Guru extended support to the movement.
231.tq: Distinguish participation from leadership in related temple-entry movements.

231.s: Which statement regarding the Guruvayur Satyagraha is correct?
o: It was an Andhra movement led by Siddhantam Congress leaders.
It took place in Travancore during 1924–25.
It opened the Lakshminarayan Temple to Dalits in 1928.
It took place in Malabar during 1931–32, with K. Kelappan undertaking a fast.
231.x: The Guruvayur Satyagraha took place in Malabar in 1931–32. K. Kelappan fasted and A.K. Gopalan was associated with the movement; Gandhi asked Kelappan to end his fast.
231.tq: Separate the place and dates of Guruvayur from those of Vaikom.

231.s: The Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha was opened to Dalits in 1928 by:
231.x: Jamnalal Bajaj opened the Lakshminarayan Temple at Wardha to Dalits in 1928.
231.tq: Apply the founder-or-doer trap to a temple-entry reform.

231.s: Siddhantam temple entry movement, an early Andhra initiative, took place in which year and district?
231.x: Siddhantam was an early Andhra temple-entry movement led by Congress leaders in Krishna district in 1933.
231.tq: Use the Andhra-specific place-year combination to eliminate nearby movements.

231.s: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the Indian National Congress reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under:
231.x: After the Mahad Satyagraha, the INC reconstituted its Anti-Untouchability Subcommittee under Madan Mohan Malaviya.
231.tq: Test the person placed in charge rather than the movement associated with the issue.

231.s: Which of the following correctly describes Gandhi's Harijan tour?
o: November 1933 to July 1934, covering about 20,000 km from Wardha Ashram
August 1934 to March 1935, covering about 10,000 km from Sabarmati
January 1933 to December 1933, covering about 5,000 km from Poona
November 1932 to July 1933, covering about 20,000 km from Mumbai
231.x: Gandhi's Harijan tour ran from November 1933 to July 1934, covered about 20,000 km, began from the Wardha Ashram and collected funds for the Harijan Sevak Sangh. Orthodox groups disrupted some meetings.
231.tq: Combine the duration, distance, starting point and purpose instead of relying on a single date.

231.s: The term ‘Harijan’, meaning ‘children of God’, was taken from the writings or usage associated with:
231.x: Gandhi adopted the term ‘Harijan’, meaning ‘children of God’, from the Gujarati saint Narsi Mehta.
231.tq: Distinguish the source of a term from later critics of its usage.

231.s: Gandhi described untouchability as:
o: A necessary feature of village organisation
A political question unrelated to religion
A temporary form of economic inequality
231.x: Gandhi called untouchability ‘a blot on Hinduism’ and advocated reform from within Hindu society.
231.tq: Recall the exact quotation rather than a broad paraphrase.

231.s: Which of the following represents Gandhi's route for the uplift of communities subjected to untouchability?
o: Separate electorates, political boycott and armed resistance
Exclusive reliance on litigation and legislative vetoes
Moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work
Economic isolation of orthodox Hindu groups
231.x: Gandhi's approach combined moral persuasion, temple entry, funds, schools and hostels, and constructive work.
231.tq: Identify the complete constructive programme rather than a single method.

231.s: The Congress ministries after 1937 are associated with which measure concerning Harijans?
o: A ban on temple entry campaigns
Abolition of all caste identities by executive order
231.x: After 1937, Congress ministries provided free education to Harijans as part of their social reform measures.
231.tq: Match the historical period with the specific administrative measure.

231.s: Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as:
o: Paternalistic and weak on civil rights
Opposed to education and hostel facilities
Too radical in demanding separate electorates
A purely religious organisation with no social programme
231.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma considered the Sangh paternalistic and criticised it for being weak on civil rights.
231.tq: Test the exact nature of the criticism rather than the organisation's stated activities.

231.s: Which statement best distinguishes Gandhi's position on varna from his position on untouchability?
o: Gandhi regarded untouchability as the purest form of varna.
Gandhi considered caste and untouchability identical in every respect.
Gandhi regarded varna ideally as a division of labour but considered untouchability a corruption.
Gandhi rejected all forms of social organisation but supported untouchability.
231.x: Gandhi distinguished ideal varna as a division of labour from untouchability, which he regarded as a corruption.
231.tq: Separate two closely related concepts instead of treating them as synonyms.

231.s: Which of the following correctly represents the contrast between Gandhi and Ambedkar on caste?
o: Gandhi advocated annihilation of caste, whereas Ambedkar defended the existing caste system.
Gandhi sought reform of varna, whereas Ambedkar advocated annihilation of the caste system.
Both regarded the existing caste system as ideal and unchangeable.
Both confined their approaches exclusively to temple entry.
231.x: Gandhi viewed varna ideally as a division of labour, while Ambedkar regarded the whole caste system as oppressive and advocated its annihilation.
231.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish the two thinkers.

231.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gandhi — Harijan
2. Ambedkar — Dalit / Scheduled Castes
3. Gandhi — Moral persuasion and temple entry
4. Ambedkar — Legal, constitutional and political rights
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
231.x: All four pairs are correct. Gandhi used the term Harijan and stressed moral persuasion and temple entry, while Ambedkar preferred Dalit or Scheduled Castes and emphasised legal, constitutional and political rights.
231.tq: Match each thinker with both terminology and method before choosing the full combination.

231.s: Which statement accurately describes the positions of Gandhi and Ambedkar during the Poona Pact episode?
o: Ambedkar fasted against joint electorates, while Gandhi accepted separate electorates.
Gandhi fasted against separate electorates, while Ambedkar accepted joint electorates with more reserved seats.
Gandhi demanded separate electorates, while Ambedkar opposed all reservations.
Both demanded separate electorates and rejected reserved seats.
231.x: Gandhi fasted against separate electorates. Ambedkar accepted joint electorates with more reserved seats in order to save Gandhi's life.
231.tq: Track the change from separate electorates to joint electorates with reserved seats.

231.s: Which of the following activities brought women into the Gandhian satyagraha movement?
o: Serving only as members of legislative councils
Picketing liquor shops, making salt and facing lathi charges
Restricting participation to spinning within the home
231.x: Gandhi brought women into public action through activities such as picketing liquor shops, making salt and facing lathis.
231.tq: Recognise the concrete activities that indicate public participation in satyagraha.

231.s: Gandhi opposed which of the following social practices and supported remarriage of child widows?
o: Inter-dining, widow remarriage and basic education
Temple entry, female education and village industries
231.x: Gandhi opposed purdah, child marriage and dowry, and supported the remarriage of child widows.
231.tq: Group the practices by Gandhi's reform position and reject unrelated constructive activities.

231.s: Which of the following statements regarding women's participation in Andhra is correct?
o: Desasevikalu functioned as a women's wing, and Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921.
Durgabai met Gandhi at Wardha in 1937 and opposed the Tilak Fund.
Women in Andhra contributed only labour and not jewellery to nationalist causes.
Desasevikalu was a Harijan men's organisation formed in Nellore in 1946.
231.x: Desasevikalu was a women's wing. Durgabai met Gandhi at Kakinada in 1921, raised Rs 5,000, and Andhra women donated jewellery to the Tilak Fund.
231.tq: Combine the organisation, place, year and contribution to identify the precise statement.

231.s: Sarva dharma samabhava signifies:
o: Separation of religion from all public prayer
The superiority of one religion over all others
Acceptance of only reformist Hindu sects
231.x: Sarva dharma samabhava means equal respect for all religions. Gandhi's ashram prayers drew upon several faiths.
231.tq: Test the exact meaning of the Sanskrit expression.

231.s: Which statement best reflects Gandhi's view of Hindu-Muslim unity?
o: It was the bedrock of nationalism, and Gandhi supported the Khilafat movement.
It was limited to private prayer and not public action.
It was unrelated to nationalism, and Gandhi opposed the Khilafat movement.
It required the political dominance of one religious community.
231.x: Gandhi regarded Hindu-Muslim unity as the bedrock of nationalism and supported the Khilafat movement.
231.tq: Link the principle with the associated political action.

231.s: Gandhi undertook fasts during communal riots in which places during 1946–47?
231.x: Gandhi fasted during communal disturbances in Calcutta and Noakhali in 1946–47.
231.tq: Match the place pair with the correct period and purpose.

231.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Gandhi's work in Andhra is correctly matched?
o: Kolla Tayaramma — Tenali; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Nellore
Kolla Tayaramma — Nellore; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Tenali
Kolla Tayaramma — Kakinada; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Vijayawada
Kolla Tayaramma — Machilipatnam; Alladi Annapurna Devi — Wardha
231.x: Kolla Tayaramma led Harijan schools and hostels at Tenali, while Alladi Annapurna Devi was associated with similar work at Nellore.
231.tq: Start with the place-person pair and eliminate the reversed match.

231.s: Gandhi's work in Andhra included which combination?
o: Collecting funds for Harijan work, campaigning against untouchability, visiting Machilipatnam for Swaraj Nidhi and promoting Ponduru khadi
Organising the Poona Pact and drafting the Zakir Hussain Committee report
Leading the Vaikom Satyagraha and founding the Lakshminarayan Temple
Starting the Khilafat movement in Noakhali and Calcutta
231.x: Gandhi toured Andhra extensively for Harijan uplift and anti-untouchability work, visited Machilipatnam for Swaraj Nidhi and was associated with Ponduru khadi.
231.tq: Select the option containing only Andhra-specific activities.

231.s: Which of the following statements about the constitutional significance of Gandhi's anti-untouchability campaign is correct?
o: The Constitution abolished caste itself through Article 17.
It kept untouchability outside the constitutional framework.
Article 17 constitutionally protected untouchability as a customary practice.
It helped make untouchability a national issue, and the Constitution abolished untouchability through Article 17.
231.x: Gandhi's campaign made untouchability a national issue, and Article 17 of the Constitution abolished untouchability. Article 17 did not abolish the entire caste system.
231.tq: Avoid the Article-number and scope trap by distinguishing untouchability from caste.

231.s: Justice B.V. Nagarathna observed, in the context of the Sabarimala reference, that untouchability:
o: May be practised for three days a month
Was abolished only in temple premises
Is exclusively a matter for religious authorities
Cannot be practised even three days a month
231.x: Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that untouchability cannot be practised ‘three days a month’ in the Sabarimala reference.
231.tq: Test the exact qualification in a judicial observation rather than its broad theme.

231.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the stated 2026 observance or initiative?
o: Sree Narayana Guru's 172nd birth anniversary — 11 April 2026
231.x: PM-AJAY provides funds for development of SC habitations. Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on 11 April 2026, while Sree Narayana Guru's 172nd birth anniversary was on 28 August 2026.
231.tq: Separate the scheme's purpose from the anniversary dates in the same theme.

231.s: Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on:
231.x: Jyotirao Phule's 200th birth anniversary was observed on 11 April 2026.
231.tq: Discriminate between two closely related social-reform anniversary dates.

231.s: Which statement about criticism of Gandhi's terminology and approach is correct?
o: Dalit leaders rejected constitutional rights but supported paternalism.
Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term ‘Harijan’ and criticised caste-Hindu paternalism.
Ambedkar accepted ‘Harijan’ as the preferred political designation.
The criticism was directed only against khadi and not against caste reform.
231.x: Ambedkar and Dalit leaders rejected the term ‘Harijan’ and criticised what they regarded as caste-Hindu paternalism.
231.tq: Distinguish the reform programme from the terminology and power-relationship critique.

231.s: Potti Sriramulu's temple-entry fasts in Nellore are associated with which year?
231.x: Potti Sriramulu undertook temple-entry fasts in Nellore in 1946. Accounts differ on the precise duration, reporting 23 days in one source and a 10-day followed by a 19-day sequence in another.
231.tq: Use the year while avoiding an uncertain duration claim.

232.s: Rajkumar Shukla, who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to visit Champaran, was a:
o: Lawyer of the Bihar High Court
232.x: Rajkumar Shukla was a local indigo cultivator and agriculturist of Champaran who persuaded Gandhi to investigate the peasants’ condition. Rajendra Prasad was an associate, not the inviter.
232.tq: Distinguish the inviter from the prominent associate.

232.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Champaran Satyagraha:
1. European planters compelled peasants to cultivate indigo.
2. The unprofitability of indigo after the emergence of synthetic dyes led planters to demand illegal dues and enhanced rents.
3. The movement was primarily directed against the collection of forest tax.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Champaran struggle concerned forced indigo cultivation and illegal exactions, not forest tax.
232.tq: Find the statement that introduces a different agrarian issue.

232.s: The system under which Champaran peasants were compelled to cultivate indigo on three-twentieths of their land was known as:
232.x: Under the Tinkathia system, Champaran peasants were compelled to grow indigo on three-twentieths of their land.
232.tq: Use the exact term for a distinctive agrarian arrangement.

232.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gandhi’s method during the Champaran Satyagraha?
o: He began an armed resistance against the European planters.
He accepted the order to leave the district and confined his work to petitions.
He called upon peasants to stop cultivating all food crops.
He defied the order to leave and, with his lawyers, recorded peasants’ complaints in the villages.
232.x: Gandhi defied the official order to leave Champaran and toured villages with his lawyers to record complaints against forced indigo cultivation. This compelled the government to order an inquiry.
232.tq: Apply the principle of non-violent civil disobedience to the historical situation.

232.s:
With reference to the outcome of the Champaran Satyagraha, consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi became a member of the official inquiry committee.
2. The Tinkathia system was abolished.
3. Peasants received a refund of 25 per cent of the illegal exactions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: All three statements are correct. Gandhi served on the inquiry committee, the Tinkathia system was abolished through the Champaran Agrarian Act, and 25 per cent of illegal exactions was refunded.
232.tq: Check whether all outcome-related statements belong to the same settlement.

232.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched in the context of Champaran?
o: Mahadev Desai — Leader of the European planters
232.x: Mahadev Desai was Gandhi’s secretary and pledged himself to the Champaran work in 1917. He was not a leader of the European planters.
232.tq: Identify the wrong person-role association.

232.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the struggle with its distinctive description?
o: Rowlatt Satyagraha — first civil disobedience by Gandhi in India
232.x: Kheda is identified as Gandhi’s first non-cooperation movement. Champaran was the first satyagraha and first civil disobedience by Gandhi in India, while Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first all-India mass strike.
232.tq: Compare the closely related ‘firsts’ instead of recalling them in isolation.

232.s: The immediate agrarian cause of the Kheda Satyagraha was:
o: Demand for a 50 per cent increase in industrial wages
Crop failure due to drought or famine and refusal of revenue remission
232.x: The Kheda peasants suffered crop failure caused by drought or famine and sought remission or suspension of land revenue, which the government initially refused.
232.tq: Separate agrarian grievances from industrial labour disputes.

232.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kheda Satyagraha:
1. It took place in Kheda district of Gujarat.
2. Peasants refused to pay land revenue despite threats of confiscation of land.
3. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel provided field leadership to the movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: All three statements are correct. The 1918 movement occurred in Kheda, Gujarat; peasants resisted revenue payment despite threats, and Vallabhbhai Patel gave field leadership.
232.tq: Verify place, method of resistance and field leadership together.

232.s: The Kheda Satyagraha was called off after the government agreed to:
o: Abolish the Tinkathia system throughout Gujarat
Collect revenue only from those able to pay, suspend it for poor peasants and return confiscated property
Appoint Gandhi as the sole member of a revenue commission
Grant a 50 per cent wage increase to agricultural labourers
232.x: The settlement provided that revenue would be collected only from those able to pay, revenue would be suspended for poor peasants, and confiscated property would be returned.
232.tq: Distinguish the settlement terms from the original grievance.

232.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
232.x: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike took place in Gujarat in 1918. Champaran was in Bihar in 1917, while Kheda was in Gujarat in 1918.
232.tq: Use the place-year combination to separate similar contemporary movements.

232.s: In the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, the workers’ demand and the mill owners’ offer were, respectively:
o: 20 per cent wage increase and 35 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and 20 per cent increase
35 per cent wage increase and 50 per cent increase
50 per cent wage increase and complete withdrawal of wages
232.x: The workers demanded a 50 per cent wage increase because of wartime inflation, while the mill owners offered only 20 per cent.
232.tq: Match the two competing numerical demands without reversing them.

232.s: Why did the Ahmedabad textile workers approach Anusuya Sarabhai?
o: She was the government-appointed chairperson of the Kheda inquiry.
She supported their dispute and appealed to Gandhi on their behalf.
She represented the European planters of Champaran.
She had introduced the Tinkathia system in Gujarat.
232.x: The workers approached Anusuya Sarabhai, who supported their cause and appealed to Gandhi. Her brother Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners.
232.tq: Track the mediator’s role rather than confusing her with the employer.

232.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ahmedabad Mill Strike:
1. Ambalal Sarabhai led the mill owners.
2. Gandhi advised the workers to demand a 35 per cent increase.
3. A tribunal awarded the workers a 35 per cent increase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: All three statements are correct. Ambalal Sarabhai represented the mill owners, Gandhi advised a 35 per cent demand, and the tribunal awarded a 35 per cent increase.
232.tq: Combine the employer, Gandhi’s advice and the final adjudication.

232.s: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, also known as Majoor Mahajan Sangh, was founded in 1920 by:
o: Ambalal Sarabhai with Vallabhbhai Patel’s guidance
J.B. Kripalani with Anugrah Narayan Sinha’s guidance
232.x: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, or Majoor Mahajan Sangh, was founded in 1920 by Anusuya Sarabhai with Gandhi’s guidance.
232.tq: Distinguish the labour organisation’s founder from the mill-owner representative.

232.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the wider significance of the Champaran, Kheda and Ahmedabad struggles?
o: They confined Gandhi’s work exclusively to urban middle-class politics.
They connected Gandhi with peasants and labour, and constituted an early large-scale test of non-violent protest.
They immediately resulted in the end of British rule in India.
They were all movements against the Rowlatt Act.
232.x: The three struggles connected Gandhi with peasants in Champaran and Kheda and with labour in Ahmedabad. They provided an important large-scale test of non-violent protest before the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
232.tq: Select the option that covers the common significance without an extreme claim.

232.s: Which of the following leaders was associated with the Kheda Satyagraha and became an important partner in the Gandhi–Patel alliance?
232.x: Vallabhbhai Patel provided field leadership in Kheda and thereby began the important Gandhi–Patel alliance. The other names were associated mainly with the Champaran work.
232.tq: Match the leader with the correct satyagraha rather than the associate group.

232.s: Which of the following was NOT among the leaders recruited or closely associated with Gandhi through the Champaran work?
232.x: Ambalal Sarabhai led the Ahmedabad mill owners. Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha and Mahadev Desai were associated with the Champaran work.
232.tq: Find the person belonging to the neighbouring Ahmedabad dispute.

232.s: The Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda struggles took place during the viceroyalty of:
232.x: All three struggles occurred during the viceroyalty of Lord Chelmsford, who served from 1916 to 1921.
232.tq: Use the common chronological frame to identify the viceroy.

232.s: The Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee was appointed by the:
232.x: The Bihar and Orissa government appointed the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee in 1917 after Gandhi’s investigation into the peasants’ complaints.
232.tq: Identify the authority from the geographical location of the inquiry.

232.s:
Consider the following statements about the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee:
1. Gandhi was a member of the committee representing the ryots.
2. F.G. Sly chaired the committee.
3. The committee consisted exclusively of representatives of European planters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Gandhi represented the ryots and F.G. Sly chaired the committee. Statement 3 is false because the committee was not exclusively composed of planters’ representatives.
232.tq: Reject an exclusive-composition statement when the committee included the ryots’ representative.

232.s:
Arrange the following developments in the correct chronological order:
A. Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee appointed
B. Champaran Agrarian Act abolishing Tinkathia
C. Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association founded
D. Champaran Satyagraha begins

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
232.x: The Champaran Satyagraha began in 1917, the inquiry committee was appointed during the same inquiry, the Agrarian Act followed in 1918, and the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association was founded in 1920.
232.tq: Fix the years first and then place events within the 1917–1920 sequence.

232.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the result of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee’s recommendations?
o: Introduction of a permanent settlement in Gujarat
Grant of a 50 per cent wage increase to Ahmedabad workers
Abolition of Tinkathia and partial refund of illegal exactions
Suspension of all land revenue throughout India
232.x: The recommendations led to the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918, which abolished Tinkathia and secured a partial refund—25 per cent—of illegal exactions.
232.tq: Match the committee with its specific legislative outcome.

232.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
232.x: Champaran concerned forced indigo cultivation and illegal dues. The wartime industrial wage dispute and plague bonus were associated with the Ahmedabad Mill Strike.
232.tq: Separate the agrarian issues from the industrial labour issue.

232.s:
The later exactions imposed on indigo cultivators in Champaran included:
1. Sharahbeshi, or enhanced rent.
2. Tawan, or lump-sum compensation demanded when indigo lost its value.
3. Abolition of all rent obligations of tenants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: Sharahbeshi was enhanced rent, while tawan was lump-sum compensation extracted when indigo became less valuable. The system did not abolish the tenants’ rent obligations.
232.tq: Separate the two genuine exactions from the absolute claim about abolition of rent.

232.s: Which event is regarded as the precursor to the Champaran indigo movement?
232.x: The Bengal Indigo Revolt of 1859 preceded and served as an important precursor to the later indigo-related mobilisation in Champaran.
232.tq: Identify the earlier related movement rather than the later Gandhian campaign.

232.s: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike associated with Mahatma Gandhi took place during:
232.x: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike took place in February–March 1918.
232.tq: Use the month range to distinguish closely placed movements.

232.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was observed on an all-India basis on:
232.x: The all-India hartal and Satyagraha against the Rowlatt legislation took place on 6 April 1919.
232.tq: Distinguish the date of the satyagraha from the dates of the Act, massacre and withdrawal.

232.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Jallianwala Bagh firing is correct?
1. It took place on Baisakhi, 13 April 1919.
2. Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer blocked the exits.
3. Dyer ordered firing without giving the gathering a warning.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
232.x: All three statements are correct. The firing occurred on Baisakhi, Dyer blocked the exits and ordered firing without warning.
232.tq: Confirm each statement against the event’s date, commander and immediate action.

232.s: How many rounds were fired by the troops under General Dyer at Jallianwala Bagh?
232.x: The troops fired 1,650 rounds at the unarmed gathering.
232.tq: Choose the precise numerical figure rather than a nearby casualty-related number.

232.s: According to the official figures, the casualties in the Jallianwala Bagh firing were approximately:
232.x: The official figures recorded 379 deaths and 1,100 injuries, although the Indian National Congress estimated a higher death toll.
232.tq: Keep official figures separate from alternative estimates and firing-round data.

232.s: Who was the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab when the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred?
232.x: Michael O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab. Reginald Dyer was the officer who ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh.
232.tq: Separate the provincial administrator from the officer who conducted the firing.

232.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hunter Committee:
1. It was appointed after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
2. It condemned the conduct of General Dyer.
3. The House of Lords supported Dyer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: The Hunter Committee was appointed after the massacre and condemned Dyer’s conduct, while the House of Lords backed him.
232.tq: Test the contrast between the official inquiry’s condemnation and the House of Lords’ support.

232.s: Mahatma Gandhi gave up which distinction in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
o: Order of the Star of India
232.x: Gandhi surrendered the Kaiser-i-Hind medal in protest. Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood.
232.tq: Match the protester with the specific honour he relinquished.

232.s: Mahatma Gandhi stayed in South Africa from 1893 until his return to India. Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
232.x: Phoenix Settlement was established in 1904 near Durban. Tolstoy Farm was established in 1910 near Johannesburg.
232.tq: Start with the sure pair linking the settlement, year and location.

232.s: Tolstoy Farm, associated with Gandhi’s South African phase, was established in 1910 near:
232.x: Tolstoy Farm was established in 1910 near Johannesburg.
232.tq: Discriminate between the locations of Gandhi’s two South African settlements.

232.s: Which of the following was the journal published by Mahatma Gandhi during his South African period?
232.x: Indian Opinion was the journal associated with Gandhi’s South African period. Young India, Harijan and Navajivan were associated with his later Indian activities.
232.tq: Use the geographical phase to identify the corresponding publication.

232.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Gandhi’s intellectual influences?
o: Lord Curzon — political mentor of Gandhi
Henry David Thoreau — influence on Gandhi
232.x: Lord Curzon was not Gandhi’s political mentor. Tolstoy, Ruskin’s Unto This Last and Thoreau influenced Gandhi, while Gopal Krishna Gokhale was his political mentor.
232.tq: Find the mismatched person among a group of genuine intellectual influences.

232.s: Gandhi returned to India on 9 January 1915. This date is commemorated as:
232.x: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas commemorates Gandhi’s return to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
232.tq: Link the exact date with the commemoration rather than with a movement.

232.s: After returning to India, Gandhi spent about a year touring the country without taking political positions on the advice of:
232.x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale advised Gandhi to tour India for a year without taking political positions, enabling him to understand the country’s conditions.
232.tq: Identify the mentor connected with the specific advice rather than a general nationalist association.

232.s: Which one of the following was NOT a journal associated with Mahatma Gandhi?
232.x: Mathrubhumi was not associated with Gandhi. Young India, Navajivan and Harijan were among his journals.
232.tq: Eliminate the outsider from a closely related list of publications.

232.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: The Story of My Experiments with Truth — 1915
Young India — Gandhi’s South African autobiography
Harijan — a work written by Henry Thoreau
232.x: Hind Swaraj was written in 1909. The Story of My Experiments with Truth was Gandhi’s autobiography, while Young India and Harijan were journals.
232.tq: Match a writing with its correct year while rejecting swapped genres and authors.

232.s:
Arrange the following ashrams in chronological order of their establishment:
A. Sabarmati Ashram
B. Sevagram Ashram
C. Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
232.x: The Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab was established in 1915, Sabarmati Ashram in 1917 and Sevagram in Wardha in 1936.
232.tq: Place the earliest and latest ashrams first, then resolve the middle date.

232.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
232.x: Gandhi’s Satyagraha Ashram was established at Kochrab in Ahmedabad in 1915. Sabarmati was in Ahmedabad, Sevagram was in Wardha and Phoenix Settlement was near Durban.
232.tq: Use location-based elimination among Gandhi’s Indian and South African settlements.

232.s: Sevagram Ashram at Wardha was established in:
232.x: Sevagram Ashram at Wardha was established in 1936.
232.tq: Distinguish the late ashram date from the two early Ahmedabad ashram dates.

232.s: Who is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’?
232.x: Rabindranath Tagore is credited with giving Gandhi the title ‘Mahatma’. Subhas Chandra Bose is associated with the title ‘Father of the Nation’ for Gandhi.
232.tq: Distinguish the persons associated with Gandhi’s two well-known titles.

232.s: Gandhi’s first arrest by the British Government for sedition occurred when he was detained at:
232.x: In April 1919 Gandhi was stopped and detained at Palwal while proceeding towards Punjab; the incident contributed to riots.
232.tq: Separate the place of the first detention from the place of the later sedition trial.

232.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Gandhi’s Great Trial:
1. It was held at Ahmedabad in March 1922.
2. The charge was sedition under Section 124A.
3. The charge arose from articles published in Young India.
4. Gandhi was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: All four statements are correct. Gandhi’s 1922 Ahmedabad trial concerned sedition under Section 124A in relation to his Young India articles and resulted in a six-year sentence.
232.tq: Verify the venue, year, legal provision, publication and sentence together.

232.s: Who presided as the judge in Gandhi’s Great Trial at Ahmedabad in 1922?
232.x: Judge Broomfield presided over Gandhi’s sedition trial at Ahmedabad in March 1922.
232.tq: Match the judicial officer with the trial rather than with the political administration.

232.s: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 extended the repressive powers earlier provided under the:
232.x: The Rowlatt Act extended the emergency powers of the Defence of India Act, 1915 into the post-war period.
232.tq: Identify the earlier statute whose extraordinary powers were continued.

232.s:
Which of the following provisions was associated with the Rowlatt Act?
1. Detention without trial for up to two years.
2. Suspension of habeas corpus.
3. The legal formula ‘No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal’.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
232.x: The Act permitted detention without trial for up to two years and suspended habeas corpus, giving rise to the description ‘No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal’.
232.tq: Recognise the three linked features of the repressive legislation.

232.s: Which of the following combinations is correctly matched with the Rowlatt Act protests?
o: Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — resigned in opposition to the Act
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — drafted the Hunter Committee report
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — served as members of the Satyagraha Sabha
Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq — defended General Dyer
232.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Rowlatt legislation.
232.tq: Match the group of political figures with their common act of protest.

232.s: The Satyagraha Sabha was established in:
232.x: The Satyagraha Sabha was formed in Bombay in February 1919, using the networks of the Home Rule League.
232.tq: Combine the organisation’s location and date to distinguish it from later events.

232.s: The Rowlatt Satyagraha hartal of 6 April 1919 was observed through:
o: A campaign for compulsory military recruitment
Armed rebellion and seizure of courts
232.x: The 6 April 1919 hartal involved fasting and prayer and became the first all-India mass strike of the movement.
232.tq: Identify the method of action from the non-violent character of the satyagraha.

232.s: Why did Gandhi call off the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919?
o: The Hunter Committee accepted all nationalist demands
The Rowlatt Act had been repealed
The British Government granted complete independence
232.x: Gandhi withdrew the movement on 18 April 1919 after violence occurred, later describing the decision to launch it as a ‘Himalayan blunder’.
232.tq: Link the withdrawal to its immediate cause rather than to a political concession.

232.s: Gandhi described his decision to launch the Rowlatt Satyagraha as a:
232.x: After the movement led to violence and was called off, Gandhi described the decision to launch it as a ‘Himalayan blunder’.
232.tq: Recall the distinctive phrase associated with Gandhi’s self-assessment.

232.s: The year of Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran pro-ryot movement was
232.x: The Champaran pro-ryot movement took place in 1917. The year 1915 is an incorrect attribution sometimes made in secondary material.
232.tq: Use the confusable-year trap by distinguishing the correct date from a nearby but incorrect year.

232.s: The period 1917–1919 is considered significant in Gandhi’s political career because it
o: resulted in the adoption of Complete Independence as the Congress objective
marked the beginning of his political work in South Africa
established Gandhi as a national leader and Satyagraha as a method of struggle
marked the launch of the Quit India Movement
232.x: The Champaran, Ahmedabad and related struggles between 1917 and 1919 established Gandhi as a national leader and Satyagraha as an important method of anti-colonial struggle.
232.tq: Identify the option that combines the precise significance of a historical period without importing later events.

232.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the Gandhian sequence of firsts?
232.x: Kheda is associated with Gandhi’s first non-cooperation in this sequence. Champaran was the first Satyagraha in India, while Ahmedabad was associated with his first fast.
232.tq: Separate closely related Gandhian movements by matching each movement with its distinctive first.

232.s: Champaran Satyagraha and Kheda Satyagraha were important in the history of Andhra Pradesh because they
o: led to the establishment of Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika
directly resulted in the formation of Andhra State
were organised by Andhra leaders in Bihar and Gujarat
232.x: The Champaran movement of 1917 and the Kheda movement of 1918 inspired peasant movements in Andhra. They did not directly lead to the formation of Andhra State.
232.tq: Apply a national movement fact to its stated regional significance rather than confusing influence with direct causation.

232.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the hartal associated with the Rowlatt Act in Andhra:
1. Vizag and Rajahmundry observed the peaceful hartal on 6 April.
2. Guntur, Vijayawada and Nellore were among the other places where the peaceful hartal was observed on 6 April.
3. The hartal in these places was held on 8 April.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
232.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the peaceful hartal was observed on 6 April in Vizag, Rajahmundry, Guntur, Vijayawada and Nellore. Statement 3 is false; 8 April is associated with Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada.
232.tq: Find the false date statement while preserving the correct list of places.

232.s: Mahatma Gandhi visited Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, and his speech there was translated by
232.x: Gandhi visited Vijayawada on 8 April 1919, and Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao translated his speech.
232.tq: Use the place-date-person combination to avoid swapping a regional associate with another Andhra leader.

232.s: Which of the following newspapers opposed the Rowlatt Act in Andhra?
232.x: Andhra Patrika and Krishna Patrika opposed the Rowlatt Act. The other pairs contain newspapers associated with different regions or contexts.
232.tq: Match the regional newspapers with the political issue with which they were associated.

232.s: A report published on 14 January 2026 traced the history of “indigo blue” from the Bengal peasants’ refusal to grow indigo in 1859 to Champaran nearly six decades later. The report was published in
232.x: The Hindu traced the connection from the Bengal indigo refusal of 1859 to Champaran nearly sixty years later, presenting Champaran as a launch pad for a new anti-colonial method.
232.tq: Link the current-affairs publication with the historical event and its long-term significance.

232.s: The Gandhi profile published by LENS in February 2026 repeated which of the following triad?
o: First Home Rule movement, first boycott and first individual Satyagraha
First mass arrest, first revolutionary movement and first peasant revolt
First civil disobedience, first hunger strike and first non-cooperation
First national flag, first fasting campaign and first constitutional reform
232.x: The LENS profile repeated the triad of Gandhi’s first civil disobedience, first hunger strike and first non-cooperation, associated respectively with Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda in the stated sequence.
232.tq: Recognise the exact three-part formulation and reject options that substitute unrelated movements or events.

233.s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on which of the following occasions?
233.x: The massacre took place on 13 April 1919, the day of Baisakhi.
233.tq: Use the exact date-place association rather than relying on nearby Rowlatt Satyagraha dates.

233.s:
With reference to the Jallianwala Bagh incident, consider the following statements:
1. The incident took place at Amritsar in Punjab.
2. Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy of India.
3. Sir Michael O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
233.x: All three statements are correct. The massacre occurred at Amritsar, Lord Chelmsford was Viceroy, and Sir Michael O'Dwyer was Punjab's Lieutenant Governor.
233.tq: Split the statements into place, Viceroy and provincial authority before selecting the coded option.

233.s: Who were arrested in connection with the anti-Rowlatt protests at Amritsar and became the immediate focus of the crowd's demand for release?
o: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal
233.x: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were arrested for organising anti-Rowlatt protests. They symbolised Hindu-Muslim unity in Punjab.
233.tq: Distinguish the arrested local leaders from later inquiry-committee members and national leaders.

233.s: On 10 April 1919, troops opened fire at Amritsar when a crowd was demanding the
o: release of Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal
abolition of the Home Rule Leagues
release of Motilal Nehru and C.R. Das
233.x: The firing on 10 April followed public demands for the release of Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal.
233.tq: Link the immediate local confrontation to the two arrested leaders, not to later national movements.

233.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the action taken by Sir Michael O'Dwyer before the Jallianwala Bagh firing?
o: He appointed the Hunter Committee and suspended martial law.
He ordered Udham Singh to address the gathering peacefully.
He transferred Amritsar to Lord William Hunter and permitted public meetings.
He handed Amritsar to Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer and imposed a ban on assemblies.
233.x: O'Dwyer handed Amritsar to Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer, who banned assemblies before the firing.
233.tq: Use the wrong-authority and swapped-person trap carefully: O'Dwyer was the provincial authority, while Dyer commanded the troops.

233.s: Which of the following statements regarding the firing at Jallianwala Bagh is NOT correct?
o: The firing continued for about ten minutes and involved 1,650 rounds.
The crowd had assembled in a walled garden.
The only exit was blocked by Dyer's troops.
The crowd was given a clear warning and sufficient time to disperse before firing began.
233.x: Dyer blocked the only exit and fired without warning for about ten minutes, using 1,650 rounds.
233.tq: Find the statement that reverses the central feature of the incident: firing without warning and with the exit blocked.

233.s:
Consider the following statements about the reported casualties at Jallianwala Bagh:
1. The official figure recorded 379 deaths.
2. The official estimate mentioned about 1,100 injured.
3. The Indian National Congress estimated the deaths at over 1,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
233.x: The official figures were 379 dead and about 1,100 injured, while the Congress estimate placed deaths above 1,000.
233.tq: Keep official and nationalist estimates separate instead of treating the casualty figures as identical.

233.s: Who wrote the Telugu play ‘Panchala Parabhavam’ on General Dyer?
233.x: Damaraju Pundarikakshudu wrote the Telugu play ‘Panchala Parabhavam’ on Dyer.
233.tq: Test the author-work association directly, a common history matching trap.

233.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Rabindranath Tagore
b. C. Sankaran Nair
c. Mahatma Gandhi

List-II (Protest)
i. Returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal
ii. Renounced the Knighthood
iii. Resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: Tagore renounced his Knighthood, C. Sankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council, and Gandhi returned the Kaiser-i-Hind medal.
233.tq: Start from the sure pair Tagore–Knighthood and then eliminate the remaining combinations.

233.s: Which of the following correctly pairs an event with its year?
o: Home Rule Leagues and Lucknow Pact — 1916
233.x: The Home Rule Leagues and the Lucknow Pact are associated with 1916. Champaran was in 1917, the Dandi March in 1930 and Quit India in 1942.
233.tq: Use the year-event pair directly and reject options shifted to adjacent milestones.

233.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact belongs to which year?
233.x: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was concluded in 1931.
233.tq: Differentiate the pact year from the nearby Dandi March of 1930 and Communal Award-Poona Pact of 1932.

233.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
233.x: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928. The events of 1942 were the Cripps Mission and the Quit India Movement.
233.tq: Find the swapped event-year association among closely spaced national movement milestones.

233.s: The Hunter Committee was appointed by the British Government in October 1919 primarily to inquire into
o: the Chauri Chaura incident and withdrawal of Non-Cooperation
the constitutional reforms proposed by the Home Rule Leagues
the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and disturbances in Punjab
the causes of the Swadeshi Movement in Bengal
233.x: The committee was appointed to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the disturbances in Punjab.
233.tq: Identify the exact event and regional disturbances associated with the committee.

233.s: Who chaired the Hunter Committee appointed to inquire into the Punjab disturbances?
233.x: The committee was chaired by Lord William Hunter.
233.tq: Avoid the officer-swapping trap by separating the committee chairman from the Viceroy and Punjab officials.

233.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian members of the Hunter Committee:
1. Chimanlal Setalvad was an Indian member.
2. Jagat Narayan was an Indian member.
3. Sultan Ahmed Khan was an Indian member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
233.x: Chimanlal Setalvad, Jagat Narayan and Sultan Ahmed Khan were among the Indian members of the Hunter Committee.
233.tq: Check every listed member rather than assuming that only the best-known name belongs to the committee.

233.s: The minority report of the Indian members of the Hunter Committee was particularly critical of
233.x: The Indian members submitted a minority report that was more critical of Dyer's conduct.
233.tq: Distinguish the subject criticised in the report from the person who chaired the inquiry.

233.s: Which one of the following statements about the outcome of the Hunter Committee inquiry is correct?
o: Dyer was censured and relieved of command, but received no real punishment.
Dyer was sentenced to life imprisonment by the House of Lords.
The committee fully exonerated Dyer and retained him in command.
The committee ordered the immediate abolition of martial law throughout India.
233.x: The committee censured Dyer, who was relieved of command, but he did not receive real punishment. The House of Lords backed him, and Gandhi called the findings a whitewash.
233.tq: Separate formal censure and relief from command from the absence of substantial punishment.

233.s: The Rowlatt Act was based on the recommendations of the Sedition Committee headed by
233.x: The Sedition Committee, also known as the Rowlatt Committee, was headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt.
233.tq: Use the committee-chairman association and avoid confusing the Rowlatt and Hunter inquiries.

233.s:
Which of the following provisions was associated with the Rowlatt Act?
1. Arrest and detention without trial for up to two years
2. Suspension of habeas corpus
3. Establishment of special tribunals
4. Curbs on the press
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: The Act extended extraordinary wartime powers, including detention without trial up to two years, suspension of habeas corpus, special tribunals and press restrictions.
233.tq: Read the list as a cluster of coercive provisions and reject partial combinations when all four are supported.

233.s: The phrase “No Vakil, No Dalil, No Appeal” was associated with opposition to the
233.x: The phrase expressed opposition to the denial of ordinary legal safeguards under the Rowlatt Act, popularly called the Black Act.
233.tq: Associate the slogan with the legal disabilities created by the Rowlatt legislation.

233.s: The hartal called by Gandhi against the Rowlatt Act was observed on
233.x: Gandhi called a nationwide hartal for 6 April 1919, involving fasting, prayer and protest against the Act.
233.tq: Separate the dates of the warning, Act, hartal and withdrawal of the Satyagraha.

233.s: Which statement best describes the character of the Rowlatt Satyagraha?
o: It began as a military rebellion against the British Indian Army.
It was the first all-India mass strike and was primarily urban-centred.
It was a constitutional campaign conducted only inside legislative councils.
It remained exclusively confined to rural Punjab and never spread elsewhere.
233.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first all-India mass strike and was urban-centred, although it later became violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad.
233.tq: Choose the precise description and reject absolute claims such as ‘exclusively’ and ‘never’.

233.s: Why did Gandhi withdraw the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919?
o: The Hunter Committee accepted all Congress demands.
The Home Rule League advised him to suspend the campaign permanently.
The British Government repealed the Rowlatt Act immediately.
Violence in Punjab and Ahmedabad led him to describe the campaign as a Himalayan blunder.
233.x: The movement turned violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad, prompting Gandhi to call it a Himalayan blunder and withdraw it on 18 April 1919.
233.tq: Connect the decision to withdraw with the movement's violence and Gandhi's stated assessment.

233.s:
Which of the following places in Andhra witnessed peaceful hartals against the Rowlatt Act?
1. Visakhapatnam
2. Rajahmundry
3. Guntur
4. Vijayawada
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: Peaceful hartals were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry, Guntur, Vijayawada and Nellore.
233.tq: Treat the regional list as cumulative; the omitted fifth place does not make the four listed places incorrect.

233.s: Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer at which place?
233.x: Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall in London on 13 March 1940.
233.tq: Distinguish Michael O'Dwyer from General Dyer and match the assassination with its London location.

233.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Udham Singh:
1. He shot Michael O'Dwyer.
2. The incident occurred in London.
3. The shooting took place on 13 March 1940.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
233.x: Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer in London on 13 March 1940. The target was O'Dwyer, not Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer.
233.tq: Check target, place and date separately to avoid the Dyer–O'Dwyer confusion.

233.s:
The Congress's non-official inquiry into the Punjab events was conducted by the Punjab Sub-Committee consisting of which of the following persons?
1. Motilal Nehru
2. C.R. Das
3. Abbas Tyabji
4. M.R. Jayakar
5. Mahatma Gandhi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: The Punjab Sub-Committee included Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, Abbas Tyabji, M.R. Jayakar and Gandhi.
233.tq: Verify all names in the complete committee list before choosing a partial code.

233.s: The Congress inquiry committee characterised Dyer's firing as inhuman and described martial law as
233.x: The Congress inquiry condemned Dyer's firing as inhuman and considered the martial law measures disproportionate; it demanded action against Dyer.
233.tq: Identify the precise evaluative term used for the martial-law measures.

233.s:
Which of the following measures was associated with martial law in Amritsar and Lahore after 13 April 1919?
1. Public floggings
2. Aircraft strafing of protestors
3. The crawling order
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: Martial law included public floggings, aircraft strafing of protestors and the humiliating crawling order.
233.tq: Group the coercive measures under martial law and test whether the option covers the full set.

233.s: The crawling order required Indians to crawl on their bellies through the lane where which person had been assaulted?
o: Marcella Sherwood, an English woman missionary
233.x: The order was imposed in the Amritsar lane where Marcella Sherwood, an English woman missionary, had been assaulted.
233.tq: Match the humiliating order with the specific incident and person involved.

233.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Mahatma Gandhi during the Punjab disturbances?
o: He commanded the troops at Jallianwala Bagh.
He was appointed chairman of the Hunter Committee.
He was stopped from entering Punjab.
233.x: Gandhi was stopped from entering Punjab during the disturbances.
233.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ test to separate Gandhi's role from official military actions.

233.s: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre had which broader political consequence?
o: It immediately resulted in the repeal of the Government of India Act, 1935.
It destroyed Indian faith in British justice and fed directly into the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation Movement.
It led to the permanent suspension of all mass movements by Gandhi.
It ended opposition to British rule and strengthened confidence in colonial justice.
233.x: The massacre severely damaged Indian faith in British justice and contributed directly to the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements.
233.tq: Select the consequence that follows historically from the event rather than an immediate constitutional claim.

233.s:
Which of the following regional bodies condemned the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
1. Ganjam district conference
2. Godavari district conference
3. Krishna district conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
233.x: The Ganjam, Godavari and Krishna district conferences condemned the massacre.
233.tq: Check each regional conference individually before selecting the complete combination.

233.s: At which meeting and in which month of 1919 did Prakasam demand fundamental rights in connection with the political response to the massacre?
233.x: Prakasam demanded fundamental rights at the Nellore meeting in September 1919.
233.tq: Combine the local place and month instead of selecting a better-known national venue.

233.s: On the 106th anniversary of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 2025, the Prime Minister recalled the resignation of
233.x: The Prime Minister recalled C. Sankaran Nair's resignation from the Viceroy's Executive Council on the 106th anniversary in April 2025.
233.tq: Link the current-affairs reference to the specific form of protest, not to title renunciation or medal return.

233.s: K. Kamaraj joined the freedom struggle after which event?
233.x: K. Kamaraj joined the freedom struggle after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
233.tq: Distinguish the personal turning point from the major movements and incidents used as distractors.

234.s: Which one of the following was NOT a background factor behind the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
234.x: The Simon Commission Report was not a background factor in the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement. The Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Khilafat issue were important causes.
234.tq: Find the historically later event that does not belong among the immediate causes.

234.s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920?
234.x: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided over the Nagpur session of the Congress in December 1920.
234.tq: Match the session with its presiding president rather than with the president of the Calcutta session.

234.s:
Which of the following decisions was taken at the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920?
1. The Non-Cooperation programme was ratified unanimously.
2. The goal was defined as attainment of Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means.
3. Provincial Congress Committees were organised on linguistic lines.
4. Congress membership fee was fixed at one rupee.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: The Nagpur session unanimously ratified the programme, defined Swaraj in peaceful and legitimate terms, and reorganised Congress units on linguistic lines with committees extending to village level. The membership fee was fixed at one-fourth of an anna, not one rupee.
234.tq: Check the precise numerical detail in the programme instead of accepting a broad statement about membership.

234.s: The membership fee fixed by the Nagpur session for the Indian National Congress was
234.x: The Nagpur session fixed the Congress membership fee at one-fourth of an anna.
234.tq: Test the small numerical figure directly, as such details are easily confused with other Congress fees.

234.s: Which one of the following was the final stage contemplated in the programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: Formation of a separate Muslim state
234.x: Non-payment of taxes was contemplated as the final stage of the Non-Cooperation programme. The movement initially emphasised peaceful boycott and constructive work.
234.tq: Identify the final stage of escalation within a stated programme.

234.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents a boycott measure and a constructive measure of the Non-Cooperation Movement respectively?
o: Boycott of foreign cloth and promotion of khadi
Participation in legislatures and promotion of imported cloth
Promotion of government schools and boycott of panchayat courts
Payment of taxes and establishment of durbars
234.x: Boycott of foreign cloth was a negative programme measure, while promotion of khadi was a constructive measure. Panchayat courts, national education and prohibition were also constructive activities.
234.tq: Separate the boycott programme from the constructive programme by comparing the nature of each activity.

234.s:
With reference to the programme of the Non-Cooperation Movement, consider the following statements:
1. It included surrender of titles.
2. It encouraged the boycott of government schools and colleges.
3. It advocated justice through panchayat courts.
4. It required participation in the November 1920 legislative elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: Surrender of titles, boycott of government educational institutions and replacement of government courts by panchayat courts formed part of the programme. The November 1920 legislative elections were to be boycotted.
234.tq: Reject the reversed-action statement concerning the legislative elections.

234.s: The Tilak Swaraj Fund associated with the Non-Cooperation Movement had a target of
234.x: The Tilak Swaraj Fund had a target and collection of one crore rupees.
234.tq: Test the exact fund target with nearby monetary distractors.

234.s: Which of the following persons was NOT included among the lawyers who gave up legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
234.x: Motilal Nehru, Jawaharlal Nehru, C.R. Das, C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, Asaf Ali, T. Prakasam and Rajendra Prasad were among the lawyers who gave up practice. B.R. Ambedkar was not included in this group.
234.tq: Find the person inserted from a nearby national-leader group but absent from the specified list.

234.s: Approximately how many national schools and colleges emerged during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
234.x: Approximately 800 national schools and colleges came up during the movement as part of the programme of national education.
234.tq: Test the approximate scale of institutional expansion using distinct numerical ranges.

234.s: Which one of the following statements best describes the larger political significance of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: It confined nationalism to constitutional moderates.
It immediately achieved Swaraj within one year.
It ended all communal tensions permanently.
It made the Indian National Congress a mass force for the first time.
234.x: Although Swaraj was not achieved within one year, the Non-Cooperation Movement became the first nationwide mass movement and transformed the Congress into a mass force.
234.tq: Distinguish the lasting political outcome from the unfulfilled slogan and exaggerated claims.

234.s: Mahatma Gandhi returned which distinction at the time of launching the Non-Cooperation Movement?
234.x: Gandhi returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal when he launched the Non-Cooperation Movement on 1 August 1920.
234.tq: Distinguish Gandhi’s returned honour from other titles associated with the national movement.

234.s: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn through the Bardoli resolution adopted on
234.x: The Bardoli resolution of 11–12 February 1922 turned the Congress towards constructive work after the movement was withdrawn.
234.tq: Distinguish the withdrawal resolution date from the date of the Chauri Chaura incident and Gandhi’s arrest.

234.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a consequence of the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
o: M.N. Roy described it as a complete triumph of revolutionary leadership.
Subhas Chandra Bose described it as sprinkling cold water on national enthusiasm.
The Khilafat issue became stronger and more influential.
234.x: Subhas Chandra Bose criticised the withdrawal as the equivalent of sprinkling cold water on national enthusiasm. M.N. Roy described it as evidence of weak leadership; subsequently the Khilafat issue declined and communal riots occurred during 1921–27.
234.tq: Use attributed quotations and reversed consequences as traps in a result-based question.

234.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I (Event)                         List-II (Date)
a. Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh    i. 1919
a. Treaty of Sevres                     ii. May 1920
c. Prince of Wales boycott              iii. 17 November 1921
d. Bardoli resolution                   iv. 11–12 February 1922

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: The Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh belong to 1919; the Treaty of Sevres was signed in May 1920; the Prince of Wales boycott occurred on 17 November 1921; and the Bardoli resolution was adopted on 11–12 February 1922.
234.tq: Start with the sure date pair and eliminate codes containing a shifted event.

234.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chauri Chaura incident:
1. It occurred in Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces.
2. The police fired upon or lathi-charged a procession.
3. The crowd burnt the police station.
4. The incident occurred during the boycott of the Prince of Wales visit in November 1921.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: Chauri Chaura occurred in Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces after police action against a procession, following which the crowd burnt the police station. The incident occurred in February 1922, not during the Prince of Wales boycott of November 1921.
234.tq: Identify the correct event setting while rejecting the chronology trap in statement 4.

234.s: Which person among the following was beaten by the police during the events leading to the Chauri Chaura incident?
234.x: Bhagwan Ahir was among those beaten by the police before the crowd attacked and burnt the Chauri Chaura police station.
234.tq: Test the lesser-known individual connected with the immediate local event rather than the nationally famous leaders.

234.s: How many policemen were generally reported to have been killed when the Chauri Chaura police station was burnt?
234.x: The incident is generally reported to have resulted in the death of 22 policemen, although some accounts mention 21.
234.tq: Handle a close numerical pair by selecting the figure identified as the general report while recognising the recorded variation.

234.s: Who provided legal defence to the accused in the Chauri Chaura case?
234.x: Madan Mohan Malaviya defended the accused persons in the Chauri Chaura case.
234.tq: Use the lawyer–case association rather than confusing the defence counsel with prominent Congress lawyers.

234.s: Of the 172 persons sentenced to death in the Chauri Chaura case, how many were finally hanged?
234.x: Although 172 persons were sentenced to death, 19 were finally hanged after the legal proceedings and intervention in the case.
234.tq: Separate the original sentence figure from the final execution figure.

234.s:
Which of the following statements regarding reactions to the Chauri Chaura incident is correct?
1. Gandhi fasted for three days.
2. Subhas Chandra Bose called the withdrawal a national calamity.
3. M.N. Roy described the withdrawal as weak leadership.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: Gandhi fasted for three days after the incident. Subhas Chandra Bose called the decision a national calamity, while M.N. Roy criticised it as weak leadership.
234.tq: Combine three attributed reactions and verify each before choosing the coded option.

234.s:
Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order of the events listed below?
A. Moplah uprising
B. Prince of Wales boycott
C. Chauri Chaura incident
D. Formation of the Swaraj Party
234.x: The Moplah uprising occurred in August 1921, the Prince of Wales boycott on 17 November 1921, Chauri Chaura in February 1922 and the Swaraj Party was formed in 1923.
234.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1921 events by month.

234.s: Which one of the following institutions was founded in 1915 and was therefore not a Non-Cooperation-era national institution?
234.x: The Besant Theosophical College at Madanapalle was founded by Annie Besant in 1915. Gujarat Vidyapith was founded in 1920, while Kashi Vidyapith and Bihar Vidyapith were founded in 1921.
234.tq: Use the founding-year distinction to identify the institution predating the movement.

234.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the founding year and place of a national institution?
234.x: Gujarat Vidyapith was founded in Ahmedabad in 1920. Kashi Vidyapith was founded at Varanasi in 1921, Bihar Vidyapith at Patna in 1921, and Jamia Millia Islamia was founded at Aligarh in 1920 before later shifting to Delhi.
234.tq: Check both the year and location in each pair, not just one part of the association.

234.s: Which of the following institutions was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi?
234.x: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded at Aligarh in 1920 and later shifted to Delhi.
234.tq: Distinguish the institution’s original location from its later well-known location.

234.s:
Consider the following statements about Aligarh Muslim University:
1. It developed from the MAO College.
2. The MAO College was established in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
3. It was itself founded as a Non-Cooperation-era national institution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: Aligarh Muslim University developed from the MAO College, established in 1875 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. Although the university received legal status in 1920, it was not founded as a national institution of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
234.tq: Separate an institution’s legal university date from the earlier founding of its parent college and its movement affiliation.

234.s:
Which of the following institutions were founded during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
1. Kashi Vidyapith
2. Gujarat Vidyapith
3. Bihar Vidyapith
4. Besant Theosophical College
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: Kashi Vidyapith, Gujarat Vidyapith and Bihar Vidyapith were founded in 1921, 1920 and 1921 respectively, during the movement. Besant Theosophical College was founded in 1915.
234.tq: Classify institutions by their founding year and then exclude the pre-movement institution.

234.s: Mahatma Gandhi was associated with the founding of which institution in 1920?
234.x: Gujarat Vidyapith was founded at Ahmedabad in 1920 with Mahatma Gandhi’s association.
234.tq: Match the founder or associate with the institution while avoiding nearby national-education alternatives.

234.s:
Which of the following persons was associated with the national institutions established during the Non-Cooperation era?
1. Acharya Narendra Dev
2. Zakir Hussain
3. Subhas Chandra Bose
4. C.R. Das
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
234.x: Acharya Narendra Dev, C.R. Das, Lala Lajpat Rai, Zakir Hussain and Subhas Chandra Bose were among the leaders associated with the national institutions of the period.
234.tq: Verify the complete association list before selecting the all-inclusive code.

234.s: The Khilafat Movement sought primarily to secure which of the following?
o: Restoration of the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and protection of his territories
Abolition of the zamindari system in India
Withdrawal of British troops from Afghanistan
Establishment of a separate Muslim state in India
234.x: The movement aimed to restore the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and preserve the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire after the First World War.
234.tq: Identify the precise objective rather than a related political demand.

234.s: Which treaty was particularly associated with the territorial settlement imposed on the Ottoman Empire after the First World War and opposed by the Khilafat leaders?
234.x: The Treaty of Sevres, signed in May 1920, threatened the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire and intensified the Khilafat agitation.
234.tq: Use the exact treaty-name distinction among closely related international settlements.

234.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Khilafat Movement:
1. It was led prominently by Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
2. The Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919.
3. Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
234.x: Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali were the leading Ali brothers, the Khilafat Committee emerged in 1919, and Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
234.tq: Test a cluster of names, institutional details and a terminating date.

234.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Khilafat Movement?
234.x: Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. M.A. Ansari were associated with the Khilafat Movement. Tej Bahadur Sapru is not listed among its leaders here.
234.tq: Find the outsider in a group of closely associated leaders.

234.s: Which event occurred in June 1920 in relation to the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements?
o: The Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott and requested Gandhi to lead
The Karachi Khilafat conference asked Muslims to quit the Army
234.x: The June 1920 Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott and requested Gandhi to assume leadership. The Karachi conference followed in July 1921.
234.tq: Separate closely spaced conferences by matching each one with its distinctive outcome.

234.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Joint Khilafat deputation to the Viceroy failed
B. Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott
C. Karachi Khilafat conference asked Muslims to quit the Army
D. Turkey abolished the Caliphate
234.x: The sequence was the failed deputation in February 1920, the Allahabad conference in June 1920, the Karachi conference in July 1921 and abolition of the Caliphate in 1924.
234.tq: Use the dated anchors and place the 1924 event last.

234.s: The Khilafat agitation lost much of its relevance after which development?
o: The British granted complete independence to India
The Ali brothers joined the Swaraj Party
The Treaty of Sevres was withdrawn by Britain in 1920
234.x: The abolition of the Caliphate by Turkey in 1924 removed the central institutional issue around which the Khilafat agitation had developed.
234.tq: Link the decline of a movement with the event that removed its central issue.

234.s: The July 1921 Karachi Khilafat Conference was notable for urging Muslims to
