Jawaharlal Nehru—Chairman; M.S. Ahluwalia—first Deputy Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda—last Deputy Chairman
M.S. Ahluwalia—Chairman; Jawaharlal Nehru—first Deputy Chairman; Gulzarilal Nanda—last Deputy Chairman
254.x: The Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the ex officio Chairman. Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman and M.S. Ahluwalia was the last Deputy Chairman.
254.tq: Use the office-holder sequence and watch for swapped authorities.

254.s: The National Planning Committee, constituted by the Congress in 1938, was headed by:
254.x: The Congress's National Planning Committee of 1938 was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru.
254.tq: Direct person–institution recall with neighbouring national leaders as distractors.

254.s:
With reference to the National Development Council, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up on 6 August 1952.
2. It was chaired by the Prime Minister.
3. It gave final approval to Five Year Plans.
4. Its membership included all Chief Ministers, Union Cabinet Ministers, representatives of Union Territories and members of the Planning Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: All four statements correctly describe the date, chairmanship, composition and plan-approval role of the National Development Council.
254.tq: Test a complete institutional profile through an all-inclusive option.

254.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Plan)
 a. First Five Year Plan
 b. Second Five Year Plan
 c. Third Five Year Plan
List-II (Model or description)
 i. Gadgil Yojana
 ii. Harrod-Domar model
 iii. P.C. Mahalanobis model

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
254.x: The First Plan used the Harrod-Domar model, the Second Plan followed the P.C. Mahalanobis model, and the Third Plan was called the Gadgil Yojana.
254.tq: Start from the sure plan–model pair and eliminate the swapped codes.

254.s: The First Five Year Plan was launched on 1 April 1951. Its principal priorities were:
o: Heavy industry, capital goods and urbanisation
254.x: The First Plan, launched on 1 April 1951, prioritised agriculture, irrigation and power, including projects such as Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud.
254.tq: Compare the sectoral priorities of successive plans rather than their names alone.

254.s: Which one of the following statements about the First Five Year Plan is correct?
o: Its actual growth was 3.6 per cent against a target of 2.1 per cent.
It recorded no measurable growth because it was confined to irrigation.
Its actual growth was 2.1 per cent against a target of 4.5 per cent.
Its target growth rate was 3.6 per cent and actual growth was 2.1 per cent.
254.x: The First Plan achieved 3.6 per cent growth against its target of 2.1 per cent.
254.tq: Separate target from achievement and avoid reversing the two figures.

254.s: The Second Five Year Plan is associated primarily with which of the following?
o: Village and cottage industries under a decentralised model
Food self-sufficiency under the Gadgil Yojana
Heavy and capital-goods industries under the P.C. Mahalanobis model
Agriculture and irrigation under the Harrod-Domar model
254.x: The Second Plan, covering 1956–61, followed the P.C. Mahalanobis or Nehru-Mahalanobis-Feldman model and gave priority to heavy and capital-goods industries.
254.tq: Direct plan–model–priority matching with closely related alternatives.

254.s: A major consequence associated with the strategy of the Second Five Year Plan was:
o: Food shortages and inflation following the neglect of agriculture
Immediate food self-sufficiency and price stability
The replacement of central planning by annual plans
254.x: The Second Plan's emphasis on heavy industry neglected agriculture, contributing to food shortages and inflation.
254.tq: Apply the plan's sectoral imbalance to its stated outcome.

254.s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Five Year Plan:
1. It covered the period 1961–66.
2. It aimed at self-sufficiency in food.
3. Its guiding idea included growth with stability.
4. It was based on the John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: The Third Plan ran from 1961 to 1966, used the John Sandy and S. Chakravarty model, and sought food self-sufficiency and growth with stability.
254.tq: Combine period, model and objectives in a full plan profile.

254.s: The Third Five Year Plan was derailed mainly by:
o: The Green Revolution and excess food production
The Suez Crisis and the Korean War
The abolition of the Planning Commission and the 1971 war
254.x: The Third Plan was adversely affected by the wars of 1962 and 1965 and by drought.
254.tq: Cause–effect recall using historically adjacent but unrelated crises as traps.

254.s: Which of the following correctly describes the period immediately following the failure of the Third Five Year Plan?
o: A Plan Holiday from 1966 to 1969 with three annual plans, accompanied by rupee devaluation
A permanent suspension of planning from 1966 to 1971 without annual plans
A fourth Five Year Plan beginning immediately in 1966 without currency changes
A return to the First Plan model without any change in the rupee
254.x: The failure of the Third Plan led to the Plan Holiday of 1966–69, during which three annual plans were implemented and the rupee was devalued.
254.tq: Identify the transition period and distinguish annual plans from a regular Five Year Plan.

254.s: The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and replaced by NITI Aayog in:
254.x: The Planning Commission was dissolved in 2014 and NITI Aayog replaced it in 2015.
254.tq: Separate the year of dissolution from the year of replacement.

254.s: Jawaharlal Nehru set out the objective of keeping India independent of power blocs in a broadcast delivered on:
254.x: Nehru articulated the goal of staying independent of power blocs in his broadcast of 7 September 1946.
254.tq: Direct date recall from the evolution of non-alignment.

254.s: Panchsheel was stated in the preamble of the India-China Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with the Tibet Region, signed by Nehru and Zhou Enlai on:
254.x: The India-China agreement containing the Panchsheel principles was signed by Jawaharlal Nehru and Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954.
254.tq: Match the agreement, leaders and date without confusing it with Bandung or Belgrade.

254.s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the five principles of Panchsheel?
o: Mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty
Collective military defence against power blocs
254.x: The five principles included mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful co-existence. Collective military defence against power blocs was not a Panchsheel principle.
254.tq: Find the non-member of a named five-item list.

254.s: Which country was the first outside the India-China pair to adopt Panchsheel in 1954?
254.x: Burma was the first country outside India and China to adopt Panchsheel in 1954.
254.tq: Discriminate among the Colombo Powers by identifying the specifically stated first adopter.

254.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bandung Conference:
1. It was held in Indonesia in 1955.
2. It was sponsored by the Colombo Powers.
3. Panchsheel was absorbed into its Ten Principles.
4. The Colombo Powers included India, Indonesia, Burma, Ceylon and Pakistan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: All four statements correctly describe the Bandung Conference, its sponsors and the incorporation of Panchsheel into its Ten Principles.
254.tq: Test the venue, year, sponsoring group and principle together.

254.s: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally established in 1961 at:
254.x: The Non-Aligned Movement was formalised in 1961 at Belgrade.
254.tq: Direct venue recall with other locations associated with non-alignment as distractors.

254.s: India's role in the Korean conflict included chairing the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission, which dealt with:
o: Refugee settlement after the Suez Crisis
Border demarcation between India and China
254.x: The Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission handled prisoners of war, and India chaired it in 1953.
254.tq: Identify the function of an international body from the conflict context.

254.s: Who led India's role in the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission during the Korean conflict?
254.x: The commission was led by General K.S. Thimayya.
254.tq: Direct person–mission association with prominent Nehru-era figures as traps.

254.s: India's response to the Suez Crisis of 1956 was to:
o: Remain neutral and refuse any United Nations role
Send troops to support the invasion
Support the Anglo-French-Israeli invasion and withdraw from the United Nations
Condemn the invasion and send troops to the UN Emergency Force
254.x: India condemned the Anglo-French-Israeli invasion during the Suez Crisis and sent troops to the UN Emergency Force.
254.tq: Test diplomatic position and action together, avoiding reversal of the response.

254.s: Jawaharlal Nehru served as Prime Minister of India from:
254.x: Nehru was Prime Minister from 15 August 1947 until his death on 27 May 1964.
254.tq: Use both endpoints of a tenure and distinguish office tenure from constitutional dates.

254.s: At the time of his death in 1964, Nehru was in which term of office, counting the interim government and the elections of 1952, 1957 and 1962?
254.x: Counting the interim government and the elected governments formed after the 1952, 1957 and 1962 elections, Nehru was in his fourth term.
254.tq: Count the stated sequence rather than treating only elected governments as terms.

254.s: Jawaharlal Nehru represented which constituency in Parliament?
254.x: Nehru's parliamentary seat was Phulpur, not Rae Bareli.
254.tq: Directly separate two easily confused constituency names.

254.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Book)
 a. The Discovery of India
 b. Glimpses of World History
 c. An Autobiography
 d. Letters from a Father to His Daughter
List-II (Associated fact)
 i. Written in Ahmednagar Fort jail
 ii. A work by Nehru
 iii. A work by Nehru
 iv. A work by Nehru

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
254.x: The Discovery of India was written in Ahmednagar Fort jail. Glimpses of World History, An Autobiography and Letters from a Father to His Daughter are also books by Nehru.
254.tq: Start with the unique place association and then assign the remaining works.

254.s: Which one of the following was NOT identified as an influence on Jawaharlal Nehru?
254.x: Nehru was influenced by Fabian socialism or socialism, British liberalism, Gandhi and Soviet planning. German nationalism was not identified as an influence.
254.tq: Find the outsider in a list of intellectual and political influences.

254.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts Gandhi's and Nehru's economic approaches?
o: Gandhi favoured a decentralised village and cottage-industry economy, while Nehru favoured heavy industry, science and central planning.
Gandhi favoured heavy industry, while Nehru favoured only cottage industries.
Both favoured an exclusively decentralised cottage-industry economy.
Both rejected central planning and industrialisation.
254.x: Gandhi emphasised decentralised villages and cottage industries, whereas Nehru supported heavy industry, science and central planning.
254.tq: Test a paired comparison by matching each thinker with the correct economic orientation.

254.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Liberation of Goa through Operation Vijay
B. Khrushchev-Bulganin visit to India
C. Dalai Lama flees to India
D. Chou En-lai's visit to India for border talks
254.x: The correct sequence is the 1955 Khrushchev-Bulganin visit, March 1959 Dalai Lama flight, April 1960 Chou En-lai visit and December 1961 liberation of Goa.
254.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.

254.s: The Dalai Lama fled to India in:
254.x: The Dalai Lama fled to India in March 1959.
254.tq: Distinguish month-specific dates in the chronology of Nehru-era events.

254.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chou En-lai's visit for border talks—April 1960
254.x: The India-China war took place in October–November 1962, not December 1963. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
254.tq: Check the date against the established chronology and identify the reversed year trap.

254.s:
Which of the following were causes of the India-China war of 1962?
1. Disputes over the McMahon Line and Aksai Chin
2. China's construction of a road through Aksai Chin
3. India's grant of asylum to the Dalai Lama
4. India's Forward Policy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
254.x: The war was associated with the McMahon Line and Aksai Chin disputes, China's road through Aksai Chin, asylum to the Dalai Lama and India's Forward Policy.
254.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each stated cause.

254.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the consequences of the 1962 India-China war:
1. A National Emergency was declared on 26 October 1962.
2. Defence Minister V.K. Krishna Menon resigned.
3. China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: All three statements are correct: the National Emergency was declared on 26 October, V.K. Krishna Menon resigned, and China announced a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.
254.tq: Verify dates and consequence statements before selecting the complete code.

254.s: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under the leadership of:
254.x: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under Homi J. Bhabha.
254.tq: Direct institution–year–person association with other Nehru-era figures as distractors.

254.s: Which one of the following institutions was the first IIT, established in 1951?
254.x: IIT Kharagpur was the first IIT and was established in 1951.
254.tq: Test the superlative claim and year together.

254.s:
Consider the following statements about the University Grants Commission:
1. It was set up in 1953.
2. It became a statutory body under the UGC Act, 1956.
3. It was established as a constitutional body in 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: The UGC was set up in 1953 and became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956. It was not a constitutional body.
254.tq: Distinguish the year of establishment from the year and nature of statutory recognition.

254.s: AIIMS, New Delhi, was established in 1956 under the:
254.x: AIIMS, New Delhi, was established in 1956 under the AIIMS Act.
254.tq: Match the institution with its specific establishing Act.

254.s: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research was established in:
254.x: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, or CSIR, was established in 1942; its national laboratories expanded under Nehru.
254.tq: Direct year recall while separating CSIR from other institution-building dates.

254.s: Rabindra Bharati at Hyderabad was built to commemorate the birth centenary of Rabindranath Tagore and was inaugurated by Nehru on:
254.x: Rabindra Bharati, Hyderabad, was built for Tagore's birth centenary and was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru on 11 October 1961.
254.tq: Combine purpose, place and inauguration date in a precise institutional recall question.

254.s: Which of the following was one of the sectors reserved exclusively for the State under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948?
254.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 reserved arms, atomic energy and railways for the State.
254.tq: Identify the sector directly associated with the correct policy resolution.

254.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 is associated with which of the following economic arrangements?
o: A command economy without private enterprise
An economy based exclusively on foreign investment
254.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 laid down the framework of a mixed economy, combining public and private sectors.
254.tq: Test the exact meaning of the policy label rather than a broader economic description.

254.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is popularly known as the:
254.x: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 is popularly called the Economic Constitution of India.
254.tq: Direct recall of a well-known title associated with a policy document.

254.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 was based primarily on the:
254.x: The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution rested on the Mahalanobis model of industrial development.
254.tq: Use the person–model association to distinguish competing economic approaches.

254.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the schedules under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:
1. Schedule A contained 17 industries reserved for the State.
2. Schedule B contained 12 industries in which the State took the lead and the private sector supplemented it.
3. Schedule C comprised the remaining industries left to the private sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: All three statements are correct. Schedule A had 17 State-only industries, Schedule B had 12 industries led by the State with private supplementation, and Schedule C covered the remaining industries left to private enterprise.
254.tq: Check each schedule separately, especially the numerical distinction between Schedules A and B.

254.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Schedule B of the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956?
o: It contained 12 industries in which the State took the lead and private enterprise supplemented it.
It comprised all industries left entirely to foreign investors.
It contained only small-scale and cottage industries.
It contained 17 industries reserved exclusively for the State.
254.x: Schedule B included 12 industries in which the State took the lead, while the private sector was permitted to supplement it.
254.tq: Separate the middle schedule from the State-only and private-sector schedules.

254.s: Which of the following developments was associated with the adoption of the socialistic pattern of society under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956?
o: Abolition of all State control over industry
Withdrawal of the State from basic industries
The emergence of the Licence Raj
254.x: The socialistic pattern of society adopted in 1956 led to extensive State controls over industry, commonly described as the Licence Raj. The policy also promoted small-scale and cottage industries.
254.tq: Link the policy objective with its institutional and economic consequence.

254.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Schedule C — Industries left to the private sector
Schedule B — State lead with private-sector supplementation
Schedule A — Industries exclusively reserved for the private sector
254.x: Schedule A consisted of industries reserved exclusively for the State, not for the private sector. The descriptions in the other three pairs are correct.
254.tq: Find the reversed State–private sector relationship in the schedules.

254.s: Indian secularism is best described by which of the following expressions?
o: Strict separation of religion and public life in every circumstance
Complete exclusion of the State from social reform
254.x: Indian secularism is associated with Sarva Dharma Sambhava, under which the State has no official religion and treats religions neutrally while retaining the possibility of social reform.
254.tq: Recall the distinctive Indian expression and distinguish it from the strict Western model.

254.s:
With reference to Indian secularism, consider the following statements:
1. India has no State religion.
2. The State remains neutral towards religions.
3. The State may intervene to reform certain social practices.
4. Indian secularism is identical to the Western model of strict separation in all respects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 correctly describe Indian secularism. Statement 4 is incorrect because Indian secularism differs from the Western model of strict separation and permits State intervention for social reform.
254.tq: Reject the absolute comparison created by the phrase 'identical in all respects'.

254.s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the educational institutions of minorities?
254.x: Article 30 protects the rights of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.
254.tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional Articles by their specific subject.

254.s: Article 325 of the Constitution is significant in the context of minority rights because it:
o: prescribes Hindi in Devanagari as the official language
bars religious exclusion from electoral rolls
254.x: Article 325 prohibits exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex; in this context it bars religious exclusion from electoral rolls.
254.tq: Separate Article 325 from Articles 30 and 343 by matching the provision to its function.

254.s:
Arrange the following enactments connected with the Hindu Code Bills in chronological order:
A. Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act
B. Hindu Marriage Act
C. Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act
D. Hindu Succession Act
254.x: The Hindu Marriage Act was passed in 1955, followed in 1956 by the Hindu Succession Act, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, and Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act.
254.tq: Fix the 1955 enactment first and then arrange the three 1956 enactments.

254.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
254.x: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act was enacted in 1956. The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in 1955, while the Hindu Succession Act and Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act were enacted in 1956.
254.tq: Use the single 1955 enactment to eliminate the incorrectly dated pairs.

254.s: Article 343 provides for which of the following language arrangements?
o: Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language, with English continuing for 15 years
Sanskrit as the official language with Hindi for 15 years
English as the sole official language of India
Hindi and all regional languages as equally official Union languages
254.x: Article 343 made Hindi in the Devanagari script the official language and provided for the use of English for 15 years.
254.tq: Combine the constitutional Article with both the script and the specified time period.

254.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is associated with the:
o: Recognition of only regional languages for Union purposes
Continuation of English in official use
Replacement of Hindi by English as the sole official language
254.x: The Official Languages Act of 1963 continued the use of English for official purposes along with Hindi.
254.tq: Distinguish continuation of English from replacement or abolition of Hindi.

254.s: Who was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, the successor to the Planning Commission, in the current-affairs reference cited?
254.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog, which succeeded the Planning Commission.
254.tq: Match the current appointment with the institution and its predecessor.

254.s: The Indian Council of World Affairs (ICWA) was associated with which of the following events and milestones?
o: It hosted the Non-Aligned Movement summit in 1961 and marked 50 years as an Institution of National Importance.
It hosted the Simla Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as a national university.
It hosted the Bandung Conference in 1955 and marked 15 years as an Institution of National Importance.
It hosted the Asian Relations Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as an Institution of National Importance.
254.x: ICWA hosted Nehru's Asian Relations Conference in 1947 and marked 25 years as an Institution of National Importance.
254.tq: Pair the institution with both its associated conference and numerical milestone.

254.s: The Asian Relations Conference hosted by the Indian Council of World Affairs took place in:
254.x: The Asian Relations Conference hosted by ICWA was held in 1947 and was associated with Jawaharlal Nehru.
254.tq: Use the chronological position of the conference to distinguish it from later Asian and international meetings.

254.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mahalanobis strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture.
2. Panchsheel succeeded in preventing the war of 1962.
3. The Mahalanobis strategy gave primary emphasis to industrial development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
254.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Mahalanobis strategy was criticised for neglecting agriculture, while Panchsheel did not prevent the 1962 war, making statement 2 false.
254.tq: Identify the reversed historical outcome in the statement about Panchsheel.

254.s: Panchsheel is criticised in the context of the Nehru era because it:
o: did not prevent the war of 1962
254.x: Although Panchsheel represented principles of peaceful coexistence, it did not prevent the India–China war of 1962.
254.tq: Connect a diplomatic principle with the historical event that tested its effectiveness.

254.s: Rabindra Bharati in Hyderabad was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in:
254.x: Rabindra Bharati in Hyderabad was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1961.
254.tq: Use the place–person–year combination to test the Andhra-specific historical association.

255.s: The ministry of Tanguturi Prakasam in Andhra State lost its majority primarily over the issue of:
255.x: Tanguturi Prakasam's ministry lost its majority over the prohibition issue, leading to mid-term polls in 1955.
255.tq: Identify the cause-effect link rather than confusing the issue with a territorial demand.

255.s: Who was the Speaker of the Andhra State Legislative Assembly in 1956?
255.x: Laxmi Narasimham was the Speaker of the Andhra State Legislative Assembly in 1956. Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of Andhra State.
255.tq: Discriminate between the first Speaker and the Speaker in 1956.

255.s:
Consider the following pairs regarding the districts of Andhra State in 1953:
1. Coastal Andhra — 7 districts
2. Rayalaseema — 4 districts
3. Total districts — 11
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
255.x: The Coastal Andhra region had seven districts and Rayalaseema had four, making a total of eleven districts.
255.tq: Break the regional total into its two component figures before selecting the coded option.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the districts of Andhra State at the time of its formation?
255.x: Vizianagaram district did not exist at the time of Andhra State formation. Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor were included.
255.tq: Find the later-created district among the districts belonging to the 1953 arrangement.

255.s: The Bellary taluks that were associated with the formation of Andhra State were ultimately transferred to:
255.x: The taluks of Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli and Hadagali went to Mysore State. Madras city remained with Madras.
255.tq: Use the territorial-transfer trap by distinguishing the transferred taluks from the excluded Madras city.

255.s: On 19 December 1952, Jawaharlal Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from:
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
255.x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.
255.tq: Separate the accepted Telugu areas from the specifically excluded Madras city.

255.s: Who inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool?
255.x: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool.
255.tq: Distinguish the inaugurating national leader from the constitutional authorities associated with state reorganisation.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's fast preceding the formation of Andhra State lasted for how many days?
255.x: Potti Sriramulu died after a 58-day fast. The fast began on 19 October 1952 and ended with his death on 15 December 1952.
255.tq: Use the duration figure rather than confusing it with the beginning or date of death.

255.s: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed by the Centre to examine the Andhra issue on:
255.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953. His report is associated with March 1953.
255.tq: Distinguish the appointment date from the report date and the date of state formation.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dar Commission:
1. It was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly.
2. It was appointed in June 1948.
3. Its chairman was S.K. Dhar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The Dar Commission was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly in June 1948, with S.K. Dhar as its chairman.
255.tq: Verify the appointing authority, year and chairperson as a three-part institutional identification.

255.s: The principal mandate of the Dar Commission was to examine the formation of which group of provinces and their boundaries and consequences?
o: Karnataka, Gujarat, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
255.x: The Dar Commission examined the formation of Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra, including their boundaries and consequences.
255.tq: Recall the complete named set; do not replace the listed provinces with later state names.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the criteria emphasised by the Dar Commission for reorganisation of provinces?
255.x: The Dar Commission emphasised geographical contiguity, financial self-reliance, administrative viability and development potential, rather than language alone.
255.tq: Find the criterion that reverses the Commission's administrative rather than linguistic approach.

255.s: The Dar Commission recommended that provinces should be reorganised primarily on the basis of:
255.x: The Dar Commission recommended administrative convenience rather than language as the primary basis for reorganisation.
255.tq: Use the central recommendation and distinguish it from the linguistic principle later adopted.

255.s: The Dar Commission warned that the creation of linguistic states could threaten:
255.x: The Commission warned that linguistic states threatened national unity and thereby rejected the linguistic basis at that stage.
255.tq: Link the distinctive warning directly with the Commission that issued it.

255.s: The report of the Dar Commission was dated and published, respectively, on:
255.x: The report was dated 10 December 1948 and published on 13 December 1948.
255.tq: Keep the closely spaced report and publication dates in chronological order.

255.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the evidence placed before the Dar Commission is correct?
1. The Andhra Mahasabha demanded all Telugu areas.
2. The Rayalaseema Mahasabha demanded a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as its capital.
3. N. Sanjiva Reddy demanded that the entire question be postponed.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
255.x: All three statements correctly describe the positions presented before the Dar Commission in Madras in 1948.
255.tq: Compare the three regional and individual submissions instead of treating the Andhra demand as uniform.

255.s: The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee submitted a memorandum to the Dar Commission on 10 September 1948 under the leadership of:
255.x: The Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, under N.G. Ranga, submitted the memorandum on 10 September 1948.
255.tq: Match the organisation, date and leader without confusing the separate Rayalaseema representation.

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position taken by Neelam Sanjiva Reddy before the Dar Commission?
o: He supported the merger of Andhra with Telangana immediately.
He demanded Madras city as the permanent capital of all Telugu areas.
He demanded immediate formation of a linguistic Andhra State without conditions.
He opposed linguistic states or sought incorporation of the Sribagh terms.
255.x: Speaking for 20 Rayalaseema MLAs, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy opposed linguistic states or asked that the Sribagh terms be incorporated.
255.tq: Use the qualified position and the associated group of Rayalaseema MLAs to avoid an absolute-demand trap.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the JVP Committee:
1. It was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session in December 1948.
2. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was its president.
3. Its report was submitted in 1949.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The JVP Committee was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session in December 1948, with Pattabhi Sitaramayya as president, and submitted its report in 1949.
255.tq: Combine the committee's venue, office-holder and report year to identify the complete statement set.

255.s: The JVP Committee recommended that the demand for Andhra could be considered if the claim to which city was given up?
255.x: The JVP Committee stated that Andhra could be considered if its claim to Madras city was relinquished.
255.tq: Distinguish the disputed metropolitan city from the proposed Andhra capital and other Telugu cities.

255.s: Which one of the following best reflects the recommendation of the JVP Committee regarding the creation of new provinces?
o: Creation of provinces solely on financial criteria
Postponement of the creation of new provinces
Merger of all Telugu areas with Hyderabad
Immediate creation of all provinces on a linguistic basis
255.x: The JVP Committee recommended postponing the creation of new provinces, while allowing Andhra's claim to be considered subject to giving up the claim to Madras city.
255.tq: Identify the committee's cautious recommendation rather than the later outcome of Andhra State formation.

255.s:
Which of the following statements about the background to the linguistic reorganisation issue is correct?
1. Nehru's declaration in November 1947 raised hopes regarding linguistic provinces.
2. The Constituent Assembly retained only the provinces that existed before Independence.
3. During Nehru's 1948 visit to Visakhapatnam, he promised a committee.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
255.x: All three statements describe the political background preceding the appointment of the Dar Commission and the later JVP Committee.
255.tq: Arrange the background developments as connected preliminary events rather than isolated committee facts.

255.s: The committee formed by the Madras Government under Chief Minister P.S. Kumaraswami Raja was primarily concerned with:
o: Selecting the first Governor of Andhra State
Dividing the assets and liabilities between Madras and Andhra
Drafting a constitution for Andhra State
255.x: The committee was constituted to divide assets and liabilities between the proposed Andhra region and Madras. It failed because Madras leaders refused to surrender Madras city to Andhra.
255.tq: Identify the purpose of the committee before examining why it failed.

255.s: The committee headed by Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on:
255.x: Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953 to report on the implications of the proposed Andhra State.
255.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely related Andhra movement events.

255.s: Justice K.N. Wanchoo submitted his report on the proposed Andhra State in:
255.x: Wanchoo submitted his report in March 1953. The material gives differing exact dates within March, so the month is the reliable point.
255.tq: Choose the reliable time unit when exact dates are uncertain.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sreebagh Pact:
1. It was concluded on 16 November 1937.
2. It provided that the capital and the High Court should be located in different regions.
3. It gave Rayalaseema the first choice in selecting the location.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The Sreebagh Pact was concluded on 16 November 1937. It separated the locations of the capital and High Court and gave Rayalaseema the first choice, helping the claim of Kurnool.
255.tq: Verify each statement against the date, provision and regional preference of an agreement.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Site)
a. Kurnool
b. Tirupati
c. Vijayawada/Guntur

aList-II (Supporter)
i. Communists
 ii. Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders
 iii. Krishikar Lok Party

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
255.x: Kurnool was supported by Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders; Tirupati was associated with the Krishikar Lok Party; and Vijayawada/Guntur was supported by the Communists.
255.tq: Start from the sure regional association and eliminate incompatible codes.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political position of the Krishikar Lok Party during the Andhra capital debate?
o: It supported Guntur as the permanent capital
It initially agreed on Kurnool and changed its stand to support Tirupati during the Assembly session
It opposed the formation of Andhra State altogether
It consistently supported Vijayawada from the beginning
255.x: The Krishikar Lok Party initially agreed to Kurnool but changed its position during the Assembly session and supported Tirupati.
255.tq: Track the change in position rather than treating a party's final stand as its initial stand.

255.s:
With reference to the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, consider the following statements:
1. Kurnool secured 79 votes.
2. Vijayawada secured 53 votes.
3. The difference between the two votes was 26.
4. T. Prakasam voted in favour of Kurnool.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Kurnool secured 79 votes and Vijayawada 53, a margin of 26 votes. T. Prakasam did not vote, so statement 4 is false.
255.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking the numerical result and the voting exception.

255.s: Kurnool won the capital vote in the Madras Assembly with the assistance of:
o: The casting vote of the Chief Minister
255.x: Kurnool won by 79 votes to 53, and its victory was helped by five non-Andhra votes. Six members were absent and T. Prakasam did not vote.
255.tq: Separate the decisive numerical detail from other voting circumstances.

255.s: In June 1953, the Andhra MLAs met under the leadership of:
255.x: The Andhra MLAs met in June 1953 under T. Prakasam to consider the capital question. Congress, Prakasam's group and N.G. Ranga's Krishikar Lok Party initially agreed on Kurnool.
255.tq: Match the political meeting with its presiding leader.

255.s: The reorganisation of the Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines was undertaken at the:
255.x: The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines at the Nagpur session in 1920. Linguistic provinces had therefore been a Congress commitment since the 1920s.
255.tq: Distinguish the organisational decision at Nagpur from later constitutional debates.

255.s: Why did the Central Government proceed cautiously on the demand for linguistic states after 1947?
o: It believed that linguistic identity had disappeared after independence
The Constitution prohibited states based on language
It feared that reorganisation might weaken national unity while Partition, Kashmir and the princely-state question remained unresolved
The Congress had rejected linguistic provinces at Nagpur
255.x: After Partition, the Government feared that linguistic reorganisation could endanger national unity. Kashmir and the integration of the princely states were also still unsettled.
255.tq: Link the policy delay to the contemporary national-security and integration context.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines before independence.
2. The Government accepted the principle of linguistic states in 1947.
3. Acceptance of the principle was followed immediately by the creation of all linguistic states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Although the principle was accepted in 1947, implementation was delayed; therefore statement 3 is false.
255.tq: Separate acceptance of a principle from its immediate implementation.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's ancestral village, as identified in the available account, was:
255.x: Gajula Dinne in Nellore district is identified as Potti Sriramulu's ancestral village. Mylapore was associated with the later venue of his fast, not his ancestral village.
255.tq: Distinguish a person's ancestral place from the place of a later political event.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to Potti Sriramulu's earlier fasts is correctly matched?
o: 1948 — 10 days at the Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple
1946 — 10 days at the Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple
1952 — 10 days at the Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple
255.x: In 1946, Sriramulu fasted for 10 days at the Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple. In 1948, he undertook a 29-day fast at Wardha.
255.tq: Discriminate between the two earlier fasts by pairing each year with its duration and place.

255.s: The immediate response associated with Potti Sriramulu's 29-day Harijan fast at Wardha in 1948 was that:
o: The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees
The Madras Assembly selected Kurnool as capital
255.x: Following Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948, Jawaharlal Nehru declared a Harijan Day.
255.tq: Connect the event with its immediate political or social consequence.

255.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Potti Sriramulu began his final fast
B. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament
C. Potti Sriramulu died
D. Justice K.N. Wanchoo was appointed

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
255.x: Wanchoo was appointed on 7 February 1953, after Sriramulu's final fast began on 19 October 1952. Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952, and Nehru announced Andhra State on 19 December 1952.
255.tq: Place the two December events carefully: death first, announcement four days later.

255.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence of events relating to Potti Sriramulu's final fast?
o: Death on 15 December 1952, announcement on 19 December 1952, fast beginning on 19 October 1952
Fast beginning on 19 October 1952, death on 15 December 1952, announcement on 19 December 1952
Announcement on 19 December 1952, fast beginning on 19 October 1952, death on 15 December 1952
Fast beginning on 15 December 1952, death on 19 October 1952, announcement on 19 December 1952
255.x: The final fast began on 19 October 1952, Sriramulu died on 15 December 1952, and Nehru announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
255.tq: Use first-and-last dates to distinguish the death date from the later announcement date.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu began his final fast at the house of:
255.x: Although the fast initially began at the St. George's Fort gate, Bulusu Sambamurthy moved Sriramulu to his house in Mylapore, which is generally given as the venue.
255.tq: Distinguish the initial location from the recognised venue of the fast.

255.s: Potti Sriramulu's final fast lasted for:
255.x: The final fast is recorded as lasting 58 days. Some accounts mention 56 days, but the specified exam-oriented figure is 58 days.
255.tq: Give priority to the stated standard figure when nearby numerical variants are distractors.

255.s: Which one of the following statements about the aftermath of Potti Sriramulu's death is correct?
o: The States Reorganisation Commission was dissolved after his death
The Congress rejected the demand for a separate Andhra State
There were riots and police firing in which seven persons died, followed by Nehru's announcement of Andhra State
The Madras Government immediately accepted Madras city as the capital of Andhra
255.x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died. Nehru announced the formation of Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.
255.tq: Select the option combining the immediate consequence with the subsequent governmental response.

255.s: Mahatma Gandhi is reported to have said that, with how many selfless patriots like Potti Sriramulu, he would have won Swaraj long before?
255.x: Gandhi stated that with 10–12 selfless patriots like Sriramulu, he would have won Swaraj long ago.
255.tq: Test the exact numerical expression in a famous quotation.

255.s: The first Andhra Mahasabha, held at Bapatla in 1913, is significant because it:
o: Opposed the demand for a separate Andhra province
Began the demand for a separate Andhra province
Selected Kurnool as the capital of Andhra State
255.x: The First Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla in 1913 began the demand for a separate Andhra province. Kurnool's selection and the Sreebagh Pact belonged to later developments.
255.tq: Identify the historical significance of the event rather than a later associated development.

255.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra Mahasabhas is/are correct?
1. The First Andhra Mahasabha was held at Bapatla in 1913.
2. Konda Venkatappayya was associated with the first Mahasabha as a secretary and leader.
3. The Rayalaseema Mahasabha held in 1935 opposed a separate Andhra State.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
255.x: All three statements are correct. The Bapatla conference of 1913 initiated the separate Andhra demand, Konda Venkatappayya was its secretary and leader, and the 1935 Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra State.
255.tq: Combine venue-year, individual association and regional political position in one statement set.

255.s:
Arrange the following events of the Andhra State movement in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
B. Swami Sitaram's fast
C. Setting up of the States Reorganisation Commission
D. Setting up of the Dhar Commission
255.x: The Dhar Commission was set up in 1948, followed by the Visalandhra Mahasabha in 1949, Swami Sitaram's fast in 1951 and the States Reorganisation Commission in December 1953.
255.tq: Use the first-and-last events to eliminate sequences before checking the middle events.

255.s: The Andhra Mahasabha held at Bapatla in 1913 is significant in the history of Andhra because it marked the:
o: Signing of the Sri Bagh Pact
First formal organisation of the Andhra movement
Launch of the separate Telangana movement
255.x: The Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla in 1913 was an early organised expression of the demand for a separate Andhra province.
255.tq: Identify the earliest organisational milestone rather than a later constitutional development.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
255.x: The Dhar Commission functioned during 1948. The JVP Committee belonged to 1948–49, the Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed in 1949 and the States Reorganisation Commission was appointed in December 1953.
255.tq: Match each institution with its year, rejecting the options with shifted dates.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dhar Commission was followed by the JVP Committee.
2. The Madras Partition Committee functioned during 1949–50.
3. The Wanchoo inquiry was conducted during February–March 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The sequence included the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee, the Madras Partition Committee in 1949–50 and the Wanchoo inquiry in early 1953.
255.tq: Check the dates of successive commissions and inquiries rather than relying only on their names.

255.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the period of the JVP Committee in relation to the Andhra State movement?
255.x: The JVP Committee functioned from December 1948 to April 1949. The other periods refer respectively to the Dhar Commission, the Madras Partition Committee and the Wanchoo inquiry.
255.tq: Discriminate between closely placed date ranges belonging to related bodies.

255.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha, formed in 1949, was intended to represent the demand for a state comprising:
o: The Telugu and Tamil-speaking areas jointly
255.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed to advocate the integration of all Telugu-speaking areas.
255.tq: Distinguish the geographical scope of an organisation from the narrower regional demands.

255.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Andhra State movement is correct?
o: The Constitution itself fixed 1 October 1953 as the date of Andhra State formation.
The Andhra State was formed before the Constitution came into force.
The Constitution of 26 January 1950 already included a separate Andhra State.
The Constitution of 26 January 1950 did not include a separate Andhra State.
255.x: There was no separate Andhra State in the Constitution as it came into force on 26 January 1950, although the Partition Committee had proposed that date in its deliberations.
255.tq: Watch for the false constitutional assumption created by a proposed date.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra State movement:
1. The Dhar Commission was set up before the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
2. Swami Sitaram's fast preceded the formation of Andhra State.
3. The second Visalandhra Mahasabha was held at Hyderabad in June 1954.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct. The Dhar Commission preceded the 1949 Visalandhra Mahasabha, Swami Sitaram fasted in 1951, and the second Visalandhra Mahasabha met at Hyderabad on 13–14 June 1954.
255.tq: Combine chronology with place and date details to test more than one dimension of the sequence.

255.s: Who presided over the second Visalandhra Mahasabha held at Hyderabad on 13–14 June 1954?
255.x: The second Visalandhra Mahasabha, held at Hyderabad on 13–14 June 1954, was presided over by Sri Sri.
255.tq: Use the event–place–president association to distinguish organisational leaders.

255.s: Which of the following changes best describes the position of B. Ramakrishna Rao in 1954?
o: He shifted in favour of the merger of Telugu-speaking areas.
He opposed the formation of any Andhra State.
255.x: In 1954, B. Ramakrishna Rao shifted to favour the merger of Telugu-speaking areas.
255.tq: Test a leader's change of position rather than merely identifying his office.

255.s: The States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953 is associated with which of the following persons?
255.x: The States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953 is identified with Fazal Ali.
255.tq: Apply the person–institution association while avoiding similarly placed Andhra leaders.

255.s: The Sri Bagh Pact was signed on:
255.x: The Sri Bagh Pact was signed on 16 November 1937.
255.tq: Distinguish the exact day and year from nearby milestones in the Andhra movement.

255.s: The Sri Bagh Pact was concluded between leaders representing:
255.x: The pact brought together leaders of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema to address regional concerns before pursuing a common Andhra demand.
255.tq: Identify the two negotiating regional groups rather than the later state units.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: A university centre at Anantapur along with the university at Waltair
Irrigation priority for Rayalaseema for ten years
Exclusive legislative control for Coastal Andhra over the Andhra region
Equal district-wise representation in the legislature
255.x: The pact did not provide exclusive legislative control to Coastal Andhra. It provided equal district-wise representation, university facilities at Waltair and Anantapur, and irrigation priority for Rayalaseema for ten years.
255.tq: Find the option that contradicts the pact's safeguards against regional domination.

255.s:
With reference to the Sri Bagh Pact, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra University was to remain at Waltair.
2. A university centre was to be established at Anantapur.
3. Rayalaseema was to receive irrigation priority for ten years.
4. Legislative seats were to be allotted district-wise on an equal basis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All four statements accurately describe the educational, irrigation and legislative safeguards included in the pact.
255.tq: Use the comprehensive option only after verifying every clause independently.

255.s: Under the Sri Bagh Pact, the capital and the High Court were to be:
o: Located at Waltair and Anantapur respectively
Located in separate regions, with Rayalaseema having the first choice
255.x: The pact provided that one of the capital and High Court would be in Rayalaseema and the other in the Circars, with Rayalaseema's choice being honoured first.
255.tq: Translate a negotiated regional safeguard into its practical institutional arrangement.

255.s: The irrigation provision of the Sri Bagh Pact related specifically to priority for Rayalaseema and Nellore in the waters of:
255.x: The pact granted Rayalaseema and Nellore priority for ten years in the utilisation of Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters.
255.tq: Start from the sure river pair and reject options containing an unrelated river.

255.s: The Sri Bagh Pact primarily sought to:
o: End the demand for a separate Andhra province
Establish Hyderabad as the permanent capital of Andhra
Allay Rayalaseema fears of Coastal Andhra domination
Create a separate university for Telangana
255.x: The pact was designed to remove Rayalaseema's fears of domination by Coastal Andhra and thereby facilitate a common Andhra demand.
255.tq: Identify the underlying political purpose rather than a specific clause.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Kadapa Koti Reddy — presided over the 1937 Silver Jubilee session
Kalluri Subbarao — drafted the Kurnool Circular
H.M. Sitaram Reddy — presided over the second Visalandhra Mahasabha
255.x: Kadapa Koti Reddy presided over the 1931 Special Andhra Sabha and the 1937 Silver Jubilee session. The Kurnool Circular was drafted by Kala Venkatarao, the second Visalandhra Mahasabha was presided over by Sri Sri, and H.M. Sitaram Reddy inaugurated the 1937 session.
255.tq: Use the person–role association and reject swapped office-holder traps.

255.s: Which one of the following statements about the 1937 political context is correct?
o: The absence of Coastal Andhra ministers ended regional distrust.
Rajaji's cabinet consisted entirely of Rayalaseema ministers.
Rajaji's cabinet had no Rayalaseema minister, which deepened the regional rift.
The cabinet was formed only after Andhra State was created in 1953.
255.x: The absence of a Rayalaseema minister in Rajaji's cabinet in 1937 deepened the existing regional rift.
255.tq: Link a political circumstance with its stated regional consequence.

255.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pappuri Ramacharyulu stayed away from the anti-Andhra second Rayalaseema Mahasabha of 1935.
2. Koti Reddy stayed away from that meeting.
3. Gadicherla stayed away from that meeting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Pappuri Ramacharyulu, Koti Reddy and Gadicherla all stayed away from the anti-Andhra second Rayalaseema Mahasabha held at Kadapa in 1935.
255.tq: Check each named participant separately before selecting the combined option.

255.s: Kalluri Subbarao is associated with which of the following events?
o: Presiding over the second Visalandhra Mahasabha
Leading the Salt Satyagraha in Bellary
Establishing the university centre at Anantapur
255.x: Kalluri Subbarao led the Salt Satyagraha in Bellary. The Kurnool Circular was drafted by Kala Venkatarao, while the other actions are not associated with him.
255.tq: Match a leader with his specific activity and avoid neighbouring Andhra movement roles.

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the implementation of the Sri Bagh Pact in 1953?
o: The capital was established at Guntur and the High Court at Kurnool.
The capital was established at Kurnool and the High Court at Guntur.
The capital was established at Anantapur and the High Court at Madras.
Both the capital and High Court were established at Waltair.
255.x: When the pact was put into effect in 1953, Kurnool became the capital and Guntur became the location of the High Court.
255.tq: Compare the two institutions and avoid reversing their locations.

255.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao — venue of the Sri Bagh Pact
Kalluri Subbarao — Salt Satyagraha in Bellary
N.G. Ranga — Rayalaseema signatory to the Sri Bagh Pact
H.M. Sitaram Reddy — inauguration of the 1937 session
255.x: N.G. Ranga was a Guntur leader and should not be treated as a Rayalaseema signatory. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
255.tq: Identify the regional-membership error in a list of otherwise plausible pairings.

255.s: The Sri Bagh Pact later served as a model for the:
255.x: The Sri Bagh Pact established a pattern of regional safeguards that was later used in the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956.
255.tq: Connect an earlier regional arrangement with the later agreement that followed its pattern.

255.s: Swami Sitaram, who undertook a fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951, was also known as
255.x: Swami Sitaram was the popular name of Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri, a Gandhian associated with the Andhra movement.
255.tq: Use the direct identity link between a popular name and the full name.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Swami Sitaram's fast:
1. He undertook the fast for a separate Andhra State.
2. The fast lasted for 35 days.
3. It was undertaken in August 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Swami Sitaram fasted for a separate Andhra State for 35 days in 1951, not 1953. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct.
255.tq: Split the statements by checking the year against the established chronology.

255.s: Swami Sitaram's fast in 1951 was conducted during which period?
255.x: Swami Sitaram fasted from 15 August to 20 September 1951, a period of 35 days.
255.tq: Match the precise beginning and ending dates rather than relying on the associated demand date.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT a demand associated with Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast?
o: Settlement of Madras city's status within three years
Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra State
Formation of Andhra State by 2 October 1951
Neither Andhra nor Tamil interests controlling Madras city during the interim
255.x: The demands concerned the formation of Andhra State, settlement of Madras city's status, and an interim arrangement over the city. Merger of Telangana was not one of the stated demands.
255.tq: Find the option outside the specific demand set.

255.s: Swami Sitaram ended his fast following the appeal of
255.x: Swami Sitaram withdrew his fast on the appeal of Acharya Vinoba Bhave, whose assurances did not produce the expected result.
255.tq: Discriminate between the person who appealed and the person who criticised the fast.

255.s: What was one important consequence of the failure to secure gains after Swami Sitaram ended his fast?
o: Confidence in the Congress leadership among Andhras was weakened
Madras became a shared Union Territory
The Andhra movement immediately achieved a separate state
The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party was dissolved
255.x: The fast ended without gain, which hurt Andhra confidence in the Congress leadership and weakened the movement temporarily.
255.tq: Trace the stated cause-and-effect relationship instead of selecting a later political outcome.

255.s: Swami Sitaram had earlier led which campaign during the Civil Disobedience Movement?
255.x: Swami Sitaram was a Gandhian who had led the palm-tree cutting campaign during the Civil Disobedience Movement.
255.tq: Link the leader with the specific campaign rather than a general Gandhian activity.

255.s:
Consider the following statements about the political context of Swami Sitaram's fast:
1. Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga in the April 1951 APCC election.
2. Sanjiva Reddy's margin of victory was five votes.
3. Prakasam and Ranga subsequently formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: All three statements are correct: Sanjiva Reddy defeated N.G. Ranga by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga left to form the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.
255.tq: Check the linked sequence of election result, margin and subsequent political action.

255.s: Who wrote the series of articles titled “On the present position of the Telugu people” in The Hindu in 1911?
255.x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham of the Youngmen's Literary Association, Guntur, wrote the series in The Hindu in 1911.
255.tq: Match the article series with its author and newspaper.

255.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 1911 articles by Jonnavittula Gurunatham?
o: Six articles, including “Are Telugu people backward?”, published in The Hindu
Four articles on Madras city published in Deshabhimani
Six articles on Andhra capital published in Andhra Patrika
A single editorial on linguistic states published in Krishna Patrika
255.x: Gurunatham wrote six articles in The Hindu in 1911; one of them was “Are Telugu people backward?”
255.tq: Use the combined author–newspaper–article-count clue.

255.s: “Are Telugu people backward?” was published on which date?
255.x: The article “Are Telugu people backward?” appeared on 15 April 1911 as part of the series in The Hindu.
255.tq: Distinguish the precise article date from the dates of newspaper events.

255.s: Which newspaper was described as the only daily from British Andhra?
255.x: Deshabhimani was an Anglo-Telugu paper from Guntur and was described as the only daily from British Andhra.
255.tq: Identify the newspaper through its distinctive status and location.

255.s: Deshabhimani first called for a political meeting on the problems of Andhras on
255.x: Deshabhimani made the first call for a political meeting on Andhra problems on 4 February 1910.
255.tq: Separate the newspaper's call date from its later supplement and founding dates.

255.s: Who edited Deshabhimani and argued that the distant Madras capital and officials unfamiliar with Telugu harmed Andhra?
255.x: Seshagirirao, the editor of Deshabhimani, criticised the distance of the Madras capital and the lack of Telugu knowledge among administrators.
255.tq: Use the editor–argument association to distinguish among newspaper personalities.

255.s: Deshabhimani's English supplement in December 1911 was published in connection with
o: The coronation of George V at Delhi
The formation of the Youngmen's Literary Association
255.x: Deshabhimani printed an English supplement in December 1911 for George V's Delhi coronation.
255.tq: Match the newspaper supplement with the event for which it was issued.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Patrika:
1. It was founded in Bombay and later moved to Madras.
2. It became a daily in 1914.
3. Its name was chosen to popularise the word “Andhra”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Andhra Patrika was founded in Bombay, moved to Madras, became a daily in 1914, and helped popularise the word “Andhra”.
255.tq: Verify each newspaper attribute independently before selecting the coded combination.

255.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Janmabhumi — English supplement for George V's coronation
255.x: The English supplement for George V's coronation was published by Deshabhimani. Janmabhumi carried the view on 25 August 1920 that the Andhra movement could serve national unity.
255.tq: Find the swapped newspaper contribution in a closely related list.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Newspaper)
a. Deshabhimani
b. Andhra Patrika
c. Andhra Advocate
 d. Janmabhumi
List-II (Contribution)
i. Propaganda by the Vizag district committee
 ii. The Andhra movement can serve national unity
 iii. Popularisation of the word “Andhra”
 iv. Demand for protection of Telugu culture through its own government
Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: Deshabhimani argued for protection of Telugu culture through its own government; Andhra Patrika popularised “Andhra”; Andhra Advocate was used for propaganda; and Janmabhumi linked the Andhra movement with national unity.
255.tq: Start from the sure newspaper–contribution pairs and eliminate inconsistent codes.

255.s: The Telugu-medium resolution of 1915 was supported by which Tamil daily?
255.x: The Tamil daily Swadesamitran supported the Telugu-medium resolution of 1915.
255.tq: Test the cross-linguistic newspaper support rather than the Andhra newspapers themselves.

255.s: Who proposed the Cooum river as the boundary between the Andhra and Tamil areas in the early 1920s?
255.x: Panaganti Ramarayaningar, popularly known as the Raja of Panagal and Madras Chief Minister in the early 1920s, proposed the Cooum as the boundary.
255.tq: Use the office-and-proposal association to identify the correct person.

255.s: Under the proposal of the Raja of Panagal, which arrangement was suggested regarding the Cooum river?
o: The river would have no role in demarcating Andhra and Tamil areas
The area south of it would go to Andhras and the area north of it to Tamils
The area north of it would go to Andhras and the area south of it to Tamils
The entire river basin would become a Union Territory
255.x: Panaganti Ramarayaningar proposed the Cooum river as the boundary, with the northern side for Andhras and the southern side for Tamils.
255.tq: Check the direction of the proposed division carefully because the comparison is easily reversed.

255.s: Who proposed in 1933 that Madras should be the capital of Andhra?
255.x: Kadapa Koti Reddy, associated with the Rayalaseema Mahasabha of 1933, proposed Madras as the Andhra capital.
255.tq: Match the specific year and organisation with the person making the proposal.

255.s: Which book argued the Telugu claim over Madras by declaring that Madras was an Andhra city?
o: The Telugu People and Madras Presidency
On the Present Position of the Telugu People
255.x: Tanguturi Prakasam's book “Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae” argued that Madras was an Andhra city.
255.tq: Identify the work through its distinctive title and claim.

255.s: Which of the following correctly represents the position of Telugu leaders regarding Madras?
o: They demanded that Madras remain exclusively under Tamil administration
They accepted Madras only as the capital of Telangana
They opposed any political status for Madras
They wanted Madras either as the Andhra capital or as a shared Union Territory
255.x: Telugu leaders sought Madras as the Andhra capital or, alternatively, as a shared Union Territory.
255.tq: Distinguish the principal demand from the alternative compromise position.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Madras city issue:
1. Rajaji and later Kamaraj opposed sharing Madras.
2. The JVP formula of 1948 allowed an Andhra State only if the claim to Madras was abandoned.
3. The fifth session of the Andhra Mahasabha at Nellore in 1917 accepted the demand to include Madras city.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Rajaji and Kamaraj opposed sharing Madras, and the JVP formula required Andhra leaders to drop their claim to Madras. The Nellore session of 1917 rejected, rather than accepted, the demand to include Madras city.
255.tq: Spot the reversed historical decision in the third statement.

255.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the Madras city question in chronological order:
A. The fifth session of the Andhra Mahasabha rejected the demand to include Madras city.
B. Kadapa Koti Reddy proposed Madras as the Andhra capital.
C. The JVP formula required the claim to Madras to be dropped for an Andhra State.
D. Panaganti Ramarayaningar proposed the Cooum river as the boundary.
255.x: The correct sequence is the Nellore session of 1917, the Cooum proposal in the early 1920s, Koti Reddy's proposal in 1933, and the JVP formula in 1948.
255.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two intermediate proposals by date.

255.s: The Rayalaseema Mahasabha was formed in which year?
255.x: The Rayalaseema Mahasabha was formed in 1934.
255.tq: Use direct year recall for the formation of an organisation.

255.s:
With reference to the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha, consider the following statements:
1. It was held on 28 January 1934.
2. Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao presided over it.
3. It demanded the inclusion of Rayalaseema in Andhra University.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on 28 January 1934 and was presided over by Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao. It opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati, making statement 3 false.
255.tq: Find the single reversed demand in a group of related statements.

255.s: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha demanded a separate university at:
255.x: The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.
255.tq: Test the exact institution-place association.

255.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Meeting)
a. Rayalaseema districts Mahasabha
b. First Rayalaseema Mahasabha
c. Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha
d. Rayalaseema meeting at Mahanandi

List-II (President or associated figure)
i. Guthi Kesava Pillai
ii. Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao
iii. T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy
iv. Kalluri Subbarao

Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: Guthi Kesava Pillai was associated with the Mahanandi meeting, Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao presided over the first Mahasabha, and T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy presided over the second Mahasabha. Kalluri Subbarao presided over the October 1931 Madras meeting.
255.tq: Start from the sure president–meeting pairs and eliminate the codes.

255.s: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha, held in September 1935, adopted which of the following resolutions?
o: Opposition to a separate Andhra state
Demand for immediate merger with Telangana
Demand for a separate Andhra province without safeguards
Demand for Madras as the capital of Andhra State
255.x: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha held at Kadapa in September 1935 opposed the creation of a separate Andhra state.
255.tq: Test the precise resolution rather than the general regional demand.

255.s: Which one of the following was NOT present at the second Rayalaseema Mahasabha in 1935?
255.x: Koti Reddy, Pappuri Ramachari and Gadicherla were absent from the second Rayalaseema Mahasabha. T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy presided over the meeting.
255.tq: Find the odd membership detail among closely related names.

255.s: The 1935 opposition of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha to a separate Andhra state eventually contributed to the:
255.x: The 1935 resolution opposing a separate Andhra state led to the Sri Bagh Pact, which addressed Rayalaseema safeguards.
255.tq: Test the cause-and-effect link between a regional resolution and its outcome.

255.s:
At the 1937 Silver Jubilee session, Rayalaseema leaders demanded safeguards relating to which of the following?
1. Cabinet representation
2. Irrigation
3. Capital
4. Separate army recruitment

Select the correct answer using the code below.
255.x: The safeguards demanded in 1937 concerned representation in the Cabinet, irrigation and the capital. Separate army recruitment was not among the stated demands.
255.tq: Reject the unrelated addition to a known three-item list.

255.s: Who formed a new Rayalaseema Mahasabha in 1938 opposing the Andhra province?
o: Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao and T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy
R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry
Guthi Kesava Pillai and Kalluri Subbarao
255.x: R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry formed a new Rayalaseema Mahasabha in 1938 to oppose the Andhra province.
255.tq: Use the founder–organisation association as the deciding clue.

255.s: What position did the Rayalaseema Mahasabha communicate to the Dhar Commission in 1948?
o: A united Andhra province with Vijayawada as capital
Immediate merger with the Hyderabad State
A separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Continuation of the Madras Presidency without reorganisation
255.x: In 1948, the Rayalaseema Mahasabha told the Dhar Commission that it wanted a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as its capital.
255.tq: Discriminate between a regional demand and the proposed capital.

255.s: Guthi Kesava Pillai, at the Mahanandi meeting of April 1913, described the demand for separation as:
o: A movement led by the Madras Government
255.x: At Mahanandi in April 1913, Guthi Kesava Pillai considered separation impractical and called it a “Brahmin movement.”
255.tq: Recall the exact characterization used in a regional debate.

255.s: In October 1931, at Madras, Kalluri Subbarao sought:
o: Madras as the capital of Rayalaseema
255.x: At the October 1931 Madras meeting presided over by Kalluri Subbarao, separate representation for Rayalaseema was sought.
255.tq: Link the meeting, presiding person and specific demand.

255.s: Which of the following correctly explains the employment imbalance faced by Telugu people in the Madras Presidency around 1910?
o: Telugus formed about 40 percent of the population but held a disproportionately small share of senior posts.
Telugus and non-Telugus held equal shares in all government posts.
Telugus formed about 40 percent of the population and held all district-level posts.
Telugus formed less than 10 percent of the population and dominated the highest posts.
255.x: Telugus constituted about 40 percent, or nearly two crore people, of the Madras Presidency around 1910, but were under-represented in senior government employment.
255.tq: Compare population share with administrative representation rather than reading either figure in isolation.

255.s:
Consider the following statements regarding government employment in the Madras Presidency:
1. Telugus held 21 of the Deputy Collector posts.
2. Telugus held no District Judge posts.
3. Telugus held 30 District Munsif posts.
4. Telugus held 56 high State jobs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
255.x: Telugus held 21 Deputy Collector posts, no District Judge posts and 30 District Munsif posts. They held 8 high State jobs, while non-Telugus held 56; therefore statement 4 is false.
255.tq: Check each numerical row against the comparison table, especially the reversed final figure.

255.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the distribution of posts between Telugu and non-Telugu officials?
255.x: The distribution for Deputy Collectors was 21 Telugu and 39 non-Telugu officials. The other pairs interchange figures belonging to different categories or reverse the actual order.
255.tq: Use row-by-row comparison and reject swapped numerical pairs.

255.s: In 1915, how many colleges in the Madras Presidency were located in Andhra?
255.x: Only 8 of the 31 colleges in the Madras Presidency were located in Andhra in 1915.
255.tq: Test the exact numerator from a population-distribution figure.

255.s: Which of the following educational facilities was absent in Andhra in 1915?
255.x: In 1915, Andhra had no engineering, medical or law college, although it had 8 colleges and 163 secondary schools.
255.tq: Identify the absent category in a list of educational deficiencies.

255.s: How many secondary schools out of 583 in the Madras Presidency were located in Andhra in 1915?
255.x: There were 163 secondary schools in Andhra out of a total of 583 in the Madras Presidency in 1915.
255.tq: Distinguish the exact figure from nearby numerical distractors.

255.s: The political, educational and employment dominance of which group in the Madras capital intensified Telugu grievances?
255.x: Tamils dominated politics, education and government employment in the Madras capital, contributing to Telugu dissatisfaction.
255.tq: Test the dominant regional group associated with the grievance.

255.s: The Rayalaseema leadership alleged that surplus revenue from the Andhra deltas was spent mainly on:
255.x: The Mahasabha alleged that surplus revenue generated in the Andhra delta districts was spent on Tamil areas.
255.tq: Identify the alleged direction of regional revenue transfer.

255.s: Which districts were the most enthusiastic supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province?
255.x: Krishna and Guntur were the most eager supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province.
255.tq: Separate the leading districts from the lukewarm regions.

255.s: Why were Nellore, Rayalaseema, Ganjam and Visakhapatnam comparatively lukewarm towards the separate Andhra demand?
o: They were close to or connected with competing administrative and regional interests.
They opposed all forms of provincial representation.
They had already become part of Hyderabad State.
255.x: Nellore was close to Madras, while Rayalaseema and the northern districts of Ganjam and Visakhapatnam were less enthusiastic for regional and administrative reasons. They were not devoid of Telugu population or opposed to all representation.
255.tq: Apply the regional comparison to explain differing levels of political enthusiasm.

255.s: At the Nellore session of 1917, which fact affected the method of voting?
o: Most delegates came from Krishna, so voting was conducted by village.
480 of 740 delegates came from Nellore, so voting was conducted district-wise.
The absence of Rayalaseema delegates led to voting by language group.
740 of 480 delegates came from Nellore, so voting was conducted state-wise.
255.x: Since 480 of the 740 delegates came from Nellore, voting was conducted district-wise to avoid domination by one district.
255.tq: Connect the numerical imbalance with the procedural consequence.

255.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Partition of Bengal
B. Separation of Bihar and Orissa
C. Mahanandi meeting of Rayalaseema leaders
D. Nellore session of the Andhra movement
255.x: The Partition of Bengal occurred in 1905, Bihar and Orissa were separated in 1912, the Mahanandi meeting was held in April 1913, and the Nellore session took place in 1917.
255.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the two middle events.

255.s: The separation of Bihar and Orissa in 1912 demonstrated that:
o: The Madras Presidency could not be divided.
Provinces could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
Language had no role in territorial administration.
Only princely states could be reorganised.
255.x: The separation of Bihar and Orissa was cited as evidence that provincial boundaries could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
255.tq: Infer the political significance of a historical example.

255.s: The Vande Mataram movement of 1905–1911 contributed to the Andhra movement by:
255.x: The Vande Mataram movement between 1905 and 1911 politicised Andhra youth and helped create a favourable climate for regional mobilisation.
255.tq: Match a movement with its stated social and political effect.

255.s: Which of the following was cited by Andhra leaders as a precedent for linguistic reorganisation?
o: The formation of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha in 1934
The abolition of the Madras Presidency
The creation of Bihar and Orissa as separate provinces and their multiple Congress circles
The merger of Andhra with Hyderabad State
255.x: Andhra leaders referred to Bihar and Orissa, including their multiple Congress circles, as a precedent for provincial reorganisation on linguistic lines.
255.tq: Identify the historical precedent used to support a later demand.

255.s: The Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur, founded in 1903, is regarded as the:
o: Venue of the Sri Bagh Pact
