261.s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed in November 1949 at
261.x: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed at Vijayawada in November 1949.
261.tq: Distinguish the organisation’s formation venue from the venue of its first meeting.

261.s: Who was associated with the formation of the first Visalandhra Mahasabha?
261.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was associated with the formation of the first Visalandhra Mahasabha.
261.tq: Use the founder–organisation association rather than a later opponent or supporter.

261.s: The first meeting of the Visalandhra Mahasabha, held in 1950, resolved that the capital should be
261.x: The first meeting at Warangal in 1950 resolved in favour of Hyderabad as the capital.
261.tq: Separate the organisation’s formation venue from its proposed capital.

261.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha under Hayagreevachari proposed that Hyderabad State be
o: divided into three linguistic regions, with Telugu districts merged with Andhra
261.x: Hayagreevachari’s proposal divided Hyderabad State into three linguistic regions and supported merging its Telugu districts with Andhra.
261.tq: Test the exact territorial proposal rather than the broader demand for Visalandhra.

261.s: The proposal of the Visalandhra Mahasabha under Hayagreevachari was opposed by
o: Sri Sri and Swami Ramananda Tirtha
Marri Chenna Reddy and K. V. Ranga Reddy
261.x: Marri Chenna Reddy and K. V. Ranga Reddy opposed the proposal associated with Hayagreevachari.
261.tq: Avoid swapping supporters and opponents in a regional political debate.

261.s: Who argued that Telangana would develop under Visalandhra at the second Visalandhra Mahasabha?
261.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha stated that Telangana would develop under Visalandhra.
261.tq: Distinguish the advocate of integration from those associated with opposition or alternative proposals.

261.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Sundarayya — Visalandhra Prajarajyam
2. Sundarayya — Vishalandhra magazine
3. Hyderabad Congress, June 1953 — support for a three-way division of Hyderabad State
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
261.x: Sundarayya was associated with Visalandhra Prajarajyam and the magazine Vishalandhra. The Hyderabad Congress in June 1953 supported a three-way division of Hyderabad State.
261.tq: Check all three organisation–position associations before choosing the combined code.

261.s: The statement that Visalandhra represented ‘Andhra imperialism’ was made by Jawaharlal Nehru in
261.x: In October 1953, Nehru described Visalandhra as ‘Andhra imperialism’, strengthening the separate-Telangana position.
261.tq: Pair the political statement with its precise date and context.

261.s: The States Reorganisation Commission submitted its report on
261.x: The Commission submitted its report on 30 September 1955; it was made public on 9 October 1955.
261.tq: Distinguish submission from publication dates.

261.s: The report of the States Reorganisation Commission was made public on
261.x: The report was made public on 9 October 1955, shortly after its submission on 30 September 1955.
261.tq: Use the paired-date trap involving submission and public release.

261.s: Which of the following was included among the states recommended by the States Reorganisation Commission?
261.x: Hyderabad and Vidarbha were among the states included in the Commission’s recommendation.
261.tq: Use named examples from the recommended state list.

261.s: The States Reorganisation Commission proposed the abolition of the classification into
o: Part A, Part B and Part C states, with Part D units also removed from the classification
Part A, Part B and Part C only
Part A, Part B and Part C states
261.x: The Commission proposed abolishing the Part A, Part B and Part C classification, while the broader reorganisation replaced the old Part A–D arrangement with states and Union Territories.
261.tq: Choose the most complete formulation when a constitutional classification is described.

261.s: In the report structure of the States Reorganisation Commission, Chapter 5 dealt with
261.x: Chapter 5 dealt with Hyderabad State, while Chapter 6 dealt with Andhra State.
261.tq: Separate adjacent chapter subjects rather than relying on the common regional theme.

261.s: Which chapter of the States Reorganisation Commission report dealt with Andhra State?
261.x: Chapter 6 of the report dealt with Andhra State.
261.tq: Test the paired chapter numbering for Hyderabad and Andhra.

261.s: The paragraphs dealing with the division of Hyderabad in the States Reorganisation Commission report were
261.x: Paragraphs 359–368 dealt with the division of Hyderabad.
261.tq: Distinguish adjacent paragraph ranges by subject.

261.s: The case for Visalandhra was discussed in paragraphs
261.x: Paragraphs 369–374 set out the case for Visalandhra.
261.tq: Match the precise paragraph range with the issue discussed.

261.s: What arrangement for Telangana was recommended in paragraph 386 of the States Reorganisation Commission report?
o: Formation as a Union Territory under the Centre
Initial functioning as a separate state called Hyderabad State
261.x: Paragraph 386 recommended that Telangana initially function as a separate state to be called Hyderabad State.
261.tq: Test the exact recommended arrangement rather than the eventual political outcome.

261.s: Under the review mechanism proposed for Telangana, reconsideration of its merger with Visalandhra could take place after
261.x: The Telangana Legislative Assembly could reconsider the merger after the 1961 general elections.
261.tq: Use the exact election year as the decisive chronological marker.

261.s: The Telangana Legislative Assembly could support unification with Visalandhra only if at least what proportion of its elected members supported it?
261.x: The proposed review mechanism required support from two-thirds of the elected members of the Telangana Legislative Assembly.
261.tq: Distinguish constitutional-style fractions by comparing the exact threshold.

261.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the SRC recommendation on Telangana:
1. Telangana was to function initially as a separate state.
2. The separate state was to be called Hyderabad State.
3. Merger could be reconsidered after the 1961 general elections.
4. Unification required support from two-thirds of the elected members of the Telangana Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
261.x: All four statements correctly describe the arrangement and review mechanism recommended for Telangana.
261.tq: Verify each condition in a multi-part constitutional recommendation before selecting the complete code.

261.s: Which of the following was cited as an argument in favour of Visalandhra by the States Reorganisation Commission?
o: The merger would eliminate all regional disparities immediately
Coastal Andhra would be kept outside the proposed state
The proposed state would have about 3.2 crore people and rich raw materials and minerals
Telangana would retain exclusive control over Krishna-Godavari waters
261.x: The SRC noted that Visalandhra would be a large state of about 3.2 crore people with considerable raw materials and mineral resources.
261.tq: Identify the argument that belongs to the correct side of a comparison.

261.s: The proposed inclusion of Hyderabad in Visalandhra was considered advantageous primarily because it would
o: transfer the capital of India to the Deccan
place all administrative institutions under Telangana control
ensure that Telangana retained a separate capital
provide a solution to the capital problem of Andhra State
261.x: The SRC regarded Hyderabad as a common capital that could solve the capital problem faced by Andhra State.
261.tq: Match a specific proposal with its stated administrative advantage.

261.s: Which one of the following was NOT mentioned as an economic or administrative advantage of Visalandhra?
o: Permanent protection of Telangana's revenue surplus from outside expenditure
Unified control over Krishna-Godavari waters, dams and power
261.x: Protection of Telangana's revenue surplus was an apprehension of opponents of immediate merger, not an advantage of Visalandhra.
261.tq: Find the option belonging to the opposite side of the debate.

261.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the objections to an immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra:
1. Educationally and administratively more advanced Coastal Andhra might dominate government services.
2. Mulki rules and local employment opportunities might be affected.
3. Telangana's revenue surplus might be spent in other regions.
4. Regional disparities might widen.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
261.x: All four statements represent concerns recorded in the Telangana case against an immediate merger.
261.tq: Test all rows of a comparison table through coded statements.

261.s: The States Reorganisation Commission gave weight to Telangana's grievances mainly in which two fields, despite noting majority support among Telangana legislators for Visalandhra?
261.x: The SRC observed majority support for Visalandhra among Telangana legislators but gave serious consideration to grievances relating to finance and education.
261.tq: Separate the general political preference from the specific reservations recorded by the Commission.

261.s: Tenneti Viswanatham criticised the States Reorganisation Commission's report for being
o: opposed to the use of Hyderabad as a capital
favourable only to a separate Telangana
261.x: Tenneti Viswanatham described the report as self-contradictory.
261.tq: Directly identify the criticism associated with a particular political leader.

261.s: Who moved in the Andhra Assembly a resolution guaranteeing Telangana priority and population-based shares in jobs, education, irrigation and development?
261.x: Andhra Chief Minister Bezawada Gopala Reddy moved the resolution containing guarantees for Telangana.
261.tq: Use the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap carefully by identifying the office-holder linked to the action.

261.s:
The resolution moved in the Andhra Assembly concerning safeguards for Telangana provided for population-based shares in which of the following areas?
1. Jobs
2. Education
3. Irrigation
4. Development
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
261.x: The resolution covered jobs, education, irrigation and development, with priority and shares linked to population.
261.tq: Reconstruct a resolution by checking every component named in it.

261.s: The Andhra Assembly resolution guaranteeing safeguards for Telangana was passed
o: by a two-thirds majority with opposition abstaining
after being rejected once and reintroduced
261.x: The resolution guaranteeing safeguards for Telangana was passed unanimously.
261.tq: Distinguish the manner of adoption from the content of a resolution.

261.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Communist position during the Visalandhra debate is correct?
o: Communists consistently opposed all linguistic states.
Communists supported a separate Telangana but opposed Andhra State.
Communists took no position on the linguistic reorganisation of states.
Communists consistently supported integrated linguistic states and Visalandhra.
261.x: The Communist movement consistently supported integrated linguistic states and specifically backed Visalandhra.
261.tq: Discriminate between a genuine political position and its reversed form.

261.s: The advocates of a separate Telangana generally reacted to the States Reorganisation Commission's report by
o: supporting the immediate merger without safeguards
rejecting it as a plan for immediate Visalandhra
demanding the abolition of Hyderabad State
261.x: Special-Telangana advocates welcomed the report because its approach did not favour an immediate merger with Andhra.
261.tq: Link the political reaction to the practical consequence of the Commission's recommendation.

261.s: In the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra, how many members voted in favour of the proposal?
261.x: Of the members who voted, 103 supported Visalandhra, while 29 opposed it and 15 remained neutral.
261.tq: Separate the total membership from the voting figures and test the exact number.

261.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hyderabad Assembly vote on Visalandhra:
1. The Assembly had 174 members.
2. 103 members voted in favour of Visalandhra.
3. 29 members voted against it.
4. 15 members remained neutral.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
261.x: The Hyderabad Assembly had 174 members; the recorded vote was 103 in favour, 29 against and 15 neutral, with 147 members voting.
261.tq: Check whether the total membership and each component of a numerical distribution are retained.

261.s: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao worked to allay Telangana's fears primarily
o: under instructions from the States Reorganisation Commission
at the request of the Communist Party
on the direction of the Congress High Command
on the direction of the Hyderabad Assembly Speaker alone
261.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, then Chief Minister, acted on the direction of the Congress High Command to reduce Telangana's apprehensions.
261.tq: Identify the correct authority behind a political action.

261.s: Who among the following supported a separate Telangana at the Telangana convention held in November 1955?
261.x: Harishchandra Heda supported the demand for a separate Telangana at the November 1955 Telangana convention.
261.tq: Match a leader with the specific forum and position associated with him.

261.s: Jawaharlal Nehru compared the merger of Andhra and Telangana to a
o: temporary administrative arrangement imposed by Parliament
military treaty between two sovereign states
matrimonial alliance with a provision for divorce
federal compact without any provision for separation
261.x: In 1956 Nehru likened the merger to a matrimonial alliance, adding that there could be a provision for divorce if the partners could not get along.
261.tq: Recall the exact metaphor used for a politically significant arrangement.

261.s: Nehru's "matrimonial alliance" remark was made in the context of a merger that
o: followed the SRC's advice without conditions
was made against the SRC's advice and rested on safeguards
created a separate Telangana outside Hyderabad State
261.x: The remark referred to the Andhra-Telangana merger, which proceeded politically despite the SRC's advice and was based on safeguards.
261.tq: Use the context rather than the metaphor alone to identify the correct historical event.

261.s: The later political significance of Nehru's matrimonial-alliance remark was that it was cited by
o: supporters of the abolition of linguistic states
the advocates of a permanently centralised India
the proponents of retaining the Part A-D classification
261.x: Separate-Telangana advocates later invoked the remark as evidence that the merger was conditional rather than irrevocable.
261.tq: Connect a historical statement with the later group that used it politically.

261.s:
Which of the following correctly explains the broader outcome of linguistic reorganisation in India?
1. It was feared that linguistic reorganisation might weaken national unity.
2. It also made administration more workable in people's languages.
3. Border disputes, including the Belgaum dispute between Maharashtra and Karnataka, continued.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
261.x: Linguistic reorganisation raised concerns about national unity, but improved administration through people's languages; disputes such as Belgaum nevertheless continued.
261.tq: Balance the stated advantages, criticisms and continuing consequences.

261.s: Which border dispute is cited as an example of a continuing dispute after linguistic reorganisation?
o: Chandigarh between Kerala and Tamil Nadu
261.x: The Belgaum dispute between Maharashtra and Karnataka is an example of a border dispute that continued after linguistic reorganisation.
261.tq: Identify the correctly paired place and states in a continuing dispute.

261.s: The States Reorganisation Commission's approach to Telangana, according to the Andhra Pradesh perspective, was that it
o: kept Telangana out of the proposed Visalandhra
recommended the immediate creation of Telangana as a Union Territory
261.x: The SRC plan kept Telangana outside Visalandhra, whereas the eventual merger was effected through a political decision.
261.tq: Distinguish the Commission's recommendation from the later political outcome.

261.s: The political merger of Andhra State and Telangana was later associated with regional questions during which periods?
261.x: The politically effected merger contributed to regional questions that became prominent in 1969-72 and again in 2014.
261.tq: Select the pair of later periods directly connected with the regional consequences.

261.s: Which of the following was one of the safeguards associated with the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956?
o: Permanent exclusion of Hyderabad from Andhra Pradesh
261.x: The Regional Council was one of the safeguards associated with the 1956 arrangement; Mulki rules were another.
261.tq: Identify a genuine safeguard among administratively unrelated alternatives.

261.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of Andhra State
B. Formation of Andhra Pradesh under the States Reorganisation Act
C. Telangana movement of 1969
D. Re-emergence of the Telangana issue in 2014
261.x: Andhra State was formed in 1953, Andhra Pradesh in 1956, the Telangana movement intensified in 1969, and the issue re-emerged prominently in 2014.
261.tq: Use the first and last events, then place the two intermediate developments.

261.s: Which of the following statements regarding the significance of Andhra State is correct?
o: It was created after Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956.
It was the first state created under the States Reorganisation Act of 1956.
It was the first linguistic state of independent India and set a precedent for nationwide linguistic reorganisation.
It ended the Part A-D system before independence.
261.x: Andhra State, formed in 1953, was the first linguistic state of independent India and provided the precedent for wider linguistic reorganisation.
261.tq: Distinguish the first linguistic state from the first state formed under the 1956 Act.

261.s: The formation of Andhra State in 1953 had which immediate institutional consequence?
o: It abolished the need to examine the Andhra-Telangana question.
It converted Hyderabad into a Union Territory.
It ended all demands for linguistic states.
It triggered the appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission.
261.x: The formation of Andhra State triggered the appointment of the SRC, whose Hyderabad chapter addressed the Andhra-Telangana question.
261.tq: Trace the cause-and-effect chain from a regional development to a national institution.

261.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 is significant because it
o: made language the sole consideration without regard to viability
rejected linguistic states and restored the pre-independence provincial system
settled the linguistic principle while balancing administrative and economic viability and ended the Part A-D system
created only Union Territories and no states
261.x: The Act accepted linguistic reorganisation while attempting to preserve administrative and economic viability, and it ended the Part A-D classification.
261.tq: Choose the comprehensive significance statement rather than an extreme formulation.

261.s: The Centre's political handling of the Andhra-Telangana question differed from the SRC's formula because the Centre
o: referred the matter back to the Hyderabad Assembly indefinitely
overrode the recommendation to wait until 1961 and settled the issue through a political agreement
accepted the SRC plan of permanent separation without modification
waited until 1961 before considering any merger
261.x: The Centre did not follow the SRC's wait-till-1961 formula; it proceeded through a political agreement that resulted in the 1956 merger.
261.tq: Compare the Commission's proposed timing with the Centre's eventual political decision.

261.s: The departure from which paragraph of the States Reorganisation Commission's approach remained a core grievance of later Telangana movements?
261.x: The departure from paragraph 386 was identified as a central grievance in the Telangana movements of 1969 and 2001-14.
261.tq: Test an exact paragraph reference using nearby numerical distractors.

261.s:
Which of the following statements about the current relevance of state reorganisation is correct?
1. The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting was held in Tamil Nadu on 21 August 2026.
2. The Union Cabinet approved renaming Kerala as “Keralam” under Article 3.
3. A Private Member's Bill proposed a Permanent Framework for State Reorganisation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
261.x: All three developments are identified as contemporary examples of continuing issues relating to state organisation and reorganisation.
261.tq: Check dates, constitutional provisions and the nature of the current proposal together.

261.s: The constitutional provision associated with the Union Cabinet-approved renaming of Kerala as “Keralam” is
261.x: The proposed renaming was associated with Article 3 of the Constitution, which concerns the formation and alteration of states and their areas, boundaries or names.
261.tq: Match a constitutional article with the specific territorial action it governs.

261.s: Who again cited the Fazal Ali Commission recommendation in January 2026 to criticise the Congress over the 1956 merger?
261.x: BRS leader K. T. Rama Rao invoked the Fazal Ali Commission recommendation in January 2026 while criticising the Congress over the merger.
261.tq: Connect a contemporary political reference with the historical issue it invokes.

262.s:
With reference to the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956, consider the following statements:
1. The 11 districts of Andhra State were merged with the nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.
2. The Kannada-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were transferred to Mysore State.
3. The Marathi-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were transferred to Bombay State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh was formed by merging the 11 districts of Andhra State with the nine Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State, while the Kannada and Marathi areas went to Mysore and Bombay respectively.
262.tq: Use the regional-transfer pattern and verify each linguistic area separately.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the first office-holders of Andhra Pradesh formed in 1956?
o: Chief Minister — Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; Governor — C.M. Trivedi
Chief Minister — Bezawada Gopala Reddy; Governor — Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
Chief Minister — Tanguturi Prakasam; Governor — C.M. Trivedi
Chief Minister — Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; Governor — Kashinatha Rao
262.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy became the first Chief Minister and C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh after its formation in 1956.
262.tq: Match each constitutional office with the correct first holder and reject pre-merger office-holders.

262.s: The Andhra State, which was later merged with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State, came into existence on:
262.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953, with Kurnool as its capital, before the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.
262.tq: Distinguish the earlier formation date of Andhra State from the later formation date of Andhra Pradesh.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the political steps preceding the formation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Andhra Legislature met at Kurnool and unanimously resolved in favour of the merger.
2. Both the Andhra and Hyderabad ministries resigned to facilitate the formation of the unified state.
3. The merger was opposed by the Andhra Legislature through a divided vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Andhra Legislature unanimously supported the merger at Kurnool, and both ministries resigned; statement 3 is false.
262.tq: Find the single reversal in a question about unanimity and ministerial resignation.

262.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the naming of the unified Telugu-speaking state in chronological order:
A. The draft Bill used the name ‘Andhra Telangana’.
B. Communists proposed the name ‘Visalandhra’.
C. The Lok Sabha settled on the name ‘Andhra Pradesh’ through the Seventh Amendment Bill.

Select the correct sequence.
262.x: The draft Bill initially used ‘Andhra Telangana’; the Communists proposed ‘Visalandhra’; and the Seventh Amendment Bill finally settled on ‘Andhra Pradesh’.
262.tq: Track the evolution of the name from the draft proposal through the political suggestion to the final legal name.

262.s: The Seventh Amendment Bill, which settled the name ‘Andhra Pradesh’, was dealt with by the Lok Sabha on:
262.x: The Lok Sabha settled on the name ‘Andhra Pradesh’ through the Seventh Amendment Bill on 10 August 1956.
262.tq: Separate the date of the amendment decision from the dates of the agreement, Andhra State and Andhra Pradesh formation.

262.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic basis of the territorial adjustments preceding the formation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kannada-speaking areas of Hyderabad State went to Mysore and Marathi-speaking areas went to Bombay.
Marathi-speaking areas went to Mysore and Kannada-speaking areas went to Bombay.
Kannada-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were merged with Andhra State, while Marathi-speaking areas remained in Hyderabad State.
Both Kannada- and Marathi-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were merged with Andhra State.
262.x: The Kannada-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were transferred to Mysore, while the Marathi-speaking areas were transferred to Bombay, in accordance with linguistic reorganisation.
262.tq: Use the linguistic identity of each region to detect the swapped destination.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs relating to the pre-merger states is NOT correctly matched?
o: Andhra State — Bezawada Gopala Reddy as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Andhra State — Laxmi Narasimham as Speaker at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Burgula Ramakrishna Rao as Chief Minister at the time of merger
Hyderabad State — Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao as Speaker at the time of merger
262.x: The pair in option d is incorrect. Kashinatha Rao was the Speaker of Hyderabad State at the time of merger; Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao became the first Speaker of Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Identify the wrong office-holder by distinguishing pre-merger Speakers from the first Speaker of the unified state.

262.s:
Assertion (A): Andhra Pradesh was formed through the merger of Andhra State with the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State.
Reason (R): The reorganisation of states in 1956 was principally guided by linguistic considerations.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
262.x: Both statements are true, and the linguistic basis of state reorganisation explains why Andhra State and the Telugu-speaking districts of Hyderabad State were brought together.
262.tq: Test whether the stated principle directly explains the territorial merger described in the assertion.

262.s: Which of the following correctly describes the legal status given to the Gentlemen's Agreement in connection with the formation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It remained only a private political understanding without statutory support
It was enforced through the Andhra State Act, 1953
It was incorporated into the Constitution through a constitutional amendment
It was given statutory support through the States Reorganisation Act
262.x: The Gentlemen's Agreement was given statutory support through the States Reorganisation Act. It therefore formed part of the framework associated with the creation of Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Identify the correct legal instrument instead of confusing constitutional, statutory and political arrangements.

262.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed at which of the following places?
262.x: The agreement was signed at Hyderabad House in New Delhi. Some accounts refer to the venue as Hyderabad Guest House, Delhi, but the commonly recorded venue is Hyderabad House.
262.tq: Use location-based recall while distinguishing the venue from the place represented by the agreement.

262.s: Which one of the following was NOT a safeguard provided for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement?
o: Sales of agricultural land in Telangana were to be controlled by the Regional Council
All cabinet portfolios were to be permanently reserved for Telangana
Telangana's surplus revenue was to be spent only in Telangana
Urdu was to continue in Telangana's administration and courts for five years
262.x: The agreement did not reserve all cabinet portfolios permanently for Telangana. It provided a 60:40 cabinet arrangement, representation in key portfolios and other regional safeguards.
262.tq: Find the absolute and overextended claim among safeguards that were actually limited or proportionate.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding financial safeguards for Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. Common administrative costs were to be shared proportionately.
2. Telangana's surplus revenue was to be spent only in Telangana.
3. The financial arrangement was to be reviewed after five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. The agreement provided proportionate sharing of common expenditure, exclusive use of Telangana's surplus in Telangana and a review after five years.
262.tq: Check each statement against the separate components of a financial safeguard before selecting the combined option.

262.s: Under the educational safeguards of the Gentlemen's Agreement, Telangana students were to receive which of the following benefits in technical institutions?
o: Admission only through a separate entrance examination
Exactly one-half of all seats irrespective of institutional capacity
Priority in admission or at least one-third of the seats, whichever was more favourable
Admission exclusively in institutions established after 1956
262.x: The agreement protected existing educational facilities and provided Telangana students admission priority or at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
262.tq: Match the precise safeguard, especially the alternative wording 'whichever is more favourable'.

262.s: A technical institution has an admission policy under which Telangana students would receive either regional priority or a minimum quota. Which provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement is directly applicable to this situation?
262.x: The education safeguard dealt with admission priority for Telangana students or at least one-third of seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
262.tq: Translate the practical situation into the corresponding subject-specific safeguard.

262.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Services — Proportionate retrenchment and recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules
Land — Exclusive power of the Union Government over agricultural sales
Urdu — Abolition from Telangana administration immediately after the agreement
Prohibition — Uniform compulsory prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh
262.x: The services safeguard provided for recruitment according to population ratio under domicile rules and proportionate retrenchment from both regions. The other pairs contradict the agreed provisions.
262.tq: Start from the sure services pair and eliminate options that reverse or exaggerate the safeguard.

262.s: The domicile safeguard associated with recruitment in Telangana required residence for how many years?
262.x: The agreed safeguard referred to Mulki or domicile rules requiring 12 years of residence for recruitment in Telangana.
262.tq: Separate the exact numerical requirement from nearby duration figures used in related provisions.

262.s: Which statement regarding Urdu under the Gentlemen's Agreement is correct?
o: Urdu was to be retained in Telangana's administration and courts for five years, subject to later review by the Regional Council.
Urdu was declared the sole official language of the entire State for five years.
Urdu was excluded from courts but retained in educational institutions for five years.
Urdu was to be immediately replaced by English in Telangana's administration.
262.x: Urdu was to continue in Telangana's administration and courts for five years, after which the matter could be reviewed by the Regional Council.
262.tq: Watch the scope of the provision: it applied to Telangana administration and courts, not to the entire State.

262.s: Who was to exercise control over the sale of agricultural land in Telangana under the Gentlemen's Agreement?
262.x: The sale of agricultural land in Telangana was to be controlled by the Regional Council. This was intended as a regional safeguard over land matters.
262.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the authority assigned the regional power.

262.s: With regard to prohibition in Telangana, the Gentlemen's Agreement provided that the matter would be decided by
262.x: The question of prohibition in Telangana was left to the Telangana legislators. It was not made an automatically uniform policy for the entire State.
262.tq: Distinguish a regional legislative choice from powers assigned to the Governor or Union Parliament.

262.s: The cabinet composition agreed under the Gentlemen's Agreement was based on which ratio between Andhra and Telangana?
262.x: The finally agreed cabinet share was 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana. It was also provided that at least one Muslim minister would be included from Telangana.
262.tq: Prefer the precise percentage ratio when both a simplified ratio and a rounded formulation may appear in sources.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about political safeguards under the Gentlemen's Agreement:
1. The Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister were to be from different regions.
2. If the Chief Minister belonged to Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister was to belong to Telangana, and vice versa.
3. At least two among Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, and Commerce and Industry were to be allotted to Telangana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements correctly describe the political safeguards. The agreement also provided for at least one Muslim minister from Telangana and a 60:40 cabinet share.
262.tq: Read the political safeguards together and verify both the reciprocal rule and the specified portfolio list.

262.s: Which of the following was the proposed institutional safeguard specifically intended for Telangana?
o: A separate Supreme Court bench with exclusive jurisdiction
A Union Territory administration under the President
A statutory Regional Council or Committee
A permanent bicameral Parliament for Telangana
262.x: The agreement provided for a statutory Regional Council or Committee for Telangana. The other institutions were not part of the agreed safeguards.
262.tq: Identify the institution actually created for regional protection rather than choosing unrelated constitutional bodies.

262.s: The separate Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee contemplated under the agreement was to continue up to which year?
262.x: A separate Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee was provided for up to 1962, while the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee did not object to this arrangement.
262.tq: Use the end-year clue to distinguish a party-organisation safeguard from the broader political provisions.

262.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. The Andhra Assembly resolved to give Telangana priority and population-based allocations.
B. The Gentlemen's Agreement was signed.
C. The States Reorganisation framework gave statutory support to the arrangement.
D. The proposed name 'Andhra Telangana' was changed to 'Andhra Pradesh'.
262.x: The Andhra Assembly resolution preceded the signing of the agreement. Statutory support followed through the States Reorganisation framework, after which the proposed name was changed to Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Fix the earliest regional resolution first, then place the agreement, statutory support and name change.

262.s: The earlier resolution of the Andhra Assembly under Chief Minister Bezawada Gopala Reddy related to giving Telangana priority and population-based allocations in which areas?
o: Defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications
Language, forests, ports and public health only
262.x: The Andhra Assembly resolution supported Telangana priority and population-based allocations in jobs, education, irrigation and development.
262.tq: Recall the complete cluster of subjects rather than selecting a list containing Union subjects.

262.s: Which one of the following statements about the draft name of the proposed State is correct?
o: The draft bill initially used the name 'Andhra Telangana', which was later changed to 'Andhra Pradesh'.
The name 'Andhra Pradesh' was replaced by 'Andhra Telangana' after the Act was passed.
The State was initially named 'Hyderabad Andhra' and later renamed 'Telangana'.
The draft bill initially used the name 'Telangana Andhra', which was later changed to 'Visalandhra'.
262.x: The draft bill initially named the proposed State 'Andhra Telangana'. The name was subsequently changed to 'Andhra Pradesh'.
262.tq: Discriminate between closely related name formulations and track the direction of the change.

262.s: Who founded the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949?
262.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949 under the leadership of Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.
262.tq: Use the founder–organisation association directly.

262.s: Which of the following works was written by P. Sundarayya in support of the Visalandhra idea?
262.x: P. Sundarayya wrote “Visalandhra Prajarajyam” in support of the Visalandhra concept.
262.tq: Apply the author–work matching approach.

262.s: Which of the following was the newspaper or party paper associated with the Communist advocacy of Visalandhra?
262.x: The Communist Party paper associated with the Visalandhra campaign was “Vishalandhra”.
262.tq: Distinguish the exact title from nearby political publications.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sri Sri — President of the Second Visalandhra Mahasabha
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao — Founder of Visalandhra Mahasabha
Marri Chenna Reddy — Strong supporter of Visalandhra throughout
262.x: Marri Chenna Reddy was an opponent of Visalandhra. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
262.tq: Find the swapped political position among otherwise familiar associations.

262.s:
Consider the following persons:
1. Swami Ramananda Tirtha
2. Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
3. Mandumula Narsing Rao
4. Pandit Narendraji
Which of the above supported the Visalandhra movement?
262.x: All four—Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Burgula Ramakrishna Rao, Mandumula Narsing Rao and Pandit Narendraji—supported Visalandhra.
262.tq: Test a complete supporter list through coded combinations.

262.s: The Socialists supported the Visalandhra idea through meetings held at which place in 1954?
262.x: The Socialists held meetings at Gudivada and Kurnool in 1954 in support of the Visalandhra idea.
262.tq: Recall the paired venues associated with a political group.

262.s: Which political organisation, in addition to the Socialists, supported the Visalandhra movement?
262.x: The Hindu Mahasabha was also listed among the supporters of Visalandhra.
262.tq: Identify the organisation from a closely related political grouping.

262.s: The resolution supporting Visalandhra adopted by the Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee was passed at Kurnool on:
262.x: The APCC adopted the relevant resolution at Kurnool on 30 September 1953.
262.tq: Use the date–event association and reject nearby movement dates.

262.s: Who changed his position from supporting Visalandhra to opposing it?
262.x: The poet Kaloji initially supported Visalandhra but later opposed it. K.V. Ranga Reddy is separately noted as having changed sides in the opposite political context.
262.tq: Separate two similar instances of changing political position.

262.s: Which of the following opponents of Visalandhra belonged to the Praja Socialist Party (PSP)?
262.x: Mahadev Singh of the PSP was an opponent of the Visalandhra proposal.
262.tq: Link the individual with the correct political organisation.

262.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Founding of the Visalandhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada
B. First Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal
C. APCC resolution at Kurnool
D. Second Visalandhra Mahasabha at Hyderabad
262.x: The sequence is: founding at Vijayawada in November 1949, first Mahasabha at Warangal in February 1950, APCC resolution in September 1953, and second Mahasabha at Hyderabad in June 1954.
262.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the middle events by year.

262.s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha was held at Warangal on 12–13 February 1950 under the presidency of:
262.x: Hayagreevachari presided over the first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal on 12–13 February 1950.
262.tq: Match the session venue and date with its presiding person.

262.s: Which of the following demands was associated with the first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal?
o: Hyderabad should be the capital and Hyderabad State should be divided into three linguistic parts
Telangana should remain permanently separate from Andhra
Kurnool should be the permanent capital of Hyderabad State
262.x: The first Mahasabha called for Hyderabad as the capital and for Hyderabad State to be divided into three linguistic parts.
262.tq: Select the precise programme associated with a particular conference.

262.s: The slogan “Visalandhra nirmanam…” was associated with which leader at the Warangal meeting of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
262.x: Tanguturi Prakasam gave the slogan “Visalandhra nirmanam…” at the Warangal meeting.
262.tq: Recall the speaker associated with a distinctive slogan.

262.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the 1954 Visalandhra discussions is correct?
1. Some leaders argued for a separate Telangana.
2. Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra.
3. Ramananda Tirtha warned that a separate Telangana would be weak and vulnerable to suppression of democratic forces.
4. The Second Mahasabha was held at Warangal.
262.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Second Mahasabha was held at Hyderabad, not Warangal.
262.tq: Find the single wrong venue while retaining the substantive conference facts.

262.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
262.x: The Socialists’ Kurnool meeting took place on 21–22 March 1954 and adopted a joint Andhra–Hyderabad resolution. The other dates and venues are mismatched.
262.tq: Start with the date–venue pair that is directly fixed in the chronology.

262.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh from 1964 to 1971?
262.x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh from 1964 to 1971, with a second term beginning on 6 March 1967.
262.tq: Recall the tenure of the office-holder rather than only the name.

262.s: Who served as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before the imposition of President’s Rule in January 1973?
262.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao served as Chief Minister from 1971 until President’s Rule began on 18 January 1973.
262.tq: Use the tenure boundary to distinguish adjacent Chief Ministers.

262.s: President’s Rule in Andhra Pradesh during the early Chief Ministerial sequence lasted from:
262.x: President’s Rule was imposed from 18 January to 10 December 1973.
262.tq: Distinguish the exact start and end dates from other political transition periods.

262.s: Which Chief Minister succeeded Jalagam Vengala Rao in March 1978?
262.x: Marri Chenna Reddy succeeded Jalagam Vengala Rao on 6 March 1978.
262.tq: Test succession between two adjacent administrations.

262.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Chief Minister and tenure immediately preceding T. Anjaiah?
262.x: M. Chenna Reddy served from 6 March 1978 to 1980, immediately before T. Anjaiah, who began his tenure on 11 October 1980.
262.tq: Check the immediate predecessor and the adjoining tenure dates.

262.s: Which Chief Minister was in office when the Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982?
262.x: The Telugu Desam Party was founded on 29 March 1982 during the tenure of Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy.
262.tq: Place the party’s founding date within the correct Chief Ministerial tenure.

262.s: Who was the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh immediately before N.T. Rama Rao assumed office in January 1983?
262.x: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy served from 20 September 1982 until January 1983, immediately before N.T. Rama Rao became Chief Minister.
262.tq: Use the last pre-1983 succession link to identify the correct office-holder.

262.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Damodaram Sanjivayya?
1. He was the second Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
2. He became Chief Minister on 11 January 1960.
3. He later became President of the Indian National Congress.
4. He was never defeated in an election.
262.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect; the claim that Damodaram Sanjivayya was never defeated in an election is the false statement.
262.tq: Identify the incorrect biographical claim among several true details.

262.s: Which Chief Minister had the shortest tenure in the listed history of Andhra Pradesh, serving for 31 days in August–September 1984?
262.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao had the shortest tenure, lasting 31 days from 16 August to 16 September 1984.
262.tq: Match the exceptional duration with the correct office-holder.

262.s: Who held the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh during 1995–2004?
262.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu had the longest continuous tenure as Chief Minister of united Andhra Pradesh, from 1995 to 2004.
262.tq: Compare the durations rather than merely recalling the sequence of office-holders.

262.s:
Which of the following statements about the early political history of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. All Chief Ministers up to January 1983 belonged to the Congress.
2. N.T. Rama Rao was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Congress rule continued uninterrupted from 1956 until 1983.
4. The first non-Congress Chief Minister was Nadendla Bhaskara Rao.
262.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because N.T. Rama Rao, not Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.
262.tq: Reject the swapped-person trap in a political succession statement.

262.s: Which group of four Chief Ministers represents the successive administrations through which Congress changed four Chief Ministers in four years before the rise of the Telugu Desam Party?
o: M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
Jalagam Vengala Rao, P.V. Narasimha Rao, M. Chenna Reddy and N.T. Rama Rao
Kasu Brahmananda Reddy, P.V. Narasimha Rao, T. Anjaiah and N.T. Rama Rao
M. Chenna Reddy, Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
262.x: The four Congress Chief Ministers were M. Chenna Reddy, T. Anjaiah, Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy and Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy. Their rapid succession contributed to political fatigue before the TDP emerged.
262.tq: Select the complete and correctly ordered succession set.

262.s:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers in chronological order of assuming office:
A. Jalagam Vengala Rao
B. M. Chenna Reddy
C. T. Anjaiah
D. Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy
262.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao assumed office in 1973, followed by M. Chenna Reddy in 1978, T. Anjaiah in 1980 and Bhavanam Venkatarami Reddy in February 1982.
262.tq: Arrange the administrations using their tenure years and transition dates.

262.s: Hyderabad State was classified as a Part B State during which of the following periods?
262.x: Hyderabad State was a Part B State from 1950 until 31 October 1956, immediately before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
262.tq: Use the exact constitutional period and distinguish the final date from the appointed day.

262.s: Who headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State that took office in 1952?
262.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State, which assumed office in 1952.
262.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap by separating Hyderabad leaders from Andhra leaders.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Hyderabad Congress:
1. In June 1953, it resolved to divide Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka.
2. In 1954, the earlier three-way division resolution was set aside.
3. The 1954 position supported the separation of Hyderabad State into regions corresponding to their linguistic states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. The Hyderabad Congress first adopted the three-way division proposal in June 1953, set it aside in 1954, and then supported linguistic reorganisation of its regions.
262.tq: Track the change in an organisation’s position chronologically rather than treating all resolutions as one.

262.s: B. Ramakrishna Rao initially supported a separate Telangana but changed his stand in 1954 and subsequently advocated which of the following?
o: The continuation of Hyderabad as a bilingual State
The merger of Telangana with United Maharashtra
The immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra
The creation of a separate Kannada-speaking State
262.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao changed his position in 1954 and advocated the early merger of Telangana with Andhra; he later kept Delhi informed in favour of Visalandhra.
262.tq: Test the before-and-after position of the same leader instead of confusing his initial stand with his later one.

262.s: At the Warangal Congress meeting held on 8 July 1954, B. Ramakrishna Rao stated that, before the States Reorganisation Commission report, the Hyderabad Government had:
o: Accepted the three-way division of Hyderabad State
No official opinion, while ministers expressed personal views
Officially rejected the merger with Andhra
262.x: At Warangal on 8 July 1954, he stated that the Hyderabad Government had no official opinion before the SRC report and that ministers had expressed only personal views.
262.tq: Use the precise date and distinguish an official government position from individual ministerial opinions.

262.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the event with its date concerning the merger discussions?
1. Meeting of the Chief Ministers at Hyderabad House, New Delhi — 22 October 1955
2. Gentlemen’s Agreement — 20 February 1956
3. Warangal Congress meeting — 8 July 1954
262.x: All three date-event pairs are correctly matched: the Warangal meeting was on 8 July 1954, the Chief Ministers met at Hyderabad House on 22 October 1955, and the agreement was signed on 20 February 1956.
262.tq: Start from the sure date-event pair and verify the remaining chronological pairs.

262.s: Which of the following correctly represents the linguistic composition of Hyderabad State as given in the demographic figures?
262.x: The population of Hyderabad State was 18.7 million, comprising Telugu speakers at 47.8%, Marathi speakers at 24.3%, Urdu speakers at 11.6% and Kannada speakers at 10.5%.
262.tq: Compare each percentage with its language rather than relying only on the largest group.

262.s: The Telangana Regional Committee was constituted in 1958 under which constitutional provision?
262.x: The Telangana Regional Committee was constituted in 1958 under Article 371(1), with appointment by the President.
262.tq: Use the exact Article-number distinction among special constitutional provisions.

262.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana Regional Committee:
1. It consisted of elected representatives from Telangana.
2. All Telangana ministers except the Chief Minister were ex officio members.
3. Disputes between the Committee and the State Government were to be referred to the Centre for final decision.
4. Its working was to be reviewed after ten years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All four statements are correct. The Committee represented Telangana legislators, included Telangana ministers other than the Chief Minister ex officio, referred disputes to the Centre and was subject to review after ten years.
262.tq: Check composition, dispute settlement and review clauses separately before selecting the complete combination.

262.s: Which of the following was NOT among the subjects assigned to the Telangana Regional Committee?
262.x: The Committee dealt with regional matters such as planning, irrigation, agriculture, industry, recruitment, health, education and prohibition. Foreign affairs was not among its subjects.
262.tq: Find the subject outside the regional administrative and developmental sphere.

262.s: The Mulki Rules originated during which period and required approximately how much local residence for eligibility for local government employment?
262.x: The Mulki Rules originated in the Nizam’s era in 1919 and required about 15 years of residence for eligibility for local jobs. This differed from the 12-year domicile provision in the 1956 Agreement.
262.tq: Separate the Mulki residence requirement from the different domicile period in the Gentlemen’s Agreement.

262.s: Which of the following statements regarding the later history of the Telangana Regional Committee is correct?
o: It was extended for five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973.
It was extended for ten years in 1968 and abolished by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
It was abolished in 1968 after the 32nd Amendment.
262.x: The Committee was extended for five years in 1968 and was subsequently wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973 removed Andhra Pradesh from Article 371(1).
262.tq: Link the extension, constitutional amendment and final consequence in sequence.

262.s: Under the power-sharing clause concerning the Deputy Chief Minister, if the Chief Minister belonged to Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister was to belong to:
o: The majority linguistic group in the Assembly
262.x: The agreement provided that the Deputy Chief Minister should come from Telangana when the Chief Minister came from Andhra, and vice versa.
262.tq: Apply the reciprocal regional-balance rule to the stated hypothetical.

262.s: Besides the Deputy Chief Minister’s post, the agreement provided that Telangana should receive one of which of the following portfolios?
o: Defence, External Affairs, Finance, or Railways
Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, Commerce, or Industry
Education, Culture, Tourism, or Irrigation only
262.x: Telangana was to receive one of the portfolios of Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, Commerce or Industry.
262.tq: Choose the option containing the exact set of regional power-sharing portfolios.

262.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the fate of the Deputy Chief Minister’s post under Sanjiva Reddy?
o: Sanjiva Reddy appointed a Telangana Deputy Chief Minister immediately.
Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and described the post as a “sixth finger”.
Sanjiva Reddy retained the post but transferred its powers to the Regional Committee.
The post was abolished by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
262.x: Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and dismissed the post as a “sixth finger”. This breach contributed to the grievances that led to the 1969 Jai Telangana movement.
262.tq: Use the exact action and quoted description to distinguish the event from later constitutional changes.

262.s: The Pataskar Award was associated with which of the following matters?
o: Distribution of Hyderabad State’s linguistic population
Appointment of the Telangana Regional Committee
Allocation of Telangana seats in the Legislative Assembly
Settlement of the Andhra–Madras boundary dispute
262.x: The Pataskar Award was concerned with settling the Andhra–Madras border. Most of Tiruttani taluk of Chittoor went to Tamil Nadu.
262.tq: Distinguish a boundary award from committees dealing with state formation and regional safeguards.

262.s: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha developed out of which organisation founded in 1921?
262.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the Andhra Jana Sangham, which was founded in 1921.
262.tq: Use the organisation-to-successor relationship rather than confusing it with later political bodies.

262.s: Which of the following best describes the historical role and later development of the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It was a body created after 1956 to administer the Telangana Regional Committee.
It functioned only as a religious organisation and opposed all political activity.
It was formed exclusively to settle the Andhra–Madras boundary and remained administratively united.
It served Telugu cultural and political awakening in the Nizam’s State and later split into moderate and Communist groups.
262.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha became a vehicle for Telugu cultural and political awakening in the Nizam’s State and later divided along moderate and Communist lines.
262.tq: Identify the option combining the organisation’s purpose with its later internal division.

262.s: The term ‘Visalandhra’, meaning ‘Greater Andhra’, referred to the proposal for:
o: A separate Telangana state under Hyderabad
One state for all Telugu-speaking people of the Madras and Hyderabad regions
A federation of all southern Indian states
The merger of Andhra with the Madras Presidency without Hyderabad
262.x: Visalandhra, or Greater Andhra, envisaged one state for Telugu-speaking people living in the Madras region and Nizam’s Hyderabad.
262.tq: Identify the exact meaning of the movement rather than confusing it with later Telangana movements.

262.s: Who was the first to use the word ‘Visalandhra’?
262.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first to use the word ‘Visalandhra’.
262.tq: Direct person-term association.

262.s: Puchalapalli Sundarayya’s book published in 1946 was titled:
262.x: Sundarayya’s 1946 book was titled Visalandhralo Prajarajyam, meaning ‘People’s Rule in Greater Andhra’.
262.tq: Match the author with the precise title of the work.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the early roots of the Visalandhra idea:
1. Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched the idea of a united Andhra in 1912.
2. The proposed united Andhra included Telangana, the Circars and the Ceded districts.
3. Nyapati Subbarao proposed one rule for all Telugu areas at the second Andhra Mahasabha in 1914.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All three statements are correct. The early proposal emerged in 1912, covered the three specified regions, and was advanced further at the second Andhra Mahasabha in 1914.
262.tq: Use the chronology and the associated names to verify each statement.

262.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the Visalandhra idea in chronological order:
A. Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto
B. Proposal of a united Andhra by Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham
C. Proposal of one rule for all Telugu areas by Nyapati Subbarao
D. Publication of Visalandhralo Prajarajyam
262.x: The correct sequence is 1912 proposal, 1914 Andhra Mahasabha proposal, 1936 manifesto and 1946 publication of Sundarayya’s book.
262.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the intermediate developments.

262.s: The concept of Visalandhra was dated by the Andhra Pradesh authorities to which year in the Circar districts?
262.x: The Andhra Pradesh reference dated the concept of Visalandhra in the Circar districts to 1937.
262.tq: Distinguish the regional dating of the concept from the dates of the manifesto and book.

262.s: Who described the Visalandhra idea in 1954 as being about 50 years old and as old as the Andhra Movement?
262.x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao made this observation at the 1954 Mahasabha.
262.tq: Link the distinctive chronological remark with its speaker.

262.s: Which one of the following was NOT an argument advanced in favour of Visalandhra?
o: Combination of Andhra agriculture and coastline with Telangana minerals and industry
Integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari basins
Permanent protection of separate Telangana political institutions
262.x: Protection of separate Telangana political institutions was not a pro-Visalandhra argument. The other three were arguments advanced in favour of unification.
262.tq: Find the option belonging to the opposing camp rather than the pro-merger arguments.

262.s: The economic argument for Visalandhra stressed the combination of:
o: The Nizam’s revenue with Madras city’s industries
Andhra’s agriculture and coastline with Telangana’s minerals and industry
262.x: The economic case rested on combining Andhra’s agricultural and coastal resources with Telangana’s minerals and industrial potential for balanced growth.
262.tq: Keep the regional resources in their correct combination.

262.s: The river-water argument for Visalandhra was based mainly on:
o: Transfer of the Cauvery waters to Hyderabad
Exclusive control of the Pennar by coastal districts
Integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari basins from upper Telangana to the coastal deltas
Separate development of all river basins
262.x: Supporters argued that a united state would permit integrated planning of the Krishna and Godavari river basins from upper Telangana to the coastal delta regions.
262.tq: Apply the federal-integration argument to river-basin planning.

262.s: Who argued that Telangana would develop through Visalandhra and that a separate Telangana would be weak?
262.x: Swami Ramananda Tirtha argued that Telangana would develop within Visalandhra and that a separate Telangana would be weak.
262.tq: Match the development argument with its proponent.

262.s: The agrarian argument advanced by the Communists in favour of Visalandhra was that unification would help to:
o: Transfer all land revenue to Hyderabad
Push land reforms and weaken feudal structures
262.x: The Communist agrarian argument held that unification could promote land reform and weaken feudal structures.
262.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link in the agrarian argument.

262.s:
The argument that Hyderabad should serve as the capital of Visalandhra was put forward by which of the following bodies or forums?
1. Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, 1950
2. Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee, 1953
3. Visalandhra Mahasabha, 1950
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: The capital argument was advanced by the APCC in 1950 and 1953 and by the Visalandhra Mahasabha in 1950.
262.tq: Check whether the institutional references all belong to the same argument.

262.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: K.V. Ranga Reddy — Initially supported Visalandhra, later supported separate Telangana
262.x: Tanguturi Prakasam supported Visalandhra. Marri Chenna Reddy and Mahadeva Singh opposed the merger, while K.V. Ranga Reddy changed his position from support to separate Telangana.
262.tq: Use the swapped-stand trap involving leaders of the two camps.

262.s: Who preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949?
262.x: C. Rajagopalachari preferred retaining Hyderabad as a multilingual state in 1949.
262.tq: Match the position with the correct national leader and year.

262.s: The fear among less-developed Telangana groups regarding Visalandhra mainly concerned the possible loss of:
o: River water and mineral rights only
Hyderabad’s status as a multilingual city
Jobs and educational seats to better-educated Andhras
262.x: The principal fear was that Telangana would lose employment opportunities and educational seats to the better-educated people of Andhra. The Mulki domicile rules had earlier provided protection against such competition.
262.tq: Translate the social and administrative concern into its practical consequence.

262.s: The Mulki rules were relevant to the Telangana opposition because they were intended to provide protection based on:
262.x: The Mulki rules were domicile rules that protected local residents in employment and related opportunities.
262.tq: Distinguish domicile protection from language, caste or land-based protection.

262.s: What did the States Reorganisation Commission recommend in paragraph 386 regarding Telangana?
o: Immediate merger with Andhra without conditions
A separate Telangana state initially, with reconsideration after the 1961 elections and merger only with a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature
Merger only after a referendum in Madras
Permanent continuation of Hyderabad as a multilingual state
262.x: The SRC recommended that Telangana remain separate initially, that the issue be reconsidered after the 1961 elections, and that merger require a two-thirds majority in the Telangana legislature.
262.tq: Retain all conditions in a recommendation instead of selecting only its headline.

262.s: Which leader initially supported the merger but later opposed it?
262.x: Kaloji initially supported the merger and later opposed it.
262.tq: Test a change of position rather than a fixed alignment.

262.s:
Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Founding the Visalandhra Mahasabha in 1949
2. Raising the Visalandhra demand at the 1951 Bangalore Congress manifesto meeting
3. Resigning when no decision was taken
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: All three statements describe Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao’s role in the Visalandhra movement.
262.tq: Verify a leader through a sequence of connected actions.

262.s: Who changed from being an early supporter of Visalandhra to supporting a separate Telangana after becoming Telangana Congress president?
262.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy initially supported Visalandhra but later supported separate Telangana after becoming president of the Telangana Congress.
262.tq: Identify the leader associated with a reversal of political stand.

262.s: Which leader demanded a separate Telangana and, along with K.V. Ranga Reddy, opposed the Visalandhra resolutions of the first Visalandhra Mahasabha?
262.x: Marri Chenna Reddy demanded a separate Telangana and opposed the Visalandhra resolutions along with K.V. Ranga Reddy.
262.tq: Match the opposition action with the correct leader.

262.s: The statement ‘Visalandhra nirmanam... is the mother’s right of all Andhras’ is associated with:
262.x: Tanguturi Prakasam used this expression while supporting the construction of Visalandhra.
262.tq: Recognise the leader through a distinctive quotation.

262.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Communist Party’s position and electoral expectation in the early 1950s?
o: It remained neutral because it had no presence in Hyderabad State
It started the movement, won many seats in both regions in 1952 and expected a majority in a united state
It supported separate Telangana and boycotted the 1952 elections
It opposed Visalandhra and expected a majority only in Madras State
262.x: The Communist Party started the Visalandhra movement, won many seats in both regions in 1952 and expected to secure a majority in a united state.
262.tq: Combine the party’s action, electoral performance and expectation without reversing them.

262.s: Why was the Congress initially cautious about the Visalandhra proposal?
o: It opposed the use of Hyderabad as a capital for linguistic reasons
It considered Telangana economically stronger than Andhra
It feared that the proposal had originated with the Communists and that a united state might produce a Communist majority
It favoured immediate separation of all Telugu-speaking districts
262.x: The Congress was initially cold towards Visalandhra because the idea had been advanced by the Communists and a united state might give them a majority.
262.tq: Connect the party’s initial position with its political calculation.

262.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the Congress positions on the capital of a possible Visalandhra state?
1. The APCC Madras meeting in January 1950 favoured Madras as a temporary capital and Hyderabad as a permanent capital.
2. The APCC Kurnool meeting of 30 September 1953 demanded Visalandhra with Hyderabad as capital.
3. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was associated with the 1953 Kurnool demand.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: All three statements are correct. The 1950 position treated Madras as temporary and Hyderabad as permanent, while the 1953 Kurnool meeting demanded Visalandhra with Hyderabad as capital under Neelam Sanjiva Reddy’s association.
262.tq: Check both the dates and the changing capital formulation.

262.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mahila Sabha — Supported Visalandhra at Hyderabad in May 1954
Praja Socialist Party under Mahadeva Singh — Opposed Visalandhra
People’s Democratic Front — Congress electoral front in Hyderabad State in 1952
Hindu Mahasabha — Supported Visalandhra at Hyderabad in May 1954
262.x: The People’s Democratic Front was the Communists’ electoral front in Hyderabad State in 1952, not the Congress front. The other pairs are correctly matched.
262.tq: Use the party-affiliation trap to identify the incorrectly assigned electoral front.

262.s: Which of the following was a Communist daily associated with the Visalandhra movement?
262.x: Visalandhra was a Communist daily that began publication in June 1952. Kakatiya, Andhra Janata and Telugu Desam were also newspapers associated with the period.
262.tq: Separate the named daily from the broader list of newspapers.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding literature and press connected with Visalandhra:
1. The daily Visalandhra began publication in June 1952.
2. K.V. Narayana Rao wrote The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao contributed pamphlets.
4. Sri Sri presided over the 1954 Mahasabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: All four statements are correct. The press-literary contribution included the Communist daily Visalandhra, Narayana Rao’s book, Ramanuja Rao’s pamphlets and Sri Sri’s presidency of the 1954 Mahasabha.
262.tq: Test authorship, publication date and conference association together.

262.s: From which year did the Communist Party of India demand the formation of Visalandhra?
262.x: The Communist Party of India demanded Visalandhra from 1946 and subsequently popularised the demand through various forms of publicity.
262.tq: Directly identify the earliest year associated with the movement.

262.s: Which of the following was NOT used by the Communist Party to propagate the demand for Visalandhra?
262.x: The Communist Party propagated Visalandhra through songs, poems, books, pamphlets and its press. Constitutional amendments in Parliament were not mentioned as a method of its campaign.
262.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of propaganda methods.

262.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Puchalapalli Sundarayya — Communist leader associated with the Visalandhra campaign
Ravi Narayana Reddy — Founder of the Visalandhra Mahasabha
Baddam Ella Reddy — Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission
Arutla Ramachandra Reddy — Editor of the first issue of Visalandhra
262.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was one of the principal Communist leaders associated with the Visalandhra campaign. The other persons were also associated with the Communist movement, but the roles assigned to them are not supported here.
262.tq: Use the person–role association and reject swapped political roles.

262.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Communist Party and the Visalandhra movement:
1. The Hyderabad State Communist Party practically functioned as a branch of the Andhra Communist Party headquartered at Vijayawada.
2. Communists became a major political force in Telangana.
3. The Communist Party opposed integrated linguistic states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
262.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Communists propagated Visalandhra and supported the integration of Telugu-speaking areas.
262.tq: Identify the single reversed political position among otherwise related statements.

262.s: Why did the Communist Party intensify its campaign for a united state after the 1952 elections?
o: It had lost all representation in Telangana and Andhra.
The Hyderabad State Congress had formally joined the Communist Party.
It had made major gains in both Telangana and Andhra and expected a united state to give it a majority.
The States Reorganisation Commission had already recommended Visalandhra.
262.x: The Communists made substantial gains in both Telangana and Andhra in the 1952 elections and believed that a united state would provide them a majority.
262.tq: Link the electoral result with the political strategy that followed.

262.s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded on 26 November of which year at Vijayawada?
262.x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded at Vijayawada on 26 November 1949.
262.tq: Distinguish the organisation’s founding year from the years of its later sessions.

262.s: Who was the founder-leader of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
262.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the founder-leader of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
262.tq: Use direct founder–organisation recall rather than confusing the later presidents or campaign leaders.

262.s: Who presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
262.x: Hayagreevachari presided over the 1950 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
262.tq: Separate the session president from the founder and the president of the later session.

262.s: Who presided over the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha?
262.x: Sri Sri was the president of the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
262.tq: Use the year to distinguish the 1954 session from the 1950 session.

262.s: Who coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and wrote Visalandhralo Prajarajyam?
262.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya coined the expression ‘Visalandhra’ and authored Visalandhralo Prajarajyam.
262.tq: Directly associate the slogan-related publication with its author and campaigner.

262.s:
Which of the following statements about Puchalapalli Sundarayya is correct?
1. He started the Visalandhra paper.
2. He later became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964.
3. He presided over the 1954 session of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: Sundarayya started the Visalandhra paper and became the first General Secretary of the CPI(M) in 1964. Statement 3 is incorrect; Sri Sri presided over the 1954 session.
262.tq: Separate a leader’s documented roles from the role of another associated person.

262.s: Which group mainly explained the benefits of Visalandhra through books, pamphlets and tours?
o: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar
Mir Mohammed Ali Khan, Makhdoom Mohiuddin and Mehdi Nawaz Jung
Harishchandra Heda, J.V. Narsing Rao and Arige Ramaswamy
Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari, Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao and Paga Pulla Reddy
262.x: Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari, Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao and Paga Pulla Reddy explained the benefits of Visalandhra through books, pamphlets and tours.
262.tq: Identify the complete group associated with a particular campaign activity.

262.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the mobilisation of Muslim support in Hyderabad?
o: Mir Mohammed Ali Khan — Deputy Mayor
Makhdoom Mohiuddin — Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission
Mehdi Nawaz Jung — General Secretary of CPI(M)
Mir Mohammed Ali Khan — President of the 1954 Visalandhra Mahasabha
262.x: Mir Mohammed Ali Khan was a Deputy Mayor and, along with Makhdoom Mohiuddin and Mehdi Nawaz Jung, helped educate Muslim opinion in Hyderabad.
262.tq: Use the precise office attached to one member of the Muslim-support group.

262.s: In which month and year did the daily Visalandhra, started by the Communists on Sundarayya’s initiative, begin publication?
262.x: The daily Visalandhra began publication in June 1952 on the initiative of Puchalapalli Sundarayya.
262.tq: Combine the publication’s month with its year to distinguish it from related political events.

262.s: Which publications were associated with the Communist campaign for the merger of Telugu-speaking areas?
262.x: The Communist Party organ Visalandhra and Sundarayya’s Visalandhra Prajarajyam campaigned for the merger of Telugu-speaking areas.
262.tq: Match the campaign with the two publications directly linked to it.

262.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Event)
a. Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha
b. States Reorganisation Commission was constituted
c. Report of the Commission

d. Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded
List-II (Date/Year)
i. 1949
 ii. 22 December 1953
 iii. 29 December 1953
 iv. 1955
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
262.x: Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953; it was constituted on 29 December 1953; its report came in 1955; and the Visalandhra Mahasabha was founded in 1949.
262.tq: Start from the sure date and complete the chronological pairs.

262.s: Who announced the appointment of the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha on 22 December 1953?
262.x: Jawaharlal Nehru announced the States Reorganisation Commission in the Lok Sabha on 22 December 1953.
262.tq: Distinguish the political authority making the announcement from the members of the Commission.

262.s: The States Reorganisation Commission was constituted on 29 December 1953 through which instrument?
262.x: The Commission was constituted on 29 December 1953 through Home Ministry Resolution 53/69/53.
262.tq: Test the exact official instrument and number rather than only the date.

262.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission?
262.x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.
262.tq: Identify the person outside the formal membership list.

262.s: Which of the following correctly states the recommendation in paragraph 386 of the States Reorganisation Commission report regarding Telangana?
o: Telangana should merge immediately without any further condition.
Telangana should permanently remain part of Hyderabad State.
Telangana should merge only after a simple majority vote before 1956.
Telangana should initially remain separate and merger could be reconsidered after 1961 with a two-thirds vote.
262.x: Paragraph 386 recommended that Telangana remain a separate state initially, with reconsideration of merger after 1961 subject to a two-thirds vote.
262.tq: Read the recommendation as a sequence of condition, time and voting requirement.
