263.tq: Match a clause number with its precise administrative provision.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Clause of the Five-Point Formula)
a. Clause 1
b. Clause 3
c. Clause 4
d. Clause 5

List-II (Provision)
i. Better educational facilities for Andhra students in the twin cities
ii. First two gazetted posts in various services localised
iii. Twin-cities police recruited from both regions
iv. Mulki Rules continued for specified periods and applied to certain posts

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
263.x: Clause 1 concerned continuation and application of the Mulki Rules; Clause 3 localised the first two gazetted posts; Clause 4 concerned educational facilities; and Clause 5 concerned police recruitment.
263.tq: Start with the distinctive clause concerning police recruitment and eliminate codes.

263.s: P.V. Narasimha Rao resigned as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on:
263.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao, who had become Chief Minister on 30 September 1971, resigned on 18 January 1973.
263.tq: Distinguish appointment, resignation and succession dates.

263.s: Who became the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh on 10 December 1973 after the end of President’s Rule?
263.x: Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister on 10 December 1973 after President’s Rule ended.
263.tq: Apply the successor trap to closely connected political figures.

263.s:
Which of the following pairs correctly represents the institutional changes associated with the Six-Point Formula?
1. Mulki Rules — abolition
2. Telangana Regional Committee — abolition
3. Direct recruitment — local preference in specified posts
4. Promotion disputes — special tribunal
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
263.x: The Six-Point Formula abolished the Mulki Rules and Telangana Regional Committee, introduced local preference in specified direct recruitment, and provided a special tribunal for promotion disputes.
263.tq: Combine institutional abolition with the replacement safeguards.

263.s: Under the Six-Point Formula, which arrangement was intended to address grievances of government employees?
o: A common police force for both successor states
A committee to select the capital at Amaravati
A committee to settle their grievances
A separate state for Coastal Andhra
263.x: The third point of the Six-Point Formula provided for a committee to settle government employees’ grievances.
263.tq: Identify the administrative remedy from the stated problem.

263.s: The Six-Point Formula provided for backward-area development through:
o: An Administrative Tribunal with zonal committees
A State Planning Commission with local sub-committees
A Central University with local sub-committees
The Telangana Regional Committee with district committees
263.x: Backward-area development was to be addressed through a State Planning Commission with local sub-committees.
263.tq: Distinguish planning institutions from tribunals and regional bodies.

263.s: Article 371E, associated with the Six-Point Formula, provides for:
o: Local cadres and six administrative zones
A State Planning Commission for backward areas
263.x: Article 371E provides for the establishment of a Central University at Hyderabad. Local cadres and zones are associated with Article 371D.
263.tq: Separate the closely related constitutional articles 371D and 371E.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 371D:
1. It is associated with local cadres and zonal arrangements.
2. It is connected with the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal.
3. It established the Central University at Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Central University at Hyderabad is associated with Article 371E, not Article 371D.
263.tq: Use the article-number distinction to reject a swapped provision.

263.s: Which committee submitted a report on the separate-Telangana demand on 30 December 2010 and presented six options?
263.x: The Committee on Telangana headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna submitted its report on 30 December 2010 and presented six options.
263.tq: Match the committee chairman with its subject and report date.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee or study)
a. Committee on Telangana
b. Expert Committee on AP capital
c. GN Rao Committee
d. BCG study

List-II (Association)
i. K.C. Sivaramakrishnan
 ii. Separate-Telangana demand
 iii. Basis of the three-capitals plan
 iv. Options for a new capital

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
263.x: The Committee on Telangana studied the separate-state demand; the Expert Committee on AP capital was associated with K.C. Sivaramakrishnan and considered capital options; the GN Rao Committee and BCG study formed the basis of the three-capitals plan.
263.tq: Use the mandate first, then identify the capital-related pair.

263.s: The Expert Committee on AP capital constituted under Section 6 was chaired by:
263.x: The Section 6 Expert Committee on a new capital was chaired by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan.
263.tq: Avoid swapping the chairmen of the Telangana and capital committees.

263.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Expert Committee on AP capital is correct?
o: It submitted its report in December 2010 and proposed six options for Telangana.
It submitted its report in August 2014 and opposed the idea of a super capital.
It was formed in 2020 and recommended the three-capitals plan.
It selected Amaravati in 2015 after land pooling of 33,000 acres.
263.x: The K.C. Sivaramakrishnan Committee submitted its report in August 2014 and opposed the concept of a super capital.
263.tq: Distinguish committee mandate, report year and later policy outcomes.

263.s: Amaravati was selected as the capital of Andhra Pradesh in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately:
263.x: Amaravati was chosen in 2015 after land pooling involving approximately 33,000 acres.
263.tq: Use the middle-value numerical trap for approximate figures.

263.s: The three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, associated with 2020, failed in court in:
263.x: The three-capitals plan introduced in 2020 failed in court in 2022.
263.tq: Separate the year of proposal from the year of judicial outcome.

263.s:
The Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 included provisions relating to which of the following?
1. IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS
2. Central and tribal universities
3. A new railway zone, steel plant, port and metros
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: The Thirteenth Schedule included institutions such as IIT, NIT, IIM and AIIMS, central and tribal universities, and infrastructure proposals including a railway zone, steel plant, port and metros.
263.tq: Treat every item in a statutory schedule as a separate checklist entry.

263.s:
Under Article 3 of the Constitution, Parliament may by law:
1. Form a new State.
2. Increase or diminish the area of a State.
3. Alter the boundaries or name of a State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States and to increase or diminish the area, alter the boundaries, or change the name of any State.
263.tq: Test the full constitutional power list by checking whether any item has been wrongly excluded.

263.s: A Bill for the formation of a new State under Article 3 can be introduced in Parliament only after obtaining the recommendation of the:
263.x: The prior recommendation of the President is necessary for introducing a Bill under Article 3.
263.tq: Use the authority-based trap by identifying who constitutionally recommends the Bill.

263.s:
With reference to the procedure under Article 3, consider the following statements:
1. The President refers the Bill to the legislature of the affected State for expressing its views.
2. The views of the State Legislature are binding on Parliament.
3. The State Legislature is required to express its views within the period specified by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: The President refers the Bill to the affected State Legislature for its views within a specified period. Those views are not binding on Parliament.
263.tq: Find the single reversed constitutional effect: consultation does not make the State Legislature’s views binding.

263.s: A law made under Article 3 for reorganisation of States is passed by Parliament by:
o: A two-thirds majority of all State Legislatures
263.x: A law under Article 3 requires only a simple majority in Parliament and is not a constitutional amendment under Article 368 by virtue of Article 4.
263.tq: Discriminate between the simple-majority procedure and the special-majority procedure for constitutional amendments.

263.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 2 — Admission or establishment of new States
Article 2 — Alteration of the name of an existing State
Article 3 — Admission of a foreign territory as a new State
Article 4 — Laws under Articles 2 and 3 deemed amendments under Article 368
263.x: Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new States. Article 3 concerns the formation or alteration of existing States, while Article 4 excludes such laws from being treated as amendments under Article 368.
263.tq: Separate the closely related Articles 2, 3 and 4 instead of relying on the common word ‘State’.

263.s: As of 2026, India consists of:
263.x: The current count is 28 States and 8 Union Territories.
263.tq: Use the current-count pair as a two-part numerical fact and reject options that alter either figure.

263.s: Which one of the following is NOT a Union Territory of India?
263.x: Telangana is a State. Ladakh, Puducherry and Lakshadweep are Union Territories.
263.tq: Find the odd administrative category among a list of Union Territories.

263.s: The Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu were merged into a single Union Territory with effect from:
263.x: The merger of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu became effective on 26 January 2020.
263.tq: Distinguish the effective date of a reorganisation from the dates of other recent territorial changes.

263.s: The Union Cabinet’s approval to rename Kerala as “Keralam” represents the beginning of the procedure under:
263.x: A change in the name of an existing State is dealt with through the procedure under Article 3.
263.tq: Apply the Article 3 name-change rule to a current territorial proposal.

263.s: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 resulted in the creation of which two Union Territories?
263.x: The 2019 Act reorganised the former State of Jammu and Kashmir into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.
263.tq: Use the paired-territory identification method for a reorganisation statute.

263.s: The reorganisation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir into the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh took effect on:
263.x: The two Union Territories came into existence on 31 October 2019.
263.tq: Separate the date of the constitutional order from the date on which the new Union Territories came into existence.

263.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Union Territories formed under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 is correct?
o: Jammu and Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly, whereas Ladakh has no legislature.
Ladakh has a Legislative Assembly but Jammu and Kashmir has none.
Both Union Territories have Legislative Assemblies.
Neither Union Territory has any High Court arrangement.
263.x: The Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir has a Legislative Assembly, while Ladakh has no legislature. Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh share a common High Court.
263.tq: Compare the two successor Union Territories on the precise institutional difference.

263.s:
Which of the following statements about the constitutional position after the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir is correct?
1. The former State Legislature, including its Legislative Council, was abolished.
2. The Legislative Assembly of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir replaced the former State Legislature.
3. Ladakh was provided with a legislature under the 2019 Act.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: The former State Legislature and its Legislative Council were abolished, and Jammu and Kashmir now has a Legislative Assembly as a Union Territory. Ladakh has no legislature.
263.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the institutional comparison between Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

263.s: The Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh during the Telangana agitation of 1969 was:
263.x: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was the Chief Minister during the 1969 Telangana agitation.
263.tq: Match the political leader with the correct phase of the movement rather than with the later Jai Andhra period.

263.s:
Consider the following events:
1. P.V. Narasimha Rao was sworn in as Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
2. P.V. Narasimha Rao was elected CLP leader.
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
263.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was elected CLP leader on 25 September 1971 and sworn in on 30 September 1971.
263.tq: Arrange closely spaced political events by identifying the earlier organisational step and the later assumption of office.

263.s: The Telangana Praja Samiti merged with the Congress after reaching an agreement with:
263.x: The Telangana Praja Samiti merged with the Congress after an agreement with Indira Gandhi. Those opposing the merger formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.
263.tq: Apply the ‘agreement with’ trap by identifying the national leader associated with the merger.

263.s: The Complete Telangana Praja Samiti was formed by those who:
o: Led the first student strike at Khammam
Supported the merger of the TPS with the Congress
Opposed the merger of the TPS with the Congress
263.x: Those who opposed the merger of the Telangana Praja Samiti with the Congress formed the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti under B. Satyanarayana Reddy.
263.tq: Infer the organisation’s political position from the consequence of the merger agreement.

263.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an alleged violation of the 1956 safeguards?
1. Mulki rules — Recruitment of non-locals in large numbers
2. Revenue surplus — Diversion away from Telangana
3. Telangana Regional Committee — Safeguards could not be enforced in court
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: All three pairs are correct: non-locals were alleged to have been recruited, Telangana’s revenue surplus was allegedly diverted, and the political safeguards were considered unenforceable in court.
263.tq: Match each safeguard with its corresponding alleged violation before selecting the code.

263.s: The safeguard that required Telangana’s revenue surplus to be spent only in Telangana was associated with the:
263.x: The Gentlemen’s Agreement of 20 February 1956 included the safeguard that Telangana’s revenue surplus should be spent only in Telangana.
263.tq: Identify the named agreement behind a specific financial safeguard.

263.s:
The Telangana Regional Committee was intended to supervise matters relating to:
1. Development
2. Recruitment
3. Education
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: The Telangana Regional Committee was intended to supervise development, recruitment and education in the Telangana region.
263.tq: Test the complete scope of a regional institution rather than one isolated function.

263.s: The extension of the Telangana Regional Committee for five years and the request to extend the Mulki rules occurred in:
263.x: In 1968, the Telangana regional sub-committee was extended for five years and the State requested the Centre to extend the Mulki rules.
263.tq: Use the year as the decisive clue in a sequence of closely connected movement developments.

263.s: The Telangana agitation began as a student strike at:
263.x: The agitation began as a student strike in Khammam in January 1969.
263.tq: Test the movement’s place of origin directly, using nearby regional locations as distractors.

263.s: Who undertook the first hunger strike during the Telangana agitation of 1969?
263.x: The first hunger strike was undertaken by the student Ravindranath at Khammam in January 1969.
263.tq: Distinguish the student hunger-strike participant from the political leaders and organisers of the movement.

263.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Telangana agitation intensified
B. First hunger strike by Ravindranath
C. Telangana Praja Samiti was formed
D. Telangana regional sub-committee was extended for five years
263.x: The regional sub-committee was extended in 1968; the first hunger strike occurred in January 1969; the TPS was formed in February 1969; and the agitation intensified by March 1969.
263.tq: Anchor the sequence with the only 1968 event and then arrange the January–March 1969 developments.

263.s: The Telangana Praja Samiti was formed in:
263.x: The Telangana Praja Samiti was formed in February 1969. It was renamed in December 1970.
263.tq: Distinguish the organisation’s formation date from its later renaming and merger-related developments.

263.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Telangana Praja Samiti?
263.x: Marri Channa Reddy was the president of the Telangana Praja Samiti. Its election symbol was the spade, while B. Satyanarayana Reddy led the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti after the merger dispute.
263.tq: Use the wrong-person and wrong-symbol traps in an organisation–leader matching question.

263.s: In the 1971 Lok Sabha election, the Telangana Praja Samiti won:
o: 14 of the 10 seats it contested in Telangana
14 of all seats in Andhra Pradesh
10 of the 14 seats it contested in Telangana
10 of all seats in Andhra Pradesh
263.x: The Telangana Praja Samiti won 10 of the 14 Lok Sabha seats it contested in Telangana in the 1971 election.
263.tq: Preserve the numerator–denominator relationship instead of reversing the number of seats contested and won.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the political context of the Telangana Praja Samiti’s 1971 electoral performance:
1. Indira Gandhi dissolved Parliament on 27 December 1970.
2. Indira Gandhi subsequently won a two-thirds majority.
3. Congress lost ground in the Telangana seats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. Parliament was dissolved on 27 December 1970, Indira Gandhi won a two-thirds majority, and Congress nevertheless lost ground in the Telangana seats.
263.tq: Handle a mixed-result question by recognising that a national electoral victory can coexist with regional losses.

263.s: The Eight-Point Formula relating to Telangana was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on:
263.x: The Eight-Point Formula was announced by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi at a special meeting in Delhi on 11 April 1969.
263.tq: Use the exact date associated with the formula and distinguish it from the later Five-Point and Six-Point arrangements.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the clauses of the Eight-Point Formula:
1. It provided for a high-level committee headed by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge.
2. It provided for a special committee on Telangana surplus funds.
3. It provided for a supervisory committee over schemes in Telangana.
4. It provided for a special committee to inspect development schemes.
5. It provided special powers for Telangana officers.
6. It sought the opinion of legal experts on constitutional job promises.
7. It provided for an advisory committee under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
8. It required the Prime Minister to review the arrangements every six months with Central Ministers and the Vice-Chairman of the Planning Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All eight statements correctly describe the clauses of the Eight-Point Formula, including the six-monthly review by the Prime Minister with Central Ministers and the Planning Commission Vice-Chairman.
263.tq: Check each clause individually before selecting the comprehensive combination.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Bhargava Committee
B. Lalit Committee
C. Wanchoo Committee

List-II (Task)
1. Legal opinion on the constitutional validity of job safeguards
2. Official accounting of surplus funds
3. Assessment of Telangana's revenue surpluses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
263.x: The Bhargava Committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses, the Lalit Committee undertook official accounting of surplus funds, and the Wanchoo Committee examined the constitutional validity of job safeguards.
263.tq: Start from the sure committee-task pair and eliminate codes with swapped assignments.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Five-Point Formula from the Eight-Point Formula in the context of the Telangana and Jai Andhra movements?
o: The Five-Point Formula was announced on 11 April 1969, whereas the Eight-Point Formula was announced on 27 November 1972.
The Five-Point Formula abolished the Mulki Rules in 1969, whereas the Eight-Point Formula introduced the zonal system.
The Five-Point Formula is associated with 27 November 1972 and the Jai Andhra phase, while the Eight-Point Formula was announced on 11 April 1969.
Both formulas were announced in 1973 after the imposition of President's Rule.
263.x: The Eight-Point Formula dates to 11 April 1969. The Five-Point Formula is associated with 27 November 1972 and the Jai Andhra phase; its statutory basis for local employment rules is separately described as extending to 1971 in some chronologies.
263.tq: Separate the two similarly named formulas by their dates and movement context.

263.s: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, decided in 1969, the Supreme Court:
o: Struck down the Telangana residence clause of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
Upheld the Mulki Rules as applicable to all public posts in Andhra Pradesh
Repealed the Mulki Rules under the Six-Point Formula
263.x: In A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck down the Telangana residence requirement in the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, invoking Article 16(3).
263.tq: Match the case name with its specific law and judicial outcome rather than with the later Mulki ruling.

263.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In October 1972, the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules.
2. The 1972 judgment permitted non-locals to be barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
3. The 1972 judgment immediately contributed to the Jai Andhra Movement.
4. The 1972 judgment concerned the Telangana residence clause of the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957, which had been struck down in 1969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the October 1972 ruling concerned the older Mulki Rules; the residence clause of the 1957 Act had been struck down in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao in 1969.
263.tq: Discriminate between the 1969 residence-law case and the 1972 Mulki Rules case.

263.s: The case Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy, decided in October 1972, is associated with which of the following?
o: The introduction of the zonal system throughout Andhra Pradesh
The validation of the Mulki Rules and the restriction of non-locals from specified public posts
The striking down of the 1957 residence law under Article 16(3)
The dissolution of the Telangana Regional Committee
263.x: In Director of Industries v. V. Venkata Reddy, the Mulki Rules were held valid and still in force, allowing non-locals to be legally barred from public posts in Hyderabad and Telangana.
263.tq: Use the case-to-outcome association and avoid confusing it with the earlier 1969 judgment.

263.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
B. The Supreme Court judgment in A.V.S. Narasimha Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh
C. The Supreme Court judgment upholding the Mulki Rules
D. Repeal of the Mulki Rules under the Six-Point Formula
263.x: The correct sequence is 1957 Act, 1969 A.V.S. Narasimha Rao judgment, October 1972 judgment upholding the Mulki Rules, and 1973 repeal under the Six-Point Formula.
263.tq: Fix the first and last events, then place the two judicial decisions by year.

263.s: The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and were replaced by the:
263.x: The Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973 under the Six-Point Formula and replaced by the zonal system. The Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974.
263.tq: Identify the institutional replacement, not merely the date of repeal.

263.s: The Telangana martyrs of 1969 are associated with the death of approximately how many students and agitators in police firings?
263.x: Severe police firings during the 1969 movement resulted in the death of over 360 students and agitators, remembered as the Telangana martyrs.
263.tq: Retain the specific casualty figure and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.

263.s: President's Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh during the movement for the period:
263.x: President's Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh from 18 January 1973 to 10 December 1973, for approximately eleven months.
263.tq: Use both the beginning and ending dates to avoid confusing the period with the movement's later conclusion.

263.s: The Telangana movement ended primarily as a result of the:
o: Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
abolition of the Mulki Rules alone
formation of a separate Telangana State in 1973
dissolution of the Telangana Regional Committee
263.x: The movement ended with the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government on 21 September 1973. Neither repression nor abolition of the Mulki Rules alone ended the movement.
263.tq: Identify the decisive political settlement and reject events that were only associated with the transition.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. The Central Government proposed the Six-Point Formula.
B. The agitation was called off.
C. The Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved.
D. The Mulki Rules were repealed under the Six-Point Formula.
263.x: The Six-Point Formula was proposed on 21 September 1973, the Mulki Rules were repealed in 1973, the agitation was called off on 1 October 1973, and the Telangana Regional Committee was dissolved on 1 January 1974. Thus, among the listed events, the intended sequence is A, D, B, C.
263.tq: Place events by their dates and distinguish the policy proposal, repeal, withdrawal of agitation and committee dissolution.

263.s: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, which inserted Articles 371D and 371E, came into force on:
263.x: The 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in 1973 and came into force on 1 July 1974.
263.tq: Use the year-and-date distinction carefully instead of treating enactment and commencement as identical.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 371D:
1. It provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education for different parts of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It permits the organisation of local cadres and the fixing of local areas for direct recruitment and admissions.
3. It places all service disputes within the exclusive jurisdiction of the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 371D provided for an Administrative Tribunal for service disputes, taking them out of the High Court's jurisdiction.
263.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking the authority assigned to service disputes.

263.s: Article 371E of the Constitution enables Parliament to establish which of the following in the State?
263.x: Article 371E empowers Parliament to establish a Central University in the State, represented by the University at Hyderabad.
263.tq: Test the precise constitutional function attached to the Article.

263.s: Under the Presidential Order of 1975, Andhra Pradesh civil-service recruitment was decentralised through the creation of:
263.x: The Presidential Order of 1975 created six zones to make civil-service recruitment more decentralised and equitable.
263.tq: Use the exact numerical value rather than a nearby administrative division.

263.s: Which of the following statements regarding local cadres is correct?
o: Local cadres abolished all forms of direct recruitment.
Local cadres applied only to educational admissions and not to public employment.
Posts could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, with direct recruitment reserved for locals of the area.
All posts were reserved exclusively for persons born in the concerned district.
263.x: Local cadres could be organised district-wise, zone-wise or multi-zone-wise, and direct recruitment was reserved for locals of the relevant area.
263.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish residence-based local recruitment from birth-based exclusivity.

263.s:
With reference to residence requirements for public employment, consider the following statements:
1. Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament to prescribe residence requirements.
2. Article 371D provides a special constitutional route for Andhra Pradesh.
3. The President alone can prescribe residence requirements for every State under Article 16(3).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 16(3) refers to Parliament, while Article 371D is the special route for Andhra Pradesh.
263.tq: Use the authority trap by distinguishing Parliament's power from the President's role.

263.s: Who among the following spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation as a prominent Congress leader?
263.x: Kakani Venkataratnam was the prominent Congress leader who spearheaded the Jai Andhra agitation. B.V. Subba Reddy was another Congress leader associated with it.
263.tq: Test the leader-role association directly, a common history-paper trap.

263.s: M. Venkaiah Naidu participated in the Jai Andhra Movement in the capacity of a:
o: Presiding officer of the Legislative Council
263.x: M. Venkaiah Naidu took part in the Jai Andhra Movement as a student leader. Student groups formed the core of the movement.
263.tq: Discriminate between a leader's role in the movement and later public offices.

263.s: The core support base of the Jai Andhra Movement consisted mainly of:
o: Non-local employees appointed to Telangana zones
263.x: Student groups formed the core of the Jai Andhra Movement.
263.tq: Identify the social base of the movement rather than its political leadership.

263.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
263.x: The Six-Point Formula belongs to 1973. The 1985 event was the issuance of GO 610 to correct violations of the Presidential Order.
263.tq: Find the mismatched year by separating the constitutional compromise from its later implementation measures.

263.s: The Jai Telangana agitation of 1969 primarily demanded:
o: Implementation of Mulki safeguards and a separate State
Merger of Telangana with the Madras State
Repatriation of all Andhra employees to Hyderabad State
Abolition of all local cadres in Andhra Pradesh
263.x: The 1969 Jai Telangana agitation was centred in Telangana and demanded implementation of Mulki safeguards along with a separate State.
263.tq: Link the movement with both its region and its principal demand.

263.s: The Jai Andhra agitation of 1972 emerged primarily in response to:
o: The issue of the Presidential Order of 1975
The signing of the Gentlemen's Agreement
The Supreme Court upholding the Mulki Rules
The formation of the Girglani Commission
263.x: The Jai Andhra agitation arose in Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema after the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules.
263.tq: Use the cause-and-effect link between a judicial decision and a regional movement.

263.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Girglani Report
B. Jai Andhra agitation
C. GO 610
D. Jai Telangana agitation
E. 32nd Constitutional Amendment
263.x: The correct sequence is Jai Telangana agitation (1969), Jai Andhra agitation (1972), 32nd Amendment (1973), GO 610 (1985), and Girglani Report (2004).
263.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the constitutional and administrative measures between them.

263.s: The Six-Point Formula and the 32nd Constitutional Amendment represented which of the following in the sequence of regional developments?
o: A movement against the Mulki Rules followed by their complete abolition
The final report of the Girglani Commission
The first demand for a separate Telangana State
A compromise following the Jai Telangana and Jai Andhra agitations
263.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 and the 32nd Amendment represented a compromise after the regional agitations concerning Mulki safeguards.
263.tq: Place a constitutional settlement in its political sequence rather than confusing it with an agitation.

263.s: GO 610 was issued primarily to:
o: Introduce the Mulki rules in Hyderabad State
Repatriate non-local employees appointed in violation of the Presidential Order and restore posts to Telangana locals
Create six local zones for the first time
263.x: GO 610 sought to repatriate non-local employees appointed contrary to the 1975 Presidential Order and restore local posts to Telangana candidates.
263.tq: Test the purpose of an executive order through the action it required.

263.s: GO 610 was issued on 30 December 1985 by the government headed by:
263.x: GO 610 was issued on 30 December 1985 by the N.T. Rama Rao-led TDP government.
263.tq: Combine the exact date with the issuing authority to avoid a swapped-leader trap.

263.s: The Girglani Commission was constituted in 2001 by the government headed by:
263.x: The one-man Girglani Commission was constituted in 2001 by the Chandrababu Naidu government and submitted its report in 2004.
263.tq: Use the government-commission association rather than confusing the commission with GO 610.

263.s: The Girglani Commission submitted its report in:
263.x: The commission was constituted in 2001 and submitted its report in 2004.
263.tq: Distinguish the constitution year from the report year.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Girglani Commission:
1. It was a one-man commission headed by J.M. Girglani.
2. It examined violations of GO 610 and the 1975 Presidential Order.
3. It found large-scale appointment of non-locals in Telangana zones, especially Zone VI or Hyderabad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. The commission headed by J.M. Girglani examined violations and highlighted large-scale non-local appointments in Telangana zones, particularly Zone VI.
263.tq: When all statements describe distinct findings of the same commission, verify each independently before choosing the complete combination.

263.s: The weak implementation of which measure led to the constitution of the Girglani Commission?
263.x: GO 610 was weakly implemented, leading to the constitution of the Girglani Commission to examine continuing violations of the Presidential Order and GO 610.
263.tq: Trace the institutional consequence of inadequate implementation.

263.s: The Mulki rules originated in:
263.x: The Mulki rules originated in Hyderabad State in 1888, during the rivalry between Mulki and non-Mulki groups in the Nizam's bureaucracy.
263.tq: Test the origin by matching the rule with its original State and year.

263.s: Under the original Mulki rules of 1888, an outsider could be appointed to a State post only with the permission of the:
263.x: The 1888 rules reserved State posts for local residents, while an outsider required the permission of the Prime Minister, or Diwan, for appointment.
263.tq: Use the authority-holder trap in an administrative-history question.

263.s: The 1919 Nizam's Farman made the Mulki rules stricter by requiring outsiders to obtain:
o: A certificate from the Girglani Commission
The personal permission of the Nizam
The approval of the Hyderabad Legislative Council
The permission of the Prime Minister of India
263.x: The 1919 Farman required outsiders to obtain the Nizam's personal permission, strengthening the protection of local employment.
263.tq: Separate the 1888 Diwan-permission rule from the stricter 1919 requirement.

263.s: In the context of the Nizam's Mulki rules, the term 'Mulki' referred to a person who had:
o: Served in the Nizam's army for fifteen years
Obtained a recommendation from a local zamindar
Completed a fixed period of continuous residence in the State
Been born only in Hyderabad city
263.x: A Mulki was defined as a person who had completed a fixed period of continuous residence in the State. Under the Nizam's rules, the period was 15 years.
263.tq: Distinguish a residence qualification from birth, service or official recommendation.

263.s: The residence requirement for being considered a Mulki under the Nizam's rules was:
263.x: The Nizam's Mulki rules required 15 years of continuous residence. The 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement separately suggested domicile rules such as 12 years' residence.
263.tq: Discriminate between the Nizam's rule and the later Gentlemen's Agreement proposal.

263.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Nizam's Mulki rules from the domicile proposal associated with the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956?
o: The Nizam's rules referred to 12 years' residence, whereas the 1956 proposal referred to 15 years' residence only.
The Nizam's rules referred to 15 years' residence, whereas the 1956 proposal referred to 12 years' residence.
Neither system used residence as a qualification.
263.x: The Nizam's rules used a 15-year continuous residence requirement, while the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested domicile rules such as 12 years' residence.
263.tq: Compare the two closely related residence requirements instead of merging them into one rule.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the zonal system under the 1975 Order in undivided Andhra Pradesh:
1. Zones I to III comprised Coastal Andhra.
2. Zone IV comprised Rayalaseema.
3. Zones V and VI comprised Telangana.
4. Hyderabad was included in Zone V.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Zones I to III were in Coastal Andhra, Zone IV was Rayalaseema, and Zones V and VI were in Telangana. Hyderabad was included in Zone VI, not Zone V.
263.tq: Find the single reversed classification in an otherwise familiar regional grouping.

263.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the zones of undivided Andhra Pradesh under the 1975 Order:

List-I (Zone)
a. Zone I
b. Zone II
c. Zone III
d. Zone IV

List-II (District group)
i. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
ii. Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
iii. Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
iv. East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
263.x: Zone I consisted of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam; Zone II of East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna; Zone III of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore; and Zone IV of Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor.
263.tq: Start from the sure coastal pair and eliminate the codes with mismatched zone groups.

263.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched under the zonal classification of undivided Andhra Pradesh?

1. Zone V — Adilabad, Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam
2. Zone VI — Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy, Nizamabad, Mahbubnagar, Medak and Nalgonda
3. Zone IV — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
4. Zone II — Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
263.x: The districts listed in statements 1 and 2 correctly belong to Zones V and VI respectively. Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore belonged to Zone III, while Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor belonged to Zone IV.
263.tq: Use the zone number to detect swapped district groups.

263.s: After the reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, which zones of the undivided State were retained by Andhra Pradesh for its 13 districts?
263.x: After 2014, Andhra Pradesh retained Zones I to IV for its 13 districts; Zones V and VI related to the Telangana region.
263.tq: Test the boundary of the retained range rather than recalling an individual district.

263.s:
With reference to the revised Andhra Pradesh Public Employment Order-2025, consider the following statements:
1. The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved six zones and two multi-zones.
2. The revised arrangement was approved in April 2026.
3. The Department of Personnel completed the final mapping in May 2026.
4. A multi-zone restricts candidates to posts available only within their own zone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: Six zones and two multi-zones were approved in April 2026, and final mapping was completed in May 2026. A multi-zone enables candidates from adjacent zones to compete for a wider set of posts, so statement 4 is false.
263.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the practical effect of a multi-zone.

263.s: The district-wise composition of the six new zones and two multi-zones for the 26 districts of Andhra Pradesh is presently:
o: Provided in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014
Not available in the stated material
Identical to the six zones of undivided Andhra Pradesh
263.x: The district list of Andhra Pradesh's six new zones and two multi-zones for its 26 districts is not provided in the stated material.
263.tq: Distinguish a stated structural fact from an unspecified detailed list.

263.s: Which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provided for Hyderabad to serve as the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
263.x: Section 5 provided for Hyderabad to be the common capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for the prescribed transitional period.
263.tq: Separate the section dealing with the common capital from the neighbouring sections on the Governor and security.

263.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

1. Section 5 — Common capital arrangement
2. Section 7 — One Governor for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
3. Section 8 — Governor's special responsibility in the common capital
4. Section 90 — Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh
263.x: Section 90 declared Polavaram a national project. Special Category Status was an assurance made by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not included in the Act.
263.tq: Use section-number association and isolate the option that substitutes an assurance for a statutory provision.

263.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 relating to the Polavaram submergence area primarily provided for:
o: Creation of seven new districts in Andhra Pradesh
Transfer of Polavaram administration to the Union Government
Transfer of seven mandals from Andhra Pradesh to Telangana
Transfer of seven mandals from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh
263.x: The Ordinance amended Section 3 to transfer seven mandals, including Khammam villages in the submergence zone, from Telangana to Andhra Pradesh.
263.tq: Track the direction of territorial transfer instead of focusing only on the number of mandals.

263.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the original name of the Polavaram project is correct?
o: It was originally known as Polavaram Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.
It was originally known as Ramapada Sagaram and was proposed by Arthur Cotton.
It was originally known as Godavari Sagaram and was proposed by K. L. Rao.
263.x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, and the proposal was associated with Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy. Arthur Cotton and K. L. Rao are incorrect attributions in this context.
263.tq: Separate the correct project name from the commonly substituted names of other engineers.

263.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It was granted through the Polavaram Amendment Ordinance, 2014.
It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not included in the Act.
It was expressly enacted as a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
It was recommended by the Srikrishna Committee in December 2010.
263.x: Special Category Status was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha, not a provision of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act. Andhra Pradesh has stated that the assurance was not fulfilled in full.
263.tq: Distinguish a political assurance from a statutory provision.

263.s: The 1969 agitation for Telangana was associated with which organisation and which date of Indira Gandhi's eight-point formula?
263.x: The 1969 agitation was associated with the Telangana Praja Samithi, and Indira Gandhi's eight-point formula is dated 11 April 1969.
263.tq: Link the movement organisation with its precise historical date.

263.s:
Arrange the following events relating to the separate Telangana movement in chronological order:
A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Centre's announcement after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast
C. Srikrishna Committee report
D. Million March
263.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001, the Centre's announcement followed in December 2009, the Srikrishna Committee report came in December 2010, and the Million March occurred in March 2011.
263.tq: Fix the sequence using the formation year first and the event months at the end.

263.s: Who founded the Telangana Rashtra Samithi, and in which year was it formed?
263.x: The Telangana Rashtra Samithi was formed in 2001 by K. Chandrasekhar Rao.
263.tq: Match the movement organisation with its founder and formation year.

263.s: The Centre's announcement following K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast for Telangana was made in:
263.x: The Centre made the relevant announcement in December 2009 after K. Chandrasekhar Rao's fast.
263.tq: Distinguish the announcement date from the later committee and resolution dates.

263.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

1. Srikrishna Committee report — December 2010
2. Million March at Tank Bund — March 2011
3. Sakala Janula Samme — September–October 2011
4. Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana — July 2013
263.x: All four pairs are correct: the Srikrishna Committee report was issued in December 2010, the Million March occurred at Tank Bund in March 2011, Sakala Janula Samme took place during September–October 2011, and the CWC resolution came in July 2013.
263.tq: Confirm each event-date pair before selecting the complete combination.

263.s: Sakala Janula Samme, associated with the separate Telangana movement, was:
o: An eight-point formula announced in April 1969
A parliamentary resolution adopted in July 2013
A one-day march at Tank Bund during March 2011
A general strike lasting approximately 42 days during September–October 2011
263.x: Sakala Janula Samme was a general strike that lasted approximately 42 days during September–October 2011. The Tank Bund march was the Million March, held in March 2011.
263.tq: Distinguish the prolonged general strike from the one-day Million March.

263.s: The Million March associated with the Telangana movement was held at Tank Bund in:
263.x: The Million March was held at Tank Bund in March 2011.
263.tq: Use the location as the anchor and distinguish its date from the neighbouring movement events.

263.s:
Which event occurred latest among the following?

A. Formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi
B. Srikrishna Committee report
C. Sakala Janula Samme
D. Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana
263.x: The Congress Working Committee resolution for Telangana was adopted in July 2013, later than the TRS formation in 2001, the Srikrishna Committee report in 2010 and Sakala Janula Samme in 2011.
263.tq: Identify the latest event by comparing the years before comparing the months.

263.s: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was passed by the Lok Sabha after which event?
o: Resolution of the Andhra Pradesh Assembly on 28 March 2026
Operationalisation of the South Coast Railway on 1 June 2026
Request of the Telangana Deputy Chief Minister on 21 August 2026
End of Hyderabad's joint-capital period in June 2024
263.x: The Andhra Pradesh Assembly adopted a resolution on 28 March 2026, following which the Lok Sabha passed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
263.tq: Link the legislative event to its immediately preceding constitutional and political step.

263.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026:
1. It amended Section 5 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
2. It fixed Amaravati as the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh.
3. Its effect was made retrospective from 2 June 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. The 2026 amendment altered Section 5, made Amaravati the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh and gave the change retrospective effect from 2 June 2024.
263.tq: Check each statement against the amendment, its subject and its effective date.

263.s: Hyderabad's period as the joint capital of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana ended in:
263.x: The ten-year joint-capital period of Hyderabad ended in June 2024.
263.tq: Distinguish the fixed duration from the date on which the period actually ended.

263.s: The requirement that Andhra Pradesh should construct a new capital after reorganisation principally led to the development of:
263.x: Section 5 required Andhra Pradesh to establish a new capital, a process that led to the development of Amaravati.
263.tq: Connect the statutory obligation with its political and administrative outcome.

263.s: The land-pooling exercise associated with Amaravati covered approximately:
263.x: The Amaravati capital project involved land pooling of approximately 33,000 to 34,000 acres.
263.tq: Use the distinctive numerical range rather than confusing it with a rounded estimate.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a criticism of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: It transferred the entire public debt to Telangana.
It denied Andhra Pradesh any share in the revenue of the undivided State.
It was passed without the consent of the State Legislative Assembly.
It was passed only after obtaining the binding consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
263.x: A major criticism was that the Act was passed without the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly. The reorganisation also involved revenue and debt-sharing arrangements rather than the complete transfer of either to one State.
263.tq: Identify the precise criticism and reject absolute statements about consent, revenue and debt.

263.s: Which of the following best represents the fiscal consequence faced by the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after reorganisation?
o: It received no revenue but inherited the entire debt.
It received the entire revenue but bore no share of the debt.
It received about 54% of the revenue and a smaller share of the debt.
It received about 46% of the revenue but bore a larger share of the debt.
263.x: The residuary State of Andhra Pradesh received about 46% of the revenue but had to bear a larger share of the debt.
263.tq: Separate the revenue share from the debt burden instead of treating them as identical ratios.

263.s: The number of districts in Andhra Pradesh changed in which of the following sequence between 2014 and 2025?
263.x: Andhra Pradesh had 13 districts in 2014, 26 in 2022 and 28 in 2025.
263.tq: Arrange successive administrative changes in their time sequence.

263.s: Which two districts were identified as new additions in the 2025 district count of Andhra Pradesh?
263.x: Polavaram and Markapuram were identified as the new districts in the 2025 count, which took the total to 28.
263.tq: Discriminate between newly identified districts and established cities or districts.

263.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana movement:
1. It was the first mass movement to place separate statehood prominently on the political agenda.
2. Its broad sequence involved students, followed by a political party and then a central formula.
3. A similar sequence was visible during the movement of 2001–2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
263.x: All three statements are correct. The movement was significant for making separate statehood a major political issue, and its student-party-central formula sequence was repeated in 2001–2014.
263.tq: Test the significance, sequence and later recurrence of a movement together.

263.s: Prof. K. Jayashankar, associated with the Telangana movement, was a former Vice-Chancellor of:
263.x: Prof. K. Jayashankar was a former Vice-Chancellor of Kakatiya University and was widely regarded as the ideologue of the Telangana movement.
263.tq: Use the person–institution association to distinguish prominent regional figures.

263.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: K. Jayashankar — Ideologue of the Telangana movement
K. Jayashankar — Founder of the South Coast Railway
K. Jayashankar — First Governor of Andhra Pradesh
K. Jayashankar — Chairman of the Krishna River Management Board
263.x: K. Jayashankar is widely called the ideologue of the Telangana movement. The other descriptions do not belong to him.
263.tq: Start with the sure person–role association and eliminate unrelated institutional posts.

263.s: The 1969 agitation and the 1972 Jai Andhra counter-movement were followed by which combination?
o: The States Reorganisation Act and Article 370
263.x: The two regional agitations were followed by the Six-Point Formula in 1973 and Article 371D, which provided the constitutional basis for local cadres and related arrangements.
263.tq: Pair the political settlement with its constitutional provision.

263.s:
Assertion (A): The Six-Point Formula brought roughly two decades of relative peace between the Andhra and Telangana regions.
Reason (R): It replaced earlier political assurances with a constitutional zonal system.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
263.x: Both statements are true, and the constitutional zonal system created by the Six-Point Formula explains the period of relative regional peace.
263.tq: Test whether the institutional change in the Reason explains the political consequence in the Assertion.

263.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate criticism of the constitutional zonal system associated with Article 371D?
o: It completely ended all disputes over local appointments.
It applied exclusively to railway recruitment.
Disputes over non-local appointments continued despite the system.
It abolished the principle of regional equity in public employment.
263.x: Although the system replaced political assurances with constitutional zoning, disputes over non-local appointments continued, including issues associated with GO 610 and the Girglani Commission.
263.tq: Reject absolute claims and identify the continuing limitation of an institutional arrangement.

263.s: According to the AP Public Employment Order-2025 framework referred to for 2026, Andhra Pradesh's local-cadre system is being reorganised into:
263.x: The new framework provides for six zones and two multi-zones, with final mapping undertaken in 2026.
263.tq: Distinguish the exact composition of the zonal framework from nearby numerical alternatives.

263.s: The long-running Mulki question is described as extending from:
263.x: The Mulki question is traced from 1888 to 2014 and is linked with the 1969 and 1972 agitations, Article 371D, GO 610 and bifurcation.
263.tq: Use the distinctive beginning and ending years to identify the historical span.

263.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal tension in local-cadre rules?
o: They apply only to private-sector employment.
They make merit irrelevant in public employment.
They replace regional equity entirely with unrestricted mobility.
They balance merit and mobility against regional equity.
263.x: Local-cadre rules involve a trade-off between merit and mobility on the one hand and regional equity on the other.
263.tq: Apply the policy principle to the competing objectives rather than choosing an absolute statement.

263.s: Which of the following issues was specifically raised by Telangana's Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka in August 2026?
o: A demand to restore Hyderabad as Andhra Pradesh's capital
A request to transfer Amaravati to Telangana
A request to close pending reorganisation disputes and protect Telangana's Krishna water rights
A proposal to merge the two State Legislative Assemblies
263.x: Bhatti Vikramarka sought time-bound closure of pending Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act disputes and protection of Telangana's rights relating to Krishna waters.
263.tq: Match the public official with the specific contemporary demand, avoiding broader but unrelated reorganisation issues.

263.s: Which of the following correctly states the present profile of Andhra Pradesh given in the 2026 reference?
o: Capital Amaravati, area 1,25,000 sq km and coastline 650 km
Capital Visakhapatnam, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
Capital Hyderabad, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
Capital Amaravati, area 1,60,205 sq km and coastline 974 km
263.x: The stated 2026 profile gives Amaravati as the capital, an area of 1,60,205 square kilometres and a coastline of 974 kilometres.
263.tq: Check the capital, area and coastline as a combined profile and reject one-variable substitutions.

263.s:
According to the stated 2026 profile of Andhra Pradesh, which combination is correct?
1. Population: 4.96 crore according to the 2011 figure
2. Governor: S. Abdul Nazeer
3. Chief Minister: N. Chandrababu Naidu
4. Coastline: the second longest in India
263.x: All four statements are correct according to the stated profile: the 2011 population is 4.96 crore, the Governor is S. Abdul Nazeer, the Chief Minister is N. Chandrababu Naidu and the coastline is described as the second longest.
263.tq: Use a multi-fact profile question and verify each independent datum before selecting the combination.

264.s: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, is best described as which of the following?
o: A paramilitary unit under the Ministry of Home Affairs
A dog squad attached to the Forest Department
An elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police
A Central disaster-response force trained for flood rescue
264.x: Greyhounds is an elite anti-Naxal special police force unit of the Andhra Pradesh Police, raised in 1989. It is not a dog squad or disaster-response unit.
264.tq: Use the exact institutional description and reject look-alike options.

264.s: The People's War Group (PWG) was banned in Andhra Pradesh in:
264.x: The PWG was banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992.
264.tq: Fix the year by distinguishing the ban from the formation and policing milestones.

264.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Greyhounds operations under DGP H.J. Dora:
1. H.J. Dora served as DGP during 1996–2002.
2. Greyhounds neutralised several top Naxalite leaders during this period.
3. More than 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: All three statements are correct. H.J. Dora was DGP from 1996 to 2002, Greyhounds neutralised several top leaders, and over 1,200 cadres surrendered during 1998–2001.
264.tq: Check the linked office, operational outcome and surrender figures together.

264.s: Government–Maoist peace talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the tenure of which government?
264.x: Government–Maoist talks were held in Hyderabad in October 2004 during the YSR government.
264.tq: Match the event, place, month and government rather than relying on the year alone.

264.s: After bifurcation, the Greyhounds Training Centre was built at:
o: Warangal near the North Telangana stronghold
264.x: The post-bifurcation Greyhounds Training Centre was built at Anandapuram, near Visakhapatnam.
264.tq: Test the precise location and distinguish it from other Naxalite-affected areas.

264.s: The Greyhounds base at Anandapuram is associated with securing the Left-Wing Extremism corridor in which districts?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam
264.x: The Anandapuram Greyhounds base is credited with securing the LWE corridor in the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts along the Odisha–Chhattisgarh borders.
264.tq: Use the paired-district clue and avoid substituting neighbouring Andhra districts.

264.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the major components of the national toolkit for addressing Naxalism?
o: Exclusive reliance on military rule without dialogue
Development of roads and mobile towers
264.x: The national toolkit includes intelligence-led operations, stronger state police, rehabilitation, dialogue, and development of roads and mobile towers. Exclusive reliance on military rule is not included.
264.tq: Find the option that reverses the combined security, rehabilitation, dialogue and development approach.

264.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally placed in the period:
264.x: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle is generally dated to 1968–70, although 1968–69 is also used in some references.
264.tq: Distinguish the standard period from nearby movement and Emergency dates.

264.s: The Srikakulam Girijan struggle was primarily a tribal-peasant uprising against:
o: Municipal authorities, contractors and port officials
Industrial workers, traders and railway officials
Colonial soldiers, zamindars and missionaries only
264.x: The uprising in the Srikakulam Agency was directed against landlords, moneylenders and forest officials.
264.tq: Identify the correct combination of immediate rural and forest-area adversaries.

264.s: Which of the following tribal communities were associated with the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
264.x: The principal tribal communities associated with the struggle were the Savaras, also called Soras, and the Jatapus.
264.tq: Discriminate between the named Srikakulam tribes and other tribal groups of India.

264.s: Who among the following was NOT one of the principal leaders associated with the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
264.x: Vempatapu Satyam, Adibhatla Kailasam and Subbarao Panigrahi were associated with the Srikakulam struggle. Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the People’s War Group in 1980.
264.tq: Separate leaders of the Srikakulam struggle from a later Andhra Naxalite organisation founder.

264.s:
Consider the following statements about the political course of the Srikakulam struggle:
1. It began under the CPI(M).
2. It shifted to the CPI(ML) in 1969.
3. Kanu Sanyal and Tarimela Nagi Reddy are named as having spread the struggle.
4. It was led from the beginning by the CPI(ML) formed in 1969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The struggle began under the CPI(M) and shifted to the CPI(ML) in 1969; therefore, it was not led by the CPI(ML) from the beginning.
264.tq: Track the organisational transition and reject the overbroad ‘from the beginning’ claim.

264.s: Which one of the following best describes the immediate historical significance of the Srikakulam Girijan struggle?
o: It led directly to the formation of the Greyhounds in 1989.
It was suppressed by the State but seeded the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra.
It ended all tribal land conflicts in Andhra Pradesh through a constitutional settlement.
It established the CPI(ML) as the sole recognised political party in Andhra Pradesh.
264.x: The struggle was suppressed by the State, but it helped seed the Naxalite movement and revolutionary literature in Andhra.
264.tq: Choose the option that captures both suppression and longer-term political and cultural impact.

264.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organisation)
 a. CPI(ML)
 b. AP extremist CPI(ML) wing
 c. People’s War Group
 d. CPI (Maoist)

List-II (Founder or origin)
 i. Merger of PWG and MCC
 ii. Charu Majumdar with Kanu Sanyal
 iii. Kondapalli Seetharamaiah
 iv. Tarimela Nagi Reddy, Chandra Pulla Reddy, Kolla Venkaiah and Nagabhushana Patnaik

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
264.x: CPI(ML) is associated with Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal; the AP extremist wing with the four Andhra leaders; PWG with Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; and CPI (Maoist) with the PWG–MCC merger.
264.tq: Start with the sure founder–organisation pairs and then complete the code.

264.s: The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing associated with the 1967 split was based in:
264.x: The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing associated with the 1967 split had Andhra Pradesh as its base.
264.tq: Distinguish the Andhra-based wing from the West Bengal-based CPI(ML).

264.s: The People’s War Group was founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah in:
264.x: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah founded the People’s War Group in 1980.
264.tq: Separate the PWG formation year from the CPI(ML), split and merger years.

264.s: The CPI (Maoist) emerged through the merger of:
264.x: The CPI (Maoist) emerged in 2004 through the merger of the People’s War Group and the Maoist Communist Centre.
264.tq: Test the exact organisational merger rather than the broader ideological relationship.

264.s:
Arrange the following organisations or developments in chronological order:
A. Formation of CPI (Maoist)
B. Formation of CPI(ML)
C. Formation of People’s War Group
D. Formation of the AP extremist CPI(ML) wing
264.x: The AP extremist CPI(ML) wing dates to 1967, CPI(ML) to 1969, PWG to 1980, and CPI (Maoist) to 2004.
264.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the 1969 and 1980 developments.

264.s: Naxalbari is located in the Siliguri sub-division of which district and State?
264.x: Naxalbari is in the Siliguri sub-division of Darjeeling district in West Bengal.
264.tq: Use the precise sub-division–district–State geographical chain.

264.s: The Naxalbari peasant uprising of March–May 1967 was led by:
o: Kondapalli Seetharamaiah and Tarimela Nagi Reddy
264.x: The Naxalbari uprising of March–May 1967 was led by Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal.
264.tq: Match the movement with its principal leaders, avoiding leaders from Andhra phases.

264.s: Which slogan was associated with the Naxalbari uprising?
264.x: “Land to the tiller” was the slogan associated with the Naxalbari peasant uprising.
264.tq: Recall the movement-specific slogan rather than a general nationalist slogan.

264.s: The expression “Ballot to Bullet” indicated the rejection of:
o: The Chinese model of guerrilla warfare
264.x: The “Ballot to Bullet” line rejected the CPI(M)’s parliamentary path and favoured armed revolutionary struggle.
264.tq: Distinguish the rejected parliamentary route from the alternative guerrilla strategy.

264.s:
Consider the following statements about the CPI(ML):
1. It was formed in 1969.
2. It viewed the Indian State as semi-feudal.
3. It followed the Chinese-model concept of protracted guerrilla war.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
264.x: All three statements are correct. The CPI(ML) was formed in 1969, described India as semi-feudal and followed the Chinese-model strategy of protracted guerrilla war.
264.tq: Verify the formation year, ideological assessment and strategic doctrine as a single cluster.

264.s: Which of the following was NOT identified as a cause of the Naxalite movement?
o: Failure of land reforms, including tenancy reforms
Universal success of zamindari abolition and land ceilings
264.x: Land concentration, failed reforms such as zamindari abolition, ceilings and tenancy reforms, and tribal exploitation were identified as causes. Universal success of these reforms was not a cause.
264.tq: Reject the option that reverses the stated land-reform failure.

264.s: The Revolutionary Writers’ Association, popularly known as Virasam, was founded on:
264.x: Virasam was founded on 4 July 1970 in Hyderabad.
264.tq: Distinguish the founding date from the February 1970 pamphlet episode and later cultural organisations.

264.s: Which pair correctly identifies the vice-presidents of Virasam at its founding?
o: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
264.x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam.
264.tq: Discriminate the office-holders from the president and associated cultural-body founders.

264.s: The seed for Virasam was a pamphlet challenging writers distributed by Andhra University students at:
o: The launch of Jana Natya Mandali in 1971
Sri Sri’s 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag on 1–2 February 1970
The first meeting at Khammam in 1970
The formation meeting at Hyderabad on 4 July 1970
264.x: The pamphlet was distributed by Andhra University students at Sri Sri’s 60th-birthday celebrations in Vizag on 1–2 February 1970.
264.tq: Place the preparatory pamphlet episode before the formal founding and later organisational developments.

264.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First revolutionary poetry collection — Jana Natya Mandali, 1971
Art Lovers — Sri Sri and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
Jana Natya Mandali — founded in 1967 by Charu Majumdar
264.x: The first Virasam meeting was held at Khammam in 1970. Jhamjha was the first revolutionary poetry collection, while Art Lovers was associated with B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar.
264.tq: Find the one correctly matched event and reject swapped cultural organisations and names.

264.s: The first revolutionary poetry collection associated with this literary movement was:
264.x: Jhamjha, published in 1970, is identified as the first revolutionary poetry collection.
264.tq: Distinguish the title of the poetry collection from names of organisations and slogans.

264.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation was tightened in 1970 primarily to:
o: Transfer tribal land to industrial corporations
Abolish all cooperative procurement of forest produce
Create a separate State for tribal areas
Prevent land from passing from tribals to non-tribals
264.x: Regulation 1 of 1970 was intended to stop land in Scheduled Areas from passing from tribals to non-tribals.
264.tq: Identify the protective purpose of the regulation rather than a broader administrative objective.

264.s: Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs) were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from:
264.x: ITDAs were set up under the Tribal Sub-Plan from the Fifth Plan, beginning in 1974–75.
264.tq: Link the institutional arrangement with the correct Five-Year Plan and starting year.

264.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation headquartered at Visakhapatnam primarily:
o: Administers peace talks between the government and Maoists
Investigates alleged encounter killings during the Emergency
Conducts anti-Naxal operations and trains Greyhounds personnel
Procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials to reduce tribal dependence on moneylenders
264.x: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, helping free tribals from moneylenders.
264.tq: Match the institution with its economic function and reject security or inquiry functions.

264.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the impact of the movement on political priorities?
o: It removed land issues from tribal politics and focused exclusively on urban labour.
It placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics; Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.
It opposed all land redistribution and cooperative institutions.
It treated land alienation as solely a cultural issue without an economic dimension.
264.x: The movement placed land to the tiller and tribal land alienation at the centre of politics, and Dalits within it later concentrated on land struggles.
264.tq: Select the comprehensive statement that preserves both the general and Dalit-related land dimensions.

264.s: During the Emergency period, many Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh were killed in alleged encounters during:
264.x: Many Naxalite cadres were killed in alleged encounters in Andhra Pradesh during the Emergency, 1975–77.
264.tq: Separate the Emergency period from the Srikakulam struggle and PWG formation dates.

264.s: The Bhargava Commission was set up in 1977 to inquire into:
o: The reorganisation of Andhra Pradesh districts
Alleged encounter killings of Naxalite cadres in Andhra Pradesh
The procurement activities of the Girijan Cooperative Corporation
264.x: The Bhargava Commission, headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava, was set up in 1977 to inquire into alleged encounter killings during the Emergency.
264.tq: Match the commission with its subject of inquiry and its historical context.

264.s: Who headed the Bhargava Commission?
264.x: The Bhargava Commission was headed by Justice Vashist Bhargava.
264.tq: Use the commission-name and chairperson pairing rather than importing unrelated judges.

264.s: Which one of the following statements best expresses the wider significance of the Srikakulam movement for Andhra Pradesh?
o: It made Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and reshaped Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
It ended all Maoist activity in Andhra Pradesh after 1970.
It led only to the creation of a police training institution and had no social impact.
It remained confined to a short electoral campaign with no literary influence.
264.x: Srikakulam helped make Andhra Pradesh a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.
264.tq: Choose the option that combines the political and literary consequences without using an absolute claim.

265.s: The anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh began in 1991 at which place?
265.x: The movement began in 1991 at Dubagunta village in Nellore district.
265.tq: Use the location-specific direct-recall approach.

265.s: The anti-arrack agitation of 1991 emerged primarily from discussions held in which programme?
o: Workers' education classes under the Kisan Sabha
265.x: Women discussed the effects of men's arrack drinking during Aksharajyothi adult-literacy classes, which helped initiate the agitation.
265.tq: Identify the immediate institutional origin of a movement.

265.s: Who was the prominent woman leader of the Dubagunta anti-arrack movement?
265.x: Vardhineni Rosamma of Dubagunta was a prominent leader of the anti-arrack movement.
265.tq: Test the leader associated with the specific locality and movement.

265.s: Which of the following best describes the immediate demand of the anti-arrack movement?
o: Stopping the sale and auction of arrack
Abolition of land revenue and tenancy
265.x: The movement demanded an end to the sale and auction of arrack.
265.tq: Match the movement with its central demand rather than its method of protest.

265.s: Women protesters in the anti-arrack movement used which of the following methods to close arrack shops?
265.x: Women used broomsticks and chilli powder to close arrack shops, after which the protest spread across Andhra Pradesh.
265.tq: Discriminate between a movement’s distinctive method and its general objective.

265.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to prohibition in Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. Prohibition was lifted.
B. Arrack was prohibited in Andhra Pradesh.
C. Total prohibition was imposed across the State.
265.x: Arrack was prohibited on 1 October 1993, total prohibition followed in 1995, and prohibition was lifted in 1997.
265.tq: Use the first-middle-last sequence to order closely related years.

265.s:
Consider the following statements about prohibition in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Arrack was prohibited in the State on 1 October 1993.
2. Total prohibition was imposed across the State in 1995.
3. Prohibition was lifted in 1997.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
265.x: All three statements are correct: arrack prohibition began on 1 October 1993, total prohibition followed in 1995, and it was lifted in 1997.
265.tq: Verify each date independently before selecting the combined option.

265.s:
With reference to the two National Backward Classes Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. The First Backward Class Commission was chaired by Kaka Kalelkar.
2. The Second Backward Class Commission was chaired by B.P. Mandal.
3. The First Commission was set up in 1979.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
265.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First Commission and B.P. Mandal chaired the Second. The First Commission was set up in 1953, whereas the Second was set up in 1979.
265.tq: Separate the correct chairmen from the deliberately shifted year.

265.s: The First Backward Class Commission submitted its report in which year?
265.x: The First Backward Class Commission was set up in 1953 and submitted its report in 1955.
265.tq: Distinguish the year of constitution from the year of reporting.

265.s: The First Backward Class Commission listed how many backward castes?
265.x: The First Backward Class Commission listed 2,399 backward castes.
265.tq: Compare similar numerical options digit by digit.

265.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kaka Kalelkar Commission — OBCs constituted 52 percent of the population
Kaka Kalelkar Commission — set up in 1979
265.x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 percent reservation for OBCs. It was set up in 1979 and submitted its report in 1980, while the Kalelkar Commission was set up in 1953 and reported in 1955.
265.tq: Eliminate by checking the commission–year and commission–recommendation pairs.

265.s: The Mandal Commission estimated the Other Backward Classes to constitute approximately what proportion of India’s population?
265.x: The Mandal Commission estimated that OBCs constituted about 52 percent of the population.
265.tq: Keep the population estimate separate from the reservation percentage.

265.s: The 27 percent reservation recommended by the Mandal Commission was implemented in which year?
265.x: The 27 percent reservation recommendation of the Mandal Commission was implemented in 1990.
265.tq: Distinguish the year of recommendation from the year of implementation.

265.s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2018 granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes under which Article?
265.x: The 102nd Amendment of 2018 gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes under Article 338B.
265.tq: Use the exact Article-number association rather than nearby constitutional provisions.

265.s: Bhu Poratam in Andhra Pradesh was launched jointly by which parties?
265.x: Bhu Poratam was jointly launched by the CPI and CPI(M) in Andhra Pradesh.
265.tq: Test the exact composition of the alliance.

265.s: Bhu Poratam, the land struggle in Andhra Pradesh, was launched in which year?
265.x: The CPI and CPI(M) launched Bhu Poratam in Andhra Pradesh in 2007.
265.tq: Use the movement–year pair directly and reject nearby later years.

265.s: The principal objective of Bhu Poratam was to occupy and distribute which land to the landless?
265.x: Bhu Poratam sought the occupation and distribution of government and surplus land to landless people.
