265.tq: Identify the precise scope of land targeted by the campaign.

265.s: Bhu Poratam continued which earlier Communist tradition in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Industrial strikes and railway campaigns of 1942–45
265.x: Bhu Poratam continued the Communist tradition of tenancy and land campaigns carried out during 1956–69.
265.tq: Link a later movement with its stated historical continuity.

265.s: The Karamchedu massacre of Dalits took place in which district?
265.x: The Karamchedu massacre occurred in Prakasam district on 17 July 1985.
265.tq: Apply the event–district location pair.

265.s: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in which district?
265.x: The Chunduru massacre occurred on 6 August 1991 in Guntur district.
265.tq: Combine the date with the correct district to avoid event-location reversal.

265.s: Which of the following developments followed the Karamchedu incident?
o: Dalits formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas after breaking away from Congress and Communist parties.
Total prohibition was imposed across Andhra Pradesh.
The Mandal Commission was immediately constituted.
The MRPS was founded at Eedumudi.
265.x: After Karamchedu, Dalits broke away from the Congress and Communist parties and formed independent Dalit Mahasabhas.
265.tq: Identify the political consequence directly linked to the event.

265.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with modern Dalit assertion in Andhra Pradesh?
265.x: Kaka Kalelkar chaired the First National Backward Class Commission and is not listed among the leaders of modern Dalit assertion in Andhra Pradesh. Katti Padmarao, Manda Krishna Madiga and Endluri Sudhakar are associated with that assertion.
265.tq: Find the outsider in a group of movement leaders.

265.s: Who founded the Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha?
o: Katti Padmarao, with Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder
265.x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985 after Karamchedu, with Katti Padmarao identified as its founder and Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.
265.tq: Handle a multiple-founder distinction without reducing it to a single-name association.

265.s: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in which year?
265.x: The Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha was founded in 1985, following the Karamchedu incident.
265.tq: Match the organisation with its founding year.

265.s: Which pair correctly represents an early precursor and its associated leader or event?
o: Adi-Andhra movement — Bhagya Reddy Varma; Machilipatnam conference — 1919
Adi-Andhra movement — Manda Krishna Madiga; Vizianagaram — 1919
265.x: The Adi-Andhra movement was associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, whose Machilipatnam conference took place in 1919.
265.tq: Start from the sure leader–movement pair and verify the place and year.

265.s: The 1936 Adi-Andhra Mahasabha associated with Kusuma Dharmanna was held at which place?
265.x: Kusuma Dharmanna was associated with the 1936 Adi-Andhra Mahasabha held at Vizianagaram.
265.tq: Distinguish the two Adi-Andhra milestones by place and year.

265.s: The Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS) was founded by whom?
265.x: Manda Krishna Madiga founded the MRPS in 1994.
265.tq: Use the organisation–founder association.

265.s: The MRPS was founded in 1994 at which place?
265.x: The MRPS was founded in 1994 at Eedumudi in Prakasam district.
265.tq: Combine organisation, year and founding location.

265.s: What was the principal demand of the Madiga Dandora movement?
o: Categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups
265.x: Madiga Dandora demanded categorisation of Scheduled Caste reservations into A–B–C–D groups, or reservation within reservation.
265.tq: Distinguish reservation sub-categorisation from general reservation demands.

265.s: The Anantharaman Commission of Andhra Pradesh is correctly described as the commission that:
o: Checked whether minorities were included in the BC list in 1982
Was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories
Granted constitutional status to the NCBC
265.x: The Anantharaman Commission, functioning during 1968–70, was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories.
265.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive function and period.

265.s: The Anantharaman Commission functioned during which period?
265.x: The Anantharaman Commission functioned during 1968–70.
265.tq: Compare the State commission period with the national commission years.

265.s: The Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge on which date?
265.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982.
265.tq: Use the exact day–month–year detail to separate commissions and movements.

265.s: Which function was associated with the Muralidhar Rao Commission?
o: It introduced the A–B–C–D categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
It examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
It imposed prohibition throughout Andhra Pradesh.
It conducted the first national survey of OBC population.
265.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission examined whether minorities were included in the Backward Class list.
265.tq: Match the commission with its precise terms of reference.

265.s: The Muralidhar Rao Commission combined BC, ST and religious-group populations as what percentage?
265.x: The commission combined the BC, ST and religious-group populations as 29.08 percent, contributing to a substantial rise in the State reservation quota.
265.tq: Distinguish a State population calculation from national reservation figures.

265.s: How many castes were recognised as Backward Classes in Andhra, with a separate list maintained for Telangana?
265.x: Eighty-six castes were recognised as Backward Classes in Andhra, while Telangana had a separate list.
265.tq: Check the exact count and the territorial qualification together.

265.s: Who founded the Indian Peasants’ Institute at Nidubrolu in 1933?
265.x: N.G. Ranga founded the Indian Peasants’ Institute at Nidubrolu in 1933.
265.tq: Use the founder–institution–place association.

265.s: N.G. Ranga was one of the founders of the All India Kisan Sabha in which year?
265.x: N.G. Ranga was one of the founders of the All India Kisan Sabha in 1936.
265.tq: Distinguish the year of the Indian Peasants’ Institute from that of the AIKS.

265.s: The All India Kisan Sabha was one of the mass organisations through which which party worked?
265.x: The All India Kisan Sabha was one of the mass organisations through which the CPI worked.
265.tq: Identify the party–mass organisation relationship.

265.s: The power tariff agitation of 2000 was directed against which issue?
o: Auction of arrack shops under prohibition policy
Hikes in electricity tariffs under power-sector reforms
265.x: Left parties and farmers protested electricity tariff hikes introduced under power-sector reforms during the 2000 agitation.
265.tq: Connect the agitation with the policy issue that triggered it.

265.s: The Bashir Bagh firing associated with the power tariff agitation took place on:
265.x: Police opened fire at Bashir Bagh in Hyderabad on 28 August 2000 during the power tariff agitation.
265.tq: Combine the incident, date and location before choosing.

265.s: Which one of the following best expresses the broader significance of the social movements discussed in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They replaced all electoral politics with peasant organisations.
They were confined exclusively to urban industrial workers.
They shifted politics from a national-movement elite orientation towards caste, gender and class assertion.
They ended all political contestation based on caste and class.
265.x: These movements broadened the political arena from the national-movement elite towards caste, gender and class assertion through organisations such as Mahasabhas, MRPS and women’s anti-arrack groups.
265.tq: Select the option that captures the common political significance without using an absolute claim.

265.s: Which pair of movements influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Bhu Poratam and Power Tariff Agitation
265.x: Phule’s Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873, and Periyar’s Self-Respect Movement influenced the Adi-Andhra leaders.
265.tq: Match the ideological influences with the social movement they inspired.

265.s: Which statement correctly reflects a debate following the Mandal Commission period?
o: Sub-categorisation was rejected by every Dalit organisation.
All OBC and Dalit organisations merged into one movement.
The debate centred exclusively on prohibition in Andhra Pradesh.
OBC and Dalit movements split over the issue of sub-categorisation.
265.x: After Mandal, divisions emerged between OBC and Dalit movements over sub-categorisation.
265.tq: Identify the stated political consequence without extending it into an absolute claim.

265.s: Which statement about prohibition in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Prohibition was first imposed in 1991 and never lifted.
The anti-arrack movement demanded continuation of arrack sales.
The 1995 prohibition continued without interruption thereafter.
The 1995 prohibition was later largely abandoned.
265.x: Although total prohibition was imposed in 1995, it was later largely abandoned; prohibition was lifted in 1997.
265.tq: Watch for the reversal between the introduction and later fate of a policy.

266.s: Who led the Anti-arrack movement that began at Dubagunta?
266.x: The movement was led entirely by rural women, with Vardhineni Rosamma identified as its leader.
266.tq: Test the leader–movement association without confusing it with founders of women’s organisations.

266.s: The Anti-arrack movement in Andhra Pradesh grew out of which programme?
266.x: The movement grew out of Aksharajyothi adult-literacy, or Total Literacy, classes.
266.tq: Identify the institutional origin of a movement rather than its later outcome.

266.s:
Which of the following issues were discussed by women in the literacy classes before the Anti-arrack movement expanded?
1. Arrack consumption
2. Debt
3. Domestic violence
4. Men missing work
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: The literacy lessons enabled women to discuss arrack, debt, domestic violence and the problem of men missing work.
266.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after checking every listed social issue.

266.s:
Which methods were notably used by women during the Anti-arrack movement?
1. Closing arrack shops
2. Stopping arrack auctions
3. Using broomsticks and chilli powder
4. Conducting legislative elections
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: Women closed arrack shops and stopped arrack auctions, using broomsticks and chilli powder. Legislative elections were not a stated method of the movement.
266.tq: Find the one unrelated activity among concrete movement methods.

266.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the geographical spread of the Anti-arrack movement?
o: It remained confined to Dubagunta village.
It spread from Machilipatnam to Madras Presidency.
It began in Hyderabad and spread only to Telangana.
It spread from Nellore to the whole State.
266.x: The movement spread from Nellore district to the whole of Andhra Pradesh.
266.tq: Test the movement’s origin-to-spread pattern using nearby geographical distractors.

266.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the outcome of the Anti-arrack movement:
1. Arrack was banned from 1 October 1993.
2. Total prohibition was introduced in 1995.
3. The prohibition was later abandoned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: Arrack was banned from 1 October 1993, total prohibition followed in 1995, and the prohibition was later abandoned.
266.tq: Combine date, sequence and later-development facts in a coded statement question.

266.s: The Anti-arrack movement is regarded as one of India’s most successful movements led by which group?
266.x: It is regarded as one of India’s most successful women-led movements, and it was led entirely by rural women.
266.tq: Match the movement’s significance with its principal social constituency.

266.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Organisation)
a. Andhra Mahila Sabha
b. Progressive Organisation of Women
c. Stree Shakti Sanghatana
d. Mahila Dakshata Samiti
List-II (Year)
i. 1978
ii. 1937
iii. 1990
iv. 1974
Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
266.x: Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded in 1937, POW in 1974, Stree Shakti Sanghatana in 1978 and Mahila Dakshata Samiti in 1990.
266.tq: Start from the sure year–organisation pair and eliminate codes containing inconsistent matches.

266.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha, established in 1937?
266.x: Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by Durgabai Deshmukh in 1937.
266.tq: Test the founder–organisation pair directly, a common history question pattern.

266.s: The Andhra Mahila Samakhya and the AP Mahila Sangham were associated with which group and year?
266.x: The Andhra Mahila Samakhya and AP Mahila Sangham were two Communist bodies formed after the CPI split in 1964.
266.tq: Discriminate between similar organisations by combining ideological association and year.

266.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Progressive Organisation of Women — Radical-Left women activists, Hyderabad — 1974
2. Stree Shakti Sanghatana — Vasantha Kannabiran and K. Lalita — 1978
3. Mahila Dakshata Samiti — Suman Krishnakant — 1990
4. Abhyudaya Mahila Samstha — Malladi Subbamma — family counselling
Select the correct answer using the code below.
266.x: All four pairings are correct. Abhyudaya Mahila Samstha was associated with family counselling and Malladi Subbamma; no year is specified for it.
266.tq: Verify each organisation against its activist base, founder or activity before selecting the complete combination.

266.s: The first State women’s Mahasabha in Andhra Pradesh was organised in which year and by whom?
266.x: The first State women’s Mahasabha was organised by Communist women in 1947.
266.tq: Separate an organisation’s founding year from the year of the first State-level women’s Mahasabha.

266.s: Which programme was introduced in 1982–83 and provided group-based credit to rural poor women?
266.x: DWCRA, or Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas, was introduced in 1982–83 and provided group-based credit to rural poor women.
266.tq: Associate the programme with its distinctive year and economic feature.

266.s:
Consider the following statements about the self-help group movement in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Velugu began in 2000.
2. Velugu was aided by the World Bank.
3. Velugu promoted SHG federations through village organisations and mandal samakhyas.
4. Indira Kranthi Patham was the earlier name of Velugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: Velugu began in 2000, was World Bank-aided and operated through village organisations and mandal samakhyas. Indira Kranthi Patham was the later renamed form, not the earlier name.
266.tq: Use the reversed-name trap to distinguish the original programme from its renamed version.

266.s: Indira Kranthi Patham was introduced in 2004 as the renamed form of which programme and was run by which organisation?
266.x: Indira Kranthi Patham was introduced in 2004 as the renamed Velugu programme and was run by the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP).
266.tq: Test the programme-renaming and implementing-agency relationship together.

266.s: Which of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh’s position in the SHG movement?
o: It replaced all SHGs with individual bank accounts.
It became India’s SHG leader through DWCRA-based initiatives.
It prohibited group-based credit for rural women.
It confined SHGs to urban municipalities.
266.x: Andhra Pradesh became India’s SHG leader through the group-based credit and later federation-based initiatives.
266.tq: Apply the programme feature to identify the correct state-level consequence.

266.s: As stated in the current national position, approximately how many women are associated with how many SHGs?
266.x: The stated current figure is 10 crore women associated with 90 lakh SHGs nationally.
266.tq: Keep the scale and the two numerical units in the correct order.

266.s: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj’s Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are proposed to be aligned with which institutions?
266.x: The Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are to be aligned with self-help groups.
266.tq: Identify the institutional linkage in a current policy proposal.

266.s: What was the principal significance of the Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986?
o: It reserved one-third of Assembly seats for women.
It established the Central Social Welfare Board.
It abolished the Devadasi system in Andhra Pradesh.
It gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property.
266.x: The 1986 Andhra Pradesh amendment gave daughters coparcenary rights in joint family property, well before the Central amendment of 2005.
266.tq: Match a legislation with its precise legal effect and distinguish it from reservation laws.

266.s: The Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act preceded the corresponding Central amendment by approximately how many years?
266.x: The Andhra Pradesh amendment was enacted in 1986, while the Central amendment came in 2005, a difference of 19 years.
266.tq: Calculate the interval between two legislatively significant years rather than recalling either year in isolation.

266.s: Which constitutional provisions provide for at least one-third reservation of seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?
266.x: Articles 243D(3) and 243T provide for at least one-third reservation of seats for women in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively.
266.tq: Use the article-number trap by distinguishing reservation provisions from general equality and legislative-seat provisions.

266.s: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments relating to women’s reservation in local bodies were enacted in which year?
266.x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments were enacted in 1992 and provided at least one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities.
266.tq: Distinguish the year of constitutional amendments from the years of later women-specific legislation.

266.s:
Consider the following statements about the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023:
1. It provides for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
2. It provides for 33% reservation for women in State Assemblies.
3. Its implementation is tied to delimitation.
4. As of August 2026, it was already in force throughout India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: The Act provides 33% reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, but implementation is tied to delimitation. As of August 2026 it was not yet in force, making statement 4 false.
266.tq: Spot the current-status reversal in an otherwise correct legislative description.

266.s: What happened to the Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026, which sought to accelerate implementation of women’s reservation by redistributing Lok Sabha seats?
o: It was referred to the Central Social Welfare Board.
It was withdrawn after the 73rd Amendment.
266.x: The Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026 was defeated in April 2026.
266.tq: Test the fate and purpose of a recent constitutional proposal without confusing it with an enacted amendment.

266.s: Who was the editor of the Telugu feminist magazine Bhumika, founded in 1993?
266.x: Bhumika was founded in 1993 and its editor was Kondaveeti Satyavathi.
266.tq: Distinguish a journal’s editor from activists, reformers and political leaders listed in the same field.

266.s: Which of the following statements about earlier feminist publishing and reform is correct?
o: Satihita Bodhini was an SHG federation started in 2000.
Bhumika was founded by Kandukuri Veeresalingam in 1883.
Janana and Satihita Bodhini were associated with Kandukuri Veeresalingam and promoted women’s education and widow remarriage.
Janana was the official journal of the Central Social Welfare Board.
266.x: Kandukuri Veeresalingam’s Janana and Satihita Bodhini promoted women’s education and widow remarriage. Bhumika was a later Telugu feminist magazine founded in 1993.
266.tq: Reject the wrongly dated or wrongly attributed journal by checking the reformer–publication association.

266.s: In which year did Sharda Mukherjee become the first woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh?
266.x: Sharda Mukherjee became the first woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 1977.
266.tq: Associate the first office-holder with the correct year while separating it from other leadership milestones.

266.s: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in which year?
266.x: Pratibha Bharati became the first woman Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 1999.
266.tq: Use chronological discrimination among the years of women’s political milestones.

266.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act
B. First woman Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly
C. First woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh
D. First chairperson of the Central Social Welfare Board
Choose the correct sequence.
266.x: The relevant years are 1953 for D, 1977 for C, 1986 for A and 1999 for B. Therefore, the sequence is D, C, A, B—not option a.
266.tq: Place the dated milestones first and verify the middle positions carefully.

266.s: The Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act was enacted in which year?
266.x: The Madras Devadasis (Prevention of Dedication) Act was enacted in 1947.
266.tq: Distinguish the law year from earlier campaign and bill dates.

266.s: Which law and year are correctly associated with the prohibition of the Devadasi or Jogini system in Andhra Pradesh?
266.x: The AP Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in 1988.
266.tq: Separate the Madras law, the AP law and the dowry law by jurisdiction, subject and year.

266.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in which year?
266.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act was enacted in 1961.
266.tq: Test the law–year pair directly using nearby social-reform dates as distractors.

266.s: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference demanded the abolition of which systems?
266.x: The 1919 Machilipatnam Adi-Andhra conference, associated with Bhagya Reddy Varma, demanded abolition of the Jogini and Devadasi systems.
266.tq: Link a conference with its specific reform demand rather than with later legislation.

266.s: Which sequence correctly reflects the background to Devadasi abolition efforts?
o: Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign, followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly
Ammannaraja’s campaign, followed by Muthulakshmi Reddy’s 1947 bill in Andhra Pradesh
The 1988 AP Act, followed by the 1919 Machilipatnam conference
The 1961 Dowry Prohibition Act, followed by the 1937 anti-dedication bill
266.x: Muthulakshmi Reddy’s campaign was followed by Ammannaraja’s 1937 anti-dedication bill in the Madras Assembly.
266.tq: Track the reform campaign and bill in sequence, while rejecting reversed dates and jurisdictions.

266.s: Which sequence best represents the broad evolution of the women’s movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Reform bodies, Left and autonomous groups, mass action, SHG economics
SHG economics, reform bodies, mass action, princely-state administration
Mass action, constitutional courts, reform bodies, military organisations
Autonomous groups, colonial administration, SHG economics, reform bodies
266.x: The movement moved from reform bodies such as Andhra Mahila Sabha to Left and autonomous groups, then to mass action such as Anti-arrack and SHG-based economic activity.
266.tq: Arrange movements by their broad institutional and social progression rather than by isolated dates.

266.s: Which initiative was launched to build the leadership skills of women elected representatives?
266.x: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan was launched to build leadership skills among women elected representatives.
266.tq: Match a programme with its stated target group and purpose.

266.s:
Which of the following statements about women-oriented support services in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. One Stop Centres function in all 26 districts.
2. The 181 Women Helpline has operated since 2016.
3. Andhra Pradesh has 28 Shakti Sadans.
4. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao covers all 26 districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
266.x: All four statements are correct: One Stop Centres cover all 26 districts, the 181 helpline has run since 2016, there are 28 Shakti Sadans, and BBBP covers all 26 districts.
266.tq: Check each numerical coverage claim before choosing the complete combination.

266.s: How many cases had been handled by One Stop Centres in Andhra Pradesh, according to the stated state profile?
266.x: The stated figure for cases handled by One Stop Centres is 22,692.
266.tq: Distinguish similar-looking figures by preserving the exact number of digits.

266.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the dates associated with Beti Bachao Beti Padhao?
o: It dates from 1993 and was launched in 2000.
It dates from 1988 and was launched in 1992.
It dates from 2015 and was launched in 2006.
It dates from 2006 and was launched in 2015.
266.x: The APSES states that BBBP dates from 2006, while the scheme was launched in 2015.
266.tq: Separate a scheme’s stated origin or dating from its formal launch year.

266.s: Which of the following figures was recorded by NCRB for dowry cases and dowry deaths in 2023?
o: About 6,100 dowry cases and 15,000 dowry deaths
About 15,000 dowry cases and 4,41,534 dowry deaths
About 4,41,534 dowry cases and 15,000 dowry deaths
About 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths
266.x: NCRB recorded about 15,000 dowry cases and 6,100 dowry deaths in 2023.
266.tq: Do not reverse paired statistics; match each figure with its correct category.

266.s: The number of crimes against women recorded in 2024 was approximately:
266.x: The stated 2024 figure for crimes against women was 4,41,534.
266.tq: Identify the exact large-scale current-affairs figure rather than confusing it with dowry-case statistics.

267.s: Which one of the following institutions was established in 1964 for training in drama at Vijayawada?
o: Nataka Vidyalayam of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad
267.x: Nataka Vidyalayam of the Andhra Nataka Kala Parishad was established at Vijayawada on 1 August 1964 for training in drama.
267.tq: Use the institution–purpose–place linkage to eliminate neighbouring cultural bodies.

267.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. International Telugu Institute — 1975
2. Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University — 1985
3. Ravindra Bharathi — 1961

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
267.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The International Telugu Institute was established in 1975, Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985, and Ravindra Bharathi in 1961.
267.tq: Check each institution against its establishment year before selecting the coded combination.

267.s:
With reference to national cultural academies, consider the following statements:
1. Sangeet Natak Akademi was the first national arts academy.
2. Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad.
3. Sahitya Akademi is a statutory body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: Sangeet Natak Akademi was the first national arts academy and was inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad. Sahitya Akademi was established as a society, not as a statutory body.
267.tq: Identify the false institutional-status statement before using the coded options.

267.s: Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated on which date?
267.x: Sangeet Natak Akademi was inaugurated on 28 January 1953.
267.tq: Distinguish the inauguration date of Sangeet Natak Akademi from the dates associated with other national academies.

267.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the establishment of the Sahitya Akademi?
o: It was established in 1975 and inaugurated on 12 March 1954 as a statutory body.
It was set up in 1952 and inaugurated on 12 March 1954 as a society.
It was set up in 1954 and inaugurated on 28 January 1953 as a statutory body.
It was established in 1961 and inaugurated on 1 August 1964 as a society.
267.x: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1952 and inaugurated on 12 March 1954. It is a society and not a statutory body.
267.tq: Watch for the swapped year, inauguration date and institutional status trap.

267.s:
Arrange the following national cultural institutions in chronological order of their establishment or setting up:
A. Lalit Kala Akademi
B. Sahitya Akademi
C. Sangeet Natak Akademi
D. Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University
267.x: The Sahitya Akademi was set up in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1953, Lalit Kala Akademi in 1954, and Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University in 1985.
267.tq: Fix the earliest and latest institutions first, then distinguish the middle years.

267.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Conference)
A. First World Telugu Conference
B. Second World Telugu Conference
C. Third World Telugu Conference
D. Fourth World Telugu Conference

List-II (Venue)
1. Tirupati
2. Mauritius
3. Hyderabad
4. Kuala Lumpur

Choose the correct answer using the code below:
267.x: The First Conference was held at Hyderabad, the Second at Kuala Lumpur, the Third in Mauritius and the Fourth at Tirupati.
267.tq: Start from the sure venue of the First Conference and complete the one-to-one matching.

267.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Second World Telugu Conference — Kuala Lumpur, 1981
267.x: The Fourth World Telugu Conference was held at Tirupati in 2012, not at Vijayawada.
267.tq: Find the single altered venue while retaining the correct year.

267.s:
Match the following newspapers with their founders:

A. Andhra Jyothi
B. Eenadu
C. Udayam
D. Sakshi

1. Ramoji Rao
2. Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy
3. K.L.N. Prasad
4. Dasari Narayana Rao

Choose the correct answer using the code below:
267.x: Andhra Jyothi was founded by K.L.N. Prasad, Eenadu by Ramoji Rao, Udayam by Dasari Narayana Rao and Sakshi by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
267.tq: Use the founder–newspaper pair as the anchor and reject swapped-founder options.

267.s: Which one of the following newspapers was launched in 1984 by Dasari Narayana Rao?
267.x: Udayam was launched in 1984 by Dasari Narayana Rao.
267.tq: Discriminate among closely related newspaper names by matching both founder and year.

267.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960.
2. Eenadu was launched from Visakhapatnam in 1974.
3. Sakshi was launched in 2008.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Jyothi was launched in 1960, Eenadu in Visakhapatnam in 1974, and Sakshi in 2008.
267.tq: Verify the newspaper year and, where given, the place of launch before choosing the code.

267.s: Which of the following statements regarding early Telugu journals is correct?
o: Andhra Patrika was the first communist Telugu journal and Prajasakti was launched after Independence.
Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal and Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence.
Bharati was the first Telugu journal after Independence and Andhra Patrika was founded in 1956.
Jaya Bharat was founded before Independence and Bharati was the first communist Telugu journal.
267.x: Prajasakti was the first communist Telugu journal, while Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal after Independence. Andhra Patrika and Bharati are associated with Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao and the year 1924.
267.tq: Distinguish the superlatives and historical sequence of the early Telugu journals.

267.s: Gurram Jashuva received the Sahitya Akademi Award in Telugu in which year?
267.x: Gurram Jashuva received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1964. The award was not for Gabbilam; he received the Padma Bhushan in 1970.
267.tq: Avoid the famous-work trap by separating the award year from the Padma Bhushan year.

267.s: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award for which work?
267.x: Rayaprolu Subbarao received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1965 for Misra Manjari.
267.tq: Match the author with the specific award-winning work rather than with a better-known Telugu title.

267.s: Who was the first Telugu recipient of the Jnanpith Award?
267.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana was the first Telugu recipient of the Jnanpith Award. His work associated with the award is Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu.
267.tq: Use the first-recipient clue and distinguish the three Telugu Jnanpith awardees.

267.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Viswanatha Satyanarayana — Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu
2. C. Narayana Reddy — Jnanpith Award recipient
3. Ravuri Bharadwaja — Jnanpith Award recipient
4. Bapu — Telugu Velugu award for literature in 2012
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
267.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bapu received the Telugu Velugu award for painting in 2012, whereas C. Narayana Reddy received it for literature.
267.tq: Identify the reversed-category trap between literature and painting.

267.s: At the Ugadi 2012 Telugu Velugu awards, who was associated with literature and who with painting, respectively?
267.x: C. Narayana Reddy received the Telugu Velugu award for literature, while Bapu received it for painting.
267.tq: Split the paired categories first, then assign the two personalities.

267.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award currently carries which combination of languages and prize amount?
267.x: The Sahitya Akademi Award covers 24 languages—22 Eighth Schedule languages along with English and Rajasthani—and carries Rs 1 lakh.
267.tq: Distinguish the language count and prize amount from figures associated with other awards.

267.s: Who founded the Surabhi family theatre tradition?
267.x: The Surabhi family theatre tradition was founded by Vanarasa Govinda Rao at Sorugu near Jammalamadugu in Kadapa.
267.tq: Apply the founder–institution trap used frequently in culture questions.

267.s:
Consider the following statements about Surabhi theatre:
1. It originated at Sorugu near Jammalamadugu in Kadapa.
2. Its first play was Keechaka Vadham.
3. Live actors replaced the puppets of Tholu Bommalata.
4. The village of Sorugu came to be called Surabhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All four statements are correct. Surabhi began at Sorugu, its first play was Keechaka Vadham, live actors replaced Tholu Bommalata puppets, and the village came to be known as Surabhi.
267.tq: Treat each numbered statement as a separate place, play or development clue.

267.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Padya Natakam?
o: A modern television drama festival conducted by the AP Government
A puppet theatre performed without any human actors
A form of Telugu theatre in which dialogue is mainly in verse
267.x: Padya Natakam is classical Telugu theatre in which the dialogue is mainly presented in verse.
267.tq: Identify the exact defining feature instead of choosing an associated theatre institution.

267.s: Nandi Natakotsavams are organised by the Government of Andhra Pradesh primarily as a festival for which field?
267.x: Nandi Natakotsavams are the Andhra Pradesh Government's theatre festival for Telugu drama, new playwrights and artists.
267.tq: Match the festival with its field and its support for new theatre talent.

267.s: Which statement regarding the Nandi Awards is correct?
o: They are theatre awards instituted by the Government of India in 1969.
They are national literary awards instituted in 1952.
They are Andhra Pradesh Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
They are awards exclusively for Telugu newspapers, instituted in 1975.
267.x: Nandi Awards are Andhra Pradesh Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.
267.tq: Use the awarding authority, fields and year together to reject swapped-award descriptions.

267.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dadasaheb Phalke Award:
1. It was instituted in 1969.
2. Devika Rani was its first recipient.
3. It carries a Swarna Kamal, a shawl and a cash prize.
4. The cash prize was raised from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh in 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All four statements are correct. The award was instituted in 1969, first given to Devika Rani, and carries a Swarna Kamal, shawl and cash prize, which was raised to Rs 15 lakh in 2024.
267.tq: Verify the award's institution, first recipient, components and revised monetary amount separately.

267.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
267.x: B.N. Reddy, Akkineni Nageswara Rao and K. Viswanath are among the Telugu recipients of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Dharmavaram Ramakrishnamacharyulu is associated with Telugu theatre, not this list of film awardees.
267.tq: Use the domain distinction between Telugu cinema awardees and theatre personalities.

267.s: In 1985, the State akademis were merged into which institution by the NTR Government?
267.x: In 1985, the NTR Government merged the State akademis into the newly established Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University.
267.tq: Identify the institution created through restructuring rather than the pre-existing cultural bodies.

267.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the recent position regarding Andhra Pradesh cultural awards and festivals?
o: The Telugu Language Awards were discontinued from 29 August.
The Kandukuri Awards and Nandi Awards were permanently abolished by the coalition government.
Nandi Natakotsavams were replaced exclusively by the National Theatre Festival.
The Kandukuri Awards were revived, while revival of Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams was announced.
267.x: The coalition government revived the Kandukuri Awards and announced the revival of the Nandi Awards and Nandi Natakotsavams. The previous government had allowed these awards or festivals to lapse.
267.tq: Track the change from lapse to revival and distinguish announcement from abolition.

267.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the current cultural initiative?
o: National Theatre Festival — exclusively at one venue
Telugu Language Awards — to be held on 15 July
Telugu Mahotsavam — to be held annually
267.x: Telugu Mahotsavam was announced as an annual event. Telugu Language Awards are associated with 29 August, and the National Theatre Festival is being held across 150 locations.
267.tq: Separate the dates, scale and status of the different current cultural initiatives.

267.s: The Telugu Mahotsavam was announced at which location in July 2026?
267.x: The annual Telugu Mahotsavam was announced at the Undavalli Caves in July 2026 by Minister Kandula Durgesh.
267.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the current announcement from historic conference venues.

267.s: On which date are the Telugu Language Awards to be observed according to the current cultural announcements?
267.x: The Telugu Language Awards are scheduled for 29 August.
267.tq: Distinguish the current award date from inauguration and festival dates.

267.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Theatre Festival of the Sangeet Natak Akademi:
1. It was scheduled for 15 July 2026.
2. It was planned across 150 locations.
3. Its theme was connected with 150 years of Vande Mataram.
4. Two plays from Andhra Pradesh were selected.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
267.x: All four statements are correct. The festival was scheduled for 15 July 2026 at 150 locations in connection with 150 years of Vande Mataram, with two Andhra Pradesh plays selected.
267.tq: Check the date, number of locations, commemorative theme and state representation independently.

267.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed among the Andhra Pradesh cultural awards?
267.x: Ugadi Kala Ratna, Kandukuri, Telugu Language and Gurram Jashuva awards are listed among Andhra Pradesh cultural awards. Lalit Kala Akademi is a national cultural academy, not one of the listed Andhra Pradesh awards.
267.tq: Distinguish a state award list from the name of a national academy.

268.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a Dalit literary anthology?
o: Chikkanavutunna Pata — G. Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas
268.x: Chikkanavutunna Pata was edited by G. Lakshmi Narasaiah and Tripuraneni Srinivas. Nallapoddu is associated with Gogu Syamala, while Padunekkina Pata was edited by G. Lakshmi Narasaiah.
268.tq: Start from the sure author–work pair and eliminate swapped editors.

268.s:
Consider the following statements about Dalit poetry anthologies:
1. Chikkanavutunna Pata was published in 1995.
2. Padunekkina Pata was published in 1996.
3. Both works are associated with Dalit poetry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
268.x: Chikkanavutunna Pata is a 1995 Dalit poetry anthology, while Padunekkina Pata is a 1996 Dalit poetry anthology. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
268.tq: Use the dates and genre together to identify the complete combination.

268.s: Gurram Jashuva is regarded as the first modern Telugu poet associated with which literary stream?
268.x: Gurram Jashuva is regarded as the first modern Telugu Dalit poet.
268.tq: Test the identity of a pioneering literary figure directly.

268.s: The Karamchedu incident referred to in the context of the Dalit movement took place in:
268.x: The Karamchedu incident took place in 1985. The 1982 reference is an erroneous date appearing in one compilation and is not the year of the incident.
268.tq: Discriminate between closely placed year options.

268.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
268.x: Ditta Pullayya is associated with Adi Andhra Patrika. Vempatapu Satyam was associated with the Srikakulam peasant struggle, not Adi Andhra Patrika.
268.tq: Find the mismatched person–association pair.

268.s: Who among the following authored the novel Jakkadona?
268.x: Jakkadona was written by R.C. Krishnaswamy Raju.
268.tq: Test a direct author–work association.

268.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Veyi Padagalu — Viswanatha Satyanarayana
2. Athadu Adavini Jayinchadu — Kesava Reddy
3. Ramayana Vishavruksham — Ranganayakamma
