270.tq: Test the pen name directly from the birth-name association.

270.s: The pen name ‘Vapa’ refers to which artist?
270.x: Vaddadi Papaiah was known by the pen name Vapa.
270.tq: Discriminate between closely grouped artist pen names.

270.s: Salar Jung Museum is located in Hyderabad and is associated with the collection of which person?
o: Mir Osman Ali Khan, Nizam VII
Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III
270.x: The Salar Jung Museum at Hyderabad contains the collection of Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, also known as Salar Jung III, gathered over more than 40 years.
270.tq: Link the institution with its collector and location.

270.s: The marble statue ‘Veiled Rebecca’ in the Salar Jung Museum was bought in which place and year?
270.x: The ‘Veiled Rebecca’ marble statue was bought in Rome in 1876 and is part of the Salar Jung Museum collection.
270.tq: Combine the location and year instead of relying on a single date.

270.s: Which museum is situated on an island in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir and houses rescued Ikshvaku-Buddhist remains?
270.x: The Nagarjunakonda island museum, located in the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir, houses archaeological material rescued from the submerged area, including Ikshvaku-Buddhist finds.
270.tq: Use the location–collection combination to identify the museum.

270.s: The Amaravati site museum is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Rescued Ikshvaku remains from an island museum
Modern paintings of Damerla Rama Rao
The collection of Salar Jung III
Amaravati Mahachaitya and white limestone sculpture of the Amaravati School
270.x: The Amaravati site museum is associated with the Amaravati Mahachaitya and white limestone sculptures of the Amaravati School. Many Amaravati relics are also held in London and Madras museums.
270.tq: Identify the museum through its characteristic archaeological collection.

270.s:
Which of the following statements regarding museums in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. Bapu Museum at Vijayawada was formerly known as Victoria Jubilee Museum.
2. Baudhasree Archaeological Museum is located at Guntur.
3. Both museums hosted International Museum Day events on 18 May in 2026.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
270.x: All three statements are correct. Bapu Museum is the former Victoria Jubilee Museum at Vijayawada, Baudhasree Archaeological Museum is at Guntur, and both hosted events on 18 May 2026.
270.tq: Check the institution, location and date together.

270.s: Nagarjunakonda was first found in 1926 by whom?
270.x: Nagarjunakonda was found in 1926 by A. Ranganatha Saraswati. Later excavation work involved Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam.
270.tq: Distinguish the initial discoverer from later excavators.

270.s: Which archaeological site was excavated by Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam after its discovery by A. Ranganatha Saraswati?
270.x: The excavation of Nagarjunakonda involved Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam after its discovery by A. Ranganatha Saraswati.
270.tq: Match the group of excavators with the correct site.

270.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
270.x: Nagarjunakonda is associated with Palnadu district, not Guntur district. Bavikonda and Thotlakonda are in Visakhapatnam district, while Salihundam is in Srikakulam district.
270.tq: Locate the wrong district by comparing all site–district pairs.

270.s: Bavikonda is best described as which of the following?
o: A hilltop monastery representing one of the oldest Hinayana phases
A Mahayana-Vajrayana port town with Tara bronzes
An amphitheatre possibly constructed with Roman assistance
270.x: Bavikonda is a hilltop monastery associated with one of the oldest Hinayana phases. The other descriptions relate to Salihundam, Gudiwada Dibba and Nagarjunakonda respectively.
270.tq: Use the distinctive archaeological description to identify the site.

270.s: Which site was spotted by the Indian Navy and later excavated by the Andhra Pradesh State Archaeology Department?
270.x: Thotlakonda was spotted by the Indian Navy and excavated by the Andhra Pradesh State Archaeology Department. It contains a stupa, apsidal chaityas and evidence of rainwater harvesting.
270.tq: Identify the site through the unusual discoverer–excavator combination.

270.s:
Which of the following features are associated with Nagarjunakonda?
1. An acoustic building and an amphitheatre
2. Santamula’s Ashvamedha altar and a Sati sculpture
3. More than 30 stupas
4. Continuous habitation from the Palaeolithic to 1960 CE
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
270.x: All four features are associated with Nagarjunakonda. The amphitheatre is considered possibly to have involved Roman assistance, and the site records habitation extending from the Palaeolithic to 1960 CE.
270.tq: Test a dense site description by checking each independent feature.

270.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bojjannakonda — Monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra; Mahayana-Vajrayana association
Gudiwada Dibba — Tara bronzes and Buddha footprint
Salihundam — Mauryan to Satavahana remains only
Thotlakonda — Monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra
270.x: Bojjannakonda is associated with a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra and Mahayana-Vajrayana remains. Gudiwada Dibba is associated with Mauryan-to-Satavahana remains, while Tara bronzes and a Buddha footprint belong to Salihundam.
270.tq: Separate similar Buddhist sites by their distinctive finds.

270.s:
Arrange the following sites according to the district indicated for them in the material, beginning with Palnadu and ending with Srikakulam:
A. Salihundam
B. Bavikonda
C. Nagarjunakonda
D. Thotlakonda
Select the correct sequence.
270.x: Nagarjunakonda is associated with Palnadu, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda with Visakhapatnam, and Salihundam with Srikakulam. Therefore, the sequence is C, B, D, A.
270.tq: Use the fixed first and last locations to arrange the middle entries.

270.s: Which statement regarding UNESCO and World Heritage status in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Lepakshi has been an inscribed World Heritage Site since 1958.
Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site, while Lepakshi was placed on UNESCO’s tentative list in 2022.
The Amaravati site was placed on the tentative list in 2022 instead of Lepakshi.
Andhra Pradesh has 28 inscribed World Heritage properties under UNESCO.
270.x: Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site. Lepakshi, including the Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi, was placed on UNESCO’s tentative list in 2022.
270.tq: Distinguish tentative-list status from inscribed World Heritage status.

270.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The ASI functions under the Ministry of Culture.
2. It conserves 3,688 centrally protected monuments.
3. The centrally protected monuments include 28 World Heritage properties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
270.x: All three statements are correct. The ASI operates under the Ministry of Culture and is stated to conserve 3,688 centrally protected monuments, including 28 World Heritage properties.
270.tq: Check the administrative authority and both numerical figures together.

270.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ICOMOS — Established in 1972 at New Delhi
ICOMOS — Evaluates only natural heritage nominations
270.x: The Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act is from 1958. The Antiquities and Art Treasures Act is from 1972, while ICOMOS was established in 1965 in Paris and evaluates cultural nominations.
270.tq: Check the law, year and institutional function for swapped details.

270.s: ICOMOS, established in Paris in 1965, is primarily associated with which function?
o: Excavation of all Buddhist sites in Andhra Pradesh
Administration of the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department
Transfer of antiques under the AP Reorganisation Act
270.x: ICOMOS was established in Paris in 1965 and evaluates cultural nominations. It is distinct from the ASI and from state archaeological departments.
270.tq: Identify the international body by its specialised heritage function.

270.s: Why were monuments at Anupu and on Nagarjunakonda island rebuilt on higher ground?
o: They were moved for the Srisailam project.
They were damaged by an earthquake during the Tagore centenary.
They were shifted to create the Salar Jung Museum.
They were threatened by submergence after construction of the Nagarjunasagar Dam.
270.x: The area was submerged after 1960 because of the Nagarjunasagar Dam project. The ASI dismantled and rebuilt monuments at Anupu and on Nagarjunakonda island, a process described as transplantation of monuments.
270.tq: Apply the cause–effect relationship between dam submergence and relocation.

270.s: The relocated monuments at Anupu and Nagarjunakonda are commonly referred to as what?
270.x: The monuments dismantled and rebuilt on higher ground because of Nagarjunasagar Dam submergence are called Transplanted Monuments.
270.tq: Recall the exact official descriptive term for the relocation process.

270.s: Ravindra Bharathi auditorium at Hyderabad was constructed in which year and on what occasion?
o: 2014, to commemorate the AP Reorganisation Act
1972, to commemorate the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act
1958, to commemorate the formation of Andhra Pradesh
270.x: Ravindra Bharathi auditorium in Hyderabad was constructed in 1961 as part of the observance of the Tagore centenary.
270.tq: Combine the public building with its construction year and commemorative occasion.

270.s: The present Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums traces its origin to which institution and year?
270.x: The department traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department established in 1914. Its Commissioner’s office is presently at Vijayawada.
270.tq: Distinguish the state department’s origin from national and international heritage bodies.

270.s: Where is the Commissioner’s office of the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums presently located?
270.x: The Commissioner’s office of the Andhra Pradesh Department of Archaeology and Museums is located at Vijayawada.
270.tq: Test the current headquarters location against nearby museum locations.

270.s:
Consider the following statements about the Divi Pump Scheme:
1. It is located at Puligadda.
2. It was restored as an irrigation museum in 2014.
3. About Rs 27 lakh was spent out of an estimated Rs 30 lakh.
4. It was later neglected because of lack of funds.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
270.x: All four statements are correct. The Divi Pump Scheme at Puligadda was restored as an irrigation museum in 2014, with about Rs 27 lakh spent of Rs 30 lakh, but was later neglected for lack of funds.
270.tq: Verify the location, year, expenditure and subsequent condition separately.

270.s: Which body formed a committee to identify and transfer Andhra Pradesh’s share of antiques from the former AP State Museum at Hyderabad under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
270.x: The Government of Andhra Pradesh formed a committee to identify and transfer its share of antiques under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014. The committee was chaired by Tejaswi Podapati.
270.tq: Identify the responsible authority in an administrative heritage issue.

270.s: The Government Order concerning the committee for identifying and transferring Andhra Pradesh’s share of antiques from the former AP State Museum at Hyderabad was issued on which date?
270.x: The relevant Government Order was issued on 31 December 2025. The related report was published on 2 January 2026.
270.tq: Separate the Government Order date from the dates of subsequent reports and events.

270.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri is correct?
o: The Archaeological Survey of India has begun scientific conservation of the temple, which includes a 16th-century mandapam and a 19th-century 153-foot gopuram.
The Archaeological Survey of India has begun cosmetic restoration of a 16th-century gopuram and a 19th-century mandapam at the temple.
The temple has a 15th-century mandapam and an 18th-century 135-foot gopuram under conservation by the Archaeological Survey of India.
The temple's conservation concerns only its 19th-century mandapam and does not include the gopuram.
270.x: The Archaeological Survey of India began scientific conservation of the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri. The temple complex includes a 16th-century mandapam and a 19th-century gopuram measuring 153 feet.
270.tq: Use the precise combination of institution, conservation method, dates and measurements.

270.s: The Tourism Department's “Discover Andhra” campaign promotes a Buddhist heritage circuit comprising which of the following sites?
o: Amaravati, Thotlakonda and the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple
270.x: The “Discover Andhra” campaign promotes a Buddhist heritage circuit comprising Amaravati, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda.
270.tq: Test the complete named list by identifying the option without a non-Buddhist site.

270.s: Which one of the following was identified as an unfinished item of the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Reconstruction of the 153-foot gopuram at Mangalagiri
Transfer of all temple conservation functions to the Archaeological Survey of India
270.x: The division of museum antiques remained one of the unfinished items arising from the 2014 bifurcation.
270.tq: Apply the institutional consequence to the specific unresolved bifurcation issue.

270.s: A heritage site has been given a superficial facelift without proper study of its historical fabric or the likely effects of surrounding development. Which approach best addresses the criticism involved?
o: Scientific conservation along with heritage impact assessment
Promotion of the site only through tourism campaigns
Replacement of all old structures with modern replicas
270.x: Cosmetic restoration is criticised for failing to protect the authentic historical character of heritage sites. Scientific conservation and heritage impact assessment provide the appropriate corrective approach.
270.tq: Distinguish the criticised cosmetic approach from the conservation-based solution in an applied situation.

271.s: Bhoodan Movement was begun by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at which place on 18 April 1951?
271.x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan Movement at Pochampalli on 18 April 1951.
271.tq: Combine the founder, date and place to identify the initiating event.

271.s: At the time of the beginning of the Bhoodan Movement, Pochampalli was situated in which administrative unit?
271.x: Pochampalli was in Nalgonda district of the then Hyderabad State; it is now in Telangana.
271.tq: Use the historical administrative setting rather than the present-day location.

271.s: Who was the first donor in the Bhoodan Movement, and how much land did he donate?
271.x: Vedire Ramachandra Reddy was the first donor and donated 100 acres of land.
271.tq: Match the individual with the precise quantitative detail.

271.s: Gramdan represented which subsequent stage of the Bhoodan Movement?
o: Transfer of surplus land only to government employees
A whole village being gifted to the community
Abolition of all tenancy rights by the State
271.x: Gramdan was the next stage of Bhoodan in which an entire village was gifted to the community.
271.tq: Apply the distinction between individual land donation and community donation.

271.s: The first Gramdan village, established in 1952, was:
271.x: Mangroth in Hamirpur district of Uttar Pradesh was the first Gramdan village in 1952.
271.tq: Discriminate between the first Bhoodan village and the first Gramdan village.

271.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Goa, Daman and Diu — Operation Vijay
2. Dadra and Nagar Haveli — Operation Vijay
3. Pondicherry — French enclave
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
271.x: Goa, Daman and Diu were integrated through Operation Vijay, while Pondicherry was a French enclave. Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed separately in 1954.
271.tq: Separate the Portuguese integration operation from the French and separately liberated enclaves.

271.s: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was freed in 1954 and subsequently made a Union Territory by which Constitutional Amendment?
271.x: The Tenth Amendment Act of 1961 made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory.
271.tq: Match the territory with the correct Constitutional Amendment.

271.s: Pondicherry was transferred de facto to India on:
271.x: The de facto transfer of Pondicherry took place on 1 November 1954.
271.tq: Use the exact transfer date rather than the later constitutional status date.

271.s: Pondicherry was made a Union Territory under the:
271.x: The Fourteenth Amendment Act of 1962 made Pondicherry a Union Territory.
271.tq: Identify the amendment by linking it to the French enclave concerned.

271.s: Goa acquired full statehood in:
271.x: Goa became a full-fledged State in 1987 after having been a Union Territory.
271.tq: Distinguish liberation, Union Territory status and later statehood.

271.s: Which law abolished zamindari in the Andhra area?
o: AP Land Reforms (Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings) Act
AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation
Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
271.x: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act abolished zamindari in the Andhra area.
271.tq: Match the land-reform law with its specific institutional target.

271.s: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in:
271.x: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in 1949 to abolish intermediaries in Telangana.
271.tq: Use the adjacent-year distinction among the early Hyderabad and Andhra land laws.

271.s: Which of the following laws was enacted in 1950?
o: Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act
Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
271.x: The Hyderabad Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act was enacted in 1950.
271.tq: Identify the law from its year among closely related land-reform enactments.

271.s: The AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the:
271.x: The AP Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the Subba Rao Committee.
271.tq: Match the committee with the legislation it influenced.

271.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956:
1. It required lease deeds to be written.
2. It prescribed a lease period of at least six years.
3. It came into force in 1961.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: The Act required written lease deeds, prescribed leases of at least six years and came into force in 1961.
271.tq: Test several connected statutory features together.

271.s: The Hyderabad (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 was primarily enacted in the context of:
271.x: The Telangana tenancy law was passed in the context of the Telangana armed struggle of 1946–51.
271.tq: Link legislation to the regional political and social circumstance that prompted it.

271.s: Under the Telangana tenancy law, six years of cultivation qualified a tenant for the status of a:
271.x: A tenant with six years of cultivation became a protected tenant and acquired hereditary rights.
271.tq: Identify the legal consequence of the specified cultivation period.

271.s: Under the Telangana tenancy law, a tenant could purchase ownership at 60 per cent of the market price in:
271.x: The tenant could purchase ownership at 60 per cent of the market price in 20 instalments.
271.tq: Pair the percentage with the corresponding number of instalments.

271.s: By 1964–68, ownership under the Telangana tenancy reform had been acquired over approximately:
271.x: Ownership had been acquired over 85,409 acres during 1964–68.
271.tq: Retain the precise area figure associated with implementation of the tenancy reform.

271.s: The AP Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1961 was considered weak mainly because of:
o: Absence of any ceiling provisions and lack of exemptions
Its exclusive application to forest land
Compulsory Gramdan and excessive rent ceilings
271.x: The 1961 ceiling law was weakened by benami transfers and exemptions.
271.tq: Identify the implementation loopholes rather than the formal purpose of the law.

271.s: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1/1959, amended by 1/1970, primarily:
o: Barred transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals
Created the National Land Reforms Council
Permitted unrestricted transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
Abolished all tenancy in the Andhra area
271.x: The Regulation barred the transfer of land in Scheduled Areas to non-tribals.
271.tq: Apply the protective purpose of a tribal-area land-transfer regulation.

271.s: The Land Reforms Bill passed by the Andhra Pradesh Cabinet under Chief Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao provided for:
o: Transfer of all land to intermediaries
Ceiling on holdings and transfer of surplus land to the landless
271.x: The Bill imposed a ceiling on holdings and provided for distribution of surplus land to the landless.
271.tq: Distinguish the operative measures of a reform bill from unrelated agrarian systems.

271.s: Under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act, the ceiling for a family unit ranged from:
o: 15–35 acres wet and 40–60 acres dry land
5–15 acres wet and 20–40 acres dry land
20–40 acres wet and 50–75 acres dry land
10–27 acres wet and 35–54 acres dry land
271.x: The ceiling ranged from 10–27 acres of wet land or 35–54 acres of dry land, depending on land classification.
271.tq: Compare the two land categories and retain both numerical ranges.

271.s: The maximum area retainable under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act was:
271.x: The maximum retainable area was 54 acres of ‘K’ grade, the lowest-grade, land.
271.tq: Match the maximum ceiling with the specific land-grade classification.

271.s: Which Constitutional provisions were inserted or placed under protection by the First Amendment of 1951 in relation to land-reform laws?
o: Articles 44 and 51A and the Eighth Schedule
Articles 243A and 243B and the Eleventh Schedule
Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule
271.x: The First Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and placed laws in the Ninth Schedule to protect land reforms.
271.tq: Match the constitutional shield with the amendment and its purpose.

271.s: The National Council for Land Reforms, set up in 2008, was chaired by the:
271.x: The National Council for Land Reforms was set up in 2008 under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister.
271.tq: Identify the authority associated with the institutional body.

271.s: The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) began originally as the NLRMP in:
271.x: DILRMP began as the National Land Records Modernization Programme in 2008.
271.tq: Distinguish the programme’s original form and starting year from its later status.

271.s: DILRMP became a Central Sector Scheme in:
271.x: The programme became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016.
271.tq: Separate the launch year from the year of conversion into a Central Sector Scheme.

271.s: Which of the following is associated with Phase 2 of DILRMP for 2016–26?
o: The Fifth and Sixth Schedules only
271.x: Phase 2 of DILRMP for 2016–26 covers ULPIN and NGDRS.
271.tq: Match the programme phase with its named components.

271.s: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru after the:
271.x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the National Integration Conference.
271.tq: Link the institution to its immediate constitutional-political origin.

271.s: The National Integration Conference that preceded the formation of the National Integration Council addressed which set of issues?
o: Inflation, unemployment, taxation and foreign trade
Land ceilings, tenancy, irrigation and consolidation
Disarmament, nuclear energy, space and cyber security
271.x: The conference considered communalism, casteism, regionalism and linguism as threats to national integration.
271.tq: Recognise the thematic cluster associated with national integration policy.

271.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a constitutional or institutional tool against regionalism?
271.x: The listed tools include the National Integration Council, Articles 44 and 51A, and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules. Article 32 exclusively is not included in that set.
271.tq: Find the option outside the stated group of integration tools.

271.s: Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu that contributed to the two-language formula occurred in:
271.x: The relevant anti-Hindi agitations occurred in 1937, 1965 and 1986.
271.tq: Retain the three separate years and identify the complete chronological set.

271.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 provided for the continued use of:
271.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 continued the use of English alongside the official language arrangements.
271.tq: Discriminate the statutory language provision from the languages involved in the agitations.

271.s:
Consider the following statements about the phases of land reform in India:
1. Phase I covered 1947–70.
2. Phase II began in 1970 and continued thereafter.
3. The Kumarappa Committee of 1949 helped set the agenda.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: The first phase covered 1947–70, the second began in 1970, and the Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the reform agenda.
271.tq: Combine periodisation with the committee associated with the reform agenda.

271.s: Which land-reform measure was regarded as the most successful and brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State?
271.x: Abolition of intermediaries was regarded as the most successful reform and brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.
271.tq: Match the reform measure with its recorded outcome.

271.s: Abolition of intermediaries covered approximately what share of cultivated area?
271.x: Abolition of intermediaries covered about 40 per cent of the cultivated area.
271.tq: Use the quantitative coverage figure to distinguish the reform’s scale.

271.s: Under tenancy reforms, rent was generally capped at what proportion of the produce?
271.x: Tenancy reforms generally capped rent at between one-fourth and one-sixth of the produce.
271.tq: Identify the precise range rather than reversing the numerator and denominator.

271.s: Tenancy reform was weakened in many areas by the practice of:
271.x: The practice of ‘voluntary surrenders’ enabled landlords to evade the protection intended by tenancy reforms.
271.tq: Identify the implementation device that undermined an otherwise protective reform.

271.s: Which one of the following was an exception to the general weakness caused by ‘voluntary surrenders’ in tenancy reform?
271.x: Operation Barga, introduced in West Bengal in 1977, was an important exception to the general failure of tenancy reform.
271.tq: Find the exceptional programme among similarly named movements and operations.

271.s: The two major rounds of land-ceiling legislation occurred during the:
271.x: Ceiling legislation was enacted in two major rounds, during the 1950s and the early 1970s.
271.tq: Place the two reform waves in their correct decades.

271.s: From 1972, which unit was adopted for applying land ceilings?
271.x: The family was made the unit for applying land ceilings from 1972.
271.tq: Distinguish the legally relevant unit from administrative units such as village or district.

271.s: Which of the following was a major method of evading land-ceiling laws?
271.x: Benami transfers were used to evade land-ceiling laws.
271.tq: Identify the evasion mechanism associated with ceiling legislation.

271.s: Land consolidation succeeded particularly in:
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
271.x: Land consolidation achieved notable success in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.
271.tq: Match the reform with the geographical region where it succeeded.

271.s: Which State was the first to abolish zamindari in 1950?
271.x: Uttar Pradesh was the first State to abolish zamindari in 1950.
271.tq: Match the reform milestone with the pioneering State.

271.s: Raj Krishna classified land reforms into which four categories?
271.x: Raj Krishna classified land reforms as liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental.
271.tq: Recall the complete four-part classification without substituting broader policy categories.

271.s: Which approach to tribal policy was favoured by Jawaharlal Nehru over both isolation and forced assimilation?
o: Forced assimilation into the dominant society
271.x: Nehru rejected both the museum approach of isolation and forced assimilation, favouring integration while respecting tribal identity and institutions.
271.tq: Directly distinguish between two rejected approaches and the preferred policy.

271.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel?
o: Respect for tribal rights in land and forests
Training tribes to run their own administration
271.x: Nehru's Tribal Panchsheel called for encouraging and preserving tribal languages, not replacing them. The other three are principles of the Panchsheel.
271.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated principle.

271.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tribal Panchsheel:
1. Tribes should develop along the lines of their own genius.
2. Tribal languages should be encouraged and preserved.
3. Tribal communities should be trained to run their own administration.
4. Tribal areas should be subjected to maximum administrative control.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 express the Tribal Panchsheel. Statement 4 is false because the Panchsheel advocated avoidance of over-administration.
271.tq: Reject the extreme statement that reverses the principle of limited administration.

271.s: Verrier Elwin's work titled A Philosophy for NEFA primarily argued for which of the following?
o: Cultural autonomy and limits on land alienation
Complete assimilation and unrestricted land transfer
Expansion of commercial farming in tribal areas
271.x: A Philosophy for NEFA argued for cultural autonomy and limitations on the alienation of tribal land.
271.tq: Link the author and work with its central argument.

271.s: With reference to the formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It was proposed by the Madras Assembly in 1947.
It was formulated exclusively by the Naga National Council.
It was credited to Verrier Elwin under Nehru's influence.
It was introduced through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
271.x: The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.
271.tq: Use the author-influence association to avoid a swapped institution or year.

271.s: The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution primarily deals with Scheduled Areas in:
o: Only the state of Arunachal Pradesh
States other than the North-Eastern states
271.x: The Fifth Schedule applies to Scheduled Areas in states other than the North-Eastern states covered by the Sixth Schedule arrangement.
271.tq: Discriminate between the geographical scopes of the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.

271.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 applies to:
o: All urban areas in the North-East
Scheduled Areas covered by the Fifth Schedule
Only Union Territories with tribal populations
Autonomous districts under the Sixth Schedule only
271.x: PESA 1996 applies to Scheduled Areas in states covered by the Fifth Schedule; it does not apply to the Sixth Schedule autonomous district areas.
271.tq: Separate PESA's Fifth Schedule coverage from Sixth Schedule autonomous councils.

271.s: Autonomous district councils are provided for under the Sixth Schedule in which group of states?
o: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Sikkim
Meghalaya, Sikkim, Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh
271.x: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
271.tq: Use the complete four-state list to distinguish the Sixth Schedule from other North-Eastern arrangements.

271.s: NEFA, which is now known as Arunachal Pradesh, was administered initially through the:
271.x: NEFA was run through the Governor of Assam and served as a policy laboratory for Elwin's approach.
271.tq: Test the administrative authority associated with a former regional name.

271.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to NEFA in chronological order:
A. NEFA became a Union Territory
B. NEFA became a state
C. NEFA was administered through the Governor of Assam
Which of the following is the correct sequence?
271.x: NEFA was first administered through the Governor of Assam, became a Union Territory in 1972 and became a state in 1987.
271.tq: Use the first administrative arrangement and then the two dated status changes.

271.s: NEFA became a Union Territory and later a state in which years respectively?
271.x: NEFA became a Union Territory in 1972 and attained statehood in 1987.
271.tq: Test a paired year sequence with closely spaced regional milestones.

271.s: Which organisation, led by A.Z. Phizo, demanded independence for the Naga areas?
271.x: The Naga National Council, associated with A.Z. Phizo, demanded independence for the Naga areas.
271.tq: Match the organisation with its leader and demand.

271.s: The Centre responded to the Naga question in 1963 principally by granting:
o: Sixth Schedule status to the whole of Assam
271.x: The Centre addressed the Naga question in 1963 by creating the state of Nagaland. The demand for Greater Nagalim associated with the NSCN continued thereafter.
271.tq: Distinguish the actual constitutional response from the continuing political demand.

271.s: The demand for Greater Nagalim is associated with which organisation?
271.x: The continuing Greater Nagalim demand is associated with the NSCN.
271.tq: Separate an organisation's continuing demand from the earlier independence demand.

271.s: The Koneru Ranga Rao Committee of the Andhra Pradesh Government was constituted in:
271.x: The Land Committee headed by Koneru Ranga Rao was constituted in 2006 during the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government.
271.tq: Directly test the committee's year using nearby but distinct year distractors.

271.s: The Koneru Ranga Rao Committee primarily dealt with:
271.x: It was a Land Committee concerned with land-related problems in Andhra Pradesh.
271.tq: Identify the committee by its subject rather than its chairperson alone.

271.s: Which one of the following was NOT a focus area of the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee?
271.x: The Committee focused on assignment lands, confirmation of land rights, tenancy regulation and land records. Corporate farming was not among its focus areas.
271.tq: Find the unrelated policy area among a list of genuine land-reform concerns.

271.s: Which law made Telugu the official language of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966
The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1956
271.x: The Andhra Pradesh Official Language Act, 1966 made Telugu the official language of the State.
271.tq: Match the language policy with its exact Act and year.

271.s: Telugu was declared a Classical Language in:
271.x: Telugu was declared a Classical Language in 2008.
271.tq: Test a language-status milestone through exact year discrimination.

271.s: The Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was enacted in:
271.x: The Andhra Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act was enacted in 1956.
271.tq: Discriminate among the closely related abolition-law years.

271.s: The Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation was introduced in:
271.x: The Hyderabad Jagir Abolition Regulation was introduced in 1949 after the Police Action.
271.tq: Link the regional abolition measure with its exact post-Police Action year.

271.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the abolition of intermediaries is correct?
o: Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani or ryotwari lands.
Ryotwari lands were converted into Jagirs.
Sarfekhas lands were excluded from all land reforms.
Jagir lands were converted into zamindari estates.
271.x: Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.
271.tq: Test the direction of institutional land-status conversion.

271.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Telangana inams legislation:
1. The Telangana Inams Act was enacted in 1955.
2. Religious and charitable inams were exempted.
3. The Act was stalled in courts.
4. The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was upheld by the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was struck down by the High Court.
271.tq: Identify the legally reversed statement in a group of related facts.

271.s: The Prakasam Committee, constituted in 1938, recommended:
o: Declaration of Telugu as a Classical Language
271.x: The Prakasam Committee of 1938 recommended the abolition of intermediaries.
271.tq: Match the committee with its reform recommendation.

271.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rs 2 per kg rice scheme — N.T. Rama Rao — 1983
271.x: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme, along with subsidised housing and Janata cloth, was associated with N.T. Rama Rao and introduced in 1983.
271.tq: Start from the sure scheme-chief minister-year combination.

271.s: Janmabhoomi, associated with people's participation in development, was introduced under which Chief Minister in 1997?
271.x: Janmabhoomi was introduced in 1997 under N. Chandrababu Naidu and emphasised people's participation in development.
271.tq: Combine the scheme's objective with its chief minister and year.

271.s: Which of the following welfare schemes was associated with Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy and higher education of poor students?
271.x: The Fee Reimbursement scheme, introduced in 2008, supported higher education for poor students and was associated with Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
271.tq: Identify a scheme from its beneficiary group and policy purpose.

271.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fee Reimbursement — higher education of poor students — 2008
Rajiv Aarogyasri — health insurance for the poor — 2007
Janmabhoomi — health insurance for the poor — 1997
271.x: Janmabhoomi concerned people's participation in development, not health insurance. Indiramma, Rajiv Aarogyasri and Fee Reimbursement are correctly matched with their purposes and years.
271.tq: Find the scheme whose purpose has been swapped with another scheme.

271.s: Which State was the first to adopt the three-tier Panchayati Raj system?
271.x: Rajasthan adopted the three-tier Panchayati Raj system first on 2 October 1959. Andhra Pradesh followed as the second State on 1 November 1959.
271.tq: Distinguish first and second adopters rather than confusing their dates.

271.s: Andhra Pradesh adopted the three-tier Panchayati Raj system at Shadnagar on:
271.x: Andhra Pradesh, the second State to adopt the system, introduced three-tier Panchayati Raj at Shadnagar on 1 November 1959.
271.tq: Test the exact date and location of the second State's adoption.

271.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the reform introduced by N.T. Rama Rao in 1985?
o: Enactment of the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
Creation of the first open university in India
Abolition of the hereditary Patel-Patwari system and introduction of the Mandal system
Introduction of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in Andhra Pradesh
271.x: In 1985, N.T. Rama Rao abolished the hereditary village officer Patel-Patwari system and introduced the Mandal system.
271.tq: Match the reform, year and political leader while rejecting later milestones.

271.s: Mandal Praja Parishads were established under the:
271.x: Mandal Praja Parishads were established under the 1986 Act.
271.tq: Separate the Act creating Mandal Praja Parishads from the later Panchayat Raj Act.

271.s: After the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act was enacted in:
271.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act was enacted in 1994 following the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
271.tq: Connect the constitutional amendment with the subsequent State legislation.

271.s: The first residential school in Andhra Pradesh was established at Sarvail in which year?
271.x: Sarvail in Nalgonda was the first residential school, established in 1971 under P.V. Narasimha Rao.
271.tq: Test the landmark institution through its place, year and associated leader.

271.s: Sarvail residential school is located in:
271.x: The first residential school was established at Sarvail in Nalgonda in 1971.
271.tq: Use place-based recall for an educational landmark.

271.s: Which of the following university-year pairs is correctly matched?
271.x: Nagarjuna University at Guntur was established in 1976. Kakatiya University was also established in 1976, while Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University and NTR University of Health Sciences were established in 1985 and 1986 respectively.
271.tq: Use the institution-location-year association and reject swapped years.

271.s: Which institution was the first open university in India?
o: Andhra Pradesh Open University, now Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University
271.x: The Andhra Pradesh Open University, now named Dr B.R. Ambedkar Open University, was the first open university in India and was established in 1982.
271.tq: Identify the institution by its distinctive national distinction.

271.s: Which university was the first health university in India?
271.x: NTR University of Health Sciences, established in 1986, was the first health university in India.
271.tq: Match the university with its unique institutional distinction and year.

271.s: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act was passed in:
271.x: The Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act was passed in December 1947 and was piloted by Muthulakshmi Reddy.
271.tq: Test the precise month and year of a social-reform law.

271.s: Who piloted the Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act?
271.x: Muthulakshmi Reddy piloted the Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act.
271.tq: Distinguish the legislative pilot from other social reformers associated with the issue.

271.s: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was associated with campaigns against the:
271.x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was among the reformers who campaigned against the Bhogam or Devadasi system.
271.tq: Link the reformer with the specific social practice opposed by him.

271.s: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in:
271.x: The Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act was enacted in 1988 and also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi dedication.
271.tq: Test the exact year of the State social-legislation measure.

271.s: Which of the following practices were also covered by the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988?
271.x: The 1988 Act also covered Jogini, Basivi and Matangi forms of dedication.
271.tq: Recall the complete group of practices covered by the legislation.

271.s: The Dubagunta women's movement in Nellore in 1992 was directed against:
271.x: Women in Dubagunta, Nellore, launched an anti-arrack movement in 1992.
271.tq: Identify the issue from the place, year and movement association.

271.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to prohibition in Andhra Pradesh in chronological order:
A. Dubagunta women's anti-arrack movement
B. Arrack ban under Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy
C. Total prohibition under N.T. Rama Rao
D. Prohibition lifted under N. Chandrababu Naidu
Which of the following is the correct sequence?
271.x: The Dubagunta movement occurred in 1992, the arrack ban in 1993, total prohibition under N.T. Rama Rao in 1995 and lifting of prohibition in 1997.
271.tq: Arrange the events by their successive years from 1992 to 1997.

271.s: Who imposed total prohibition in Andhra Pradesh in 1995?
271.x: N.T. Rama Rao imposed total prohibition in 1995, after the 1993 arrack ban under Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy.
271.tq: Discriminate between the chief ministers associated with successive prohibition steps.

271.s: Prohibition in Andhra Pradesh was lifted in 1997 under:
271.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu lifted prohibition in 1997.
271.tq: Test the final stage of a policy sequence through the responsible chief minister and year.

271.s: Who headed the first Backward Classes Commission in Andhra Pradesh, whose report was submitted in 1970?
271.x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and submitted its report in 1970.
271.tq: Match the commission with its role and year.

271.s: The Anantharaman Commission classified Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh into which groups and recommended what reservation?
o: Groups A to C and 18 percent reservation
Groups A to D and 25 percent reservation
Groups B to D and 20 percent reservation
Groups A to E and 27 percent reservation
271.x: The Commission classified BCs into Groups A, B, C and D and recommended 25 percent reservation.
271.tq: Test the classification and numerical recommendation together.

271.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Muralidhar Rao Commission:
1. It was associated with the year 1982.
2. It was connected with the raising of the BC quota in Andhra Pradesh.
3. The enhanced quota was struck down by the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: The Muralidhar Rao Commission was associated with 1982; NTR raised the BC quota to 44 percent in 1986, and the High Court struck down the enhanced quota.
271.tq: Combine the commission, year, policy outcome and judicial response.

271.s: The BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh was raised to 44 percent in 1986 during the tenure of:
271.x: N.T. Rama Rao raised the BC quota to 44 percent in 1986. The enhanced quota was subsequently struck down by the High Court.
271.tq: Use the person–year–policy association.

271.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Six-Point Formula and Article 371D?
o: The Six-Point Formula was incorporated through Article 370 by the 35th Amendment.
The Six-Point Formula led to Article 371D through the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.
Article 371D was inserted through the 44th Amendment to implement the Mandal Commission recommendations.
Article 371D led to the Six-Point Formula through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976.
271.x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.
271.tq: Discriminate between closely related formula, Article and Amendment numbers.

271.s: Article 371D primarily provides for which of the following in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Creation of separate High Courts for every district
Abolition of land ceilings in tribal areas
Reservation exclusively for backward Muslims in Parliament
Reservation of local cadres in public employment and education
271.x: Article 371D provides for local-cadre arrangements and reservation in jobs and education on a regional basis.
271.tq: Identify the constitutional provision from its practical application.

271.s: The reservation introduced in 2007 for backward Muslims in Andhra Pradesh was associated with which category?
271.x: The 2007 reservation for backward Muslims was associated with the BC-E category and amounted to 4 percent.
271.tq: Test the exact category attached to a reservation measure.

271.s: The 4 percent reservation for backward Muslims in Andhra Pradesh was introduced in:
271.x: The reservation of 4 percent for backward Muslims under the BC-E category was introduced in 2007.
271.tq: Use year-based discrimination among reservation milestones.

271.s:
Consider the following statements about Vibrant Villages Programme-II:
1. It covers 1,954 border villages.
2. The villages are located in 15 States and 2 Union Territories.
3. It covers borders with Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Myanmar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers 1,954 villages in 15 States and 2 Union Territories along the borders with Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Myanmar.
271.tq: Check a multi-part scheme description without dropping its numerical details.

271.s: Vibrant Villages Programme-II was cleared in April 2025 and launched at:
271.x: The programme was cleared in April 2025 and launched at Nathanpur in Cachar.
271.tq: Pair the programme with its approval date and launch location.

271.s: The launch of Vibrant Villages Programme-II at Nathanpur, Cachar, took place on:
271.x: The programme was launched at Nathanpur, Cachar, on 19 February 2026.
271.tq: Distinguish among closely placed current-affairs dates.

271.s: The 75th anniversary of the First Amendment to the Constitution fell on:
271.x: The 75th anniversary of the First Constitutional Amendment fell on 18 June 2026.
271.tq: Test an anniversary date directly rather than the date of the original event.

271.s: The First Constitutional Amendment was significant for land reforms because it:
o: abolished all tenancy arrangements throughout India
shielded zamindari abolition measures from legal challenge
271.x: The First Amendment provided constitutional protection to zamindari abolition measures, helping shield them from legal challenge.
271.tq: Connect a constitutional amendment with its land-reform consequence.

271.s: The Tana Bhagats opposed a Bharatmala highway primarily by invoking which legal provisions?
o: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the Fifth Amendment
The CNT Act, 1908 and the Sixth Schedule only
Article 371D and the Forest Rights Act, 2006
PESA and the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908
271.x: The Tana Bhagats cited the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, or PESA, and the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
271.tq: Identify the legal basis cited in a tribal and infrastructure dispute.

271.s: The failure of land reforms to overcome ceiling and tenancy problems contributed to the emergence of the:
271.x: The failure of land reforms, particularly regarding ceilings and tenancy, contributed to the Naxalbari revolt of 1967.
271.tq: Link a policy failure to its stated historical consequence.

271.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the two broad aspects of post-independence land reform?
o: Abolition was liberative, while tenancy and ceiling reforms were distributive.
Abolition was distributive, while tenancy and ceiling reforms were liberative.
Abolition dealt only with crop loans, while ceiling reforms dealt only with tribal autonomy.
Both abolition and tenancy reforms were exclusively administrative.
271.x: Raj Krishna described abolition as a ‘liberative’ reform, while tenancy and ceiling measures were ‘distributive’ reforms.
271.tq: Separate two similar reform categories through their stated objectives.

271.s: Which of the following was a major limitation of the abolition of zamindari and jagirdari systems?
o: It abolished land ceilings before introducing tenancy reform.
It applied only to urban property and not to agricultural land.
It completely eliminated all intermediaries and transferred land to tenants.
It changed the revenue hierarchy but did not by itself resolve tenancy and landholding inequalities.
271.x: Abolition mainly altered the revenue hierarchy. It did not by itself eliminate problems relating to tenancy and unequal landholding.
271.tq: Find the precise limitation rather than accepting an absolute reform claim.

271.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the failure of tenancy and ceiling laws:
1. Oral leases weakened the enforcement of tenancy protections.
2. Benami transfers helped defeat the objectives of ceiling laws.
3. Exemptions reduced the effectiveness of both tenancy and ceiling measures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
271.x: Oral leases, benami transfers and exemptions were all identified as practices that weakened the implementation of tenancy and ceiling laws.
271.tq: Combine several implementation weaknesses into a coded statement question.

271.s: The proposed Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024 is associated with which of the following measures?
o: Abolition of all land ceilings in Andhra Pradesh
Reservation of government jobs for agricultural labourers
Ownership titles for all tenants over the land they cultivate
Tenant entitlement cards and access to crop loans
271.x: The proposed Act provides for tenant entitlement cards and access to crop loans. It does not transfer ownership of the land to tenants.
271.tq: Distinguish tenant-use rights from ownership rights.

271.s: Under the proposed Andhra Pradesh New Tenancy Act, 2024, tenants are intended to receive rights relating primarily to:
o: The land, and not the crop
The crop, and not the land
Both land and crop ownership automatically
271.x: The proposal gives tenants rights relating to the crop they cultivate, not ownership rights over the land.
271.tq: Separate two closely related concepts—rights over produce and rights over land.

271.s: Bhoodan began at Pochampalli in the:
271.x: The Bhoodan Movement began at Pochampalli in the Telugu country, making it an important Andhra-related land reform milestone.
271.tq: Test the regional association of a movement’s place of origin.

271.s: The Andhra Pradesh ceiling law mentioned in connection with land reforms was passed under the leadership of:
271.x: The Andhra Pradesh ceiling law was passed under the leadership of P.V. Narasimha Rao.
271.tq: Match the legislation with the political leadership associated with it.

271.s: The Eluru agency land dispute illustrates the continuing legal relevance of which Andhra Pradesh regulations?
o: The AP Ceiling Act, 1973 and Regulation 2/59
The Andhra Tenancy Act, 1956 and Regulation 1/73
271.x: The Eluru agency land dispute involves APSALT Regulation 1/59 and Regulation 1/70, showing that tribal land law remains subject to litigation.
271.tq: Identify the exact legal instruments from a contemporary regional dispute.

271.s: Which one of the following statements best captures the significance of the Eluru agency land dispute?
o: It shows that tribal land law has ceased to have legal relevance after land reform.
It demonstrates that tribal land protection provisions continue to be contested in courts.
It concerned only reservation in educational institutions and not land rights.
It resulted in the replacement of all agency regulations by Article 371D.
271.x: The dispute demonstrates that tribal land regulations continue to be invoked and contested before courts.
271.tq: Infer the broader significance from a specific legal dispute.

272.s: The tribal settlements of Andhra Pradesh are predominantly associated with which of the following geographical regions?
o: The deltaic plains of the Krishna and Godavari rivers
The Eastern Ghats and the Nallamala belt
The coastal lagoons and mangrove islands
The Deccan plateau around the major urban centres
272.x: The tribal settlements of Andhra Pradesh mainly follow the forested uplands of the Eastern Ghats and the Nallamala belt, rather than the deltas.
272.tq: Use the geographical contrast between forested uplands and deltaic plains.

272.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chenchu — Nallamala forest and Srisailam region
Koya — plains of the southern districts
272.x: The Chenchus are associated with the Nallamala forests and the Srisailam region. Koya and Konda Reddi are mainly associated with the Godavari region, while Sugali are found largely in Rayalaseema and interior tracts.
272.tq: Start with the sure tribe–region pair and eliminate reversed locations.

272.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Koya — Godavari basin and agency tracts
2. Konda Reddi — Godavari hill tracts
3. Savara and Jatapu — North coastal hills
4. Yanadi and Yerukula — Plains of southern districts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
272.x: All four pairs are correctly matched with the regions specified for these tribes in Andhra Pradesh.
272.tq: Test a regional table through multiple independent tribe–location statements.

272.s: The tribes Gadaba, Bagata, Valmiki, Kotia, Porja and Khond are primarily associated with which area?
o: Araku Valley and the Visakhapatnam agency region
The Nallamala forest and Srisailam region
The plains of Nellore and Prakasam
272.x: These tribes are associated with the Araku Valley and the Visakhapatnam agency, presently included largely in the Alluri Sitharama Raju district.
272.tq: Use a cluster-based location question for a group of neighbouring tribes.

272.s: Which one of the following tribes is mainly associated with Rayalaseema and the interior tracts of Andhra Pradesh?
272.x: Sugali, also known as Lambada or Banjara, are mainly found in Rayalaseema and the interior tracts.
272.tq: Directly identify the tribe linked with the specified region.

272.s: The Chenchu name is traditionally interpreted as referring to people who
272.x: Chenchus are traditionally described as “those who live under trees,” reflecting their forest-based way of life.
272.tq: Test the exact meaning of a distinctive community name.

272.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Chenchu sub-tribes or sub-groups?
272.x: The listed Chenchu sub-groups are Koya, Konda, Yanadi, Ura Chenchus and Chenchu Dasarus. Muria is associated with the Ghotul dormitory tradition, not the listed Chenchu sub-groups.
272.tq: Find the outsider in a closely related tribal classification.

272.s: The mythic origin of the Chenchus is associated with the marriage of Ahobilam Narasimha and
272.x: The Chenchu origin legend associates their community with the marriage of Ahobilam Narasimha and the Chenchu girl Chenchita.
272.tq: Directly test a mythological association and its named figure.

272.s:
With reference to Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, consider the following statements:
1. The concept of PVTGs originated from the Dhebar Commission.
2. The Dhebar Commission associated with this concept was constituted in 1960–61.
3. India has 75 PVTGs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: The PVTG concept is associated with the Dhebar Commission of 1960–61, and India has 75 PVTGs according to the cited current figure.
272.tq: Combine a historical origin, a year and a current numerical fact.

272.s: How many PVTGs are included in the Ministry’s combined list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
272.x: The combined Ministry list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contains 12 PVTGs.
272.tq: Test the exact count using closely spaced numerical options.

272.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the combined PVTG list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
272.x: Bhil is not included in the stated combined list. The list includes Dongaria Khond, Konda Savara and Parengi Poroja, among others.
272.tq: Identify the outsider from a named official list.

272.s: Which of the following pairs of PVTGs is associated with the Telangana side of the combined Andhra Pradesh–Telangana list?
272.x: Kolam and Thoti belong to the Telangana side, although the list was not split after the 2014 bifurcation.
272.tq: Discriminate between the combined list and the State-wise location of entries.

272.s: Which of the following statements regarding the PVTG list for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana is correct?
o: It was never split after 2014 and continues as a combined list.
It contains only tribes living in Andhra Pradesh.
It was completely divided into two separate lists immediately after 2014.
It excludes tribes located in Telangana.
272.x: The Ministry’s list was not split after the 2014 bifurcation and continues as a combined Andhra Pradesh and Telangana list.
272.tq: Watch for an absolute administrative claim that reverses the stated position.

272.s: PM-JANMAN, launched in 2023, is primarily associated with
272.x: PM-JANMAN is the central mission for habitations of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups.
272.tq: Match the named mission with its specific target group.

272.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, habitat rights of PVTGs are covered under
272.x: Habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 are specifically referred to in Section 3(1)(e).
272.tq: Test an exact statutory provision with nearby article-like distractors.

272.s: Which PVTG was the first to receive habitat rights under the Forest Rights Act framework?
272.x: Bharia of Madhya Pradesh was the first PVTG stated to have received habitat rights.
272.tq: Use a first-occurrence question with geographically close tribal distractors.

272.s: Eetela Panduga, also known as Chaitrapurab, is associated with
o: the harvest festival of the Lambadas
the birth ceremony of Koya boys
the spring festival of the Araku tribes
272.x: Eetela Panduga or Chaitrapurab is the spring festival of the Araku tribes, during which Dhimsa is danced.
272.tq: Link a regional festival with its tribe and season.

272.s: Which festival is associated with Lambadi communities and is observed in Ashada?
272.x: Seethala Panduga is a Lambadi festival observed in Ashada. It is also associated with Seethala Mata, who is believed to guard against smallpox.
272.tq: Separate closely related festivals by tribe and occasion.

272.s:
Consider the following statements about Lambadi festivals:
1. Balula Panduga is associated with cattle.
2. Heli Panduga or Jari Gundu is associated with newborn sons.
3. Jojer Nrutyam is associated with Heli Panduga.
4. Deepavali is called Kalimas by the Lambadis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: All four statements correctly describe the stated Lambadi festivals, their occasions and associated terminology.
272.tq: Test several entries from a festival cluster through a coded combination.

272.s: Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of which area?
272.x: Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of the Paderu agency, where an annual tribal jatara is held.
272.tq: Match a deity with the precise agency region associated with her worship.

272.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
272.x: Kommu is the Koya dance and is associated with bison-horn headgear. Gussadi is associated with Gond communities, Lambadi dance with Lambada women, and Dhimsa with several tribes.
272.tq: Use a familiar dance–tribe pair and reject over-exclusive distractors.

272.s: Gussadi is primarily associated with which tribal community?
272.x: Gussadi is a dance associated with the Gond community on the Telangana side.
272.tq: Directly identify the community associated with a named dance.

272.s: Lambadi dance is traditionally performed by
272.x: Lambadi dance is associated with Lambada or Sugali women, also known as Banjara women.
272.tq: Test performer identity rather than merely the dance name.

272.s:
Which of the following statements about Dhimsa is correct?
1. It is performed by groups of about 15–20 women in circles.
2. The dancers place their hands on one another’s shoulders.
3. Its themes include mythology, kinship and livelihood.
4. Its origin is traced to Koraput.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: All four statements describe the form, themes and stated origin of Dhimsa.
272.tq: Combine performance structure, themes and origin in a multi-statement question.

272.s: Which of the following sets contains only instruments associated with Dhimsa?
272.x: The instruments associated with Dhimsa include dappu, tudumu, mori, kidgi, gilka and jodukommulu.
272.tq: Identify the correct instrument cluster rather than a single item.

272.s: Dhimsa is particularly associated with which regions of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts
Nellore and Sri Sathya Sai districts
272.x: The stated regional association of Dhimsa is with the Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam areas.
272.tq: Test the regional spread of a cultural practice through district pairs.

272.s: The Kommu dance of the Koyas is especially associated with
272.x: Koya performers of the Kommu dance are associated with bison-horn headgear.
272.tq: Test a distinctive visual feature of a dance tradition.

272.s: Among the following, which correctly describes Chenchu social organisation?
o: Endogamous tribe and absence of clans
272.x: The Chenchus are an endogamous tribe with exogamous clans or kulams/gothrams; their organisation is patriarchal and patrilineal.
272.tq: Discriminate between tribe-level endogamy and clan-level exogamy.

272.s:
Which of the following statements about Chenchu clans is correct?
1. Chenchu clans are exogamous.
2. The clan system has no hierarchy.
3. Chenchu society is patriarchal and patrilineal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: Chenchu clans are exogamous, there is no clan hierarchy, and the society is patriarchal and patrilineal.
272.tq: Combine kinship rules with the broader social structure.

272.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to Chenchu village offices and clans?
272.x: Raju is associated with the Bhoomani clan. Mantri is associated with Kumakula, while Kolagadu belongs to Dasari, Uttaluri or Mandla clans.
272.tq: Start from a sure office–clan pair and distinguish the remaining entries.

272.s: In each Chenchu village, the offices of Raju, Mantri and Kolagadu are significant because
o: their holders come from different clans and officiate marriages
they administer only forest produce collection
they are appointed by the Governor
they represent three divisions of one clan
272.x: The three village office holders come from different clans and officiate marriages in each Chenchu village.
272.tq: Apply an institutional relationship to a social situation.

272.s: The Ghotul, as a youth dormitory institution, is associated with the
272.x: Ghotul is the example of a youth dormitory associated with the Muria of Chhattisgarh.
272.tq: Match a distinctive social institution with its tribe.

272.s: The description of a tribe as a “segmental organisation” of equivalent multi-family groups is associated with
272.x: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent multi-family groups.
272.tq: Match a sociological formulation with its scholar.

272.s: Under Article 366(25) of the Constitution, Scheduled Tribes are defined by reference to
272.x: Article 366(25) defines Scheduled Tribes by reference to the communities notified under Article 342.
272.tq: Use an exact constitutional cross-reference with nearby article distractors.

272.s:
Consider the following statements regarding notification and amendment of the Scheduled Tribes list:
1. The President notifies the Scheduled Tribes after consulting the Governor.
2. Parliament alone can amend the list.
3. Article 342(2) is associated with amendment of the list.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: The President notifies the list after consulting the Governor, while Parliament alone can amend it under the constitutional framework including Article 342(2).
272.tq: Separate the notifying authority from the amending authority.

272.s: Scheduled Areas are provided for under which Schedule of the Constitution?
272.x: Scheduled Areas are provided for under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution.
272.tq: Test an exact constitutional Schedule number.

272.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated criteria used in identifying tribal communities?
272.x: The stated criteria include primitive traits, distinctive culture, shyness of contact, geographical isolation and backwardness. Compulsory urban residence is not one of them.
272.tq: Find the clearly incompatible criterion in a standard list.

272.s: Idital wall paintings are associated with which tribal community?
272.x: Idital wall paintings are associated with the Savara, also known as Sora, community.
272.tq: Match a distinctive art form with its tribal community.

272.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
272.x: Warli art is associated with Maharashtra. Pithora is associated with the Rathwa of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, while Gond and Bhil are listed as comparative tribal arts.
272.tq: Use location reversal as the main trap in an art-form question.

272.s: Pithora painting is particularly associated with the
o: Rathwa of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
272.x: Pithora is associated with the Rathwa community of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
272.tq: Identify the community and region linked with a named art tradition.

272.s: Which combination best represents the traditional and emerging components of the agency economy in the Araku belt?
o: Tea plantations, jute mills and inland shipping
Rice deltas, marine fishing, salt production and shipbuilding
Coal mining, petroleum refining and heavy engineering
Podu, minor forest produce, coffee and horticulture
272.x: The agency economy includes podu or shifting cultivation, minor forest produce, and coffee and horticulture in the Araku belt.
272.tq: Distinguish the agency economy from plains and industrial economies.

272.s: Which language–tribe–family combination is correctly matched?
272.x: Sora is the language of the Savara and belongs to the Munda branch of the Austroasiatic family. Koya and Kuvi are Dravidian, while Lambadi is Indo-Aryan.
272.tq: Use a three-column match and eliminate by language-family reversal.

272.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Koya language — Koya tribe — Dravidian
2. Kuvi or Kui — Khond tribe — Dravidian
3. Gutob — Gadaba tribe — Munda
4. Lambadi or Gor Boli — Lambada tribe — Indo-Aryan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
272.x: All four language–tribe–family pairs are correctly matched.
272.tq: Verify all three dimensions of a language classification table.

272.s: Which language is associated with the Gadaba tribe and belongs to the Munda family?
272.x: Gutob is associated with the Gadaba tribe and belongs to the Munda family.
272.tq: Distinguish similar tribal language names by tribe and family.

272.s: The Guinness World Record relating to Dhimsa in Andhra Pradesh involved the participation of
o: more than 13,000 tribal women and girl students
272.x: The record was for the largest Dhimsa dance, involving more than 13,000 tribal women and girl students.
272.tq: Test the headline numerical figure with nearby figures from the same subject.

272.s: The record-setting large Dhimsa performance was held at
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
272.x: The large Dhimsa performance was held at Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in the Vizianagaram area.
272.tq: Match a current cultural event with its exact venue.

272.s: The certificate for the largest Dhimsa dance was awarded to the
o: All India Council for Technical Education
Tribal Research Institute of Madhya Pradesh
272.x: The certificate for the record was awarded to the Andhra Pradesh Tribal Welfare Department.
272.tq: Identify the receiving institution rather than the event venue.

272.s: World Adivasi Day tribal dance festival and art exhibition in Vijayawada was organised by the Tribal Welfare Department along with the
o: Tribal Cultural Research and Training Mission
272.x: The Vijayawada event was organised by the Tribal Welfare Department and the Tribal Cultural Research and Training Mission.
272.tq: Match an event with its two organising institutions.

272.s: The World Adivasi Day tribal dance festival and art exhibition was held at
272.x: The festival and exhibition were held at Tummalapalli Kalakshetram in Vijayawada.
272.tq: Separate similar current events by venue and city.

272.s: The Centre’s Tribes Art Fest was held at Travancore Palace, New Delhi, during
272.x: The Tribes Art Fest was held from 2 to 13 March 2026 at Travancore Palace in New Delhi.
272.tq: Test the exact date range of a current cultural event.

272.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Centre’s Tribes Art Fest?
o: It was held at Vijayawada during World Adivasi Day.
It displayed exactly 75 works from 12 PVTGs.
It focused exclusively on Dhimsa performers from Andhra Pradesh.
It displayed more than 1,000 works representing over 30 traditions.
272.x: The Tribes Art Fest presented more than 1,000 works representing over 30 traditions at Travancore Palace, New Delhi.
272.tq: Select the option combining the correct scale, diversity and event identity.

272.s: Who led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 in the Eastern Ghats?
272.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion in the Eastern Ghats from 1922 to 1924.
272.tq: Match a regional tribal movement with its leader and period.

272.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Dhebar Commission period associated with the PVTG concept
B. Rampa Rebellion
C. Enactment of the Forest Rights Act
D. Launch of PM-JANMAN
272.x: The Rampa Rebellion occurred in 1922–24, the Dhebar Commission period was 1960–61, the Forest Rights Act was enacted in 2006, and PM-JANMAN was launched in 2023.
272.tq: Fix the earliest movement first, then place the commission, legislation and mission.

272.s:
Which of the following statements regarding India’s Scheduled Tribe demographic profile is correct?
1. Scheduled Tribes constituted 8.6% of India’s population according to Census 2011.
2. Bhil is the largest tribe.
3. Gond is the second-largest tribe.
4. Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
272.x: All four statements reflect the stated comparative profile: STs formed 8.6% of India’s population, Bhil was the largest tribe, Gond the second-largest, and Madhya Pradesh had the largest tribal population.
272.tq: Combine percentage, rank and State-level comparison in one coded question.
